en: The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume One. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree. [279(36), 296, 297]
The Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Inconceivable Realm of Liberation. Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, within the Greatly Adorned Upper Chamber, together with five thousand Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, headed by the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Samantabhadra and the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Mañjuśrī;
their names were as follows:
The Bodhisattva Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Attachment-Free-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom,
the Bodhisattva Flower-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Sun-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Moon-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom,
the Bodhisattva Stainless-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Vajra-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom, and the Bodhisattva Free-from-Dust-and-Defilement-Wisdom-Surpassing Wisdom.
...the Bodhisattva Vairocanajñānavijaya, the Bodhisattva Nakṣatradhvaja, the Bodhisattva Merudhvaja,
the Bodhisattva Ratnavijayadhvaja, the Bodhisattva Asaṅgadhvaja, the Bodhisattva Puṣpadhvaja,
the Bodhisattva Vimaladhvaja, the Bodhisattva Sūryadhvaja, the Bodhisattva Sudhvaja, and the Bodhisattva Virajadhvaja.
Vairocanadhvaja Bodhisattva, Bhūmīryaśasprabha Bodhisattva, Ratneryaśasprabha Bodhisattva, Mahātejaḥprabha Bodhisattva,
Vajrajñānaprabha Bodhisattva, Vimalaprabha Bodhisattva, Dharmasūryaprabha Bodhisattva, Puṇyaparvataprabha Bodhisattva, and Jñānajvālāprabha Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadraśrīprabha, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadrārciḥprabha, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, Gaganagañja Bodhisattva, Padmagarbha Bodhisattva, Ratnagarbha Bodhisattva,
Sūryagarbha Bodhisattva, Viśuddhaguṇagarbha Bodhisattva, Dharmasāgaragarbha Bodhisattva, and Vairocanagarbha Bodhisattva.
Satsaṃgama Bodhisattva, Padmaśrīgarbha Bodhisattva, Sunetra Bodhisattva, Vimalanetra Bodhisattva,
Vimalacakṣus Bodhisattva, Asaṅganetra Bodhisattva, Samantadarśinetrā Bodhisattva,
Sunirīkṣaṇanetra Bodhisattva, Nīlotpalanetra Bodhisattva, and Vajranetra Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva Jewel-Eye, the Bodhisattva Space-Eye, the Bodhisattva Universal-Eye, the Bodhisattva Celestial-Crown,
the Bodhisattva Mani-Wisdom-Crown Illuminating the Dharma-Domain, the Bodhisattva Altar-of-Enlightenment-Crown,
the Bodhisattva Radiance-Illuminating-the-Ten-Directions-Crown, the Bodhisattva Crown Praised by All Buddhas, and the Bodhisattva Transcending...
The Bodhisattva Crown of All Worldly Sovereigns, the Bodhisattva Crown of Universal Radiance, the Bodhisattva Invincible Crown,
the Bodhisattva Crown Holding the Lion Thrones of All Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Crown of Great Light Universally Illuminating the Dharmadhātu and Space,
the Bodhisattva Brahmā-King Topknot, the Bodhisattva Śakra-Lord Topknot, and all others...
The Bodhisattva Buddha-Transformation-Differentiation-Light-Radiance-Crest, the Bodhisattva True-Bodhimanda-Crest,
the Bodhisattva Mani-King-Crest of the Sound of the Ocean of All Vows, the Bodhisattva Mani-King-Crest of the Circular Halo of All Buddhas Born from Great Renunciation,
and the Bodhisattva Mani-King-Crest of All Jewel Parasols Manifesting Equally with the Realm of Space.
The Bodhisattva Maṇirāja-keśa-canopied-with-the-network-of-all-Buddhas’-supernatural-powers-light-banner;
the Bodhisattva Sarvabuddha-mahādharmacakra-nirghoṣa-keśa; the Bodhisattva Mahāpuṇya-paripūrṇa-nāma-svara-keśa;
the Bodhisattva Mahājvālāprabha; the Bodhisattva Vimalajvālāprabha; and the Bodhisattva Vigatamala.
The Bodhisattva Tejoraśmi, the Bodhisattva Ratnaraśmi, the Bodhisattva Jyotiraśmi, the Bodhisattva Dharmaraśmi,
the Bodhisattva Śāntaraśmi, the Bodhisattva Sūryaraśmi, the Bodhisattva Abhijñāraśmi, the Bodhisattva Devaraśmi, the Bodhisattva Puṇyaskandha, and the Bodhisattva Jñānaskandha.
...the Bodhisattva Dharmarāśi, the Bodhisattva Abhijñārāśi, the Bodhisattva Arciṣmadrāśi,
the Bodhisattva Kusumarāśi, the Bodhisattva Bodhirāśi, the Bodhisattva Brahmārāśi, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvaprakāśarāśi,
the Bodhisattva Maṇiratnarāśi, the Bodhisattva Brahmaghoṣa, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsamudraghoṣa.
...the Bodhisattva Earth-Roar, the Bodhisattva World-Lord-Roar, the Bodhisattva Mountain-King-Sovereign-Roar,
the Bodhisattva Pervading-All-Dharma-Realm-Roar, the Bodhisattva All-Dharma-Ocean-Tide-Roar,
the Bodhisattva Destroying-All-Māra-Power-Roar, and the Bodhisattva Great-Compassion-Cloud-Thunder-Instruction-Roar.
The Bodhisattva Swift Protector of All Worlds from Suffering and Distress,
the Bodhisattva Dharma-Born, the Bodhisattva Supreme-Born, the Bodhisattva Wisdom-Born, the Bodhisattva Merit-Sumeru-Born,
the Bodhisattva Most Excellent Jewel-King of Virtues-Born, the Bodhisattva Renown-Born, and the Universal...
The Bodhisattva Born of Noble Light, the Bodhisattva Born of Great Compassion, the Bodhisattva Born of the Accumulation of Wisdom,
the Bodhisattva Born of the Tathāgata Lineage, the Bodhisattva Light-Auspiciousness, the Bodhisattva Supreme Auspiciousness,
the Bodhisattva Auspiciousness Born of Right Heroism, and the Bodhisattva Vairocana-Auspiciousness.
...the Bodhisattva Padmaśrī, the Bodhisattva Candraśrī, the Bodhisattva Gaganāśrī,
the Bodhisattva Ratnaśrī, the Bodhisattva Puñjaśrī, the Bodhisattva Prajñāśrī, the Bodhisattva Śailendrarāja, the Bodhisattva Dharmeśvararāja, and the Bodhisattva Lokendrarāja.
Brahmā-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva, Saṃkhyā-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva,
Nāga-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva, Śānti-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva, Acala-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva,
Prabhāva-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva, Parama-jaya-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva, and Parama-śāntaghoṣa Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Asamaprabha, the Bodhisattva Earth-Trembling Sound, the Bodhisattva Great Ocean Tide Sound, the Bodhisattva Great Cloud Thunder Sound,
the Bodhisattva Dharma-Light Sound, the Bodhisattva Space Sound, the Bodhisattva Sound of the Vast and Great Roots of Goodness of All Sentient Beings,
the Bodhisattva Sound of Expounding Past Great Vows, and the Bodhisattva Subduer of Māras.
The Bodhisattva Multitudinous Sound, the Bodhisattva Jewel Awakening, the Bodhisattva Sumeru Awakening,
the Bodhisattva Space Awakening, the Bodhisattva Stainless Awakening, the Bodhisattva Unattached Awakening, the Bodhisattva Vast Awakening,
the Bodhisattva Blossoming Awakening, the Bodhisattva Universally Illuminating the Three Times Awakening, and the Bodhisattva Vast Adornment Awakening.
The Bodhisattva Universal Observation-Awakening, the Bodhisattva Dharma-Realm Radiance-Awakening,
and other such leading Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas— all of whom were born from the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—
were unimpeded in all their actions.
Because they universally pervade all Buddha-fields; because they manifest infinite bodies to attend upon all Tathāgatas;
because, free from all veils and hindrances like the pure lunar disc, they universally manifest all the spiritual transformations of the Buddhas;

because they have attained the wisdom of present awakening and fully perceive the spheres of the sovereign supernormal powers manifested by all Buddhas; and because they have attained immeasurable luminosity.
Because they possess the light of wisdom that illuminates the ocean of the great Dharma-teachings of all Buddhas;
because they possess unimpeded analytical knowledge and, through pure eloquence, can expound the virtues of the Buddhas for immeasurable eons without exhaustion;

because they abide in the most supreme wisdom which is like space, their conduct being pure and free from attachment; and because they have no fixed dependence, acting in accordance with the minds of all sentient beings.
Because he manifests the body of form as he pleases; because he is free from all obscurations and understands that sentient beings, persons, and life-spanners are all non-existent;
and because his wisdom is universal like space, illuminating the dharma-realm with a great net of light.

Furthermore, he was accompanied by a community of five hundred śrāvakas. These śrāvakas possessed great majestic virtue; they had all awakened to the True Truths and realized the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). They had deeply entered the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) and forever emerged from the ocean of existence. Relying upon the space-like realm of the Tathāgata, they were free from the bonds of the fetters (*saṃyojana*) and clung to no basis. Their minds were as tranquil as empty space; having forever severed doubt and confusion in the presence of all Buddhas, they entered with deep faith into the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom.

Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable world-protectors who had already made offerings to countless Buddhas; they constantly and diligently worked for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, acting as uninvited friends to all beings and tirelessly protecting those without refuge. They did not abandon the mundane world to enter into superior wisdom, but were born from the realm of the Buddhas' teachings. They upheld all the True Dharma of the Tathāgatas, gave rise to great vows to ensure the lineage of the Buddhas was never severed, and were born into the family of the Tathāgatas through the power of their practices and vows, single-mindedly seeking the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes.
At that time, the bodhisattvas, the great śrāvakas, and the kings of the world together with their retinues all had this thought:
"The realm of the Tathāgata, the wisdom-practice of the Tathāgata, the supernormal powers of the Tathāgata,
the powers of the Tathāgata, the fearlessnesses of the Tathāgata, the samādhis of the Tathāgata, the dwelling of the Tathāgata, and the supremacy of the Tathāgata— "
The body of the Tathāgata and the wisdom of the Tathāgata cannot be penetrated,
cannot be entered, cannot be believed and understood, cannot be fully known, cannot be discerned,
cannot be contemplated, cannot be investigated, cannot be analyzed, and cannot be revealed by any gods or humans in all the worlds.
There is no one capable of causing sentient beings to awaken and enter [this state], except through the power of the Buddhas' empowerment,
the Buddhas' supernormal powers, the Buddhas' majestic virtue, the Buddhas' power of original vows, the power of their own roots of goodness from past lives,
the power of associating with virtuous friends, the power of profound and pure faith and understanding, and the power of vast aspiration and resolve.
The power of the pure mental force directed toward awakening; the power of the vast vows and practices for seeking all-knowledge;

we only pray that the World-Honored One, through the power of skillful means, will accord with the various capacities of mind, various inclinations, various wisdoms, various modes of expression, and various names of ourselves and all sentient beings.
Regarding names, various realizations, various stages, various purifications of the faculties,
various mental skillful means, various mental objects, and various supports—
the Tathāgata’s merit follows the ability to hear and receive all the teachings he has proclaimed, manifesting the path by which the Tathāgata formerly sought after omniscience.
The great vows of bodhisattvas raised in the past; the various pāramitās purified in the past;
the various bodhisattva stages realized in the past; the various bodhisattva practices fulfilled in the past;
the path adorned with wisdom mounted in the past; the various pure paths traversed in the past; and the sublime renunciations of the past.

The ocean of the supreme Dharma; the ocean of great adornments of playful supernatural powers formerly manifested; the ocean of immeasurable oceans of practices corresponding to past events formerly accumulated;
the ocean of supernatural wisdom that universally displays the gateways through which Tathāgatas manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment;
the ocean of the Tathāgata’s sovereign turning of the wheel of Dharma; and the supernatural power of the Tathāgata.
The ocean of purifying Buddha-fields; the ocean of Tathāgatas’ skillful means for subduing all sentient beings;
the Tathāgata’s revelation of the city of omniscience; the Tathāgata’s manifestation of the paths for all sentient beings;
the Tathāgata’s skillful entry into the realms of birth and death of all sentient beings; and the Tathāgata’s supreme merit for the sake of all sentient beings.
O Field of Merit, the Tathāgata universally expounds the merit of giving for the sake of all sentient beings;
the Tathāgata has prophesied the various mental activities of all sentient beings; the Tathāgata universally proclaims instructions and admonitions for all sentient beings;
and the Tathāgata is able to manifest various images through samādhi and supernormal powers—may such dharmas as these be graciously bestowed.
"Out of great compassion, he shall universally expound it.

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of all the bodhisattvas and the entire great assembly, took great compassion as his body, great compassion as his gateway, and great compassion as his head; employing the dharma of great compassion as his skillful means, he filled the void and pervaded the entire dharma-realm, entering the Lion’s Stretching Samādhi.
Having entered this samādhi, all worlds were universally purified and adorned.
At that time, this Great Adorned Pavilion suddenly became high, vast, and magnificent, pervading the entire Dharma-realm;

its floor was made of vajra, adorned with various jewels, and within it were arrayed nets of wish-fulfilling gems and banners of invincible victory; countless jewel-flowers and various maṇi-gems were scattered everywhere upon it, and heaps of all kinds of treasures filled every place; pillars made of vaidūrya gem radiated light that illuminated the world.

Adorned with the sovereign maṇi-jewel kings, and embellished all around with Jāmbūnada gold and various maṇis, all the doors, gates, windows, and casements reflect one another’s radiance in mutual array. The steps, courtyards, balconies, and railings are all decorated with exquisite jewels; their wondrous shapes and diverse forms manifest the various oceans of signs of all world-rulers and sentient beings. Maṇi-jewel nets cover them above, and beside each gate, banners and streamers are erected, each with its own adornments, emitting streams of light that pervade the entire Dharma-realm.

Outside the towers and pavilions, the number of steps, ledges, and railings is immeasurable and beyond description; they are all fashioned from maṇi-jewels and decorated throughout with a multitude of diverse, exquisite gems.

At that time, again by the spiritual power of the Buddha, the Jeta Grove suddenly became vast and expansive, equal in measure to as many Buddha-worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields; it was adorned with an interlacing array of all kinds of exquisite jewels.
Its ground was embellished with unspeakable numbers of gems, its perimeter was enclosed by walls of countless mani-jewels, and rows of precious tala trees stood in solemn procession between them.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable fragrant rivers filled with scented water, surging and swirling in eddies;
all manner of jewel flowers turned to the right with the current, producing the sounds of all Buddha-dharmas, while inconceivable jewel *puṇḍarīka* flowers bloomed in full splendor;
and all kinds of exquisite jewel *padma* flowers spread about in brilliant profusion.
Inconceivable numbers of exquisite jewel-flower trees, tall, prominent, and luxuriantly flourishing, were planted in rows along its banks;
inconceivable numbers of various miscellaneous jewels, terraces, pavilions, and watchtowers were arranged in successive lines upon those banks, all completely covered by nets of *maṇi* jewels.

Incalculable mani-jewels radiated great light, and the ground was adorned with incalculable varieties of exquisite treasures; heaps of fragrant treasuries rose up as clouds of incense, their pervasive scent wafting throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Furthermore, he erected immeasurable varieties of jeweled banners,
namely: immeasurable banners of precious incense, immeasurable banners of precious garments, immeasurable banners of precious pennants,
immeasurable banners of precious silken streamers, immeasurable banners of precious flowers, immeasurable banners of precious necklaces, and immeasurable banners of precious...
Garland banners; banners of immeasurable jewel bells; banners of immeasurable majestic jewel nets;
banners of immeasurable jewel-kings parasols; banners of immeasurable mani-jewel kings that universally illuminate with light;
banners of immeasurable mani-jewel kings that produce the perfect sounds of the names of all Tathāgatas; and immeasurable lion [banners].
There were mani-jewel king banners of wandering steps, mani-jewel king banners of the ocean of practices corresponding to the past deeds of all Tathāgatas as expounded in measureless ways,
and mani-jewel king banners that universally manifest the differentiated images of the dharma-realm;
such wonderful jewel banners as these pervaded the ten directions, adorning every place.
At that time, in the sky above the Jeta Grove, there appeared inconceivable clouds of celestial jewel palaces and multi-storied towers.

Furthermore, there were countless clouds of fragrant trees; unspeakable clouds of Mount Sumerus; unspeakable clouds of musical instruments that produced exquisite sounds to sing praises of the Tathāgata; unspeakable clouds of precious lotuses that covered and adorned everywhere; unspeakable clouds of precious lion thrones spread with celestial robes upon which Bodhisattvas sat and extolled the Buddha’s merits; unspeakable clouds of mani-jewels in the form of celestial kings; unspeakable clouds of white pearls; and unspeakable clouds of red pearl jewel pavilions that covered and adorned everywhere. Unspeakable clouds of all kinds of solid vajra-jewels rained down ornaments, such that all these clouds of precious adornments completely filled and decorated the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.
Why is this? Because the pure roots of goodness planted by the Tathāgata are inconceivable; because the accumulation of pure, white dharmas accomplished by the Tathāgata is inconceivable;
and because the secret empowerment of the Tathāgata’s majestic power is inconceivable.
It is inconceivable how the Tathāgata, through his supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*), can universally pervade all Buddha-worlds with a single body;
it is inconceivable how the Tathāgata, through his supernormal powers, can cause all Buddhas of the ten directions and all their Buddha-lands to enter into his own body;
and it is inconceivable how the Tathāgata can universally manifest everything within a single minute atom (*paramāṇu*).
Because the differentiation of worlds is inconceivable, the Tathāgata is able to manifest, upon each and every tip of a hair,
the successive order of the appearance of all Buddhas throughout the past limit; because this is inconceivable,
the Tathāgata is able to emit great rays of light from each and every pore, and each ray of light is able to illuminate all worlds— this is inconceivable.
Because of this deliberation, the Tathāgata is able to emit from each and every pore clouds of emanations as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields,
filling all Buddha-lands in an inconceivable manner; because of this deliberation, the Tathāgata is able to universally manifest within each and every pore the formation,
abiding, and destruction kalpas of all worlds throughout the ten directions in an inconceivable manner.
This is because of deliberation;

just as one sees the Buddha-land pure and adorned here in this Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Garden, so too does one see all worlds throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space in the ten directions.
That is to say:
he saw the body of the Tathāgata pervading the Jeta Grove, with the assemblies of bodhisattvas each perfectly complete;
he saw clouds of all kinds of ornaments raining down everywhere, establishing a magnificent array.
He saw clouds of light-radiance with the power to rain down all jewels, illuminating the entire dharma-realm;
he saw clouds raining down all mani-jewels, providing universal adornment;
he saw clouds raining down all kinds of ornamental canopies, covering all lands.
He saw clouds of transformations of all celestial bodies raining down everywhere, all exquisitely adorned;
he saw clouds of all flower-trees raining down everywhere, their blossoms in full bloom like the treasures of the ocean;
he saw clouds of all silken fabrics raining down everywhere, swirling and turning in graceful spirals.
He saw clouds of all kinds of garments raining down everywhere, falling in profusion;
he saw clouds of all kinds of flower garlands and necklaces raining down everywhere, continuing without interruption;
he saw clouds of all kinds of burning incense raining down everywhere, their forms swirling like the bodies of sentient beings.
He saw clouds of nets of exquisite jewel flowers raining everywhere, universally adorning all and continuing without interruption;
he saw clouds of powdered incense raining everywhere, their fragrance circulating and spreading throughout the ten directions;
he saw clouds of banners and pennants made of all kinds of jewels raining everywhere, held by celestial maidens who moved about within the realm of space.

He saw clouds of all kinds of precious canopies raining down everywhere; these canopies were perfectly circular, composed of various jewels, adorned above with exquisite lotuses, and emitted the sounds of music that reached throughout the dharma-realm.
He saw clouds of all kinds of precious lion thrones raining down everywhere, appearing in the forms of all sentient beings and adorned with various jewel garlands, nets, and necklaces.

At that time, Vairocana Tathāgata dwelt in this Lion’s Yawn Samādhi. Immediately, to the east, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, there was a world-ocean named Golden Sand Lamp Cloud Banner. There, the Buddha was named Vairocana Auspicious Majestic Virtue King.

Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vairocana Flame-Vow-Treasury Radiance, who, together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, received the teachings of that Buddha.

Departing from the ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment in that Buddha-land, he came toward the presence of Vairocana Buddha in this Sahā World, manifesting various clouds of offerings through his spiritual power.
That is to say:

clouds of celestial flowers, clouds of celestial incense, clouds of celestial jewel lotuses, clouds of celestial garlands, clouds of celestial jewels, clouds of celestial necklaces, bracelets, and armlets, clouds of celestial jewel parasols, clouds of celestial exquisite robes, clouds of celestial jewel banners and pennants, and clouds of all kinds of celestial exquisite jewel ornaments—all of which completely filled the dharma-realm of empty space;
having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet as an act of worship.
Having completed their acts of reverence, they immediately manifested in the eastern direction a pavilion adorned with jewels, covered above by a net of *maṇi* gems;

within this pavilion, they manifested lion thrones of great lotus-wombs made of the king of *maṇi* jewels that radiate light throughout the ten directions. Upon these thrones, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, each covering their body with a great *maṇi* jewel net of sovereign power.

To the south, beyond as many oceans of worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is an ocean of worlds named Vajra-ocean-treasury. Therein resides a Tathāgata named King of the Auspicious Treasury of Universal Radiance and Pervasive Illumination.

Within that assembly of the Tathāgata’s great ocean-like gathering, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named King of Unconquerable and Swift Diligence, accompanied by as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many oceans of worlds. From that Buddha’s assembly, they proceed toward the place where the Tathāgata dwells, all carrying various subtle and wondrous jeweled garlands and articles of offering through their supernatural powers, interlacing and adorning them.
These are as follows:

Carrying garlands of all kinds of exquisite jewel incense and flowers; carrying garlands of all kinds of exquisite jewel wheel-nets; carrying garlands of all kinds of precious flower necklaces; carrying garlands of all kinds of vajra-jewel necklaces; carrying garlands of all kinds of mani-jewel nets; carrying garlands of all kinds of precious silk ribbons; carrying garlands of all kinds of precious image necklaces; carrying garlands of all kinds of mani-jewels that manifest auspicious light; carrying garlands of all kinds of Vairocana-mani-adorned jewel nets; and carrying garlands of all kinds of lion-striding mani-jewel necklace-nets—they filled all oceans of worlds with their spiritual powers. Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, they prostrated themselves at the Buddha’s feet as an act of worship.

Having completed their acts of reverence, they immediately manifested in the southern direction a magnificent pavilion adorned with the various jewels of Vairocana, its surface completely covered by nets of *maṇi* gems;

within this pavilion, they manifested lion thrones made of *maṇi* lotus-blossoms that universally illumine the ten directions. Upon these thrones, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, their bodies draped in celestial nets of exquisite *kusuma* jewel-flowers.

To the west, beyond as many oceans of worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is an ocean of worlds named Sumeru-Ketu-Vairocana-Mani-Jewel-Lamp. Therein resides a Tathāgata named Dharma-Dhātu-Jñāna-Dīpa-Rāja (King of the Lamp of Wisdom of the Dharma Realm).

Within the great ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Samanta-Utpāda-Śrī-Tejas-Rāja (King of Universal Birth and Auspicious Splendor), who, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many oceans of worlds, departs from that Buddha’s assembly toward the place where the Tathāgata dwells. By means of their spiritual powers, they manifest various clouds of Mount Sumerus, namely:
Clouds of Mount Sumeru made of various colored banners, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
clouds of Mount Sumeru made of various colored ointments, incenses, and powdered perfumes, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
clouds of Mount Sumeru made of exquisite requisites consisting of mani-jewel kings adorned with various colors of golden light, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Clouds of Sumeru mountains like banners of constellations, perfectly adorned with various flames as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
clouds of Sumeru mountains of spheres adorned with various exquisite colors of *vajra*-moon-treasury *maṇi* jewel-kings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
clouds of Sumeru mountains of *jāmbūnada* gold *maṇi* king-banners, whose various radiances universally illuminate the dharma-realm, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
Clouds of Sumeru mountains of various dharma-realm distinctions, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, with light universally illuminating all mani-jewel king banners;
clouds of Sumeru mountains of mani-jewel kings representing the various marks and signs of all Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;

and clouds of Sumeru mountains of mani-jewel king banners with subtle sounds of the ocean of practices corresponding to the original causes and conditions of all the bodhisattva practices formerly cultivated by all Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
Clouds of Sumeru mountains made of mani-jewel kings, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields, with all Tathāgatas seated throughout their sites of enlightenment,
completely filling the space of the Dharma-realm;
having arrived at the presence of the Buddhas, they prostrated themselves at the Buddhas' feet as an act of worship.

Having completed their acts of reverence, they immediately manifested in the western direction a pavilion made of all kinds of kings of incense, its surface completely covered by nets of genuine jewels.

Within that pavilion, they manifested lion thrones of various *indrala* differentiated-light banners and *maṇi*-jewel kings, which were treasuries of wondrous lotuses. Upon these, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, each wearing a crown of *cintāmaṇi* jewels and having their bodies draped with nets of *maṇi* pearls of diverse exquisite colors.

To the north, beyond as many oceans of worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is an ocean of worlds named Jewel-Raiment Radiant Flame Banner. Therein resides a Tathāgata named Auspicious Great Radiance Illuminating All Space and the Dharma Realm.

Within that assembly of the Tathāgata’s great multitude, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Unobstructed Auspicious Supreme Treasury King, who, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many oceans of worlds, departs from that Buddha’s assembly for the place where the Tathāgata is. By means of their supernatural powers, they manifest clouds of all kinds of exquisite jewel raiments, universally adorning the entirety of space. These are as follows:
Clouds of yellow-light maṇi-jewel king robes; clouds of various fragrant-incense-scented maṇi-jewel king robes;
clouds of pure and wondrous sun-banner maṇi-jewel king robes; clouds of golden-flame-blazing auspiciously radiant maṇi-jewel king robes;
clouds of multicolored jewel-flowing-light maṇi-jewel king robes; one...
Clouds of garments of the king of mani jewels in the form of all supreme and sublime constellations;

clouds of garments of the king of mani jewels of Indra’s net with the radiant flames of white jade; clouds of garments of the king of mani jewels of Vairocana’s most excellent, brilliant, and auspicious radiant flames;
illuminating all realms and able to cause all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions [to be manifest].
All these clouds— clouds of Vairocana-maṇi-rāja garments, clouds of ocean-adornment maṇi-rāja garments,
and so forth— each emit light rays that interpenetrate one another, filling the entirety of space and the dharma-realm.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, they prostrated themselves at the Buddha’s feet as an act of worship.

Once their respectful salutations were complete, they immediately manifested in the northern direction a great ocean from which arose a pavilion made of the king of *maṇi* jewels and a lion throne within a treasury of exquisite *vaiḍūrya* lotuses. Upon these, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged; each wore a crest-jewel of the *maṇi* king known as the "Wondrously Adorned Treasury of the Constellation Banner," and their bodies were draped with nets of *maṇi* jewels called the "King of Lion’s Gait and Sublime Majesty."

To the northeast, beyond as many world-oceans as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, there is a world-ocean named All-Earth-Kings. Therein resides a Tathāgata named Jewel-Light-Net-Radiance-Pervading-Dharma-Domain-Formless-Eye;
within that ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Wondrous-Manifestation-Pervading-Dharma-Domain-Vow-Moon-King.

Together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans, he departs from that Buddha’s assembly toward the place where the Tathāgata dwells, manifesting through his spiritual power various clouds of pavilions adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels.

That is to say: clouds of pavilions manifesting all jewel banners; clouds of pavilions manifesting all kings of incense; clouds of pavilions manifesting all burning incense; clouds of pavilions manifesting all white sandalwood incense; clouds of pavilions manifesting all *kusuma* flowers; clouds of pavilions manifesting all *maṇi-ratna* kings; clouds of pavilions manifesting all *vajra-ratna* kings; clouds of pavilions manifesting all Jāmbūnada gold; clouds of pavilions manifesting all silken garments; and clouds of pavilions manifesting all various wondrous lotuses—such clouds as these each completely pervade the space of the Dharma-realm.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s abode, they prostrate at the Buddha’s feet as an act of worship.

Having completed their acts of reverence, they immediately manifested in the northeastern quarter a pavilion made of the king of mani-jewels atop a mountain peak of exquisite jewels, which serves as a gateway to all dharma-realms, along with lion thrones of the treasury of lotuses made of incomparable king-of-incense mani-jewels. Upon these, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, each adorned with a magnificent crown of various colored king-of-mani jewels and their bodies draped in nets of *kusuma* flowers and wish-fulfilling jewels.

To the southeast, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, there is a world-ocean named Fragrant Cloud Adorned Banner; the Buddha there is named Dragon Sovereign King.

Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Dharma-Wisdom Radiance Majestic Virtue King, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans, departs from that Buddha’s assembly toward the place where the Tathāgata resides. By means of their spiritual powers, they manifest various clouds of perfect radiance in the colors of exquisite, superior jewels; namely:

Clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of golden banners; clouds of perfect radiant light in the colors of immeasurable jewels; clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of the Tathāgata’s uṣṇīṣa; clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of the Tathāgata’s ūrṇā-kośa between the eyebrows; clouds of perfect radiant light in the colors of various jewels; clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of the lotus treasury; clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of hanging branches of jewel trees; clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of the king of maṇi-jewels; clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of Jāmbūnada gold; and clouds of perfect radiant light in the color of the sun, moon, and stars—each of these clouds filled the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm. Having arrived at the presence of the Buddha, they prostrated at his feet as an act of worship.

Having completed their acts of veneration, they immediately manifested in the southeastern direction a pavilion made of the auspicious Vairocana-maṇi-rāja jewels and *kusuma* flowers of stainless maṇis, as well as lion thrones within lotus calyxes of vajra-maṇi jewels. Upon these, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, their bodies covered by nets of maṇi-kings with the blazing radiance of various jewels.

To the southwest, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is a world-ocean named Solar Treasury Radiance Maṇi Jewel King. Therein resides a Tathāgata named Universal Wisdom Illumination Dharma Moon King.

Within that assembly of the Tathāgata’s great ocean-like congregation, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Wisdom Banner King Who Shatters All Mara’s Powers. Accompanied by as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans, he departs from that Buddha’s assembly for the place where the Tathāgata resides, emitting from every pore various clouds of flames equal in extent to the realm of empty space; namely:

Clouds of jewel-flame *kusuma* flowers, clouds of jewel-flame from various musical instruments, clouds of jewel-flame of all colors, clouds of adamantine jewel-flame, clouds of jewel-flame from various fragrant incense-scented robes, clouds of jewel-flame like the lightning of dragons, clouds of jewel-flame from Vairocana-maṇi jewels, clouds of jewel-flame from soaring-radiance maṇi jewels, clouds of jewel-flame from auspicious, blazing light-treasury maṇi jewels, and clouds of jewel-flame from the maṇi jewels of the ocean of universal light teachings of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time—each of these clouds issued forth from every pore and pervaded the realm of empty space;
having reached the presence of the Buddha, they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet as an act of worship.

Having completed their acts of reverence, they immediately manifested in the southwest a tower-palace made of various *maṇi* jewel-kings of light that universally appear throughout the ten directions of the Dharma-realm, as well as lion thrones within a supreme lotus treasury made of *maṇi* jewel-kings of fragrant flame-light. Upon these, the assembly of bodhisattvas each sat cross-legged, their bodies covered by exquisite nets of light from *maṇi* jewel-kings of the stainless treasury.

To the northwest, beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, there is a world-ocean named Vairocana-Vow-Treasury. Therein resides a Tathāgata named Universal Radiance Pervading the King of Sumeru Mountains.

Within that assembly of the Tathāgata’s ocean-like congregation, there is a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Vairocana-Vow-Wisdom Constellation Banner, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many world-oceans. From that Buddha’s assembly, they proceed toward the place where the Tathāgata is; in every thought-moment, from every mark and sign, every limb, and every single pore of their bodies, they each produce clouds of all images of the three periods of time.
These are as follows:

They emitted clouds of images of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of all Bodhisattvas; clouds of images of the assemblies of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of the wheels of emanations of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of bodies corresponding to the oceans of past deeds of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; clouds of images of the various colors and lights of the Bodhi trees of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of the supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas; clouds of images of the bodies of all world-protectors; and clouds of images of all pure Buddha-fields.

Moment by moment, they produced such clouds as these, each filling the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm. Having arrived at the presence of the Buddha, they prostrated at his feet as an act of worship.

Having completed their acts of veneration, they immediately manifested in the northwest direction a pavilion adorned with the king of *vairocana* mani-jewels that universally illumines the ten directions, as well as lion thrones within a great lotus treasury made of the king of *maṇi* jewels whose light shines throughout all worlds. Upon these, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, each wearing a *maṇi* jewel crown of universal flaming radiance, and their bodies were draped with nets of pearls of invincible light.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume One;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśa, by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra for Entering the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation.

At that time, beyond an ocean of worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields in the direction below, there was an ocean of worlds named Universal Radiance of the Perfect Flames of All Tathāgatas. The Buddha there was named King of the Banner of Unattached Wisdom Stars.

Within the great ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Sovereign King of Courageous Wisdom Who Shatters All Veils and Obstructions. Together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many oceans of worlds, he departed from that Buddha’s assembly toward the place where the Tathāgata was. By means of his spiritual powers, from every single pore upon his body, he emitted clouds of wondrous sounds that expounded various oceans of Dharma.
That is to say:
they manifest clouds of oceanic sounds proclaiming the *dhāraṇī* of all sentient beings’ languages and the meanings of all phenomena;
they manifest clouds of oceanic sounds proclaiming the methods of practice of all Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time; they manifest... [proclaiming]...
The cloud of sounds of the ocean of skillful means of all bodhisattvas' vows;
the cloud of sounds proclaiming the ocean of all bodhisattvas' perfectly pure *pāramitās*;
the cloud of sounds proclaiming the ocean of all bodhisattvas' perfected practices throughout all lands; the cloud of sounds proclaiming the fulfillment of all bodhisattvas...

Clouds of sounds from the ocean of wheels of various supernormal powers; clouds of sounds from the ocean of wheels of supernormal powers that manifest the preaching of all Tathāgatas approaching the site of enlightenment, destroying the hosts of Māra, and exhausting all afflictions to achieve equal and perfect awakening;
clouds of sounds from the ocean of sūtras consisting of various names and phrases that manifest the preaching of all Tathāgatas turning the sublime wheel of Dharma.
Clouds of sound that manifest and proclaim the ocean of skillful means for teaching and taming sentient beings according to their needs of all Tathāgatas;

clouds of sound that manifest and proclaim the ocean of skillful means for causing all to universally attain the wisdom of all-knowledge at all times, in accordance with their roots of goodness and the power of their vows of all Tathāgatas.
Clouds such as these, each filling the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, arrived at the presence of the Buddha.

They prostrated at the Buddha’s feet as an act of offering; having completed their expressions of reverence, they immediately manifested below, creating palaces of all Tathāgatas, jewel towers with various treasuries of radiant colors, and all [other adornments].
Upon exquisite lion thrones of precious lotus-blossom matrices, the assembly of bodhisattvas each sat cross-legged,
their bodies adorned with crowns of sovereign maṇi-jewels that emitted light-pennants manifesting the images of all sites of enlightenment.

Above, passing through as many oceans of worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is an ocean of worlds named Endless Buddha-lineage. Therein dwells a Tathāgata named Great Sound King of Universal Wisdom, Perfectly Differentiated Radiance;

within that Tathāgata’s great ocean-like assembly, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Ultimate of Vows Pervading the Dharma-realm, accompanied by as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many oceans of worlds.
Having received the teachings of those Buddhas and set out from their respective sites of enlightenment, they have come toward this Sahā world to the presence of Vairocana Tathāgata;
by means of their supernatural powers, each has [manifested] within all the marks and signs of excellence,
all the parts of their bodies, all their limbs and joints, all their pores, and all their voices—
Within all names and phrases, all garments, and all ornaments,
there appear Vairocana and all other Buddhas of the past limit, all Buddhas of the future limit,
and all Buddhas of the present limit, together with their assemblies, in the pure lands of the ten directions.
The various defilements, whether broad or narrow, large or small, all appear therein;

it also manifests the *dānapāramitā* practiced by that Buddha in the past—the ocean of practices corresponding to the recipients, the material goods, the original events, and the reflected images, all accumulated in accordance with them;
it also manifests the *śīlapāramitā* practiced by that Buddha in the past—the ocean of practices corresponding to the original events and reflected images, all accumulated in accordance with them.

They also manifest the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of past events, in which that Buddha, while practicing the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*) in the past, had his limbs severed yet remained undisturbed in mind, accumulating them in accordance with those events;

they also manifest the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of past events, in which that Buddha, while practicing the perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*) in the past, was courageous and non-regressive, accumulating them in accordance with those events;

they also manifest the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of past events, in which that Buddha, seeking all the perfections of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-pāramitā*) of the Tathāgatas in the past, attained accomplishment by accumulating them in accordance with those events.

They also manifest the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of the fundamental events of that Buddha’s past seeking of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Tathāgatas, and the dharmas he accomplished—including the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of his fundamental events of generating a courageous mind and relinquishing everything;

they also manifest the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of the fundamental events of that Buddha’s past accomplishment of the *upāyapāramitā*, including his delight in beholding all Buddhas, his delight in practicing all bodhisattva paths, and his delight in transforming all realms of sentient beings;

they also manifest the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of the fundamental events of that Buddha’s past generation of the *praṇidhānapāramitā*, including the vast vows of all bodhisattvas and their pure adornments.

They also manifested the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of all the past deeds of that Buddha’s various powers of the *pāramitās* of a bodhisattva, which are the harmonious union of purified and diverse activities;

they also manifested the ocean of practices corresponding to the images of all the past deeds of that Buddha’s various wisdoms of the *pāramitās* of a bodhisattva, which are the perfected and purified gateways to the realization of diverse dharmas.
Thus, the oceans of practices corresponding to the images of all the past deeds of all Tathāgatas completely filled the vast realm of the Dharma.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, they prostrated themselves at the Buddha’s feet as an act of worship. Once their reverent salutations were complete, they immediately manifested above in the sky a pavilion adorned with various treasuries of all kinds of vajra-jewel kings, as well as lion thrones of the lotus-treasury made of indranīla-vajra-jewel kings. Upon these, the assembly of bodhisattvas sat cross-legged, proclaiming the ocean of great sounds that are the names of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
they wore crests of mani-jewel kings, crowns adorned with bright pearls, and their bodies were covered by nets of mani-kings blazing with the light-flames of all exquisite jewels.

In this way, all Bodhisattvas from the ten directions, each employing various supernormal powers, raised clouds of diverse offerings and came to the site of enlightenment, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.

These Bodhisattvas, together with their retinues, were all born from the practices and vows of Samantabhadra; with the eye of pure wisdom, they universally beheld all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

Beholding the ocean of various marks that all delight in seeing, they attain unimpeded ears; having universally heard the ocean of sūtras of the wheel of Dharma turned by all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions, they reach the ultimate further shore of the most supreme mastery of all bodhisattvas. In every thought-moment, they manifest great spiritual transformations, able to draw near to all Buddhas of the ten directions; a single body fills all worlds, appearing universally in the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas, with light shining everywhere throughout all worlds.

Within a single atom, they universally manifest throughout the ten directions, across all worlds as far as the limits of space; in those worlds, they manifest various bodies to tame and bring to maturity those sentient beings who are ready for transformation, never missing the proper time.
From every pore, they emit great sounds that reach everywhere throughout the ten directions, expounding the clouds of the Tathāgata’s wondrous wheel of Dharma and its vast realms.

They know that all sentient beings are entirely like illusions; they know that all Tathāgatas are entirely like reflections; they know that the karmic actions and births within the various realms and destinies are entirely like dreams; they know that the retributions manifested in all worlds are like images in a mirror; they know that the arising of all births in all worlds is like a mirage in the heat; and they know that all lands abide based upon the mind and thoughts, being entirely like magical transformations.

They have attained mastery over the majestic power of the Tathāgata’s ten kinds of intellectual strength; like great bull-kings, they have attained fearlessness and can roar the lion’s roar. They have entered deeply into the ocean of inexhaustible eloquence and thoroughly understood the ocean of all sentient beings’ secrets. They have entered deeply into the ocean of wisdom regarding letters and languages, and they have realized that the dharma-realm is like space.

Having attained the spiritual powers, wisdom, and majestic might of all bodhisattvas, they are courageous and valiant, subduing the armies of Māra. Their intellectual power is clear and penetrating, and they understand the three periods of time. Knowing that all phenomena are without conflict, they constantly seek the ground of omniscience.

With uninterrupted wisdom, they enter all worlds; with the wisdom of the dharma-realm, they bring forth the ocean of teachings. Having attained the power of spiritual penetrations, they are able to cause all worlds throughout the ten directions to enter into one another.
Having attained the power of roots of goodness, they take birth with sovereign mastery throughout all worlds;
having attained the all-pervading eye, they universally behold all worlds in the ten directions, whether broad or narrow, large or small;

having attained unimpeded wisdom, they manifest vast lands within subtle realms and manifest subtle lands within vast realms; by the power of their sovereignty, they receive the empowerment of the merit, wisdom, and majestic spiritual authority of all Buddhas within a single Buddha-field; they universally behold the ten directions without doubt or hesitation, and in a single thought-moment, they are able to pervade all oceans of lands in the ten directions through their supernormal powers.
The Great Bodhisattvas, endowed with such immeasurable merits, filled the Jeta Grove entirely through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata. At that time, the foremost great Śrāvakas—

Mahāmati Śāriputra, the supernaturally gifted Maudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Revata, Subhūti, Aniruddha, Nanda, Kapphiṇa, Kātyāyana, and Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra— though present in the Jeta Grove, were all unable to perceive the Tathāgata’s spiritual power, the Tathāgata’s magnificent adornments, the Tathāgata’s realm, the Tathāgata’s playful manifestations, the Tathāgata’s miraculous transformations, the Tathāgata’s supreme excellence, the Tathāgata’s wondrous conduct, the Tathāgata’s majestic virtue, the Tathāgata’s empowerment, or the Tathāgata’s ocean of buddha-fields.
Furthermore, they do not see the inconceivable realm of bodhisattvas, the assemblies of bodhisattvas,
the universal entry of bodhisattvas, the approach of bodhisattvas, the supernormal powers of bodhisattvas, the playful manifestations of bodhisattvas,
the retinues of bodhisattvas, the regions of bodhisattvas, the lion thrones of bodhisattvas, the palaces of bodhisattvas, or the... [of bodhisattvas].
The majestic deportment of bodhisattvas, the samādhi of bodhisattvas, the universal observation of bodhisattvas, the lion’s stretch of bodhisattvas,
the valor of bodhisattvas, the offerings of bodhisattvas, the prophecy of bodhisattvas, the maturation of bodhisattvas,
the purity of the physical karma of bodhisattvas, the perfection of the wisdom-body of bodhisattvas, and the vows of bodhisattvas.
The manifestation of the body, the universal pervasiveness of the Bodhisattva’s form-body, the complete perfection of the Bodhisattva’s marks and signs,
the fullness of the Bodhisattva’s constant radiance, the emission of the Bodhisattva’s great net of light, the arising of the Bodhisattva’s clouds of transformations,
the universal pervasion of the Bodhisattva’s network of directions, and the perfection of the Bodhisattva’s various practices— all such varieties as these are entirely non-existent.
They see it.
Why is this? Because their roots of goodness are not the same.
This is because they did not, in the past, cultivate and accumulate the various roots of goodness of the wondrous supernatural powers of all Buddhas;
because they did not, in the past, praise and proclaim the pure merits of the universal adornments throughout the oceans of lands in the ten directions;
and because they did not, in the past, extol the various matters of the supernatural transformations of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
Because originally they were unable to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* within the cycle of birth and death;
because originally they did not exhort all sentient beings to abide in the vast bodhicitta;
and because originally they were unable to ensure that the lineage of the Tathāgatas would not be severed.
Because they did not originally apply themselves with diligence to gathering in all sentient beings;
because they did not originally exert themselves in practicing all the bodhisattva pāramitās;
and because they did not originally exhort sentient beings within saṃsāra to seek the eye of wisdom.

Because they did not originally cultivate the roots of goodness that accord with all-knowledge; because they did not originally awaken to the supreme roots of goodness of the Tathāgata’s appearance in the world;
because they did not originally attain the supernormal knowledge that universally adorns and purifies all Buddha-fields;
and because they did not originally attain the pure eye of the vast realm known by Bodhisattvas.
Because they originally did not seek the supreme, uncommon great roots of goodness that transcend the world;
because they originally did not give rise to the vast vows and the wisdom of renunciation of all bodhisattvas;
and because they were originally not born from the majestic empowerment of all Tathāgatas.
Originally, they were unable to know that all dharmas are like illusions;
originally, they were unable to know that the thoughts, conceptions, and mental graspings of what Bodhisattvas know are like dreams;
and originally, they were unable to attain the courageous, vast, and great aspiration and profound joy of Bodhisattvas.
All such various things are the realm of Samantabhadra’s eye of wisdom, which is not shared with any of the followers of the two vehicles.

For this reason, those eminent and virtuous śrāvakas were unable to hear it, unable to believe it, unable to know it, unable to see it, unable to recollect it, unable to observe it, unable to deliberate upon it, unable to contemplate it, unable to realize and enter it, and unable to discern it.
Why is this? Because the realm of the supernormal powers of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is not the narrow and inferior domain of those of the two vehicles.
Therefore, although they were within the Jeta Grove, they did not see the Tathāgata’s vast and great miraculous transformations.

Furthermore, those śrāvakas lack such supreme roots of goodness cultivated by bodhisattvas; they lack such pure eyes of wisdom for seeing the Buddha’s supernormal powers; they lack such profound samādhis for subtle observation; they lack such vast supernormal powers through which they are sustained; they lack such inconceivable gates of liberation; they lack such mastery over supernormal powers; they lack such great influence; they lack such great majesty and virtue; they lack such a supreme dwelling place; and they lack such a sphere of activity for the eye of wisdom.

Therefore, regarding this, they are unable to know it, unable to see it, unable to enter it, unable to attain it, unable to fully comprehend it, unable to give rise to it, unable to observe it, unable to endure it, unable to practice it, unable to abide in it, unable to reveal it, nor can they further explain it extensively for others; they are unable to praise it, unable to point it out, unable to bestow it, unable to take hold of it, unable to exhort them toward it, and unable to instruct and admonish them to cultivate it, to abide in it, and to realize and enter the realm of all Buddhas.

Why is this? It is because those śrāvakas do not possess such great wisdom; because they have attained liberation by relying on the Śrāvaka Vehicle; because they have entered the path of the śrāvakas to obtain wisdom; because they cultivate the practices of the śrāvakas seeking fulfillment; because they abide in the fruit of the śrāvakas as their ultimate goal; because they have realized the knowledge of the true reality of the śrāvakas; because they abide in the distinct sphere of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); because they delight in dwelling in tranquility for the sake of nirvāṇa; because they have abandoned great compassion for all worlds; because they remain far removed from protecting and rescuing all sentient beings; and because they constantly abide in their own affairs, tending toward personal extinction.
Therefore, although they were within the Jeta Grove, they did not see such various miraculous transformations.

Why is this? Because they were originally unable to aspire to, accumulate, desire, produce, cultivate, or purify the Tathāgata’s nature of omniscience; nor were they able to enter, practice, know, see, or realize the Tathāgata’s samādhis and supernormal powers.
Why is this? Such realms can only be seen and known by the vast eye of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, for they are not within the sphere of activity of the śrāvakas.

For this reason, although the great śrāvakas were staying within the Jeta Grove, they did not see the Tathāgata’s various miraculous transformations, various empowerments, various buddha-fields, or various pure adornments; nor did they see the universal display of supernatural powers by the great bodhisattvas throughout the assembly.

For example, on both banks of the Ganges there are many hundreds of billions of immeasurable hungry ghosts (*preta*). They are naked, famished, parched, emaciated, and haggard; their skin, flesh, sinews, and bones—both internally and externally—are scorched. Blown by the wind and blasted by the sun, their entire bodies are withered and dry, while crows, vultures, jackals, wolves, and various other malevolent birds and beasts compete to seize and devour them.

Driven by thirst and seeking water to drink, though they dwell by the river’s side, they do not see the river. Even if some should see it, they see it as parched and dried up, or they see flowing fire, or they see glowing embers.
Why is this? Because they are shrouded by profound and heavy karmic obstructions.
It is the same with the great śrāvakas; although they dwell within the Jeta Grove, they do not see the Tathāgata’s vast and great supernormal transformations.
Why is this? Because they do not delight in the knowledge of all modes, their eyes being obscured by the cataracts of ignorance;
and because they have never planted the supreme roots of goodness within the ground of omniscience.

For example, suppose there were a person who, while drowsily sleeping in a great assembly, suddenly dreamed of the Sudarśana Palace atop Mount Sumeru where Śakra dwells—a magnificent jeweled hall adorned with gardens;
where hundreds of thousands of millions of *devaputras* and *devakanyās* stand upon soft jewel grounds strewn everywhere with celestial flowers;
and where various trees of garments produce exquisite robes.
Various flowering trees were in full bloom with exquisite blossoms;
various jewel-trees produced all kinds of precious gems;
and various adornment-trees yielded all manner of ornaments.
The various musical trees played celestial music;
immeasurable devas sported therein.

Those people saw themselves wearing celestial garments, dwelling, moving about, and experiencing every kind of happiness; yet, although all the people within that assembly were in the same place, they could not see, know, or perceive one another.

Why is this? It is because the realms perceived by this person in his dream cannot be seen by that assembly. Likewise, the vast adornments and miraculous transformations perceived before them by all the Bodhisattvas and World-Rulers are also such:

because they have obtained the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Buddhas; because of the power of roots of goodness accumulated over a long time; because they have made the vast vows for omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); because they have cultivated the supreme merits of the Tathāgatas; because they are well-established in the path of Bodhisattva adornments; because they have perfected the gateways of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); because they have accomplished the various practices and vows of Samantabhadra; because they have entered the pure understanding of the Bodhisattva stages of omniscience; because they sport in the ocean of all Bodhisattva samādhis and supernatural powers (*abhijñā*); and because their wisdom observing all Bodhisattva realms is unimpeded.
Therefore, they are able to see and know the inconceivable realm of the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One’s sovereign play of supernatural powers;
whereas all the great disciples among the śrāvakas, despite possessing wisdom and superior supernatural powers, are unable to see it and unable to know it.
Why is this? It is because they lack the pure eye of a bodhisattva.

For example, on the Snowy Mountains there are many medicinal herbs, growing everywhere as if planted; yet there is a great physician who has achieved clear wisdom and knows the distinct natures and efficacies of all medicines, so that according to what each illness requires, he gathers them from among them. However, the hunters and herdsmen who dwell within those mountains neither see nor know of them, much less are able to gather them.
This case is also like that:

because the bodhisattvas universally enter the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom and give rise to the various playful manifestations (*vikrīḍita*) of a bodhisattva, they are able to comprehend the realm of the Tathāgata’s samādhis. The great disciples, however, have fundamentally not cultivated the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor can they bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings; thus, although they dwell within the Jeta Grove, they neither see nor know the vast and divine transformations of the Tathāgata’s samādhi.

It is like the great earth, which is the basis for all treasures and contains many hidden hoards; hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rare and diverse jewels fill every place, each one adorned and perfectly complete.
There is a man of great wisdom and discernment who knows well the locations of these treasure stores and understands the power and efficacy of the various jewels.

Furthermore, this man possesses great merit and power, enabling him to take whatever he desires with ease. He uses them to support his parents, provide for his kinsmen, and impartially relieve the elderly, the sick, and the destitute, ensuring that all who have needs are fully satisfied. Yet other people, lacking merit and wisdom, though they walk, stand, sit, or lie down upon that very ground of treasures, fail to see or know them because of their ignorance.

It is the same here: because the great bodhisattvas possess the pure and universal eye of wisdom, they are able to enter the inconceivable and profound realm of the Tathāgata within the Jeta Grove; they are able to behold the vast and great miraculous transformations of all Buddhas; they are able to comprehend all the Dharma-gates of the Buddhas; they are able to enter the boundless ocean of Buddha-samādhis; they are able to diligently serve and attend upon all Tathāgatas; they are able to awaken sentient beings through the supreme Dharma; and they are able to gather and sustain all classes of beings through the four means of integration. Although those śrāvakas dwell within the grove, they cannot perceive the supernatural power of the Tathāgata, nor do they see the assembly of bodhisattvas.

It is, for example, as if there were a person whose eyes were covered with a silken cloth; though they walk, stand, sit, or lie down upon a great island of jewels, they are unable to see the jewel-trees, jewel-garments, jewel-fragrances, or jewel-fruits, nor can they perceive the forms, colors, or the noble and base qualities of the various treasures. Yet another person, with eyes open, reaches that same place and sees everything, being able to discern it all clearly. So it is with the Bodhisattvas: when they arrive at the Tathāgata’s great island of Dharma-jewels, the place adorned with the most supreme merits, they see everything with perfect clarity. Although the Great Disciples remain in the grove in close proximity to the World-Honored One, they do not see the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual transformations or the realm of his samādhi, nor do they behold the universally adorned assembly of Bodhisattvas.

Why is this? Because the śrāvakas are not in accord with the Buddha’s wisdom; because ignorance covers and obstructs their eyes; because they lack the unimpeded knowledge of bodhisattvas; and because they cannot enter the dharma-realm in its successive stages—for these reasons, they do not see the Tathāgata’s sovereign samādhi and its various miraculous transformations.

It is like a medicinal herb named Stainless Light (*vimalaprabhā*); if a person applies it to their eyes, their vision becomes pure and no dark forms can obstruct it. Suppose this person is at night amidst a multitude of hundreds of thousands of people; they can clearly see the physical forms, postures, and the modes of walking, standing, sitting, and lying down of that entire assembly. Yet, none of those people in the crowd can perceive the person’s own postures, physical form, advances and retreats, or comings and goings. This case is exactly like that.

Those bodhisattvas have accomplished the Tathāgata’s pure eye of wisdom and are able to clearly perceive all worlds without any obstruction. The vast realm of their manifested samādhis and supernormal powers is surrounded by a multitude of great bodhisattvas, such that none of the great śrāvakas can see it at all.
For example, suppose a bhikṣu, in the midst of a great assembly, enters the meditative absorptions of the totalities (*kṛtsnāyatana*), namely:

the totality of earth, the totality of water, the totality of fire, the totality of wind, the totality of blue, the totality of yellow, the totality of red, the totality of white, the totality of heaven, the totality of the bodies of various sentient beings, the totality of all sounds and speech, and the totality of all objects of focus. When one enters these absorptions, they perceive the signs of the objects of focus—earth, water, and so forth—with light pervading everywhere, even unto the entire meditative sphere of all objects; yet the rest of the great assembly cannot see them at all, except for those who themselves abide in this samādhi.

This is also like that: the inconceivable realm of samādhi and supernormal powers manifested by the Tathāgata can be entered and known by all bodhisattvas, but it is neither known nor seen by any of those of the two vehicles.

For example, suppose there were a person who obtained a medicine for invisibility; by applying it to his eyes, his body would become concealed within a great assembly, such that no one could see him as he walked, stood, went, or came, yet he could perceive all the affairs within that assembly.

You should know that the Tathāgata is likewise: having achieved the eye of wisdom that transcends the world, he perceives the entire world universally without obstruction. The realms of samādhi and supernormal powers manifested by him cannot be known by any śrāvakas; they can be seen only by the great bodhisattvas who are progressing toward the realm of omniscience.
For example, when a person is first born into this world, two deities are born simultaneously with them: one is called "Born Together" (*sahaja*) and the other is called "Same Name" (*samānanāman*).
These deities constantly follow the person; the deity always sees the person, yet the person does not see the deity.

It is the same with the Tathāgata: he dwells in the vast samādhi and the sphere of supernormal powers of inconceivable omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), adorned by the assembly of great bodhisattvas, which all the śrāvakas are utterly unable to see.

For example, it is like a bhikṣu who has attained mastery over the mind and enters the meditative absorption of cessation (nirodha-samāpatti); in this state, perception and feeling are both extinguished, the functions of the six sense organs no longer operate, and yet it is not nirvāṇa. He neither knows nor perceives the shifting flow of the world.
Why is this? It is because they are sustained by the power of this samādhi.

Those great śrāvakas are likewise; although they dwell within the Jeta Grove and possess all six sense faculties, they do not see, know, understand, or enter into the vast realm of the Tathāgata’s sovereign supernormal transformations, nor do they see the samādhis and supernatural powers of the assembly of bodhisattvas.

Why is this? Because the realm of the Tathāgata is subtle, profound, secret, and vast; it is difficult to see, difficult to know, difficult to measure, and difficult to fathom. It transcends all that is conceivable within the mundane and supramundane worlds, is indestructible by any, and is not an object of knowledge for śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.

Therefore, the inconceivable realm manifested through the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual power—the adornment of his retinue, the assembly of bodhisattvas, and the Jeta Grove, which pervades all infinite asaṃkhyeya pure worlds—none of these things can be seen by any of those belonging to the two vehicles.
Why is this? Because they are not vast vessels for bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vairocana-jvālā-praṇidhāna-garbha-āloka, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
“Behold the Buddha’s wisdom, subtle and inconceivable;
within this Jeta Grove, his miraculous transformations are unsurpassed.
Through the majestic spiritual power of the Great Awakened One, countless practices are manifested.”
The world is deluded and does not understand the Buddha’s profound Dharma.
The Dharma of the King of the Profound is immeasurable and inconceivable;
the various supernormal powers he manifests cannot be fathomed by anyone in all the world.
The manifestations displayed by all Buddhas are beyond full praise;
though they adorn their bodies with marks, what they manifest is entirely without marks.
Through various supernatural transformations, the Buddhas appear within the Jeta Grove.
All that is manifested is profoundly deep, beyond the reach of words.
From inconceivable billions of lands, bodhisattvas endowed with virtue have gathered like clouds to honor the Buddha, adorning the great assembly with vast splendor.
His great vows are all fulfilled; his majestic deportment is free from attachment.
The realm of his inconceivable mind is such that no one in the world can know it.
Even pratyekabuddhas of sharp wisdom and those great śrāvakas [cannot fathom it].
None at all can know the sphere of the Bodhisattva’s practice.
The Bodhisattva’s wisdom is profoundly deep; most supreme and difficult to transcend, he raises the banner of diligence, which none can shake.
"Having entered immeasurable samādhis, Having attained great renown, Manifesting great supernormal powers,
Pervading throughout the entire dharma-realm. At that time,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva King of Unconquerable and Swift Diligence from the southern quarter, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
“Behold these sons of the Buddhas, Treasure-houses of wondrous wisdom and merit;
Able to gather the practices for enlightenment, They bring peace and happiness to all the worlds.
With the sublime majestic power of samādhi, And wisdom that is without limit.”
That mind and its objects are both utterly profound.
Now, in this Jeta Grove, the dwelling place of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
a multitude of bodhisattvas has gathered, universally manifesting great adornments.
Behold the ocean-like assembly of Bodhisattvas, free from attachment;
each sits upon a lotus throne, dwelling peacefully within the site of enlightenment.
They neither go nor come; they have no dependence and are free from all clinging.
Ultimately free from conceptual discrimination, they appear universally throughout the ten directions.
A banner of courageous great wisdom, firm and unshakable,
they manifest signs within the signless ocean, filling every realm as numerous as atoms.
To billions of lands in the ten directions, at the abodes of all Buddhas,
you go everywhere without dividing your body, entirely free from the marks of existence and non-existence.
Behold the Lion of the Śākyas and his various powers and supernormal faculties.
It causes bodhisattvas of great majestic power to gather like clouds;
the dharma-realm is without discrimination, and the bodies of all Buddhas are likewise so.
The world is merely a conventional designation, and the sons of the Buddha have fully realized this.
“The Buddhas abide in reality, at the limit of quiescent equality;
they constantly turn the wheel of distinctions, yet are unmoving and without conceptual discrimination.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Birth Auspicious Majestic Virtue King of the West, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Behold the Unsurpassed One, whose vast wisdom is perfected;
without discriminating between the opportune and the inopportune, he expounds the Dharma eternally without exhaustion.
He is able to subdue all non-Buddhists and their various divergent views.”
Universally following the minds of sentient beings, He manifests the power of spiritual transformations.
Perfect Awakening is neither finite nor infinite;
Whether finite or infinite, the Muni has transcended them all.
Like the sun dwelling in the void, its radiance constantly shines everywhere;
the Buddha’s wisdom is likewise able to dispel the darkness of the three periods of time.
Like the pure, full moon, all beings delight in beholding it.
When the Buddha’s virtues are perfected, all who behold him rejoice.
Like the sun in the sky, which traverses its course without ceasing for even a moment,
so too do the Buddhas manifest supernormal powers, continuing in an endless succession.
Just as the emptiness of the ten directions Does not obstruct any world-systems,
So too is the unobstructed mind Of the King who Illuminates the World with the Lamp of Wisdom.
Just as the earth of the world Is the common support for all things,
The Buddhas are likewise the refuge for all sentient beings.
Just as a swift wind moves through space without obstruction,
so too is the Buddha’s wisdom unimpeded within the world.
"Just as the great wheel of water is the support upon which the world rests, so too are the Buddhas of the three times; they always abide supported by the wheel of wisdom.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva King of the Unobstructed Auspicious Supreme Treasury from the northern direction, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
"Just as a great mountain of jewels universally benefits all sentient beings,
seeing the Buddha is likewise able to give rise to supramundane wisdom.
Just as the waters of the great ocean are deep, vast, pure, and stainless,"
Seeing the Buddha is likewise thus: it can extinguish all thirst and craving.
Just as Mount Sumeru rises high above the great ocean, so too is the mountain of wisdom, securely abiding within the deep ocean of the Dharma.
Just as the deep great ocean is the source from which all manner of jewels arise,
so too is the ocean of awakening, capable of producing all the jewels of wisdom.
The profound wisdom of the Hero of the World is both countless and immeasurable.
The various supernormal powers that are manifested cannot be measured by anyone.
Just as a skillful illusionist conjures forth all manner of forms, so too is the Buddha’s wisdom:
the extent of its manifestations and transformations is inconceivable.
Just as a maṇi jewel grants all desires according to one's will,
so too is the Jewel of the Buddha, able to fulfill all pure aspirations.
Just as a luminous and pure gem shines throughout the entirety of space, so does the Buddha illuminate the world.
The Jewel of the Buddha is likewise: it shines universally upon all beings.
Like a jewel with eight facets that reflects light in every direction, the lamp of unimpeded great wisdom illuminates the entire dharma-realm.
"Just as the water-purifying jewel can clear all turbid waters, so too is it when one sees the Buddha: all the faculties become completely pure.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva King of the Moon of Vows, whose Wondrous Transformations Pervade the Dharma Realm, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Just as the sapphire, when illuminating objects, makes them all the same color,
so too when sentient beings behold the Buddha, they share the color of the Buddha’s bodhi.
Within every atom of every land, all Buddhas manifest their spiritual transformations."
Moment by moment, they are ever-undying; those they transform are all made pure.
This profound and rare wisdom is inconceivable;
only Bodhisattvas can know it, while the multitudes of living beings cannot enter it.
The Buddha’s body is utterly pure, Adorned with the full complement of marks;
Pervasively entering the Dharma-realm, He brings all Bodhisattvas to fulfillment.
In inconceivable lands, He manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment everywhere.
Having subdued Māra and sat at the site of enlightenment, the Bodhisattvas surround him.
Śākyamuni, the Unsurpassed Honored One, is eternally sovereign over all dharmas;
throughout all atoms of lands, his supernormal powers are immeasurable.
