The various practices of the Bodhisattvas, Their unimpeded and wondrous radiance,
And the inconceivable power of the Buddhas— All these they are able to manifest.
Sons of the Buddha should skillfully study The most profound teachings of all Buddhas.
Having realized entry into all phenomena, The sphere of non-attached wisdom;
With the great majestic power of the Dharma King, He constantly turns the sublime Wheel of Dharma.
The various supernormal powers he manifests Are able to purify the realms of the ten directions.
"Profound and perfect wisdom, the true jewel of the world,
the great dragon king of Buddha-wisdom, can deliver all according to their hearts' desires. At that time,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharma-Wisdom Radiance Majestic Virtue King, in the southeast, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time,
all the great śrāvakas cannot know the subtle and wondrous Dharma possessed by the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, throughout those three periods of time, the pratyekabuddhas of the ten directions [cannot know it either]."
They do not even know the supernatural powers possessed by the Tathāgata;
how much less could the ordinary worldlings— who dwell in the cycle of saṃsāra, who are blind and ignorant,
and who are bound by the fetters of the defilements— be able to fathom the realm of the Buddha?
The Tathāgata’s unimpeded wisdom transcends both the measurable and the immeasurable;
it lies beyond the path of language, such that no one can describe it.
The Buddha adorns his body with the marks [of a great man], his concentrated radiance like that of the full moon.
Having cultivated patience through causes in past eons, you manifest throughout the ten directions.
To contemplate the power of all Buddhas, their samādhis, and their supernormal faculties—
even if one were to deliberate upon them for billions of eons— one could not know even a small fraction of them.
Contemplate with clarity the wisdom of all Buddhas; self-realized and wondrous, it is inconceivable.
Each and every gateway of merit—none can fathom its limits.
If there be those who give rise to great vows and take delight in the Buddha-dharma,
Regarding this realm that is difficult to perceive, it is not difficult to attain thorough penetration.
If one employs a pure mind, diligently accumulates merit and wisdom,
and is endowed with great virtue, one will be able to enter accordingly upon hearing the teaching.
“If a person relies upon the Buddha’s wisdom, And their aspiration is likewise vast and profound,
They are heading toward the Buddha’s Bodhi, And shall surely attain all-encompassing knowledge. At that time,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Wisdom Banner King Who Shatters All Māra-Powers from the southwest, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
“The body of wisdom is without attachment, Far removed from the characteristics of the physical body;
The inconceivable realm of the Buddha Cannot be known by any of the sages.
Through inconceivable pure karma, This subtle and wondrous body arises.”
The marks and signs, as well as the radiance, cannot be obstructed throughout the three periods of time.
They illuminate the world universally; the Dharma-realm is eternally pure.
Opening the gate of the Buddha’s Bodhi, one constantly gives birth to all-encompassing wisdom.
Your essence is pure and free from all defilements; having distanced yourself from every hindrance, you are like the sun in the world, universally radiating the light of wisdom.
You have forever severed the flow of the three realms and can eliminate the fear of birth and death.
They bring all bodhisattvas to fulfillment, causing their vows for enlightenment to be perfected.
They manifest immeasurable forms, yet these forms have no basis or abode;
though those manifested are immeasurable, all of them are inconceivable.
In a single thought-moment, the Buddha universally manifests inconceivable deeds;
the profound realm of Bodhi cannot be fathomed or known by anyone.
In a single thought-moment, the Buddha manifests the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Though that which appears is inexhaustible, the nature of mindfulness is never different.
The wise should reflect well: with every thought-moment constantly succeeding one another, there is only wisdom and no other activity, as they focus single-mindedly on the Bodhi of the Buddha.
"This Dharma is inconceivable; its nature is free from verbal expression and is not the domain of the mind—from this, all Buddhas are born.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vairocana-Pranidhijñāna-Jyotirdhvaja of the northwest, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
With pure mindfulness free from delusion and confusion, Bravely and constantly upholding the Dharma,
One with perfected wisdom can contemplate The inexhaustible ocean of bodhi.
If one attains definitive understanding, Then one can enter the realm of the Buddha.
From the arising of sovereign wisdom, all doubts and delusions are forever severed.
Moment by moment the mind advances; in all actions there is no weariness.
Always aspiring toward the Dharma, one shall ultimately realize all Buddha-dharmas.
From those various roots of goodness, one can give rise to vast faith;
always delighting in constant observation, one dwells without signs and without dependence.
Having constantly cultivated and gathered them for billions of eons, all roots of goodness are brought to fulfillment.
All for the sake of Buddha-enlightenment, they realize incomparable bliss.
Moving within the cycle of birth and death, they are not attached to birth and death;
having no doubt regarding the Dharma, they always delight in the realm of the Buddha.
Regarding all conditioned phenomena, And the worldly, illusory pleasures,
They have forever abandoned the mind of craving and attachment, Dedicating themselves solely to seeking the Buddha’s virtues.
Ordinary beings are deluded regarding the Buddha’s wisdom, Sinking and drowning in the flow of birth and death.
The Bodhisattva’s mind is free from attachment, universally rescuing all so that they may emerge [from suffering].
The Bodhisattva’s conduct is unshakable; throughout the world, none can fathom it.
Manifesting bodies in accordance with the various classes of beings, they bestow equal happiness upon all living creatures.
"Having purified the wisdom of enlightenment, You give rise to compassion for the world;
Like the sun appearing in the world, Your light shines without limit.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vīryaketu-vijitāvaraṇa-jñāneśvararāja from the direction below, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
"Throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, the name of a Buddha is difficult to hear;
how much more so to behold him face-to-face and have one's doubts dispelled.
The Tathāgata’s inexhaustible wisdom is the perfect lamp that illuminates the world."
The river of merit flows through the three periods of time, Capable of purifying all beings.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body Is pure and free from all faults;
though one gazes upon it for billions of eons, The mind never tires of it.
O Son of the Buddha, observe well the Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body:
his wisdom is pure and eternally unattached, capable of accomplishing the benefit of both self and others.
The Tathāgata’s profound power of wisdom and his inexhaustible, wondrous eloquence—
Opening the gateway to the Buddha’s bodhi, his teachings are entirely unimpeded.
The Honored One, the Muni of Universal Radiance, guides that inconceivable multitude,
bestowing upon them the prediction of supreme bodhi and causing them to ascend the gate of liberation.
A vast accumulation of merit has arisen in the world,
awakening all sentient beings and causing them to gather the practices of bodhi.
Having made offerings to all Buddhas, their wisdom-paramita is ever pure.
Able to shatter the net of all delusions, Forever eliminating the fear of the evil realms.
Able to behold the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings, One gives rise to the vow for great Bodhi;
Obtaining the Buddha’s power of mastery, One is able to produce the light of great wisdom.
"If one beholds the Honored One among Men, And the resolve for Buddhahood is firm,
Know that such a person as this Will surely attain the wisdom of the Tathāgata.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pervasive Dharma-Domain Great Vow Limit (Samantadharmadhātumahāpraṇidhānakoṭi), receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
“The Muni, the most distinguished and honored one, Whose manifold virtues are all perfected;
Those who behold him find their minds purified, And dedicate themselves toward Great Bodhi.
The Tathāgata has arisen in the world, Tranquil, with great compassion.”
Universally turning the sublime wheel of Dharma, Benefiting all sentient beings;
Throughout immeasurable kalpas, The Buddha toiled with hardship for the sake of living beings—
How can all these sentient beings Ever repay the Great Teacher’s kindness?
I would rather undergo the sufferings of the three miserable realms, Enduring them fully for immeasurable kalpas,
Than ever forsake the Tathāgata In my quest for liberation.
I would rather take the place of all sentient beings And endure the sufferings of saṃsāra forever.
One would never abandon the Tathāgata to seek even a slight pleasure;
rather, one would prefer to suffer in the evil realms for many eons while hearing the Buddha’s name than to be born in the good realms for a moment without hearing the Buddha.
It would be better to endure suffering in hell for many eons while constantly seeing the Buddha,
than to wish to leave the three miserable realms only to be born in a place where the Buddha-Dharma does not exist.
For what reason do you have no heart of weary detachment toward the evil paths?
By beholding the Dharma King, wisdom constantly increases.
Seeing the Buddha’s power of mastery, one can eliminate all suffering and enter the profound realm of the Tathāgatas’ wisdom.
When one is able to see the Buddha, all evil realms are extinguished,
the sprouts of merit and wisdom grow, and the fruit of Bodhi will surely be attained.
If sentient beings see the Buddha, they can shatter all manner of doubts.
"May all worldly and world-transcending joys, and all that is wished for, be fully perfected.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle Two;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle Three.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation through the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra surveyed the entire assembly of bodhisattvas. Desiring to reveal the Tathāgata’s supreme Great Lion-Stretching Samādhi, he addressed the bodhisattvas with skillful means equal to the realm of empty space, skillful means equal to the three periods of time, skillful means equal to the dharma-realm, and skillful means equal to all worlds, equal to all karmas, equal to the minds of all sentient beings, equal to the inclinations of all sentient beings, equal to the faculties of all sentient beings, equal to the timing for the maturation of all sentient beings, and equal to the light and shadows of all dharmas, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!
I shall now, for your sake, reveal and expound the realm of supernatural power of the Great Lion-Stretch Samādhi by means of ten kinds of pure phrases and names.”
What are these ten? They are:

the names and phrases of the Dharma-gate concerning the sequential appearance of all Buddhas within every atom of all Buddha-lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm, as manifested by Tathāgatas equal to the realm of empty space; and the sequential order of the formation and destruction of all lands.

The names and phrases of the Dharma-gates that praise the supreme merits of the Tathāgatas throughout all Buddha-fields equal to the realm of space, for as many eons as there are until the end of the future;
the names and phrases of the Dharma-gates that manifest the ocean of infinite gates to Bodhi whenever a Tathāgata appears in all Buddha-fields equal to the realm of space;

and the names and phrases of the Dharma-gates regarding the most excellent sites of enlightenment where Tathāgatas sit and the perfected realms of their assemblies of Bodhisattvas in all Buddha-fields equal to the realm of space.
The dharma-gate name and phrases for emitting clouds of transformation bodies of all Buddhas of the three periods of time from every pore in every moment of thought, filling the entire Dharma-realm;

the dharma-gate name and phrases for being able, through sovereign spiritual power, to universally manifest a single body throughout all oceans of lands in the ten directions, with light shining everywhere across the worlds of all Buddhas;

and the dharma-gate name and phrases for being able, through sovereign spiritual power, to universally manifest the various spiritual transformations of all Buddhas of the three periods of time within all realms of experience, appearing as clearly as if looking into the palm of one’s hand.

The names and phrases of the dharma-gate that can cause all Buddhas of the three periods of time to appear universally within every atom of all Buddha-lands of the three periods of time, manifesting various realms of supernatural power, continuing without interruption through oceans of kalpas;

the names and phrases of the dharma-gate that can cause every pore to emit sounds proclaiming the ocean-like voices of the great vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, sustaining and giving birth to all bodhisattvas until the end of the future;

and the names and phrases of the dharma-gate that can cause the lion throne upon which one sits to equal the measure of the Dharma-realm, with the assembly of supreme, awakened, and understanding Great Bodhisattvas adorning the site of enlightenment, pervading all places, turning the wheel of Dharma until the end of the future, maturing beings without interval and continuing without cessation.
O Son of the Buddha!

Taking these ten dharma-phrases as their head, there are pure names and phrases, numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, which are subtle and wondrous Dharma-gates. All of these are the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, and are not something that can be realized or known by me or you.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to further proclaim a small portion of the sphere of this Great Lion’s Stretching Samādhi entered by the Tathāgata, received the Buddha’s spiritual power and, with single-minded devotion, gazed up at the Tathāgata and observed the inconceivable ocean-like assembly of bodhisattvas;
he observed the inconceivable samādhis and supernormal powers of the Tathāgata, their various manifestations;
and he observed the inconceivable manner in which the Tathāgata enters and emerges from all oceans of worlds.
He observed the inconceivable realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom that enters into the illusion-like nature of all phenomena;
he observed the inconceivable universal manifestation of the Tathāgata, in which all Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely equal;
and he observed the inconceivable, immeasurable, and boundless paths of speech of the Tathāgata, which awaken one to the ocean of all dharma-gates. Then, he spoke these verses:
Within each and every pore, oceans of lands, equal in number to the atoms of all lands, exist;
in each, a Buddha sits at the site of enlightenment, surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas.

In every single pore are all the lands; The Buddhas sit within them all at the site of enlightenment, Dwelling peacefully upon the most supreme lotus thrones, Universally manifesting spiritual powers throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Upon the tip of a single hair, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within all lands;
within the assemblies of Bodhisattvas, they all proclaim and extol the practices of Samantabhadra.
The Tathāgata sits serenely within a single land, yet he manifests his presence in all lands;
from the ten directions, infinite clouds of bodhisattvas come together to assemble at that place.
The ocean of Bodhisattvas of Merit and Radiance, As numerous as the atoms within hundreds of billions of lands,
Arise together from this assembly to praise the Tathāgata, Traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions to fill the Dharma-realm.
They roam with mastery through the profound realm of phenomena, Abiding entirely in the peerless practices of Samantabhadra;
Manifesting in all lands and radiating light, They universally enter the assemblies of infinite Buddhas.
Throughout all lands in the ten directions, Abiding in the presence of the most supreme Buddhas,
They hear the True Dharma and practice it fully, In each and every land for immeasurable eons.
The Bodhisattva constantly cultivates various practices, Entering entirely into the ocean of Samantabhadra’s vows;
Abiding in the realm of the Buddha with boundless virtue, The radiance of the ocean of Dharma pervades everywhere.
Thoroughly penetrating the vast practices of Samantabhadra, Giving birth to the inexhaustible Dharma of all Buddhas,
Praising the boundless ocean of the Buddhas' merit, He manifests manifold spiritual powers that fill the entire Dharma-realm.
Bodies appear as clouds, as numerous as motes of dust, Constantly pervading all lands in every thought-moment;
The nectar rain of Dharma moistens all living beings, Universally throughout the Dharma-realm, causing them to awaken.

At that time, the World-Honored One, with a most supreme, profound, and vast intention, reflecting with right mindfulness, desired to cause the bodhisattvas in the assembly to dwell in the Tathāgata’s Great Samādhi of the Lion’s Stretch. Thereupon, from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows, he emitted a great light named "The Door of the Universal Illumination Manifesting the Dharma-Realm of the Three Times," accompanied by a retinue of light rays as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields, universally illuminating all oceans of lands throughout the ten directions.
At that time, the assembly of bodhisattvas in the Jeta Grove all beheld every single atom within all worlds throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space;

in each and every atom, there were buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, with various names, various forms and appearances, various adornments, various purities, various bases of support, and various shapes.
Within all such lands, there was a most supreme site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), and at each site of enlightenment, there was a majestic, precious lion throne.

Upon each and every seat, there was a bodhisattva who had attained equal and perfect enlightenment, surrounded by all the bodhisattvas and venerated and made offerings to by all the lords of the world.
In some instances, they see him dwelling amidst great assemblies in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, turning the wheel of the true Dharma, its sound unimpeded and pervading the entire Dharma-realm;

or they see him dwelling within the palaces of the kings of devas, the kings of nāgas, the kings of yakṣas, and the palaces of gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others—within all such royal palaces—as well as in other human dwellings such as villages, camps, cities, capitals, hamlets, and even various abodes of sentient beings, manifesting diverse supernatural powers and expounding various Dharma-gates. Namely:
They are born into various lineages, assume various physical forms, abide in various modes of deportment,
manifest various marks and signs of excellence, wear various halos, emit various nets of light,
dwell amidst various assemblies, enter various samādhis, display various supernatural transformations, and manifest various powers.
They emit various sounds and utter various words, expounding various teachings through various phrases and sentences;
thus, within this assembly, the great multitude of Bodhisattvas beholds the Tathāgata’s profound samādhi and vast, divine transformations.
In this same manner, throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—in the east, west, south, [and north]—[the Tathāgata manifests these wonders].
In the north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below— throughout all places,
within the transformations of various directions, within the methods of various directions, within the abidings of conceptions of various directions,
within the arisings of various directions, within the boundaries of various directions, within the emergence of understandings of various directions, and within the oceans of various directions.
Within these, all abide in accordance with the mental conceptions of sentient beings; from the beginningless past until the present,
within all lands, all bodies of sentient beings, all pores, all atoms, and throughout the entire realm of space— each measured by the tip of a single hair— [they are all present].
In every location, there are oceans of various lands, as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields, arising from various karmic causes and continuing in an uninterrupted succession,
abiding in their proper order; all the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment within them likewise behold the Buddha’s spiritual power in this same way,
and because they have beheld the Buddha’s power of supernatural penetration, they are all able to enter everywhere.
Within the minds of all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions and the three periods of time, they manifest their images;

according to the various inclinations and desires of those beings, they produce sublime sounds and voices, expounding all dharmas as appropriate to each, universally entering into all assemblies and appearing before all beings;
while their physical forms and appearances differ, their wisdom is without distinction.
These manifestations are diverse, pervading all lands throughout the limits of the future, appearing with sovereign ease and never ceasing,

teaching and taming all sentient beings; those who behold this power of spiritual transformation are all sustained by the roots of goodness and the power of vows cultivated by Vairocana Tathāgata in the past.
Either they have been embraced by the roots of goodness of the four means of attraction in the past;
or they have been brought to maturity through having seen, heard, recollected, associated with, or made offerings to [the Buddhas] in former times.
Or perhaps they were caused in the past to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
or perhaps they were gathered by roots of goodness through their courageous diligence at places where they once traveled while practicing the bodhisattva path under the Tathāgatas;
or perhaps they planted similar roots of goodness together with the Buddhas in the presence of all those Buddhas in the past.
Or perhaps it is because, in the past, the Tathāgata sought the unsurpassed all-knowledge (*anuttara-sarvajñatā*) and, through various skillful means (*upāya*), taught and brought them to maturity.

Therefore, they are all able to enter the Tathāgata’s inconceivable and profound samādhi, wherein he manifests great spiritual transformations (*ṛddhi-vikurvaṇa*) throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space:
some are able to see him entering the Buddha's Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*).
Some may attain the vision of entering the Buddha’s form-body;
some may attain the vision of entering the Buddha’s wisdom-body;
and some may attain the vision of entering the ocean of pure conduct practiced by the Tathāgata in the past.
Some may attain the vision of entering the ultimate, perfect, and complete shore of the Tathāgata’s qualities;
some may attain the vision of entering the wheel of the Bodhisattva’s adorned practices;
and some may attain the vision of entering the various stages realized by Bodhisattvas.
Some may obtain the vision of entering the Tathāgata’s wisdom of attaining perfect enlightenment;
some may obtain the vision of entering the various gates of samādhi and the equalized miraculous transformations in which the Buddha dwells;
and some may obtain the vision of entering the Tathāgata’s ten powers of knowledge and four fearlessnesses.
Some attain the vision of entering the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s eloquence and the four kinds of unimpeded analytical knowledge;

they enter such oceans of the various great supernormal transformations of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields. Those bodhisattvas, by means of various faiths, various understandings, various paths, various gateways, various entries, various teachings, various conformities, various locations, various faculties, various lands, various worlds, various wisdoms, various collections of dharmas, various supernormal transformations, various skillful means, and various samādhis—through these and other such means—they enter the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s supernormal transformations.
What are the various samādhis of a bodhisattva?
They are as follows:
the samādhi of entering the universally adorned dharma-realm of all bodhisattvas; the samādhi of the bodhisattva’s light illuminating the three periods of time; and so forth.
The Samādhi of Unobstructed Objects; the Samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s Light of Wisdom that is Uninterrupted within the Dharma-realm;
the Samādhi of the Bodhisattva Abiding in the Sphere of All Buddhas; the Samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s Radiance Illuminating the Boundless Limits of Space;
the Samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s Playful Mastery in Entering and Emerging from the Sovereign Power of the Tathāgatas; and the Bodhisattva’s Courageous [Samādhi]...
The Samādhi of the Majestic Array of Fearlessness; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Treasury of the Vortex of Skillful Means for Entering All Dharma Realms;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Manifesting Universally Like the Moon Throughout the Entire Dharma Realm and Expounding All Dharmas with Unobstructed Sound;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Equal Array of Various Dharma Clouds; and the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement.
The Samādhi of the Dharma King’s Banner Tied with Silken Cloth; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Contemplating the Ocean of Wisdom of All Buddhas;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Banner of Non-conceptual Light Illuminating the Distinctive Bodies of All Worlds;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Entering the Non-conceptual Realm-Body of the Tathāgata; and the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Following One [Aspect] from the Treasury of Great Compassion.
The samādhi of turning all worlds; the bodhisattva’s samādhi of the power of abiding in the traceless non-reliance upon all phenomena;
the bodhisattva’s samādhi of the perfectly complete wisdom that illuminates the ultimate tranquility of all phenomena;
the bodhisattva’s samādhi of knowing the emptiness of all phenomena and skillfully manifesting throughout all worlds; and the bodhisattva’s majestic power.
The samādhi of universally and equally giving birth to all buddha-fields; the bodhisattva’s samādhi of manifesting the marks of attaining perfect enlightenment in all buddha-fields;
the bodhisattva’s samādhi of contemplating the emptiness of the forms of all worlds;
the bodhisattva’s samādhi of non-attachment to the most supreme and perfect emptiness of all worlds; the bodhisattva’s emergence...
The samādhi of the Mother of the Power of All Tathāgatas; the bodhisattva samādhi of entering the ocean of the ultimate merits of all Buddhas through practice;
the bodhisattva samādhi of the power that observes all realms, gives rise to spiritual transformations, and endures until the end of the future;
and the bodhisattva samādhi of entering the ocean of the successive past deeds of all Tathāgatas.
The samādhi by which a bodhisattva, through the power of their majesty, protects and sustains the lineage of all Tathāgatas until the end of the future;
the samādhi by which a bodhisattva, through the power of resolute understanding, causes all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions in the present to be purified;
and the samādhi by which a bodhisattva, in a single instant, universally illumines the distinct abodes of all Buddhas.
The samādhi of abiding; the bodhisattva’s samādhi of deeply penetrating and observing the unobstructed limit;
the bodhisattva’s samādhi of being able, through sovereign power, to cause all worlds to become a single buddha-field;
the bodhisattva’s samādhi of giving birth to all the transformation bodies of the Buddhas; and the bodhisattva’s samādhi of knowing the ocean of all faculties through vajra-like wisdom.
The samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s knowledge that all Tathāgatas share a single matrix-body;
the samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s knowledge that all dharma-realms, in accordance with their established positions, entirely abide within the limit of mental recollection;
and the samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s great majestic power to manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment and parinirvāṇa within the vast lands of all dharma-realms.

...the Bodhisattva’s samādhi of abiding in the state of supreme majestic power; the Bodhisattva’s samādhi of the non-discriminative majestic power that illuminates the bodies of sentient beings in all Buddha-fields; the Bodhisattva’s samādhi of entering the revolving treasury of the wisdom of all Buddhas;
the Bodhisattva’s samādhi of knowing the distinctions between the characteristics and natures of all phenomena; the Bodhisattva’s...
The samādhi of universally perceiving the phenomena of the three periods of time through non-conceptual wisdom in a single kṣaṇa;
the samādhi of universally manifesting the body that is the treasury of the dharma-realm in every thought-moment of a bodhisattva;
the samādhi of a bodhisattva following and awakening to the lineage of all Tathāgatas with lion-like courageous wisdom; and the bodhisattva’s contemplation of all phenomena.
The samādhi of the wisdom-eye of the perfection of realms; the samādhi of the bodhisattva’s correct valor in advancing toward the ten powers;
the samādhi of the bodhisattva observing all perfect merits with the universal eye;
the samādhi of the bodhisattva universally illuminating and giving rise to the perfection of the physical forms of all sentient beings; the bodhisattva’s revolving... [text truncated]
The Samādhi of the Moving Treasury; the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Expounding a Single Dharma that Universally Enters All Dharmas;
the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Eloquence in Explaining and Interpreting a Single Dharma through the Differentiation of All Words and Phrases;
the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of the Banner of Power of the Non-dual Dharma-Phrases Expounded by All Buddhas; and the Bodhisattva’s Knowledge of the Three Times.
The Samādhi of the Unobstructed Limit; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Accordant Realization that All Kalpas are Without Differentiation;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Entering the Skillful Means of the Subtle Ten Powers; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Arousing All Bodhisattva Practices through Vajra-like Wisdom;
and the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Universally Manifesting Swiftly Throughout the Ten Directions According to the Mind.
The Samādhi of the Body-Cloud; the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Manifesting the Various Supernatural Transformations of the Body that Attains Perfect Enlightenment Pervading the Entire Dharma Realm;
the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of the Banner of Bliss Receiving All Touches; the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Adorning the Realm of Space with All Ornamental Implements;
and the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Emanating [Bodies] Equal to All Worlds in Every Thought-Moment.
The Samādhi of Clouds of Various Transforming Forms; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Stainless Moonlight of the Tathāgatas Illuminating Space;

the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Adornment of the Distinctions of the Root of All Dharmas Illumined by a Single Light; and the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Extensively Expounding the Meaning of All Dharmas.
The Lamp Samādhi; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Perfectly Illuminating the Realm of the Ten Powers;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Constellation Banner of All Buddhas of the Three Times; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Single Secret Treasury of All Buddhas;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Contemplating All Phenomena as Ultimately Exhausted; and the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit.
The Bodhisattva Samādhi of Seeing the Boundless Buddha-Spheres of Exhaustion; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Power of the Lion’s Roar of All Dharmas Like a Vajra;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Manifesting the Equality of Right View in the Transformations of All Tathāgatas;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Sun of All Buddhas Circumambulating in Every Thought-Moment. The Bodhisattva...
The samādhi of a single thought-moment universally illuminating the dharmas of the three periods of time;

the bodhisattva samādhi of universally sounding speech that expounds the pure light equally illuminating the self-nature purity of all dharmas; the bodhisattva samādhi of seeing the distinct powers of all Buddhas;
and the bodhisattva samādhi of seeing all Buddhas awaken to all the distinct dharma-realms, like the blossoming of lotus flowers.
the samādhi of the Bodhisattva observing all phenomena as being like space and having no place of abiding;
the Bodhisattva’s samādhi of the revolving treasury that universally issues forth from one direction into the oceans of the ten directions;
the Bodhisattva’s samādhi of entering the gates of all dharma-realms; the Bodhisattva’s samādhi of the body of the distinct treasuries of the ocean of all dharmas; and by the Bodhisattva...
The samādhi of emitting various lights from a tranquil body that illuminates the bodies of all sentient beings;
the samādhi of generating all supernatural powers from a single moment of mind through the power of great vows;
the samādhi of the universal majesty of constant perfect awakening in all places; and the samādhi of the single adornment through conforming to and awakening to understanding.
The Bodhisattva Samādhi of Entering All Dharma Realms with Rigor; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Universal Illumination through Right Mindfulness of All Buddha-Bodies;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Awakening to and Understanding the Supreme Wisdom of Supernatural Powers Pervading All Worlds;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Causing Immeasurable Letters of Teaching and Root-Mothers to Pervade the Dharma Realm in a Single Thought; and by the Bodhisattva...
The Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Radiance of the Dharma that Adorns All Dharmadhātus with the Teachings;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Perfect Wheel of the Radiance of the Sovereign Power of All Buddhas;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Gathering All Realms of Sentient Beings with the Net of Vows and Practices; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Seeing All Worlds Without Interruption; the Bodhisattva...
The samādhi of the universal stride of various miraculous manifestations of the auspicious lotus;

the samādhi of the bodhisattva’s wisdom that knows the revolving of the bodies of all sentient beings; the samādhi of the bodhisattva’s majestic power to manifest universally before all sentient beings;
and the samādhi of the bodhisattva’s realization of the secret ocean of the sounds and speech of all sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva Samādhi of Wisdom Discerning the Differences among All Sentient Beings;
the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Treasury of Non-conceptual Great Compassion; the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Entering the Ultimate Limit of All Tathāgatas;
and the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Lion’s Stretch Observing the Sphere of Liberation of All Tathāgatas.
By means of such samādhis of bodhisattvas—as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields—those bodhisattvas entered the vast merits cultivated by Vairocana Tathāgata in the past;
in every thought-moment, they entered the ocean of great spiritual transformations of the samādhis of all Buddhas that fill the entire dharma-realm. Their...
While dwelling in the Jeta Grove, the bodhisattvas did not depart from the assembly at the Tathāgata’s place of enlightenment;

each of them individually beheld themselves throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions—within vast worlds as numerous as the atoms of those fields—seated upon lion thrones of various precious lotus-blossom matrices, having all fully perfected vast wisdom. Universally...
They manifest various realms of supernatural power; having already dwelled in the stages of bodhisattvas that are characterized by tranquility, they have attained sovereign and sharp wisdom.
Having attained the practice of universal wisdom that accords with reality, they are born from the lineage of the Buddha’s wisdom.
They have realized the omniscience of all-knowledge before them, attaining the pure eye of wisdom free from the cataracts of delusion.
Skillfully taming and guiding all sentient beings, they abide in the equal dharma-nature of all Buddhas;
they accord with and awaken to the understanding of all phenomena, having already been able to observe that the self-nature of all dharmas is pure.
Knowing that all worlds are ultimately quiescent and without any basis for dependence, they travel everywhere to all lands throughout the ten directions.
Though dwelling in the earth, they have no attachment; they constantly and diligently observe all worlds without abiding anywhere;
they travel universally to all lands in the ten directions without going anywhere; having entered the palaces of all sublime dharmas, they do not come from anywhere;
pervading all phenomena, they thoroughly realize their nature is empty, knowing there is no accumulation, and they constantly teach others.
They transform and mature sentient beings, showing them the place of peaceful and happy practice, and revealing the realm of wisdom and liberation;
they constantly abide with their bodies of wisdom at the limit of detachment from greed, transcending the entire ocean of suffering of birth and death,
universally demonstrating to sentient beings the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the aggregates, and with the perfection of the light of wisdom, they illuminate all powers of meditative concentration.
Firm and unshakable by any power, they constantly give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings;

they understand that all phenomena are entirely like illusions, know that all worlds are entirely like dreams, observe that the various bodies manifested by all Buddhas are entirely like shadows, and know that the sounds, voices, and languages of the teachings they proclaim are entirely like echoes. Manifesting...

He perceives that the arising, formation, abiding, and maintenance of all phenomena are entirely like magical illusions; he is skillfully able to accumulate the most supreme vows and practices, possesses universal wisdom, and is perfectly pure.

He is adept at following [the path], attains ultimate tranquility, and skillfully enters the realm of the *dhāraṇīs* and the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*). Endowed with the power of various fearlessnesses and *samādhis*, he is courageous.
With fierce diligence, they cultivate all practices, abide at the limit of the dharma-realm, and attain the eye of clear wisdom;
reaching the place where all dharmas have no abiding, they practice the ocean of boundless wisdom-conduct,
arrive at the ultimate further shore of the perfection of knowledge, are sustained by the perfection of wisdom, and through supernormal powers—
By means of the *pāramitās*, they deliver all sentient beings; through the *dhyāna-pāramitā*, they attain mastery over the mind and realize the true realm of all Buddhas.
With skillful wisdom, they reveal the treasury of the Dharma; with lucid wisdom, they explain the words and phrases;
with the power of eloquence, they preach inexhaustible teachings; and being heroic, fearless, and capable, they serve as teachers.
The Lion’s Roar constantly delights in observing the non-differentiated Dharma; with the pure eye of wisdom, he universally contemplates all things.

The moon of the knowledge of non-arising shines equally upon the world. Observing all sentient beings and seeing the truth of reality, his merit and wisdom are as firm and solid as a mountain of diamond, such that no analogy can reach them; they continue to increase.
The root and sprout of all wisdom, possessing courageous and diligent vigor, he has crushed the hosts of Māras;
with immeasurable wisdom and perfect majestic radiance, his physical form is extraordinary, transcending all worlds.
Having attained unimpeded wisdom regarding all phenomena, he understands all dharmas to their ultimate limit of exhaustion and non-exhaustion, abiding in pure wisdom.
The universal limit (*samantaparyanta*) is able to universally accord with and enter the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*);

the wisdom of the contemplation of signlessness (*animitta*) is constantly present before them; they skillfully perfect all bodhisattva practices; they observe all worlds with non-dual wisdom (*advayajñāna*);
they know the destinations to which sentient beings go and from whence they come; they attain perfected wisdom throughout all Buddha-fields; and regarding one...
All phenomena are free from all darkness and obscurations; they universally radiate the light of Dharma, illuminating the worlds of the ten directions.
They serve as the most supreme field of merit for all the world. Their vast wheel of vows appears everywhere like the moon;
their merit and virtue are preeminent like Mount Sumeru, such that no one in any world can surpass them. They crush and subdue all externalists and heterodox arguments.
They manifest their bodies universally in all lands, expounding all dharmas with subtle and wondrous voices; they behold all Buddhas everywhere without ever feeling satiety.
Having attained the sovereign power and majesty of all Buddhas, they manifest various bodies according to those who are to be transformed.
Riding the great vessel of wisdom, they navigate the ocean of birth and death, circulating everywhere to provide universal salvation.
Moving without obstruction, his wisdom was perfected and his bodily radiance was brilliantly penetrating, like the rising sun that shines universally upon the world.
He manifested various forms and images according to the minds of sentient beings, knowing their faculties, dispositions, and inclinations.
He entered the pure realm of non-contention and realized that the self-nature of all phenomena is unborn; by means of this—
Through wisdom, they cause all small and great realms to interpenetrate one another; they decisively comprehend the profound principles of the Buddha-ground;
they know the words and meanings of all worlds; they expound inexhaustible teachings through inexhaustible phrases;
and from within a single phrase, they manifest an ocean of all *sūtras*, fully attaining these qualities.
The body of the dhāraṇī of vast wisdom, which, according to what is received and upheld, remains without the slightest forgetfulness throughout all kalpas until the end of the future;
which in a single thought-moment can remember the events of unspeakable kalpas of past lives;
which in a single thought-moment can comprehend the minds of all sentient beings across the three periods of time; and which bestows upon all sentient beings the dhāraṇī-dharma of all Buddhas.
Guṇākara constantly turns the pure, non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma, causing all sentient beings to give rise to great wisdom,
enter the realm of the Buddha, and possess all-encompassing knowledge. He always dwells securely in profound samādhi,
skillfully discerns all dharma-terms, yet remains entirely unattached to any phenomena.

They sport with mastery in supreme wisdom and have attained liberation from all realms of experience. Observing their bodies adorned with every purity, those bodies enter universally into the dharma-realm of the ten directions; according to those who are to be transformed, they are able to go everywhere. They know every atom within the oceans of lands and manifest perfect enlightenment within each one. Within the nature of formlessness, they manifest all forms; they are able to enter all directions through a single direction. These bodhisattvas are fully endowed with such an immeasurable treasury of wisdom and merit that all Buddhas throughout the ten directions collectively praise them, yet even speaking of their merits could never exhaust them. There is none among them who is not present in the Jeta Grove, and all behold the light radiated by the Buddha as they enter deeply into the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s merits.

At that time, because those bodhisattvas were illuminated by the light of the inconceivable True Dharma, their minds were filled with joy, peace, and happiness. From within their own bodies, their lion thrones, the various jewel pavilions, all the ornaments throughout the Jeta Grove, and from among all the objects they used, they manifested clouds of manifold great adornments that filled all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions.
That is to say:
in every thought-moment, they universally emit clouds of subtle, vast, and great nets of light that fill the Dharma-realm, everywhere awakening all sentient beings and causing them all to rejoice;

in every thought-moment, they manifest clouds of all kinds of mani-bells that fill the Dharma-realm, producing subtle and wondrous sounds that extol and praise all the merits of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
In every thought-moment, clouds of all celestial music appear, filling the Dharma-realm, producing subtle and wondrous sounds that proclaim the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;

in every thought-moment, clouds of the various bodies, colors, and marks of all great Bodhisattvas’ diverse practices and vows appear, filling the Dharma-realm, all using exquisite voices to expound every one of the vast and great practices and vows of the Bodhisattvas;

in every thought-moment, clouds of the various sovereign and wondrous transformations of the supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas appear, filling the Dharma-realm, using voices adapted to each type of being to pervade the realms of sentient beings and proclaim the vast and great speech of all Buddhas.

In every thought-moment, they manifest clouds of Bodhisattva bodies adorned with all manner of marks and secondary characteristics, filling the Dharma-realm and pervading all lands, proclaiming the continuous and uninterrupted succession of the appearance of all Tathāgatas throughout all lands in the ten directions;

in every thought-moment, they manifest clouds of the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, filling the Dharma-realm, manifesting the Buddhas’ attainment of perfect enlightenment, universally observing and displaying the merit of the adornments of their Buddhahood;

in every thought-moment, they manifest clouds of bodies resembling all the great dragon kings, filling the Dharma-realm, each individual cloud of bodies pervading all Buddha-lands and raining down all kinds of supreme and wondrous fragrances.

In every thought-moment, they manifest clouds of semblance bodies resembling all the lords of the worlds, filling the Dharma-realm; each lord of the world universally observes and expounds the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

In every thought-moment, they manifest clouds of pure Buddha-lands of wondrous jewel-light, filling the Dharma-realm, displaying the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Buddhas of the ten directions. Because these bodhisattvas are illuminated by such inconceivable light, they enter the vast and inconceivable realm of spiritual powers (*ṛddhi-viṣaya*); it is the natural law that they thus bring forth these clouds of great adornments of various spiritual transformations, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-lands.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, wishing to further reveal the various miraculous transformations within the Jeta Grove, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
“You should behold this Jeta Grove, Vast, magnificent, and boundless in extent;
All clouds of bodies are manifested therein, Filled throughout the Dharma-realm by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power.”
Adorned with a body of pure and radiant form, the infinite sons of the Buddhas from the ten directions all come to manifest within this site of enlightenment;
the entire assembly gazes upon them, and there is none who does not see.
From the pores of all the Buddha-sons, the sound of the Buddha-dharma resounds like a thunderclap;
with various ornaments of blazing clouds, it pervades all lands throughout the ten directions.
Furthermore, from within the flowers and leaves of the jewel trees, there appear the majestic forms of Brahmā and Śakra;
their movements and postures are ever serene as they rise from meditative concentration and proceed on foot.
Within each and every pore of the Buddha’s body, There constantly appear inconceivable multitudes of bodhisattvas;
Their marks and signs are dignified and most subtle, All equal to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
The various ornaments above the Jetavana Grove fill the entirety of space,
emitting wondrous sounds that praise and describe the oceans of merit and diverse adornments of all Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
The various jewel trees within the Jeta Grove also produce immeasurable, wondrous sounds,
expounding upon the ocean of diverse karmic retributions for all living beings.
All realms within the forest manifest all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
within every atom of the oceans of lands in the ten directions, they give rise to spiritual powers that reach everywhere.
Within every atom of all oceans of lands, All the realms of the ten directions Are universally adorned and clearly manifest Within each and every pore of the Buddha.
Clouds of fragrant incense with jewel-like flames all manifest Buddhas, equal in number to sentient beings and pervading the world;
each one gives rise to great supernormal powers, employing skillful means as appropriate to transform and deliver them.
Jeweled palaces and cities as vast as space, Adorned with exquisite beauty like the sun’s appearance;
Treasure repositories and Bodhi trees— None fail to pervade the ten directions.
The Tathāgatas of the ten directions and three periods of time, And all the assemblies of Bodhisattvas in their sites of enlightenment—
The marks of their meritorious cultivation throughout oceans of kalpas, All appear here within this forest.
The Bodhisattvas of Samantabhadra’s Great Conduct, who have already perfected the adornments within oceans of lands—
numberless as all living beings— are all seen here within this grove.

At that time, because those bodhisattvas were illuminated by the light of the Buddha’s samādhi, each and every one of them attained gates of great compassion as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many buddha-fields.

Because they have attained such a gate of great compassion, they gather in and benefit sentient beings with peace and happiness; from every single pore of their bodies, they emit clouds of multicolored light rays as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields. From each of these light rays, they manifest clouds of Bodhisattva bodies as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, and further emit clouds of bodies resembling all the lords of the world, filling all dharma realms throughout the ten directions. Appearing before all sentient beings, they teach and subdue them through various skillful means according to their physical forms and voices, bringing them to maturity. Or, they manifest the gates of impermanence and decline within unspeakably many celestial palaces, as numerous as the atoms in Buddha-fields.
Or they manifest gates of all sentient beings being born according to their karma, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
or they manifest gates of awakening the mind through dream-state realms, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
or they manifest gates of the perfection of all practices of all bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
In some instances, they manifest the gateways of all bodhisattvas’ fulfillment of great vows, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
in others, they manifest the gateways of shaking worlds, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;

and in yet others, they manifest the gateways of all Tathāgatas’ practice of the perfection of giving by relinquishing both internal and external things, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.

In some places, they manifest the gate of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), wherein all Tathāgatas of as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in an ineffable number have fulfilled the correct practice of cultivating all merits;

in some places, they manifest the gate of the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), wherein all Bodhisattvas of as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in an ineffable number have their limbs severed yet remain undisturbed in mind;

in some places, they manifest the gate of the perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*), wherein all Bodhisattvas of as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in an ineffable number diligently cultivate various forms of wisdom and supernormal powers.

In some instances, they manifest the gates of the perfection of dhyāna, practicing meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), absorptions (*samādhi*), attainments (*samāpatti*), supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), and meditative trances, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

in other instances, they manifest the gates of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*) through the illumination of the world by the light of knowledge, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

and in yet other instances, they manifest the gates of diligently seeking the Buddha-dharma, wherein for the sake of each and every phrase and each and every word and meaning, they relinquish kingdoms, cities, wives, children, wealth, and countless lives, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.

Or they manifest the gate of approaching, making offerings to, seeking instruction from, and inquiring about all the essential points of the Dharma with all Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, with a mind free from weariness;

or they manifest the gate of the light of the ocean of wisdom that awakens and guides sentient beings according to their faculties and inclinations toward maturity, proceeding to their respective locations as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

or they manifest the gate of the majestic power of the supreme banner that subdues all Māras and restrains all non-Buddhists, consisting of the great mass of merit and wisdom of all Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
In some instances, they manifest an inconceivable number of gateways of wisdom for knowing all arts and crafts and technical skills, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

in other instances, they manifest an inconceivable number of gateways of wisdom for knowing the subtle distinctions in the mental activities of all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

and in yet other instances, they manifest an inconceivable number of gateways of wisdom for knowing the distinct categories and superior qualities of all phenomena, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Or they manifest the gate of the clear wisdom that knows the differences in the various mental inclinations of all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

or they manifest the gate of the clear wisdom that knows the differences in the faculties and conduct of all sentient beings, causing their afflictions and habitual tendencies to be extinguished, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

or they manifest the gate of the clear wisdom that knows the differences in the karmic retributions of the various classes of all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.

By means of such inconceivable numbers of skillful methods, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable Buddha-fields, they go to the dwellings of all sentient beings to gather them in, discipline them, and bring them to maturity.
That is to say:
sometimes he goes to the palace of Brahmā;

sometimes he goes to the palace of Śakra; and at times he visits the palaces of the kings of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and the realm of Yama.
Or they go to the abodes of animals, hungry ghosts, and hell-beings, where—through equal great compassion, equal great vows, equal wisdom, and equal samādhi—they teach, gather, and subdue them.

Those sentient beings may be subdued upon seeing him, or subdued upon hearing him, or subdued by recollecting him, or subdued by hearing his voice, or subdued by hearing his name, or subdued by seeing his halo, or subdued by seeing his lattice of light; according to the inclinations of the hearts of those sentient beings, he goes to each of their places to cause them to obtain benefit.
Furthermore, within this grove, all the bodhisattvas, for the sake of bringing sentient beings to maturity,
employ their supernormal powers such that they may at times appear dwelling in various exquisitely adorned palaces;

or at other times, they manifest themselves residing upon precious lion thrones in their own pavilions, surrounded by assemblies in places of enlightenment, filling the oceans of all lands throughout the ten directions, universally manifesting themselves so that all may see them— yet even while doing so, they never depart from this Jeta Grove where the Tathāgata resides.

Furthermore, this bodhisattva, desiring to bring all sentient beings to maturity, manifests immeasurable clouds of transformation bodies; he may manifest his body adorned with a retinue, or he may manifest his body alone and without companion.
That is to say:

they may manifest the body of a śramaṇa, or the body of a brāhmaṇa, or the body of one who has left home as a non-Buddhist ascetic, or the body of an ascetic practicing austerities, or the body of one in full vigor, or the body of a king of physicians, or the body of a merchant leader, or the body of a courtesan, or the body of a musician, or the body of Vaiśravaṇa, or the body of a world ruler, or the body of one serving the various devas, or the body of a craftsman or technician; manifesting such various bodies of transformation, they go to the abodes of all sentient beings and, according to what is appropriate for them, give rise to wisdom that is like an illusion.

Throughout all worlds, they carry out the bodhisattva practice like the net of Indra, expounding all dharmas through various forms, various modes of conduct, various voices, various discourses, and various dwellings.

That is to say: some speak of all the crafts and occupations of the world; some speak of the lamps of wisdom and merit that illuminate the world; some speak of the true power and empowerment of all that is realized; some speak of the adornments of the worldly realms sustained by the force of all karma; some speak of the establishment of all pure vehicles and stages throughout the ten directions; and some speak of the realm of phenomena illuminated by the lamp of perfect wisdom. Although such Bodhisattvas pervade the entire Dharma-realm of the ten directions, teaching, taming, and bringing sentient beings to maturity, they never depart from this Jeta Grove, the abode of the Tathāgata.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Three;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Inconceivable Realm of Liberation.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī emerged from the Pavilion of Good Abiding, accompanied by an immeasurable assembly of fellow great bodhisattvas,
as well as the various vajra-spirits who constantly serve and protect him, manifesting himself throughout the world for the sake of all beings.
The Earth-Ruling Spirit who possesses a body of great majesty; the Spirit who has long made firm vows to serve the feet of all Buddhas;
the Earth-Ruling Spirit who remembers past great aspirations and ensures that the hearing of the True Dharma continues without interruption;

the Water-Ruling Spirit who adorns the Dharma-realm with profound and pure great compassion and universally moistens all sentient beings; and the Fire-Ruling Spirit whose wisdom-power and radiance shine everywhere.
The Fire God, who adorns his head with a crown of mani-jewels; the Wind-Governing God, who illuminates the ten directions and presides over various rituals;
the Directional God, who is dedicated to eliminating the darkness of ignorance; the Night-Governing God, who single-mindedly manifests the sun of Tathāgata-wisdom;
and the Space-Governing God, who universally adorns the dharma-realm of empty space.
The Earth Deity, who diligently employs skillful means to rescue sentient beings from the ocean of birth and death;
the Ocean Deity, who constantly and diligently accumulates roots of goodness that transcend the measure of the mind and tend toward all-knowledge like a supreme banner;
the River Deity, who makes great vows to transport and deliver sentient beings, praising the Buddhas with courageous vigor and without weariness; and the Constant... [Deity].
The City Guardian Deity who Diligently Protects the Bodhicitta of All Sentient Beings;
the Great Dragon Kings who Constantly and Diligently Protect All Sentient Beings; the Yakṣa Kings who Constantly and Diligently Protect the City of Omniscience;
the Gandharva King who Constantly Causes Sentient Beings to Increase in Joy; and those who Constantly and Diligently Eliminate All...
The King of the Pretas, who possesses hunger and thirst; the King of the Kumbhāṇḍas, who constantly vows to rescue all sentient beings and deliver them across the ocean of birth and death;
the King of the Garuḍas, who vows that all sentient beings may universally achieve the body of a Tathāgata’s power that transcends all worlds;
and the King of the Asuras, who bows with reverence and delights in beholding the various merits of the Buddhas.
The King of the Mahoragas deeply loathed birth and death and constantly delighted in gazing upon the marks and signs of the Buddhas;

the Great Heavenly Kings revered the Buddha and respectfully made offerings to him while extolling and praising him; and the Great Brahma Kings likewise honored the Buddha with respectful worship and laudatory praise.

Mañjuśrī, surrounded before and behind by such a multitude of great bodhisattvas adorned with various forms, appearances, and majestic virtues, as well as by the lords of the world, came from his own abode to the place where the Buddha was. He circumambulated the Tathāgata to the right for immeasurable circuits, made offerings of various kinds of ritual implements, and having completed these offerings, prostrated himself, took his leave, and departed to the south after circumambulating once more.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, beheld Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva together with such great bodhisattvas and world-protectors, adorned by an assembly of various supernatural powers and sovereign majesty, emerging serenely from the Jeta Grove. He then reflected:
"I shall now go to the southern region together with Mañjuśrī."
Then, Śāriputra, surrounded by his retinue of sixty bhikṣus, emerged from his dwelling and proceeded to where the Buddha was.

Upon arrival, he prostrated himself, gazed at the Buddha with single-minded devotion, and reported the matter in detail to the World-Honored One. Having received the World-Honored One’s permission, he circumambulated him three times to the right, paid homage, took his leave, and went to the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was.
All these bhikṣus were those converted and delivered by Śāriputra; they had not long since left the household life and resided together with him.
They were as follows:

the bhikṣu Sāgarabuddhi, the bhikṣu Guṇarāja, the bhikṣu Puṇyaprabha, the bhikṣu Mahākāruṇika, the bhikṣu Vidyurjñāna, the bhikṣu Viśuddhacaryā, the bhikṣu Devaguṇa, the bhikṣu Bhūtamatī, the bhikṣu Brahmajaya, and the bhikṣu Śāntamati. Together with these sixty persons, they had all in the past made offerings to various Buddhas and deeply planted roots of goodness.

They are all able to awaken to and understand the profound Dharma; with deep faith they enter into the most utterly pure state, their resolve and conduct being as vast as the realm of the Buddhas. They are able to practice correctly according to the Buddha’s teachings and fully comprehend the intrinsic nature of all phenomena. They bring great benefit and bring sentient beings to maturity, and they always joyfully and diligently seek the merits of all Buddhas—all of these are those who have been taught and transformed by the youth Mañjuśrī.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra was traveling along the road with a group of bhikṣus. Observing the bhikṣus, he addressed Samudgata, saying:
"You should observe the body of Mañjuśrī, adorned with pure marks and signs, which neither gods nor humans can conceive;
you should observe the halo of Mañjuśrī, its radiance penetrating and illuminating the ten directions, able to cause joy to arise in the hearts of sentient beings."
You should observe the net of light rays emitted by Mañjuśrī, which is exquisitely adorned and eliminates the immeasurable suffering and afflictions of sentient beings;
you should observe the majestic power of Mañjuśrī’s assembly, all of whom are sustained by the roots of goodness cultivated by Bodhisattvas in the past;
you should observe the path traversed by Mañjuśrī, eight paces on either side of which are pure, level, and adorned with various jewels.

You should observe the place where Mañjuśrī dwells: throughout the ten directions, there are always sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), manifesting with majestic adornments that follow him as he moves.

You should observe the path upon which Mañjuśrī travels: it is fully endowed with the majesty of immeasurable merit; on both its left and right sides there are hidden treasures, from which various kinds of precious jewels spontaneously emerge.

You should observe how, due to the roots of goodness from his past offerings to the Buddhas, wherever Mañjuśrī is, there are trees of various jewels, and amidst those trees, treasuries of jewels open up to produce ornaments of adornment.
You should observe how, wherever Mañjuśrī resides, all the lords of the world raise clouds of offerings, raining down various articles of worship that are spread out and arrayed as an offering;

you should observe how, when the Buddhas of the ten directions are about to preach the Dharma, they all emit the light from the white tuft between their eyebrows, which comes to illuminate Mañjuśrī’s body and enters through the crown of his head.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, for the sake of the bhikṣus, extolled and praised Mañjuśrī, revealing and expounding upon his such immeasurable and manifold virtues, fully adorned with excellence.

At that time, having heard this praise, the minds of the bhikṣus became pure; their faith and understanding were firm, and they leaped for joy, unable to contain themselves. Their bodies became supple, their faculties harmonious and serene, and all defilements and obstructions were utterly exhausted. All sorrow and suffering were eliminated; they constantly beheld the Buddhas and perpetually heard the True Dharma. They dedicated themselves toward seeking the wisdom of all-knowledge, accomplishing the unimpeded roots of goodness of a bodhisattva, attaining the immeasurable powers of a bodhisattva, giving rise to inexhaustible and perfect great compassion, and initiating boundless and vast vows. They entered deeply into the ultimate shore of the various perfections, and the oceans of Buddhas of the ten directions all appeared before them. Developing deep faith and delight in the realm of the Buddhas, they addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:
“We only pray that the Upādhyāya will lead us to approach that most excellent and sublime Great Being.”
Then, Śāriputra went together with him to the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was; having seen him, he prostrated and said:
"O Noble One!
"May these bhikṣus be granted the opportunity to behold him.

At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, surrounded by immeasurable bodhisattvas endowed with sovereign supernatural powers, together with his great assembly and various retinues, turned to look at the bhikṣus like an elephant king.
Then, all the bhikṣus prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed him thus:

“We pray that the Great Sage Mañjuśrī, the Upādhyāya Śāriputra, and the World-Honored One Śākyamuni will all bear witness: by virtue of the roots of goodness we have now acquired from beholding this Great Being, this Supreme Hero, and from attending upon, gazing upon, and reverently honoring him with faith and joy; and by virtue of the roots of merit and wisdom we have accumulated in the past—by these roots of goodness, may we come to fully possess such a physical body as yours, such secondary marks and primary signs, such a voice, such sovereign power, and all such merits.”
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva addressed the bhikṣus, saying:

"If good sons or good daughters accomplish ten kinds of tireless minds directed toward the Mahāyāna Dharma, they will be able to swiftly and deeply enter the ultimate stage of the Tathāgata, let alone the stages of a bodhisattva."
What are these ten? They are:
seeing all Tathāgatas and approaching them with a vast mind to offer worship, without weariness of heart;
Accumulating and perfecting all roots of goodness, they never regress and their minds feel no weariness;
diligently seeking the true Dharma of all Buddhas, their minds feel no weariness;
diligently practicing all the sublime pāramitās of the bodhisattvas, their minds feel no weariness.
Universally practicing all the profound samādhis of bodhisattvas, their minds never grow weary;
sequentially entering into all phenomena as they flow through the three periods of time, their minds never grow weary;
adorning all oceans of lands throughout the ten directions and causing them all to be purified, their minds never grow weary.
They teach and discipline all sentient beings, bringing them all to maturity without weariness of mind;
they practice the bodhisattva conduct in all lands throughout all kalpas without weariness of mind;

and for the sake of maturing even a single sentient being, they cultivate as many gates of *pāramitā* as there are atoms in all lands to achieve the perfection of a single power of the Tathāgata, and thus proceed in this sequence to achieve all the powers of a Tathāgata for all sentient beings without weariness of mind.

Bhikṣus, you should know that if a son of good family or a daughter of good family accomplishes deep faith and gives rise to these ten kinds of tireless minds, they will be able to nurture all roots of goodness, abandon all wandering in the cycle of birth and death, and completely transcend all worlds. They will not fall into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but will accomplish the lineage of all Tathāgatas, fulfill the pure great vows of bodhisattvas, accumulate all the merits of the Tathāgatas, and practice all the various conducts of bodhisattvas. They will obtain the powers and fearlessnesses of a Tathāgata, subdue all Māras and non-Buddhist teachers, extinguish all afflictions and habitual tendencies, enter the bodhisattva stages, and draw near to the stage of a Tathāgata.
At that time, having heard this Dharma, all the bhikṣus immediately and together realized the vast samādhi called "The Unobstructed Eye that Perceives the Realms of All Buddhas."

By virtue of the majestic spiritual power of this samādhi, they see all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, and their respective assemblies at their sites of enlightenment in all worlds throughout the ten directions;
they also see all the various classes of sentient beings in those worlds, each with their distinct differences;
and they also see all the similarities and differences, as well as the defilement and purity, within those worlds, each with their distinct differences.
They also clearly perceive all the various distinctions among the atoms within those entire worlds;

they also clearly perceive all the various palaces where the sentient beings in those worlds dwell, their diverse adornments, their various accomplishments, and the distinct differences among the various articles of utility they enjoy;
and they hear the oceans of voices of those Buddhas.
They are able to fully comprehend and explain the various names, phrases, syllables, definitions, essential natures, characteristics, and secrets of all dharmas;
they are also able to observe the differences in the mental activities, faculties, and desires of all sentient beings within those worlds;
and they are also able to recollect the ten past and ten future lifetimes of all sentient beings within those worlds.
They are also able to recollect the events of ten eons each in the past and future of those worlds;

they are also able to recollect the ten matters of the original births, the ten attainments of perfect enlightenment, the ten turnings of the wheel of Dharma, the ten kinds of supernormal powers, the ten kinds of telepathy, the ten kinds of admonitions, the ten kinds of preaching the Dharma, and the ten kinds of eloquence of all those Tathāgatas.

Furthermore, by virtue of attaining the power of this samādhi, he immediately attained ten thousand true bodhicittas, accomplished ten thousand profound samādhis, became fully endowed with ten thousand pāramitās, perfected ten thousand radiances of wisdom, and gave rise to ten thousand sovereign supernormal powers. Because he was thus adorned by the various majestic spiritual powers and unimpeded forces of these bodhisattva samādhis, his body and mind became supple and subtle, his faith and joy increased, and he dwelt in a bodhicitta that was firm and immovable.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, fully established in the true, auspicious, and subtle merit of the supreme practices of Samantabhadra, exhorted the bhikṣus to dwell securely in those supreme Samantabhadra practices. Having dwelled in these supreme practices, they entered the ocean of profound and vast vows;
having entered the ocean of vows, they universally accomplished their profound great vows.
Because they had accomplished this ocean of great vows, they attained purity of mind.
Because the mind is pure, one attains purity of body;
because the body is pure, one attains lightness and agility of body;
because the body is light and agile, one then attains vast and non-regressive supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).

Because he has attained such great supernormal powers, he never leaves the presence of Mañjuśrī’s feet, yet manifests his body before all Tathāgatas in all worlds throughout the ten directions, fully accomplishing all Buddha-dharmas.

At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī had exhorted the bhikṣus to resolve their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, he traveled southward by stages through human settlements, cities, towns, and villages, until he reached the city of Puṇyavatī.
To the east of that city, he dwelt in the Śāla Grove of the Banner of Adornment, a site of great stūpas where former buddhas had once resided to teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
it was also a place where, in the past, the World-Honored One Vairocana practiced the bodhisattva path and was able to relinquish that which is most difficult to give up.

Therefore, the fame of this grove is heard throughout immeasurable Buddha-fields; it is constantly honored and venerated here by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.

At that time, Mañjuśrī, together with his retinue, arrived at this grove and sat upon a lion throne in that very place. There he preached a sūtra titled *The Perfect Radiance That Universally Illumines the Dharma Realm*, which had a retinue of one hundred trillion nayutas of sūtras.

While this sutra was being taught, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of great nāga kings, together with their retinues, having heard this Dharma, felt spontaneous revulsion for the nāga realm and gave rise to deep love and joy for the Buddha’s merits;
they all cast off their nāga bodies and were reborn among humans and devas. Ten thousand nāgas attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings each attained maturity within the three vehicles.

At that time, when the people of the city of Puṇyavatī heard that Mañjuśrī was dwelling in the great stūpa within the Śāla grove of the Banner of Adornment, they all came out from the city to visit him. Among them was an upāsaka named Mahāmati, who was accompanied by a retinue of five hundred people, namely:

The upāsaka Sudatta, the upāsaka Ratnaśrī, the upāsaka Parimaṇḍalābha, the upāsaka Yaśodeva, the upāsaka Candrasaumanasya, the upāsaka Candraprīti, the upāsaka Candramati, the upāsaka Mahāmati, the upāsaka Bhadrapāla, and the upāsaka Bhadraśrī—surrounded by such a multitude in front and behind—they approached the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was. Having arrived, they prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit to one side.
Furthermore, there was a laywoman named Mahāmati, who came together with a retinue of five hundred people, namely:

the laywoman Sucakraprabhā, the laywoman Brahmaguṇā, the laywoman Śrī, the laywoman Subāhu, the laywoman Bhadrābhā, the laywoman Bhadraśrī, the laywoman Candraprabhā, the laywoman Jyotiḥprabhā, the laywoman Bhadraguṇā, and the laywoman Sunetra. Surrounded by such a multitude in front and behind, she approached the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was, and having arrived, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side.
Furthermore, there was a youth named Sudhana, accompanied by a retinue of five hundred persons, namely:

the youth Suvinīta, the youth Suvrata, the youth Susamsthāna, the youth Sucarita, the youth Sucintita, the youth Sujñāna, the youth Sumati, the youth Sunetra, the youth Subhuja, and the youth Suprabha. Surrounded by such a multitude before and behind him, he approached the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was. Having arrived, he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side.
