Furthermore, there was a maiden named Miaoxian (Wonderful Virtue), who, together with a retinue of five hundred people— namely, the maiden Mahāmati, the maiden Subhadra,

the maiden Supratibhānamukhī, the maiden Dṛḍhamati, the maiden Śrīmatī, the maiden Śrījñānā, the maiden Pūjyaguṇā, the maiden Śrīpariṣvaṅgā, and the maiden Sujātā— surrounded by such a multitude before and behind her, came to the place where the youth Mañjuśrī was.
Having arrived, he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit to one side.

At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, knowing that the people of Puṇyavatī had all assembled, surveyed them thoroughly; then, according to their inclinations and joys, he manifested a body of sovereign power through his supernatural faculties, its majestic radiance so brilliant that it eclipsed the entire assembly.
By the power of his great compassion, he caused the entire congregation to attain peace, security, coolness, and happiness.
Through the power of great compassion, they give rise to the mind of teaching the Dharma and achieve universal success;
through the power of great wisdom, they cause beings to awaken and eliminate all mental defilements of affliction;
and with unimpeded eloquence, they are about to expound the profound and vast Buddha-dharma.
Furthermore, at that time, he observed Sudhana to discern by what causes and conditions this name was established;

he knew that when this youth first entered the womb, within his residence there spontaneously appeared a pavilion made of the seven treasures, beneath which were seven hidden treasuries, and upon those treasuries grew sprouts of the seven treasures, namely:
gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, red pearl, musaragalva, and agate.

The youth Sudhana remained in the womb for ten months before his birth; his physical form was upright and his limbs were perfectly proportioned. At that time, seven hidden treasures—each measuring seven cubits in length, breadth, and height—suddenly opened and manifested, radiating brilliant light so that the members of both his inner and outer families could gaze upon them without ever growing weary.
Furthermore, within the house there spontaneously appeared five hundred precious vessels, each filled with various rare and wonderful jewels, namely:
diamond vessels filled with all kinds of perfumes, perfume vessels filled with various garments, and vessels of fine jade...
Vessels filled with food and drink; maṇi vessels filled with various jewels;
golden vessels filled with silver grain; silver vessels filled with gold grain; gold and silver vessels filled with lapis lazuli;
lapis lazuli vessels filled with gold and silver; and vessels made of maṇi jewels and crystal.
Chank shells were filled to the brim; within chank-shell vessels, crystal was filled;
within agate vessels, red pearls were filled; within red-pearl vessels, agate was filled;
within star-bannered *maṇi* vessels, crystal and *maṇi*-crystal were filled; within *maṇi* vessels, star-bannered *maṇis* were filled, just as...
These five hundred precious vessels appeared spontaneously;

furthermore, within the house, all kinds of rare jewels, wealth, and various necessities rained down everywhere, filling every storehouse to capacity. Because of these events, his parents, relatives, and skilled physiognomists collectively named this boy Sudhana (Good Wealth).
Moreover, they knew that this youth had already made offerings to the Buddhas of the past and had deeply planted roots of goodness.

Their resolute understanding is vast; they always delight in drawing near to spiritual friends; their physical, verbal, and mental actions are entirely free from fault; they are courageous and diligent, purifying the bodhisattva path and seeking all-knowledge; they become vessels for the Buddha-dharma, and the conduct of their minds is as pure as space.

At that time, after Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva had thus observed the extraordinary marks of Sudhana, he smiled with a joyful countenance, comforted and exhorted him, and extensively expounded all the Buddha-dharmas, namely:

the teaching on the accumulation of all Buddhas; the teaching on the continuity of all Buddhas; the teaching on the successive and profound entry of all Buddhas; the teaching on the purity of the assemblies of all Buddhas; the teaching on the turning of the wheel of Dharma and the guidance of all Buddhas; the teaching on the purity of the physical marks and signs of the form bodies of all Buddhas; the teaching on the universal accomplishment of the dharma-bodies of all Buddhas; the teaching on the unimpeded eloquence of all Buddhas; the teaching on the perfect adornments of all Buddhas; and the teaching on the equality and non-duality of all Buddhas.

At that time, after the youth Mañjuśrī had expounded this Dharma for the youth Sudhana and the great assembly, he further used various skillful means to earnestly exhort and instruct them, causing them to awaken, increase their spiritual power, give rise to great joy, and resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
He also caused Sudhana to recollect the roots of goodness he had planted in the past.

Furthermore, for all the people of Puṇḍravardhana, he manifested supernatural powers according to their faculties and inclinations, extensively preaching the Dharma as was appropriate for those to be saved, and then departed.

At that time, having heard from the youth Mañjuśrī such various, supreme, and wondrous merits and great powers of the Buddhas, the youth Sudhana ardently sought and delighted in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Following after Mañjuśrī, gazing longingly and never leaving him, he turned toward him with single-minded devotion, joined his palms, gazed intently, and spoke these verses:
"O you of great wisdom and majestic power, Who practice the bodhisattva path to benefit sentient beings, I vow to seek your immeasurable realms;
I only pray that the Benevolent Honored One will compassionately grant me leave."
The deep and vast waters of craving form its moats; pride and arrogance stand as its high walls;
the coming and going among the various realms of existence serve as its gates; and the three worlds, so difficult to transcend, constitute its citadel.
Constantly shrouded by the darkness of delusion and ignorance, They are perpetually scorched by the blazing fires of greed and hatred.
The King of Māra holds sovereign power within them; Ignorant children and ordinary worldlings dwell there in dependence.
Deceit, guile, anger, resentment, delusion, and frivolity— entangled by craving as if by a snare,
shrouded by doubt like one born blind— they constantly travel through perilous realms and all manner of false paths.
Constantly bound by stinginess and envy, they enter the three miserable realms and the eight difficulties;
unaware of the cycle of the five destinies, they perpetually undergo the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death.
The sun of great compassion that extinguishes delusion, The perfect wheel whose light of wisdom shines everywhere,
Able to dry up the ocean of afflictions of birth and death— I pray you send down your compassionate light and deign to look upon me.
The full moon of great compassion, pure and stainless, A wheel of merit and radiance, free from defilement—
Bestowing peace upon all sentient beings, I pray you, look upon me briefly and grant me cool relief.
The King of Merit of all Dharmadhātus, Whose white karma has been perfected as the Wheel-Treasure,
Proceeding before you with unimpeded guidance— I pray that you comply with my heart and grant your instructions.
Great caravan leader of vast merit and wisdom, Brave and indomitable in seeking enlightenment,
Universally benefiting all sentient beings— I pray only that you will look upon me with compassion and deliver me.
Clad in the armor of supreme patience, Holding aloft the sharp sword of wisdom,
Ever able to freely vanquish the armies of Māra— May that heroic and valiant one protect me!
Abiding atop the Sumeru peak of the sublime Dharma, surrounded by the celestial maidens of samādhi,
you who crush the asuras of karma and delusion— O true Śakra, may you look upon me.
The three realms of existence are a dark abode for the ignorant and foolish, the cause of the cycle of afflictions and rebirth in the various destinies;
O Benevolent Honored One, you have eternally extinguished them all without remainder, and as a true lamp illuminating the world, you show me the Way.
The evil destinies of sentient beings have been eliminated, And the cultivation of the wholesome paths has been made entirely pure.
To those who serve as a bridge across the ocean of existence, You show me the true vehicle and the gate of liberation.
The inverted perceptions of permanence, bliss, self, and purity, And the heavy, thick, and false attachments that constantly obscure and delude—
The sharp and keen eye of wisdom can eliminate them all, Opening the path of liberation for my True Vehicle.
Thoroughly understanding the true reality without delusion, Fearless among all phenomena,
you who have tamed sentient beings and attained mastery— I pray that you show me the path to bodhi.
Abiding securely on the ground of the Tathāgata’s right view, Growing the trees of merit of all Buddhas,
And raining down the wonderful Dharma-flowers of all Buddhas— I pray that you swiftly show me the path to Bodhi.

All Buddhas of the past, future, and present, like the radiance of the sun appearing in the world, are able to open the gate of ambrosia for the sake of all beings; may you proclaim the path they have attained.
Able to skillfully untie the bonds of all karma, Expertly turning the wondrous Dharma-wheel of the various vehicles,
A person of wisdom who has attained decisive realization and mastery— Reveal to me the Mahāyāna of Universal Radiance.
With great compassion as the hub and the wheel of practice and vows, With faith as the linchpin and firm endurance as the axle,
With the jewels of pure merit as the true yoke— May I be mounted upon this vehicle of Bodhi.
The complete casket of all dhāraṇīs, The majestic canopy of universal compassion,
And the ringing bells of wondrous eloquence— May they carry me upon this Supreme Vehicle.
The pure precepts serve as my bedding, and the various sublime samādhis are my handmaidens;
the great sound of the Dharma drum awakens sentient beings, enabling me to mount this Mahāyāna.
Fully possessing the inexhaustible treasury of the four means of integration, adorned with the jewels of merit as necklaces and ornaments,
and using self-reproach and reproach of others as the traces and bit— may these enable me to mount this unsurpassed vehicle.
Constantly emitting the perfect light of great equanimity, Perpetually anointing oneself with the true fragrance of pure precepts,
And forever extinguishing the sores of the afflictions— May you cause me to mount this most supreme vehicle.
The wheel of non-retrogression that tames the three karmas, The box of samādhi in which the six sense-faculties are stilled,
And the yoke of supreme wisdom and skillful means— May you cause me to mount this wondrous vehicle of Dharma.
Great Vow, who skillfully turns [the wheel] toward merit, Whose power is firm in upholding all dharmas,
And whose wisdom revolves everywhere and at all times— May you cause me to mount this swift vehicle.
Interwoven with the net of Samantabhadra’s myriad practices, The vast movement of compassion turns slowly;
His conduct is fearless and his manner serene— May he cause me to mount this unsurpassed vehicle.
Holding fast with a firmness like vajra, With wondrous wisdom skillfully accomplishing illusory deeds,
Able to sever all obstacles— May you swiftly cause me to mount the vehicle of Samantabhadra.
Great compassion, stainless, equal toward all sentient beings, Universally bestows upon the world the bliss of sages and saints;
Pure wisdom, like space, illuminates the Dharma-realm— May you swiftly cause me to mount this vehicle.
Able to purify all karmic obscurations and delusions, And sever the suffering of worldly transmigration;
Subduing all māras and non-Buddhists, May you cause me to mount this vehicle of the sublime Dharma.
The realm of wisdom is equal to space, Adorned by the power of practice throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
May it universally fulfill the desires of all sentient beings— I pray that you may swiftly cause me to mount this vehicle.
The aspiration for pure joy is immeasurable and difficult to fathom; Ignorance, craving, and views are all extinguished.
Benefiting all beings with an inexhaustible mind— May I swiftly be enabled to mount this vehicle.
The power of aspiration moves as swiftly as the wind, While the mind of meditative concentration remains ever unmoving;
It universally carries all sentient beings— May I be swiftly enabled to mount this vehicle.
Firm vows are like the earth, forever without tilting; Great compassion is like water, constantly benefiting others;
Courageous and strong, they bear the burden without weariness— I pray that you may quickly cause me to mount this vehicle.
The sun of wisdom that universally illumines sentient beings, The perfect wheel of light of the four means of integration,
And the supreme, wondrous, and pure light of dhāraṇī— I pray you reveal these to me, so that I may see them all.
Able to diligently practice and study throughout oceans of eons, The cause for the perfection of all-knowledge,
Who destroys the fortress of stubborn attachment to the conditioned— Grant me such vajra-wisdom as this.
O Benevolent One, regarding the great ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas, you have attained this ocean of wisdom, vast and boundless;
all the virtues of the Buddhas are fully present within you. How excellent! Great Sage, please proclaim it.
Having entered the wondrous Dharma-city of the Dharma King, Having donned the great wisdom-crown of the Wisdom King,
And having bound the stainless silk ribbon of all Buddhas, O Eye of Supreme Wisdom, I pray that you look upon me.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī turned like an elephant king to look at Sudhana and spoke these words:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

"Noble son! You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and you further desire to draw near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), practice the conduct of a bodhisattva, and inquire about the path traversed by all bodhisattvas."
"Good son! To draw near to and make offerings to spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) is the primary causal condition for gathering all-knowledge (sarvajñatā).
Because one delights in drawing near to spiritual friends, all-knowledge will swiftly be brought to fulfillment."
"Therefore, do not give rise to weariness or fatigue regarding this. Sudhana said, "Noble One!"
I only pray that, out of compassion, you will explain this extensively for me: how should I learn the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should I cultivate the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should I initiate the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one practice the bodhisattva conduct?
How should one fulfill the bodhisattva conduct?
How should one purify the bodhisattva conduct?
How should one transform the bodhisattva practice?
How should one enter deeply into the bodhisattva practice?
How should one give birth to the bodhisattva practice?
How should one observe the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one expand the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How should one bring the conduct of a bodhisattva to fulfillment?
"How should one act so that the conduct of Samantabhadra may be swiftly brought to full completion?
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva spoke these verses for the sake of the youth Sudhana:
"Excellent, O ocean of pure merit! Son of the Buddha, you have come to my presence."
Having aroused a vast and great heart of compassion, He courageously aspires to seek supreme enlightenment.
Desiring to deliver all sentient beings From the sufferings of wandering through all worlds,
He has already made great vows deep as the ocean, And diligently cultivates all bodhisattva practices.
If there is a bodhisattva whose mind is firm and steadfast, who dwells long in birth and death without weariness or fatigue,
they shall fulfill the practices of Samantabhadra and attain the indestructible merits of a Buddha.
Merit, majestic light, merit-star, Source of merit, ocean of merit—
You are able to act universally for all sentient beings, Vowing to cultivate the pure conduct of Samantabhadra.
You behold the boundless buddha-fields, And all buddhas of the past, future, and present;
You also hear the sublime wheel of Dharma they turn, Retaining it through the power of mindfulness without forgetfulness.
In all lands throughout the ten directions, you shall universally behold immeasurable Tathāgatas;
may the ocean of your vows be purified and fully realized, as you perfect bodhisattva practices as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
You have entered the great ocean of the Dharma of skillful means and dwell securely upon the ground of the Tathāgata’s merit;
you should cultivate the supreme practices of the Guide and shall attain all-encompassing wisdom that requires no teacher.
Throughout all vast lands, for as many eons as there are atoms within those realms,
you shall cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and accomplish the most supreme path to enlightenment.
Throughout oceans of boundless eons, you have pervaded all lands in the ten directions;
desiring to fulfill all great vows, you have practiced the wondrous deeds of Samantabhadra.
Within this assembly, immeasurable sentient beings, having heard your vow, are all filled with joy;
they have all resolved upon the vast mind of enlightenment and single-mindedly aspire to train in the vehicle of Samantabhadra.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī had spoken these verses, he addressed the youth Sudhana, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good son! If there are sentient beings who are able to resolve their minds toward Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, that is difficult;
but once they have resolved their minds, to further desire to diligently seek and practice the bodhisattva conduct is twice as difficult."
"Good son! Since you have now resolved to seek the Bodhisattva path and desire to accomplish the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, you should diligently seek out true spiritual friends."

"Good son! In seeking a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), do not give rise to weariness or indolence; upon seeing a spiritual friend, do not give rise to complacency. Regarding all the instructions of a spiritual friend, you should mindfully follow them and not oppose them; regarding the skillful means (upāya-kauśalya) of a spiritual friend, you should only show reverence and not look for faults."
“Good son! To the south of here there is a land called Supreme Bliss;

in that land there is a mountain named Wondrous Peak, where there dwells a bhikṣu named Auspicious Cloud. You should go to him and ask: how should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva practice? How should a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva practice? And so on, until: how does a bodhisattva swiftly attain the full perfection of the conduct of Samantabhadra?”
"Noble son! That spiritual friend shall explain to you the complete and perfect practices and vows of Samantabhadra.

When the youth Sudhana heard these words, his heart was filled with joy; he leaped for immeasurable delight, conceiving a profound longing for that bhikṣu and a fervent devotion toward Mañjuśrī. He prostrated at the bhikṣu’s feet, circumambulated him countless times, and departed while weeping with tears streaming down his face.

At that time, the youth Sudhana traveled south by stages until he reached Mount Sumeru in the country of Supratiṣṭhita. Upon the mountain, he searched everywhere—in the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below—for seven days, yet he was unable to find him.

Because of his diligent quest for the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), he disregarded even his own life; free from thoughts of hunger or thirst, he observed with right mindfulness, his mind peaceful and undaunted.

After seven days had passed, he saw that bhikṣu walking slowly in meditation on a separate mountain peak; he immediately went to him, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and stood with palms joined, saying:
"Noble One!..."
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva practice.
How does one initiate the bodhisattva practices?
How does one carry out the bodhisattva practices?
And how, furthermore, does one swiftly attain the complete fulfillment of the practices of Samantabhadra?

I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction and guidance; I only pray that, out of compassion, you will explain for me how a bodhisattva may swiftly achieve anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the bhikṣu Śrīmegha said to Sudhana:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

"Good son! That you have already been able to resolve your mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is a difficult thing; furthermore, that you are now able to inquire about the practice of the bodhisattva path is the most difficult among difficulties. Namely:"

Diligently seeking the bodhisattva path; diligently seeking the bodhisattva realm; diligently seeking the vast and pure conduct of a bodhisattva; diligently seeking the miraculous manifestations appearing by a bodhisattva; diligently seeking the manifestation of the various gates of great liberation by a bodhisattva; diligently seeking the manifestation of the various activities in the world by a bodhisattva; diligently seeking to accord with the various mental activities of sentient beings by a bodhisattva; diligently seeking the manifestation of entering and emerging from birth-and-death and nirvana by a bodhisattva; diligently seeking a mind that is unattached to the conditioned and the unconditioned by a bodhisattva; and diligently seeking to sever and eliminate the various afflictions and subtle transgressions of sentient beings by a bodhisattva.

"Good son! I have attained the power of sovereign and decisive understanding; the eye of faith is pure, the light of wisdom shines forth, and the universal eye is clear and penetrating. Possessing pure conduct, the eye of insight surveys all realms universally. Through skillful means, I am free from all obstructions. With a purified body, I travel everywhere to all lands in the ten directions to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas;
and by the power of faith and resolve, I constantly keep in mind all Buddhas of the ten directions."
By the power of dhāraṇī, they uphold all the Buddha-dharmas of the ten directions;
by the eye of wisdom, they constantly see all Buddhas of the ten directions, namely:
They see one Buddha, two Buddhas, ten Buddhas, a hundred Buddhas, a thousand Buddhas, a hundred thousand Buddhas,
a billion Buddhas, ten billion Buddhas, a hundred billion Buddhas, a trillion Buddhas, ten trillion Buddhas,
a hundred trillion Buddhas, a quadrillion Buddhas, and ten quadrillion Buddhas in the eastern direction.

One sees a thousand nayuta koṭis of Buddhas, even up to seeing innumerable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;
even up to seeing as many Buddhas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa. Four...
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in the entire world-system; Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a small thousand-world system;
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a medium thousand-world system; Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a great trichiliocosm; Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred buddha-fields; Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a thousand buddha-fields...
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a mote of dust; Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields; Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in billions of Buddha-fields;
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of billions of Buddha-fields; Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in trillions of Buddha-fields;
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddha-fields; and Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in nayuta-billions of Buddha-fields.
From Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a single buddha-field, up to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields—
just as one sees all the Buddhas in the eastern direction, so too does one see all the Buddhas in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.

According to what is seen, within each and every direction, there are Buddhas with various physical marks, various appearances, various supernormal powers, various enjoyments, various playful manifestations, various assemblies adorning their sites of enlightenment, various lights shining boundlessly, various palaces adorning their realms, and various lifespans displayed as being long or short; in accordance with the diverse inclinations of sentient beings, they manifest various gateways to attaining perfect enlightenment, extensively displaying spiritual transformations amidst great assemblies, uttering the lion’s roar, and liberating sentient beings.
Good son! I have attained only this Dharma-door of the unimpeded wisdom that universally perceives the equal realm of all Buddhas through recollection.
How could I possibly know the limits of the immeasurable wisdom and the fully perfected, pure practice-doors of the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?
That is to say:

the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through the universal illumination of the light of wisdom upon diverse realms, because the various lands of all Buddhas and their adorned palaces are all manifested before one;

and the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through abiding in various superior aspirations, because according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, they are all enabled to see the Buddha and attain purity.

They cause them to dwell securely in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through the ultimate powers of a Buddha, so that they may enter and practice in accordance with the ten powers of the Tathāgata;

they cause them to dwell securely in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through the various ultimate true dharmas of the Tathāgatas, so that they may see all Buddhas expounding the true dharma and hear it all;

and they cause them to dwell securely in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha as the non-differentiated treasury that universally illumines the ten directions, so that they may universally behold the oceans of Buddhas who are entirely without distinction throughout all worlds.

The gate of mindfulness of the Buddha by entering the realm of the invisible and most subtle, because one thoroughly perceives the Tathāgata’s sovereign miraculous transformations within all subtle objects;
the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha by abiding through various eons, because one constantly sees all Buddhas performing buddha-works throughout all eons and remains in close proximity to them;
the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha by abiding at all times, because one constantly attains the vision of the Buddha and dwells together with the Buddha without ever being separated.
They dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all lands, because they see the Buddha-body in all buddha-fields as transcending the world and being without equal;

they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all worlds, because they universally behold all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time according to whatever aspirations exist within their own minds;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all objects, because they universally see the continuous manifestation of all Buddhas within all objective realms.
They dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through the quiescence of all natures, because in every thought-moment they see all Buddhas in all lands manifesting parinirvāṇa;
they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all times and places, because within a single day they see all Buddhas departing from their respective abodes to transform beings;

they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through the vastness of all objects, because they see all Buddhas sitting in the full lotus posture, each individual Buddha-body filling the entire Dharma-realm.

They dwell in the gateway of mindfulness of the Buddha through the subtlety of all phenomena, because within a single pore they see unspeakably many Buddhas appearing in the world, all arriving at that place to be served;

they dwell in the gateway of mindfulness of the Buddha through the adornment of the limits of moments, because within a single thought-moment they see all lands where Buddhas attain equal and perfect enlightenment and manifest spiritual transformations;
they dwell in the gateway of mindfulness of the Buddha through all phenomena, seeing all Buddhas appearing in the world and turning the wheel of Dharma with the light of wisdom.

They dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through mastery of mind, because they see the reflected images of all Tathāgatas appearing according to whatever desires and inclinations exist within their own minds;

they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all karmic actions, because they manifest their bodies in accordance with the practices performed by all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm in order to bring them to awakening;

they dwell in the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha through all spiritual transformations, because they see all Buddhas dwelling within the vast ocean of fragrant water, seated upon lotus pedestals, universally manifesting spiritual transformations that fill the ten directions.

There is the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha abiding in the realm of space, because it observes the clouds of bodies manifested by the Tathāgata, which adorn the dharma-realm and the realm of space;
regarding such immeasurable and innumerable gates of mindfulness of the Buddha, how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious practices?

"Good son! To the south there is a land called Sāgaramukha. There dwells a bhikṣu named Sāgaramegha; go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."

The bhikṣu Sāgaramegha is able to skillfully discern and develop the causes and conditions of vast roots of goodness; he shall cause you to enter the stage of the vast aids to the path, cause you to accomplish the power of vast roots of goodness, explain to you the causes for generating the bodhicitta, cause you to give rise to the radiance of the Great Vehicle, cause you to attain the vast pāramitās, cause you to enter the ocean of vast practices, cause you to turn the wheel of vast vows, cause you to purify the gateways of vast adornments, and cause you to arouse the power of vast compassion.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the bhikṣu Śrīmegha, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and departed with deep longing.
The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha of Great Extensive Radiance, Scroll Four;
The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha of Great Extensive Radiance, Scroll Five.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśa, by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation," at that time,
the youth Sudhana, having heard the instructions of the spiritual friend, maintained right mindfulness with a single-minded focus.

The gateways of the light of wisdom that accord with contemplative reflection; the gateways of profound liberation that accord with thorough penetration; the gateways of sovereign samādhis that accord with mindful retention; the gateways of pure instructions that accord with reverent service; the gateways of the majestic power of all Buddhas as seen through observation; the gateways of the abodes of all Buddhas as seen through joyful aspiration; the gateways of the modes of conduct of all Buddhas as seen through understanding; the gateways of the manifestations of all Buddhas as seen through recollection; the gateways of the dharma-realm of all Buddhas as seen through entry; and the gateways of the spheres of all Buddhas as seen through peaceful dwelling.

Traveling south by stages toward the country of Samudramukha, he went to where the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha was staying. He prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined before him, addressed him, saying: "Noble One!

I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to enter the most profound and supreme ocean of wisdom; yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva is able to fulfill the bodhisattva practices and nurture the seeds of enlightenment.
How can one abandon the household of ordinary beings and be born into the household of the Tathāgatas?
How can one cross the ocean of birth and death and enter the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom?
How can one leave behind the stage of the foolish and ordinary, and enter the most supreme stage of the Buddha?
How can one sever the stream of birth and death and enter the stream of the Buddha’s pure conduct?
How can one destroy the wheel of birth and death and accomplish the wheel of great vows?
How can one extinguish the realm of Māra and manifest the realm of the Buddha?
How can one exhaust the ocean of craving and desire, and increase the ocean of great compassion?
How can one close the gates of the three evil realms and the eight difficulties, and open the gates to the human and celestial realms and to nirvana?
How can one emerge from the city of the fetters of the three realms of existence and enter the city of liberation through the knowledge of all modes?
How can one renounce all precious playthings and requisites to benefit and gather in all sentient beings?
"I only pray that you will take pity on me and explain this for my sake.
Then, the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha said to Sudhana: "Noble son!
"Have you already resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
Sudhana replied, "Indeed!"
"I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Sāgaramegha replied, "Excellent!"
Excellent! Son of good family,
even the hearing of those who have resolved their minds toward bodhicitta is difficult to encounter, let alone being able to personally and deeply resolve one's mind to set out upon it.
"Good son! If sentient beings have not previously cultivated and planted deep and firm roots of goodness, they will be unable to give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Therefore, a bodhisattva must attain the realm of equality and non-obstruction, because it is illuminated by the light of universal roots of goodness;
they must attain the treasury of true skillful means, because it is illuminated by the light of the samādhi of the right path;
and they must attain the ocean-treasury of accumulated merit, because their bodies are adorned by a vast mass of blessings.
One must increase various wholesome dharmas (*śukladharma*), because they arise in every thought-moment without ceasing;
one must be able to serve true spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), because one asks about the essentials of the Dharma without weariness;
and one must abandon stinginess, having no hoarding, because one has no attachment to body, life, or wealth.
One must abandon arrogance, remaining with a mind free from highs and lows, dwelling as immovable as the great earth;
one must always maintain compassion and accord with sentient beings, benefiting them equally without opposition;
and one must remain within birth and death, never forsaking the resolve to deliver suffering beings from the evil realms.
One must constantly observe the realm of the Tathāgata, seeking with joy to cultivate it until its ultimate perfection;
one must constantly benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings—
it is only by doing so that one can give rise to the bodhicitta.
"Regarding those who resolve upon Bodhicitta: it is said that they give rise to the mind of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) for the sake of rescuing and delivering all sentient beings from suffering;
and they give rise to the mind of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) for the sake of bestowing equal blessings and benefits upon all sentient beings."
One generates a mind of peace and happiness in order to eliminate the aggregates of suffering of sentient beings;
one generates a mind of benefit in order to quell the unwholesome minds of sentient beings;
and one generates a mind of compassion in order to rescue and protect sentient beings who are terrified.
They give rise to the mind of non-attachment by relinquishing attachment to obstructive dharmas;
they give rise to the vast mind by pervading all Buddha-fields throughout the dharma-realm;
they give rise to the boundless mind by reaching everywhere, equal to the realm of empty space.
Because they behold the wondrous form-body of all Buddhas, they give rise to a stainless mind;
because they contemplate the inexhaustible wisdom regarding the phenomena of the three periods of time, they give rise to a pure mind;
and because they desire to universally enter the profound and vast ocean of the knowledge of all-knowledge, they give rise to a mind of great wisdom.
Because they give rise to such various kinds of minds as these, this is called a bodhisattva’s arousal of the bodhicitta. "Good son!
When I first resided in this country of Sāgaradvāra for twelve years, I constantly took the great ocean as my object of contemplation, observing it through ten aspects."

That is to say: contemplating that the great ocean is vast and immeasurable; contemplating that the great ocean is deep and its bottom difficult to reach; contemplating that the great ocean has a single uniform salty taste; contemplating that the great ocean gives birth to all manner of jewels; contemplating that the great ocean swallows and receives all flowing streams; contemplating that the differences in the colors of the water in the great ocean are inconceivable; contemplating that the great ocean is the dwelling place for various kinds of sentient beings; contemplating that the great ocean accommodates immeasurable sentient beings with massive bodies; contemplating that the great ocean can receive the rain poured down by great clouds; and contemplating that the great ocean is ultimately ever-full, without increase or decrease.
"Good son! I further reflected:
'Is there anything in this world that is more profound and vast than this ocean?'"
"Does this ocean ever increase or decrease as it receives [all things]? "Good son!

While I was reflecting in this way, a great lotus flower, adorned with various jewels, suddenly appeared from within the great ocean. It had a stem made of the invincible *indranīla* lapis lazuli diamond-mani king jewel, a pedestal made of *vaiḍūrya* mani king jewel, and petals made of stainless, pure Jāmbūnada gold. Its interior was filled with the fragrant white sandalwood and aloeswood incense that blooms according to the season; its filaments were made of yellow, translucent agate king jewels, and a net of a million mani jewel ornaments was spread across its surface."
All that was adorned and arrayed was boundless and circular, its radiant glory shining in the four directions and covering the great ocean.

A million kings of the desire realm rained down various celestial jewels, celestial flowers, celestial garlands, celestial incense, celestial burning incense, celestial unguents, celestial powdered incense, celestial exquisite garments, and celestial banners, pennants, and canopies, descending like clouds;
a million dragon kings raised great clouds of fragrance and rained down various fragrant waters.
A million yakṣa kings offered various rare and wondrous treasures;
a million rākṣasa kings, each with a mind of loving-kindness, joined their palms and gazed upon him;
and a million gandharva kings sang praises with the sounds of exquisite music.
A million asura kings held its stalks and stood with bodies bowed;
a million garuḍa kings held various necklaces in their beaks, with exquisite jeweled silk ribbons hanging down on all four sides;
and a million kiṃnara kings gave rise to a mind of benefit, filled with joy and delight.
A million mahoraga kings gave rise to pure hearts, prostrating with reverence;
a million human kings gave rise to hearts of profound respect, joining their palms in gazing adoration;
and a million universal monarchs each offered worship, adorning it with the seven treasures.
A million Brahmā kings prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet;
a million Śuddhāvāsa devas paid homage with palms joined;
and a million lords of the ocean deities appeared simultaneously, paying respectful obeisance.
One million fire-god lords each held various kinds of exquisite jewels as adornments;

one million flavor-light *maṇi* jewels radiated light everywhere; one million pure-merit *maṇi* jewels were scattered about as adornments; one million all-pervading *maṇi* jewels formed a treasury of purity; one million stainless-treasury *maṇi* jewels shone with brilliant splendor; one million auspicious-treasury *maṇi* jewels emitted wondrous light; one million exquisite-treasury *maṇi* jewels illuminated boundless realms; one million Jambū-dhvaja *maṇi* jewels were arranged in rows all around; and one million indestructible vajra-*maṇi* jewels provided pure adornment.
A million sun-treasury maṇi jewels were vast, pure, and their circular halos shone everywhere;
a million delightful maṇi jewels manifested myriad colors and were fully adorned;
a million sovereign-heart maṇi jewels emitted light of variegated hues and rained down inexhaustible treasures.

"All the adornments of this great lotus arise from the vast supramundane roots of goodness accumulated by the Tathāgata in the past; they cause the various bodhisattvas to fulfill their faith and vows within each of these flowers;
they manifest everywhere throughout all worlds in the ten directions without exception;
and they are produced from the karma of the King of Fragrances through the contemplation of illusion, being adorned by the dharma of non-arising."
It arises from the contemplation of phenomena as being like dreams, because it is sealed by the markless dharma;
it arises from the dharma of non-attachment and freedom from contention, because it observes objects without clinging;
it constantly emits sublime sounds expounding the vast realm of the Tathāgata, its resonance filling all the pure buddha-fields.
Even if one were to praise this flower with wondrous eloquence for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas, its merit would never be exhausted. "Good son!
At that time, upon this lotus flower, I saw a Tathāgata sitting cross-legged, endowed with all the marks and signs of perfection, his form vast and towering, reaching up to the Peak of Existence."
The precious lotus throne upon which the Tathāgata sits is inconceivable; the assembly at the site of enlightenment is inconceivable;
his perfected wisdom is inconceivable; the radiance of his circular halo is inconceivable;
the manifestation of his majestic deportment is inconceivable; the blazing intensity of his light is inconceivable; and his various marks [of physical perfection] are inconceivable.
The secondary marks are inconceivable; the mastery of manifestations is inconceivable; the subduing through supernormal powers is inconceivable;
the pure and wondrous physical form is inconceivable; the mark of the invisible crown of the head is inconceivable;
the mark of the long and broad tongue is inconceivable; and the skillfulness of eloquence is inconceivable.
The universal resonance of his voice is inconceivable; his immeasurable power of wisdom is inconceivable;
his pure fearlessness is inconceivable; his knowledge of unimpeded analytical comprehension is inconceivable;
the recollection of that Buddha’s past cultivation of fundamental practices is inconceivable; his mastery over enlightenment is inconceivable; the Dharma...
The thunderous roar is inconceivable; the universal manifestation through the Gate of All Doors is inconceivable;
the various adornments are inconceivable; the distinct differences perceived according to one's left or right are inconceivable;
and the universal benefit that brings all to maturity is inconceivable.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata extended his right hand from atop the lotus and stroked my head, expounding for me the Dharma-gate of the Universal Eye;

he revealed all the practices of Bodhisattvas, elucidated the realms of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed the wondrous teachings of all Buddhas, illuminated all Buddha-lands, perfected the primary and secondary marks of all Buddhas, subdued all heterodox arguments of external paths, and dispersed and extinguished all hosts of Māras.

They are able to bring joy to all sentient beings, to subdue the afflictions of all sentient beings, to illuminate the mental activities of all sentient beings, and to skillfully understand the faculties and natures of all sentient beings. By means of their majestic power, they can universally turn the wheel of Dharma, causing all sentient beings to attain awakening according to their respective minds.
"I have heard this Dharma-door of the Universal Eye from that Buddha; I have received, upheld, recited, and contemplated it.

Suppose there were someone who, using ink as vast as the great ocean and pens as numerous as Mount Sumeru, were to write down this inexhaustible, vast ocean-treasury of the Universal Eye Dharma-door—writing even a single gate within a single chapter, a single dharma within a single gate, a single meaning within a single dharma, or a single phrase within a single meaning, or even a mere fraction thereof—it would still be impossible to achieve, let alone to write it out in its entirety."
"Good son! For twelve hundred years under that Buddha, I have upheld this Universal Eye Dharma-door, maintaining it without interruption.
Day by day, I constantly receive and retain ten incalculable chapters through ten kinds of dhāraṇī-doors, namely: [The list of ten dhāraṇīs follows]"
By the light of the *dhāraṇī* of hearing and retaining, they receive countless chapters;
by the light of the *dhāraṇī* of the gate of tranquility, they enter into countless chapters;
by the light of the *dhāraṇī* of infinite revolution, they universally enter countless chapters.
By means of the light of the *dhāraṇī* of Universal Illumination through Observation According to the Grounds, they distinguish countless categories;
by means of the light of the *dhāraṇī* of Endowed Power, they universally gather countless categories;
by means of the light of the *dhāraṇī* of Lotus Adornment, they bring forth countless categories.
By the light of the *dhāraṇī* of Subtle and Wondrous Speech, they expound countless chapters;
by the light of the *dhāraṇī* of the Treasury of Space, they manifest countless chapters;
by the light of the *dhāraṇī* of the Mountain of Massed Radiance, they expand and broaden countless chapters.
By means of the light of the *Samudragarbha-samantadhāraṇī*, one analyzes countless chapters.
"Good son! At that time, in every world throughout the ten directions, there were immeasurable sentient beings who came to my presence for the sake of hearing the Dharma."
That is to say:

the kings of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, human kings, and Brahmā kings—these various kings, together with their retinues, came to where I was to inquire about my Dharma.

I have expounded this for them all in successive order, analyzing and explaining it so that they may all be filled with joy, develop a heart of love and delight, enter into it with deep faith, achieve realization and mastery, and abide securely in this Dharma-door of the Universal Eye of the Radiant and Sublime Conduct of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

"Good son! I know only this Universal Eye Dharma-door. As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, they have deeply entered the ocean of all bodhisattva practices, because their powers of aspiration are entirely purified;
they have deeply entered the ocean of all vast vows, because they remain in the world throughout the exhaustion of all kalpas."
They enter deeply into the ocean of all sentient beings, because they universally benefit them according to their mental activities;
they enter deeply into the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings, because they give rise to the unimpeded wisdom of the ten powers;
they enter deeply into the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings, because they tame and bring them to maturity at the appropriate times.
They enter deeply into the ocean of all identical and diverse lands, in order to fulfill their original vows by completely purifying them;
they enter deeply into the ocean of all inexhaustible Buddhas, constantly vowing to serve them and offer worship;
they enter deeply into the ocean of the Dharma of all Perfectly Enlightened Ones, being able to awaken to and enter it through wisdom.
They have deeply entered the ocean of all Buddhas' merits, because they have fully cultivated the path of reality;
they have deeply entered the ocean of all speech and expression, because they turn the wheel of Dharma throughout all lands.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

“Good son! From here, travel sixty yojanas to the south; along the way to Laṅkā, there is a village called Seashore. There dwells a bhikṣu named Sunetra. Go to him and ask: ‘How does a bodhisattva cause the bodhisattva practice to quickly attain purification?’”
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Samudramegha, circumambulated him to the right while gazing up at him in reverence, and took his leave to depart.
At that time, Sudhana reflected upon the instructions of the spiritual friend;

he focused his mind on recollecting the Dharma-gate of the Universal Eye, concentrated his thoughts on the miraculous power and majesty of the Tathāgata, and retained in memory the clouds of bodies of subtle Dharma-phrases. He entered the ocean-like teachings of the boundless Dharma-gates, observed the dignified conduct and ritual protocols of the spiritual friend, swam through the eddies and whirlpools of the profound ocean of Dharma, universally entered the space of the Dharma-realm, purified all veils and obscurations of the Dharma-eye, and gathered the Dharma-jewels accumulated by the spiritual friend.
Maintaining this mental attention, he traveled south by stages until he reached the coastal village of Laṅkāmārga; there he surveyed the ten directions, searching everywhere for the bhikṣu Subhūti.
He saw that bhikṣu walking back and forth in mid-air.
Inconceivable numbers of Śuddhāvāsa devas, together with their palaces, joined their palms in reverence in the sky and made great vows as an offering;
inconceivable numbers of Brahmā kings bowed their bodies and joined their palms, producing wondrous sounds and praising him according to human conventions as an offering.

Countless tens of millions of devas of the desire realm and their respective kings respectfully surrounded him, filling the void of space; they spread clouds of celestial flowers and rained down showers of blossoms, performing divine music that produced wondrous sounds. Countless silken banners, precious standards, and parasols, adorned with every variety of ornament, completely pervaded the sky as an offering.

Furthermore, countless great nāga kings arose in the sky, producing inconceivable clouds of agalloch incense that filled the entire expanse, accompanied by rolling thunder and flashing lightning as an offering.
Immeasurable and inconceivable numbers of yakṣa kings, each with their own retinues, surrounded him on all sides, respectfully guarding and making offerings to him.

Innumerable and inconceivable numbers of rākṣasa kings, together with their retinues—whose forms were immense and most terrifying—all gave rise to hearts of compassion, drawing near to gaze upon him in reverence and made offerings;

immeasurable asura kings raised inconceivable clouds of maṇi jewels, emitting great radiance that filled the void of space, raining down various precious ornaments that shone brilliantly as they made offerings;

countless garuḍa kings assumed the forms of youths, surrounded by exquisite celestial maidens, and giving rise to great kindness and pity without any intent to harm, they joined their palms in reverence and made offerings.

Countless kings of the kinnaras struck various musical instruments, producing all manner of subtle and exquisite sounds; furthermore, with various words and phrases in accordance with the Dharma, they sang praises as an offering.
Countless kings of the mahoragas held inconceivable, supreme, and delicate celestial garments, approaching and following closely, arrayed all around as an offering.
Immeasurable lords of the ocean spirits performed various musical performances, blowing harmonious and elegant melodies as an offering.
When the youth Sudhana saw this bhikṣu walking with sovereign ease through the air, and further beheld such acts of offering filling the void,
he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness, unable to contain himself; prostrating his body upon the ground,
he paid homage with single-minded devotion, and only after a long while did he rise.
With palms joined, he said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should diligently seek the Buddha-dharma."
How does one accumulate the Buddha-dharmas?
How does one fulfill the Buddha-dharmas?
How does one perfuse the Buddha-dharmas?
How does one practice the Buddha-dharma?
How does one purify the Buddha-dharma?
How does one accord with the dharma practiced by the Buddha?
How does one penetrate the Buddha’s method of calculation?
How does one increase the Buddha’s pervasive dharma?
How does one purify the Buddha’s ultimate dharma?
"How does one comprehensively encompass the dharmas of a Buddha’s qualities?
How can one enter the dharmas that accord with a Buddha?
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction."
I only pray that, out of compassion, you will explain for me how a bodhisattva may constantly behold all Buddhas, hear the Dharma, and practice with diligence without ever abandoning them;
and how a bodhisattva may always be one with the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas without ever abandoning them.
How does a bodhisattva constantly realize all Buddha-dharmas through wisdom without ever abandoning them?
How does a bodhisattva constantly benefit sentient beings through great vows without ever abandoning them?
How does a bodhisattva constantly cultivate all bodhisattva activities without ever abandoning them?
How does a bodhisattva constantly dwell throughout oceans of eons, practicing without weariness and never forsaking their resolve?
How does a bodhisattva constantly abide within the ocean of lands, universally adorning them without ever abandoning them?
How does a bodhisattva constantly rely on the power of the Buddhas, being able to fully know and see the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas without ever abandoning them?
How does a bodhisattva constantly take birth at will within the six realms of existence, abiding in the path of non-abiding without ever abandoning it?
How does a bodhisattva constantly receive the rain-clouds of the true Dharma from all Buddhas, being able to remember and uphold them all without ever abandoning them?
How does a bodhisattva constantly emit the light of wisdom that universally illumines the spheres of practice of the Buddhas of the three periods of time without ever abandoning them?
I pray only that you will, out of compassion, expound this for me.
At that time, the bhikṣu Sunetra said to Sudhana: "Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and now you further aspire to seek the dharma of all-knowledge and the dharma of self-awakening."

"Good son! Since you have been able to give rise to a mind of deep faith and joyful affection, and have inquired of me with such earnestness and persistence, you should listen attentively; I shall now explain it for you."
“Good son! I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door of universal, swift, and courageous non-empty offerings to all Buddhas that mature sentient beings.
Within this door, whether walking or standing still, I constantly practice and contemplate it;”
Entering and emerging [into states of concentration], they observe in accordance with reality;
immediately, they attain the light of wisdom named "Universally Illuminating All Dharmas Ultimately Without Obstruction.
By virtue of attaining such light of wisdom, they know the various mental activities of all sentient beings without any hindrance.
Unimpeded: they know the various deaths and births of all sentient beings without obstruction;
they know the past lives of all sentient beings without obstruction; they know the events of future eons for all sentient beings without obstruction;
they know the affairs of the present world for all sentient beings without obstruction; they know the various [aspects] of all sentient beings...
Their speech and sounds accord with worldly conventions and distinctions without obstruction; they know the various nets of doubt held by sentient beings and resolve them all without obstruction;
they know the various faculties and natures of sentient beings and the differences in how they receive the Dharma without obstruction;
and they know the proper time for sentient beings to be transformed, going to each to subdue them without obstruction.
Unimpeded, they know all time divisions—kṣaṇas, lava-muhūrtas, days and nights, years and kalpas—their extensions and contractions, and their mutual interpenetration, without any obstruction;
they know the succession and continuity of the flow of all phenomena within the ocean of the three periods of time without any obstruction;
and they know the infinite distinctions of all Buddha-fields, being able to...
With their bodies they travel everywhere throughout the ten directions without any obstruction;
why is this? Because they have attained the supernormal powers that are non-abiding, unconditioned, and without activity.

“Good son! By virtue of having attained this power of supernatural faculties, I may walk, stand, sit, or lie down within the void; furthermore, I manifest various modes of deportment with mastery over appearing and disappearing.”
Or they may divide a single body into many bodies, or combine many bodies into one;
or they may come and go, enter and exit, or pass through stone walls without obstruction;
or they may sit cross-legged in mid-air, traveling freely like a bird.
He enters the earth as if it were water and treads upon water as if it were solid ground;
smoke and flames issue forth from every part of his body above and below, their brilliant radiance blazing like a great mass of fire;
and at times, he causes the entire great earth to tremble.
At times they touch the sun and moon with their hands;
at times they manifest majestic power surpassing that of Maheśvara;
at times they manifest a great body exceeding the world of Brahmā.
Some, through their supernormal powers, exercise mastery over transformations;
some manifest clouds of burning incense that swirl like parasols, completely covering the ten directions;
and some manifest clouds of jewel-flames, their brilliant light blazing intensely to illuminate all things.
Some manifest clouds of transformations, their bodies assuming various forms equal in number to the realms of sentient beings;
others manifest clouds of nets of light, complete with all colors, transparent and unimpeded.

Or, in a single thought-moment, he may manifest his body so as to pass beyond one world in the eastern direction, ten worlds, a hundred worlds, a thousand worlds, a hundred-thousand worlds, a billion worlds, ten billion worlds, a hundred billion worlds, a hundred-thousand billion worlds, a hundred-thousand-billion-nayuta worlds, and even beyond countless worlds, immeasurable worlds, boundless worlds, incomparable worlds, inconceivable worlds, unquantifiable worlds, ineffable worlds, unspeakable worlds, and unspeakably-unspeakable worlds; or even beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa, and even beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of unspeakably-unspeakable Buddha-fields.

Thus, throughout all oceans of world-systems—in the arising of all worlds, in the spatial locations of all worlds, in the revolutions of all worlds, in the pervasiveness of all worlds, in the transformations of all worlds, in the names of all worlds, in the dharma-gates of all worlds, in the temporal kalpas of all worlds, in the subtleties of all worlds, in the bodhimaṇḍas of all worlds, in the ornaments of all worlds, and in the great assemblies of all worlds.
In all such various worlds, within every single realm therein, there are Tathāgatas manifesting perfect enlightenment;

each of those Tathāgatas further manifests bodies in the distinct assemblies of great multitudes, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, and I universally manifest my own body before all those Buddhas.
From each and every body, they universally rain down clouds of all manner of offerings, as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of all Buddha-fields—namely:

clouds of all flowers, clouds of all fragrances, clouds of all garlands, clouds of all canopies, clouds of all banners, clouds of all pennants, clouds of all curtains, clouds of all nets, clouds of all powdered incense, clouds of all ointment-incense, and clouds of all garments;
with all their bodies, each holding such clouds of offering implements, they perform this worship.
The various ways in which each Tathāgata turns the wheel of Dharma— namely, through extensive exposition,

concise exposition, praise, censure, clear exposition, esoteric exposition, incomplete exposition, complete exposition, indeterminate exposition, and definitive exposition— I have fully understood, recollected, and upheld them all.
In every single land, within all the oceans of Buddha-fields, I remember and maintain all their adornments without ever forgetting them.
As it is in the eastern direction, so it is likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.

“Good son! All sentient beings in all these worlds, whether they hear my name, see my body, or behold the place where I walk, stand, or sit; whether they single-mindedly prostrate and make offerings, or at times are distracted, harboring doubts and lacking faith—all such beings will certainly attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.”

I clearly perceive all sentient beings in those worlds; according to their size, their superiority or inferiority, and their suffering or happiness, I manifest in forms identical to theirs. As appropriate for their deliverance, I teach, transform, and bring them to maturity.
To whatever sentient beings approach me, I cause them all to dwell securely within this Dharma-gate.
“Good son! I only know this unobstructed gate of liberation called ‘Universal, Swift, and Valiantly Unfailing Worship of All Buddhas to Mature Sentient Beings.
As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who fully uphold the precepts of great compassion and the precepts of the pāramitās...”
Abiding in the precepts of the Mahāyāna, not departing from the precepts of the bodhisattva path, not clinging to any phenomena,
not abandoning the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), not falling into the stages of the two vehicles, always taking the Buddha-dharma as the object of focus,
the mind constantly recollecting all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and the resolve and aspiration thus generated being equal to space.
The precepts that have no basis in any world; the precepts that are without deficiency or leakage; the precepts that are not turbid or confused; the precepts that are without loss;
the precepts that are not defiled by admixture; the precepts that are without regret; the precepts that are without weariness or indolence;
the pure precepts; the precepts free from dust; the stainless precepts—such are the merits of the bodhisattva’s practice of the precepts.
"Immeasurable and boundless; how could I possibly know or speak of them? 'Good son!
To the south from here there is a land named Daratīṭa; in that land there is a city named Vajrasānu."
Within it dwells a great being named Megha;
go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Sughoṣa, circumambulated him to the right while gazing up at him with reverence, and took his leave.
At that time, Sudhana followed the instructions of the spiritual friend with single-minded devotion; with right mindfulness, he contemplated that gateway to the light of the Dharma;

with a pure mind, he entered into it with deep faith; he recollected the majestic power of the Dharma, followed the conduct of the Buddhas, maintained it with focused attention, continued the lineage of the Triple Gem, and praised the nature of detachment from desire.
Mindfully recollecting spiritual friends, he observes them universally, illuminating the three periods of time; remembering his original great vows, he practices in accordance with them;
with an unimpeded mind, he enters the realms of sentient beings, constantly and diligently applying his attention to rescue and protect the world;

regarding all conditioned phenomena, his mind has no attachment or reliance; observing the fundamental self-nature of all dharmas, moment after moment he flows into the ocean of omniscience, universally adorning and purifying all Buddha-lands.

With a mind that dwells nowhere among the assemblies at the bodhimaṇḍas of all Tathāgatas, he observed in this manner and gradually traveled south until he reached the country of Draviḍa. There, he entered the city of Vajrasānu and searched everywhere for the Mahāsattva Megha.

Then he saw that person in the midst of a marketplace, standing upon a high platform and seated upon a lion throne, surrounded by a multitude of ten thousand people, extensively expounding the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of the Wheel-Syllable.
Sudhana went to him, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined in reverence, said:
"Noble One! I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct."
How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
How does one transmigrate through the various realms of existence while never forgetting the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta)?
How does one attain a firm mind, diligently seeking the Buddha-dharma without weariness?
How does one obtain a pure and humble mind that cannot be destroyed?
How does one attain the power of great compassion, remaining constantly within the cycle of birth and death without wearying of toil?
How does one attain the power of dhāraṇī, so as to freely uphold the universal gate of purity?
How does one give rise to the vast light of wisdom, free from all obscurations and hindrances?
How does one attain sublime eloquence, skillfully discerning the profound treasury of the Dharma?
How does one attain the power of right mindfulness, retaining all the wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas?
How does one attain the power of pure destinies, so as to expound all dharmas and universally purify all realms of existence?
How does one attain the bodhisattva’s power of universal wisdom, such that regarding the various distinctions among all dharmas, one is able to decisively determine their true meaning?
"I only pray that you will take pity on me and explain this for my sake.
At that time, Megha said to Sudhana,
"O son of good family!
"Have you already previously resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
Sudhana replied, "Indeed, I have."
“O Mahāsattva!
I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Megha immediately descended from his lion throne; out of deep reverence for the bodhicitta, he prostrated himself before Sudhana with his five limbs touching the ground, paying homage with a single-minded devotion.
Rising from the ground, they scattered gold and silver flowers, priceless jewels, and exquisite powdered sandalwood; they further covered them with immeasurable precious robes of variegated colors.
Furthermore, he scattered countless exquisite, pure, and pleasing fragrant flowers, along with various wonderful articles of offering, as an act of worship;
thereafter, joining his palms, he praised him with a gentle voice, saying: "Excellent!
Excellent, son of good family!
You are indeed able to resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

“Good son! If there are those who are able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they are diligently seeking the wisdom of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) and thereby ensuring that the lineage of the Buddhas is not severed;
they are forever separated from the lineage of all worldly ordinary persons.”
By nature, it is to adorn and purify all the buddha-fields of all Buddhas;
it is to discipline and bring all sentient beings to maturity; it is to awaken to the nature of all phenomena and emerge from the ocean of birth and death;
it is to illuminate and understand all karmic seeds so that one has no basis for attachment; and it is to diligently cultivate all [virtuous practices].
All the sublime practices of a bodhisattva constitute having already set forth all great vows without interruption;
they constitute conforming to the sphere of practice for the abandonment of desire that leads to all-knowledge;
they constitute having attained the firm spiritual lineage of all bodhisattvas; and they constitute having already obtained the empowerment and sustaining power of all buddhas.
One who can clearly perceive all the distinctions existing throughout the three periods of time will be protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
one’s aspirations and joys will become equal to those of all Bodhisattvas in the Dharma-realm;
one will receive the praise of all worthies and sages; and one will be visited with single-minded veneration by all Brahma Kings.
They shall receive the respectful offerings of all the celestial kings; they shall receive the constant and diligent protection of all the yakṣa kings;
they shall receive the attendance and guard of all the rākṣasa kings following them;
they shall receive the welcoming and service of all the great nāga kings; and they shall receive the singing and praise of all the kiṃnara kings.
Then one will attain the shared joy and celebration of all lords of the world, and cause the entire realm of sentient beings to obtain peace and security.
That is to say:

It causes the severing of all transmigration through the evil destinies; it causes the relinquishing of all places of suffering and hardship; it causes the cessation of all roots of poverty; it causes the arising of all happiness among humans and devas; it causes the attainment of proximity to and the making of offerings to all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); it causes the attainment of hearing, receiving, and upholding the vast Dharma of all Buddhas; it enables the cultivation and accumulation of all bodhisattva factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*); it enables the growth of the roots and sprouts of all meritorious and wholesome dharmas; it enables the perfuming and awakening of the seeds of all bodhisattvas' untainted wisdom (*anāsravajñāna*); it enables the light of wisdom to universally illumine all paths of differentiated knowledge; and it enables one to ultimately abide upon the bodhisattva’s ground of true wisdom.
“Good son! Thus, such bodhisattvas are difficult to appear in the world and difficult to encounter;
all that they do is difficult to discern and difficult to understand.”
They are able to perform extremely difficult deeds for the sake of sentient beings;
yet, to actually behold them is even more difficult. Why is this?
When Bodhisattvas appear in the world, they bring great benefit to all sentient beings:
like parents, they nurture, comfort, and bring them to fulfillment;
like necklaces, they adorn all devas and humans.
Like a shipmaster, for he ferries sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death;
like a dwelling, for he shelters and protects all worlds;
like a caravan leader, for he can guide the multitudes of living beings to the place of jewels.
Like the blazing sun, for the light of his wisdom can shine everywhere;
like a sovereign, for he has attained mastery within the city of the awakened Dharma;
like a raging fire, for he can burn away the fuel of sentient beings' craving for self.
Like a great cloud, because it universally pours down boundless rain of ambrosia;
like seasonal rain, because it causes the sprouts of wholesome roots such as faith to grow;
like a ship, because it transports sentient beings to reach the other shore.
They are like bridges, for they enable sentient beings to cross over and transcend birth and death;
they are like ferries, for they reveal all paths of deliverance;
they are like wind-circles, for they sustain sentient beings so as not to let them fall into the three evil realms.
Like the great earth, because it is able to cause all the roots of goodness of all sentient beings to grow;
like the great ocean, because it possesses the inexhaustible treasury of merit and wisdom;
like the full moon, because it universally radiates the light of wisdom to shatter the darkness of afflictions and bestow coolness.
Like a valiant general, they are able to utterly crush and subdue all demonic armies, causing them to retreat and disperse;
like Mount Sumeru, their superior wisdom and roots of goodness transcend the deep and vast ocean of birth and death.
At that time, Megha extensively praised and revealed to Sudhana the great power of the merit of generating the bodhicitta, causing the entire assembly to give rise to joy;
they cried out with one voice, "Excellent!"
Excellent! O son of good family!
Now, because this assembly has seen a superior person and heard of the bodhisattva’s meritorious practices and vows, they leap for joy and exultation, unable to contain themselves.
At that time, Megha returned to his original seat and emitted various kinds of light from the gate of his face, which universally illuminated the trichiliocosm.

At that moment, all the great Brahma kings, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—these kings along with their retinues—were illumined by the radiance and there was none who did not assemble.

At that time, the Great Being observed the minds of the assembly; they had all conceived a sense of reverence, were free from all flattery and arrogance, their minds were tranquil, and their intentions were gentle and compliant. According to their inclinations and desires, he extensively analyzed, revealed, and explained the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of the Chapter on the Syllable *Cakra*.
Having heard this Dharma, those sentient beings believed, followed, and attained realization, all becoming non-retrogressive in their progress toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having performed what was to be done, he addressed Sudhana, saying: "Good son!

I have accomplished the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of the *Ghoṣavatī* Dhāraṇī; in a single thought-moment, I am able to discern and know all the distinctions and secrets of the languages of the gods of the desire and form realms throughout the trichiliocosm."
He understands the secret distinctions of all the various languages of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans;
he also knows the secrets of the mental inclinations and the various diverse desires of all those sentient beings.
That is to say:
they thoroughly understand the secret distinctions in the mental inclinations of the Brahma Kings and the various Brahma assemblies of the Form Realm;
they also know the secret distinctions in the mental inclinations of the great celestial kings, sons of gods, and goddesses of the Desire Realm.
He also knows the secret distinctions in the mental inclinations of the nāgas and others, including their male and female human and non-human retinues;

he is also able to know all the stages of the paths and fruits of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas within this trichiliocosm, as well as the various practices of all bodhisattva vows and stages, and the secret distinctions in their subtle intentions;
furthermore, regarding all verbal expressions, analytical explanations, and the discernment of textual meanings, there is nothing he does not clearly understand.

They are also able to fully comprehend how the Buddhas of the three periods of time expound for all sentient beings the entire ocean of all profound dharmas, including their various modes of expression, underlying intentions, and secret meanings.

"Just as in a single thought-moment one knows the words, thoughts, practices, vows, and stages of all sentient beings and noble ones in this world, along with their respective differences and subtle secrets;

so too does one know, within ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, a million, ten million, a billion, nayutas of countless, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, uncountable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and even unspeakably unspeakable worlds in the eastern direction, the words, thoughts, practices, vows, and stages of all sentient beings and noble ones therein, along with their subtle secrets."

In the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—throughout every world that is unspeakably unspeakable in number—they fully comprehend all the subtle and secret distinctions in the speech, mental conceptions, practices, vows, and stages of all sentient beings and noble sages; there is nothing they do not penetrate.
“Good son! I know only this Dharma-gate of the Radiance of the Mantra of Wondrous Sound;
as for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, they are universally able to enter into the ocean of the various perceptions, conducts, and retinues of all sentient beings.”
They are able to universally enter the ocean of the various established designations of all sentient beings;
they are able to universally enter the ocean of the various appellations and names of all sentient beings;
they are able to universally enter the ocean of the various local dialects and languages of all sentient beings.
They are able to universally enter the ocean of all Buddhas’ profound and secret phrases of Dharma;
they are able to universally enter the ocean of all Buddhas’ ultimate and supreme phrases of Dharma;
they are able to universally enter the ocean of all Buddhas’ phrases of Dharma concerning all objects of focus throughout the three periods of time, as taught within a single object of focus.
They are able to universally enter into all Buddhas as they expound oceans of phrases of all superior dharmas within all languages;
