they are able to universally enter into all Buddhas as they expound oceans of phrases of all supreme dharmas within all languages;
they are able to universally enter into all Buddhas as they expound oceans of phrases of vast and diverse dharmas within all languages.
They are able to universally enter into all Buddhas’ oceans of phrases for skillfully taming beings through all varieties of speech, as they expound them;
they are able to universally enter into all Buddhas’ oceans of various secret mantras and diverse terminology as they expound them throughout all worlds;
and they are able to universally enter into the limits of the sounds and languages of all kinds of sentient beings in all worlds.
They are able to universally enter the pure wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas, reaching the limit of perfect adornment;
they are able to universally enter the various wheels of syllables of all worlds, universally giving rise to and manifesting the limits of all dharmas.
"Regarding such wisdom, merit, and conduct of a bodhisattva, how could I possibly know or describe it? 'Good son!
To the south from here there is a village named Vanavāsin. There lives an elder named Vimuktipratiṣṭhita; go to him and ask how a bodhisattva practices and accumulates the bodhisattva path.'"
How does a bodhisattva give rise to the virtues of a bodhisattva?
How does a bodhisattva accomplish the practices of a bodhisattva?
How does a bodhisattva contemplate the dharmas of a bodhisattva?
At that time, the youth Sudhana, having been deeply instructed and exhorted by his spiritual friend, conceived profound respect for the Dharma of omniscience;
his faith and delight in all roots of goodness increased;
and his diligent application toward all Buddha-dharmas redoubled.
In accordance with all the instructions of his spiritual mentors, he universally followed them.
He prostrated at Megha’s feet, weeping with tears streaming down, circumambulated him countless times, gazed upon him with longing and veneration, and then took his leave to travel south.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Five;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra, by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation and the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra.

At that time, the youth Sudhana reflected in accordance with the truth, single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting those subtle and wondrous eloquences and the dharma-gates adorned by those bodhisattvas;
he single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting the teachings expressed through the speech of those bodhisattvas.
O Ocean, focus your mind single-mindedly on the subtle skillful means of those bodhisattvas;
focus your mind single-mindedly on the pure liberation of those bodhisattvas; focus your mind single-mindedly on the radiance of the roots of goodness of those bodhisattvas;
focus your mind single-mindedly on the pure expertise of those bodhisattvas; focus your mind single-mindedly on those...
The Bodhisattva’s wisdom for gathering sentient beings consists of single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting the vast power of wisdom of those bodhisattvas;
single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting the courageous and non-retrogressive nature of those bodhisattvas;

single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting the sublime aspirations and inclinations of those bodhisattvas; and single-mindedly and exclusively recollecting the immeasurable merits of those bodhisattvas. One—
With a mind single-mindedly focused on those bodhisattvas' unimpeded Dharma-gates, he reflects in this way:
with firm and steadfast great vows, he takes courageous diligence as his armor; adorned constantly by the power of right faith, he zealously seeks the true Dharma without weariness of heart;
his aspiration is as firm as a vajra or Nārāyaṇa, such that none can destroy it.
He constantly and uninterruptedly practices in accordance with the instructions of all spiritual friends;

his mind remains unstained by any sensory objects, and the wondrous practices of the universal gate manifest before him. With the light of wisdom from the Universal Eye, he illuminates the ocean of all phenomena, perfects the dharani-gates of the various stages, perceives the ten directions, and comprehends the ultimate limits of all dharmas.

Adorned universally with unimpeded wisdom, they realize and understand the pure, non-reliant nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); they manifest the dharma-gate of non-opposition and non-duality, transcending all to reach the supreme further shore. Entering the gateway of pure wisdom, they are forever free from all conceptualizations;

they are able to scrutinize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of all phenomena, universally know the distinct dharma-gates of the three periods of time, travel universally to the distinct worlds of the ten directions, see universally the distinct bodies of Buddhas in the ten directions, enter universally into the distinct eons and kalpas of the ten directions, observe universally the distinct natures of karma in the ten directions, and universally turn the distinct wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas. With the light of the Samādhi of Universal Wisdom illuminating their minds, their minds constantly enter the realm of universal equality.
The light of the Tathāgata’s wisdom shines upon their bodies, and the flow of all-knowledge continues without interruption;
whether in body or mind, they possess sovereign power and never abandon any of the Buddha-dharmas.
By the power of deep faith, they are constantly sustained by the majestic spiritual authority of all Buddhas;
by the power of pure wisdom, they are illumined by the light of all Tathāgatas;
and by the power of their vows, they aspire for their bodies to pervade the entire network of lands and all realms of reality, universally entering into them.
Traveling by stages, he reached the city of Vanavāsin after twelve years. There, he searched everywhere for the elder Vimokṣaka.
Having found him, he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground at the elder's feet; rising up with palms joined, he addressed him, saying: "Noble One!"
That I have now been able to meet with a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) is a vast and great benefit I have obtained. Why is this?

A spiritual friend is difficult to appear, difficult to hear the name of, difficult to encounter, difficult to draw near to, difficult to receive as a mentor, difficult to dwell with, difficult to serve, difficult to please, difficult to receive instruction from, and difficult to follow.
"I have now encountered a true spiritual friend; this is the attainment of my most supreme and wholesome benefit—thus, it is the most difficult among difficulties. "Noble One!"
I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to encounter the arising of all Buddhas,
desiring to universally hear the names of all Buddhas, desiring to universally behold the bodies of all Buddhas,
desiring to universally visit all Buddha-fields, and desiring to universally enter into one...
Because of the assembly of all Buddhas; because of the desire to universally observe the realms of all Buddhas; because of the desire to universally know the intentions of all Buddhas;
because of the desire to universally receive the predictions of enlightenment from all Buddhas; because of the desire to universally uphold the power of all Buddhas;
because of the desire to universally serve all Buddhas; and because of the desire to realize awakening—into one...
In order to encompass all Buddha-dharmas; in order to accord with the minds of all Buddhas;
in order to fulfill the vows of all Buddhas; in order to attain all samādhis; in order to illuminate the wisdom of all Buddhas;
in order to adorn the assemblies of all Buddhas; and in order to universally cultivate all...
Because of the Buddha’s fundamental practices; because he desires to manifest and behold the supernatural powers of all Buddhas;
because he desires to fully realize the power of the wisdom of all Buddhas; because he desires to purify the fearlessnesses of all Buddhas; because he desires to hear all Buddha-dharmas;
because he desires to receive and uphold the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas; and because he desires to analyze and distinguish the One...
Because they wish to encompass all Buddha-dharmas; because they wish to maintain and uphold the ocean of the Buddhas' teachings; because they wish to guard the dharma-city of the Buddhas;
because they wish to observe the dharmas realized by the Buddhas; because they wish to understand and awaken to the dharmas realized by the Buddhas;
because they wish to enter deeply into the dharmas known by the Buddhas; and because they wish to see all things.
Because the Buddha-dharma is born within one's own person; because one desires to be of the same essence as all bodhisattvas;
because one desires to be of the same kind as all bodhisattvas; because one desires to equalize the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas;
because one desires to contemplate what all bodhisattvas study; because one desires to be identical with all bodhisattvas...
Because of their pure conduct, they desire to accomplish all that is practiced by bodhisattvas;
because they desire to fulfill all the pāramitās of bodhisattvas; because they desire to give rise to all the pure vows of bodhisattvas;
because they desire to enter the ocean of all the great vows of bodhisattvas; because they desire to be endowed with all the greatness of bodhisattvas...
By the power of compassion, for the sake of reaching the ultimate state of all bodhisattvas;
for the sake of obtaining the treasury of the various majestic spiritual powers of all buddhas and bodhisattvas;
for the sake of obtaining the inexhaustible treasury of the light of wisdom of all bodhisattvas; and for the sake of obtaining the vast merit of all bodhisattvas.
Because it is the treasury of samādhi; because he desires to obtain the treasury of the immeasurable power of all bodhisattvas;
because he desires to obtain the treasury of the immeasurable supernormal powers of all bodhisattvas;
because he desires to obtain the inexhaustible treasury of the great miraculous transformations of all bodhisattvas; because he desires to obtain all bodhisattvas...
Because the treasury of great sovereignty is ever-present; because one desires to adorn oneself by attaining the pure and wondrous treasury of the physical form of all bodhisattvas;
and because one desires to attain the treasury of the great compassion of all bodhisattvas in order to teach and transform sentient beings so that they may all ultimately reach the other shore.

“Noble One! With such a mind, such an intention, such a longing, such a diligent seeking, such a reflection, such a yearning, such a reverence, such a skillful means, such valor, such ultimate dedication, and such humility, I have come into the presence of the noble one, my spiritual friend.”

I have heard that the Holy One is well able to instruct and exhort the assembly of bodhisattvas; he can, through skillful means, open up the realm of the Buddha, show them the path, point out the ferry crossing, provide them with the bridge, and grant them the boat and raft.
Universally causing all beings to sever the net of ignorance, remove the obstacles of perversion, extract the arrows of doubt,
wash away the stains of affliction, illuminate the dense forest of the mind, shatter the mind's deluded attachments, purify the mind, rectify the mind’s crookedness,
eliminate the mind’s feverish distress, and cause the mind to become cool, thereby turning back the flow of birth and death and proceeding toward...
The path to nirvāṇa causes the mind to distance itself from the prison of all views;

it causes the mind to be liberated from the fetters of craving and attachment toward defiled objects of affection; it causes the mind to move forward, accord with, and enter into the nature of omniscience;
it causes one to swiftly reach the great city of the Dharma; and it causes one’s unsurpassed great compassion to become firm and secure.
Abiding in ultimate great compassion, they cause [beings] to initiate all bodhisattva practices, cause them to cultivate all gateways of samādhi,
cause them to awaken to and enter the stages realized by the noble ones, cause them to contemplate the fundamental nature of all phenomena,
and cause them to increase the power of Samantabhadra’s vows, maintaining a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings.

I only pray that you will, out of compassion, explain for me how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path, so that through such cultivation, one may swiftly attain purity, swiftly attain clarity, and achieve complete fulfillment.

At that time, by the power of the roots of goodness accumulated by the householder Vimukta in the past, by the power of the Tathāgata’s present majestic spiritual authority, by the power of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta’s mindfulness, and by the empowerment of the power of the original vows and practices of all the spiritual friends in the ten directions, he immediately entered a supreme gate of bodhisattva samādhi called the *Sarvabuddhakṣetrānantasaṃgraha-vartanī-dhāraṇī*.

Having entered this samādhi, his body became pure and its radiance was brilliantly penetrating. Within his body appeared the Buddhas of the ten directions—each numbering as many as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields—as well as their Buddha-fields, their pure and wondrous adornments, their assemblies, their sites of enlightenment, and their radiance;

he also manifested the various bodhisattvas who had practiced together with those Buddhas in the past, the supernatural transformations they had displayed in the past, the vast vows they had made in the past, the factors conducive to enlightenment they had cultivated in the past, the paths of renunciation they had purified in the past, all their pure adornments in the past, and all the bodhisattva practices they had cultivated in the past.
Furthermore, he saw those Buddhas attaining equal and perfect enlightenment, turning the sublime wheel of Dharma, and teaching and transforming sentient beings.
All of these appear clearly within his body without any obstruction.
Furthermore, he universally manifests his body within all the lands inside his body, pervading them all without exception;

his body and the Buddha-lands interpenetrate one another without mutual hindrance. Though there are various forms and images, they neither come nor go; each remains distinct and in its proper order, without being confused or intermingled.
That is to say:

the various distinct adornments of diverse Buddha-fields; the various assemblies with their retinues fully perfected; the various modes of deportment, reverence, and offerings; and the various sites of enlightenment, each uniquely decorated.

Within them, the Buddhas manifest various playful supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), establish various distinct paths of vehicles (*yāna*), reveal various gates of vast vows, and universally adorn them with various spiritual powers (*prabhāva*).
In some worlds, he manifests his ascent to the Tuṣita heaven to perform buddha-work;
in other worlds, he passes away from the Tuṣita heaven and descends into a royal palace to perform buddha-work;
or he manifests various miraculous transformations while dwelling in the womb.
In some instances, he manifests various auspicious signs of birth;
in others, he manifests various childhood games;
and in yet others, he shows himself as a youth dwelling within the inner palace.
Sometimes they manifest leaving the household life to demonstrate the practice of asceticism;
sometimes they proceed to the tree of awakening and sit at the site of enlightenment;
or they manifest supernatural powers to shatter the hosts of Māra.
Some manifest the attainment of the unsurpassed path through sovereign mastery;
some manifest as various kings requesting the preaching of the Dharma;
and some manifest accepting invitations to turn the sublime wheel of the Dharma.
Sometimes he manifests being respectfully surrounded by devas, nāgas, gandharvas, and others who constantly follow and protect him;
sometimes he manifests his body entering all realms of existence;
and sometimes he goes to the abodes of all sentient beings.
At times, having manifested the completion of the work of saving sentient beings, he enters parinirvāṇa, so as to cause all in the world to increase their longing and affection;
or he manifests whole-body or fragmented bodily relics (śarīra), distributing them among humans and devas to inspire the cultivation of merit and blessings;
or he erects great stūpas and temples throughout the realms of humans and devas, adorning the lands and benefiting sentient beings.

Those Tathāgatas, within the oceans of all such sentient beings— across various worlds, various realms of rebirth, various classes, various assemblies, various faculties, various inclinations, various karmic actions, various convictions, various powers of the faculties, various practices, various vows, various awakenings, various thoughts, and various afflictions along with their latent tendencies and habitual patterns—
manifest great supernatural powers through the Buddha’s majestic power, performing the work of Buddhas everywhere in all places.

That is to say: sometimes they dwell in a site of enlightenment the size of a single atom; sometimes in a site of enlightenment of boundless breadth; sometimes in a site of enlightenment the size of one *yojana*; sometimes in a site of enlightenment the size of ten *yojanas*; and even sometimes in a site of enlightenment for an assembly equal in measure to as many oceans of worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

By means of various supernormal powers, various sounds, various modes of expression, various eloquences, and various expositions, within the ocean of the noble truths of all Tathāgatas, they utter various fearless lion’s roars of great masters, expounding various oceans of sūtras for various sentient beings, revealing various gates of dhāraṇī, universally turning various wheels of the Dharma of the Tathāgatas, and universally bestowing various predictions of enlightenment upon bodhisattvas.

The Dharma gates taught by those Tathāgatas and the sounds of their speech, Sudhana was able to hear and receive them all; he remembered and retained them without forgetting, contemplating and examining them.
He also beheld the inconceivable gateways of samādhi and the sovereign spiritual transformations of those Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
At that time, after the householder Vimokṣa had manifested this sign, he arose calmly from samādhi and addressed the youth Sudhana, saying: "O noble son!
I have already attained mastery in entering and emerging from this profound liberation door of Unobstructed Adornment. "Good son!

While I abide in this liberation door, I see in the eastern direction the world-system of Jambūnada-gold Radiance, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nāgeśvararāja is surrounded by his assembly at the site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Vairocanagarbha as the foremost."

Furthermore, he saw in the southern direction the world called Swiftly Endowed with All Powers, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Universal Pervading Fragrance King was surrounded by a great assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Mind-King as the leader;

he also saw in the western direction the world called Perfect Light of All Fragrances, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sumeru Lamp King was surrounded by a great assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Mind as the leader;

and he also saw in the northern direction the world called Kāṣāya Banner, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vajra Firmness was surrounded by a great assembly at his site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Vajra-Walking Valiant Practice as the leader.

Furthermore, he saw the world of All Supreme and Wondrous Jewels in the northeast, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana of the Sphere Beyond Attainment was surrounded by a great assembly at his place of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Subtle Transformation Beyond Attainment as the leader;

he also saw the world of Sovereign Fragrant Flame Light-Sound in the southeast, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha King of Fragrant Lamps was surrounded by a great assembly at his place of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Wondrous Causes of Vajra-Flame Wisdom as the leader.

Furthermore, in the southwest direction, he saw the world-system named Universal Radiance of the Wisdom-Sun Flames, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana Universal Wisdom Sound was surrounded by his assembly at the site of enlightenment; there, the Bodhisattva Incense-Flower-Light Manifestation with Universally Blazing Topknot was the leader.

Furthermore, in the northwest direction, he saw the world-system named Treasury Adorned with Universally Pure Sublime Fragrance, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Infinite Merit Ocean Banner Perfect Light was surrounded by his assembly at the site of enlightenment; there, the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Power Body Wisdom Banner King was the leader.

Furthermore, I saw in the direction below the Lion-Leaping-Flame Liberation Radiance World, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Unobstructed Dharma-Dimension Banner Endowed with Wisdom Flame-Radiance, surrounded by his assembly at the site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Dharma-Dimension Wisdom Flame Radiance Pervading the World Banner as the leader;

and I saw in the direction above the Radiance Pervading Successively Appearing Inexhaustible Buddha World, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nameless Boundless Unobstructed Wisdom Perfect Radiance Banner King, surrounded by his assembly at the site of enlightenment, with the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Power of Diligence Dharma-Dimension Wisdom Banner King as the leader.

“Good son! I see these ten Buddha-Bhagavāns as my leaders, and likewise, I see as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions, surrounded by their assemblies at their places of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). Each one has a leading Bodhisattva together with his retinue, all clearly manifest;
yet none of those Tathāgatas from all those worlds come here, nor do I go to them.”
“Good son! If I wish to see the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the Land of Peace and Bliss, I see him at will;

if I wish to see the Tathāgata Candrabuddhi of the world White Sandalwood Fragrance, the Tathāgata Ratnaprabhāsa of the world Exquisite Fragrance, the Tathāgata Ratnapadmaprabha of the world Lotus, the Tathāgata Śāntiprabha of the world Exquisite Golden Light, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the world Abhirati, the Tathāgata Siṃhalakṣaṇa of the world Well-Abiding, the Tathāgata Candrabuddhi of the world Mirror-Light, or the Tathāgata Vairocana of the world Auspicious Lion Jewel Adornment, I see them at will.”
Thus, regarding all the Tathāgatas in all worlds throughout the ten directions, if I wish to see them, I see them immediately according to my will;
yet those Tathāgatas do not come here, nor do I go there.

“Good son! If I wish to see all the Buddhas throughout every kalpa from the limit of the past, as well as their variously adorned buddha-fields, assemblies at the sites of enlightenment, and their supernatural transformations for the sake of taming sentient beings;

and if I wish to see all the Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas throughout the ocean of all kalpas until the limit of the future, as well as their adorned lands, assemblies at the sites of enlightenment, and their supernatural transformations for the sake of taming sentient beings;”
In this way, all these recollections were seen:

those Tathāgatas and those kalpas, as well as all the adornments and various distinctions of every Buddha-field. Although they did not come to the present, and my own mind did not enter into that past or future, what was seen by me was entirely as if it were the present.

“Good son! I am able to fully know all matters concerning the adornments of the lands and the spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time; they come from nowhere and go nowhere, they have no place of movement and no place of abiding. Furthermore, I know that my own body neither comes nor goes, and has no place of movement or abiding.”

Why is this? Because they know that all Buddhas and their own minds are like dreams; just as what is seen in a dream arises from conceptual discrimination, they see that all Buddhas arise from their own minds.
Furthermore, they know their own mind to be like water in a vessel, and they realize that all phenomena are like reflections in water.
Furthermore, one knows that one's own mind is like a magical illusion, and that all phenomena are like the products of such an illusion;

one also knows that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are like echoes—just as an empty valley produces an echo in accordance with sound—and thus awakens to the understanding that one's own mind, following one's thoughts, perceives the Buddhas. Knowing this and recollecting it in this way, I realize that all the Buddhas I perceive arise solely from my own mind.

"Good son! You should know that when Bodhisattvas cultivate all Buddha-dharmas, purify all Buddha-fields, accumulate sublime practices, subdue sentient beings, give rise to great vows, enter into omniscience, sport with mastery in the inconceivable dharma-gates of liberation, attain the Bodhi of the Buddhas, manifest great supernormal powers, and travel everywhere throughout all dharma-realms of the ten directions—using subtle wisdom to universally enter all kalpas—all such dharmas of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas arise solely from their own minds."
“Good son! All karmas are illusory;
their accumulation is called the mind (citta). The manas deliberates, the manovijñāna discriminates, and the five consciousnesses, such as the visual consciousness, perceive objects differently.”
Ignorant ordinary beings are unable to awaken to this; fearing old age, sickness, and death, they seek to enter nirvana.
Failing to recognize either saṃsāra or nirvāṇa, they give rise to false discrimination regarding all objects.

Furthermore, because the future sense faculties and the five sensory objects are extinguished, ordinary and ignorant people take this to be *nirvāṇa*; however, when Buddhas and Bodhisattvas realize awakening for themselves, they transform the *ālayavijñāna* to attain the wisdom of original enlightenment (*mūlajñāna*).

"Good son! All ordinary and ignorant people are deluded regarding the Buddha’s skillful means; they cling to the existence of the three vehicles and fail to understand that the triple world arises from the mind. They do not know that all the Buddha-dharmas of the three periods of time are the manifestation of one's own mind. Seeing the five external sense-objects, they grasp them as being truly existent, like oxen and sheep who cannot awaken; thus, within the wheel of birth and death, there is no way for them to escape."
“Good son! The Buddha teaches that all dharmas are without arising and without cessation, and they likewise have no three periods of time. Why is this?
It is because the five sensory objects, which appear as manifestations of one’s own mind, are fundamentally non-existent.”
Because all phenomena, whether existent or non-existent, are fundamentally unarisen— like the horns of a rabbit—
the realm of self-realization by the noble ones is thus.
O son of good family!

Ignorant ordinary beings give rise to false discrimination, grasping at existence within non-existence and grasping at non-existence within existence; they seize upon the various manifestations of the ālayavijñāna and fall into the two views of arising and ceasing, failing to understand that these are their own minds and thus giving rise to discrimination.

"Good son! You should know that one's own mind is itself the dharma of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Because one knows that one's own mind is itself the Buddha-dharma, one is then able to purify all buddha-fields and enter all kalpas."
Therefore, noble son! You should support your own mind with wholesome dharmas;

you should moisten your own mind with the rain of Dharma; you should purify your own mind with sublime dharmas; you should fortify your own mind with diligence; you should humble your own mind with patience; you should clarify your own mind with meditative concentration; you should sharpen your own mind with wisdom; you should inspire your own mind with the virtues of a Buddha; you should broaden your own mind with equanimity; and you should illuminate your own mind with the ten powers and the four fearlessnesses.
“Good son! I have only attained mastery in entering and emerging from this Dharma-door of the Tathāgata’s profound and unimpeded adornment of liberation;

whereas all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas dwell in unimpeded wisdom, practice unimpeded conduct, and are thoroughly penetrating regarding all realms of experience. They constantly manifest before them the vast samādhi that perceives all Buddhas, abide at the limit of non-extinction of all Buddhas, and realize the gateway to perfect enlightenment.”
Universally comprehending the ocean of all samādhis, they are able to contemplate all spheres of experience, wherein the phenomena of the three periods of time are entirely equal;

their emanated bodies travel throughout the ocean of all lands, entering the non-discriminative state of all Buddhas, such that all spheres of experience manifest before them; they constantly contemplate all dharmas and, with perfected wisdom, are able to fully explain and practice all the meritorious deeds and vows of Bodhisattvas; within their own bodies, they can manifest the signs of the formation and destruction of all worlds, yet they do not give rise to dualistic thoughts regarding themselves or those worlds.
How could I possibly know or describe such wondrous conduct?
“Good son! From here, traveling south to the edge of Jambudvīpa, there is a dwelling place named Samantavimala;
there dwells a bhikṣu named Sāgaradhvaja.”
"Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the elder, circumambulated him to the right, gazed upon him with contemplation, and extolled and praised his immeasurable merits;

he reflected that spiritual friends are able to provide protection and refuge, always gave rise to joy toward spiritual friends, initiated practices and vows by relying on spiritual friends, realized awakening through spiritual friends, revered spiritual friends with a mind free of opposition, served spiritual friends without flattery or deception, and followed spiritual friends with a mind of constant compliance.

He conceived of the spiritual friend as a compassionate mother, thinking, "May she lead me away from all perversions," and he conceived of the spiritual friend as a compassionate father, thinking, "May she enable me to accomplish the wholesome dharmas of a bodhisattva.
Reflecting thus, he felt a profound sense of love and joy; weeping with tears streaming down his face, he took his leave and departed.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded right mindfulness, followed the instructions of that elder, observing them accordingly and practicing as he had been taught.

I remember and uphold that inconceivable gate of liberation of Bodhisattvas; I contemplate that inconceivable gate of the light of wisdom; I enter deeply into that inconceivable gate of the sequence of the Dharma-realm; I awaken to and understand that inconceivable gate of universal entry into all dharmas; I clearly behold those inconceivable spiritual transformations of the Tathāgatas; I observe those inconceivable universal entries into Buddha-lands; I have deep faith in those inconceivable adornments of the Buddha’s power; I illuminate and manifest those inconceivable samādhis of Bodhisattvas; I thoroughly comprehend those inconceivable differentiated worlds; I cultivate and accumulate those inconceivable pure karmas of Bodhisattvas; and I give rise to those inconceivable, vast, and great vows.
Observing in this manner, he gradually traveled south toward the village of Vimala on the edge of Jambudvīpa, searching everywhere for the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.

He then saw him at the side of a forest for walking meditation, sitting cross-legged with body upright and mindfulness established; having transcended inhalation and exhalation, free from discursive thoughts, he dwelt in an inconceivable, vast samādhi, manifesting great supernormal powers through the power of that samādhi.

Upon his body, from crown to feet, in all its limbs and every pore, there appeared infinite and inconceivable numbers of clouds of bodies identical in appearance to his own; these manifested throughout all places as all bodies: for the sake of making universal offerings to all Tathāgatas; for the sake of universally purifying all Buddha-fields; for the sake of universally bringing all Bodhisattvas to maturity;

for the sake of universally taming and subduing all sentient beings; for the sake of universally rescuing and extracting them from the mass of sufferings; for the sake of universally severing the three evil destinies; for the sake of universally revealing the path of humans and devas; for the sake of universally eliminating the poison of afflictions; for the sake of causing sentient beings to universally enter the profound ocean of wisdom; and for the sake of causing sentient beings to ultimately abide in omniscience.

From beneath the two feet of the Buddha, there issued forth clouds of bodies resembling those of countless multitudes of elders, householders, and brahmins, as numerous as the atoms within infinite buddha-fields. They wore flower crowns upon their heads, draped necklaces over their bodies, and bound bright pearls upon their crests; they were adorned with magnificent robes and accompanied by retinues of immeasurable youths.
They traveled everywhere to all worlds throughout the ten directions, universally bestowing all manner of supreme and exquisite offerings upon all sentient beings.
That is to say:

universally raining down all kinds of superior-flavored food and drink in accordance with the Dharma; all kinds of exquisite, multicolored jewel-flowers; all garments; all necklaces and ornaments; all garlands and sashes; all incenses; all unguents; all precious vessels; all palatial dwellings; and all requisites for the enjoyment of desires;
thereby rescuing and gathering in all impoverished sentient beings everywhere, providing for their needs and causing them to be fully satisfied.
He comforts all sentient beings afflicted by suffering, enabling them to attain physical and mental bliss and bringing them joy;
he brings to maturity all sentient beings who possess roots of goodness, making their minds supple and pure, leading them ultimately to the path of unsurpassed Bodhi;
thus he manifests himself, filling the ten directions.

From his two knees there emerged countless hundreds of thousands of millions of clouds of bodies resembling those of kṣatriyas and brahmins together with their retinues; all were wise and possessed every art and craft, being thoroughly proficient in both worldly and world-transcending matters. With various complexions, various forms, and various garments, they were magnificently adorned and pervaded all worlds throughout the ten directions, constantly gathering in sentient beings through the four means of attraction.
That is to say:
providing wealth and treasures so that they may be prosperous and happy; using agreeable speech so that they hear it with joy; or exhorting and guiding them through shared activities;

thus making all who are poor sufficient, healing those who are ill, bringing safety to those in peril, stopping the fear of those who are terrified, and causing those with sorrow and suffering to find happiness.

Furthermore, by means of skillful expedients, he causes them all to resolve their minds [on enlightenment], bestows upon them the True Dharma, and leads them to awakening. He swiftly causes them to abandon all unwholesome states and accumulate all wholesome dharmas. He rescues them from the mire of birth and death, leading them out so that they may abide in the fearless state of ultimate reality; thus he manifests himself, filling the ten directions.

From his navel wheel issued forth clouds of bodies resembling those of various sages from diverse paths, equal in number to all sentient beings; they possessed various forms and distinct ornaments, some wearing garments of grass and others clothing themselves in tree bark, all holding water-pots and maintaining a serene and tranquil demeanor.

Accompanied by a multitude of sages, they traversed the void by foot, traveling back and forth throughout the worlds of the ten directions. All of them produced immeasurable sounds of song and praise, extolling all the merits of the Buddhas, or lauding the pure conduct practiced by Bodhisattvas, the wondrous Dharma they preached, and the purity they realized. Their voices were harmonious and elegant, beautiful and crystal clear; heard universally throughout the ten directions without obstruction, they tamed and matured all sentient beings. They universally gathered in their faculties to prevent negligence, leading them to observe the realm of reality.
Some spoke of how all phenomena lack intrinsic nature, causing them to give rise to the mind of omniscience and establishing them in the ultimate path of truth.
Others spoke of worldly discourse concerning livelihoods.
In some instances, they manifest as local rulers to guide the customs and rituals of the people;
through various skillful means, they transform and deliver beings according to what is appropriate.

They open the gateway to the essential Dharma of all-knowledge, causing all sentient beings to universally obtain benefit, so that each may cultivate their respective practice according to their sequence. Manifesting in this way, they fill the ten directions.

From his two flanks there emerged inconceivable and countless clouds of bodies resembling those of dragon kings, dragon sons, and dragon daughters, along with their retinues; they manifested inconceivable supernatural transformations of dragons, filling the entirety of space.
That is to say:
raining clouds of inconceivable precious incense adornments, clouds of inconceivable precious flower adornments,
clouds of inconceivable precious garland adornments, clouds of inconceivable precious parasol adornments, and inconceivable...
Clouds of adornments of precious banners; clouds of adornments of inconceivable precious streamers;
clouds of adornments of various kinds of exquisite precious necklaces; clouds of adornments of inconceivable great *maṇi* jewel-kings;
clouds of adornments of inconceivable various precious thrones; clouds of adornments of inconceivable celestial precious ornaments.

Clouds of the adornment of inconceivable celestial jewel palaces; clouds of the adornment of inconceivable songs and praises by devas and celestial maidens; clouds of the adornment of inconceivable nets of celestial jewel beads;
clouds of the adornment of inconceivable mani-jewel stalks, leaves, pedestals, and calyxes of precious lotuses; inconceivable... one [cloud].
Clouds of adornments consisting of crowns of all kinds of mani-jewels; clouds of celestial jewel adornments with inconceivable and boundless flames of light;
clouds of celestial body adornments consisting of inconceivable flower garlands, banners, and canopies;
clouds of celestial maidens who offer inconceivable reverence with palms joined; and clouds of golden lotuses that contain radiance and emit flames.
Inconceivable clouds of great sound proclaiming the merits of all Buddhas;
such as these pervade the entirety of space as adornments, universally making offerings at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Universally causing all sentient beings to give rise to joy, removing the fever of afflictions, and attaining the bliss of coolness, he thus manifested these throughout the ten directions.

From the mark of auspiciousness upon his chest, there emerged clouds of bodies resembling innumerable asura kings and their retinues, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields; they all manifested inconceivable powers of skillful illusion and various spiritual transformations that filled the void of space.
That is to say:

it can cause immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of worlds to tremble all over; all the kings of mountains strike against one another; all the oceans surge and boil violently; the palaces of the devas shake without exception; the radiance of all Māras is obscured; and the hosts of Māra’s armies are subdued without exception;

it causes all sentient beings everywhere to abandon arrogance and pride, to have no heedlessness in mind, to remove the stains of stinginess and jealousy, to cease all resentment and harm, to universally give rise to a heart of loving-kindness, to shatter the mountains of affliction, to dry up the ocean of craving and desire, to long increase freedom from strife, and to forever dwell in harmony and goodness.

Furthermore, by means of the power of illusion and the play of supernatural faculties, they awaken all living beings, causing them to abandon greedy attachment; they constantly delight in remaining far removed from all unwholesome dharmas, fearing birth and death while joyfully seeking liberation.

They cause them to transcend all worldly realms of existence, to abide in the mind of unsurpassed bodhicitta, to cultivate the pure and wondrous conduct of bodhisattvas, to advance upon the path of the bodhisattva pāramitās, to enter all the stages of the bodhisattvas, to illuminate the subtle and wondrous Dharma-gates of the bodhisattvas, and to contemplate the skillful means and expedients of the bodhisattvas.
In this manner, he manifested throughout the entire dharma-realm.

From his back, there issued forth clouds of bodies resembling those of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields of atoms in number—consisting of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas—which extensively expounded the essential teachings for all sentient beings who were to be transformed by the two vehicles, thereby bringing them to subdual.

That is to say: for those who cling to a self, he teaches that there is no self; for those who cling to permanence, he teaches the impermanence of conditioned formations; for those whose temperament is dominated by greed, he teaches the contemplation of impurity; for those whose temperament is dominated by hatred, he teaches the contemplation of loving-kindness; for those whose temperament is dominated by delusion, he teaches the contemplation of dependent origination; and for those with balanced temperaments, he teaches objects corresponding to wisdom.
By means of these specific remedies, he causes them to engage in universal observation.

For those who give rise to attachment toward sense objects, he teaches the nature of non-existence that is free from all attachments; for those who are universally mired in the five sensory desires, he teaches the nature of non-attachment that is free from all desires; and for those bound by attachment to tranquil meditative concentrations, he teaches the gateway of great vows to cause them to develop deep love and joy.
I vow to universally benefit all sentient beings by turning the wheel of Dharma;
until the end of the future, I shall cause the aspirations of all sentient beings to be fulfilled, pervading the entire dharma-realm in this manner.

From his two shoulders issued forth yakṣa and rākṣasa kings, as numerous as the atoms in incalculable buddha-fields, possessing various forms and appearances, diverse colors and features, varying in height, length, and breadth, with diverse demeanors, fierce and majestic power, and most terrifying to behold, each surrounded by immeasurable retinues.

Manifesting various supernormal powers and uttering various great roars, they employ various skillful means as appropriate, pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions to protect all sentient beings who practice wholesome deeds, as well as all worthies and sages, and the assemblies of bodhisattvas at the sites where the Dharma is preached.

All those who uphold the pure conduct of a bodhisattva and aspire to the all-encompassing right knowledge of a Tathāgata—whether they are those who are correctly established or those who are already correctly established—may at times manifest as Vajrapāṇi deities to protect the Buddhas, serve and make offerings to them, and guard their abodes;
or they may universally protect all worlds, ensuring that beings do not enter any of the evil realms.

To those who are terrified, he grants peace and security; to those who are ill, he brings recovery; to those in distress, he removes their suffering and affliction; to those with transgressions and evils, he causes them to feel self-reproach and repentance; and to those facing calamities and misfortunes, he causes them to be extinguished.

For those great-minded beings who have accumulated merit and wisdom, may they be able to turn the wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas, abandon the wheel of birth and death, and abide in the wheel of the True Dharma; may they crush and destroy all heterodox paths and false doctrines, and may such benefits pervade all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions.

From his belly emerged as many kinnara kings as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields, each surrounded by a retinue of countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kinnara maidens; likewise, there emerged gandharva kings as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable buddha-fields, each surrounded by a retinue of countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of gandharva maidens.

Each played countless hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* celestial instruments, singing praises for the true nature of dependent origination of all phenomena; singing praises for the inconceivable merits of all Buddhas; singing praises for the universal power of generating the bodhicitta; singing praises for the perfect cultivation of practices by all Bodhisattvas; singing praises for the gateways through which all Buddhas attain perfect enlightenment; singing praises for the gateways through which all Buddhas turn the wheel of Dharma; singing praises for the gateways through which all Buddhas manifest supernatural transformations; singing praises for the gateways through which all Buddhas enter parinirvāṇa; singing praises for the gateways that protect the teachings of all Buddhas; and singing praises for the gateways that cause all sentient beings to rejoice.

They reveal and expound the gateway to purifying all Buddha-fields; they reveal and expound the subtle and wondrous Dharma-gateways of all Buddhas; they reveal and expound the gateway of unimpeded illumination of all phenomena; they reveal and expound the gateway for generating all roots of goodness;
thus do they bring benefit that fills the ten directions.

From his face issued forth as many wheel-turning sage kings (*cakravartin*) as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields; they were fully endowed with the seven treasures, surrounded by the fourfold army, and emitted the light of great renunciation. They rained down inexhaustible jewels and supreme *maṇi* gems to adorn the world, bestowing them universally upon all sentient beings to satisfy them all, causing them to sever the ten unwholesome paths and practice the ten wholesome paths.
That is to say:
to cause all cruel beings—such as those who slaughter, hunt, or fish—to give rise to compassion and refrain from taking life;

and to cause impoverished, suffering, and lowly beings to forever abandon the practice of taking what is not given, constantly practicing generosity by being able to relinquish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beautiful maidens without a single thought of stinginess.
May all sentient beings forever sever sexual misconduct and practice the pure conduct of celibacy;
may those who deceive others ultimately always speak words of truth, refraining from false, deceptive, or useless talk;
may they adopt speech that binds others together, refrain from divisive words, always delight in harmony, and never engage in discord or strife.
May those who speak harsh words be made to speak with gentleness, free from coarseness and evil;

may those who engage in frivolous speech always expound upon profound, definitive, and clear meanings, conforming to the Buddha’s teachings to benefit their practice, forever severing flowery and meaningless rhetoric, and causing all sentient beings to enter deeply into the words of the Dharma;
may those with much greed be made to have few desires, cultivating contentment, the most supreme dignity, and the right practice of non-arising.

For those who are prone to anger and harm, they cause them to eliminate hatred, so that they may constantly give rise to a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings; with minds free from blemish or defilement, he preaches great compassion for them, joyfully embracing them and leading them into the Buddha-dharma.

For those fallen into the net of views, he preaches the true meaning, causing them to contemplate all phenomena, to penetrate deeply into dependent origination, and to clearly understand the principles of the truths; he enables them to discern the correct from the false, purifies their minds, extracts the thorns of wrong views, and shatters the mountains of doubt.
He causes all sentient beings to awaken to the true nature of the mind, becoming fully proficient and penetrating the profound, such that all obstacles are completely extinguished.
Such deeds filled the entire Dharma-realm.

From his two eyes issued forth hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields, as numerous as the atoms of those vast solar discs, emitting great rays of light that universally illuminated all the great hells, causing all suffering and affliction therein to be completely extinguished;
furthermore, they illuminated the intermediate spaces between all worlds, dispelling the darkness so that light might be seen.

Furthermore, it illuminates all hungry ghosts and animals throughout the worlds of the ten directions, causing them to abandon the cataracts of ignorance and delusion, attain great wisdom, and eradicate all suffering.
Furthermore, he emitted pure light into all defiled and turbid worlds; he emitted golden light into worlds of white silver, and white silver light into worlds of gold;
he emitted crystal light into worlds of lapis lazuli, and lapis lazuli light into worlds of crystal;
he emitted agate light into worlds of musaragalva, and musaragalva light into worlds of agate.
The world of Red Pearls emits the light of the Sun-Treasury Maṇi King; the world of the Sun-Treasury Maṇi King emits the light of Red Pearls.
The world of Sapphire emits the light of the Moon-Treasury Flame-Net Maṇi Jewel King; the world of the Moon-Treasury Flame-Net Maṇi Jewel King emits the light of Sapphire.
Worlds composed of a single kind of jewel emit the light of various jewels; worlds composed of various jewels emit the light of a single kind of jewel.

In this way, that light universally illumines the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment throughout the Buddha-fields, performing the work of a Buddha; it illuminates the dense forests of the minds of all sentient beings, accomplishes the immeasurable tasks of all sentient beings, and adorns all worldly realms, causing the minds of all sentient beings to attain coolness, giving rise to great joy, peace, and happiness;
such deeds fill the entire Dharma-realm.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Six;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation," at that time,

from the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, there emerged as many Śakra-devendra kings as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields, their majestic virtue and radiance surpassing all the celestial hosts.

Having renounced all worldly desires and pleasures, they attained mastery over all sensory realms; with mani-jewels bound upon their crowns, the radiance of their bodies eclipsed the palaces of the devas, shaking all the kings of mountains, Sumerus, and awakening all the heedless hosts of devas.

They extolled the power of merit, spoke of the power of wisdom, generated the power of joy, sustained the power of resolve, increased the power of pure mindfulness, and strengthened the power of the bodhicitta they had aroused. They praised the joy of seeing the Buddha to eliminate worldly desires, praised the joy of hearing the Dharma to bring weariness toward the world, and praised the joy of contemplating wisdom to sever worldly defilements. They halted the battles of the asuras, severed the strife of afflictions, extinguished the fear of death, gave rise to the vow to subdue Māra, and established the True Dharma.
Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains, accomplishes all the activities for sentient beings, taming immeasurable beings in every thought-moment; such deeds as these pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
From his forehead emerged as many Brahma kings as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of incalculable buddha-fields.

Their physical forms were upright and majestic, peerless in the world; their deportment was tranquil, and their voices were exquisite. They entreated the Buddha to turn the wheel of Dharma, extolled the Buddha’s merits, caused the hearts of all bodhisattvas to rejoice, and were able to accomplish the immeasurable tasks of sentient beings, pervading thus the entire dharma-realm of the ten directions.

From his head emerged a multitude of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields, all of whom were adorned with the primary and secondary marks of physical perfection.

Each of those bodhisattvas emitted from every limb, joint, and pore of their bodies a universal cloud of great light, manifesting the ocean of bodhisattva practices performed by all Buddhas in the past and proclaiming the various sublime conducts of bodhisattvas. That is to say:

throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they extolled and praised the ocean of the *dāna-pāramitā* practiced by all Buddhas in the past, including the givers, the recipients, the objects given, and the oceans of corresponding and concordant practices;

They guide all stingy sentient beings to forever leave behind avarice and attachment, so that they may achieve a mind of relinquishment and constantly practice giving; they gather in sentient beings and cause them to abide in the unsurpassed *dānapāramitā*, manifesting the marks and signs (*lakṣaṇa-vyañjana*) and merits of the Buddhas so that they may attain worlds adorned with various jewels, and demonstrating the causes from which the primary and secondary environments arise, so that all sentient beings may joyfully cultivate them.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally extol and praise the *dāna-pāramitā* (perfection of giving) practiced by all Buddhas in the past, as well as the oceans of corresponding practices that accord with it;

they cause all sentient beings to develop deep revulsion for the objects of the five desires, to single-mindedly seek the realm of the Buddhas, to eliminate inverted perceptions, to constantly engage in correct reflection, to sever false discrimination, and to forever leave behind all evils; they cause them to mindfully uphold the Bodhisattva precepts, to gather in all sentient beings and establish them in great kindness and compassion, to praise liberation, to protect and maintain the ultimate category of the Tathāgata’s precepts, and to cause all sentient beings everywhere to abide in the Buddha-precepts.

He taught that all that exists is entirely like a dream, thoroughly comprehending that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty; he spoke of how sensual pleasures have no true flavor, causing all sentient beings to distance themselves from the bonds of desire and emerge from the defilements of affliction.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally extol and praise the perfection of patience practiced by all Buddhas in the past, as well as the ocean of corresponding practices that accord with it;
they cause all sentient beings to attain mastery over phenomena, mastery over the mind, and the power of forbearance;
and they extol and praise their golden physical bodies, which are free from the defilement of anger.
They give rise to compassionate conduct, cease the intent to kill, and sever the path of animal rebirth.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they proclaim and praise the past cultivation of the *pāramitās* by all Buddhas, as well as the oceans of practices that accord with and correspond to them;

they cause all bodhisattvas to be diligent and courageous, seeking the true Dharma for the sake of omniscience, making offerings to and serving all Tathāgatas, and praising them with reverence and tireless minds.
They cause all worlds to refrain from negligence, gathering in sentient beings so that they may leave behind the aggregates of suffering and enter the ocean of the Buddhas' ultimate, perfect wisdom.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they proclaim and praise the dhyāna-pāramitā practiced by all Buddhas in the past, as well as the oceans of practices that accord with and correspond to it;

they cause the obscuring veils of worldly toil to be dispersed and extinguished, forever abandon arrogance, and give rise to neither greed nor hatred. They provide the shade of cool clouds to remove the heat of afflictions, dry up the ocean of birth and death, and shatter the mountain of karmic fetters. Taming sentient beings, they establish them in the wondrous Dharma, ultimately causing their minds to attain mastery and liberation.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally extol and praise the *prajñāpāramitā* practiced by all Buddhas in the past, as well as the ocean of practices that accord with and correspond to it;

they universally radiate the lightning-flash of the wisdom of right view, causing all sentient beings to illuminate and penetrate their own fundamental nature; they universally thunder the sound of the pure, wondrous Dharma, causing all sentient beings to increase in merit and virtue, to shatter the high mountains of all pride, to extract the poisonous arrows of all views, and to decisively remove the cataracts of all doubt and confusion, so that all sentient beings may attain sovereign wisdom.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally extol and praise all Buddhas for their past cultivation of the *pāramitā* of skillful means (*upāya*), as well as the oceans of practices that accord with and correspond to them;
they act in accordance with the various activities of the world to bring all sentient beings to ultimate maturity, and although they universally subdue all beings...
Born into the world, they remain unstained by attachment toward sentient beings; though they universally illuminate the assemblies of all Buddhas, their minds have no attachment to those assemblies;
though they have transcended birth and death, they take birth with mastery within the various realms of existence;
though they manifest in the mundane world, they enter and emerge from nirvana with sovereign ease; and though they are able to fully comprehend both birth-and-death and nirvana...
While remaining non-dual and undifferentiated, they are ever skillful in benefiting sentient beings;
abiding in the perfect mastery of a bodhisattva, they transcend the world and reach the further shore.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally extol and praise all Buddhas for their past fulfillment of the perfection of vows (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*) and the ocean of corresponding practices that accord with them. They cause all bodhisattvas, until the end of the future, to ride the wheel of the four vows upon the path of perfect enlightenment, pervading the entire ocean of lands. They bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings, crushing the mountains of ignorance, tearing asunder the net of craving and desire, and untying all knots of bondage so that they are forever extinguished without remainder. They manifest various supernatural powers and transformations, causing all sentient beings to attain mastery over their lifespan.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally extol and praise all Buddhas’ past accomplishments in the perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*), as well as the oceans of practices that accord with and correspond to it;

they proclaim the great power of the Bodhisattvas’ dhāraṇīs, the power of their skillful means, Dharma-sounds, and sublime eloquence, the vast power of their vows to mature sentient beings, the sovereign power of wisdom that subdues Māras and enemies, and the fearless power of mind that restrains all non-Buddhists. Their physical strength is as firm as adamant, capable of shattering all the Great Iron Ring Mountains (*Mahācakravāḍa*), extinguishing the fires of all kalpas in the ten directions, drying up the waters of the ocean, swallowing fierce winds, and supporting all worlds within the entirety of space upon their palms without any diminution of their physical strength. They cause all sentient beings to purify their samādhis and to attain universal mastery over rebirth in all places.

Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally extol and praise all Buddhas for their past cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*), as well as the ocean of practices that accord with and correspond to it; they analytically expound the various stages of wisdom (*jñāna-bhūmi*), namely:
the stage of wisdom fully endowed with the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and all merits universally produced by all Buddhas;

the stage of wisdom fully endowed with the sovereign adornment of all the marks and signs (*lakṣaṇa-vyañjana*) universally perfected by all Buddhas; and the stage of wisdom that universally brings forth the bodhisattvas...
The stage of wisdom fully endowed with all great vows; the stage of wisdom fully endowed with the universal gathering-in of all sentient beings;
the stage of wisdom fully endowed with the universal manifestation of selflessness for the sake of sentient beings;

the stage of wisdom fully endowed with the universal observation of the various mental inclinations of all sentient beings; and the stage of wisdom fully endowed with the universal discernment of all sentient beings.

The stage of wisdom fully endowed with the distinctions of faculties and understandings; the stage of wisdom fully endowed with universal compliance with the distinctions in the faith and inclinations of all sentient beings;
the stage of wisdom fully endowed with the universal knowledge of the infinite distinctions in the ocean of profound karma of all sentient beings;
and the mind that universally enters the ocean of the infinite vows of all sentient beings.

From the uṣṇīṣa upon his crown, there emerged from within the mass of flesh as many bodies of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in immeasurable asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields; those bodies were most excellent, with nothing in the world able to equal them.

Adorned with the purity of all primary marks and secondary characteristics, his majestic radiance blazed like a mountain of pure gold, and immeasurable light shone universally throughout the ten directions.

He uttered a wondrous, perfect sound that pervaded the entire Dharma-realm and manifested immeasurable great supernormal powers. For the sake of all worlds, he rained down the rain of Dharma according to their respective needs, causing them all to obtain benefit. That is to say:
for the Bodhisattvas seated at the site of enlightenment, he rained down the great Dharma-rain named "Wisdom of Equanimous Manifestation."
For the Bodhisattvas at the stage of consecration, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called the "Universal Gateway of the Dharma Realm";
for the Bodhisattvas at the stage of Dharma Prince, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called the "Entry into the Universal Adornment Gate of All Bodhisattvas";
and for the Bodhisattvas at the stage of Youthful Truth, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called the "Great Dharma-Wisdom Cloud Abiding on the Mountain of Firmness."
For the Bodhisattvas at the stage of non-retrogression, he rains down a great Dharma rain called the Universal Adornment of the Ocean-Treasury of Equality;
for the Bodhisattvas who have accomplished the stage of the right mind, he rains down a great Dharma rain called Universally Illuminating the Realm with Vajra-Wisdom;
for the Bodhisattvas at the stage of perfection in skillful means, he rains down a great Dharma rain called the Gate of the Self-Nature Adornment that Universally Gathers All Sentient Beings.
For the bodhisattvas in the stage of birth in noble positions, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Tathāgata’s Perfect Accordance with the World";
for the bodhisattvas in the stage of practice in accordance [with reality], he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "Proclaiming the Fundamental Limit of Dharmas and Compassion for the World";
and for the bodhisattvas in the stages of mastery, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "Accumulating the Treasury of Dharma."
For the Bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds upon enlightenment, he rains down a great Dharma rain called "Universal Gathering of Sentient Beings through Equal Adornment";
for the Bodhisattvas of vast faith and understanding, he rains down a great Dharma rain called "The Inexhaustible Liberation of the Tathāgata’s Treasury of Vows";
and for the devas of the formless realm, he rains down a great Dharma rain called "The Inexhaustible Treasury of Universal-Gate Wisdom."
For the devas of the Brahma world, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called the "Inexhaustible Treasury of Universal-Gate Wisdom with the Sound of Immeasurable Teachings";
for the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called the "Inexhaustible Treasury of Dharma-Power Requisites that Can Be Produced";
and for the hosts of Māras, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called the "Various Mind-Banners Diligently Seeking All-Knowledge."
For the gods of the Nirmāṇarati heaven, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "Abiding in the Jewel of Pure Mindfulness and Wisdom through Various Skillful Bonds";
for the gods of the Tuṣita heaven, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Jewel Banner of Various Vows Arising from the Bodhisattva's Resolve";
for the gods of the Yāma heaven, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Treasury of Joy in Accordance with the Tathāgata’s Pure Mindfulness."
For the devas of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Treasury of the Joyful Adornment Born of the Rapid Vision of the Tathāgata.
For the assembly of nāga kings, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Banner of Joy from the Various Miraculous Transformations of Bodhisattvas Arising from Disgust for the Nāga Realm.

For the assembly of yakṣa kings, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Treasury of the Tathāgata’s Miraculous Transformations, Universally Pervading the Dharma Realm with Joy upon Seeing the Buddha."
For the assembly of gandharva kings, he rained down a great rain of Dharma called "The Cloud of the Collected Sounds of the Dharma of All Tathāgatas";
for the assembly of asura kings, he rained down a great rain of Dharma called "The Great Dharma Realm of the Vajra Wisdom Wheel";
and for the assembly of garuḍa kings, he rained down a great rain of Dharma called "The Birth of Boundless Radiance through the Skillful Means of All Tathāgatas."
For the assembly of Kinnara kings, they rain down a great Dharma rain named "The Supreme Cloud of Wisdom that Benefits All Worlds of All Tathāgatas";
for the assembly of Mahoraga kings, they rain down a great Dharma rain named "The Joyful and Swift Increase of the Dharma";
and for the assembly of all human kings, they rain down a great Dharma rain named "Attaining the Supreme Wisdom of All Sentient Beings."
For the sentient beings in the hells, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "Adornment of Right Mindfulness through the Sound of Tranquility";
for the sentient beings among animals, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Sound of Following the Tathāgata and Possessing the Treasury of Wisdom, Free from Paths of Evil Karma";
for the sentient beings in the realm of King Yama, he rains down a great rain of Dharma called "The Sound of Not Abandoning Sentient Beings and Giving Birth to the Perfections of the Tathāgata."

For the sake of sentient beings in places of various calamities and hardships, he rains down the great rain of Dharma called "The Universal Consolation of the Sound of Tranquility," causing all beings to forever leave behind sorrow and suffering and to enter the assemblies of the noble ones; such deeds as these fill the entire dharma-realm throughout the ten directions.
From every single pore of the body of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, there issued forth great nets of light as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields;
each individual ray of light possessed asaṃkhyeya colors and forms,
and each color and form was adorned with asaṃkhyeya ornaments.
Each and every adornment manifests incalculable realms;
within each and every realm, incalculable activities are accomplished, pervading in this manner the dharma-realm of the ten directions throughout space.

At that time, within this great net of light, Sudhana again beheld all the perfections of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) practiced by Sāgaradhvaja throughout his past lives across the three periods of time, as well as his complete practice of relinquishing all internal and external possessions.

All the *śīlapāramitā* (perfections of ethical discipline) cultivated by Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time in the past, which have been upheld since their initial resolve until the end of future kalpas—vowing to sacrifice body and life without giving rise to even a single thought of transgression.

In the past, he cultivated all the bodhisattva perfections of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*) corresponding to the three times; whether encountering harm to his head, eyes, hands, or feet, or the severing of his limbs and joints, or being reviled with evil words, he was able to accept it all with composure without any agitation.

He constantly contemplated abandoning thoughts of enmity and malice, observing that there is no mark of self (*ātman*) in his own body or the bodies of others, giving rise to great compassion to achieve all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*). By these causes and conditions, he obtained the bodhisattva’s body of sovereign form, complete with the primary and secondary marks (*lakṣaṇa-vyañjana*).

He manifested all bodies in all places, throughout all eons, undergoing all sufferings, diligently seeking the True Dharma to benefit sentient beings, never giving rise to even a single thought of weariness or retreat.
Various miraculous transformations pervade the ten directions throughout the realms of sentient beings; manifesting all bodies like shadows following forms, they fill the Dharma-realm.

These are the perfections of diligence practiced by all Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time in the past, as well as the courageous and vigorous practices free from signs studied under the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods. The various supernatural powers and transformations they manifest shake the great oceans of all worlds throughout the ten directions;

they cause all sentient beings to be diligent and untiring, to weary of the ocean of birth and death and emerge from the realm of Māra. All non-Buddhists are without exception struck with fear, and all demonic armies are without exception crushed. Their light illuminates all Dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, causing all Bodhisattvas to cultivate various practices and various miraculous transformations for the universal benefit of sentient beings.

All the dhyāna-pāramitās sought by Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time in the past—whether manifesting in various noble lineages through rebirth, or becoming kings who, upon meeting spiritual friends, gave rise to the bodhicitta, renounced their kingdoms and cities to leave the household life and study the Way, established great vows, maintained various dignified demeanors, strictly observed the prohibitions and precepts, and attained tranquility of body and mind while cultivating various meditative concentrations.

In the past, having cultivated all the Prajñāpāramitās accomplished by Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time, he diligently sought the Buddha-dharma and gave rise to a mind of right view for the sake of developing all-knowledge;

and for the sake of rescuing and delivering all sentient beings, he served spiritual friends, attending upon them and following their instructions without opposition, honoring and respecting them with deep faith, prostrating and making offerings without weariness of heart.

Diligently seeking even a single phrase of the Tathāgata’s true Dharma, they relinquish all internal and external possessions without exception; regarding their body, life, and wealth, their minds are free from stinginess. Even so is it when diligently seeking every single phrase of the Dharma. Thus, in every thought-moment until the end of the future, all their practices are performed solely for the sake of bringing all sentient beings to ultimate fulfillment in the karma of wisdom.

All the perfections of skillful means corresponding to the three periods of time, which were cultivated by Bodhisattvas in the past, enable them to universally manifest clouds of bodies resembling the physical forms of all sentient beings throughout the ocean of all realms of existence;
through various modes of conduct and skillful means, they universally cause all sentient beings to obtain great benefit.

All the perfections of the vows made by Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time that were sought in the past—namely, the vow to serve and attend all Buddhas, the vow to bring all sentient beings to maturity, and the vow to adorn and purify all Buddha-fields—all such vows as these have been fulfilled through the practice of perfected merit; they are endowed with all the marks and signs of a Tathāgata, have cultivated all remedial wholesome dharmas, have eliminated all the faults and afflictions of birth and death, and shall benefit sentient beings throughout all future kalpas, their vows being inexhaustible.
All the perfections of power corresponding to the three times practiced by Bodhisattvas in the past are as follows:

the power of generating great vows; the power of universally making offerings to all Buddhas; the power of universally purifying Buddha-fields; the power of universally cultivating sublime practices; and the power of universally transforming sentient beings.

All the perfections of wisdom practiced throughout the three periods of time by all bodhisattvas in the past consist of the power of knowledge that is perfected through every subtle realm; by means of this power, they awaken all sentient beings within the dharma-realm from the slumber of ignorance, causing them all to attain enlightenment and ultimately give rise to the path of omniscience.
In every thought-moment, the youth Sudhana clearly perceived all the realms manifested within each and every pore, from the feet to the crown of the head, of the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha.

At that time, Sudhana single-mindedly observed the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, giving rise to a profound sense of longing and reverence. He recollected that inconceivable samādhi and liberation; he accorded with the sovereign power of that inconceivable samādhi; he contemplated that inconceivable ocean of skillful means for benefiting sentient beings; he entered deeply into that inconceivable gate of wondrous, effortless, and universal adornment; he took delight in that inconceivable, pure realm of profound faith and understanding; he observed that inconceivable, pure wisdom that adorns the dharma-realm; he dwelt securely in that inconceivable wisdom sustained by the ultimate empowerment of the Buddhas; he brought forth that inconceivable power of the bodhisattva’s sovereignty; he made firm that inconceivable power of the bodhisattva’s great vows; and he expanded that inconceivable power of the bodhisattva’s various practices.

Remaining thus established, he contemplated and observed for one day and one night, and continued on for as long as seven days and seven nights, half a month and one month, and even six months; after further passing six days, the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja arose from his samādhi.
At that time, Sudhana spread his body upon the ground in reverent prostration; rising up with palms joined, he marveled at this unprecedented occurrence and praised it, saying:

"Noble One! Such a samādhi is rare and extraordinary. This gate of samādhi is most profound; this gate of samādhi is most vast. The realm of this gate of samādhi is immeasurable; the spiritual transformations of this gate of samādhi are inconceivable. The radiance of this gate of samādhi is peerless; the adornments of this gate of samādhi are innumerable. The power of this gate of samādhi is irresistible; the realm of this gate of samādhi is equal, unmoving, and undisturbed. This gate of samādhi universally illumines all worlds throughout the ten directions; the skillful means of this gate of samādhi are infinite and possess supreme capability."
Why is this? Because the benefits of this samādhi are inexhaustible, for it is able to eliminate the immeasurable aggregates of suffering of all sentient beings; namely:
Because it enables all sentient beings to sever the karma of poverty; because it brings forth an end to the suffering of the hells;

because it delivers them from the realm of animals; because it cuts off the causes for becoming a hungry ghost; because it closes the gates to all states of adversity; because it opens the paths to the human and celestial realms;
because it brings one close to all dharmas of peace and happiness; and because it gives rise to the sublime joys of humans and devas.
Because it causes them to take delight in the realm of meditative concentration; because it enables the increase of conditioned happiness;
because it can manifest the Dharma for seeking liberation from the three realms with diligence; because it can induce the arousal of the mind seeking unsurpassed bodhi with diligence;
