because it can cause the growth of the causes for the arising of the great accumulations of merit and wisdom; and because it can cause [them] to swiftly...
Because it swiftly increases and expands the mind of great compassion; because it enables the birth of the power of vast vows;
because it enables the illumination of the path of bodhisattva wisdom; because it enables the adornment of the path of the perfections;
because it enables the deep entry into the most supreme Mahāyāna; and because it enables the clear understanding of the wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra.
Because it enables entry into the light of wisdom of all bodhisattva stages; because it enables the accumulation and fulfillment of all bodhisattva vows and practices;
because it enables abiding within the sphere of the knowledge of all-knowledge;
because it enables the purification of all bodhisattva powers of transformation; and because it enables the diligent seeking of all empowerments.
"By the power of mastery,
O Noble One!
What is the name of this samādhi gate?"
Sāgaradhvaja replied, “Noble son!

This samādhi is named ‘The Universal Eye of Renunciation and Attainment,’ it is also named ‘The Pure Radiance of the Realm of Prajñāpāramitā,’ and it is also named ‘The Gate of Universal Adornment through Equanimity and Purity.’”

Good son! With this gateway of the universally adorned, equal, and pure as my foremost practice, I have fully perfected one million asaṃkhyeya of the most excellent, most honored, and incomparable samādhis.
Sudhana said, “Noble One! Is the ultimate realm of this samādhi only like this?”
Sāgaradhvaja said: "Good son!
The sphere of this samādhi-gate is profoundly deep, vast, and immeasurable; if one practices it, body and mind become tranquil."
When entering samādhi:
they understand all worlds in the ten directions without obstruction; they travel to all worlds in the ten directions without obstruction;
they enter and emerge from all worlds in the ten directions without obstruction; they adorn...
Adorning all worlds in the ten directions without obstruction, cultivating and purifying all worlds in the ten directions without obstruction,
seeing all Buddhas pervading the ten directions without obstruction, and contemplating the vast majesty and virtue of all Buddhas without obstruction.
Without obstruction, they know the playful supernatural powers of all Buddhas;
without obstruction, they realize the profound power of wisdom of all Buddhas; without obstruction, they enter the great ocean of merit of all Buddhas;
without obstruction, they raise the unsurpassed Dharma-clouds of all Buddhas; and they receive from all Buddhas...
The rain of immeasurable Dharma is unimpeded; in cultivating sublime practices within all Buddha-dharmas, they are unimpeded;
in knowing the nature of the equal wisdom that turns the sublime wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas, they are unimpeded;
in entering the oceans of assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas and manifesting supernormal powers, they are unimpeded, as they accord with the ten directions.
They give rise to sublime practices in the presence of all Buddhas without obstruction; they observe all Buddhas throughout the ten directions expounding the sublime Dharma without obstruction;
they universally enter all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions and manifest spiritual powers everywhere without obstruction;
and through great compassion, they embrace sentient beings throughout the ten directions, causing them to emerge from suffering.
Unobstructed in what is hindered, they constantly give rise to great compassion that fills the ten directions, bestowing happiness upon sentient beings without hindrance;
they universally behold all Buddhas of the ten directions with minds never weary or satisfied, without hindrance;
they universally enter the ocean of the various inclinations of all sentient beings in the ten directions without hindrance; they universally know the single... of the ten directions.
They encounter no obstacles regarding the ocean of the various faculties of all sentient beings, and they universally know,
without obstruction, the ocean of the various karmas of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions. Good son!

I know only this Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the Pure Radiance of Prajñāpāramitā; yet as for the profound and ultimate ocean of wisdom entered by the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, the most supreme realm of all dharmas purified by them, the Dharma-gates of all Buddhas reached by them, the immeasurable Buddha-fields of the ten directions visited by them, the light of the great wisdom-dhāraṇīs possessed by them, the perfect and sovereign samādhis in which they dwell, the various pure supernatural powers manifested by them, the inexhaustible ocean of eloquence endowed by them, the fearless and exquisite voices obtained by them through which they skillfully proclaim the merits of the stages, and their ability to protect all sentient beings—[I do not know these].

How could I possibly know their wondrous conduct, praise their merits, reveal their realms, extol their power of vows, manifest their radiance, enter their gates of liberation, reach their realizations, gather their sublime deeds, understand their sequence, know their universality, abide in their samādhis, perceive their mental objects, expound their true paths, discern their majestic power, or attain their all-encompassing, equalizing wisdom?
“Good son! From here, travel south until you reach the shore of the ocean tides; there is a great city named Paripūrṇaprabhā, and that city has a king named Citraprabha.”
To the east of that city there is a grove named Samantavyūha; there dwells the king’s consort, Queen Īśānā, who is an upāsikā and resides in this grove practicing the bodhisattva conduct.
Go there and ask her how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having received the most supreme Dharma from the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, attained a firm body, realized the sphere of samādhi, reached ultimate clarity and penetration, dwelt in pure understanding, and awakened to the profound realm of reality (dharmadhātu).
His mind followed the ocean of all Buddhas' teachings, and he remembered and upheld all dharma-gates without forgetting them.

Abiding in the gate of vast and universal adornment, the light of his wisdom shone forth, filling the ten directions. His heart gave rise to immeasurable joy and exultation; prostrating himself with his five limbs touching the ground, he bowed at the feet of Sāgaradhvaja. He circumambulated him countless times, bowing again and again, gazing up at him with reverence, contemplating and observing him, visualizing his deportment, holding his name, recollecting his merits, beholding his vows and practices, remembering the sound of his voice, reflecting on his samādhis, and envisioning the vast scope of his conduct. Receiving the pure radiance of the dhāraṇī-wisdom he had attained, he sighed in admiration and longing, then took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, empowered by the strength of his spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), brought the body of his merit to perfection through faith and understanding; relying on the instructions of the spiritual friends, he contemplated with right mindfulness, reflecting upon the words of the spiritual friends as they successively unfolded one another. He gave rise to deep shame and remorse regarding the conduct of the spiritual friends, cherishing them with love and respect, and observing how their minds skillfully gathered and sustained him, his joy increased all the more.
They form this thought:
"It is because of spiritual friends that I am able to see all Buddhas;
it is because of spiritual friends that I am able to hear all Buddha-dharmas."
Spiritual friends are my teachers and models, for they demonstrate and guide me toward the Dharma of all-knowledge so that I may see it universally;
spiritual friends are my eyes, for they enable me to see the realms of all Buddhas as vast as space;
spiritual friends are my channels, for they lead me to enter the lotus ponds of the Buddha-Tathāgatas.
Reflecting thus, he gradually traveled south toward the shore of the ocean.
Upon reaching the east of that city, he saw the Garden of Universal Adornment, surrounded on all sides by walls made of various jewels, with rows of every kind of jewel tree standing in solemn array.
That is to say:
the various jewel-leafed trees have branches and leaves that are lush and spreading, with brilliant luster and exquisite, flourishing beauty;
the various jewel-flowered trees rain down a multitude of wonderful jewels.
Kusuma flowers emit flames and radiate light, scattered across the ground;
various precious incense trees exude wondrous clouds of fragrance, their scent billowing forth to universally permeate the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions;
and various precious garland trees rain down great jeweled garlands, adorning the jewel groves as they hang down everywhere.
The Mani-king trees rain down all kinds of great mani jewels, spreading and filling them everywhere to adorn every place;
the celestial jewel karpāsa-cotton trees rain down all kinds of exquisite jeweled silks and multicolored garments, distributed and arrayed as appropriate for their respective locations;
the jewel-music trees produce exquisite musical instruments, which, when stirred by a gentle breeze, emit harmonious and elegant sounds, the beauty of which surpasses all the music of the heavens.
The various jewel-treasure trees, adorned with all manner of requisites, each rained down a multitude of precious gems and rare curiosities;
these various ornaments were distributed everywhere to serve as embellishments.
The ground was pure and free from elevations or depressions, vast and level, adorned in every way.

Within the garden were a million halls composed of great *maṇi* jewels; a million pavilions embellished with *Jāmbūnada* gold; and a million palaces interspersed and adorned with the *Vairocana-maṇi-rāja*. With structures soaring like clouds and winding like dragons, extending far and wide, their eaves and beams supported one another in a manner that seemed as if they were about to take flight.
A million bathing pools were composed of the seven precious jewels, with all manner of exquisite gems forming their banks;
fine golden sand was spread evenly across their bottoms;
and they were surrounded on all four sides by magnificent adornments of stairways made of the seven jewels and balustrades of *maṇi* gems.
The fragrant jewel-grasses spread along the borders and edges;
within them, sandalwood-scented water fills the pools, its temperature—warm or cool—modulated according to the inclinations of sentient beings.

Amidst the jewel-trees, jewel-canals are distributed, their waters clear and interspersed with various precious gems, constantly flowing day and night with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities.

Within the water there are many variously colored birds—wild ducks, geese, mandarin ducks, white cranes, peacocks, *kalaviṅkas*, *kinnaras*, *kokilas*, and others—flying together, gathering and dispersing, sporting and appearing and disappearing, preening their feathers and arranging their wings, swimming and soaring, emitting exquisite and beautiful sounds that are clear, piercing, and harmonious, like celestial music that delights the ear.
Ratna-tāla trees stood in rows all around, covered with jeweled nets from which golden bells hung; as a gentle breeze stirred them, they constantly produced exquisite sounds.
Countless mani-jewel banners and variegated silk streamers were erected, draped as ornaments on all four sides, their radiance illuminating hundreds of thousands of yojanas.

Within it, there were furthermore a million ponds and pools, their fragrant waters serene, limpid, and crystal clear; at all times, they were firm and fine, with sandalwood-scented mud settled as sediment beneath them. All manner of exquisite, multicolored jewel lotuses were in full bloom, while great maṇi flowers radiated brilliant light and color.

Within the garden, there was further a vast palace named Ocean-Treasury of Adorned Banners. Its ground was composed of exquisite jewels, and all manner of forms and images appeared within it. Columns were made of lapis lazuli, and nets adorned with Jambūnada gold covered its summit. With its multi-storied towers and side galleries, it rose loftily and majestically like a mountain of precious gold, bringing joy to all who beheld it.
It was adorned with various kinds of supreme jewels;
mani-jewels from treasuries of light constantly emitted wondrous radiance to provide illumination;
and it was exquisitely embellished by the king of mani-jewels, the Vairocana-treasury, which shone with brilliant clarity.
All the priceless kings of fragrances among all manner of jewels emit exquisite scents that universally permeate everything.
These are called:
the king of fragrances consisting of all supreme and wondrous jewels, whose scent rises everywhere in dense, swirling mists;
The Sovereign Jewel Incense King that Universally Manifests as Desired emits fragrances that pervade the entire Dharma-realm according to the needs of beings;

the Sovereign Jewel Incense King that Awakens According to Faculties causes all who smell it to have their faculties become sharp and keen, enabling them to apply themselves with diligence and tirelessness to the True Dharma.
Within those palaces, there were further immeasurable jewel lotus thrones arranged in every direction.

They were as follows: the Lotus Throne of the Wondrous Treasury Maṇi Jewel that Illumines the Ten Directions; the Lotus Throne of the Vairocana Wish-Fulfilling Maṇi Jewel; the Lotus Throne of the Stainless Treasury Maṇi Jewel; the Lotus Throne of the Maṇi Jewel Adorned with Various Jewels; the Lotus Throne of the Maṇi Jewel Adorned with Universal Gateways; the Lotus Throne of the Maṇi Jewel Adorned with Circular Radiance; the Lotus Throne of the Maṇi Jewel Purely Adorned and Abiding in the Ocean Treasury; the Lotus Throne of the Maṇi Jewel Universally Illuminated by Blazing Flames; the Lotus Throne of the Vajra-Treasury Lion Maṇi Jewel; and the Lotus Throne of the Maṇi Jewel Shining upon the World.

Thus, these immeasurable lotus seats made of mani jewels were each adorned with inconceivable, wondrous jewel silk ribbons hanging down from the four sides, and embellished with mani gems of inconceivable colors; within the palaces, their radiance and reflections illuminated one another in a state of uniform majesty.
In the sky there were also a million jeweled canopies, namely:

canopies of precious garments, canopies of precious garlands, canopies of precious flowers, canopies of precious incense, canopies of Jāmbūnada gold, canopies draped with precious branches, canopies of various mani-jewels, canopies of exquisite jewel necklaces, canopies of flaming vajras, canopies of celestial music and dance, canopies of the miraculous transformations of elephant kings, canopies of the miraculous transformations of horse kings, and canopies of the mani-jewels upon which Śakra sits;
such various canopies adorned with precious ornaments embellished the void.
Furthermore, there were ten million great jewel nets covering it from above, namely:

nets of jewel bells, nets of jewel canopies, nets of jewel bodies, nets of sea-treasury pearls, nets of sapphire-mani jewels, nets of lion-mani jewels, nets of moon-love radiance mani jewels, nets of various forms of precious incense for all humans and devas, nets of crowns of all miscellaneous colors, and nets of exquisite jewel necklaces;
such nets as these hung down and covered each part, providing adornment.
Furthermore, there were ten million great jewel radiances that shone forth, namely:

the radiance of the flame-light maṇi jewel, the radiance of the sun-treasury maṇi jewel, the radiance of the moon-treasury maṇi jewel, the radiance of the fragrance-flame maṇi jewel, the radiance of the auspicious-flame-treasury maṇi jewel, the radiance of the lotus-flame-treasury maṇi jewel, the radiance of the flame-banner maṇi jewel, the radiance of the great-flame maṇi jewel, the radiance of the maṇi jewel that universally illumines the ten directions, and the radiance of the maṇi jewel that manifests clouds of pervasive fragrant ornaments;
such were the great jewel radiances that shone forth.
Constantly raining clouds of a million ornaments for enjoyment according to one's wishes;
clouds of a million fragrant white sandalwood incenses that emit seasonal scents, universally perfuming the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa);
and clouds of a million celestial musical instruments with exquisite and beautiful sounds.
A hundred million clouds of celestial māndārava flowers were scattered abroad;
a hundred million clouds of celestial garlands and sashes hung down everywhere as adornments;
and a hundred million clouds of celestial precious silks and brocades were draped and spread everywhere as garments.
A million clouds of celestial jewel necklaces issued forth, adorning the forest trees and all the pavilions.
A million sons of the gods from the desire realm gazed upon him with joy, paying homage with reverence;
a million celestial maidens who had practiced together in the past constantly came to his presence, casting themselves down before him to attend and serve him with devotion.
A million great bodhisattvas constantly flocked to the site of enlightenment, always delighting in hearing the Dharma.

At that time, Īśāna, endowed with the marks of a great man, sat upon a throne of pure gold. He wore a crown of ocean-treasury pearl nets; he had golden armlets of surpassing purity that exceeded those of all the devas;

his deep blue hair hung down, his topknot being magnificently adorned. A garland of auspicious flame-treasury maṇi-jewel kings served as his sash; lapis lazuli maṇi jewels formed his earrings; lion-mouth maṇi jewels adorned the rims of his ears; and great wish-fulfilling maṇi-jewel kings served as necklaces, adorning his neck. A net of great majesty sapphire maṇi jewels covered his head, and a net of various blazing, radiant maṇi jewels enveloped his entire body.
Hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings bowed with reverence, drawing near to offer worship.
From the eastern direction, immeasurable sentient beings came to his presence.
That is to say:
the Great Brahmā Heaven, the Brahma-purohita Heaven, and the Brahma-kāyika Heaven—thus all the devas of the form realm;

as well as in the desire realm, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, and the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; and the various nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and kumbhāṇḍas; the realm of King Yama, the powerful ghosts and spirits, and even all humans and non-humans, including the assemblies of kings in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—all were likewise thus.

Whoever beholds this upāsikā shall have all physical and mental illnesses, as well as the various afflictions that entangle them—all delusions and sufferings arising from false views, obstacles, and attachments—completely extinguished;

they shall swiftly depart from the defilements of all afflictions, swiftly extract the poisonous thorns of all views, rapidly shatter the mountains of all obstacles, and deeply enter the unimpeded, pure realm.

He plants all roots of perfect goodness, nurtures the sprouts and roots of all wholesome dharmas, enters all gates of pure wisdom, universally attains all gates of *dhāraṇī*, universally realizes the great ocean of all *samādhis*, penetrates the ocean of teachings of all Buddhas, brings forth all the vast gates of the vows of all Buddhas, manifests before him all the sublime practices cultivated by all Bodhisattvas, and purifies the great ocean of merits of all Tathāgatas.
Their minds are vast and expansive, fully endowed with all sovereign spiritual powers;
their bodies are unimpeded, reaching everywhere without exception, universally visiting the ten directions without attachment, and accordantly accomplishing all dharma-gates.
At that time, the youth Sudhana entered the Universal Adornment Garden and surveyed it thoroughly;
seeing the laywoman Īśānā there, he approached her, prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, stood before her with palms joined, and said:
"Noble Lady!..."

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice, nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Noble One is well able to instruct and guide the assembly of bodhisattvas; I pray that you will explain this to me.
At that time, Īśāna said to Sudhana:
"Son of good family!
I have attained a single gate of liberation for Bodhisattvas, which I practice without interruption."

If there are sentient beings who even for a moment behold my body, hear my name, listen to my Dharma, remember me, dwell with me, draw near to me, follow me, or provide for me, none of these shall be in vain.
Good son! If there are sentient beings who have not planted roots of goodness, who are not sustained by virtuous friends, and who are not protected and remembered by the Buddhas;
even if they dwell near me for a long time and live together with me, they will ultimately never see me.
"Good son! Any sentient beings who behold me shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Good son!"
All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas from the eastern direction constantly come to this place and preach the Dharma for me upon exquisite lion thrones made of various jewels.
From the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and from above and below, may all Tathāgatas come to this place and preach the Dharma for me upon these jewel thrones.
"Good son! I am never separated from seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma, dwelling together with all bodhisattvas, and never departing from the samādhis and liberations of the bodhisattvas."

"Good son! In this assembly of mine, there are eighty-four thousand *koṭi-nayuta* beings who constantly dwell here with me in this Universally Adorned Garden. Because they all practiced the same categories of bodhisattva conduct as I did in the past and were never separated from one another, they have all attained non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."

As for the other sentient beings who have dwelt in this garden for either a long or short time, they all cultivate practices and gates identical to my own, and have likewise universally entered the stage of non-retrogression.
Sudhana said, “Noble One,
how long has it been since you first resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?”
He replied, "Good son!
I recall that in the past, I personally attended upon and served the Buddha Dīpaṃkara, practiced the holy life, paid respectful offerings, and heard and upheld the Dharma."
Prior to that, he went forth from home to study the Way under the Buddha Vigatarajas and upheld the True Dharma;
prior to that, he heard the Dharma and practiced it under the Buddha Jyotirdhvaja, making offerings with joy;

prior to that, under the Buddha Viśeṣaśrī; prior to that, under the Buddha Padmaguṇagarbha; prior to that, under the Buddha Vairocana; prior to that, under the Buddha Samantacakṣus; prior to that, under the Buddha Brahmāyuṣ; prior to that, under the Buddha Vajramukha; and prior to that, under the Buddha Varuṇadeva.

"Good son! I recall that in the past, throughout immeasurable kalpas and immeasurable births, I have successively approached thirty-six Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. In every case, I drew near to them, served them with a single mind, honored and made offerings to them, left the household life to study the Way, received their true Dharma, made my vows, entered various samādhis, and realized liberation. All such diverse gateways of practice I remember and uphold, never failing to keep them in mind; beyond this, however, is what is known by the Buddha’s wisdom, which is not within my power to fathom."
“Good son! You should know that the initial resolve of a bodhisattva is immeasurable, for it fills the entire dharma-realm;
the gate of a bodhisattva’s great compassion is immeasurable, for it universally enters the realm of all sentient beings.”
The gateways of the Bodhisattvas' great vows are immeasurable, for they reach the ultimate limit of all dharma-realms in the ten directions;
the gateways of the Bodhisattvas' great compassion are immeasurable, for they universally cover all realms of sentient beings;
the practices cultivated by the Bodhisattvas are immeasurable, for they are constantly practiced throughout all lands and all eons.
The power of the bodhisattva’s samādhi is immeasurable, for it causes the bodhisattva path to be non-retrogressive;
the power of the bodhisattva’s dhāraṇī is immeasurable, for it can sustain the ocean of teachings to be heard according to what is appropriate for the world;
the power of the bodhisattva’s illumination of wisdom is immeasurable, for it can universally penetrate and skillfully accord with the Buddha-teachings of the three periods of time.
The power of the bodhisattva’s spiritual penetrations is immeasurable, for they universally manifest throughout all the networks of lands in the ten directions;
the power of the bodhisattva’s eloquence is immeasurable, for with a single utterance of their perfect voice, they cause all sentient beings to understand according to their respective types;
the purity of the bodhisattva’s body is immeasurable, for they manifest bodies that pervade all buddha-fields.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Seven;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation," at that time, the youth Sudhana said: "Noble One!
"How long will it be before you attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi? He replied:
"O son of good family!"
A bodhisattva does not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and taming even a single sentient being;
nor do they resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and taming a hundred sentient beings; nor do they resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and taming a thousand sentient beings;
nor do they resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and taming a hundred thousand sentient beings.
They resolve their minds on enlightenment, not even for the sake of teaching, transforming, and subduing unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings;
they do not resolve their minds on enlightenment for the sake of teaching and bringing to maturity the sentient beings of a single world-system,
nor even for the sake of teaching and bringing to maturity the sentient beings of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of world-systems.

One generates the bodhicitta for the sake of all sentient beings; one does not generate the bodhicitta for the sake of teaching, transforming, and bringing to maturity the sentient beings of a world-system as numerous as the atoms in a single Jambudvīpa;
one does not generate the bodhicitta for the sake of bringing to maturity the sentient beings of a world-system as numerous as the atoms in a single four-continent world (cāturdvīpaka);
one does not [generate the bodhicitta] for the sake of bringing to maturity the sentient beings of a small thousandfold world-system...
They resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of maturing sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the atoms in a world-system;
they do not resolve upon bodhicitta merely for the sake of maturing sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the atoms in a medium chiliocosm,
nor do they resolve upon bodhicitta merely for the sake of maturing sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the atoms in a great trichiliocosm.

The mind, even to the extent that one does not resolve to attain bodhicitta for the sake of teaching and maturing sentient beings in as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of trichiliocosms.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of approaching and making offerings to a single Tathāgata,
nor even for the sake of approaching and making offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of Buddha-fields;
nor do they do so for the sake of approaching and making offerings to a single world-system.
They resolve upon the bodhicitta for the sake of approaching and making offerings to all the Tathāgatas who will arise in succession throughout all future kalpas;
even to the point of not resolving upon the bodhicitta merely for the sake of approaching and making offerings to a single Buddha,
but rather for the sake of approaching and making offerings to all the Tathāgatas who will arise in succession throughout all future kalpas within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of world-systems.
They resolve to generate the bodhicitta for the sake of all Tathāgatas who will successively appear in worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field throughout all future kalpas;

and even for the sake of approaching and making offerings to all Tathāgatas who will successively appear throughout all future kalpas in worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of buddha-fields.
Therefore, they resolve upon bodhicitta.

Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of adorning and purifying a single world-system, nor even for the sake of adorning and purifying worlds as numerous as unspeakably unspeakable multiples; they do not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of adorning and purifying worlds as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field, nor even for the sake of adorning and purifying worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable multiples of buddha-fields.

Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not generate the mind of enlightenment for the sake of upholding the teaching of a single Tathāgata, nor even for the sake of upholding the teachings of as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable times the number of Buddha-fields.

Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of cultivating the vow of a single Tathāgata, nor even for the sake of cultivating vows as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of Buddha-fields.

Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not resolve upon awakening for the sake of traveling to a single buddha-field, nor even for the sake of traveling to as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable multiples of buddha-fields.

Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not resolve upon awakening for the sake of adorning the assembly of a single Tathāgata, nor even for the sake of adorning assemblies of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable multiples of Buddha-fields.

Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not resolve upon enlightenment for the sake of upholding the sublime wheel of Dharma turned by a single Buddha, nor even for the sake of upholding the sublime wheels of Dharma turned by as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva does not generate the mind of enlightenment for the sake of upholding the legacy of a single Tathāgata’s Dharma;
nor do they generate the mind of enlightenment for the sake of upholding the legacy of as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
nor for the sake of upholding [the Dharma] within a single world-system throughout the entirety of the future.
They resolve upon the mind of enlightenment for the sake of maintaining the bequeathed Dharma of the Tathāgatas appearing in succession throughout the kalpas;

even to the extent of not doing so merely for the sake of maintaining the bequeathed Dharma of the Tathāgatas appearing in succession throughout all future kalpas within as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields,
they do not resolve upon the mind of enlightenment for the sake of maintaining even one...

They resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to successively manifest the bequeathed Dharma of the Tathāgatas throughout all future kalpas within as many worlds as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa;

they do not resolve their minds on enlightenment merely for the sake of maintaining the bequeathed Dharma of the Tathāgatas throughout all future kalpas within as many worlds as there are atoms in a single four-continent world-system.

...up to: they do not resolve their minds on enlightenment for the sake of maintaining the bequeathed Dharma of the Tathāgatas as they appear in succession throughout all future eons within worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
Thus, this brief exposition is not for the sake of fulfilling the vow of a single Buddha, nor for the sake of going to a single Buddha-land,
nor for the sake of entering a single Buddha’s assembly, nor for the sake of upholding the Dharma-eye of a single Buddha,
nor for the sake of turning the wheel of Dharma of a single Buddha, nor for the sake of knowing the succession of kalpas within a single world-system.
Therefore, it is not for the sake of knowing the various oceans of the minds of a single sentient being;
nor for the sake of knowing the various oceans of the faculties of a single sentient being; nor for the sake of knowing the various oceans of the karma of a single sentient being;
nor for the sake of knowing the various oceans of the conduct of a single sentient being; nor for the sake of knowing the various afflictions of a single sentient being.
It is not for the sake of knowing the ocean of various afflictions and habitual tendencies of a single sentient being that they resolve upon bodhicitta;
nor is it for the sake of knowing the oceans of various afflictions and habitual tendencies of even unspeakably unspeakable multiples of Buddha-fields of atoms that they resolve upon bodhicitta.
Why is this? It is because Bodhisattvas resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of teaching, transforming, and subduing all sentient beings without exception;
and they resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of drawing near to, honoring, and making offerings to all Buddhas without exception.
They resolve their minds on enlightenment because they desire to adorn and purify all buddha-fields without exception;
they resolve their minds on enlightenment because they desire to protect and preserve all the Buddha’s teachings without exception;
they resolve their minds on enlightenment because they desire to accord with the path traversed by all Tathāgatas without exception.
They resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to fulfill the vast vows of all Tathāgatas without exception;
they resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to travel to all Buddha-lands without exception;
they resolve their minds on enlightenment because they wish to enter all assemblies of Buddhas without exception.
One generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to know, without exception, the sequential order of all kalpas within all worlds;
one generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to know, without exception, the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings;
one generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to know, without exception, the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings.
One generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to know the ocean of karma of all sentient beings without exception;
one generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to know the ocean of conduct of all sentient beings without exception;
one generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to extinguish the ocean of all afflictions of all sentient beings without exception.
One generates the bodhicitta because one desires to uproot the ocean of afflictions and habitual tendencies of all sentient beings without exception.
"Good son! To state the essential point: [one generates the bodhicitta]..."
It is because Bodhisattvas have practiced such hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* skillful means that they resolve upon Bodhicitta.
Good son! It is because Bodhisattvas practice the universal entry into all dharmas and realize them all.
Because they universally enter all lands and completely purify them.
Therefore, O son of good family!
My vow shall not end until all worlds have been purified; I fully know all worlds throughout the ten directions.
My vows shall only end when the succession of kalpas has reached its ultimate end; my vows shall only end when I have fully attained the ocean of merits of all Buddhas of the ten directions;
my vows shall only end when I have successively cultivated and accumulated the ocean of vigor of all Bodhisattvas;
my vows shall only end when I have adorned the oceans of assemblies of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions.
My vows shall not be exhausted until I have fully perceived the ocean of the mental inclinations of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
my vows shall not be exhausted until I have fully known the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions;

my vows shall not be exhausted until I have universally observed the ocean of the various practices of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions; [and] until I have universally dried up the afflictions of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions.
My vow shall end only when the ocean of karma is exhausted; my vow shall end only when the ocean of all the sufferings of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions is completely extinguished;
my vow shall end only when the ocean of habitual tendencies of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions is entirely uprooted.
"Good son! In this way, even unto hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* bodhisattva practice-gates, all are completely fulfilled without exception; thus my vow is fulfilled."

Therefore, in order to bring all-knowledge to full completion, to accord with the bodhisattva practices, and to adorn and purify all buddha-fields, the bodhisattva seeks all dharmas with courageous diligence, never ceasing.
"Good son! You should know that the vows practiced by a bodhisattva who has resolved upon bodhicitta, and all his aspirations and inclinations, are as vast as the dharma-realm and ultimate as space;
because space is ultimately inexhaustible, my vow is likewise ultimately inexhaustible."
Because the dharma-realm is vast and without limit, my vow is also vast and without limit;
because the realm of all sentient beings is ultimately inexhaustible, my vow is also ultimately inexhaustible.
Sudhana the youth said:
"Noble One! What is the name of this door of liberation?"
Iśāna said: "Good son! This liberation is named 'The Banner of Peaceful Security Free from Sorrow.'"

"Good son! I know only this single gate of liberation. As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, their aspiration is profound and vast, like the great ocean, which receives the Buddha-dharma with a mind that knows no satiety;
their resolve is as firm and solid as Mount Sumeru, such that the right practices they cultivate cannot be shaken."
Their actions are not in vain, like the "Good-to-See" medicine that can eliminate the grave illnesses of sentient beings' afflictions;
their body of unimpeded wisdom is like the bright, pure sun that destroys the dark obstructions of ignorance for all sentient beings;
and their inexhaustible great compassion is like the great earth, universally serving as the support for all sentient beings.
The merit of their blessings and wisdom is like a favorable wind, performing great benefit for all sentient beings;
they universally illumine the world like a lamp or candle, able to produce the light of all wisdom;
they universally manifest their bodies like great clouds, able to rain down the Dharma of nirvana upon sentient beings.
The radiance of their merit is like the full moon, bringing peace and happiness to all who behold it;

their majestic virtue and supreme excellence are like those of Śakra, capable of protecting all sentient beings. How then could I know or describe the meritorious practices and vows of those bodhisattvas—the inconceivable ocean of their infinite discipline and concentration?
"Good son! To the south of here, at the place where the ocean tides come, there is a land named Nalasū. Therein dwells a rishi named Mahāvikramaśvara;
go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the upāsikā Īśānā, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and wept tears of sorrow as he reflected:
"A spiritual friend is difficult to appear, like the udumbara flower;
a spiritual friend is most difficult to encounter; a spiritual friend is difficult to approach; a spiritual friend is difficult to serve; and a spiritual friend is difficult to please."

He further reflected: "It is difficult to attain Bodhi; it is difficult to attain the faculties of a bodhisattva; it is difficult to purify the faculties of a bodhisattva; it is difficult to encounter a spiritual friend who practices the same path; it is difficult to accumulate the vast roots of goodness of a bodhisattva; it is difficult to realize the vast sphere of a bodhisattva; it is difficult to contemplate the conduct and vows of a bodhisattva according to principle; it is difficult to reflect in accordance with the teachings of a bodhisattva; it is difficult to practice the sublime conduct of a bodhisattva in reliance upon those teachings; it is difficult to give rise to the virtuous mind of a bodhisattva through mindfulness; it is difficult to swiftly initiate the skillful means of a bodhisattva; and it is difficult to skillfully increase the light of the Dharma of omniscience."
Having formed this thought, he took his leave and departed.

At that time, the youth Sudhana reflected in accordance with the true teaching of the bodhisattvas; he reflected in accordance with the pure conduct of the bodhisattvas. He gave rise to a mind that swiftly increases all the power of a bodhisattva’s merit; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly and universally beholds the light of all Buddhas; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly attains the treasury of all dharmas; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly increases all great vows; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly manifests and perceives all phenomena throughout the ten directions; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly and clearly illuminates the fundamental nature of all dharmas; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly disperses and extinguishes all obstacles; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly observes the dharma-realm without darkness; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly destroys internal defilements like a vajra; he gave rise to a mind that swiftly crushes and subdues the hosts of Māra’s armies; and he gave rise to a mind that swiftly adorns the jewel of the purified mind.

Reflecting thus, he gradually traveled on until he reached the kingdom of Nalasa, where he searched everywhere for the Great Majestic Sage. He saw a vast forest, lush and verdant, adorned with incalculable trees.
That is to say:
various leafy trees with branches and twigs spreading luxuriantly, their dense foliage a vibrant green;
various flowering trees with boughs and leaves spreading wide, their blossoms profuse and exquisite.
Various fruit trees ripen in continuous succession;
various jewel trees rain down mani fruits;
and great sandalwood trees stand in rows everywhere.
The various *agaru* trees constantly emit exquisite fragrances;
the Jambūnada trees perpetually rain down sweet fruits;
and the delightful incense trees are adorned with wondrous scents.
The *pāṭala* trees were in full bloom with radiant flowers, their fragrance wafting in all directions;
the *nyagrodha* trees rose tall and straight, their branches and leaves spreading thickly in a canopy-like formation;
and *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* lotuses bloomed everywhere, adorning the ponds and pools.

At that time, the youth Sudhana entered this great forest and beheld a sandalwood tree whose trunk was massive and straight, its branches spreading downward, its flowers and leaves dense and thick, forming a canopy of deep shade.
At that time, the seer sat beneath this tree with his hair wound into a topknot and resting upon fragrant grass;
ten thousand seers surrounded him from before and behind.
Those seers wore either deerskins, or bark garments, or various robes woven from fine grass; with their topknots and ringlets hanging down, they stood gazing up at him.
Having seen him, Sudhana went to his place, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground in deep devotion, and spoke these words:
"I have now encountered a true spiritual friend."
He further thought:
"A spiritual friend is the gateway to all-knowledge, for they enable me to enter the path of reality;
a spiritual friend is the vehicle to all-knowledge, for they enable me to reach the stage of the Tathāgata."
A spiritual friend is a ship for proceeding toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to reach the island of the jewels of wisdom;
a spiritual friend is a torch for proceeding toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to give birth to the light of the ten powers;
a spiritual friend is a path for proceeding toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to swiftly enter the city of Nirvana.
A spiritual friend is a lamp leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to distinguish the paths of the heterodox and the orthodox;
a spiritual friend is a bridge leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to cross the stream of birth and death;
a spiritual friend is a parasol leading toward all-knowledge, for they enable me to obtain the shade of compassion.
A spiritual friend is a ferry for proceeding toward omniscience, for they cause me to swiftly reach the shore of merit;
a spiritual friend is an eye for proceeding toward omniscience, for they enable me to see the gateway of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*);
a spiritual friend is a tide for proceeding toward omniscience, for they ensure that I do not miss the proper time according to my capacity.
Having spoken these words, he rose from the ground, circumambulated him countless times, and stood before him with palms joined, saying:

"Noble One! I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me."
Then, that rishi looked toward the assembly of rishis and addressed them, saying:
"O virtuous ones!
You should know that this youth has already resolved his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. This youth..."
This youth desires to bestow fearlessness upon all sentient beings; this youth desires to grant benefit to all sentient beings;
this youth desires to bestow peace and happiness upon all sentient beings; this youth desires to contemplate the ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas;
this youth desires to be sheltered by the Dharma-clouds of all Tathāgatas; this youth...
This youth wishes to traverse the ocean of all Buddhas' teachings; this youth wishes to kindle the great lamp of omniscient wisdom;
this youth wishes to raise the clouds of great compassion; this youth wishes to drink the nectar-water of the Dharma;
this youth wishes to rain down the vast rain of the Dharma. This youth...
You wish to universally illuminate the world with the moon of wisdom; this youth wishes to extinguish the poisonous heat of the afflictions of sentient beings;
this youth wishes to bestow the coolness of the wholesome dharmas upon the world; this youth wishes to cause all roots of goodness in conscious beings to grow.

When the assembly of sages heard these words, they each scattered various kinds of exquisite incense and flowers upon Sudhana, prostrated their bodies in worship, circumambulated him countless times, and extolled him with praise, saying:
"This youth will surely be able to rescue and protect all sentient beings; he will surely be able to extinguish the sufferings of the various hells;
he will surely be able to forever sever the paths of the animal realm; and he will surely be able to eternally leave behind the realm of King Yama."
They will surely be able to close the gates to all places of peril; they will surely be able to dry up the ocean of craving and desire;
they will surely be able to liberate themselves from the fetters of greed and lust; they will surely be able to eternally extinguish the mass of suffering of sentient beings;
they will surely be able to forever shatter the darkness of ignorance; and they will surely protect the world with the great mountain range of merit, ensuring its stability.
Śāntamati, you must certainly manifest to the world the mountain of Sumeru made of the great jewel of wisdom—the accumulation of merit and knowledge;
you must certainly reveal the treasury of all roots of goodness through the sun of pure, unobstructed wisdom;
and you must certainly cause sentient beings to open the eye of pure wisdom, clearly discerning the world and returning to the right path.
Then, Mahātejasvara addressed the assembly of sages, saying:
"O sons of good family!

If there are those who can resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they will surely be able to courageously practice the bodhisattva path; they will surely be able to benefit all sentient beings; they will surely provide vast benefit and happiness to sentient beings; and they will surely be able to accomplish the way of omniscience."
"This son of good family has already resolved his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; he shall purify the ground of all the merits of the Buddhas.
Having spoken these words, he addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Son of good family!"
"I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door called 'Inconquerable Banner.
Sudhana said, "Noble One!"
"What is the sphere of this gate of liberation?
At that time, the Great Seer extended his right hand to stroke Sudhana’s head and took Sudhana’s hand;

immediately, Sudhana saw his own body go everywhere throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields in the ten directions, and visit the presence of Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields in the ten directions. He beheld the various adornments of those Buddha-fields and their assemblies, and he also saw the various marks and signs of those Buddhas, their radiant light blazing forth, and he heard those Buddhas preaching the Dharma according to the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings.

They thoroughly penetrate every word and every phrase, individually receiving the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas; they each separately retain and elucidate their meanings and principles, following the proper sequence without any confusion.

They also know the sentient beings saved by that Buddha, whose various inclinations and desires are met according to their faculties and natures, so that the rain of all Dharmas falls upon them, each attaining maturity;
they also know how that Buddha, in times past, purified the ocean of vows through various understandings;
and they also know how that Buddha, by means of pure vows, accomplished all the powers.
I also saw that Buddha manifesting various distinct physical bodies according to the minds of sentient beings;
I also saw that Buddha’s great net of light, with its various colors and forms, perfectly pure and complete;
and I also knew that Buddha’s unobstructed wisdom and the pure adornments of the assembly at his site of enlightenment.
Furthermore, one sees oneself everywhere in the presence of all Tathāgatas, drawing near to them, making offerings, and upholding the True Dharma—
whether for a single day and night in the presence of a Buddha, or for seven days and seven nights,
or for half a month, or for a month, a year, ten years, or a hundred years, or a thousand [years].

For a year, or for hundreds or thousands of years; or having passed through ten million years, a hundred million, a thousand million, or a hundred thousand million years; or for *ayuta* billion years, or *nayuta* billion years;
or having passed through half a kalpa, or one kalpa, a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, or a hundred thousand million *ayuta* kalpas.
For nayuta-billions of kalpas, even up to as many kalpas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields—
they know all such things completely and without exception, penetrating them all.
At that time, because the light of the wisdom of the Bodhisattva’s liberation of the Invincible Banner illuminated him, the youth Sudhana attained the light of the Samādhi of the Vairocana Treasury;

because the light of the Samādhi of the liberation of inexhaustible wisdom illuminated him, he attained the light of the Dhāraṇī of Manifesting Bodies in All Directions while Universally Encompassing All Directions;
and because the light of the Vajra-Wheel Dhāraṇī illuminated him, he attained the light of the Samādhi of the Mass of Wisdom in Pure Realms.

Because they are illuminated by the light of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Treasury of Adornments of the Universal Gate’s Boundless Realm, they attain the light of the Buddha’s Samādhi of the Perfect Space-Treasury;

because they are illuminated by the light of the Samādhis of the Dharma-Wheel of the Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom of all Buddhas, they attain the light of the Samādhi of Perfect, Inexhaustible Wisdom throughout the Three Times.
Then, that rishi released Sudhana’s hand, and the youth Sudhana immediately saw himself returned to his original place.
The rishi said to him:
“O son of good family!
"Do you remember? Sudhana replied, "Indeed,
it is solely through the power of the holy spiritual friend that I have been able to remember this so clearly and vividly."
The seer replied: "Good son!
I know only this bodhisattva liberation door called 'Incomparable Banner. As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have accomplished all supreme samādhis and attained mastery at all times—"
In a single thought-moment, they give birth to the subtle realm of the immeasurable wisdom of all Buddhas;
adorned with the wisdom of the Buddhas, they universally illumine the world without obstruction;

in a single thought-moment, they universally enter the realms of the three periods of time, manifesting diverse forms to travel throughout the oceans of lands in the ten directions, their bodies of wisdom—
They universally enter all dharma realms and appear before all sentient beings in accordance with their minds,
emitting pure light to inspire joy in them; observing their faculties and conduct, they bring them benefit—
how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious deeds, their sublime vows, their adorned lands, or their wisdom?
Their spheres of activity; their range of samādhis; their miraculous transformations of supernormal powers;
their playful mastery of liberation; the distinctions among their physical bodies; the purity of their voices; the radiance of their wisdom;

their spheres throughout the three periods of time; the universal reaching of their form-bodies; the universal illumination of their wisdom-bodies; and their accordance with the inclinations [of beings].
How does he universally manifest? How does he benefit beings according to the times? How does he accord with worldly conventions and protocols?
What is taught by his perfect voice? What are his pure and wondrous practices? And how is he illumined by his net of light?
"Noble son! To the south of here there is a village named Īśāna;
there is a dwelling place there called Ayaṭana, where a brahmin named Jvalanānta resides."
“Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, filled with joy and exultation, gave rise to a heart of love and reverence; he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and then took his leave to travel south.
At that time, because the light of the Bodhisattva’s liberation door of the Invincible Banner (Anabhibhū-dhvaja) illuminated his mind,
the youth Sudhana attained the various supernormal powers within the inconceivable realm of all Buddhas;
he realized the various supernormal wisdoms of the inconceivable liberation of Bodhisattvas, and obtained the inconceivable [wisdom] of Bodhisattvas.
He attains the light of wisdom that is free from obscuration; he attains the light of wisdom of the samādhi that is constantly perfumed at all times;
he attains the light of wisdom of the samādhi that thoroughly knows all objects abide in dependence upon conceptualization;
and he attains the light of wisdom that enters into all worlds with their full excellence. Because he has attained such lights of wisdom, [he...]
In all places, he manifests bodies in accordance with [the needs of beings];
through each and every body, by means of ultimate wisdom, he expounds the Dharma that is ultimately equal, non-dual, undifferentiated, and free from conceptual construction.
With luminously pure wisdom, he universally illuminates all realms; whatever profound liberation one hears, it is the treasury of the pure Dharma.
They are able to endure all things, possessing pure faith and understanding that is resolute and clear;
they have no doubts regarding the self-nature of all phenomena, and their minds never abandon the cultivation of all the sublime practices of bodhisattvas,
proceeding with courageous diligence toward omniscience without ever turning back.
Having attained the light of wisdom that distinguishes the ten powers, they take delight in the profound Dharma without ever becoming weary;
through correct practice, they abide in omniscience, their minds directed rightly as they enter the realm of the Buddhas,
giving rise to the vast adornments of a bodhisattva, fulfilling boundless and pure great vows, and remaining unobstructed.
With unimpeded wisdom, they know the infinite network of worlds; with a mind free from indolence, they deliver the infinite ocean of sentient beings;
they universally and thoroughly comprehend the boundless spheres of all bodhisattva practices; they universally perceive the various distinctions of all infinite worlds;
and they universally enter all infinite worlds, whether vast or narrow, coarse or subtle.
They universally know the various nets of conceptualization in all boundless worlds;
they universally know the established truths of all boundless worlds; they universally comprehend the verbal praises of all boundless worlds;
they universally know the various inclinations and understandings of all boundless sentient beings; they universally know all boundless sentient beings...

At the time of maturation, they universally know the various thoughts and intentions of all infinite sentient beings and universally perceive the various physical forms of all infinite sentient beings, maturing them through skillful means according to what is appropriate for each.

Mindful of the spiritual friend, he traveled by stages until he reached the village of Īśāna, where he saw the Brahmin Jvalanāmukha performing various ascetic practices in the scorching sun. On four sides were masses of fire like great mountains, and in their midst stood a mountain of blades, towering and boundless; desiring to diligently seek the knowledge of all-knowledge, he climbed that mountain of blades and cast himself into the fire.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, having arrived at his location, prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said:

"Noble One! I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me."
The brahmin said: "Good son!
If you can now ascend this mountain of blades and cast yourself into this mass of fire, all the practices of the bodhisattvas will become completely purified."
At that time, the youth Sudhana thought to himself: "It is difficult to obtain a human body; it is difficult to be free from all calamities;

it is difficult to attain a state free from calamity; it is difficult to be free from unwholesome dharmas; it is difficult to attain pure dharmas; it is difficult to encounter a Buddha appearing in the world; it is difficult to possess all the sense faculties; it is difficult to hear the True Dharma; it is difficult to meet virtuous people; it is difficult to encounter a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra); it is difficult to receive correct instruction according to the principle; it is difficult to sustain one's life through right livelihood; it is difficult to practice in accordance with the Dharma. Could this not be Mara, or one sent by Mara?"

Could it not be that these are demons, wicked associates, or impostors who falsely manifest the appearance of Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends, acting as enemies to all Bodhisattvas? They seek to create obstacles for my roots of goodness, obstacles to my life-span, and obstacles to my pure conduct; they obstruct my cultivation of the path to omniscience, drag me into evil destinies, hinder the Dharma-gate of liberation I have realized, and block the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma I seek.
While he was thinking this, ten thousand Brahmā gods dwelling in the midst of space spoke these words:
"Good son! Do not think such thoughts; do not think such thoughts!"

Now this noble one has attained the radiance of the *vajrajvālā-samādhi* and exerts great diligence with heroic vigor, never retreating; he vows to enter the cycle of birth and death to deliver all sentient beings. He desires to exhaust the ocean of all cravings, to sever the net of all false views, to burn the firewood of all afflictions, and to universally transport those across treacherous difficulties and desert wastes. He desires to utterly eliminate the fears of old age, sickness, and death; to completely blow apart the mountain of the obstructions of ignorance; to universally guide others out of the dense forest of delusion; and to radiate the light of all sublime Dharmas to universally illuminate the dark ignorance of the three periods of time.
"Good son! We Brahmā devas cling to false views;
we all claim for ourselves that we are the sovereign, the creator, and the most supreme among all worlds."
This brahmin was performing the austerity of "scorching the body with five fires.

At that time, the radiance of his fire illuminated my palace, and I immediately attained awakening; I no longer took pleasure in my own abode or in various meditative concentrations, and we all came together to the place where the brahmin was.

Then, by means of his supernormal powers, the brahmin manifested great ascetic practices for us, causing us to eliminate all false views. He preached the Dharma for us, causing us to sever all arrogance, to universally dwell in the practice of great loving-kindness for all sentient beings in the world, to give rise to a vast mind of great compassion, to resolve upon Bodhicitta, to abide in firm vows, to joyfully seek liberation, to constantly see all Buddhas, and to perpetually hear the wondrous Dharma.
"In all places, his mind is without attachment; he is able to turn the perfect wheel of Dharma everywhere, its sound unimpeded and pervading all.
Furthermore, ten thousand māra-deva hosts dwelling in the air scattered celestial maṇi jewels upon the brāhmaṇa and said to Sudhana: "O noble son!

When this brahmin was performing the ascetic practice of scorching his body with five fires, the radiance of those flames eclipsed all our palaces, as well as the necklaces and various ornaments upon our bodies; all our own splendors appeared like a mass of ink, causing us to feel no pleasure or attachment therein, so we, together with our retinues, came to where he was.
At that time, the brahmin preached the Dharma for me, causing me and immeasurable other sons of gods and daughters of gods to attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Furthermore, ten thousand kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven scattered celestial flowers from the midst of the sky, speaking these words:
"O son of good family!
This brahmin is performing the penance of being scorched by the five fires."

At that time, the radiance of that fire eclipsed all my palaces, necklaces, and ornaments; all my own splendors became like a mass of ink, causing me to feel no attachment toward them, and so I came to that place together with my retinue.

At that time, the brahmin preached the Dharma for me, causing my body and mind to attain mastery; I attained mastery over afflictions, mastery over rebirth, mastery over the span of life, mastery over karmic obstructions, mastery over all samādhis, mastery over the articles of adornment, mastery over the bodhicitta, and even mastery over all Buddha-dharmas.
Furthermore, ten thousand kings of the Nirmāṇarati devas remained in mid-air, performing celestial music and making offerings with reverent, exquisite voices, saying these words:
“O son of good family!

When this brahmin was performing the austerity of scorching his body with five fires, the radiance of those flames illuminated my palace and all its ornaments; their brilliance so overwhelmed all other lights that they became invisible. This caused me and my retinue of court ladies to feel no attachment to the five sensual pleasures and to cease seeking their enjoyment, leaving our bodies and minds supple and serene. Thereupon, I came to where he was together with my attendants.

At that time, the brahmin preached the Dharma for me, enabling our minds to attain purity, clarity, adaptability, and sublime goodness; making our minds exceedingly supple and giving rise to joy; even leading us to attain the pure body of wisdom endowed with the ten powers, to manifest immeasurable pure form-bodies, to issue forth immeasurable pure speech, to produce immeasurable Tathāgata-voices, to awaken to and enter the immeasurable mind of the Tathāgatas, and to fully obtain the knowledge of all-knowledge.

Furthermore, ten thousand Tuṣita kings, sons of gods, goddesses, and immeasurable retinues arose in the sky, raising clouds of incense and raining down various exquisite fragrances as an offering of respectful worship, saying these words:
"O Son of Good Family!
When this brahmin performed the ascetic practice of scorching his body with the five fires,

light illuminated my palace, causing all the gods and their retinues to cease feeling attachment toward their own palaces and lose their craving for sensual pleasures, so that they came to where he was.

At that time, the brahmin preached the Dharma for us, enabling us to sever all attachment to the five desires, to give rise to joy through fewness of wishes and contentment, to have our minds become fully satisfied, to produce various roots of goodness and resolve for Bodhicitta, and even to bring all Buddha-dharmas to perfection.

Furthermore, ten thousand kings of the Yāma Heaven, together with their retinues of devaputras and devīs, surrounded him in the air from front and behind. They scattered celestial māndārava flowers, mahāmāndārava flowers, and kusuma flowers upon the brahmin, making offerings with reverence and speaking these words: "O noble son!
When this brahmin performed the ascetic practice of "scorching the body with five fires," his light illuminated my palace.

It enabled us, at the time of our assemblies, to feel no attachment to celestial music, nor any craving for our own bodies or retinues. We came to where he was, heard his preaching of the Dharma, and gave rise to a complete renunciation of all sensual pleasures, turning toward and seeking after all Buddha-dharmas.

Furthermore, ten thousand Śakras, kings of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, together with their retinues of devaputras and apsaras, surrounded him in the air from front and behind, raining down celestial garments, various precious necklaces, celestial ornaments, and kusuma flowers as an offering of reverent worship, saying these words:
“O Son of Good Family!
When this brahmin was performing the austerity of being scorched by the five fires, his light illuminated my palace.

Consequently, my celestial hosts, within their palaces, no longer found delight in their superior assemblies, their sporting in the groves, the celestial music, or their places of entertainment; they immediately came with their retinues to where he was.

At that time, the brahmin taught us that all phenomena are entirely impermanent—subject to flux, change, decay, and extinction—and he caused us to sever arrogance and negligence, leading us to cherish and delight in unsurpassed bodhi.
"Good son! When I beheld this brahmin, at that moment the summit of Mount Sumeru shook in six ways.

Having seen this omen, we devas were seized with extreme terror and a mind of weary detachment; we immediately resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and all vowed to seek after the wisdom of all-knowledge."
Furthermore, there were ten thousand great nāga kings, namely:

the nāga king Elāpattra, the nāga king Nanda, the nāga king Upananda, and others. In the midst of the sky, they spread great clouds of incense and rained down everywhere an immeasurable, timely rain of subtle sandalwood fragrance. Countless nāga maidens played celestial music and rained down exquisite celestial flowers and celestial perfumed water as an offering of respect, saying these words:
"O Son of Good Family!..."
When this brahmin performed the ascetic practice of scorching his body with five fires, the radiance of those flames illuminated my palace.

It caused all the nāgas to be freed from their fear of hot sands and their fear of the garuḍas; it extinguished their anger, bringing their bodies coolness and their minds freedom from defilement and turbidity, leaving them serene and at ease. Furthermore, he preached the Dharma to us according to our needs. Having heard the Dharma, we attained faith and understanding, came to loathe the nāga realm, and gave rise to a heart of utmost sincerity to repent and eliminate all karmic obstacles. Eventually, we resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and became ultimately established in the wisdom of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Furthermore, ten thousand yakṣa kings in the sky each offered various kinds of supreme and wonderful offerings with reverence to this brahmin and Sudhana, speaking these words: "O noble son!

"When this brahmin performs the 'five-fold scorching of the body,' it enables us and our retinues to give rise to a heart of compassion for all sentient beings; even all the rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others will likewise conceive a heart of compassion. Because of this compassionate mind, they will not afflict or harm any sentient beings but will instead bestow peace and happiness upon them. Each, together with their own retinue, will come to see me, and I, along with them, shall then go together to where the brahmin is."
At that time, the brahmin preached the Dharma for us, enabling all of us to attain peace and happiness of body and mind and to increase our majestic power;
furthermore, he caused immeasurable yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others to give rise to the mind of unsurpassed bodhi.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Eight;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation," there were ten thousand gandharva kings who, from within the void, spoke these words:
"O son of noble family!

When this brahmin performed the ascetic practice of scorching his body with the five fires, the radiance of those flames illuminated my palace and all its attendants, causing us all to experience inconceivable and immeasurable bliss.
Therefore, we have come to his place; this brahmin has preached the Dharma for us, enabling us to attain non-retrogression in our progress toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Furthermore, ten thousand asura kings emerged from the great ocean and, remaining in mid-air, extended their right knees, joined their palms in reverence, and spoke these words:
"O Son of Good Family!
When this Brahmin performed the austerity of being scorched by the five fires, all my asura palaces, the great earth, and the various mountains trembled;
the waves and surging billows of the great ocean boiled up, causing my retinue to lose their power, abandon their arrogance, leave behind all negligence, and cease their hearts of combat and injury.

Therefore, he came to the place of the brahmin and heard the Dharma from him; he forever abandoned flattery and deception, entered the profound *dharmakṣānti*, dwelt in *samādhi*, and accomplished the ten powers, remaining firm and unshakable.

Furthermore, there were ten thousand garuḍa kings, with the powerful and heroic Garuḍa King Mahābaladhara as their leader. In the midst of the sky, they manifested the form of vast youths—handsome in appearance, endowed with perfect physical marks—and proclaimed these words from the sky: "O noble son!

When this brahmin performed the austerity of the five fires, the radiance of his flames illuminated my palace; everything shook, causing us all to be terrified, to find no pleasure in our dwelling, and to give rise to a mind of weary detachment, whereby we came to his side.

At that time, the brahmin immediately preached the Dharma to us as was appropriate, enabling us to practice great loving-kindness and increase our great compassion; he caused us to be diligent and never abandon the yoke of virtue; he enabled us to draw sentient beings out from the five desires, inspired us to give rise to the mind of great bodhi, led us to enter the profound and pure dharma-realm, and enabled us to attain sharp and penetrating wisdom, skillful means, and the capacity to tame sentient beings.
Furthermore, ten thousand kinnara kings, in the midst of the sky, proclaimed these words: "O noble son!

When this brahmin performed the austerity of scorching his body with the five fires, a great wind arose from within the flames. It shook my palaces, gardens, ponds, precious tala trees, nets of jeweled bells, various jeweled silks, necklaces, flower garlands and ribbons, musical trees, exquisite jewel trees, and all musical instruments and furnishings. From them, there naturally issued forth the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the assembly of non-retrogressive bodhisattvas, the sound of the bodhisattva path that initiates great vows, and the sound of abiding in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
It says:
"In such-and-such a direction, such-and-such a realm, such-and-such a country, and such-and-such a place, there is a certain bodhisattva who has resolved upon bodhicitta and brought forth great vows;

in such-and-such a direction, such-and-such a realm, such-and-such a country, and such-and-such a place, there is a certain bodhisattva who practices asceticism, being able to renounce what is difficult to renounce—namely, body, life, and wealth."

In such-and-such a direction, such-and-such a realm, such-and-such a country, and such-and-such a place, there is a certain bodhisattva who, for the sake of swiftly perfecting the knowledge of all modes of knowledge, accumulates the sublime practices of bodhisattva merit, up to the ultimate gate of non-conditioned phenomena;

and in such-and-such a direction, such-and-such a realm, such-and-such a country, and such-and-such a place, there is a certain bodhisattva who proceeds to the site of enlightenment, sits beneath the Bodhi tree, subdues the hosts of Māra’s armies, and attains equal and right awakening.
Furthermore, in such-and-such a direction, realm, country, and place, a certain Tathāgata turns the great wheel of Dharma;
in such-and-such a direction, realm, country, and place, a certain Tathāgata, having completed his buddha-work, enters parinirvāṇa.

“Good son! Suppose there were someone who ground all the land of Jambudvīpa, along with its grasses, trees, and everything else that exists, into fine dust; one might be able to know the limit of the number of these particles. Yet, as for the sounds produced by the precious tārā trees, musical instruments, ornaments, and other such things within my palace—which proclaim the names of bodhisattvas, the names of Tathāgatas, the names of the Dharma, and the names of the Saṅgha, as well as the great vows they have made, the various practices they have cultivated, and the places where Buddhas and bodhisattvas roam, dwell, speak, and transform beings—no one is able to know their limit.”

“Good son! Because we have heard the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Bodhisattva Saṃgha, and the sound of the practices, dwellings, vows, and aspirations of the Bodhisattvas, we have given rise to great joy and have come to this place.”
Then, the brahmin immediately preached the Dharma for us as was appropriate, causing me and immeasurable other sentient beings to attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Furthermore, immeasurable sons of the gods from the desire realm manifested massive bodies, dwelt in the midst of the sky, and with various kinds of supreme and exquisite offerings, they paid respectful homage and spoke these words:
"O Son of Good Family!

When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, the radiance of those flames shone downward, illuminating Avīci and all the other hells, causing all the sufferings experienced therein to cease entirely.

Because we were encountered by this radiance, pure faith arose in our hearts; through that faith, the defilements of our sins were extinguished. Having passed away from that life, we were reborn among the devas. Out of a sense of shame and remorse, and out of gratitude, we have abandoned sensual pleasures and come to this place, revering and longing for him with never-ceasing devotion.
At that time, the brahmin preached the Dharma for me, enabling us and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, having heard these various teachings on the Dharma, the youth Sudhana was filled with great joy and leaped for immeasurable delight; he conceived a perception of the brahmin as a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).
Prostrating with his head at [the Bodhisattva’s] feet, he reverently joined his palms and spoke these words:
“I have conceived a lack of faith and harbored doubts toward the Great Sage, my spiritual friend; I only pray that the Noble One will grant me forgiveness for my transgression.”
Then the brāhmaṇa spoke these verses for Sudhana:
“If there are bodhisattvas who follow the instructions of spiritual friends,
they will be entirely free from doubt and fear, dwelling securely with an unshakable mind.”
