*The Chapter on Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation and the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra* At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded right mindfulness, followed along in contemplation of the dharma-gate of illusory wisdom attained by that king; he observed the king’s illusory liberation, contemplated the king’s illusory dharma-nature, made illusory vows, purified illusory dharmas, realized illusory karma, and accorded with the methods of illusory accomplishment. He gave rise to inconceivable illusory wisdom and purified the illusory nature and characteristics of the three periods of time;
through illusory wisdom, he manifested various kinds of illusory transformations.
Reflecting thus, he proceeded by stages, passing through human villages, towns, and cities;
whether reaching wildernesses, rocky valleys, treacherous mountains and rivers, or plains and marshlands, he sought him everywhere without weariness or indolence.
Thereafter, he proceeded until he reached the great city of Prabhāsa, where, by the side of its gate, he asked the people:
"What is the name of this city?
Which king rules over it?"
The people all replied,
"This is the city of Prabhāpurī, the dwelling place of King Mahāprabha.
At that time, the youth Sudhana leaped for joy and his mind was filled with pure aspiration.
With single-minded devotion and longing, he formed this thought:

"My spiritual friend is in this city; I must now certainly go in person to behold him and hear of the practices performed by the bodhisattvas, and hear of the gateways to liberation through which the bodhisattvas emerge."
They hear of the dharmas realized by all bodhisattvas;
they hear of the inconceivable merits of all bodhisattvas;
and they hear of the inconceivable masteries of all bodhisattvas.
They hear of the inconceivable equanimity of all bodhisattvas;
they hear of the inconceivable valor of all bodhisattvas;
they hear of the inconceivable realms of all bodhisattvas.
They hear of the inconceivable nature of reality of all bodhisattvas;
they hear of the inconceivable samādhis of all bodhisattvas;
and they hear of the inconceivable playful mastery of liberation of all bodhisattvas.
"I have heard of the inconceivable, vast, and pure [qualities] of the various bodhisattvas.
Having formed this thought, he entered the City of Sublime Light and surveyed it thoroughly.

He saw that this great city was adorned with various jewels, composed of the seven treasures—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, red pearls, musaragalva, and agate—and was surrounded on all sides by seven tiers of jeweled moats.
It is filled with water possessing the eight virtues; its bottom is strewn with golden sand, radiating brilliant light.
*Utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers cover its surface everywhere.
The water is crystal clear, becoming warm or cool according to the season.
White sandalwood mud settles as silt at its bottom;
the water follows the color of this mud, appearing like the hue of sandalwood.
The precious *tāla* trees were arranged in seven rows, their branches and leaves lush, verdant, and magnificent.
Sevenfold walls of vajra formed the enclosure, namely:

the Vajra Wall of Lion Radiance, the Vajra Wall of Insuperability, the Vajra Wall of Indestructibility, the Vajra Wall of Invincible Diligence, the Vajra Wall of Firm Non-attachment, the Vajra Wall of the Treasury of Celestial Garment Nets, and the Vajra Wall of Stainless Wondrous Colors.
Thus, these seven tiers encircle one another, all adorned with countless exquisite mani-jewels interspersed throughout.
The battlements are fashioned from Jambūnada gold and various other precious gems, while silver, lapis lazuli, red pearls, agate, crystal, and sea-treasure pearls serve as further embellishments.
The city was ten yojanas in length and breadth, with eight sides and eight gates opening on each face, all extensively adorned with the seven precious gems.
Its ground was made of deep-blue lapis lazuli, and various colored jewels were arrayed as ornaments throughout every location.
It was filled with all manner of rare and wondrous things, most delightful to behold.
Within the city were ten billion streets, and along the side of each street, exquisite jewels were arranged as adornments.
Passing along the paths traversed by Śakra, Lord of Devas, there were countless tens of billions of sentient beings dwelling within each and every path.
There were hundreds of thousands of vast palaces, each composed entirely of various precious jewels.
Furthermore, there were countless, inconceivable pavilions of Jambūnada gold, covered above by nets of indranīla lapis lazuli and maṇi jewels;
countless, inconceivable pavilions of white silver, covered above by nets of red pearl and maṇi jewels;
and countless, inconceivable pavilions of vaidūrya, covered above by nets of vast and wondrous treasury maṇi jewels.
Inconceivable and countless crystal pavilions were covered by nets of the sun-treasury maṇi-kings;
inconceivable and countless maṇi-jewel pavilions that illuminate the world with light were covered by nets of the auspicious light-treasury maṇi-kings;
inconceivable and countless pavilions of the sovereign indranīla maṇi-jewels were covered by nets of the exquisite light maṇi-kings.
There were countless, inconceivable palaces of the king of mani jewels from the ocean-treasury of sentient beings, covered above by nets of the king of mani jewels from the treasury of flaming light;
countless, inconceivable palaces of the king of vajra jewels, covered above by nets of the king of mani jewels from the banner of invincibility;
countless, inconceivable palaces of the king of sandalwood incense, covered above by nets of celestial *mandārava* flowers and great *mahāmandārava* flowers.
There were countless, inconceivable, and peerless pavilions of the king of fragrances, their surfaces covered by nets of various flowers.
There were likewise countless, inconceivable, and diverse pavilions of wondrous jewels, their surfaces covered by nets of various precious gems.
Each and every pavilion was surrounded on all sides by railings made of various jewels;
rows of precious tāla trees were arranged in succession, with paths demarcated by cords of jewels.
Each jeweled cord was hung with golden bells;

each golden bell was entwined with clusters of various precious flowers, as beautiful and variegated in color as a peacock’s tail. When stirred by the wind, they produced sounds that were pleasing to the ear.

That city further possessed incalculable nets of maṇi jewels, incalculable nets of precious bells, incalculable nets of celestial perfumes, incalculable nets of celestial flowers, and incalculable nets of precious images.

That city was further covered by incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) canopies of vajras, incalculable canopies of precious garments, incalculable canopies of precious parasols, incalculable canopies of precious banners, incalculable canopies of precious mountains, incalculable canopies of precious flower garlands, and incalculable canopies of precious pavilions; everywhere, precious parasols, standards, and banners were arrayed.
Within the city is a precious pond, filled to the brim with water of virtue;
its bed is spread with golden sand, whose radiance reflects both within and without;
and various exquisite celestial flowers bloom and flourish upon its surface.
Celestial jewel-birds float and play amidst them, emitting harmonious and elegant sounds that delight the human heart;
the tiered embankments of the pond are adorned with the seven treasures, such that even the precious ponds of Śakra cannot compare to them.

Within this city there was a tower named Treasury of the Sublime Dharma, adorned with countless varieties of multicolored jewels; its radiance shone forth, most supreme and peerless, such that sentient beings delighted in beholding it, never wearying of it, and King Mahāprabha constantly resided therein.

At that time, the youth Sudhana had no attachment whatsoever toward all such precious and wonderful things in that great city—the jeweled pavilions, jewel ponds, jewel moats, jewel trees, jewel walls, jewel canopies, jewel banners, jewel bells, and jewel nets—as well as the articles of daily use and enjoyment, even including the objects of the six sense-fields consisting of men and women;
he only deeply yearned for the garden of the True Dharma, contemplating exclusively the ultimate teaching with a focused mind, wishing and delighting to see a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).

Proceeding gradually forward and observing everywhere, he saw King Mahāprabha, not far from his dwelling, seated upon a vast and magnificently adorned lion throne made of wish-fulfilling maṇi-jewel lotus-treasury at the crossroads.
Its legs were made of deep-blue lapis lazuli jewels;
it had canopies of golden silk and nets of various precious gems.

It was adorned with Jambu-river gold cords interlaced as ornaments, with exquisite celestial garments serving as cushions and rugs; images of incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) wonderful jewels were spread out everywhere, adorning every location.
That king possessed the thirty-two marks of a great man and was adorned with the eighty secondary signs.
He was like a mountain of pure gold, his radiant complexion blazing intensely;
he was like the sun in a clear sky, his majestic light shining brilliantly.
Like the full moon at its zenith, those who behold it feel refreshing coolness, their hearts never wearying of it;
like the Brahmā King dwelling among the Brahmā assembly, his majestic virtue is preeminent;
and like the great ocean, he gathers the jewels of merit, immeasurable and boundless.
He is also like a great cloud that pervades the emptiness of the nature of phenomena, with the thunder of the Dharma resounding;
like the pure realm of space, manifesting the various constellations of the Dharma-gates;
and like the king of snow mountains, adorned by the groves of the marks and signs of excellence.
Like Mount Sumeru, its four colors appear universally within the ocean of the minds of sentient beings;
like a jeweled island, it is filled with various treasures of wisdom.

Before the royal throne, there were further immeasurable heaps of precious gems—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, pearls, mani-jewels, coral, amber, conch shells, and jade—as well as various jeweled garments, flower garlands, necklaces, and all kinds of food and drink, all of which were fully present.

Furthermore, he saw countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of precious chariots drawn by teams of four horses; hundreds of thousands of millions of celestial musical performances; hundreds of thousands of millions of celestial, exquisite incenses; hundreds of thousands of millions of medicinal decoctions for various ailments; countless cows with hooves and horns of golden color; and countless thousands of billions of beautiful women.

Her body was anointed with the finest sandalwood, and she was adorned with celestial garments and various necklaces; she was thoroughly proficient in all sixty-four arts and sciences, and she possessed complete knowledge of proper conduct and ritual etiquette.
In accordance with the inclinations of sentient beings,
he provided for them by establishing rest-houses and halls of righteousness in succession along the four crossroads of cities and villages, numbering two billion in total.
All manner of rare jewels, exquisite objects, and various foods and drinks were placed therein, filling it to capacity.
Along each and every path stood twenty billion great bodhisattvas, who bestowed these goods upon sentient beings so that none lacked for anything.

It is for the sake of gathering in all sentient beings; for the sake of inspiring love and respect in all sentient beings; for the sake of inspiring joy in all sentient beings; for the sake of inspiring exultation in all sentient beings; for the sake of purifying the right faith of all sentient beings; for the sake of making the minds of sentient beings cool and refreshing; for the sake of causing sentient beings to remove the fever of craving; for the sake of causing sentient beings to still their afflictions; for the sake of causing sentient beings to understand reality; for the sake of causing sentient beings to enter the knowledge of all modes; for the sake of causing sentient beings to abandon enemies; for the sake of causing sentient beings to leave behind all evils; for the sake of causing sentient beings to uproot false views; and for the sake of causing sentient beings to purify all karmas.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground at the feet of the king, circumambulated him countless times, and stood with palms joined, saying: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice or cultivate the bodhisattva path.
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me.
At that time, the king said:
"Good son! I have attained and fully purified the liberation door of the practice of the Bodhisattva’s Banner of Great Compassion."

"Good son! At the abodes of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis, even up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas, I have personally approached them to hear this Dharma, questioned and challenged them regarding it, reflected upon it in accordance with its truth, examined it with meticulous scrutiny, entered into it with pure realization, and cultivated it to adorn it."

"Good son! I rule as king by means of this Dharma; I issue commands by means of this Dharma; I gather and sustain beings by means of this Dharma; I follow along with the world by means of this Dharma; I carry out administration and transformation by means of this Dharma; I subdue sentient beings by means of this Dharma; I guide sentient beings by means of this Dharma; I have compassion for sentient beings by means of this Dharma; I comfort sentient beings by means of this Dharma; I transport sentient beings by means of this Dharma; I cause sentient beings to enter [the path] by means of this Dharma; I cause sentient beings to practice by means of this Dharma; I provide skillful means to sentient beings by means of this Dharma; I cause sentient beings to contemplate the ultimate true nature of all phenomena by means of this Dharma;
and I cause sentient beings to abide in great loving-kindness by means of this Dharma. Taking loving-kindness as primary, I am fully endowed with the power of loving-kindness."

In this way, they cause [beings] to abide in a mind of benefit, a mind of happiness, a mind of compassion, a mind of gathering them in, a mind of protecting sentient beings, a mind that never abandons them, a mind that tirelessly uproots the suffering of sentient beings, a mind that constantly undergoes suffering on behalf of all sentient beings, and a mind that establishes all sentient beings in peace and happiness.
To cause sentient beings to abandon all hindrances, obscurations, and fetters, so that they may attain mastery;
to cause sentient beings to achieve ultimate peace and happiness, so that they may attain mastery over all beings;
and to cause sentient beings to forever sever the spreading vines of craving that nourish the mind of birth and death.
To cause sentient beings to forever sever the mind of fetters that flow and pour forth in a continuous succession like a river;
to cause sentient beings to forever sever the mind of the habitual tendencies of afflictions;
and to cause sentient beings to abide in the mind of the quiescence of the dharma-nature.
It is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to forever bring to rest all unwholesome dharmas;
for the sake of causing all sentient beings to cut off the stream of birth and death and enter the stream of Dharma;
and for the sake of causing all sentient beings to enter the profound realm of reality with minds that never regress.

With the fire of wisdom, they burn the fuel of afflictions, forever severing rebirth in all five realms of existence; they fulfill the bodhisattva practices and advance toward omniscience. Their ocean-like mind is pure, free from all turbidity and agitation, and their power of faith is so firm that neither gods, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brahmins, humans, nor non-humans can shake it.
“Good son! Because I abide in this liberation door of the practice of the banner of great compassion, I am able to teach and transform the world with the True Dharma. Good son!”
All sentient beings within my land shall have no fear of me.
Good son! If there are any impoverished sentient beings who come to me, naked, hungry, and emaciated.

Whether they seek clothing, food and drink, or even all manner of necessary articles for their enjoyment, I open my treasuries to show them so that they may see and know them, and I address them, saying:

"In the past, you created various evil karmas of the ten unwholesome actions for the sake of these riches; because of this karma, you have become impoverished, naked, and lacking in sufficient food and clothing."
"I now bestow everything upon you; take it as you please.
Once you have satisfied yourselves, practice according to your strength: do not commit any evil, do not harm sentient beings, do not give rise to various views, and do not produce attachments."

"You who are poor and destitute, if you have anything you require, you should come to me, or to the twenty billion places of charitable halls and almshouses at the crossroads, where all manner of wealth and treasures are fully provided."
"Take as you wish; do not give rise to doubt or difficulty.
"Good son! All the sentient beings dwelling in this city of Wondrous Light are bodhisattvas who have resolved upon the Great Vehicle and practice the conduct of the Great Vehicle."

Giving rise to great compassion for all sentient beings, his mind was universally pure; according to their respective inclinations, what they saw differed. Some saw this city as small in scale, while others saw it as vast;

some saw its ground composed of earth and sand, while others saw it made of lapis lazuli and various mani-jewels; some saw its walls formed from heaped-up soil, while others saw them made of invincible diamond (*vajra*); some saw the ground uneven with highs and lows, while others saw it as level as the palm of a hand; some saw the houses built of wood and earth, while others saw palaces adorned with every kind of jewel, including towers, pavilions, steps, courtyards, windows, lattices, and doors—all of which were nothing but exquisite treasures.

“Good son! If there are sentient beings whose minds are pure, who have planted roots of goodness in the past, who have made offerings to the Buddhas, who have resolved their minds to pursue the path to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and who take all-knowledge as their refuge; and if they were previously gathered by me while I was practicing the bodhisattva conduct through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), then they shall see this city as complete with various jewels, pure and magnificently adorned, whereas others shall see it as defiled.”

“Good son! In this land, all sentient beings during the age of the five turbidities follow their habitual tendencies from past karma and delight in committing various evils. Out of compassion, I embrace their minds and desire to rescue and protect them.”
I enter the great samādhi gate that accords with the world, which is headed by the great compassion of bodhisattvas.
Son of good family!
When I enter this samādhi gate, all the fearful minds, harmful minds, hostile minds, and contentious minds of those sentient beings—all such minds—are completely extinguished of their own accord.

Why is this? Because entering into the samādhi that accords with the world, which is headed by the great compassion of bodhisattvas, is the inherent functional power of its fundamental nature; such is the nature of dharmas.
O son of good family!
"Wait but a moment, and you shall see for yourself.

At that time, King Mahāprabha entered this meditative absorption; the city, both inside and out, shook in six ways. The jeweled ground, jeweled walls, jeweled halls, jeweled palaces, towers, pavilions, balustrades, and windows—all such things as these—clashed and struck one another, all turning toward the king and assuming the appearance of bowing in respectful salutation, while all emitting wondrous sounds to praise the king’s virtue.
All the people within and without the city were simultaneously filled with joy and exultation; they all came before the king, prostrating themselves on the ground in homage.
Even the birds and beasts dwelling near the king’s presence looked upon one another, gave rise to hearts of compassion, and all together paid respectful obeisance before the king.
All mountains, plains, grasses, and trees turned without exception, all facing the king as if paying him reverential homage.
Ponds, pools, springs, wells, rivers, and seas all surged and overflowed, flowing toward the presence of the king;
ten thousand dragon kings raised great clouds of fragrance, with thunder rolling and lightning flashing, sprinkling a fine rain of incense.
Furthermore, there were ten thousand kings of the six heavens of desire—

namely, the Kings of the Four Great Heavens, the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the King of the Yāma Heaven, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven— with these kings as their leaders, who performed various musical performances in the midst of the void.
Countless celestial maidens sang songs of praise;

countless clouds of celestial jewel flowers, countless clouds of celestial jewel incense, countless clouds of celestial jewel garlands, countless clouds of celestial powdered incense, countless clouds of celestial jewel robes, countless clouds of celestial jewel parasols, countless clouds of celestial jewel banners, and countless clouds of celestial jewel pennants filled the entirety of space as an adornment, making offerings to the King.
Furthermore, there was the great elephant king Elāpattra, who, by his power of mastery, arrayed in the midst of space incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) great jewel lotuses;

he hung down incalculable celestial jewel necklaces, incalculable precious silk ribbons, incalculable precious ornaments, incalculable precious garments, incalculable precious garlands, incalculable precious flowers, incalculable precious incenses, incalculable burning incenses, and incalculable unguents—various wonderful and marvelous things used as adornments.
Countless celestial maidens produced exquisite sounds, singing and offering praises.

Within Jambudvīpa, there were also countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rākṣasa kings, yakṣa kings, kumbhāṇḍa kings, piśāca kings, and various ghost kings, some dwelling on land, some in the void, some among the mountains, and some in the great ocean;

all such beings who drank blood, ate flesh, and harmed sentient creatures, now gave rise to hearts of compassion, vowing to act for their benefit, clearly recognizing the future life and ceasing to commit any evil. With reverence and palms joined, they prostrated themselves before the King.
Fear shall not arise; body and mind will be tranquil, and all shall attain immeasurable, vast peace and happiness.

Just as it is here, so it shall be for the other three continents of Jambudvīpa, throughout the trichiliocosm, and even across hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds in the ten directions—all the venomous and evil sentient beings therein shall likewise experience this.
All of this is headed by the great compassion of the Bodhisattva; such is the power of the samādhi-dharmaparyāya that accords with the world.
At that time, King Mahāprabha arose from samādhi and addressed Sudhana, saying: "O noble son!

I have only attained this bodhisattva liberation door of the "Samādhi of the Great Compassion Banner Practice that Accords with the World. As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they are like a high canopy, because their compassionate mind universally shelters all sentient beings;
they are like a full moon, because they provide impartial protection without discrimination;
they are like a practitioner, because they practice equally in the lower, middle, and superior ways.
They are like the great earth, for they are able to sustain all sentient beings with a heart of loving-kindness;
they are like the full moon, for the radiance of their merit appears equally throughout all worlds;
they are like the pure solar orb, for they illuminate all objects of knowledge with the light of wisdom.
They are bright lamps for the world, for they can shatter the various darknesses of sentient beings;
they are water-purifying jewels, for they can clear away the turbidity of sentient beings' flattery and deception;
they are wish-fulfilling gems, for they can fulfill the aspirations in the hearts of sentient beings.
Because he acts as a fierce and swift wind to sustain sentient beings, the palaces of samādhi, and the great city of the Dharma of the knowledge of all-knowledge;

how then could I know his conduct, describe his virtues, weigh that mountain of merit, gaze upon those stars of his qualities, observe that wind-wheel of his great vows, calculate the power of his equality of dharmas, arouse that mind of great cultivation, manifest that ocean of great adornments, elucidate those gateways of Samantabhadra’s practice, enter deeply into those caves of samādhi, praise that cloud of great compassion, or pour down that rain of the nectar-like Dharma?
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a royal capital named Anvaya;
there is an upāsikā named Acalā."
"Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the king's feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.

At that time, the youth Sudhana left the city of Suprabha and traveled along the road, reflecting with right mindfulness upon the instructions of King Mahāprabha; he called to mind the practice of the Bodhisattva’s Banner of Great Compassion, contemplated the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Accordance with the World, universally beheld that inconceivable, pure body of the Bodhisattva, universally recollected that inconceivable lion throne of wondrous jewels, increased that inconceivable sovereign power of the merit of great vows, strengthened that inconceivable wisdom for maturing sentient beings, observed that inconceivable and unique majesty of enjoyment, recollected those inconceivable distinctions of supernormal powers, contemplated that inconceivable assembly of the pure multitude, and discerned those inconceivable deeds performed by the Bodhisattva.

With clear recollection, in accordance with faith and understanding, one gives rise to a heart of joy, a heart of purity, a heart of sharpness, a heart of delight, a heart of celebration, a heart of exultation, a heart free from distraction, a heart of luminous illumination, a heart of firmness, a heart of vastness, and a heart of inexhaustibility.
Reflecting thus, he wept with flowing tears.
He thought: "A spiritual friend is truly rare; they are difficult to encounter and difficult to hear of.
A spiritual friend is my mountain of jewels, from which all treasures of merit and virtue arise."

It is able to universally purify all bodhisattva practices, fulfill all pure mindfulness of a bodhisattva, purify the wheel of a bodhisattva’s dhāraṇīs, manifest the light of a bodhisattva’s samādhis, cultivate the realm of a bodhisattva’s vision of Buddhas, universally rain down the Dharma-rain of all Buddhas, reveal the inconceivable wisdom of the Tathāgata, display all gateways of bodhisattva vows, and cause the roots and sprouts of all bodhisattvas to grow.
Again, he thought:
"A virtuous friend can rescue and protect me, preventing me from falling into any of the evil realms;
a virtuous friend can guide me, enabling me to enter the impartial wisdom of the Buddhas."
A spiritual friend can illuminate me, enabling me to discern all paths, whether level or perilous;
a spiritual friend can provide instruction to me, enabling me to comprehend the profound mysteries of the Mahāyāna;
a spiritual friend can inspire me, enabling me to swiftly enter into the various practices of Samantabhadra.
A spiritual friend can awaken me, enabling me to reach the city of omniscience swiftly;
a spiritual friend can instruct and admonish me, leading me to enter the great ocean of the Dharma-realm;
a spiritual friend can encourage and entice me, allowing me to behold universally the ocean of dharmas of the three periods of time.
A spiritual friend can instruct me, enabling me to assemble with the assembly of holy ones;
a spiritual friend can cause me to grow, enabling me to give birth to all pure dharmas.
"Reflecting that a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) is able to benefit sentient beings in such a way," Sudhana thought to himself;
his eyes filled with tears as that Bodhisattva, who constantly guards and awakens him, followed him like a shadow follows a form.
A celestial messenger of the Tathāgata spoke from the midst of the sky, saying:
"O son of good family!
Those who follow the instructions of spiritual friends bring joy to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones."
Those who comply with the words of spiritual friends will draw near to the ground of omniscience;
those who are able to act according to the conduct of spiritual friends without doubt in their hearts will constantly encounter all virtuous friends;
and those who resolve their minds, vowing never to be separated from spiritual friends, will attain the fullness of all profound and supreme benefits.
"Good son! You should go to the royal capital of Anvaya, where you will surely meet the great spiritual friend, the laywoman Acalā, and from her inquire about the practices of all bodhisattvas."

At that time, the youth Sudhana arose from the light of wisdom of that samādhi and, traveling by stages, arrived at the city of Supratiṣṭhita, where he inquired everywhere as to the whereabouts of the laywoman Acalā. "Where is she now? he asked.
Upon encountering that group of people, they all pointed it out to him, saying: "Good son!
The laywoman Acalā is a maiden who attends upon her parents in her own home; surrounded on all sides by her relatives and immeasurable people, she is expounding the sublime Dharma."
Having heard this, Sudhana’s heart was filled with joy; he conceived a mind of tranquility and a mind of affectionate reverence, as if seeing his own parents.
He thought, "Now my aspirations are fulfilled."
He immediately went to where the laywoman Acalā was; arriving at the gate of her residence, he stood there and observed it.
He entered the house and saw that the halls and chambers were subtle, wondrous, pure, and adorned with various jewels.
A golden light shone everywhere, illuminating all.
When this light touched Sudhana’s body, he immediately attained five hundred sublime gates of samādhi.
That is to say:
the gate of the samādhi called Banner of Sovereignty over All Peace and Bliss;
the gate of the samādhi called Comprehending the Aspect of Universal Quiescence;
The samādhi door of being far removed from all worldly things;
the samādhi door of the universal eye’s relinquishing and attaining;
the samādhi door of the Tathāgatagarbha;
He attained five hundred such gates of samādhi.
Because he had attained these gates of samādhi, his body and mind became supple like a seven-day-old embryo, subtle, wondrous, and tranquil, such that nothing in the world could surpass it.
Furthermore, he smelled a wondrous fragrance such as no deva, nāga, gandharva, human, or non-human could possess.
He immediately went forward, joined his palms in reverence, and observed with single-minded concentration.

Beholding her form and color, she was upright and exquisitely beautiful; among all women in the worlds of the ten directions, none could equal her, let alone surpass her—save only for the Tathāgata and all the consecrated Bodhisattvas.
His body is preeminent, and his mouth emits a wondrous fragrance.
His palace is magnificently adorned, and he is surrounded by attendants; his majestic radiance is blazing and pure, untainted and peerless—how could there be anyone who surpasses him?
Among all sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions, there is none who gives rise to a mind of defiled attachment toward this upāsikā.
If any sentient being should even briefly behold her, all their afflictions will naturally be extinguished.
For example, just as the hundred thousand Great Brahma Kings certainly do not give rise to the afflictions of the desire realm,
so too it is for those who see this upāsikā— they likewise do not give rise to afflictions.
Sentient beings of the ten directions who behold this woman feel joy, love, and reverence, their hearts never wearying of her; this is true for all except those who possess great wisdom.
At that time, the youth Sudhana bowed his body, joined his palms, gazed upon her with reverence, and contemplated her with right mindfulness.
Beholding this woman, her body is autonomous and inconceivable.
Her physical form, features, and countenance are without equal in the world;
her radiance is so penetrating that no object can obstruct it.
Universally for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, he brings about great benefit without end.
From the pores of his body, wondrous fragrances constantly emanate; his retinue is boundless, and his palaces are supreme.
His merit is profound and vast, inconceivable, such that none can exhaustively fathom it or know its limits.
Giving rise to a heart of joy, he praised him with these verses:
“You always maintain the pure precepts, Universally practicing the stainless patience of a bodhisattva;
Firmly advancing and immovable like a vajra, Your wondrous fruit transcends the world, beyond all comparison.”
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had spoken these verses, he said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path."
"I have heard that the Noble One is skilled at providing instruction; I pray that you will speak for me.
Then, the laywoman Acalā, with gentle words, lovely words, and words of compassion, comforted Sudhana and addressed him, saying: "Excellent! [Continue as in the source text]."
Excellent! Son of good family,
you have already been able to resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

"Good son! I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door of the treasury of wisdom that is difficult to subdue; I have attained the bodhisattva door of firm upholding of vows and practices; I have attained the bodhisattva door of the dhāraṇī of the ground of equality of all phenomena; I have attained the bodhisattva door of eloquence illuminated by the light of wisdom regarding all phenomena; and I have attained the bodhisattva door of the samādhi-adornment of a mind that never tires in seeking all phenomena."
Sudhana the youth said: "Noble One!

What is the scope of the liberation door of the treasury of wisdom that is difficult for Bodhisattvas to overcome, and even the samādhi door of adornment through a mind that never tires in its quest for the Dharma?"
He replied: "Good son! This place is profound, difficult to know, and difficult to believe."
Sudhana said: "I only pray that the Holy One, sustained by the Buddha's spiritual power, will explain this for me.

By the power of the Holy One as my spiritual friend, I shall be able to believe, receive, understand, know, penetrate deeply, practice in accordance with it, observe it with clarity, recollect and cultivate it, remain free from all conceptual discrimination, and reach ultimate equality."
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirteen;

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation," at that time,
the laywoman Acalā addressed the youth Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!
I recall that in the past, during the stainless Radiance eon (*vimalaprabhā-kalpa*), there was a Buddha named Long Arms (*dīrghabāhu*) whose ten titles were complete.
At that time, there was a king named Lightning Bestower (*vidyudatta*) who had only one daughter; she was none other than myself.

During that night, when the music had ceased and my parents, brothers, and five hundred maidens were all fast asleep, I was gazing up at the stars from atop the tower. In the midst of the void, I beheld that Tathāgata, like a king of jewel mountains, immeasurable and boundless, surrounded by devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, as well as an inconceivable multitude of Bodhisattvas. From the Buddha’s body, a vast net of great light rays was universally emitted, pervading the ten directions without obstruction;
from every pore of the Buddha’s body, wondrous fragrances issued forth.
Upon smelling this fragrance, my body became supple and my heart gave rise to joy.
Thereupon, descending from the tower, he joined his palms in reverence and prostrated himself before the Buddha;
he gazed intently at that Buddha, yet could not see the crown of his head,
nor could he discern the limits of his body when looking to its left and right.
I contemplated the primary marks and secondary signs of that Buddha without ever becoming weary or satisfied.
Son of good family!
At that time, I thought to myself in secret:
"What karma did this Buddha, the World-Honored One, perform to obtain such a supreme and wondrous body?

Why are his marks and signs so perfectly complete, his radiance so fully endowed, his retinue so accomplished, and his palace so adorned? Why are his merit and wisdom, his dhāraṇīs and samādhis, his supernormal powers and eloquence, all so inconceivable?"
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, knowing my thoughts, addressed me, saying:
'You should give rise to an indestructible resolve and sever all afflictions;'"
You should give rise to an invincible mind to shatter all false attachments;
you should give rise to a fearless mind to enter the profound Dharma gates;
you should give rise to an unshakable mind to uproot the suffering of birth and death.
You should give rise to a mind free from delusion, taking birth throughout all realms of existence;
you should give rise to a mind free from weariness, seeking to behold all Buddhas without ceasing;
you should give rise to a mind free from contentment, receiving the rain of Dharma from all Tathāgatas.
You should give rise to a mind of right reflection that universally illumines the light of all Buddha-dharmas;
you should give rise to a mind of great upholding that universally turns the wheel of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
you should give rise to a mind of extensive circulation that bestows the treasure of the Dharma upon sentient beings according to their inclinations.
"Good son! From that Buddha, the Truly Perfectly Enlightened One, I heard such a Dharma;
accordingly, I sought after all-knowledge with a mind that never regressed."

They seek the ten powers of a Buddha; they seek the eloquence of a Buddha; they seek the radiance of a Buddha; they seek the form-body of a Buddha; they seek the primary and secondary marks of a Buddha; they seek the assemblies of a Buddha; they seek the pure buddha-field of a Buddha; they seek the majestic deportment of a Buddha; and they seek the lifespan of a Buddha.
Having generated this mind, they take deep delight in it, like one parched with thirst longing for water;
their mind is as firm and solid as a diamond (vajra),
incapable of being destroyed by any afflictions or by those of the two vehicles.

“Good son! Since I first gave rise to this mind, I recall that throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa, I have never once given rise to a single thought of desire, much less engaged in the act itself.”
Throughout all those kalpas, even toward one's own kinsmen who have committed faults, he did not give rise to a single thought of anger, much less toward other sentient beings who were without fault.
Throughout those eons, he did not give rise to the view of a self regarding his own body, much less conceive of possessions regarding external requisites.

Throughout those eons—at the time of death, at the time of birth, and during the entering, abiding, and emerging from the womb, even within dreams—he never became deluded as to give rise to the notion of a sentient being or an indeterminate mind, much less at other times.
Throughout those kalpas, even in dreams, he has never forgotten the sight of a single Buddha, let alone what is seen by the ten eyes of a bodhisattva.

Throughout those kalpas, he has upheld all the True Dharma of the Tathāgatas without ever forgetting a single word or phrase; he has not even forgotten any mundane expressions, let alone the wondrous Dharma proclaimed from within the treasury of the Tathāgata’s speech.

Throughout all those eons, regarding even a single word or a single phrase from the ocean of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas that he had received and upheld, there was nothing he did not contemplate and examine according to principle; indeed, he constantly contemplated, examined, and realized even all mundane phenomena, let alone the Tathāgata’s true, ultimate Dharma.

Throughout those eons, they upheld the ocean of all Tathāgatas' teachings; there was not a single teaching among them in which they did not attain samādhi, and it was likewise for every single art, craft, and skillful technique of the world.

Throughout those eons, they maintained the wheel of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas; in whatever they maintained, they never abandoned a single word or phrase, nor was there any error, and they never gave rise to worldly wisdom, except for the purpose of taming sentient beings.
Throughout those eons, they beheld oceans of Buddhas; there was not a single Buddha from whom they failed to achieve pure great vows, and this was likewise true even for all the manifested Buddhas.
Throughout those kalpas, I have witnessed all the bodhisattvas practicing sublime conduct; there was not a single practice that I did not master and purify.

Among the sentient beings I encountered during those kalpas, there was not a single being whom I did not exhort to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; I never once exhorted a single sentient being, even for a single thought-moment, to give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha.

Throughout all those kalpas, regarding every Dharma heard in the presence of all Buddhas—even down to a single word or a single phrase—he did not give rise to doubt, did not give rise to dualistic thoughts, did not give rise to discriminative thoughts, did not give rise to diverse thoughts, did not give rise to thoughts of attachment, did not give rise to thoughts of high and low, did not give rise to thoughts of superior and inferior, and did not give rise to thoughts of love or hatred; indeed, not even for a single thought-moment did he give rise to such thoughts.
"Good son! Since that time, I have always been able to draw near to all the Buddhas I have seen, never being separated from them;
I have always seen bodhisattvas, never being separated from them."
They constantly behold true and great spiritual friends and never abandon them;
they constantly hear the pure great vows of all Buddhas and never abandon them;
they constantly hear the wondrous practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas and never abandon them.
They constantly hear the gateways to the bodhisattva pāramitās and never abandon them;
they constantly hear the gateways to the light of wisdom of the bodhisattva stages and never abandon them;
they constantly hear the gateways to the inexhaustible treasury of bodhisattva dhāraṇīs and samādhis and never abandon them.
I have constantly heard that Bodhisattvas universally enter the gate of the infinite network of worlds without ever abandoning it;
I have constantly heard that Bodhisattvas universally enter the gate of the infinite realms of sentient beings without ever abandoning it;
I have constantly heard that Bodhisattvas eliminate the afflictions of all sentient beings with the light of wisdom without ever abandoning it.
I have constantly heard that Bodhisattvas cultivate the roots of goodness in all sentient beings and never abandon them;
I have constantly heard that Bodhisattvas are able to manifest their bodies throughout the entire Dharma-realm in accordance with sentient beings and never abandon them;
I have constantly heard that Bodhisattvas awaken all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm through wondrous speech and sounds and never abandon them.
"Good son! I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door of the treasury of wisdom that is difficult to subdue;
I have attained the bodhisattva samādhi door of the adornment of seeking all dharmas with a mind free from weariness."
I have attained the bodhisattva gateway of firm upholding of vows and practices;
I have attained the bodhisattva gateway of the dhāraṇī of the stage of equality of all phenomena;
I have attained the bodhisattva gateway of eloquence illuminated by the light of wisdom regarding all phenomena.
"I am now manifesting inconceivable and sovereign spiritual transformations; do you wish to see them?
Sudhana replied, "Yes!"
"I wish to see her.

At that time, the laywoman Acalā did not rise from her lion throne of the dragon-treasury, yet she entered the bodhisattva liberation door of the treasury of invincible wisdom; the samādhi door of the adornment of a mind that never tires in seeking all dharmas; the samādhi door of the adornment of non-empty fulfillment; and the samādhi door of the manifestation of the wheel of the ten powers' knowledge. She entered ten billion such samādhi doors.
As she entered these samādhi doors, worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions shook in six ways.
Each and every world is entirely pure, composed of lapis lazuli;
within each world are ten billion sets of four continents (*cāturdvīpaka*);

in each set of four continents there is a Tathāgata who either ascends to Tuṣita Heaven, or descends to be born, enters the womb, is first born, leaves home, practices austerities, dwells beneath the tree of enlightenment, manifests the subduing of Māra, demonstrates the realization of Bodhi, accepts the invitation of the Brahmā King, proceeds to Vārāṇasī to turn the wheel of the Four Truths, or returns from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to Jambudvīpa, descending from heaven via the three jeweled stairways.
At times he manifests himself throughout the six great cities, displaying great supernatural powers to subdue all non-Buddhists;
at times he manifests himself dwelling by the Monkey Pond in the city of Vaiśālī, where he first established the Vinaya discipline;
and at times he manifests himself at the Great City of Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak and other sites, expounding the various gates of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Even unto manifesting in the *śāla* groves of Kuśinagara to demonstrate *parinirvāṇa*;
thus all such Buddha-activities are performed, pervading the pure worlds throughout the ten directions;

each and every Tathāgata emits a web of light that encompasses the entire *dharmadhātu*, surrounded by pure assemblies at the sites of enlightenment, turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma and awakening all classes of beings.
Then, the laywoman Acalā arose from samādhi and said to Sudhana:
"Son of good family, do you see this?"
"Did you hear this?
Do you understand this? Sudhana replied:
"Yes! I have already seen, heard, and understood it all," said the upāsikā.

“Good son! I have attained only this bodhisattva’s gate of firm upholding of great vows through practice; the gate of the light of wisdom of the samādhi adorned by a mind that seeks all dharmas without weariness; the gate of liberation of the treasury of wisdom difficult to subdue; the gate of the dhāraṇī of the level of equality of all dharmas; and the gate of eloquence illuminated by the light of wisdom regarding all dharmas.

For the sake of all sentient beings, I employ skillful means and, with wondrous speech and sounds, universally proclaim the subtle and wonderful Dharma everywhere to bring joy to all, yet I am not like those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

Like the *uśīra* bird, which travels through the void without obstruction, able to enter the great ocean of all sentient beings with sovereign profundity and universal observation, it seizes those whose roots of goodness have matured and places them on the shore of Bodhi;
or like a merchant who enters the great jewel-island of omniscience to seek the precious jewels of the Tathāgata’s ten powers of wisdom;
or like a fisherman endowed with strength who, holding the net of the True Dharma, enters the sea of birth and death to filter out sentient beings.
Just as the Asura King can thoroughly stir the great city of the triple world and the ocean of all afflictions, causing all sentient beings to attain ultimate tranquility;
and just as the solar disc appears in the void, illuminating the mud of craving and causing it to dry up;
and just as the full moon appears in the void, causing the lotus-flowers of the minds of those ready for conversion to bloom.

It is like the great earth, which is universally equal; immeasurable sentient beings dwell upon it and constantly tread upon it, yet its mind is free from discrimination as it nurtures the roots and sprouts of all wholesome dharmas.
It is like a great wind that encounters no obstruction wherever it blows, able to uproot the great trees of all views and to shatter and disperse the gardens of birth and death.
It is like a wheel-turning monarch traveling through the world, gathering in all sentient beings by means of the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*).
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct? Good son,
to the south of here there is a great city named Tosalī.
Among them is a renunciant non-Buddhist practitioner named Viśvāmitra;
go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the laywoman Acalā, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.

At that time, after the youth Sudhana had heard the Dharma from the laywoman Acalā, he focused his mind on remembering and upholding all her instructions, all her guidance, all her expositions, and all her praises. He followed in accordance with every light he encountered, giving rise to a sense of rare wonder; he contemplated and examined them, practicing them universally, and maintained right mindfulness with a single-minded focus.

Gradually proceeding forward, he passed through kingdoms, cities, villages, camps, and settlements, until finally reaching the city of Dhanyākara. At sunset, he entered that city, searching everywhere—through the marketplaces, shops, neighborhoods, and crossroads—for the wandering mendicant Sarvagāmin, observing from high and prominent places.
To the northeast of that city was a great mountain named Mañjuśrī.

During the middle of the night, Sudhana saw a great radiance upon its summit; its peaks rose steeply and its rocky cliffs formed a grand arch. The grasses, trees, flowers, and forests were all brilliantly reflected, illuminating the city dwellers like the rising sun. Having witnessed this, he was filled with great joy and thought to himself:
"I shall surely behold a spiritual friend here."
He then departed from the city, observing with right mindfulness as he ascended that mountain;

standing there in contemplation, he gazed afar and beheld the non-Buddhist practitioner walking slowly in meditation upon a level spot on the mountain. His physical form was perfect, his majestic radiance shone forth, and the auspicious flames of his merit were more brilliant than a blazing fire. He was surrounded by ten thousand Brahmā assemblies, a splendor that even the Great Brahmā King could not equal.
Sudhana immediately approached him, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood before him with palms joined, saying:

“Noble One! I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct or how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me.”
The Universal Wandering One replied:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! It is well that you have been able to resolve upon the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and further inquire about the practices of all bodhisattvas. Noble son!"

I have already established myself in the state that reaches all places, following the universally pervasive conduct of a bodhisattva; I have accomplished the samādhi-door of the universal observation of all worlds as being equally without obstruction; I have accomplished the supernormal powers that are non-reliant and non-conditioned; I have accomplished the Prajñāpāramitā at the limit of the universal Dharma-realm; and thus, the fulfillment of all such wisdom-lights follows my practice.

Good son! I am able to universally [perceive] among all classes of sentient beings throughout all the various locations, forms, colors, appearances, modes of death and birth, types of conduct and understanding, and varieties of inclinations and beliefs within all realms of existence; namely:
The realms of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, hell-beings, animals, the realm of Yama, humans, non-humans, and all such classes of beings.

Whether they abide in various views, believe in the Two Vehicles, or take delight in the path of the Mahāyāna—I, through various skillful means, various wisdoms, various methods of teaching, and various ways of taming, bring equal benefit to all such sentient beings so that they may all attain fulfillment;
that is to say:
for some, I expound upon the various arts and crafts of the world to benefit sentient beings.
For some, he expounds the wisdom of the *dhāraṇī* that is as firm as a diamond and capable of destroying ignorance;
for others, he expounds the skillful means of the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) to gather all sentient beings, causing them to draw near to the path of omniscience;
and for others, he expounds the various *pāramitās*, revealing and praising them so that they may dedicate their merit toward the stage of omniscience.
In some cases, they praise the arousal of the bodhicitta so that beings do not lose their resolve for the unsurpassed path;
in some cases, they extol the practices of the bodhisattvas so that beings may fulfill their vows to purify buddha-fields and deliver sentient beings;

and in some cases, they expound upon how the commission of various evil karmas leads to the reception of manifold bitter retributions such as those in the hells, so that beings develop a profound sense of weary detachment toward unwholesome deeds.
For some, they expound upon making offerings to all Buddhas and planting roots of goodness, so that they may certainly obtain the fruit of omniscience and cause them to give rise to a heart of joy;
for others, they praise and speak of all the merits of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, causing them to delight in the Buddha-body and seek omniscience;
for yet others, they praise and speak of the majestic power of the Buddhas, causing them to aspire to and delight in the indestructible body of a Buddha.
Or I may praise and describe the sovereign body of the Buddha, so as to cause them to seek the Tathāgata’s body of great majesty and virtue that cannot be eclipsed by anything.
Son of good family!

Furthermore, throughout every location and among every class of people in this city of Tuṣāra—whether men or women, within all such multitudes—I employ skillful means to manifest in forms identical to theirs, and according to what is appropriate for each, I transform my speech and sounds to preach the Dharma through various distinctions.
All sentient beings are unable to know who I am or from where I have come;
I only cause those who hear me to practice according to the truth and realize the ultimate meaning.
"Good son! Just as you benefit sentient beings in this city, so too shall you benefit all sentient beings dwelling in every city, town, and village throughout Jambudvīpa."
"Good son! Within Jambudvīpa, the ninety-six schools each give rise to divergent views and develop attachments; I have skillfully subdued them all therein, causing them to abandon all such views."
As it is in all dwelling places throughout Jambudvīpa, so it is in the other three continents;

as it is in the four continents, so it is in the small thousand-world systems, the intermediate thousand-world systems, and the great trichiliocosm—indeed, in all dwelling places of sentient beings therein.

Just as it is in this great trichiliocosm, so it is in all dwelling places within the infinite worlds of the ten directions. For the ocean of all classes of sentient beings therein, I manifest various skillful means, various Dharma gates, various principles, various right practices, and various activities; I manifest various form-bodies, various physical forms, and various voices and sounds to preach the Dharma for them, according to the inclinations of their minds.
May all those sentient beings obtain benefit. Good son!
I know only this Bodhisattva practice of "Pervasive Following Everywhere," as practiced by all Bodhisattvas.
The Mahāsattva attains a body that is indistinguishable from that of sentient beings and acquires samādhis equal in number to all sentient beings.
By means of transformation bodies, he enters universally into all realms of existence, manifesting birth in every location.
His pure radiance shines throughout the entire Dharma-realm; those who behold it are all benefited without exception. By...
May they dwell unimpeded throughout all kalpas, attaining peerless practices like those of Indra’s net, constantly and diligently benefiting all sentient beings;
though they always cohabit with immeasurable defilements and impurities, they remain untainted by them;
being impartial toward all beings of the three periods of time, they universally illuminate them with the wisdom of non-self.
Having increased their roots of goodness through the treasury of great compassion,
how could I possibly know or describe their pure wisdom and conduct? Good son!

To the south of here is a land named Vast; there is a village there that takes its name from the country. In it dwells an incense merchant named Fully Endowed with Utpala Flowers. Go to him and ask: how should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Samantagāmin, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave.

At that time, following the instructions of his spiritual friend, Sudhana disregarded his own body and life; he was not attached to wealth and treasures, did not indulge in the five desires, had no longing for his kinsmen, and held no weight for royal rank. He dwelt in sovereign peace and happiness, aspiring only to transform and guide all sentient beings so that they might reach maturity;
he aspired only to adorn the Buddha-fields so that they might be universally pure.
I only wish that in making offerings to all Tathāgatas, my mind may never grow weary;
I only wish that I may realize and know the true nature of all phenomena, manifesting it with perfect clarity;
and I only wish that I may accord with the profound realm of reality (dharmadhātu), pervading it universally and without obstruction.
May I vow to cultivate and accumulate the great ocean of all bodhisattva merits, never regressing;
may I vow to constantly practice the bodhisattva deeds throughout all kalpas;
may I vow to universally enter the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
I only pray that you will enter a single gate of samādhi and universally manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all gates of samādhi;
I only pray that you will, within a single wheel of Dharma of the Buddha, universally uphold the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
I only pray that you will, within a single pore of the Buddha, behold all Buddhas with a mind never weary or satiated.
I only pray that I may realize the radiance of wisdom and be able to uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas;
I seek exclusively these merits possessed by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at the country of Vistīrṇa and its villages, where he searched everywhere for the elder who sold incense.
Having found him, he approached, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood with palms joined, saying: "Noble One!"

I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to seek the equal wisdom of all Buddhas, desiring to fulfill the immeasurable great vows of all Buddhas, desiring to purify the most excellent form-bodies of all Buddhas, desiring to behold the pure dharma-bodies of all Buddhas, desiring to know the vast wisdom-bodies of all Buddhas, desiring to purify and cultivate all bodhisattva practices, desiring to illuminate all bodhisattva samādhis, desiring to abide securely in all bodhisattva dhāraṇīs, desiring to make firm all bodhisattva merits, desiring to eliminate all obstacles whatsoever, and desiring to travel through all worlds in the ten directions; yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct.
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path so as to be able to give rise to all-knowledge?
The elder replied, "Excellent!"
Excellent! Son of good family,
you are indeed able to give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Good son! I am skilled in discerning all fragrances; namely:
They know the methods for compounding all perfumes, all incenses, all ointments, and all powdered fragrances;
they also know the origins from which all such kings of fragrance emerge;
furthermore, they skillfully understand all the various scents belonging to devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.

Furthermore, they skillfully understand the incenses that treat all illnesses, the incenses that sever all evils, the incenses that remove sorrow and affliction, the incenses that give rise to passionate attachment, the incenses that increase afflictions, the incenses that extinguish afflictions, the incenses that cause one to produce delight and attachment toward the conditioned, the incenses that cause one to produce weary detachment toward the conditioned, the incenses that abandon all pride and arrogance, the incenses that bring joy upon hearing the Dharma, the incenses that inspire the mind to recollect the Buddha, the incenses for realizing and understanding the Dharma-gates, the incenses enjoyed by the noble ones, the various distinct incenses of all bodhisattvas, and the incenses of all the bodhisattva stages.

Regarding such fragrances as these, as well as their methods of compounding, their forms and characteristics, their arising, their manifestation and accomplishment, their purity and tranquility, their spheres of skillful means, their majestic powers and functional applications, their fundamental sources, and their variations according to place and according to the different types of beings—all such things I fully understand.
"Good son! Among humans there is a fragrance called Dragon Treasury (Nāgagarbha), which is produced by the fighting of dragons.

If one pellet, as large as a sesame seed, is burned, it can immediately give rise to great clouds of fragrant flames, like the net of Indra, completely covering the royal capital, and for seven days it rains down fine fragrant rain."

If it touches the body, the body immediately becomes golden in color; if it touches clothing, all such garments are transformed into the color of *kusuma* flowers. If, carried by the wind, it enters a palace, all the terraces, halls, pavilions, and chambers are likewise transformed into the color of *kusuma* flowers.

Any sentient beings who smell it will, for seven days and seven nights, be filled with joy; their bodies and minds will experience happiness, the fever of delusion will be cooled, and they will be free from all diseases and afflictions. They will not harm one another, will be liberated from all sorrow and suffering, and will be without alarm, fear, confusion, or distraction.

With hearts of loving-kindness toward one another and pure intentions, I, having known this, shall preach the Dharma as appropriate to cause them to resolutely resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Good son! On Mount Malaya there grows sandalwood incense called 'Ox-head. If one anoints the body with it, even if one enters a pit of fire, the fire cannot burn them. Good son!"

In the ocean there is a fragrance named Invincible; if it is used to anoint drums and various conch shells, when their sounds are produced, all enemy armies will completely retreat and disperse. Good son!

On the banks of Lake Anavatapta grows the agalloch incense known as Lotus Treasury; if one pellet, the size of a sesame seed, is burned, its fragrance pervades the entire Jambudvīpa realm, and all sentient beings who smell it are freed from all transgressions and their precept-observance becomes pure. Good son!

On the Snowy Mountains there is a fragrance named "Endowed with Radiant Signs. If any sentient beings smell this fragrance, their minds will certainly become free from all defiled attachments; when I preach the Dharma for them, there are none who do not attain the stainless, perfect, and pure samādhi. Good son!

In the realm of the rākṣasas there is an incense called Ocean-Treasury; this incense is used exclusively by the wheel-turning monarch. If a single pellet is burned, the fragrance permeates the king and his fourfold army, causing them all to ascend into the void and move about with sovereign ease. Good son!

In the Hall of Good Dharma there is an incense named Fragrance-Nature-Adornment; if a single pellet is burned to perfume the assembly of those devas, it causes them all universally to give rise to the mind that recollects the Buddha.
O son of good family!

In the Suyāma Heaven there is an incense named Pure Treasury Nature (*viśuddhagarbha*); if a single pellet is burned to perfume the assembly of that heaven, all will gather like clouds at the abode of the Heavenly King to reverently listen to the Dharma he preaches. Good son!

In the Tuṣita Heaven there is a fragrance named Śinduvāra; if a single pellet of it is burned before the seat of a Bodhisattva bound to one more birth, it gives rise to a great cloud of incense that pervades the entire Dharma-realm, universally raining down all manner of offerings to worship the assemblies of Bodhisattvas at the sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) of all Tathāgatas. O noble son!

In the Heaven of Wondrous Transformations, there is an incense named "Captivating Essence"; if a single pellet is burned, it will rain down all manner of inconceivable ornaments everywhere for seven days.

"Good son! I know only this method of blending incense. As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who have distanced themselves from all evil habitual tendencies to become the fragrance of stainlessness; who have forever severed the snares of afflictions and Māras, transcended all realms of existence, and attained illusion-like wisdom;

who are entirely free from attachment to all worlds, being fully perfected in the precepts of non-attachment, possessing pure wisdom of non-attachment, acting within the sphere of non-attachment, and remaining entirely without clinging in all places—their minds being equanimous, unattached, and independent—how could I possibly know their wondrous conduct, describe their merits, reveal their categories of pure precepts, demonstrate their faultless deeds, expound their flawless wisdom, or discern their gateways of action of the three karmas free from defilement?"
"Good son! To the south of here there is a great city named Lokeśvaragṛha;
in it there is a mariner named Vaira."
"Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the elder, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and departed with a heart full of longing and devotion.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded right mindfulness, headed toward the city of Lokeśvararāja; he followed his reflections and observed the road, namely:

observing whether the path was high or low, observing whether the path was level or rugged, observing whether the path was pure or defiled, observing whether the path was safe or perilous, and observing whether the path was crooked or straight.
Proceeding gradually, he formed this thought:
"I shall draw near to that spiritual friend;
for a spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the superior path of practicing the various pāramitās, and is one who thoroughly knows..."
Knowledge is the cause for accomplishing the practice that universally enters the dharma-realm through the path of non-obstruction;
spiritual friends are the cause for accomplishing the practice of the wisdom-path that gathers in all sentient beings;
spiritual friends are the cause for accomplishing the practice that ensures all sentient beings do not fall into perilous and evil paths; spiritual friends...
A spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the practice that leads all sentient beings to leave behind the paths of wrong action;
a spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the practice that leads all sentient beings to extinguish the path of afflictions;
a spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the practice that leads all sentient beings to eliminate the path of false wisdom. A spiritual friend...
A spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the practice that leads all sentient beings to leave behind the path of arrogance;
a spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the practice that leads all sentient beings to extract the thorns of evil;
a spiritual friend is the cause for accomplishing the practice that leads all sentient beings to abandon evil views. A spiritual friend...
This is the cause for accomplishing the practice that leads all sentient beings to the city of omniscience. Why is this?
Because one obtains all wholesome dharmas from the presence of spiritual friends, and because one attains the path to omniscience through the power of spiritual friends.
"A spiritual friend is difficult to see and difficult to encounter.
Thinking thus of the spiritual friend, he applied himself with diligent resolve and proceeded forward by stages.

Upon reaching that city, he saw the shipmaster standing outside the city gate on the seashore, surrounded by a great multitude of hundreds of thousands of merchants, expounding upon the Dharma of the great ocean and skillfully revealing the ocean of the Buddha's merits.
He immediately went to him, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with a single-minded focus joined his palms;
he addressed him,
saying, "Noble One!"

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice, nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path. Having heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction and guidance, I pray that you will explain this to me.
The boatman said: "Excellent! Excellent!"

"Good son! You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Now you are further able to inquire about the cause for generating great wisdom; the cause for severing all causes of birth-and-death suffering; the cause for proceeding to the great jewel-island of omniscience; the cause for accomplishing the indestructible vehicle of the Mahāyāna; the cause for remaining far removed from the fear of birth-and-death characteristic of the two vehicles; the cause for dwelling in various *samādhis* and generating wisdom; the cause for universally practicing the subtle conduct of a bodhisattva; the cause for riding the chariot of great vows and traversing the pure path of bodhisattva practices; the cause for adorning the pure path of indestructible wisdom with bodhisattva practices; the cause for universally observing all Buddhas of the ten directions without obstruction on the pure path; and the cause for swiftly entering the pure path of the profound ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas."
"Good son! I am in the great city of the Pavilion on the Seashore, purely cultivating the practice of the Bodhisattva’s Banner of Great Compassion. Good son!"
I universally observe the impoverished sentient beings within Jambudvīpa; for their benefit, I cultivate various practices to fulfill all their wishes according to their aspirations.

First, I satisfy their minds with worldly treasures and food and drink; furthermore, I bestow the wealth of the Dharma to make them rejoice. I cause them to cultivate meritorious deeds, to give rise to the path of wisdom, to increase the power of their roots of goodness, to resolve upon the Bodhi-mind, to purify their Bodhi-vows, to strengthen the power of great compassion, to cultivate the path that extinguishes birth and death, to initiate the practice of not abandoning birth and death, to gather in the ocean of sentient beings, to cultivate the ocean of merit, to illuminate the ocean of all dharmas, to behold the ocean of all Buddhas, and to enter the ocean of omniscience.
"Good son! Abiding here, I contemplate in this way, attend to things in this way, seek with diligence in this way, and thus bring benefit and peace to all sentient beings."

"Good son! I know all the jewel islands in the ocean, all the places where jewels are found, all the natures of jewels, all the roots of jewels, all the seeds of jewels, and all the categories of jewels;

furthermore, I am able to know the purification of all jewels, the drilling of all jewels, the extraction of all jewels, the crafting of all jewels, all jewel vessels, all uses of jewels, all realms of jewels, and all radiances of jewels."

Furthermore, I am able to know all the palaces of the nāgas, all the palaces of the yakṣas, all the palaces of the rākṣasas, and all the palaces of the bhūtas; regarding all such distinct dwelling places, I skillfully avoid them and escape all their perils.
He also knows the eddies and depths of the great ocean, the distance of the waves, and the various differences in the quality of the water's color;

he is likewise skilled at discerning the revolutions and movements of the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, their degrees and numbers, their anomalies and portents, the lengthening and shortening of days and nights and the passage of time;

he also knows whether the ship’s iron and wood are strong or brittle, whether its mechanisms are stiff or smooth, the volume of the water, the favorability or adversity of the winds, and the signs of safety or danger in turning left or right; thus, he proceeds when it may be done and stops when it must.
By means of such various skillful expedients, I am always able to benefit all sentient beings.
Good son! I transport groups of merchants on fine ships, leading them along safe and peaceful paths, showing them the signs of tranquility and fearlessness.

He further preached the Dharma for them to bring them joy; according to their inclinations and desires, he led them to a precious island and provided them with all manner of rare treasures until they were fully satisfied, after which he escorted them back to Jambudvīpa.

"Good son! I have navigated this great ship back and forth in this manner from the past until now without ever having suffered damage. If there are sentient beings who behold my body or hear my Dharma, I cause them never again to fear the ocean of birth and death; they will surely enter the ocean of all-knowledge, they will surely be able to exhaust the ocean of all craving and desire, they will be able to illuminate the ocean of the three periods of time with the light of wisdom, they will be able to end the ocean of suffering of all sentient beings, they will be able to purify the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings, they will quickly be able to adorn and purify the ocean of all lands, they will be able to go everywhere to the ocean of Buddhas of the ten directions, they will universally know the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings, they will universally comprehend the ocean of the conduct of all sentient beings, and they will universally accord with the ocean of the natures of all sentient beings."

"Good son! I have attained only this practice of the Banner of Great Compassion. If there are sentient beings who see, hear, remember, or dwell together with me, it shall never be in vain for them. Yet, as for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are well able to traverse the great ocean of birth and death; who can remain unstained by the ocean of afflictions; who can abandon the ocean of all false views; who can contemplate the ocean of the nature of all phenomena; who can gather the ocean of sentient beings through the four means of integration; who can skillfully abide in the ocean of omniscience; who can extinguish the ocean of attachments of all sentient beings; who can dwell equanimously throughout the ocean of all times; who can deliver the ocean of sentient beings by means of supernormal powers; and who can discipline the ocean of sentient beings according to the proper time—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious practices?"
"Noble son! To the south of here there is a city named Sukalāpa;
in it dwells an elder named Varasena. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the mariner, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and wept with tears streaming down.

Unsatiated in his quest for a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), his heart of longing and affection for the spiritual friend increased; observing him with single-minded focus, he took his leave and departed.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Ten;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifteen.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation: The Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra.

At that time, the youth Sudhana gave rise to a mind of great universal loving-kindness toward all sentient beings and a mind of moistening great compassion; his contemplation was continuous and uninterrupted. Adorned with the full perfection of merit and wisdom, his right view was complete and free from all defilements. He realized the equality of all phenomena, his mind devoid of high or low.
