He followed and entered the path of omniscience, uprooting the thorns of unwholesomeness and extinguishing all obstacles. He thoroughly understood the self-nature of the profound dharmas of awakening, making firm diligence his ramparts and moats, and taking inconceivable samādhi as his garden. With the sunlight of wisdom he shattered the darkness of ignorance; with the wind of skillful means he opened the flowers of insight; with vast vows he filled the Dharma-realm, and his mind constantly manifested entry into the city of omniscience.
Thus diligently seeking the path of a bodhisattva, he gradually proceeded to the city of Ratnāvatī and, having arrived there, inquired for the most excellent elder.

I see him now in the Great Adorned Banner Forest of No-Sorrow to the east of the city, surrounded by an immeasurable multitude of merchants and hundreds of thousands of elders. He adjudicates various worldly affairs while proclaiming the supramundane Dharma for them, causing them to abandon views, pride, and the notions of "self" and "mine. They relinquish their accumulated retinues, treasures, and wealth; they eliminate stinginess, envy, and all doubt and attachment. Their minds attain purity, free from all defilement, as they acquire the power of pure faith. They constantly delight in seeing the Buddha, uphold the Buddha-Dharma, generate the power of a bodhisattva, initiate bodhisattva conduct, enter bodhisattva samādhi, attain bodhisattva wisdom, abide in bodhisattva right mindfulness, increase the bodhisattva’s aspiration, and give rise to the mind of unsurpassed enlightenment.
At that time, Sudhana went to her place, prostrated himself on the ground to worship her feet, and after a long while, he rose and addressed her with a heart of deep reverence:
"Noble One!..."
"I am Sudhana! I am Sudhana!
I am single-mindedly seeking the supreme conduct of Bodhisattvas."
How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct? How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva path?

While training and practicing accordingly, they are always able to transform and deliver all sentient beings; they are always able to manifest before and see all Buddhas; they constantly obtain the hearing of all Buddha-dharmas; they constantly maintain and uphold all Buddha-dharmas; they constantly enter into all dharma-gates; they enter all lands to train in the bodhisattva conduct; they are always able to dwell for all great kalpas, cultivating the bodhisattva path with a mind free from weariness or satiety; they are able to know the spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas; they are able to receive the protective mindfulness of all Tathāgatas; and they are able to enter the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the elder addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good son! You have already been able to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Good son!"

I have already accomplished the dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva practice that reaches all places, possessing the power of spiritual penetrations that are without substance, without dependence, without fabrication, and without abiding.
“Good son! What is called the Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva Practice that Reaches All Places and Purifies? Good son!
Within this trichiliocosm, among all sentient beings of the desire realm—

namely, all those of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, all Yāma Heaven, all Tuṣita Heaven, all Nirmāṇarati Heaven, all Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven, all Māra heavens, and all other classes of inhabitants and their retinues dwelling in the desire realm; among all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, and in all dwellings such as villages, camps, cities, and towns— I preach the Dharma to these sentient beings according to what is appropriate for each.

May they be led to abandon what is contrary to the Dharma; may they be led to cease disputes and arguments; may they be led to eliminate warfare; may they be led to stop anger and contention; may they be led to break the knots of enmity; may they be led to untie their bonds; may they be led out of prison; may they be led to escape fear; may they be led to sever the taking of life, and so forth, until all evil deeds and improper actions, including wrong views, are entirely prohibited;
may they be led to practice all wholesome dharmas in accordance with them; may they be led to correctly cultivate all that ought to be done;
may they be led to learn all arts and crafts thoroughly, thereby bringing benefit to the world.
For their sake, he analyzes various treatises, causing them to rejoice according to what is appropriate for each;
he causes them to gradually reach maturity and, in accordance with all the various non-Buddhist groups, he teaches them superior wisdom;
he causes them to sever all views and enter the Buddha-dharma.
Even unto all the Brahmā heavens of the form realm, I likewise preach this Dharma for them.

Just as within this trichiliocosm, and even throughout the worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields in the ten directions, I have extensively expounded the True Dharma for them;
that is to say:
The Buddha-dharma, the bodhisattva-dharma, the śrāvaka-dharma, and the pratyekabuddha-dharma;
the discourse on the hell realm, the discourse on the distinctions of suffering experienced by sentient beings in the hells, and the discourse on the path leading to the hells;
the discourse on the animal realm, the discourse on the distinctions of suffering experienced by sentient beings among animals, and the discourse on the path leading to the animal realm.

He speaks of the realm of King Yama; he speaks of the distinctions in suffering experienced within the realm of King Yama; he speaks of the path leading to the realm of King Yama. He speaks of the world of devas;
he speaks of the distinctions in pleasure experienced within the world of devas; he speaks of the path leading to the world of devas. He speaks of the world of humans;
he speaks of the suffering and pleasure experienced within the world of humans; he speaks of the path leading to the world of humans.
“Good son! I teach such various worlds—whether their formation, their destruction, their defilement, or their purification—for the purpose of revealing the merits of bodhisattvas;

for the purpose of causing them to abandon the faults and afflictions of birth and death; for the purpose of causing them to know and see the merits of all Buddhas; for the purpose of causing them to know and see the births within the various realms of existence; for the purpose of causing them to know and see the unobstructed Dharma; for the purpose of causing the light of wisdom to be developed; for the purpose of demonstrating the arising of the causes of suffering and pleasure; for the purpose of demonstrating the entry into the gate of signlessness; for the purpose of causing sentient beings to abandon all conceptual attachments; for the purpose of causing them to realize the Buddha’s reliance-free Dharma; for the purpose of causing the wheel of afflictions and karma to be forever extinguished; and for the purpose of enabling them to turn the pure Dharma-wheel of the Buddha—it is for these reasons that I teach such a Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.”

Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of the Bodhisattva’s Adornment of Purity that Reaches All Places, which possesses the power of spiritual penetrations that are without dependence, without fabrication, without intrinsic nature, and without abiding.

As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are fully endowed with all sovereign spiritual powers (*abhijñā*), who are able to travel everywhere to all Buddha-fields, who have attained the stage of the Universal Eye (*samantacakṣus*), who abide in the faculty of pure hearing and hear all sounds and speech, who universally enter into the wisdom that is sovereign over all phenomena, who are peerlessly courageous and free from all conflict, who produce impartial sounds with their broad and long tongues, whose bodies are wondrously beautiful like those of other Bodhisattvas, who are ultimately non-dual with all Tathāgatas, whose body of wisdom is vast and enters the three periods of time, and whose sphere of activity is boundless like space—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

"Good son! To the south of here there is a land called Anantatīra. In that land there is a city named Kalingavana, where there resides a bhikṣuṇī named Siṃhavijṛmbhitā. Go to her and ask: how should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?"
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Most Victorious One, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing.
At that time, the youth Sudhana gradually proceeded forward until he reached the Kalinga forest on the shoreless river, where he searched everywhere for the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā;
at that moment, immeasurable people all addressed him, saying:
"O son of good family!
"This bhikṣuṇī is at the site of King Prasenajit, preaching the Dharma within the Sunlight Garden (Sūryaprabha-udyāna) and benefiting immeasurable sentient beings.

Having heard this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he immediately went to that garden and observed it thoroughly. Within the garden, he saw a great tree named Exceeding the Full Moon (Aticandrapūrṇa), shaped like a multi-storied pavilion, lofty, vast, and magnificent, emitting a great radiance that illuminated one yojana.
He further saw a leafy tree named Universal Canopy (Samantacchādaka), shaped like a parasol, with a deep blue-green luster and brilliant light shining everywhere.

Furthermore, he saw flower trees named Flower Treasury (*Puṣpakośa*), their form and color pure and lofty like the Snowy Mountains; they rained down various wondrous flowers like flowing fragrant water, their pervasive fragrance being inexhaustible, just like the Pārijātaka tree in the Nandana Grove of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

There were also fruit trees named Constantly Ripening (*Nityapākā*), shaped like mountains of gold; their flavor was like nectar, soft, fragrant, and beautiful, constantly emitting light, and they were fully endowed with all kinds of fruits.

Within it, there was further a mani-jewel tree named Vairocana-garbha; its form was peerless, like Mount Sumeru, with a heart-king mani-jewel at its summit, adorned all around by mani-jewels of incalculable colors and forms. Sandalwood mani-jewels formed its fruit, and various nets of pearls covered it from above.

There was also a garland tree named Celestial Jewel, which constantly produced exquisite jewel necklaces and flower garlands; the sovereign king of wish-fulfilling jewels bloomed in radiant splendor upon it, while a treasury of mani-jewels lay buried beneath as its roots.
Furthermore, there was a clothing tree named Capable of Purifying, which constantly produced various wonderful garments of many colors, draped over the branches as adornments.
There is a tree of music named Joyful, whose sound is exquisite and surpasses all celestial music;
there is also a tree of fragrance named Universal Adornment, which constantly emits sublime scents that universally permeate everything.

Within the garden there were further various ponds and pools, all adorned with the seven precious jewels. The entrances to these pools were embellished with many treasures; their railings were made of *maṇi* gems of various colors.

Fragrant sandalwood powder accumulated within them, while exquisite golden sand was spread across their bottoms. They were filled to the brim with the pure water of eight virtues, and their surfaces were completely covered by *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* lotuses.

*Campakā*, *atimuktaka*, *bālisika*, *māndārava*, and *mahāmāndārava* flowers—such as these—were planted in rows along their banks. Various birds sang together in harmony, their voices clear and elegant.
Various celestial jewels formed wonderful and magnificent trees arranged in rows within the garden;
beneath each of these jewel-trees were placed individual precious lion-thrones, adorned with inconceivable varieties of exquisite jewels,
draped with celestial garments, and perfumed with sublime fragrances.
Precious silk streamers hung down, precious canopies were spread, and nets of Jambū-river gold covered them all above;
precious bells swayed gently, emitting wondrous sounds;
and beneath some trees, lion thrones of the Lotus-Treasury were laid out.
In some places beneath the trees were spread lion thrones of the fragrant-king *maṇi* treasury;
in some places beneath the trees were spread lion thrones of the dragon-elephant-adorned *maṇi*-king treasury;
and in some places beneath the trees were spread lion thrones of the jewel-lion-cluster *maṇi*-king treasury.
In some places, beneath the trees, lion thrones of the Vairocana-maṇi-rāja-garbha were spread;
in some places, beneath the trees, lion thrones of the Daśadig-vairocana-maṇi-rāja-garbha were spread;
and in some places, beneath the trees, lion thrones of the Indrā-maṇi-vajra-rāja-garbha were spread.
In some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones made of the Vairocana-maṇi-rāja-garbha, bearing the forms of sentient beings;
in some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones made of the Cintāmaṇi-rāja-garbha;
and in some places beneath trees were spread lion thrones made of the white-light-maṇi-rāja-garbha.
Each of these individual seats was surrounded by hundreds of thousands of precious lion-thrones, each endowed with immeasurable adornments.
This great garden was filled with various jewels like a treasure island in the ocean; precious garments were spread upon the ground as an elaborate arrangement, soft, exquisite, and wonderful.
Like *kāliṅga* cloth, they produced a pleasant tactile sensation; when stepped upon, they sank to the ankle, and as soon as one lifted the foot, they returned to their original state.
Various species of birds—ducks, geese, mandarin ducks, white cranes, peacocks, *kukila* parrots, and others—soar and wheel with ease, turning to gaze at their reflections as they call out in harmony.

Precious sandalwood groves are planted in rows beside the gates; their dense leaves are a vibrant emerald green, their towering trunks stand tall and wide-spreading, casting long shadows and providing deep shade, magnificent and exquisite in their adornment.
Various kinds of flowering trees constantly rain down wondrous blossoms, surpassing even the Garden of Miscellaneous Flowers belonging to Śakra, Lord of Devas.
The incomparable king of incense universally perfumes all things; its fragrant breeze spreads in the four directions, reaching both devas and humans.
All the multi-storied pavilions are adorned with various jewels, decorated with exquisite incense, flowers, and rare treasures, surpassing even Śakra-devānām-indra’s Hall of Good Dharma (*Sudharmā*).
Various musical trees play celestial music, and diverse instruments are suspended from their branches, namely:

Zithers, flutes, harps, lutes, pipes, and *se*—such musical instruments as these resounded spontaneously without being struck; their sounds were pleasing to the ear and free from all defiled attachments.

Jewel *tāla* trees were covered by nets of precious bells; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced subtle and wondrous sounds like those of the goddesses of the Heaven of Sovereignty (*Īśvara*) with their skillful voices.

From the various wish-fulfilling trees emerged myriad precious garments, like the *karpāsa* robes of the devas, hanging down in magnificent display; they possessed infinite colors, resembling the vast ocean.

Hundreds of thousands of pavilions were adorned with various jewels, like the palaces of Śakra, Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; jeweled canopies covered them completely, like the peak of Mount Sumeru, and their radiance shone everywhere like the palace of the Brahmā King.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld this grove, adorned with immeasurable merits and various ornaments; all were accomplished through the inconceivable karma of Bodhisattvas, arisen from supramundane roots of goodness, and constituted the merit of making offerings to all Buddhas. Having extensively cultivated pure deeds, they could not be destroyed, and nothing in all the worlds could equal them.

All of these were produced by the Bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā through her realization that phenomena are like illusions, yet without abandoning the conditioned, she accumulated vast wholesome karma. These were not shared with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas; heterodox paths and false doctrines could not shake them, and no demonic armies could oppose them; they were beyond the contemplation of the shallow wisdom of ordinary people.

The gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, as well as immeasurable sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm, according to their own roots of goodness and as they were to be delivered, all entered this garden without it becoming cramped or crowded.
Why is this? It is because of the inconceivable power of this bhikṣuṇī’s majestic spiritual authority.

At that time, Sudhana saw the bhikṣuṇī seated beneath every one of the jewel trees upon great lion thrones; her physical form was upright and dignified, her deportment was tranquil, she dwelt in the equality of all phenomena, and her movements were composed and serene.
Their faculties are disciplined and compliant like a great elephant king;
their minds are free from defilement and turbidity like a pure pond;
they universally fulfill all requests like a wish-fulfilling jewel.
Untainted by worldly dharmas, like a lotus flower;
with a mind free from fear, like a lion king;
upholding the pure precepts so as to be unshakable, like Mount Sumeru.
It enables those who see it to attain a mind of refreshing coolness, like the Gandhamādana Mountain;
it can eliminate the heat of the afflictions of sentient beings, like the exquisite sandalwood from the Snowy Mountains;
and when sentient beings behold it, all their sufferings are extinguished, like the wondrous King of Medicines, Vaidūrya.
He causes the aspirations of those who behold him to be not in vain, like the deity Varuṇa;
he is forever free from the defilement of desire, like the Great Brahmā King;
and he purifies the minds of sentient beings, like the water-clearing jewel.
They are able to nurture all virtues like a fertile field;
their three karmas are sovereign like those of a Tathāgata;
and while seated in each assembly, the congregations differ, and the Dharma-gates they preach are likewise distinct.

In some instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of Śuddhāvāsa devas, with the celestial king Maheśvara as their leader; this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a Dharma-door named "Liberation through the Exhaustless Nature of Dharmas.

In other instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of Brahmā devas, with the Brahmā king Subhakṛtsna as their leader; this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a Dharma-door named "The Wheel of Universally Pervasive, Differentiated, and Pure Vocalization.

In yet other instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by sons and daughters of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, with the celestial king Vaśavartin as their leader; this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a Dharma-door named "The Adornment of the Sovereign Freedom of the Bodhisattva’s Pure Mind."

In some places, she was seen seated among the gods of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations (*Nirmāṇarati*), surrounded by celestial sons and daughters, with the King of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations at their head; this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a dharma-gate called "The Gate of the Pure Adornment of the Sublime Dharma.

In other places, she was seen seated among the gods of Tuṣita, surrounded by celestial sons and daughters, with the King of Tuṣita at their head; this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a dharma-gate called "The Revolution of the Treasury of One’s Own Mind.

In yet other places, she was seen seated among the gods of Suyama, surrounded by celestial sons and daughters, with the King of Suyama at their head; this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a dharma-gate called "Universal Adornment."

In some places she was seen seated amidst the Trāyastriṃśa devas, surrounded by sons and daughters of the gods, with Śakra Devendra as their leader; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a Dharma-gate called the "Gate of Renunciation.

In other places she was seen seated amidst the hundred-thousand-luminosity Dragon King, Nanda Dragon King, Upananda Dragon King, Maṇasvin Dragon King, Elāpattra Dragon King, Anavatapta Dragon King, and others, surrounded by dragon sons and daughters, with Sāgara Dragon King as their leader; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a Dharma-gate called the "Radiant Adornment of the Buddha’s Realm."

In some places, she was seen seated amidst a host of yakṣas, surrounded by boys and girls, with the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa as their leader; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a dharma-gate called "The Treasury that Protects and Saves All Sentient Beings.

In other places, she was seen seated amidst a host of gandharvas, surrounded by male and female attendants, with the Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra as their leader; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a dharma-gate called "The Rain of the Inexhaustible Dharma of Great Joy.

In yet other places, she was seen seated amidst a host of asuras, surrounded by male and female attendants, with the Asura King Rāhu as their leader; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a dharma-gate called "The Gateway of Wisdom for Swift Adornment of the Dharma Realm."

In some places, she was seen seated amidst a host of *garuḍas*, surrounded by their male and female retinues, with the powerful and heroic *garuḍa* king Mahābala as their leader; this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a dharma-gate named "Terrorizing the Ocean of All Existences.
In other places, she was seen seated amidst a host of *kiṃnaras*, surrounded by their male and female retinues, with the *kiṃnara* king Mahādruma as their leader;
this bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them a dharma-gate named "The Radiant Gate of the Buddha’s Conduct."

In some places, she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of mahoragas and their male and female retinues, with the Mahoraga King Krodha-āmra as their leader; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a dharma-gate called "Giving Birth to the Joyful Mind of Seeing the Buddha.

In other places, she was seen seated, surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands of men, women, boys, and girls; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a dharma-gate called "Excellently Superior Conduct.

In yet other places, she was seen seated, surrounded by a host of rākṣasas and their male and female retinues, with the Great Tree Rākṣasa King Nitya-śukra-hāraka as their leader; for them, this bhikṣuṇī preached a dharma-gate called "Generating the Mind of Compassion."

In some instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by sentient beings who take faith and delight in the Śrāvaka Vehicle, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called "The Great Radiance of the Power of Supreme Wisdom.

In other instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by sentient beings who take faith and delight in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called "The Vast Radiance of the Buddha’s Virtues.

In yet other instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by sentient beings who take faith and delight in the Mahāyāna, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called "The Radiance of Wisdom of the Samādhi of Universal Doors."
In some instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the first stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of the Multitude of Great Vows of All Buddhas;
in other instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the second stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Stainless Wheel Samādhi;
and in yet other instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the third stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of the Adornment of Great Tranquility.
In some instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the fourth stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of Swift Birth into the Realm of All-Knowledge;
in others, she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the fifth stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of the Treasury of Exquisite Flowers;
and in yet others, she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the sixth stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of the Vairocana Treasury.
In some places she was seen seated, surrounded by Bodhisattvas of the seventh stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of Universal Adornment of the Grounds;

in other places she was seen seated, surrounded by Bodhisattvas of the eighth stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of Manifesting Bodies through Transformation within the Universal Realm of the Dharma-dhātu;

and in yet other places she was seen seated, surrounded by Bodhisattvas of the ninth stage, as this bhikṣuṇī taught them a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of the Ornament of the Power of Wisdom of Non-apprehension.
In some instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by bodhisattvas of the tenth stage who were all expounding for her a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of the Unobstructed Wheel;
in other instances, she was seen seated, surrounded by Vajradhara bodhisattvas who were all expounding for her a dharma-gate called the Samādhi of Vajra-Wisdom Nārāyaṇa Adornment.

At that time, the youth Sudhana saw this entire great assembly—born in various ways, dwelling in various places, possessing various physical forms, and having various retinues; those already matured and those already tamed, who were all fit vessels for the Dharma and had entered this grove, each sitting in a circle beneath a tree. The bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā, according to what was appropriate for them—whether their various dispositions, various inclinations, or various convictions—expounded corresponding Dharma gates according to their respective superior or inferior capacities, causing them to attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Why is this? Because this bhikṣuṇī has attained the Prajñāpāramitā gate of attaining the universal eye, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of expounding all Buddha-dharmas, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of the limit of the distinctions of the dharma-realm, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of shattering all wheels of obstruction, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of engendering and growing the wholesome minds of all sentient beings, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of supreme adornment, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of the unobstructed treasury of reality, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of the perfection of the dharma-realm, the Prajñāpāramitā gate of the treasury of the pure mind, and the Prajñāpāramitā gate of the universally produced treasury of various linguistic supernormal powers.
With these ten gates of *prajñāpāramitā* as the foremost, he enters countless millions of *asaṃkhyeya* gates of *prajñāpāramitā*.

Within this Sunlight Garden, the realms perceived by all the bodhisattvas and sentient beings, as well as the sublime Dharma they hear, each differ from one another and their realizations vary; yet all of this is due to the initial exhortation, inspiration, teaching, and transformation provided by the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā, which has caused them to attain non-retrogression in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā’s gardens, her seats, her walking paths, her assemblies, her deportment, her mastery, her universal body, her fearlessness, her supernormal powers, her eloquence, and her adornments; furthermore, having heard such an inconceivable and vast Dharma-gate, his body and mind became supple, and he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground in reverent worship. Joining his palms, he thought:
"I shall circumambulate this bhikṣuṇī to the right for countless hundreds of thousands of millions of times."

As he was thinking this, the bhikṣuṇī immediately emitted a radiance that illuminated the entire garden and reached the entire assembly. Sudhana saw his own body pervading all places; at each seat where there was a bhikṣuṇī, he circumambulated her to the right hundreds of thousands of millions of times. Having completed the circumambulations, he stood with palms joined and said: "Noble Lady!"

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice or how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Holy One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me.
The bhikṣuṇī said: “Good son!
I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called ‘The Door of Eliminating All Subtle Discriminations.’”
Sudhana said, “Noble One!
For what reason is he named ‘The One Who Eliminates All Subtle Discriminations’?”
The bhikṣuṇī said: “Good son!
This gate of liberation universally illumines all dharmas of the three periods of time within a single thought-moment, manifesting the light of wisdom of their intrinsic nature.”
Sudhana said, “Noble One! What is the sphere of this light of wisdom?”
The bhikṣuṇī said: "O son of good family!

When I entered this gate of the light of wisdom, I attained the sovereign samādhi-king that gives rise to all dharmas. Because I have attained such a sovereign samādhi-king, I manifest a mind-made body (manomayakāya) and appear universally in the Tuṣita palaces throughout all worlds in the ten directions, among those bodhisattvas bound to one more birth."
Before each and every bodhisattva, he manifests bodies as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
from each and every body, he performs the most supreme offerings as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
That is to say:

In some instances, they manifest as the bodies of celestial kings, dragon kings, yakṣa kings, and even as human kings; each holding various clouds of flowers, various clouds of garlands, burning incense, unguents, and powdered incense, as well as clothing, necklaces, banners, pennants, silk canopies, jeweled nets, jeweled curtains, jeweled treasuries, jeweled lamps, and even clouds of all manner of ornaments. I hold these all and offer them as worship. Just as I approach, serve, and make various offerings to a Bodhisattva bound to one more birth while dwelling in the Tuṣita Heaven, so too do I do likewise for him when he descends from heaven and enters the womb, dwells in the womb, emerges from the womb, lives at home, leaves the home life, proceeds to the site of enlightenment, attains equal and perfect awakening, turns the wheel of the true Dharma, and enters into nirvāṇa.
In this manner, whether dwelling in celestial palaces, dragon palaces, or even the palaces of humans and non-humans, I have made such offerings to all those Tathāgatas.

If there are sentient beings who know that I have thus seen, heard, approached, and made offerings to the Buddhas, they shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. If there are sentient beings who come to me, I shall always guide and instruct them, proclaiming for them the gateways of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
“Good son! I see all sentient beings, yet I do not discriminate the characteristics of sentient beings, because my eye of wisdom sees clearly;
I hear all speech, yet I do not discriminate the characteristics of speech, because my mind has no attachment.”
They behold all Tathāgatas, yet do not discriminate the marks of a Tathāgata, because their wisdom realizes the Dharma-body;
they maintain the wheel of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas, yet do not discriminate the marks of the wheel of the Dharma, because they have awakened to the self-nature of phenomena;
in a single thought-moment they universally know all phenomena, yet do not discriminate the marks of various phenomena, because they know that phenomena are like illusions.

"Good son! I know only this bodhisattva door of liberation, which eliminates all subtle conceptualization and accomplishes all-knowledge; [how could I know the practices or tell of the virtues of the bodhisattvas who have perfected the ocean of all roots of goodness?]"

Just as the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have minds free from discrimination and universally know all dharmas; as they sit upright in a single body filling the entire Dharma-realm; as they manifest within their own bodies the sustaining of all Buddha-fields and are able to go to the presence of all Buddhas; as they universally manifest within their own bodies the spiritual powers of all Buddhas; as a single hair of theirs can lift up unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-worlds; as within a single pore of their own body they manifest the formation and destruction of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; as in a single thought-moment they dwell together with unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings; and as in a single thought-moment they enter into unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all kalpas—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

"Noble son! To the south of here there is a village named Durga. Within it is a city called Ratnavyuha, where there lives a woman named Vasumitrā. Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and took his leave.
At that time, the great light of wisdom illuminated and opened Sudhana’s mind;
he contemplated and observed the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), single-mindedly conforming to the firm reality-nature of all phenomena, and thoroughly understanding them all.
The dhāraṇī door of the vocal sounds of sentient beings; the dhāraṇī door of receiving and upholding the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
the power of great compassion that serves as a refuge for all sentient beings;
the door of light for observing the principles and meanings of all phenomena; the swift and perfect fulfillment of the wheel of the dharma-realm; and the turning [of that wheel].
That wheel of pure great vows attains the light of wisdom that universally illumines all phenomena throughout the ten directions;
it attains the sovereign power to universally adorn all worlds; it attains the wisdom of supernatural powers that universally encompasses all bodhisattvas;
and it attains the universal arousal of the perfect vows of all bodhisattvas.
Gradually proceeding forward, he arrived at the city of Ratnavyūha in the perilous land. He searched everywhere for the maiden Vāsundharā.
There were people in the city who did not know the extent of this woman’s merit, wisdom, skillful means, or the subtle, profound, and secret realm in which she dwelt; they thought to themselves:

“Now this youth has his faculties serene and well-tamed; his wisdom is clear and lucid; he is already free from negligence, his mind is undisturbed, and he gazes steadily for the distance of a *vyāma* without weariness. He is without attachment, his eyes do not blink, and his mind is unmoved. Being as profound and vast as the great ocean, it is impossible that he could harbor a heart of lustful desire or a perverted mind toward the woman Vasumitrā, nor give rise to thoughts of purity or thoughts of sensual craving; he cannot be captivated by the beauty of this woman.”

This youth does not engage in the conduct of Māra, does not enter the realm of Māra, does not sink into the mire of desire, and is not bound by Māra; since he is already able to refrain from what ought not to be done, with what intention does he seek this girl?
Among them, there were some who had previously known that this woman possessed supreme merit and was endowed with profound wisdom;
they said to Sudhana, "Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! That you are now able to seek out and search for the woman Vāsundharā, you have already attained vast and great benefit. Noble son!"

You should resolutely seek the sublime fruit of Buddhahood; you should resolutely desire to become a refuge for all sentient beings; you should resolutely desire to extract the poisonous arrows of craving from all sentient beings; you should resolutely desire to shatter all notions of purity regarding female form held by all sentient beings; and you should resolutely desire to rain down the great rain of merit of all Tathāgatas, which pervades the entire Dharma-realm.
“Good son! The lady Vaśudharā dwells in her own home, to the north of the marketplace within this city.
Having heard these words, the youth Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; his aspirations fulfilled, he proceeded toward her door with single-minded right mindfulness.
He beheld his residence, vast and magnificent, with jeweled walls, jeweled trees, and jeweled moats, each surrounded by tenfold enclosures.

Within these jeweled moats, fragrant water overflowed, its bed strewn with golden sand; celestial jewel-flowers—blue lotuses (*utpala*), red lotuses (*padma*), yellow lotuses (*kumuda*), and white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*)—completely covered the surface of the water. Exquisite and rare perfumes wafted forth, gladdening the hearts of all, while wondrous jewels and precious treasures adorned the banks.

The steps and railings were composed of various gems, and palaces and towers were distributed everywhere. Doors, gates, windows, and casements were aligned in succession, all provided with decorative nets and bells, and banners and streamers were erected throughout, embellished with immeasurable rarities.

The ground is made of lapis lazuli, interspersed with various jewels; it is perfumed with burning aloeswood and anointed with sandalwood. Suspended from above are many jeweled bells that produce melodic sounds when stirred by the wind, and celestial flowers are scattered everywhere across the ground.

Mani-jewel lamps and candles shine with universal radiance, and there are hundreds of thousands of treasuries of rare gems. Ten great gardens serve as its adornments, where the branches and twigs of jewel-trees waft fragrance and emit brilliance.
Its various wonders were beyond description.

At that time, Sudhana beheld this woman, her countenance upright and majestic, her physical features perfect, her skin golden, and her eyes and hair deep blue. She was neither tall nor short, neither coarse nor delicate; among the humans and devas of the desire realm, none could compare to her.

Her voice was exquisite, surpassing all the Brahma worlds, and she possessed the full range of all sentient beings' diverse dialects, understanding them all without exception. She profoundly mastered the meaning of words and was skillful in discourse.
They have attained the wisdom that is like an illusion and entered the gateway of skillful means;
their bodies are adorned with necklaces of various jewels, which are completely covered by nets of all kinds of gems, and they wear upon their heads crowns of wish-fulfilling *maṇi* jewels.
Surrounded by immeasurable retinues who pay them respectful homage, they share the same roots of goodness and identical vows and practices, possessing an inexhaustible treasury of merit and virtue.

At that time, from her body, that woman emitted a vast radiance that universally illuminated all the halls and jeweled palaces within the residence; those who encountered this light attained physical coolness, and the feverish afflictions of their minds were dispelled.
At that time, Sudhana went before him, prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said: "Noble One!

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct or how to cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me."
He then replied: "Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'The Limit Beyond Greed.'"

I am able to manifest my body in accordance with whatever desires and inclinations all sentient beings may have. If a deva sees me, I appear as a celestial maiden, my form and radiance being incomparably sublime;

likewise, even when humans, non-humans, and others see me, I immediately manifest as a human or non-human woman, appearing in forms that are each uniquely excellent according to their respective characteristics, so that all may behold me according to their own inclinations and desires.

“Good son! If there are sentient beings who, being entangled by sensual desire, come to me and conceive an extreme attachment to my body, their minds becoming as if intoxicated, I preach the Dharma for them; having heard the Dharma, they then leave behind greed and desire, and attain the Bodhisattva samādhi of the state of non-attachment.
If there are sentient beings who see me even for a moment, they then leave behind greed and desire, and attain the Bodhisattva samādhi of joy.”
If there are sentient beings who briefly converse with me, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Treasury of Unobstructed and Wondrous Sounds;
if there are sentient beings who briefly take my hand, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Following and Traveling Everywhere to All Buddha-fields;
if there are sentient beings who briefly ascend my seat, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Light Transcending All Worlds.
If there are sentient beings who even momentarily gaze upon me, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Tranquil Adornment;
if there are sentient beings who see me stretching my limbs, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Subduing All Heretics;
if there are sentient beings who see me blink their eyes, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Abiding in the Radiance of the Buddha’s Realm.
If there are sentient beings who embrace me, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Constantly Not Abandoning Any Sentient Being through Universal Gathering.
If there are sentient beings who kiss my lips, they will be freed from desire and attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Increasing the Treasury of Merit for All Sentient Beings.

In this manner, all sentient beings who come to where I am and draw near to me shall all abide in the limit of freedom from desire and enter the most supreme liberation of the Bodhisattva stage of omniscience.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the lady Vasumitrā, "Noble Lady!
Why is this door of liberation called 'Most Supreme'?"
Then the woman said: "Good son!

All bodhisattvas who have resolved their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* cannot quickly accomplish the unsurpassed path of the Buddha because they are women; nor can they swiftly attain the vehicle of the *pratyekabuddha*, the fruit of an *arhat*, or the state of a rishi with the five supernormal powers."
Because of women, one loses supernormal powers; for those who bear the burden [of existence], gods and asuras constantly wage war;
the ten-headed rākṣasa burns the great city of Laṅkā in the Southern Sea;

some kings lose their kingdoms, and even brothers kill one another, creating the causes for rebirth in evil realms, becoming impoverished in this life, and willingly serving as slaves; they are disobedient to teachers and elders, and turn their backs on sovereigns and parents—all such things as these arise solely from women.

I observe countless hundreds of thousands of worlds where sentient beings driven by craving wander endlessly through the wilderness of birth and death; among all karmic sufferings, women are the foremost.

Therefore, if a bodhisattva distances themselves from female forms, they will be able to draw near to spiritual friends and further cause sentient beings to become free from desire through this means, so that all may abide in the most supreme dharma-gate of liberation.
Sudhana the youth said: "Noble One!
What roots of goodness have you planted and what meritorious deeds have you cultivated to attain such various and supreme qualities?"
At that time, the woman replied:

"Noble son! I recall that in the past there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Uccagāmin (High Conduct), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
At that time, the royal capital was named Wonderful Gate (Miomon). Good son!
At that time, for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, that Tathāgata entered the royal city and stepped upon its threshold.

The entire city shook in six ways; suddenly it became vast and expansive, adorned with various jewels, with immeasurable lights reflecting and penetrating one another. Various precious flowers were strewn upon its ground, and the music of the devas played in unison. All the devas filled the void, prostrating, paying respect, honoring, and praising [the Buddha].

"Good son! At that time, I was the wife of a householder named Miaozhi (Wonderful Wisdom). Witnessing the Buddha’s supernormal powers, my mind attained awakening; I and my husband then quickly went to where the Buddha was, gave rise to a vast resolve, and offered a single precious coin as a gift to the Buddha.
At that moment, the youth Mañjuśrī was serving as the Buddha’s attendant; he expounded the Dharma for me, causing me to give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."

"Good son! I know only this bodhisattva liberation door of the limit of detachment from desire. As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have accomplished infinite wisdom of skillful means and whose merit is as vast as space—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?"
"Good son! To the south there is a city named Pāragāminī;

in it dwells a householder named Viśuddhara, who constantly makes offerings at the sandalwood throne stūpa of the Buddha. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.

With single-minded compliance, they recollect and practice: they contemplate that Bodhisattva’s samādhi of the unattached realm,
they reflect upon that Bodhisattva’s samādhi of joy, they seek out that Bodhisattva’s samādhi of the treasury of unimpeded sound,
they practice that Bodhisattva’s samādhi of universally visiting all Buddha-fields, and they keep in mind that Bodhisattva’s detachment...
The Samādhi of Radiance for All Worlds; the Samādhi of Entering the Quiescent Adornment of those Bodhisattvas;
the Samādhi of Cultivating the Subjugation of Non-Buddhists by those Bodhisattvas; the Samādhi of Contemplating the Radiance of the Buddha-Sphere of those Bodhisattvas;
