The Bodhisattva, having entered the samādhi that increases the store of merit for sentient beings and recollecting all-knowledge, proceeded gradually until he reached the city of Pāra. Arriving at the householder’s residence, he prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said: “Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice, nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Having heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction and guidance, I pray that you will explain this to me.
The householder replied:
"Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'the limit of non-parinirvāṇa.'"
"Good son! I do not give rise to the thought:
'Such a Tathāgata has already entered parinirvāṇa; such a Tathāgata is currently entering parinirvāṇa; such a Tathāgata will enter parinirvāṇa.'"

"I know that in all worlds throughout the ten directions, there are no Buddhas, Tathāgatas, who ever enter final parinirvāṇa; it is only for the sake of taming sentient beings that they manifest such a display."
"Good son! When I opened the door of the Tathāgata’s stūpa containing that sandalwood throne, I attained a samādhi called 'The Inexhaustibility of the Buddha-seed. Good son!"
"In every thought-moment I enter this samādhi, and in every thought-moment I come to know the extraordinary deeds of all Buddhas.
Sudhana said, "What is the sphere of this samādhi?"
The householder replied,
"Good son! When I enter this samādhi, I see all the Buddhas of this world appearing in succession, one after another."
They were as follows:

Kāśyapa Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, Krakucchanda Buddha, Viśvabhū Buddha, Śikhin Buddha, Vipaśyin Buddha, Tiṣya Buddha, Puṣya Buddha, Yaśas Buddha, and Varapadma Buddha; these and others were the foremost among them.

In a single moment of thought, they are able to see a hundred buddhas, a thousand buddhas, a hundred thousand buddhas, ten million buddhas, a billion buddhas, ten billion buddhas, a hundred billion buddhas, a hundred trillion buddhas, a quadrillion buddhas, and even as many buddhas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds.
In this manner, he saw all these things in succession.

He also saw those Buddhas from their initial generation of the mind of enlightenment, through their planting of various roots of goodness, their acquisition of supreme supernormal powers, their fulfillment of great vows, their practice of sublime conduct, their perfection of the *pāramitās*, their entry into the bodhisattva stages, their attainment of pure patience, their subduing of the armies of Māra, their realization of equal and perfect enlightenment, the purification of their lands, the adornment of their assemblies, the emission of great radiance, their mastery of supernormal powers, their uttering of the lion’s roar, and their turning of the wondrous wheel of Dharma;

as well as their manifestation of various transformations and distinctions, their maturing of sentient beings through immeasurable skillful means, and their skillful proclamation of all differentiated teachings.
I am able to uphold all of them, I am able to remember all of them, I am able to observe, analyze, and elucidate them; I understand them in accordance with their meaning without any forgetfulness.

Thus, regarding the future Buddhas such as Maitreya—hundreds of Buddhas, thousands of Buddhas, hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddhas, even up to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable worlds—as well as those who have continuously maintained the initial resolve from the start, whose faith and understanding are profound, who seek diligently without slackening, and whose power of diligence increases rapidly, becoming unshakable by any worldly ordinary beings or followers of the two vehicles.

He also saw all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, in all worlds throughout the unspeakably unspeakable number of Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms in the ten directions, such as the present Vairocana Buddha; they were all likewise so.
I clearly behold all those Buddhas;
I have heard all those Dharmas, and I remember, uphold, and never forget them in my mind.
Through the power of wisdom, they understand in accordance with reality; through the power of compassion, they proclaim and reveal it. Good son!

I know only this gate of liberation—the limit of non-extinction attained by Bodhisattvas. As for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, who, with the wisdom of a single thought-moment, universally know the three periods of time, and in a single thought-moment, universally enter all samādhis—[I do not know their ways].
The sun of the Tathāgata’s wisdom constantly illumines their minds.
They are without discrimination regarding all phenomena and understand that all Buddhas are entirely equal.
The Tathāgata, myself, and all sentient beings are identical and without duality.
They know that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, its radiance universally illuminating and pervading everywhere without exception.

Without thought or movement, they are able to enter all worlds, free from all discrimination, abiding in the seal of the Buddha-dharma, and are fully capable of awakening all sentient beings within the dharma-realm.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
Son of good family!

To the south of here there is a mountain named Potalaka; there dwells a bodhisattva named Avalokiteśvara. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the householder, following this instruction, spoke these verses:
“Upon the sea there is a mountain formed of various jewels, The abode of sages and saints, supremely pure.
Springs and streams wind around it as its adornment, And flowering groves and fruit trees fill its midst.”
The Most Victorious and Valiant One who benefits sentient beings, the Honored Avalokiteśvara, dwells here;
you should go and inquire about the Buddha’s qualities, and he shall proclaim them to you in detail.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the householder, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and took his leave to depart.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having received the instruction of the householder, followed it with contemplation, maintaining single-minded right mindfulness. He entered the treasury of the Bodhisattva’s profound faith and understanding; he attained the Bodhisattva’s power of recollection; he remembered the sequence of the appearance of those Buddhas; he beheld those Buddhas attaining equal and perfect enlightenment; he upheld the names of all those Buddhas; he contemplated the Dharma-gates realized by those Buddhas; he knew the complete adornments of those Buddhas; he believed in the turning of the wheel of Dharma by those Buddhas; he reflected on the illumination of the wisdom-light of those Buddhas; he recollected the equanimous samādhi of those Buddhas; he understood the intrinsic purity of the nature of those Buddhas; he cultivated the non-discriminative Dharma of those Buddhas; he accorded with the profound Dharma-seals of those Buddhas; and he performed the inconceivable deeds of those Buddhas.
Proceeding gradually, he reached that mountain and searched everywhere for this great bodhisattva.

To its western side, amidst the rocky valleys, he saw a spring flowing with shimmering clarity; the forest was lush and verdant, and soft, fragrant grasses spread across the ground in a clockwise swirl, while various kinds of famous flowers adorned the surroundings on all sides.

The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara sat cross-legged upon a pure vajra-jewel-leafed stone, surrounded with reverence by immeasurable bodhisattvas all seated upon jewel-stones; he then proclaimed the Dharma of the Great Compassion of Wisdom-Light, causing all sentient beings to be gathered and sustained.

Having seen him, Sudhana leaped for joy with great delight; out of love and reverence for the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), he joined his palms in respect and gazed at him without blinking, thinking thus:

"The spiritual friend is the Tathāgata; the spiritual friend is the cloud of all dharmas; the spiritual friend is the treasury of all merits; the spiritual friend is difficult to encounter; the spiritual friend is the cause for the jewel of the ten powers; the spiritual friend is the inexhaustible torch of wisdom; the spiritual friend is the sprout of the roots of merit; the spiritual friend is the gateway to omniscience; the spiritual friend is the guide across the ocean of wisdom; the spiritual friend is the collection of all requisites for the path that leads to omniscience."
Having formed this thought, he immediately went to where the Great Bodhisattva was.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara saw Sudhana from afar and addressed him, saying: "Excellent!
Welcome, young man!
You have resolved upon the Mahāyāna, universally gathering in all sentient beings;
you have given rise to an upright mind, single-mindedly seeking the Buddha-dharma, and with profound and heavy great compassion, you rescue and protect all.
Abiding in inconceivable and most supreme conduct, they are universally able to rescue and deliver beings from the cycle of birth and death, transcending the world without equal.

The wondrous practices of Samantabhadra manifest continuously before them; their great vows and profound resolve are perfectly pure. Diligently seeking the Buddha-dharma, they are fully capable of receiving and upholding it; they accumulate roots of goodness without ever becoming weary or satisfied, and they follow spiritual friends without ever contravening their instructions.

Born from the great ocean of Mañjuśrī’s merit and wisdom, his mind was matured and he attained the majestic power of a Buddha; having already obtained the light of vast samādhis, he single-mindedly sought the profound and wondrous Dharma, constantly beholding all Buddhas with great joy, his wisdom pure as space.

Having attained clarity for oneself, one further explains it to others; abiding in the light of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, one upholds and practices all Buddha-dharmas. The precious treasury of merit and wisdom arrives spontaneously, and the path of omniscience swiftly manifests before one. Universally observing the minds of sentient beings without weariness, one’s great compassion is as firm and unyielding as a diamond.
At that time, the youth Sudhana went to where the Bodhisattva was, prostrated at the Bodhisattva’s feet, circumambulated him countless times, stood with palms joined, and said: "Noble One!
"I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will explain this to me."

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara emitted a radiant light of the exquisite color of Jāmbūnada gold, giving rise to clouds of jewel-flame nets of immeasurable colors and clouds of the sublime adornments of Nāga-sovereignty to illuminate Sudhana.
He then extended his right hand, stroked Sudhana’s head, and said to him:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
"Noble son! You have already been able to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Noble son!"
I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door of the swift practice of great compassion. Noble son!
By means of this bodhisattva door of the practice of great compassion, I impartially teach and transform all sentient beings, gathering them in and subduing them in an uninterrupted succession.

"Good son! I constantly abide in this gateway of great compassionate practice, ever remaining in the presence of all Tathāgatas and universally appearing before all sentient beings, benefiting them according to their needs for transformation."

They may gather in sentient beings through generosity, or through kind speech, or through beneficial conduct, or through cooperation; they may gather them by manifesting various subtle and wondrous physical forms, or by manifesting various inconceivable nets of pure light from their bodies; they may do so through skillful voices and eloquent speech, or through majestic deportment and sublime expedient means; they may do so by preaching the Dharma, or by manifesting supernatural transformations to awaken them and bring them to maturity; or they may manifest various physical appearances, various lineages, various birthplaces, and forms identical to their own, dwelling together with them to bring them to maturity.
“Good son! I have cultivated this gateway of practice of great compassion, vowing to always rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing them to be free from all fears.
These are as follows:”

May all sentient beings be free from the fear of perilous paths; free from the fear of feverish affliction; free from the fear of confusion; free from the fear of bondage; free from the fear of slaughter; free from the fear of kings and officials; free from the fear of poverty; free from the fear of being unable to survive; free from the fear of ill repute; free from the fear of death; free from the fear of various diseases; free from the fear of indolence; free from the fear of darkness; free from the fear of displacement; free from the fear of separation from loved ones; free from the fear of encountering enemies; free from the fear of physical oppression; free from the fear of mental oppression; free from the fear of sorrow, lamentation, grief, and despair; free from the fear of not obtaining what is sought; free from the fear of the majesty and power of great assemblies; and free from the fear of wandering through the evil realms.
Again, he made this vow:

"May all sentient beings, whether they think of me, recite my name, or behold my body, all be freed from every fear, have their obstacles and difficulties extinguished, and have right mindfulness manifest before them."
"Good son! By means of such various skillful expedients, I cause all sentient beings to leave behind all fears and abide in right mindfulness;
furthermore, I instruct them to resolve their minds upon Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi until they reach the stage of non-retrogression."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, wishing to further clarify the meaning of this gate of liberation, spoke these verses to the youth Sudhana:
"Welcome, you who have tamed body and mind! You bow your head in praise and circumambulate me to the right.
I always dwell here upon this mountain of jewels, Abiding in great compassion, ever sovereign."
In this Vajra Cave where I dwell, adorned with various mani jewels of wondrous color,
I always sit upon this precious lotus throne with a courageous and sovereign mind.
Devas, nāgas, and asura hosts, kinnara kings, rākṣasas, and the like—
surrounded by such retinues, I shall expound for them the gateway of great compassion.
You have been able to give rise to an incomparable mind, coming here for the sake of seeing me;
with love and joy, you seek the ocean of merit, prostrating at my feet, this body of merit.
Desiring to study and practice within my Dharma, you vow to attain the true and wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra.
I am the valiant Avalokiteśvara, Arising with profound, pure, and great compassion;
Universally emitting a wondrous light from a net of clouds, Vast as space and utterly pure.
I extend my stainless, smooth, and rounded arm, adorned with the wondrous marks of a hundred merits;
I touch the crown of you, Sudhana of deep faith, and for your sake I shall expound the Dharma of Bodhi.
Sons of the Buddha, you should know that what I have attained is the gate of liberation of a single characteristic and a single flavor;
it is called the Great Compassion Cloud of all Buddhas, the treasury adorned with secret wisdom.
I am diligent and ever protect and rescue them; I give rise to great vows to gather in all sentient beings.
Compassionate toward all as if toward my own body, I always turn in accordance with the universal gate.
Throughout countless eons of manifold suffering and calamity, I have always been able to rescue and protect all living beings;
if they bring me to mind with reverence or simply call my name, all shall be liberated at that very moment.
Should one encounter imprisonment and confinement, or be bound by shackles and fetters while facing enemies,
if they can invoke my name with a sincere heart, all sufferings shall be utterly extinguished.
Or if one has committed a crime and is about to be executed, with a sharp sword or poisoned arrow threatening their life—
by invoking the name and receiving this empowerment, they shall suffer no harm from bows, arrows, or blades.
Should there be two who compete and approach a royal official, disputing over all manner of wealth and treasures—
if they can sincerely invoke my name, they shall attain superior principles and a wide reputation.
Whether among one's internal or external relatives, or even with friends who have become enemies—
if one can sincerely invoke my name, no adversaries whatsoever shall be able to cause harm.
Whether in deep forests or perilous places, where enemies and fierce beasts seek to cause harm,
if one can invoke my name with a sincere heart, their evil intentions will naturally cease and they shall be unable to inflict injury.
Should there be an enemy harboring hateful malice, Who pushes one down from a steep and lofty mountain peak;
If one can invoke my name with a sincere heart, One shall rest peacefully in the void, unharmed.
Should there be an enemy harboring resentment and malice, who pushes one into a deep torrent or a pit of fire—
if one can invoke my name with a sincere heart, neither water nor fire shall be able to cause harm.
If there are sentient beings who encounter calamities and hardships, their bodies oppressed by various instruments of suffering,
if they can invoke my name with a sincere heart, they shall all be liberated from sorrow and fear.
If one is deceived or slandered by others, and they constantly contemplate faults to harbor resentment,
yet can sincerely invoke my name, such enmity and aversion will naturally subside.
Should one encounter the harms of ghosts, demons, or various poisons, such that body and mind become deranged and one loses all awareness—
if one can invoke my name with a sincere heart, all those afflictions shall be extinguished and no further suffering shall remain.
Whether one is beset by venomous dragons or hosts of ghosts, and all manner of terrors seize their hearts—
if they can invoke my name with utmost sincerity, they shall not see any of these things even in their dreams.
If there are those whose sense faculties are incomplete or deficient, may they obtain a body adorned with the marks and signs of excellence;
if one can sincerely invoke my name, all their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
If one makes a vow toward one's parents, to serve and obey their countenance without any opposition of will,
to bring them joy, honor, wealth, and happiness, and to ensure their security and peace, then precious treasures and hidden hoards shall be eternally inexhaustible.
May internal and external kinsmen always be in harmony, And may all enmities and hostilities refrain from invading;
If one can invoke my name with utmost sincerity, All their aspirations shall be fully realized.

If a person makes this vow: "After the end of this life, may I not receive a body in the three miserable realms or the eight difficult conditions, but always dwell among the favorable rebirths of humans and devas, constantly practicing the pure path to enlightenment."
I vow to relinquish this body to be born in the Pure Land, Appearing universally before all Buddhas;
Throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, May I always be a pure and supreme *sattva*.
May I see all Buddhas throughout the ten directions And hear the sound of the Dharma they preach.
If one can invoke my name with utmost sincerity, all their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
Whether in perilous distress or amidst great anxiety and fear, if they invoke my name six times throughout the day and night,
I will then manifest before that person and serve as their supreme refuge.
They shall be born in my pure Buddha-field, Practicing the bodhisattva path together with me;
Through my great compassion, Avalokiteśvara, I cause all of them to achieve complete success.

Some with pure minds shall offer worship, Some presenting jeweled canopies or burning incense, Or scattering exquisite flowers upon my body; They shall be born in my land as those worthy of offerings.
Or born in turbid kalpas devoid of compassion, entangled by the evil karma of greed and hatred,
they endure various sufferings most stubbornly firm, with hundreds of thousands of fetters constantly unbroken.
Though they are oppressed by all manner of afflictions, if they praise, extol, and recite my name, then through me,
Avalokiteśvara of Great Compassion, all their delusions and karmic deeds shall be utterly extinguished.
There may be sentient beings who, when their lives are ending, See various evil signs appear before them at the moment of death;
Having seen those diverse and ominous forms, Their minds become terrified and find no refuge.
If they can sincerely invoke my name, All those evil omens will be completely extinguished.
Through my great compassion, Avalokiteśvara, I cause beings to be born in the auspicious realms of gods and humans;

all of this was practiced by me in the past. May I deliver the immeasurable multitudes of living beings, remaining courageous, diligent, and without regression, so that all their endeavors may be brought to fulfillment.
If there are those who should contemplate my body as appropriate, may they all see it according to their thoughts;
and for those who delight in hearing me preach the Dharma, may they hear the wondrous teaching in measureless abundance.
All sentient beings throughout all worlds, with their infinite varieties of mental activities,
I cause to hear, see, and be tamed through various powers of skillful means.
I have attained the gate of liberation of great compassion; The Buddhas have witnessed my cultivation and study.
As for the remaining oceans of immeasurable merit, They are beyond what my wisdom can know.
"Good Wealth, throughout the realms of the ten directions, you shall serve all spiritual friends;
with single-minded devotion, practice without indolence, and listen to and receive the Buddha-dharma without ever feeling weary."
If one can hear the Dharma without weariness or satiety, then one can see all Buddhas everywhere;
how could one ever tire of seeing the Buddhas? It is because of listening to the sublime Dharma without weariness or satiety.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken these verses, he addressed Sudhana, saying:

“Good son! I have only attained this bodhisattva liberation door of the swift practice of great compassion. As for those bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who have already purified all the vows of Samantabhadra and have already dwelt in all the practices of Samantabhadra;”

They constantly practice all wholesome dharmas; they constantly enter all samādhis; they constantly abide throughout all boundless eons; they constantly visit all boundless lands; they constantly contemplate all Tathāgatas; they constantly hear all dharmas of the three periods of time; they constantly extinguish the evils of all sentient beings; they constantly increase the virtues of all sentient beings; they constantly sever the stream of birth and death for sentient beings; and they constantly enter the stream of the Tathāgata’s true Dharma.
"How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?

At that time, having heard these verses on the purity of great compassion spoken by the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the youth Sudhana was filled with such joy and exultation that it pervaded his entire body.

Giving rise to a heart of love and reverence, increasing his heart of faith and joy, and generating a pure mind, he rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and prostrated at the feet of the Bodhisattva. With palms joined, kneeling before the Bodhisattva, he gazed up at him with single-minded devotion and praised him in verse:
“The great assembly of devas, humans, and asuras, Together with all the bodhisattvas, With wondrous voices they praise in unison: The Great Sage’s wisdom is deep as the ocean.”
Able, among all sentient beings, to maintain equal great compassion of a single flavor;
with a single wisdom focused on the same object, universally rescuing and protecting them, so that all manner of sufferings and hardships are utterly extinguished.
The Bodhisattva’s most supreme power of supernatural faculties makes it no difficulty to overturn the great earth;
he can likewise dry up the vast oceans and cause even the Kings of Great Mountains to tremble.
The noble Bodhisattva of great renown, known by the name of the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara—
how could I, with my meager and inferior intellect, possibly praise your sublime virtues?
I have heard of the noble ones' manifold virtues, The gateways of great compassion that are uninterrupted and inexhaustible;
By this cause, I give rise to a pure mind, And the power of wisdom and eloquence is born within me.
Now, dwelling amidst this great assembly, I observe with great courage and valor;
I extol and praise this wondrous adornment, reverent and sincere, without weariness.
Just as the Great Brahmā King dwells among the Brahma assembly, Outshining all other Brahma devas,
So the Bodhisattva’s auspicious and wondrous form-body Stands peerless within the gathered multitude.
The Bodhisattva gazes about like a bull-king; his wondrous form is radiant and pure like a mass of gold.
Having fulfilled the vast vows for enlightenment, he universally benefits all devas and humans.
Adorned with various flower garlands, with a crown of pure gold and wondrous jewels upon his head,
his radiant and sublime purity surpasses that of all devas, and his majestic dignity exceeds that of the lords of the world.
The halo encircles him like a flowing rainbow; his outer appearance is as bright as the pure lunar disc.
His cranial protuberance rises majestically like Mount Sumeru; he sits upright in solemn dignity like the rising sun.
A golden girdle of exquisite hue is fastened at his waist; manifesting marks of supreme excellence, he radiates light.
A lower garment of antelope skin from the Eṇeya deer is worn, which brings joy to all who behold it.
The wondrous body is adorned with various marks, A mass of gathered jewels like the king of mountains;
From his waist hang exquisite, pure robes, Appearing everywhere like clouds in infinite colors.
With three lines of pearls interlaced as a network, It is like the wondrously adorned body of a world-ruler;
Constantly emitting pure light that illuminates everywhere, It is also like the bright sun traveling through the realm of space.
The color of his body is pure and wondrous like a mountain of gold, And again like a cluster of campaka flowers;
Adorned with white necklaces as his ornaments, Like a white dragon king encircling his body.
The Lord of the World holds a wondrous lotus flower in his hand;
its color is like a mass of exquisite, refined gold, with a stem made of lapis lazuli.
Through the power of his great compassion, it is caused to blossom, surpassing all that exists among gods and humans, radiating light everywhere like the orb of the sun.
Appearing like Mount Sumeru, its fragrance perfumes all things. Toward malevolent spirits,
bhūtas, and the like, as well as black snakes, intoxicated elephants, and lions—
those whose compassionate hearts are obscured by the fire of delusion, poison, and malice— and toward all other various perils, [may it prevail].
Afflicted and oppressed by the bonds of heavy suffering, all beings are terrified and without refuge.
The Lord of the World, with a single flavor of great compassion, impartially rescues those classes of sentient beings;
seated upon a supreme throne of wondrous jewel-leaved stone, he is supported by an incomparable lotus.
Accomplished through hundreds of thousands of sublime merits, surrounded by a multitude of exquisite lotuses;
with a most wondrous bodily radiance of pure color, realized from the true ultimate meaning—
may all the various celestial beings offer supreme and sublime offerings and together praise your virtuous merit.
By generating a pure intention toward the Honored One, one swiftly leaves behind all sorrow and fear;
together with one's kin, one enjoys happiness and delight, and all sublime fruits are fully perfected.
The Dragon King of the Great Ocean dwells in his own palace, as do the various hosts of dragons in other abodes;
they constantly fear the great bird-king Garuḍa, who seizes and mangles them, causing them to undergo manifold sufferings.
There may be sentient beings who enter the great ocean, Encountering winds that stir waves like the Snowy Mountains;
If they meet a makara coming to swallow them, They will be terrified and panicked, with no one to save them.
Should one encounter a maddened elephant in pursuit, or be entangled in various kinds of calamities and hardships,
by mindfully recollecting the Honored One of Great Compassion with a sincere heart, all such things will be free from sorrow and fear.
In Mount Daishaku there is a cavernous grotto; The cave is deep and dark, most terrifying.
Those who have violated the king’s law with their bodies bound in chains, Are cast into it, fettered in every way.

Those sentient beings afflicted by various sufferings, Who mindfully recollect the Honored One of Great Compassion with a sincere heart, Are liberated from shackles and their suffering is eliminated; They shall be free from all sorrow and find peace and happiness.
With the pure hands of great compassion, O Benevolent One, you gather in and sustain all sentient beings who remember you;
you cause them to obtain the joy of sorrowless peace and security amidst all calamities and hardships.
I now praise the Lord of Men and Gods, the most supreme and majestic Great Sage King;
the cataracts of the three poisons are entirely eliminated, and his merit and wisdom are boundless like the great ocean.
Taming sentient beings without weariness, Bestowing benefit and joy equally upon both enemies and kin,
May all supreme merits be fully accomplished Upon this wondrous golden mountain of the Bodhisattva.
Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, may you extinguish the minds of sentient beings clouded by false views;
may you swiftly attain the unsurpassed body of a Tathāgata, and may all sentient beings universally realize this attainment.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Samyaktvānyathāvihārin who came from the eastern void through the air and arrived at the summit of the Cakravāḍa mountain range of this world-system, pressing the ground with his foot.
At that time, this world shook in six ways and was transformed into an infinite array of various jewels as adornments.

Furthermore, his body emitted a great radiance that eclipsed all the light of Śakra, Brahmā, the World Protectors, the eight classes of beings including devas and nāgas, and the light of the sun, moon, stars, and lightning, making them all appear like masses of ink.

This light shone universally upon those in the hells, the hungry ghosts, the animals, and the realm of King Yama, as well as all other suffering sentient beings; their karmic defilements were eliminated, and their bodies and minds became pure.

Furthermore, throughout all Buddha-fields, they universally raise clouds of every kind of offering, raining down flowers, incense, necklaces, robes, banners, and canopies; with all such articles of adornment, they make offerings to the Buddhas.

Furthermore, by means of his supernormal powers, he manifested his body within all palaces according to the inclinations of the hearts of sentient beings, causing all who saw him to rejoice; thereafter, he proceeded to the place where the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara was.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara said to Sudhana:
"Good son, do you see the Bodhisattva Samyaktva-aviśiṣṭa-caryā coming here into this great assembly at the site of enlightenment?"
Sudhana replied, “Indeed! I have seen it.”
He said: "Good son! You should go and ask the Bodhisattva how one should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having attained the profound wisdom that enters the gate of great compassion from the presence of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, observed with a profound mind in accordance with reality, his heart never wearying or becoming fatigued.
He prostrated himself single-mindedly at the feet of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, circumambulated him countless times, respectfully received his instructions, took his leave, and departed.
He went to where the Bodhisattva Samantagāmin was, prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice, nor how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Having heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction and guidance, I pray that you will explain this to me.
The Bodhisattva replied:
"Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'Universal Gate, Immovable and Swift Movement.'"
Sudhana said, “Noble One, under which Buddha did you attain this liberation?”
"How far is that buddha-field from here?
How long has it been since you set out?
The bodhisattva replied:
“Good son! Such a realm is profoundly deep and difficult to understand; it cannot be comprehended by any in the world—gods, humans, asuras, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas.”

Only those bodhisattvas who possess the most supreme diligence, who are endowed with the bodhisattva practices, who are without retreat or cowardice, who have already been able to draw near to spiritual friends, who are embraced by virtuous companions, who are remembered by all Buddhas, who increase their roots of goodness, and whose aspirations are pure;
who have attained the faculties of a bodhisattva and possess the eye of wisdom, are able to hear, retain, understand, and enter [the Dharma].
Sudhana said: "I pray only that the Noble One will explain this for me.
Relying upon the power of the Buddha's majestic spirit and the power of the spiritual friend, I shall be able to believe, receive, understand, and enter into it."
The Bodhisattva replied,
“Good son! I have come from the world-system called Samantabhadraśrīgarbha, from the presence of the Buddha Samantabhadrasambhava, to this land.”
"Good son! I obtained this Dharma-door from that Buddha;
since departing from there, an unspeakably unspeakable number of kalpas, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields, have already passed."
In each and every thought-moment, I take steps as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
with each step, I pass through worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

In each and every world, I enter everywhere, approaching the presence of those Buddhas with the most supreme mind, making offerings with exquisite articles of worship, and bestowing gifts upon the ocean-like assembly of all sentient beings.
All these offerings are accomplished by the unsurpassed mind, sealed by the unconditioned Dharma, approved by all Tathāgatas, and praised by all Bodhisattvas.

"Good son! Furthermore, I universally behold all sentient beings within that world; I fully know their minds and fully know their faculties, and according to their inclinations and desires, I manifest my body and preach the Dharma.
Whether by emitting light or bestowing wealth and treasures, I employ various skillful means to teach, transform, benefit, bring joy to, and mature them, without ever ceasing."
It is likewise from the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and from above and below.

Good son, I have attained only this bodhisattva liberation of the "Universal Gate’s Immovable and Swift Movement," which enables one to swiftly reach all places; yet it does not compare to the universal conduct of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who follow it so as to reach everywhere throughout the ten directions.
The realm of wisdom is equal and without distinction;
they skillfully manifest their bodies, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
They reach all paths and enter all lands; they know all phenomena and contemplate all worlds as equal. They expound all dharma-gates and possess deep faith and joy in all sublime practices.
Simultaneously illuminating all sentient beings, they give rise to no discrimination regarding the various Buddhas and encounter no obstacles in any place.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son! To the south there is a city named Gate-Master, within which dwells a deity named Mahādeva.
Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the Bodhisattva’s feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.

Chapter on Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation through the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra.

At that time, the youth Sudhana entered the vast conduct of the bodhisattvas; with right mindfulness and reflection, his mind was free from obstruction as he sought the sphere of bodhisattva wisdom, beheld the miraculous feats of bodhisattvas, contemplated the supreme merits of bodhisattvas, donned the armor of firm and diligent progress of bodhisattvas, gave rise to the great joy of bodhisattvas, advanced toward the inconceivable of bodhisattvas, roamed the great sovereignty of bodhisattvas, cultivated the stages of bodhisattva merit, observed the stages of bodhisattva samādhi, dwelt in the stages of bodhisattva dhāraṇī, fulfilled the stages of bodhisattva great vows, attained the stages of bodhisattva eloquence, and perfected the stages of bodhisattva powers.
Proceeding by stages, he arrived at that city and inquired, "Where is Mahādeva now? Everyone replied,
"He is within this city, manifesting a vast body, seated upon a high and prominent throne, preaching the Dharma to the assembly."
Having heard this, Sudhana went to where he was, prostrated at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path."
"I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction; I pray that you will speak for me.

At that moment, Mahādeva immediately extended his four arms, took up the waters of the four oceans, washed his own face, and holding various golden flowers, scattered them over Sudhana and addressed him, saying:
"O son of good family!
"How most wonderful and rare!
You are thus able to seek out a spiritual friend in this way.
Well done, son of good family!"

The appearance of all Bodhisattvas in the world is most exceedingly rare; it is difficult to hear of and difficult to behold. They are like the *puṇḍarīka* flower among sentient beings; they serve as a refuge and a rescue in places of peril and hardship.
They are like a city of peace providing great illumination in the midst of darkness, just like the bright sun.
Furthermore, they are like a guide who leads all sentient beings into the gateway of the Buddha-dharma, and like a valiant general who is well able to protect the city of omniscience.

"Good son! A bodhisattva such as this is difficult to encounter; only after one’s body, speech, and mind are fully purified and free from all faults can one then behold their physical form, hear their eloquence, and have them ever present before one at all times."
“Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called ‘Cloud Net. Sudhana said:
“Noble One! What is the sphere of liberation of the Cloud-Net?

At that time, Mahādeva manifested before Sudhana various heaps of gold, heaps of silver, heaps of lapis lazuli, heaps of crystal, heaps of mother-of-pearl, heaps of agate, heaps of maṇi jewels, heaps of stainless-treasury jewels, heaps of Vairocana jewels, heaps of jewels universally manifesting in the ten directions, heaps of jeweled crowns, heaps of jeweled seals, heaps of jeweled garlands, heaps of jeweled earrings, heaps of jeweled bracelets, heaps of jeweled chains, heaps of jeweled bells, heaps of jeweled necklaces, heaps of jeweled nets, heaps of various colored maṇi jewels, heaps of all kinds of jewel ornaments, and heaps of various wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels; each of these accumulations was as vast as a great mountain.

Furthermore, he manifested all kinds of flowers, all kinds of incense, all kinds of garlands, all kinds of parasols, all kinds of banners, all kinds of pennants, all kinds of ointments, all kinds of powdered incense, all kinds of garments, all kinds of music, and all manner of implements for the enjoyment of the five desires, each as vast as mountain ranges; he also manifested countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of young maidens.
Then that Mahādeva said to Sudhana:
"O son of good family!

Now, as you please, take these things to make offerings to the Tathāgata, cultivate various merits, and bestow them upon all beings; by demonstrating the ability to relinquish what is difficult to give, cause them to train in the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā)."

"Good son! Just as I have manifested these objects for you to teach you to practice giving, so it shall be for all sentient beings without exception; through the power of the habitual perfuming of these roots of goodness from such giving, I shall cause them to extinguish the obstructive mind that is unwilling to practice superior deeds, so that they may reverently make offerings to the Buddhas, Dharma, Sangha, and spiritual friends—the most supreme fields of merit—planting various roots of goodness, increasing wholesome dharmas, and resolving to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi."
"Furthermore, good son!
If there are sentient beings who are greedily attached to the five desires and are self-indulgent, for their sake he manifests impure realms."
Why is this? Because those sentient beings are deluded by ignorance; their minds are intoxicated by the charms of women, just like infants who lack self-nature.
They are also like plain white cloth that easily takes dye; they are submerged by desire and cannot emerge from it.
Like worms in excrement who delight in dwelling within it;
like filthy pigs who adorn their bodies with impurity;
like criminals bound by various fetters.
They are like worldly bandits who constantly plunder the wealth of the Dharma;
they are like those condemned to the ultimate punishment who are about to be handed over to the executioner;
they are like the blind leading the blind, both falling together into pits and precipices.
It is like a ship sailing upon the sea that encounters a malignant wind, whereby its roots of goodness are damaged and its treasures of the Dharma are lost;
it is like being near a malevolent dragon whose poisonous breath infects one, causing one to be forever deprived of the fragrance of precepts and bringing premature ruin to the life of wisdom.

In short, foolish infants are blinded by desire, bound by desire, driven by desire, and deluded by desire; they constantly follow their desirous minds as servants, always turning according to desire like a calf following its mother, and being fettered by desire, they lack self-mastery.
"Good son! Out of compassion for these beings who are blind and ignorant, I employ skillful means to rescue and deliver them.
First, I manifest the body of a beautiful and lovely woman to please their hearts and cause them to become attached; then—"
Furthermore, he manifested the end of his life, his body decaying and putrefying, being devoured by various birds and beasts, appearing as utterly impure as a *śītavana* (charnel ground).

He further manifested the terrifying form of a rākṣasī, her body like a black cloud, her hair crimson, her great belly hanging down, her canine teeth protruding upward, adorned with human skulls, holding a sharp sword in her hand and emitting a great, evil sound.
I manifest such a body before those who are immersed in desire to cause them to give rise to revulsion and to feel dread and fear in their hearts.

By means of this, they develop the aspiration to see my true nature; I then assume a form corresponding to theirs to preach the Dharma for them, causing them to eliminate their aversion and fear, to abide securely in the aggregate of ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*), and to accomplish the supreme perfection of morality (*śīlapāramitā*). Thus, they become fully endowed with the ten gates of the perfections (*pāramitāmukha*) and eventually perfect the sublime fruit of Bodhi.
At that time, Mahādeva praised the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā) to Sudhana in various ways, speaking these verses:
"Just as all sentient beings and plants and trees, All grow and flourish depending upon the earth,
So too do all mundane and supramundane roots of goodness Depend upon the ground of supreme ethical discipline."
To seek rebirth in a good realm without the precepts is like a bird wishing to fly through the sky without wings,
like a person wishing to travel without feet, or like attempting to cross the ocean without a boat or raft.
Though one may practice various austerities, eating roots and fruits, drinking water to sustain life while dwelling in the mountain forests,
or wearing tree bark like a beast living in the wild— if one lacks the precepts, one cannot attain purity.
Some shave the hair around the head while leaving a topknot, or fail to wash their hair and instead coil it into a bun;
some go naked or wear strange garments—these, lacking any precepts, are all like mere play.
Some bathe in icy rivers, while others throw themselves into blazing fires to burn their bodies.
Some climb high mountains and cast themselves down; these who lack precepts die in vain.
Some bathe in lotus ponds and waters of eloquence, or constantly drink and bathe in the Ganges;
seeking merit day and night as their reliance, these who lack precepts find it empty and fruitless.
Some bathe at the three periods of day and night, or again perform homa at those three times;
yet, abstaining from grain and remaining silent like a dumb sheep, they undergo bodily mortification without the benefit of precepts.
If you wish to dwell in celestial palaces for the full span of a heavenly lifespan,
wearing divine necklaces to adorn your body and partaking of the finest flavors among the gods, you must maintain the precepts in their entirety and perfection.
Whether one belongs to a great noble clan or to the outcaste class of Caṇḍālas, if both can maintain the precepts equally, they will be reborn in heaven;
yet if those of noble or lowly lineage violate the body of precepts, they will all fall into hell without distinction.
One of low birth who maintains the precepts is born in the heavens; one of noble lineage who violates them falls into the dark realms.
Mātaṅga maintained the precepts and was likewise born in heaven; the seer broke the precepts and entered the various hells.
A member of the royal clan, though learned and endowed with beauty and strength, may possess evil views and lack precepts like a beast or a viper;
he is like a tree of sweet fruit surrounded by fierce beasts, or like a lotus pond where a venomous snake dwells.
It is better to remain poor and lowly while constantly upholding the precepts, adorning one’s person with the jewels of noble wealth and virtue;
for those who break the precepts are despised by all, whereas those who uphold them are revered and trusted by both devas and humans.

Sandalwood, saffron, aloeswood, and musk— none of these are as fragrant as the supreme incense of the Bodhisattva’s observance of the precepts, which pervades the realms of humans and devas without end.
Even those of lowly station who maintain the precepts are reborn in heaven and are presently honored by kings with their gaze and prostrations.
The Sage has taught that such is the fruit of morality: peace and happiness in this life and in future births;
birth among gods or humans, as well as nirvana—whatever one desires shall surely be attained through the proper observance of the precepts.
Therefore, exert yourself to maintain pure morality, and all your heart's aspirations will be fulfilled.
If at the time of death one suffers pain in the limbs and joints, and all kinsmen wish to part ways,
by reflecting with clarity that I possess pure precepts, the body and mind will be joyful, free from sorrow and fear.
Ethical discipline is the supreme medicine for the disease of delusion; it protects one from all suffering and calamity like parents.
It is a lamp for the darkness of ignorance and a bridge across birth and death; it is a boat and raft upon the shoreless ocean of karma.
Śakra, the Wheel-Turning King, and lords of majestic power— wealthy, noble, and peerless in dignity—
if they have servants at home who can uphold the precepts, they shall serve, provide for, and honor them with affection.
If, when the time of death approaches, one feels peace through upholding the precepts or fear through their violation,
and desires to attain the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the future, one should single-mindedly and diligently maintain them.
The jewel of precepts requires no protection from weapons; Precepts are a hidden treasure that cannot be plundered;
Precepts are a valiant companion leading the way forward; Precepts are the ornaments for transcending the world.
I praise all the merits of upholding the precepts, as truly spoken by the Buddha, the World-Honored One;
this is for the sake of awakening those who have broken the precepts, so that their minds may remain firm in maintaining pure discipline.

“Good son! Just as I employ these various skillful means to teach and transform sentient beings, causing them to abide within the perfection of pure ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), if there are sentient beings who are full of anger, arrogance, and contention, I subdue their minds through my power.

For their sake, I manifest extremely terrifying forms, such as rākṣasas who drink blood and eat flesh, so that upon seeing them, they become struck with alarm and dread, their minds become gentle and supple, and they abandon their bonds of enmity.”

If there are sentient beings who are dull-witted and indolent, [the Buddha] manifests for them kings, thieves, water, fire, and various grave illnesses and manifold perils. Upon seeing these, their hearts are filled with dread; they come to know the existence of sorrow and suffering, and through wearying detachment from their dullness and indolence, they exert themselves and practice with diligence day and night.

By means of such various skillful methods, they cause [beings] to abandon all unwholesome dharmas and cultivate all pure wholesome dharmas; they cause them to eliminate all obstacles to the pāramitās, open all gates of the pāramitās, transcend all perilous paths of obstruction, and reach all places free from hindrance.

"Good son! I have attained only this bodhisattva liberation of the 'Cloud-Net. How could I possibly know or describe the meritorious conduct of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, like Śakra, have already been able to crush the asura armies of all afflictions; who, like the waters of the great ocean, can universally extinguish the fires of affliction of all sentient beings; who, like the fire at the end of an eon, can universally dry up the waters of craving and desire of all sentient beings; who, like a great and fierce wind, can universally blow away and shatter the banners of all sentient beings' views and attachments;
and who, like a vajra, can completely destroy the mountains of the view of self in all sentient beings?"

"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa, within the Bodhimaṇḍa of the kingdom of Magadha, there is a presiding earth goddess named Akṣayamati (Self-Nature Immovable). Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Mahādeva, circumambulated him countless times, and gazing upon him with single-minded devotion, took his leave and departed.

At that time, having received the instructions of the celestial deity, Sudhana proceeded by stages toward the northeast, heading for the great site of the Bodhi tree in the kingdom of Magadha, intending to go into the presence of the goddess Sthāvarā, who is immovable by nature.
Ten thousand earth deities were all present therein, and they said to one another:

"This youth who has come is the treasure-store of all Tathāgatas; he will surely serve as a refuge for all sentient beings, and he will surely shatter the eggshell of ignorance for all sentient beings."
This person has already been born into the lineage of the Dharma King; his head shall be crowned with the silk turban of the Dharma, and he shall open the great treasury of the jewels of wisdom.
He shall grasp the vajra-sword of bodhisattva-wisdom, acting with courageous mastery and attaining fearlessness in the Dharma, thereby subduing all heterodox paths and false doctrines.
With the ship of the Dharma, he shall ferry sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death, causing them to reach the other shore.
"With wisdom and understanding perfected, like the full white moon, you shall surely extinguish the feverish afflictions and distracted minds of all sentient beings.

At that time, ten thousand earth spirits, including the spirit Svabhāva-acala, used their supernatural powers to shake the great earth, let out a roar like thunder, and emit a great radiance that illuminated the entire trichiliocosm.

Various precious objects adorned every place; their pure reflections and flowing radiance interpenetrated one another with perfect clarity. All leafy trees grew simultaneously, all flowering trees blossomed together, and all fruit-bearing trees ripened without exception. All rivers flowed into one another, and all ponds and pools were completely filled.
A great, dense cloud arose, raining down fine, fragrant showers that sprinkled the entire ground.
Fragrant breezes blew from time to time, scattering various famous flowers everywhere upon it.
Countless musical instruments played simultaneously, producing delightful sounds; all the celestial ornaments likewise emitted beautiful tones, causing everyone to rejoice.

The devas, asuras, and even non-humans, bull-kings, elephant-kings, lion-kings, and others, were all filled with great joy; they leaped about and roared, like the sound produced when great mountains collide.
A hundred thousand treasuries spontaneously welled up from the earth.
At that time, the local earth deity addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Welcome, young man!"
"You have planted roots of goodness here in the past; I shall manifest myself for you—do you wish to see me?
At that time, Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Earth Goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and stood with palms joined, saying: "Noble One!"
"Indeed, I wish to see it.

At that time, the earth deity pressed upon the ground with her foot, and hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* treasures of *maṇi* jewels spontaneously welled up from within, opening wide and becoming manifest.
The earth deity said:

"Good son! This treasure store now follows you wherever you go; it is the fruit of your past roots of goodness and is protected by the power of your merit. You should use it as you please and with full autonomy."
"Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'Inexhaustible Treasury of Wisdom,' and by means of this dharma, I constantly bring sentient beings to full maturity."
“Good son! I recall that since the time of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I have constantly followed and respectfully guarded this Bodhisattva, like a shadow following a form.
From beginning to end, without interruption in every thought-moment, I have observed all the mental activities and conduct of this Bodhisattva.”
Thoroughly seeking out and penetrating the sphere of wisdom of all bodhisattva vows;
perfecting all pure practices cultivated by bodhisattvas; contemplating all samādhis of bodhisattvas;
conforming to, clearly comprehending, and dwelling securely in all dharma-gates of bodhisattvas; and ultimately understanding all minds.
In nature, they perfect all powers of great mastery; they increase all indestructible dharmas; they travel everywhere to all Buddha-fields;
they universally receive the predictions of all Tathāgatas; they maintain in memory and realize the nature of all-knowledge;
they turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas; and they extensively expound all [dharmas].
In the gateway of the sūtras, the light of the Great Dharma universally shines forth, teaching and taming all sentient beings,
manifesting the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas, and understanding them in accordance with reality;
one upholds, recollects, and never forgets them.
"Good son! In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was an eon named Adorned and a world named Moon Banner, where the Buddha was named Wondrous Eye;
it was in the presence of that Buddha that I first attained this gate of liberation."

"Good son! Since that time, whether entering or emerging from this Dharma-gate, practicing it and increasing its cultivation, I have constantly seen all Buddhas and have never been separated from them."

From the time she first attained it until the Bhadrakalpa, throughout that interval, she encountered Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; she served them all, honoring and making offerings to them with reverence.
I also saw that Buddha when he approached the Bodhi tree and sat at the site of enlightenment, manifesting great supernormal powers and various Buddha-activities;
I also saw all the meritorious roots and virtues of that Buddha.
"Good son! I know only this liberation door of the treasury of wisdom that is difficult to subdue.

As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who are always able to attend upon all Buddhas, uphold all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas, enter the profound wisdom of all Buddhas, and in every thought-moment pervade the entire dharma-realm; who are equal to the body of a Tathāgata, give birth to the mind of all Buddhas, possess all Buddha-dharmas, and perform the works of all Buddhas; who in every thought produce the pure treasury of dharmas of all Buddhas, remaining free from discriminative thought and ever without interruption—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?"
"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa, in the kingdom of Magadha, on the northern bank of the Ganges River, there is a great city named Kapilavastu. There dwells a night goddess named Vasanti;
go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Earth Goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having received the instruction of the Earth Goddess, contemplated with single-minded focus, retaining in his memory the Bodhisattva’s liberation door of the treasury of wisdom that is difficult to subdue. He cultivated her samādhi, studied her rules of conduct, observed her spiritual play, entered her ocean of wisdom, realized its profound depth, practiced her supreme deeds, dwelt in her great vows, attained her wisdom, and mastered her equanimity.
Reflecting thus, he proceeded by stages until he crossed the Ganges to the north and headed toward the city of Kapilavastu.

Upon reaching the southern gate of the city, he circumambulated it clockwise with a reverent heart and entered through the eastern gate. Not long after he had stood there, at the time of sunset, his mind remained in accord with the practices of all bodhisattvas; yearning to see the night goddess Vāsantī, he conceived of the spiritual friend as the Tathāgata.
Again, he thought:
"Through spiritual friends, one attains the all-pervading eye, able to clearly perceive the realms of the ten directions;
through spiritual friends, one attains vast understanding, able to thoroughly comprehend all objects of perception."
Through spiritual friends, one attains the eye of samādhi, which can universally observe all dharma-gates;
through spiritual friends, one attains the eye of wisdom, which can universally and clearly illuminate the oceans of lands in the ten directions.
While he was reflecting thus, he saw that night goddess in the midst of the sky, seated upon a precious lion throne of fragrant lotus-matrix within a multi-colored jewel-maṇi pavilion;

her body was of true golden color, her hair on the crown was deep blue-black, and her eyes were like the petals of vast blue lotuses. Her appearance was upright and majestic, bringing joy to all who beheld her. She was adorned with necklaces of various jewels, wearing crimson robes and a Brahma-crown upon her head, with all the constellations shining brilliantly upon her body.

Upon each and every pore of his body, there appeared the transformation and deliverance of immeasurable and innumerable world-systems of sentient beings; those on the verge of falling into the evil realms were all enabled to escape and attain liberation.

These sentient beings—some born among humans, some born in the heavens, some proceeding toward the enlightenment of the two vehicles, and some practicing the path to omniscience—all such images appeared with brilliant clarity.
Furthermore, within each and every pore, he manifests various skillful means of teaching to bring sentient beings to maturity:

sometimes manifesting bodies of various forms and colors; sometimes manifesting teachings through various sounds and voices; sometimes manifesting the path of the Śrāvaka vehicle; sometimes manifesting the path of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle;

or sometimes manifesting the various practices of Bodhisattvas—namely, the Bodhisattva’s valor, the Bodhisattva’s samādhis, the Bodhisattva’s masteries, the Bodhisattva’s abodes, the Bodhisattva’s observations, the Bodhisattva’s reflections, the Bodhisattva’s supernormal powers, the Bodhisattva’s spheres of activity, the Bodhisattva’s lion-like yawn, and the Bodhisattva’s playful mastery of liberation—in these various ways bringing sentient beings to maturity.

Having seen and heard this, the youth Sudhana was filled with great joy; leaping for joy and celebrating, his heart’s aspiration was fulfilled. With love, reverence, and respect, he prostrated himself upon the ground at the feet of the night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and joining his palms before her, spoke these words: "O Noble One!

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. I hope that, by relying on the majestic spiritual power of a virtuous friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), I may obtain the treasury of the dharmas of the merits of all Tathāgatas. I pray only that the Noble One will become my definitive place of reliance, show me the path leading toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and enable me to practice and progress therein until I reach the stage of the Ten Powers (*daśabala-bhūmi*).
Then, that night goddess said to Sudhana:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

"Good son! Because you are able to venerate the spiritual friend with a profound mind, the power of the Dharma and the power of the sages have entered your body. This causes you to seek diligently, not sparing even your own body or life, as you draw near with a single mind, delighting in hearing his words, listening in accordance with them, and practicing his teachings.
Because of your resolute mind in drawing near, hearing the teachings, and practicing them, you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi."
"Good son! I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door of the light of the Dharma that teaches, disciplines, and shatters the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings. Good son!"

I give rise to a mind of great loving-kindness toward sentient beings of evil wisdom; a mind of great compassion toward sentient beings who engage in unwholesome karma; a mind of sympathetic joy toward sentient beings who perform wholesome dharmas; and a mind of non-duality toward sentient beings who practice both good and evil. I give rise to a mind that brings about purity in those who are defiled; a mind that brings about right conduct in those who follow wrong paths; a mind that causes the arising of great understanding in those of inferior comprehension; a mind that causes the arising of diligence in those who are indolent; a mind that causes the relinquishing of cyclic existence in those who delight in birth and death; and a mind that causes those dwelling on the paths of the two vehicles to abide in the mind of omniscience.
"Good son! Because I have attained this gate of liberation, my mind is always in constant association with such a state of mind. Good son!"

During the darkness of night when people are quiet, and at times when ghosts, spirits, thieves, and all manner of evil beings roam; when thick clouds, heavy mists, fierce winds, and torrential rains prevail, and the sun, moon, and stars are all obscured so that no forms can be seen—at such times, I see sentient beings who have entered the sea, or are traveling on land through mountains, forests, wildernesses, deserts, and perilous difficulties, amidst all manner of danger, distress, and terror.

Whether they encounter bandits and thieves, lack provisions, become confused about the directions, or lose their way, they are filled with terror and anxiety and cannot escape on their own. At such times, I employ various skillful means to rescue them: for those in maritime distress, I manifest as a shipmaster, a king of fish, a king of horses, a king of turtles, a king of elephants, a king of asuras, a sea deity, or a fisherman. For the sake of those sentient beings suffering from various perils at sea, I provide protection;

that is to say, I stop violent winds and rains, calm the great waves, and within the swirling eddies or amidst the loss of direction, I lead them along the path and show them the islands and shores, enabling them to escape fear and attain complete peace and security.
Again, he forms this thought:
"I dedicate these roots of goodness to all sentient beings, wishing that they may abandon and leave behind all sufferings.
This is for the sake of all sentient beings on land who encounter various terrors in the darkness of night:

In places where rubble and thorns abound, and where tigers, leopards, jackals, wolves, lions, and other malevolent beasts, venomous snakes, treacherous paths, bandits, and malevolent spirits roam with violence, he manifests as the sun, the moon, the various constellations, the morning glow, and evening lightning—emitting all manner of radiance—or appears as houses and dwellings, or takes the form of multitudes of people, the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and so forth, or as bodhisattvas and Tathāgatas; through these various manifestations, he guides and protects them, enabling them to escape the calamities of fear.
Again, he forms this thought:
"I dedicate these roots of goodness to all sentient beings, so that they may all eliminate the darkness of their afflictions.

There are sentient beings who cherish their lives, those who crave fame, those who covet wealth and treasures, those who value official rank, those who are attached to sons and daughters, and those who are enamored with wives, concubines, and kinsmen—caught in dense thickets of various fetters. When their diverse entanglements do not accord with their desires, they give rise to much sorrow and fear; I shall rescue and deliver them all, causing them to leave suffering behind.

For those who encounter difficulties while traveling through mountainous and perilous terrain, I shall manifest as benevolent deities to approach them; I shall manifest as beautiful birds to sing songs that bring comfort and joy; I shall manifest as divine medicinal herbs to radiate light and brilliance; I shall show them fruit trees, show them springs and wells, show them the direct path, and show them level ground; or I shall manifest as grottoes and dwellings, or as magnificent abodes, so as to cause them to escape all sorrow and suffering.

For those traveling through vast wildernesses, perilous paths, and dense forests—where poisonous trees and creeping vines entwine in dark concealment; where *śarabha* beasts lurk to maim and wound, letting out thunderous roars that terrify all who hear them;

and who fall into these calamities, beset by manifold anxieties and fears, shrouded by clouds and mist, their consciousness clouded and bewildered, trembling with terror amidst various circumstances—I manifest a body of great power to rescue them from their perils, show them the right path, and enable them to escape. I make this vow:

"May all sentient beings cut down the dense forest of views, sever the net of craving, emerge from the wilds of birth and death, extinguish the darkness of afflictions, enter the great city of omniscience free from fear, reach the level ground of ultimate peace and happiness."

“Good son! If there are sentient beings engaged in conflict over cities and towns, even down to small animals quarreling incessantly, I employ skillful means to cause them to reconcile, so that each gives rise to a heart of loving-kindness and their discord and strife are forever stilled.”
They form this thought:
"May all sentient beings be free from the strife of afflictions and attain harmony in accordance with the Dharma. Good son!

If there are sentient beings who delight in and are attached to national territories and physical contests, seeking victory and defeat with restless minds, and who suffer from various disputes and litigation, I employ skillful means to cause them to relinquish their stubborn attachments, manifesting impermanence so that they may develop weary detachment.
He forms this thought:
"May all sentient beings not be attached to the aggregates (skandhas) and abide in the realm of the omniscience (sarvajñatā) of all Buddhas. Noble son!

If there are sentient beings who delight in and cling to villages, who crave and love their dwellings, who constantly abide in darkness, who willingly endure bondage, and who undergo various sufferings, I preach the Dharma for them to give rise to weary detachment, to bring them to fulfillment in the Dharma, and to cause them to abide according to the Dharma.
They form this thought:

"May all sentient beings never crave or delight in the villages of the six sense bases; may they swiftly attain liberation from the realm of birth and death, and ultimately dwell in peace within the city of omniscience."
"Good son! If there are sentient beings walking in the darkness of night who are bewildered regarding the ten directions;

who perceive a level road as a perilous one, or give rise to the perception of a perilous road as level; who take the high to be low and the low to be high; whose minds are thus deluded and give rise to great suffering and affliction—I employ skillful means to extend my light so that it reaches them."
If they wish to go out, he shows them the gate;
if they wish to travel, he shows them the road;
if they wish to cross to the other shore, he shows them the bridge.
For those wishing to cross rivers and seas, he provides them with boats and rafts;
when it is hot, he manifests coolness and clarity; when it is cold, he manifests warmth.
The warm palaces and cool pavilions were suited to his comfort at all times.
Whenever he went out for excursions or sightseeing, [the Bodhisattva] always led the way before him, pointing out places that were perilous or safe, difficult or easy;
whenever he wished to rest, he showed him nearby cities and residences where he might find lodging.

To those who are weary and parched from traveling afar, he shows ponds, rivers, and flowing springs so that they may drink and bathe; with flowering groves and fruit trees, he enables them to attain coolness and peace of mind and body.
If there are parents, wives, children, or kinsmen who are separated by the bonds of affection, may I cause them to be reunited and free from all suffering and distress.
One should form this thought:
"Just as I here illuminate and dispel the darkness of night, rescuing beings from various calamities and disasters, and enabling all worldly affairs to be fully expressed;"

May I universally illuminate with the light of wisdom all sentient beings throughout the long night of birth and death in the darkness of ignorance; for these beings lack the eye of wisdom and are shrouded by perversions of perception, thought, and view—conceiving the impermanent as permanent, suffering as pleasure, the non-self as self, and the impure as pure;
they are stubbornly attached to the notions of self, person, sentient being, and the phenomena of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases;
they are deluded regarding cause and effect, fail to understand good and evil, and commit acts such as killing sentient beings up to the point of holding false views.
They are unfilial toward their parents; they do not revere śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas;
they do not recognize the wicked nor discern the virtuous;
they are greedily attached to evil deeds and dwell securely in false teachings.
They slander the Tathāgata and destroy the true Wheel of Dharma;
they revile, humiliate, and harm bodhisattvas, disparage the Mahāyāna path, and sever the bodhicitta;
they even commit murder against those who have been kind to them, and harbor perpetual resentment toward those who owe them no debt.
They slander the noble and holy ones and associate with evil companions;
they steal the property of stupas and monasteries and commit the five heinous crimes, and before long they shall fall into the three evil realms.
May I swiftly, by means of the light of great wisdom, shatter the dark ignorance of those sentient beings and cause them to quickly resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Once they have resolved their minds, he shows them the vehicle of Samantabhadra and the path of the ten powers; he also shows them the realm of the Tathāgatas, the Dharma Kings; he also shows them the city of the all-knowledge of all Buddhas, the conduct of all Buddhas, the sovereignty of all Buddhas, the accomplishments of all Buddhas, and the dhāraṇīs of all Buddhas. He causes them all to dwell securely in the single body shared by all Buddhas and in the state of equality of all Buddhas.

"Good son! When all sentient beings are entangled by illness, assailed by old age, afflicted by poverty, beset by calamities, or have violated the king’s law and are about to undergo execution—being without anyone to rely upon and giving rise to great fear—I rescue and deliver them all, enabling them to attain peace and security."

That is to say: by employing medical prescriptions and remedies to eliminate the suffering of various illnesses; by serving the elderly and infirm so they may spend their final years in peace and comfort; by providing them with sufficient necessities so that they lack nothing; by acting as a master for those without a master and as a refuge for those without a refuge; and by joining forces to rescue and protect those oppressed by hardships and calamities, thereby causing them to be free from sorrow and affliction, and devoid of fear.
Again, he formed this thought:
"May I universally gather in all sentient beings through the Dharma, causing them to be liberated from all afflictions, birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and distress."

By associating with virtuous friends, constantly practicing the gift of Dharma, and diligently cultivating wholesome deeds, one will swiftly attain the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body and abide in the ultimate state of immutability.

"Good son! All sentient beings have entered the dense forest of views and dwell upon deviant paths; they give rise to false discrimination regarding all sensory objects and constantly engage in unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind. They falsely perform various kinds of deviant ascetic practices, conceiving the notion of true awakening where there is no true awakening, and the notion of non-true awakening regarding what is true awakening. Held fast by evil associates, they give rise to evil views and are on the verge of falling into the evil realms. I rescue and protect them through various skillful means, causing them to abide in right view so that they shall be reborn among humans and devas."
Again, he formed this thought:

"Just as I have rescued these sentient beings who were about to fall into the evil realms, may I universally rescue all sentient beings, causing them all to be liberated from every suffering, to abide in the perfections and the supramundane noble path, to attain non-retrogression in omniscience, to fulfill the vows of Samantabhadra, to draw near to the Bodhi of the Buddhas, and without abandoning the practices of all bodhisattvas, to always diligently teach and transform all sentient beings."

At that time, the night goddess Vāsantī, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, and spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
“This ocean of my tranquil liberation Gives birth to the full radiance of wisdom;
Far removed from all darkness of ignorance, I observe the faculties of sentient beings and preach accordingly.”
In the past, throughout boundless eons, I fully cultivated vast and pure compassion;
like the sun shining universally upon the world, you should practice it with courageous diligence.
This immeasurable ocean of great compassion of mine gives birth to all Tathāgatas of the three times;
it can rescue the suffering sentient beings of the Dharma-realm—you should practice it with courageous diligence.
It can give rise to the unconditioned bliss of the noble path, And also produce the peace and security of the world;
May it cause my heart to leap with joy— You should enter this most profound gateway.

Having turned your back on conditioned phenomena that are like illusions, and having also abandoned the vehicle of the śrāvaka’s liberation, you should constantly cultivate the Buddha-powers and their adornments; you ought to enter this inconceivable teaching.
My eye is pure, vast, and boundless, Universally beholding all lands in the ten directions;
All the Buddhas therein, Are seated beneath the king of bodhi trees.
I see the Buddha dwelling amidst the great assembly, his wondrous form adorned with the marks and signs;
from every pore he emits rays of light, each ray constantly shining everywhere.
Seeing all living beings fallen into the ocean of karma, dying here and being born there in their various differences,
