they revolve in succession through the five destinies, constantly undergoing manifold and boundless sufferings.
My ears are pure and their measure is boundless; in a single thought-moment, they hear throughout all oceans of lands.
All the languages and dharmas of sentient beings, I remember and uphold them all without any loss.
And when I hear the various Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma, their voices are sublime and peerless;
all their words, explanations, and skillful means, I remember and uphold without forgetfulness.
My nose is vast and exceedingly pure; It is unattached to any phenomena.
Abiding in the gate of liberation that reaches all places, You should enter this without doubt.

My tongue’s radiance has the appearance of red copper; endowed with pure and wondrous eloquence, I skillfully proclaim the sublime Dharma to accord with the minds of all beings. You should enter into this without doubt.
My body is free from marks and eternally pure; it constantly pervades all worlds.
Universally following the minds of sentient beings according to their faith and delight, I manifest a form-body so that they may behold me.
My mind is free from attachment and devoid of all defilements; Like an echo, it universally responds to all sentient beings.
In accordance with their thoughts, they all behold the Tathāgatas, Yet within this, I make no discriminations.
The inconceivable oceans of sentient beings in all lands, their every aspiration and faculty—
I am able to know them all in a single thought-moment, yet within that, I do not engage in discrimination.
By means of my vast and wondrous supernormal powers, I universally shake inconceivable Buddha-fields;
through the radiance of my majestic power, there is nowhere it does not appear, subduing all beings who are difficult to tame.
My merit is vast and exceedingly pure, An inexhaustible treasury of immeasurable adornments;
It can universally make offerings to all Tathāgatas, Equally bestowing happiness upon all sentient beings.
My wisdom is vast and exceedingly pure; I have thoroughly realized the boundless ocean of all dharmas.
I universally sever the doubts of all sentient beings; Sons of the Buddha, you should skillfully practice and learn this.
I know the ocean of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, And have fully realized the ocean of all phenomena;
I also enter those gates of great vows— This peerless conduct should be cultivated.

Within the atoms of the lands of the three periods of time, I see all the oceans of lands in the ten directions, and I also see all the Buddhas therein; this is the peerless power of the Universal Gate.
Throughout all lands in the ten directions, one everywhere beholds the Great Wisdom Vairocana;
seated upon the site of enlightenment within every atom of dust, he proclaims the wondrous Dharma with a voice of profound stillness.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the night goddess Vasanti:
"How long has it been since you first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?"
"How long has it been since you attained this liberation, that you possess such great power of majestic virtue and are able to bring such benefit to sentient beings?
The night goddess replied,
"O Son of the Buddha!..."

I recall that in the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was an eon named Tranquil Light and a world named Source of Auspicious Jewels, in which five hundred billion buddhas appeared.
In that world, there was a continent named Jewel Moon Lamp Light;
there was a city named Lotus Light;

and there was a wheel-turning king named Wondrous Dharma Shore, who possessed the seven treasures, ruled over the four continents, and brought peace and happiness to sentient beings through the noble path of kings.
The king had a queen named Dharmajñānacandrā who amused herself with music and song; after a long time, she fell asleep at night.

At that time, to the east of that city, there was a great forest called the Forest of Tranquil Birth of Sublime Virtue (*Śāntasambhavasadguṇa*). Within it stood a great Bodhi tree named Adorned Body of the King of Maṇi-jewels of All Supreme Dharmas (*Sarvavijayadharmamaṇirājavyūhadeha*), which brought forth the light of the spiritual powers of all Buddhas.

"At that time, there was a Buddha named Sarvadharmamahānirghoṣarāja who, beneath this tree, attained equal and perfect enlightenment, emitting a vast radiance of immeasurable colors called 'The Universal Illumination of All Wondrous Jewel Worlds by the King of Maṇis.'"

Within the city was a night goddess named Pure Moonlight (*Vimalacandraprabhā*). She went to the place where the King’s consort, Dharmamati-candrā, was staying, and by causing her body ornaments, necklaces, and girdles to ring out, she awakened the lady and addressed her thus:

"Lady, you should know that the Tathāgata Great Roar of All Dharmas (*Sarvadharma-mahānirghoṣa-rāja*) has attained perfect enlightenment amidst the Great Forest of Wondrous Virtue Born of Tranquility. Furthermore, he extensively praises the merits, sovereign spiritual powers, and all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. This shall cause the King’s consort to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and to make offerings, pay respect to, and serve that Buddha, as well as the assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas."
"Good son! At that time, was the king’s consort Dharmajñānacandrā anyone else?
It was I myself."

Because I gave rise to the bodhicitta before that Buddha, and because I planted roots of goodness through deep and profound love and respect, for as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, I was not born in the evil realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals; nor was I born into lowly families. My faculties were complete, I was free from all suffering, and my merit and virtue were preeminent among gods and humans. I was never born in an evil age, and I have always remained inseparable from Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and great spiritual friends.

He constantly planted roots of goodness in that place for as many eons as there are atoms in eighty billion Mount Sumerus, always experiencing peace and happiness, yet he had not yet fulfilled the faculties of a bodhisattva.
After this kalpa has passed, and further ten thousand kalpas have elapsed, prior to the Bhadrakalpa, there was a kalpa named Aśokasamantaprabha, and the world was named Vimalavaraśrī.
In that world, purity and impurity were intermingled, and five hundred buddhas appeared therein.
The first of these buddhas was named Sumeruketu-mahāśānti-śrīcakṣus Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
at that time, I was the daughter of the elder Yaśas, named Prajñāprabhā, beautiful and exquisite, endowed with all the marks of human excellence.

“By the power of her original vow, that Night Goddess Pure Moon acts as the presiding Night Goddess named Wondrous Pure Eye within the city of King of Multicolored Banners in the world-system of Stainless Supreme Virtue, consisting of a single four-continent world.

Once, while I was sleeping late at night by my parents’ side, that Wondrous Pure Eye came to me, shaking my dwelling and emitting a great radiance as she manifested her body. She praised the virtues of the Buddha, saying that the Tathāgata sat beneath the Bodhi tree having just attained perfect enlightenment; she exhorted me, my parents, and all our kinsmen to go quickly to see the Buddha.”
Acting as my guide, he led me to the presence of the Buddha, where we extensively made offerings.

As soon as I beheld the Buddha, I immediately attained the Samādhi of Taming Beings upon Seeing the Buddha, as well as the Samādhi of the Wheel of Light-Rays of Wisdom Universally Illuminating the Three Times.

By virtue of attaining this samādhi, one is able to recollect as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, and also behold all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas appearing therein, listening to the sublime Dharma in the presence of those Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.

By virtue of hearing this Dharma, they immediately attained this liberation door of the light of the Dharma that teaches, transforms, and subdues all sentient beings, shattering their darkness of ignorance.

Having attained this liberation, they saw their own bodies pervading worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields; they also saw all the Tathāgatas in those worlds, and saw themselves drawing near to each of them. Furthermore, they saw all the sentient beings in those worlds, understanding their speech and discerning their faculties and natures. Knowing that these beings had previously been gathered and sustained by spiritual friends, they manifested forms according to what those beings delighted in, causing them to give rise to joy.

At that time, the liberation I had attained increased with every thought-moment; immediately following this state of mind, I again saw my own body traveling everywhere throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in a hundred buddha-fields;
immediately following this state of mind, I again saw my own body traveling everywhere throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in a thousand buddha-fields;
immediately following this state of mind, I again saw my own body traveling everywhere throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand buddha-fields.
In this manner, from moment to moment, even unto worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, he likewise beheld all the Tathāgatas within those worlds;

he likewise saw his own self in the presence of those Buddhas, hearing the sublime Dharma, receiving and upholding it, recollecting it, observing it, and attaining definitive understanding of it; and he also knew the oceans of past deeds and the oceans of great vows of those Buddhas.

I shall likewise purify those Buddha-fields that have been purified by those Tathāgatas; I shall also perceive the mental natures, faculties, physical dimensions, and diverse categories of all sentient beings in those worlds, and manifest bodies according to what is appropriate for them to teach, transform, and subdue them, so that they may attain this liberation, which increases moment by moment, until it fills the entire Dharma-realm.
"Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva liberation door of the light of the Dharma that teaches, disciplines, and subdues all sentient beings to shatter their darkness of ignorance.

As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have accomplished the boundless practices and vows of Samantabhadra, who universally enter all oceans of the Dharma-realm, who attain the sovereign samādhi of the Vajra-Wisdom Banner of all Bodhisattvas and sport with supernatural powers, whose minds are without obstruction, who give rise to great vows, and who sustain the lineage of the Buddhas—"

In every moment of thought, they fulfill the ocean of all great merits; they adorn and purify all vast worlds; they teach and bring to maturity all sentient beings through sovereign wisdom; they extinguish all darkness and obstructions of the world with the sun of wisdom; they awaken all sentient beings from their slumbering ignorance with courageous wisdom; they resolve all doubts and delusions of sentient beings with the moon of wisdom; they sever all attachments to existence with a pure mind; within each and every atom of the entire dharma-realm, they manifest all sovereign spiritual powers; their eye of wisdom is bright and clear, seeing equally throughout the three periods of time.
How could I possibly know their wondrous conduct, describe their merits, enter their realms, or demonstrate their sovereign spiritual powers of playful mastery?
O son of good family!

On the southern bank of the Ganges River in this Jambudvīpa, within the Bodhimaṇḍa of the kingdom of Magadha, there is a night goddess named Samantabhadra-vimalaprabhā. It was from her that I originally resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; she has constantly awakened me with the sublime Dharma.
"Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in reverence toward the night goddess Vāsantī and praised her with these verses:
"I now behold your pure body, Your form and features as majestic as those of Mañjuśrī.
Your majestic radiance transcends the world, beyond compare; Exquisite and extraordinary, like the King of Jewel Mountains.
Beholding your pure and wondrous Dharma-body, It is equal to the three times, free from discrimination;
It enters universally into all worlds, Without attachment to either their destruction or their formation.
I now survey all realms of existence and behold the diverse bodies you manifest;
like stars and the moon in the void, they are all seen within a single pore.
Your mind is vast and ever-pure, Pervading the ten directions like space;
All Buddhas enter therein, Their wisdom equal and free from discrimination.
From each and every pore of your body, you emit clouds of light as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field;
they pervade all the buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, universally raining down all manner of ornaments.
From each and every pore of your body, you manifest forms equal in number to all sentient beings;
throughout the worlds of the ten directions, you employ skillful means to transform and deliver them, bringing them to subdual.
From each and every pore of your body, you manifest inconceivable lands;
universally following the minds of all sentient beings, you adorn and manifest them to make them pure.
If there are sentient beings who see your body, Hear your name, and feel affection and joy,
They shall obtain the benefit of merit and a pure life, And will surely achieve great enlightenment.
Falling into evil realms for boundless eons, constantly undergoing various immeasurable sufferings,
one who hears your name and momentarily gives rise to a heart of joy shall have all afflictions and karmic deeds utterly extinguished.
Even if one were to spend eons as numerous as the atoms within a thousand buddha-fields praising the virtue of a single hair on your body,
those eons might come to an end, but the merit of your body would never be exhausted.

At that time, having praised the night goddess with these sublime verses, the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed upon her with earnest devotion, and took his leave to depart.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Seventeen;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Eighteen.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśa, by Imperial Decree.

The Chapter on Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation: The Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra. At that time, the youth Sudhana reflected single-mindedly upon the instructions of that night goddess.

He thoroughly understood the treasury of bodhisattvas born from that goddess’s initial aspiration for enlightenment—its perfect purity; the bodhisattva vows she had made; the bodhisattva perfections she had purified; the bodhisattva stages she had entered; the bodhisattva practices she had cultivated; and the path of renunciation she had traversed. Following the ocean of light of omniscience, he gave rise to the mind that universally rescues all sentient beings, and he brought forth clouds of great compassion to universally cover all things. Within all buddha-fields, until the end of the future, he was able to constantly give birth to the practices and vows of Samantabhadra.
Traveling by stages, he approached that night goddess, prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and with palms joined before her, spoke these words: "Noble Lady!"
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva practices the bodhisattva stages (*bhūmi*),
nor how one gives birth to the bodhisattva stages.
“How does one accomplish the stages of a bodhisattva?
The night goddess replied, “Excellent!”
Excellent! Son of good family,

you have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and you are further able to inquire about the cultivation, arising, and accomplishment of the stages (*bhūmi*) of all bodhisattvas.
"Good son! If a bodhisattva is endowed with ten dharmas, they will be able to bring all bodhisattva practices to fulfillment. What are these ten?"
First, they attain the samādhi of purity, constantly seeing all Tathāgatas appearing before them;
second, with pure eyes, they constantly contemplate the marks and signs of all Tathāgatas;
third, with profound wisdom, they know the great ocean of merit and wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
Fourth, they know the infinite ocean of light of all Buddha-dharmas, which is equal to the dharma-realm;
fifth, they know that each and every pore of the Tathāgatas emits an ocean of great light rays, as numerous as all sentient beings, to benefit all;
sixth, they see that from each and every pore of the Tathāgatas there issues forth an ocean of flaming light rays in the colors of various jewels.
Seventh, in every thought-moment, they manifest oceans of Buddha-transformations that pervade the entire Dharma-realm to subdue sentient beings;

eighth, they attain the ocean of the Buddhas' voices, which is identical to the languages and sounds of all sentient beings, enabling them to turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
ninth, they know the boundless ocean of names of all Buddhas.
Tenth, knowing the inconceivable sovereign power and majesty of all Buddhas in taming sentient beings.
Son of good family,
when a bodhisattva is endowed with these ten dharmas, they are able to fulfill all bodhisattva practices.

"Good son! I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called 'The Dharma Gate of Courageous Steadfastness in Universal Roaming within the Joy of Tranquil Meditative Concentration. Through it, I universally behold all Buddhas of the three periods of time, as well as the pure lands of those Buddhas, their sites of enlightenment, their assemblies, and the ocean of practices associated with samādhi and supernormal powers. I clearly see all their various names, their preaching of the Dharma, their lifespans, their voices, and their physical marks—all distinct from one another—filling the entire dharma-realm;
yet I enter these profound realms without grasping, nor is there any place of entry."
Why is this? Because one knows that all Tathāgatas do not go, for the realms of existence have been eternally extinguished;
they do not come, for their essential nature is unborn.
It is not arising, because the Dharma-body is equal;
it is not ceasing, because there is no characteristic of arising;
it is not real, because it abides in the manner of illusory phenomena.
It is not false, for it benefits sentient beings;
it is not subject to transition, for it transcends birth and death;
it is not subject to destruction, for its nature is eternally immutable.
It is of one mark, because it is entirely free from verbal expression;
it is markless, because its nature and characteristics are fundamentally empty. Good son!

When I thus knew all Tathāgatas, I discerned, mastered, increased, cultivated, contemplated, and observed the Bodhisattva liberation door of "Courageous Striding through the Joy of Tranquil Samādhi. I firmly adorned it, universally illuminated various realms, made them perfect and vast, followed them with profound depth, and dwelt at the limit of equality. Without giving rise to any deluded thoughts or discriminations, I protected all sentient beings with great compassion; with a single unmoving mind, I practiced the first dhyāna.
Stilling all mental activities and gathering in all sentient beings, with courageous power of wisdom and a heart of joyful gladness, I practiced the second dhyāna.
Contemplating the intrinsic nature of all sentient beings, becoming weary of and detached from birth and death, and dwelling in the bliss of nirvāṇa, I practiced the third dhyāna.
They are able to extinguish all the suffering and feverish afflictions of all sentient beings while practicing the fourth dhyāna;

they increase and perfect the vows for omniscience, skillfully give birth to oceans of samādhis, enter the gateways to the oceans of bodhisattva liberations, sport in all bodhisattva supernormal powers, accomplish all pure transformations, and through pure wisdom, universally enter the Dharma-realm.
"Good son! When I was cultivating this gate of liberation, I brought sentient beings to maturity through various skillful means.
That is to say:

Toward householders who are negligent and full of craving, they cause them to give rise to the perception of impurity, the perception of lack of delight, the perception of loathsomeness, the perception of exhaustion, the perception of oppression, the perception of bondage, the perception of a rākṣasa, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of emptiness, the perception of non-self, the perception of ownerlessness, the perception of lack of self-mastery, and the perception of old age, sickness, and death; thus, they themselves do not give rise to love or delight for the objects of desire, and they also exhort sentient beings not to cling to sensual pleasures, but to dwell solely in the joy of the Dharma, leaving the home life to enter the homeless state.

If there are sentient beings dwelling in seclusion, I shall silence all evil sounds for them; during the stillness of the night, I shall preach the profound Dharma, provide conditions for their practice in accordance with it, open the gate of renunciation, show the path of correctness, act as a light to remove the veil of darkness, extinguish their fears, praise the work of renunciation, extol the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, as well as the spiritual friends who possess all virtues, and further exhort them to draw near to, serve, and make offerings to such spiritual friends.
"Good son! When I cultivated this gate of liberation, I caused all sentient beings to leave behind unrighteous greed and abandon perverse discrimination;
as for unwholesome dharmas not yet arisen, I caused them not to arise."
If [actions] have already been performed, may they all be brought to cessation, so that they cannot be turned back by the realms of deluded conceptualization;

may all wholesome dharmas not yet arisen, the perfections not yet cultivated, omniscience not yet sought, sublime vows not yet produced, great compassion not yet aroused, and the karma of humans and devas not yet created, all be brought to birth;
and if they have already been produced, may they be made to increase.
I provide such favorable conditions for the Path as these, even unto the attainment of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Good son!
I have attained only this Bodhisattva liberation door of the courageous stride that universally wanders in the bliss of tranquil meditative concentration.

As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are fully endowed with all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, who have thoroughly realized the entire boundless dharma-realm, who are constantly able to increase all roots of goodness, who illuminate and perceive the power of wisdom of all Tathāgatas, who abide in the realm of all Tathāgatas, who dwell perpetually within birth and death with minds free from obstruction, who are swiftly able to fulfill all vows for omniscience, who are universally able to travel to all oceans of lands, who are entirely able to behold all oceans of Buddhas, who are pervasively able to hear and receive all clouds of Dharma, who are able to shatter the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings, and who are able to bring forth the light of all wisdom within the great night of birth and death—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

"Good son! Not far from here, on the right side of the path to the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Sarvasattvanirīkṣaṇaratilakṣaṇā (Joyful Eye Beholding All Beings).
Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
At that time, the Night Goddess Samantabhadra-vimalaprabhā, wishing to clarify further the meaning of this gate of liberation, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time appear through the power of faith;
if one possesses the vast and pure eye, one can universally behold the ocean of all Buddhas."
Behold the stainless bodies of all Buddhas, adorned with wondrous marks and utterly pure;
seated within the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment, they manifest spiritual powers everywhere without exception.
The Honored Sugata Vairocana, beneath the tree of enlightenment, subdued the Māras and attained perfect awakening;
universally following the minds of all sentient beings, he turns the great wheel of Dharma, filling the entire dharma-realm.
The Buddha has realized the profound and true nature of phenomena; His wondrous essence is tranquil and without distinction.
His form-body is pure and fully adorned, Universally manifesting to sentient beings without end.
The Buddha’s body is vast and inconceivable, pervading the entire Dharma realm eternally without end;
it manifests equally throughout the ten directions, so that there is no land where it is not seen.
The circular halos of all Buddhas are ever-pervasive, Universally illuminating all lands as numerous as atoms;
Their mutual reflections manifest boundless forms, Each perfectly round, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
From the pores of the Tathāgata’s body emerge clouds of light, vast and inconceivable, without end;
they universally illumine the minds of all sentient beings, causing their afflictions to be entirely extinguished.
From the pores of the Tathāgata’s body emerge clouds of emanations;
Each supernatural power is immeasurable, Taming all sentient beings, Causing all their sufferings to be extinguished.
The Tathāgata’s vast and perfect voice, a sea of speech issuing from the radiance of his sound,
rains down the great Dharma rain upon all living beings, causing them universally to awaken to the nature of Bodhi.
In the ocean of boundless kalpas of the past, the Buddha cultivated all practices to gather me in;
thus I am now able to behold the Tathāgata, whose reflection appears throughout the oceans of lands in the ten directions.
The Tathāgata appears in all worlds, Equal in number to all sentient beings;
His realm is profoundly deep and difficult to enter— It is not something my wisdom can know.
Bodhisattvas endowed with great majesty and power enter into a single pore of the Sugata;
that realm of liberation is inconceivable, beyond what my own intellect can know of the Buddhas' wisdom.
In this vicinity there is a night goddess named Jyotīrasapramuditacakṣus;
you should go and ask her about the practice to be cultivated, and she shall bestow upon you the path to enlightenment.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Night Goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and took his leave.
At that time, Sudhana, out of respect for and obedience to the instructions of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), and in accordance with the words of the spiritual friend, reflected thus:
"A spiritual friend is difficult to see and difficult to encounter; meeting a spiritual friend causes the mind to focus its attention so that there is no distraction."
Seeing a spiritual friend can shatter the great mountain of obstacles that are the afflictions;
seeing a spiritual friend can lead one into great compassion to rescue the ocean of sentient beings;
seeing a spiritual friend allows one to obtain the light of wisdom that universally illumines the Dharma-realm.
By seeing spiritual friends, one is able to practice the path to all-knowledge;
by seeing spiritual friends, one is able to universally behold the oceans of Buddhas in the ten directions;
by seeing spiritual friends, one attains the vision of all Buddhas turning the wheel of the true Dharma, retaining it in memory without forgetting.
Having formed this thought, he resolved to go to the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃprekṣaṇamukha.

At that time, the goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃprekṣaṇamukha empowered Sudhana with her majestic spiritual power, causing him to know that approaching spiritual friends can produce roots of goodness, causing them to increase and reach maturity; namely:
To cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can cultivate the requisites for enlightenment;
to cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can give rise to a courageous mind;
and to cause them to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can perform indestructible deeds.
To cause them to know that by drawing near to virtuous friends, one can attain firm and steadfast power;
to cause them to know that by drawing near to virtuous friends, one can enter boundless directions;
to cause them to know that by drawing near to virtuous friends, one can practice for a long duration.
To cause them to know that by attending upon spiritual friends, one can accomplish boundless karma;
to cause them to know that by attending upon spiritual friends, one can practice immeasurable paths;
to cause them to know that by attending upon spiritual friends, one can attain swift power and travel universally to all lands.
He caused [the youth] to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), one is able to reach all ten directions without ever leaving one's original place.
At that time, the youth Sudhana suddenly had this thought:
"By drawing near to spiritual friends, one is able to courageously and diligently cultivate the path to omniscience (sarvajñatā)."
By associating with spiritual friends, one can swiftly give birth to the ocean of great vows;
by associating with spiritual friends, one can, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings, undergo boundless suffering throughout all future kalpas;
by associating with spiritual friends, one can don the armor of courageous diligence so that, within a single atom, the sound of preaching the Dharma pervades the entire dharma-realm.
By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to swiftly travel to the oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions;
by associating with spiritual friends, one cultivates the practices of a bodhisattva within a single pore for as many eons as remain until the end of the future;
by associating with spiritual friends, one performs the practices of a bodhisattva in every thought-moment, ultimately dwelling securely on the stage of omniscience.
By associating with spiritual friends, one can enter the path of adornments of the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
by associating with spiritual friends, one constantly takes the dharma-realm as one's object, never wavering or departing from it, yet is able to travel everywhere to boundless lands;
by associating with spiritual friends, one can constantly and universally enter the gate of the pure dharma-realm, free from notions of coming and going, and travel throughout the ten directions.

At that time, having formed this thought, the youth Sudhana went to where the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā was. He saw that night goddess within the assembly of the Tathāgata’s place of enlightenment, seated upon a lion throne of the Lotus Treasury, having entered the gate of liberation called the "Stainless Banner of Universal Joy and Great Speed. From every single pore of her body, she emitted clouds of immeasurable varieties of transformation bodies;
according to what was appropriate for each, she preached the Dharma with wondrous voices, universally gathering all immeasurable sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice and obtain benefit.
That is to say:

they emit clouds of immeasurable transformation bodies that fill all worlds throughout the ten directions, proclaiming the bodhisattva practice of the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*). They are entirely without attachment to any thing; they bestow gifts universally upon all sentient beings; they perceive the single characteristic of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) with an impartial mind; they provide offerings and service without any condescension; and they are able to relinquish both internal and external things that are difficult to give up.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issued forth clouds of transformation bodies as numerous as all sentient beings, filling the entire Dharma-realm. Appearing before all beings everywhere, they proclaimed the upholding of pure precepts without any transgression; the cultivation of various ascetic practices, all brought to complete perfection; being without any dependence upon worldly things; and having no attachment to any sensory objects.

They spoke of wandering back and forth through the cycle of birth and death; of the rise and fall, and the suffering and joy of humans and devas; that all sensory realms are impure; that all conditioned phenomena are impermanent; that all outflows are suffering and devoid of flavor; and that all dharmas are empty and without self.

Causing all sentient beings to abandon conceptual mind, false views, and inversions, and to abide in the realm of the Tathāgata; to realize the inconceivable permanence, bliss, self, and purity; to ultimately and truly uphold the precepts of the Tathāgata; and thus expounding various modes of conduct regarding these precepts, so that the fragrance of the precepts universally perfumes all, causing all sentient beings to attain full maturity.
Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issued forth clouds of various bodies equal in number to all sentient beings, proclaiming the ability to endure all manner of suffering.
That is to say:

when subjected to cutting, slicing, beating, scolding, or insults and humiliation, their minds remained serene and free from anger; they accepted these conditions with composure and contemplative reflection, remaining unmoved and undisturbed. They were neither dejected nor arrogant regarding any conditioned phenomena, did not give rise to conceit toward any sentient beings, and investigated the nature of all dharmas with profound discernment.
He speaks of the bodhicitta as being inexhaustible; because the mind is inexhaustible, wisdom is also inexhaustible, universally severing the afflictions of all sentient beings.
He speaks of sentient beings who are lowly, base, and ugly, with loathsome physical forms and incomplete bodies, causing them to give rise to weary detachment.

By employing skillful means to eliminate such causes, they praise the Tathāgatas' pure, wondrously colored, and unsurpassed bodies to inspire joy; through such skillful means, they bring sentient beings to maturity.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issued forth various clouds of bodies equal in number to all sentient beings, which, according to the inclinations of the minds of those beings, proclaimed the methods for cultivating the aids to the path of omniscience through courageous diligence:
"Through courageous diligence, one subdues the enemies of Māra;
through courageous diligence, one gives rise to the bodhicitta, remaining unshakable and non-retrogressive."
With courageous diligence, they ferry all sentient beings across the sea of birth and death;
with courageous diligence, they eliminate all the hardships of the evil realms;
with courageous diligence, they shatter the mountain of ignorance through the power of wisdom.
With courageous diligence, they make offerings to and serve all Tathāgatas with minds free from weariness;
with courageous diligence, they receive and uphold the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas, never forgetting them;
and with courageous diligence, they shatter and disperse the great mountains of obstacles consisting of all heavy afflictions.
With courageous diligence, they teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
with courageous diligence, they adorn and purify all Buddha-fields;
through such skillful means, they bring sentient beings to maturity.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there emerge immeasurable clouds of bodies equal in number to all sentient beings. Through various skillful means, they cause all sentient beings to eliminate lamentation, sorrow, grief, and affliction, so that their hearts give rise to joy; they cause them to abandon evil intentions and grow weary of all desires.
They preach shame and remorse to cause sentient beings to guard and conceal their sense faculties;
they preach the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-conduct and explain that all desires are the realm of Māra, thereby causing them to feel dread.

To manifest a lack of delight in worldly sensual pleasures, they dwell in the gardens of the Dharma and experience the joy of all dharmas; following their proper sequence, they enter the bliss of profound meditative concentrations and samādhis, causing them to contemplate and investigate so as to eliminate all afflictions, praising the nature of the mind and revealing its non-arising.

Furthermore, they expound upon the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis and the sovereign play of spiritual transformations, causing all sentient beings to be joyful and content, free from delusion and fear, with pure minds and supple natures, becoming capable of receiving and utilizing [the teachings], with sharp and keen faculties, cherishing the Dharma, and cultivating it to increase.
By these skillful means, they bring sentient beings to maturity.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issued forth clouds of various bodies as numerous as all sentient beings, which taught them how to travel to all Buddha-fields to approach, serve, and make offerings to all Buddhas, as well as to teachers and true spiritual friends; they taught them to uphold the Dharma-wheels of all Buddhas with diligent and tireless effort.

Moreover, they expounded and praised the ocean of all Tathāgatas, observed the ocean of all dharma-gates, revealed the essential natures and characteristics of all dharmas, and opened up all gates of samādhi. They illuminated the realm of wisdom, dried up the ocean of doubts of all sentient beings, displayed vajra-wisdom, demolished the mountains of false views, and caused the sun-wheel of insight to rise, shattering all darkness of ignorance, bringing joy to all and enabling them to achieve all-knowledge.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issue forth clouds of various bodies equal in number to all sentient beings—manifesting inconceivable bodies of diverse colors, features, and forms—which go before all beings everywhere. According to what is appropriate for them, they expound the Dharma through various words and eloquence, providing explanations and interpretations; sometimes they speak of worldly supernatural powers and the force of merit, and sometimes they speak of how the three realms are entirely terrifying, causing beings to cease performing worldly karmic actions, to leave the realm of the three worlds, and to emerge from the dense forest of views.
In some cases, they praise the path of omniscience to cause others to transcend the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;

in other cases, they expound upon neither dwelling in saṃsāra nor dwelling in nirvāṇa, causing them to have no attachment to the conditioned or the unconditioned, and to be free from sorrow or joy regarding honor or pride;

or they expound upon dwelling in celestial palaces up until reaching the site of enlightenment to attain perfect awakening, causing them to rejoice and resolve upon bodhicitta. By manifesting such gates of skillful means and perfections, they teach and mature all sentient beings, leading them all ultimately to attain omniscience.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issued forth clouds of various bodies as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, appearing universally before all sentient beings. In every thought-moment, they manifested all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
in every thought-moment, they manifested pure great vows that fill the Dharma-realm;
and in every thought-moment, they manifested the adornment and purification of all oceans of worlds.
In every thought-moment, they manifest making offerings to the ocean of all Tathāgatas;
in every thought-moment, they manifest entering the ocean of all dharma-gates;
in every thought-moment, they manifest entering oceans of worlds as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of all lands.
In every thought-moment, they manifest throughout all lands until the end of future eons, purely practicing the path to omniscience;
in every thought-moment, they manifest entry into the powers of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
in every thought-moment, they manifest entry into the ocean of all skillful means of the three periods of time.
In every thought-moment, they manifest journeys to all lands, displaying various supernatural powers and transformations with sovereign ease;

in every thought-moment, they manifest the various practices and vows of all bodhisattvas, revealing such perfections of vow so as to cause all sentient beings to abide in omniscience—thus they act, never ceasing for an instant.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there emerge clouds of transformation bodies equal in number to the various mental states of all sentient beings. These clouds go before all assemblies of beings and proclaim the methods for bodhisattvas to gather the aids to the path toward omniscience:
the power of boundless limits;
the indestructible power; and so forth.
The power of inexhaustible strength;
the power of non-retrogression in practicing the supreme conduct;
and the power of uninterrupted continuity.
The power of being unstained by and unattached to the phenomena of birth and death;
the power to shatter all the armies of Māra;
and the power to remain far removed from all defilements of affliction.
The power to shatter all mountains of karmic obstructions;
the power to dwell through all kalpas, cultivating the practice of great compassion without weariness;
and the power to shake all Buddha-fields, causing all sentient beings to give rise to joy.
The power of turning the wheel of Dharma throughout the entire world;
by means of such powers and perfections (*pāramitā*), he brings sentient beings to maturity through skillful means (*upāya*) and leads them to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issued forth clouds of transformation bodies of various forms and colors, equal in number to the various mental states of all sentient beings. These clouds traveled everywhere to immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions, and according to the minds of sentient beings, they expounded all the wisdom-practices of bodhisattvas, namely:
they taught the wisdom of entering the ocean of all realms of sentient beings;
they taught the wisdom of entering the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings; and so forth.
He speaks of the wisdom that enters the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings;
he speaks of the wisdom that enters the ocean of the conduct of all sentient beings;
he speaks of the wisdom that delivers, matures, and tames all sentient beings without ever missing the proper time.
The wisdom that articulates the sounds of all dharma-realms;
the wisdom that, in every thought-moment, pervades the ocean of all dharma-realms;
and the wisdom that, in every thought-moment, knows the dissolution and destruction of all oceans of worlds.
It explains the wisdom that, in every thought-moment, knows the differences in the forms, characteristics, adornments, and states of formation and abiding of all oceans of worlds;

it explains the wisdom of the mastery of spiritual powers in every thought-moment, which involves approaching and making offerings to all Tathāgatas and hearing and receiving their turning of the wheel of Dharma.

He manifests such a perfection of wisdom (*jñānapāramitā*) so that all sentient beings may experience great joy, be harmonious and contented, have their minds become tranquil, and give rise to resolute understanding; seeking omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), they shall never regress. Just as he has explained the various perfections of the bodhisattvas—how they discipline and mature sentient beings at various times according to their various mentalities and diverse faculties, making them clear, sharp, and capable, enabling them to produce affection, delight, and the power of deep faith and understanding until they reach ultimate fulfillment in omniscience—in the same way, he proclaims all the various practices of the bodhisattvas for the benefit and maturation of sentient beings.
Furthermore, within each and every pore, she manifested that night goddess and the merits she had accumulated since first resolving her mind for enlightenment.
These were as follows:
serving all spiritual friends, attending upon all Buddhas, cultivating wholesome dharmas, practicing the perfection of giving, and being able to relinquish what is difficult to give;

Practicing the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*), he renounces his royal throne, wealth, sovereignty, palaces, and retinue; with a superior resolve, he leaves the household life to study the Way.

Practicing the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), he is able to endure all that is difficult to perform and all manner of sufferings in the world, as well as the ascetic practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas for their perfect purity. The True Dharma he upholds is entirely firm and steadfast, and his mind remains unshakable.
Furthermore, he is able to endure all sentient beings who direct evil actions or malicious speech toward his own body and mind.
To endure all karmic actions so that none are lost or destroyed;
to endure all phenomena with deep faith and certainty, giving rise to a mind of right understanding;
and to endure the nature of all phenomena, being able to contemplate them truthfully without conceptual discrimination.
They practice the perfection of vigor, initiating the conduct of omniscience, accomplishing all Buddha-dharmas, universally maturing beings without ever regressing;

they practice the perfection of meditation, fulfilling its purity, and fully manifesting all the requisites, all earnest seeking, all cultivation, all accomplishments, all purifications, and all fulfillments of that perfection of meditation, as well as the samādhis and supernormal powers it engenders and the ocean-gates of samādhi it enters.

When practicing the perfection of wisdom, the mind is free from grasping and attachment; all the requisites of that perfection of wisdom, its purity, the sun of great wisdom, the cloud of great wisdom, the treasury of great wisdom, the ocean of great wisdom, the practice of great wisdom, and the gateway of great wisdom are all fully revealed.

Furthermore, he revealed the gate of the perfection of skillful means in the practice of cultivation, fully displaying all its requisites, all its practices, all its essential natures, all its principles, all its purities, and all its associated matters;
he revealed the perfection of vows in the practice of cultivation, fully displaying all its essential natures, all its accomplishments, all its cultivations, and all its associated matters;

and he revealed the perfection of power in the practice of cultivation, fully displaying all its requisites, all its causes and conditions, all its principles, all its expositions, and all its associated matters.
Regarding the practice of the perfection of wisdom: all the requisites of that perfection of wisdom,
its essential nature, its cultivation, its accomplishment, its origination, its purification,
its locus, its increase, its profound penetration, and its radiance.
All manifestations, all principles, all associated matters, all that is capable of discernment,
all characteristics of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), all associated dharmas, all subsumed dharmas, all knowable dharmas,
all knowable activities, all knowable lands, all knowable eons, and all knowable worlds.
The appearance of the Buddhas to be known; the Buddhas to be known; the Bodhisattvas to be known; the minds of the Bodhisattvas to be known;
the stages of the Bodhisattvas; the requisites of the Bodhisattvas; the setting forth of the Bodhisattvas; the dedication of the Bodhisattvas; the conduct of the Bodhisattvas;
the great vows of the Bodhisattvas; the wheel of Dharma of the Bodhisattvas; and the discernment of the Bodhisattvas.
The ocean of the Bodhisattva-dharma, the ocean of the Bodhisattva-dharma-gates, the whirlpools of the Bodhisattva-dharma,
the hidden treasures of the Bodhisattva-dharma, and the principles of the Bodhisattva-dharma— all such realms corresponding to the perfection of wisdom are fully revealed;
From each and every pore of that night goddess, all these ten pāramitās were fully manifested, teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity.
At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld the Night Goddess Sarvajanapriyadarśanā, who, from each and every pore, brought forth immeasurable clouds of bodies resembling the forms of sentient beings.

That is to say, she brought forth clouds of bodies resembling those in the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, and the Abṛha Heaven; likewise, she brought forth clouds of bodies resembling those in the Bṛhatphala, Puṇyaprasava, and Anabhraka Heavens;
and she brought forth clouds of bodies resembling those in the Śubhakṛtsna, Apramāṇaśubha, and Parīttaśubha Heavens.
They bring forth clouds of bodies resembling those of the Ābhāsvara, Apramāṇābha, and Parīttābha devas;
they bring forth clouds of bodies resembling those of Mahābrahmā, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmapārṣadya devas;

they bring forth clouds of bodies resembling those of the kings of the Paranirmitavaśavartin, Nirmāṇarati, Tuṣita, Suyāma, and Trāyastriṃśa heavens, as well as their celestial maidens and hosts of devaputras.
They manifest clouds of bodies resembling the Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gandharva sons, and Gandharva daughters;
they manifest clouds of bodies resembling the Kumbhāṇḍa King Virūḍhaka, Kumbhāṇḍa sons, and Kumbhāṇḍa daughters;
they manifest clouds of bodies resembling the Nāga King Virūpākṣa, Nāga sons, and Nāga daughters.
They bring forth clouds of bodies resembling the Yakṣa King Vaiśravaṇa, Yakṣa sons, and Yakṣa daughters;
they bring forth clouds of bodies resembling the Kiṃnara King Mahādruma, Kiṃnara sons, and Kiṃnara daughters;
they bring forth clouds of bodies resembling the Mahoraga King Suvidyā, Mahoraga sons, and Mahoraga daughters.
They brought forth clouds of bodies resembling the Great Power Swift-Force Garuḍa King, his Garuḍa sons, and his Garuḍa daughters;
they brought forth clouds of bodies resembling Rāhu the Asura King, his Asura sons, and his Asura daughters;
they brought forth clouds of bodies resembling Yama the Dharma King, his Yama princes, and his Yama princesses.
They emit clouds of bodies resembling all the kings of men who arise in the world, as well as their queens, princes, and princesses;
they emit clouds of bodies of all such various kinds throughout the realms of existence.
They manifest clouds of similar bodies corresponding to all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and the assemblies of all Buddhas;

they manifest clouds of similar bodies corresponding to all earth deities, water deities, fire deities, wind deities, river deities, ocean deities, mountain deities, forest deities, deities of crops, deities of medicinal herbs, deities of trees, deities of the earth, deities of cities, deities of day, deities of night, deities of space, deities of the directions, deities of the body-hosts, deities who travel on foot, deities of the site of enlightenment, and even deities such as the Vajradharas;
pervading the ten directions and filling the Dharma-realm, they manifest various sounds before all those assemblies of beings.
That is to say: the sound of the wind-circle, the sound of the water-circle, the sound of the flame, the sound of the ocean tide,
the sound of the earthquake, the sound of great mountains colliding, the sound of celestial cities shaking, the sound of mani-jewels striking one another, and the sound of the heavenly kings.
The voice of a nāga king, the voice of a yakṣa king, the voice of a gandharva king,
the voice of an asura king, the voice of a garuḍa king, the voice of a kiṃnara king, the voice of a mahoraga king,
the voice of a human king, the voice of a Brahmā king, the sound of celestial maidens singing, and the music of all the devas.
With sounds such as the sound of the king of mani jewels, the sound of śrāvakas, the sound of pratyekabuddhas, and the sound of bodhisattvas—

through these various voices, they proclaimed the sequence of the continuous succession of merits accumulated by the night goddess Rātridevatā Priyadarśanaparivartaka since her first production of the thought of enlightenment.
The sequential continuity of the roots of goodness one has cultivated;
the sequential continuity of the arousal of the bodhicitta;
and the sequential continuity of the immeasurable pāramitās one has practiced.
The sequence of passing away from this life and being reborn there, along with their names;
the sequence of associating with virtuous friends and serving the Buddhas;
and the sequence of hearing the various wheels of Dharma of the Tathāgatas.
The sequential continuity of upholding the true Dharma;
the sequential continuity of cultivating the bodhisattva practices;
and the sequential continuity of entering all samādhis.
By the power of samādhi, they universally behold all Buddhas in their continuous succession;
they universally behold all lands in their continuous succession;
and they universally know all kalpas in their continuous succession.
Entering deeply into the dharma-realm in a continuous succession;
observing sentient beings in a continuous succession;
entering the ocean of the dharma-teachings in a continuous succession.
They know the succession of births and deaths as beings pass away from this life and arise in that;
they attain the pure divine ear and hear all sounds, reflecting upon them with various eloquences in their successive order;
they attain the pure divine eye and see all forms, skillfully observing their various characteristics in their successive order.
They attain the knowledge of others' minds, knowing the succession and sequence of sentient beings' thoughts;
they attain the knowledge of past lives, knowing the succession and sequence of events in the past;
and they attain the supernormal power of inconceivable, non-reliant, and effortless psychic travel, roaming freely throughout the lands of the ten directions in their succession and sequence.

Having attained the distinct liberations of bodhisattvas, entered the ocean of the inconceivable teachings on the liberation of bodhisattvas, dwelled in the samādhis and supernormal powers of bodhisattvas, acquired the courageous strides of bodhisattvas, abided in the mental conceptions of bodhisattvas, became the retinue of bodhisattvas, and entered the bodhisattva’s site of enlightenment—all such merits as these, in their continuous succession, were fully expounded, analyzed, and demonstrated to bring sentient beings to maturity.

When this was spoken, in every thought-moment, throughout the ten directions, he purified unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, delivered immeasurable sentient beings from the evil destinies, caused immeasurable sentient beings to be born among gods and humans with wealth,
nobility, and sovereignty, caused immeasurable sentient beings to emerge from the ocean of birth and death,
and caused immeasurable sentient beings to dwell securely on the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
Causing immeasurable sentient beings to attain the Dharma-gates of Bodhisattvas;
causing immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the ground of Tathāgata-wisdom.
