At that time, the youth Sudhana, having seen and heard all these aforementioned rare and marvelous events, observed them in every thought-moment, contemplated and understood them, practiced in accordance with them, entered deeply into them, and dwelt in them with equal accomplishment;

through the majestic power of the Buddha and the power of his own liberation, he attained the bodhisattva’s inconceivable, great, and swift power of the "Stainless Banner of Universal Joy" liberation door.

Why is this? Because she practiced together with that night goddess in the past; because she is sustained by the majestic power of the Tathāgata; because she is aided by inconceivable roots of goodness; because she has attained the faculties of a bodhisattva; because she is born into the lineage of the Tathāgatas; because she is embraced by the power of spiritual friends; because she is protected and remembered by all the Tathāgatas; because she was once transformed by Vairocana Tathāgata; because her portion of roots of goodness has already matured; and because she is capable of practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

At that time, having attained this liberation, the youth Sudhana felt great joy. Through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, he joined his palms toward the night goddess Nayanantarasamantadarśinī and praised her with these verses:
"Throughout immeasurable great eons, You have skillfully studied the profound Dharma of all Buddhas.
Universally following the various classes of sentient beings, You manifest physical forms without any attachment."
Knowing that all sentient beings are submerged [in suffering], without a lord or kinsmen, and like infants caught in delusion,
he manifests various bodies through supernormal powers and proclaims the True Dharma to bring them to subduing.

The Dharmakāya is quiescent and eternally non-dual; Without dependence, without attachment, and without discrimination, It manifests bodies everywhere to transform sentient beings, Expounding the True Dharma to bring them to subdual.
Benevolent toward the aggregates, elements, and sense bases, you realize that all phenomena are empty and free from attachment;
yet you manifest a body adorned with physical marks and proclaim the True Dharma to bring beings to subdual.
Not clinging to any phenomena, internal or external, you have already emerged from the boundless ocean of birth and death;
desiring to uproot sentient beings and lead them beyond existence and non-existence, you manifest bodies identical to theirs, reaching everywhere without exception.
With a benevolent heart, one is able, amidst all objects, to forever leave behind all desires and conceptual discriminations;
for the sake of all sentient beings shrouded in the darkness of ignorance, one manifests the Dharma of self-awakening to bring them to discipline.
With a benevolent mind, you can abide in samādhi, remaining forever unmoving throughout many kalpas;
from the pores of your body, you emit clouds of emanations to make offerings to all the Sugatas of the ten directions.
You have entered the gateway to the Tathāgata’s ten powers; In every thought-moment, your skillful means are boundless.
Manifesting various transformations according to needs, You universally gather all classes of beings.
You have clearly and thoroughly observed the ocean of all existence, adorned with the various powers of karma;
within this unobstructed path of Dharma, speak for them so that their minds may attain purity.
Your physical form and marks are like those of Samantabhadra; Pure and adorned, they are wondrous beyond compare.
According to the various desires of all sentient beings, You are able to manifest them everywhere throughout the world.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had praised the night goddess with these sublime verses, he said to her:
"O Holy Goddess!
How long has it been since you first resolved your mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?"
"How long has it been since you attained this liberation?
At that time, the Night Goddess replied in verse:
"I recall the past, spanning many kalpas, Exceeding the number of atoms within a buddha-field."
The land is named Maṇi-ānanda-prabha, and the eon is called Śānta-mahāghoṣa.
Within that land, among all its four-continent systems numbering hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas,
there is one four-continent system named Maṇi-parvata-vicitra-raśmi.
Within those vast cities, numbering in the hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas,
there was one royal capital named Gandhābhāsa-maṇidhvaja;
adorned with a perfect array of exquisite jewels, it brought joy to all who beheld it, whether gods or humans.
At that time there was a wheel-turning king, named Vipulaśarīra, who was the lord of the world;
his thirty-two marks were all perfectly complete, and his body was adorned with various secondary signs.
A mass of radiant light with the exquisite color of pure gold, born from a pristine lotus,
he rises into the air with sovereign ease, emitting bodily radiance that pervades the entire Jambudvīpa.
That Wheel-Turning King has a thousand sons, Majestic, valiant, and of handsome appearance;
He is assisted by a koṭi of excellent ministers, All of whom are fully endowed with wisdom and extensive learning.
He had ten billion queens, concubines, and attendants, all like celestial maidens who delighted the hearts of men;
they were able to accord with the King’s intentions and were gentle by nature, always giving rise to thoughts of compassion as they served him.

At that time, the King benefited all living beings through the Dharma; the True Dharma spread throughout the four continents, and the entire earth, bounded by the Iron Ring Mountains, was subject to his rule. Abounding in wealth and joy, the people lived in great happiness.

At that time, I was the King’s precious consort; my speech was perfect with the sound of Brahma, and the light from my body extended for a thousand yojanas, its radiance like that of stainless, pure gold.
Sometimes, when the sunlight has already set and the music being performed has all grown silent,
the Great King, myself, and all our consorts lie in peaceful sleep without exception.
At that time, a Buddha appeared in the world, Named Śrīguṇasāgara;
He manifested immeasurable powers of supernatural penetration, Pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions.
Furthermore, they emit immeasurable oceans of light, equal in number to the atoms within all lands;
manifesting various bodies of sovereign mastery, they pervade the ten directions without end.
The great earth and all its mountains trembled, Proclaiming with a voice that the Buddha has appeared;
Gods, humans, nāgas, and asuras— Hearing that the Buddha has come into the world, they all rejoice.
Furthermore, from each and every pore, there emerge oceans of the Buddha’s emanated bodies and miraculous transformations,
filling all worlds in the ten directions, preaching the wondrous Dharma according to the minds of sentient beings.

At that time, during the night within my dream, I beheld the Buddha’s various supernatural transformations and heard him expound the most profound Dharma; I rejoiced with love and marveled at this unprecedented wonder.
At that time, ten thousand night goddesses, dwelling in the air above the royal palace,
simultaneously praised the Buddha’s manifold virtues and awakened me with their wondrous voices.
"O Queen of Supreme Wisdom, you should arise! A Buddha has appeared in your kingdom;
he is difficult to encounter even in an ocean of hundreds of thousands of kalpas. Those who behold him will find benefit, joy, and complete purification."
At that time, awakening from sleep with a heart full of joy and reverence, I immediately beheld a pure and wondrous radiance.
Observing from where this manifestation of light came, I saw the Buddha sitting beneath the King of Trees.
The body adorned with the thirty-two marks, its wondrous color surpassing the king of jewel mountains;
furthermore, from every single pore, it universally radiates a vast ocean of great light.
Having seen this, I was filled with joy and immediately gave rise to a vast and rarefied resolve:
"May I too become like the World-Honored One, fully endowed with great and wondrous supernormal powers."

At that time, I immediately attained awakening; I caused the Great King, his consorts, and all their retinue to behold the Buddha’s great radiance, so that their entire bodies and minds were filled with joy.
At that time, together with that Wheel-Turning King, surrounded by billions of the fourfold army as well as immeasurable sentient beings, I traveled together to the place where the Tathāgata was.
At that time, for twenty thousand years, I single-mindedly made offerings to that Tathāgata;
with a heart of reverence, I presented the great earth of the four continents made of the seven treasures, never once growing weary.

At that time, that Tathāgata spoke for my sake: An ocean of sūtras and clouds of merit, By the Buddha’s majestic power, in accordance with the minds of all beings, To give rise to an ocean of adorned vows.
At that time, the night goddess awakened me, causing my vision of the Buddha’s mind to increase;
at that moment, I made the vow to attain such a body as this, in order to awaken all those who are heedless.
From the moment I first resolved my mind upon this, I vowed to pursue the path to unsurpassed bodhi;
though wandering through the ocean of all existences in birth and death, I have been able to extinguish the myriad sufferings without fail.
Thereafter, with constant and profound faith, he made offerings to ten billion nayutas of Buddhas;
he always enjoyed the peaceful bliss of humans and devas, benefiting all living beings.
The first Buddha was named Śrīsamudra; the second was named Guṇākṣayapradīpa;
the third Buddha was named Ratnaketu; the fourth Buddha was named Gaganamati;
the fifth Buddha was named Kusuma; and the sixth was named Jñānacandraprasaṅga.
The seventh was Dharmacandraprabhārāja; the eighth was Jñānacakra-prabhāsaspharaṇa.
The ninth Tathāgata, the Honored One among Two-legged Beings, was named Ratnārciḥparvata-pradīpa.
The tenth was the Tamer of Gods and Humans, named Tryadhva-mahāprabhasvara.
Thus, for ten billion nayutas of eons, I have made offerings with a joyful heart;
yet I have still not attained the eye of wisdom to enter this profound ocean of liberation.
From this sequence, there is again a land named *Sarvabuddharatnaprabhāsa*;
its eon is named *Devamaṅgala*, wherein five hundred Tathāgatas appear in the world.
The first Buddha was Full Moon Disk Radiance; the second Buddha was named Sun Lamp;
the third Buddha was titled Constellation Banner; the fourth Buddha was named Wondrous Jewel Peak;
the fifth was Flower Flame Radiance, the sixth Ocean Lamp, the seventh Flame Auspiciousness, and the eighth Celestial Virtue.
The ninth Dharma King was named Kāyadhvaja; the tenth was Samantajñānaprabhāsa-rāja.
These five hundred Tathāgatas I have all personally made offerings to, yet even they still cherished the ālayavijñāna within me, failing to realize it is without support and imagining it to exist.
Following this sequence, there was another eon named Brahma-Light of Myriad Wondrous Colors;
its world was fully adorned with jewels and was named Cloud of Victorious Auspicious Flower Lamps.

Within those realms, immeasurable Buddhas appeared; I have made offerings to each and every one of them, as well as to the great assemblies of Tathāgatas, listening to the Dharma with reverence and a joyful heart.
The first Buddha was named Ratnasumeru; the second was named Prabhāguṇasāgara;
the third was named Dharmadhātusvaraketu; the fourth was named Dharmasāgamahāghoṣarāja;
the fifth was Dharmanirghoṣa, the sixth was Ojastejas, the seventh was Dharmabalaprabha, and the eighth was Gaganajñāna.
The ninth was Dharmajvālāsumeruprabha, and the tenth Buddha was named Meghaśrī.
To these and other such supreme Buddhas, I personally made offerings one by one;
yet, being unable to fully comprehend the profound nature of phenomena, I had not yet entered the ocean of all Buddhas.
After this, there will successively follow another eon, an eon named Moon Auspiciousness;
at that time, there shall be a buddha-field known as Sun-Lamp Auspicious Banner.
At that time, there appeared in the world eighty nayutas of Buddhas;
I extensively displayed all manner of ornaments and reverently offered them all with a profound mind.
The first was the Buddha Amṛtarasendra; the second Buddha was named Mahādrumarāja;
the third was Guṇasumeruśikhara; the fourth was Samatāratnanetra;
the fifth was Prabhāsaṃvartana and the sixth was Prabhālaṃkṛta; the seventh was Dharmasāgara and the eighth was Jitabala.
The ninth was named Lokendra-Prabhāsa-Bhadra, and the tenth was Sarva-dharma-prabhāsa-rāja.
To these and all other such Buddhas as my primary teachers, I made offerings and drew near to them all;
yet even so, I had not attained the profound and wondrous wisdom capable of entering the ocean of all most deep dharmas.
Immediately thereafter, there was another eon named Silent Wisdom Power;
its world-system was called Universal Light Cloud, adorned with adamantine, solid maṇi jewels.
Countless ornaments of manifold colors; therein, a thousand Buddhas appear in the world.
Sentient beings are for the most part pure with few afflictions; the assembly, free from defilement, is fully adorned.
The first Buddha was named Vajra-Keśa; the second was Adhṛṣya-bala-dhara;
the third was Dharmadhātu-pratibimba-buddha; the fourth was Samantāloka-daśadig-rāja;
the fifth was Mahākāruṇika-tejo-buddha; and the sixth was named Duṣkaracaryā-sāgara.
The seventh was Kṣāntiparipūrṇapradīpa; the eighth, Dharmabodhiparipūrṇaprabha;
the ninth Buddha was named Sāgaravyūha; and the last was Śāntiprabharāja.
Thus, these thousand Buddhas, headed by these foremost ones, I have each and every one of them made offerings to;
yet I had not yet deeply awakened to the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), which is equal to space and pure in essence.
Having traveled throughout all buddha-fields, I practiced various deeds within those lands.
In succession, immediately following, there was another eon; that eon was named Wondrous Birth.
The world-system was called Auspicious Clouds of Fragrant Lamps, wherein purity and impurity were ever intermingled.

Within that realm, billions of Buddhas appeared in the world; the wondrous adornments of those lands and eons, and the sublime wheels of Dharma taught by those Buddhas, I am able to receive them all through the power of my mindfulness.
First was Vimalaprabha, second Dharmasāgara; Third was the Buddha named Meghaśrī, fourth Dharmapati, fifth Guṇamegha;
Sixth was named Dharmaparvata Sumerumakuṭa, Seventh was Jñānārci-tejas, Eighth was Gaganasvaraghoṣa.
The ninth was again a Honored One among Two-Legged Beings, named Universal Birth of Supreme Lamps;
the final tenth was the Unsurpassed Being, titled Wisdom-Auspiciousness of the Light from Between the Eyebrows.
Having made offerings to all those Honored Ones among men, yet being unable to purify the unimpeded path,
there followed, in uninterrupted succession, another eon named Samudita-dṛḍha-sumeru-rāja.
The realm is named Jewel Peak Supreme Banner, adorned with various exquisite jewels.
Within it appear five hundred Buddhas, their physical bodies filling the space with supreme adornment.
I made offerings to all those Self-Awakened Honored Ones, seeking this profound and true liberation:
The Buddha of Perfect Supreme Merit, Second, Silent Sound; third, Ocean Mountain;
Fourth, Majestic Virtue Buddha; fifth, King of Mountains; Sixth, Sumeru Appearance; and Great Cloud Sound.
The seven dharmas of mastery and the eight merits, The nine blessings and the ten lights of quiescence—
To these five hundred foremost Buddhas, I have made offerings in successive order;
Into all their paths of true purity, I have universally entered without exception.
Yet, within the Buddha-dharma, they were unable to achieve the profound patience of equanimity.
Following that, after an uninterrupted succession of eons, there was one named Sukhavyūhaprabha;
the world-system was called Śāntasvarālaṃkārajñāna, where sentient beings were pure and possessed few afflictions.
Within that realm, all the Buddhas who appeared— numbering eighty nayutas—
I made offerings to each of those Honored Ones among Men, cultivating the most supreme and pure path of the Buddhas.
The first was Buddha Kusuma-puṣpa-rāśi; the second, Buddha Sāgara-garbha; the third, Guṇa-udgata;
the fourth Buddha was named Devendra-śikhin; the fifth, Maṇi-vijaya-garbha-rāja;
the sixth Buddha was named Suvarṇa-parvata; and the seventh Buddha was named Ratna-rāśi-guru.
The eighth was Dharmadhvaja, the ninth was Dhanajaya; the last was named Prajñārāja.
These foremost lords of gods and men—I have made offerings to them all without exception.
After this, there shall successively follow another eon, An eon named Thousand Auspiciousnesses;
The world-system is called Banner of Transformation of Sublime Lamps, Where billions of nayutas of Buddhas appear.
The first Buddha was named Śāntadhvaja; the second Buddha was titled Śamatha.
The third was Śāntaśatapradīpamegha, and the fourth was the World-Honored One Śrīrāja.
The fifth Buddha was named Jinavararāja, and the sixth Buddha was named Meghacārin.
The seventh is Tathāgata Sūryatejas; the eighth is Varadharma Merupradīpa;
the ninth is named Devajvālā Mañjuśrī; and the tenth is Siṃhanāda Prajñādīpa.
Thus have I made offerings to all these foremost Sugatas without fail;
yet I have still not attained pure patience to enter that profound ocean of all dharmas.
After this, there will successively follow another eon named Unattached Universal Adornment;
at that time, there shall be a world named Boundless Light Universal Auspiciousness,
wherein thirty-six billion nayutas of Buddhas will appear in the world.
The first Buddha was named Universal Cloud of Merit; The second was Space of Non-interruption;
The third Buddha was Wondrous Birth Endowed with Adornments; The fourth was Great Roaring Sound of the Dharma Ocean;
The fifth was Great Sound of the Dharma Realm; The sixth was Mountain of Merit of Wondrous Transformation.
The seventh was the Honored One of Universal Power and Majesty; the eighth was the Sound Born from the Ocean of Dharma;
the ninth was the Mountain of Merit, Lamp of the Ocean; and the tenth was the Sun King of Conforming Wisdom.
All those Tathāgatas who appeared there, I made offerings to with a joyful heart.
Finally, a Buddha arose in the world named Ratnaśrīguṇadhvaja;
I was then the Queen of Heaven named Candramukhī, and I made offerings to that Honored One among Men.

At that time, the Buddha preached a sutra for me, titled "The Gate of Adornment Free from Reliance and Attachment," which accomplishes and gives birth to oceans of all vows; I have received and upheld it all through the power of mindfulness.
Having attained the vast and pure eye, through the power of the samādhi of tranquil dhāraṇī,
they constantly perceive, in every successive moment of their continuum, the oceans of all Buddhas of the ten directions.
They attain the treasury of great compassion of all Buddhas, As well as the gateway of universal skillful means and great kindness;
Increasing their vast wisdom-mind like space, They accomplish the immeasurable powers of the Tathāgatas.
Seeing all sentient beings with inverted minds, Firmly clinging to the notions of permanence, bliss, self, and purity,
Deluded by the clouds of darkness and ignorance, They give rise to various afflictions through confusion and delusion.
Their conduct and stillness constantly wander through the forest of false views; coming and going, they enter the ocean of craving and desire.
Accumulating various karmas of saṃsāra, they fall into various realms of suffering.
Among all sentient beings within the various realms of existence, each receives a body according to their own karma;
oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, and death, they constantly endure boundless suffering in both body and mind.
Desiring to bring peace and happiness to those sentient beings, I have resolved upon the most supreme aspiration for enlightenment;
may there appear in all lands throughout the ten directions as many Honored Ones of the Ten Powers as there are.
Seeking to attain Buddhahood to benefit sentient beings, They raise great clouds of vows that pervade the Dharma realm;
From this, they fully cultivate the accumulation of merit And enter the gate of the dhāraṇī of the Buddha-way.
Arising vast clouds of conduct and vows, Swiftly and universally entering the path of non-arising,
Fully endowed with the vast pāramitās, They emerge throughout the dharma-realm without exception.
Swiftly and universally entering all stages, And likewise entering the ocean of skillful means of the three times,
In a single thought universally cultivating all Buddhas, One practices the unimpeded conduct of all stages and perfections.

At that time, I became the eldest son of the Buddha; I attained entry into the profound practices and vows of Samantabhadra, Comprehended the gates of the distinctions among the ten dharma realms, And fully realized the most profound teachings of all Buddhas.
“Good son, what do you think?

Was that Universal Monarch named Lord of the Ten Directions, who was able to establish the True Dharma and succeed to the lineage of the Buddhas so that it would not be severed, anyone else? It was none other than me.”
This was the youth Mañjuśrī.
At that time, the night goddess who awakened me was none other than a manifestation of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. Noble son!
At that time, I was the King’s precious consort; I was awakened by that night goddess, who enabled me to see the Buddha and resolve my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
From that time forward, throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields, they have never been born among the evil realms;
they are always born among humans and devas, constantly attaining mastery, and in all places they do not forsake the sight of the Buddhas, their resolve remaining firm and steadfast.

Finally, in the presence of the Buddha Jewel-Auspicious-Lamp-of-the-Virtue-Flag, he attained this bodhisattva liberation called "The Stainless Banner of Universal Joy with Great Swift Power. By means of this liberation, he was able to adorn his body with such merits, perform various offerings, draw near to all Buddhas and spiritual friends, and bring sentient beings to maturity, discipline, and benefit, causing them to cultivate sublime practices.

"Good son! I know only this gate of liberation called the 'Stainless Banner of Universal Joy through Great Swift Power. As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, in every thought-moment they go before all Tathāgatas and swiftly enter the ocean of omniscience;
in every thought-moment, through the gate of setting forth, they enter the ocean of all great vows."
In every thought-moment, through the gateway of the ocean of vows, they give birth to all practices throughout all future eons;
within each and every practice, they manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands;
and each body enters universally into every gateway of the Dharma-realm.
Within every single gateway of the dharma-realm across all buddha-fields, they preach various sublime practices in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
within every single atom of all buddha-fields, they behold the infinite oceans of all Tathāgatas;
and at the site of each and every Tathāgata, they behold the sovereign and playful manifestations of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas pervading the entire dharma-realm.
In each and every Tathāgata, I clearly see all the various sublime practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas throughout past kalpas;

in each and every Tathāgata, I see the turning of the Wheel of Dharma being upheld and protected, never forgotten; and I see the ocean of skillful means and teachings of the various spiritual transformations of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time—how then could I possibly know or describe those meritorious deeds?

"Noble son! Within this great assembly of the Tathāgata, there is a night goddess named Sarvasattvatrāṇaśriyātejorājñī (Glorious Majesty Who Protects All Beings). Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva enters the bodhisattva practice and brings to full perfection and purity all the bodhisattva paths."

Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing and veneration.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard from the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā the liberation known as the Banner of Universal Joy, entered into it with deep faith and examined it in accordance with its meaning.

He kept in mind all the instructions of his spiritual benefactor (kalyāṇamitra) without ever letting them slip, reflecting upon them with focused attention and undistracted senses. With single-minded resolve, he vowed to meet spiritual benefactors, seeking them diligently throughout the ten directions without weariness. He vowed to always remain in the presence of spiritual benefactors to give rise to all merits;

to serve and make offerings to spiritual benefactors so as to always bring them joy; to become of one essence with all the roots of goodness belonging to spiritual benefactors; and to attain the skillful means of spiritual benefactors such that nothing could destroy them.
Relying on spiritual friends, they swiftly increase their merit and enter the ocean of diligence;
dwelling in accord with spiritual friends, they never remain far from them.
Having made this vow, they proceeded to the place where the spirit Universal Savior of Sentient Beings’ Majestic Virtue resided.

At that time, the night goddess manifested for Sudhana the supernatural power of a bodhisattva’s liberation for taming sentient beings; she adorned her body with all the marks and signs of excellence and emitted from between her eyebrows a great light called "Stainless Star-Standard of Universal Wisdom Flame," with immeasurable rays of light as its retinue.
That light shone universally upon all worlds; having illuminated the worlds, it entered the crown of Sudhana’s head and filled his entire body.
At that moment, Sudhana attained the extremely pure and perfect samādhi.
Having attained this samādhi, he saw all the particles of earth and water existing between the two deities, Nayanābhirāma and Viśvapāla.

Furthermore, within each and every atom of all such things as fire-dust, vajra-maṇi jewels, and various precious ornaments such as flowers, incense, and necklaces— within each of these infinitesimal atoms—
one sees the formation and destruction of worlds as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, as well as all earth, water, fire, and...
He also saw all worlds connected together, all sustained and abiding upon the earth-wheel,
with their various forms, various retinues, various mountains and seas, various rivers and ponds,
various forests, and various palaces. All were likewise composed of the accumulation of the great element of wind.
That is to say:

the palaces and mansions of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, the palaces of the yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all with their various adornments; as well as all the dwelling places of the hells, the animal realm, and the world of King Yama; the revolving of the various destinies, the coming and going of birth and death, and the distinct differences in receiving retribution according to one's karma—these are all universally produced without confusion, and there is nothing he does not know or see.
Furthermore, Sudhana saw the various distinctions among all worlds;

that is to say: there were worlds that were defiled, and worlds that were pure; worlds tending toward defilement, and worlds tending toward purity; worlds that were both defiled and pure, and worlds that were both pure and defiled; worlds whose form was level and upright, and worlds that abide according to the mental conceptions [of their inhabitants]; worlds that abide inverted, and worlds that abide sideways.

In this way, throughout all realms of existence and within all modes of birth in these worlds, one sees this Night Goddess of Majestic Virtue Who Universally Saves Sentient Beings at all times and in all places. According to the lifespan, inclinations, physical forms, speech, and differences in conduct and understanding of sentient beings, she appears before them all through the power of skillful means, taming and maturing them as is appropriate for each.
May the sentient beings in the hells be freed from all bitter suffering; may the sentient beings in the animal realm not devour one another;
may the sentient beings who are hungry ghosts in the realm of Yama be free from hunger and thirst; may the nāgas and others be liberated from all fears;
may the sentient beings of the desire realm be freed from the fears of the desire realm; and may the sentient beings of the human realm be freed from the darkness of night.
Fear of censure, fear of defamation, fear of ill repute, fear of the great assembly, fear of being unable to make a living, fear of death, fear of the evil realms,
fear of severing the roots of goodness, fear of regressing from the bodhicitta, fear of encountering evil associates,
fear of being separated from virtuous friends, fear of falling into the stages of the two vehicles, and fear of the various forms of birth and death.
May they cause all such fears— the fear of dwelling together with beings of different kinds, the fear of taking birth during evil times,
the fear of taking birth among evil lineages, the fear of committing evil karma, the fear of the obstacles of karma and afflictions,
and the fear of various fetters through attachment to signs— to be completely relinquished, and may they be dedicated toward Bodhi.

Furthermore, Sudhana saw all sentient beings—those born from eggs, from wombs, from moisture, or by transformation; those with form and those without form; those with perception, without perception, and neither with nor without perception—all appearing before him, whom he constantly and diligently sought to rescue and protect.
This was for the sake of fulfilling the power of the Bodhisattva’s great vows and because he had deeply entered the power of the Bodhisattva’s samādhis. Firmly...
It is because of the power of the Bodhisattva’s spiritual penetrations; because of the power of the arising of Samantabhadra’s practices and vows;
because of the expansion of the ocean of the Bodhisattva’s great compassion; because of the attainment of unimpeded great loving-kindness that universally covers all sentient beings;

because of the attainment of the universal bestowal of immeasurable joy and bliss upon sentient beings; because of the attainment of the wisdom and skillful means that universally gather in sentient beings; and because of the attainment of...
Because of the bodhisattvas' mastery over liberation and supernormal powers; because of their purification of all buddha-fields;
because of their awakening to and thorough knowledge of all phenomena; because of their service and offerings to all buddhas; because of their upholding of all the buddhas' teachings;
because of their accumulation of all supreme roots of goodness; and because of their cultivation of all the [practices of] bodhisattvas...
Because of sublime conduct; because of entering the minds of sentient beings without obstruction; because of knowing how to bring the faculties of sentient beings to maturity;
because of purifying the ocean of faith and understanding of all sentient beings; because of shattering the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings;
and because of attaining the pure radiance of omniscience.

At that time, having seen the night goddess Sarvasattvaparitrāṇaśrī enter the liberation door of "Taming All Sentient Beings" and manifest her inconceivable, profound realm of supernatural power, the youth Sudhana was filled with great joy and leaped for immeasurable delight; he prostrated himself with his head at her feet and gazed up at her with single-minded devotion.

At that time, the night goddess cast off her body adorned with the various marks and signs of excellence and returned to her original form, yet she did not relinquish the sovereign power of her supernatural transformations.
At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in reverence, withdrew to stand to one side, and observing the Night Goddess, praised her with these verses:
“I behold the noble venerable one manifesting now Such vast and great supernormal powers;
This causes a heart of joy to arise within me, And I speak these wondrous verses in praise.”
I behold the noble one’s vast body, adorned with the colors of supreme and wondrous jewels;
like stars and the moon situated in the sky, his inconceivable marks and signs are all exquisite.
From his body he emits wheels of pure light, equal in measure to the atoms within boundless lands;
their various colors and forms are all exquisite and wondrous, universally illuminating the ten directions without exception.
From each and every pore of yours, O Benevolent One, there issue forth as many rays of light as there are mental states of all sentient beings.
Within these lights, Buddhas sit upon precious lotus flowers, manifesting transformations that can extinguish the suffering of sentient beings.
From within the lights, furthermore, emerge clouds of wondrous fragrance, universally perfuming all classes of sentient beings.
Furthermore, they can universally rain down a multitude of exquisite flowers, Universally making offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions.
From their eyebrows, they emit vast masses of radiant light, Jewel-light, stainless and equal to Mount Sumeru, Universally illuminating the worlds throughout the ten directions;
All who are touched by it are caused to extinguish the darkness of ignorance.

His mouth constantly emits a universal, stainless light; its radiant wheel is as vast as a thousand suns, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions—the sphere of activity of Vairocana.

From his eyes, he emits clouds of stainless radiance; The light shines brilliantly like the stars and the moon, Universally illuminating all lands throughout the ten directions, And extinguishing the cataracts of ignorance within the three realms of existence.
The various bodies manifested by the Benevolent One, With physical forms equal in number to all sentient beings,
Pervade the dharma-realm throughout the ten directions, Subduing the ocean-like multitude of infinite beings.
Emanating bodies that travel everywhere throughout the ten directions, They appear before all sentient beings,
Extinguishing the fears of kings, thieves, water, and fire, Causing their minds to be tamed and filled with joy.
Receiving the instruction of the deity Hṛṣīkeśā, I have come to serve you, mindful of your venerable merits;
I behold the light-clouds emitted from your ūrṇā-kośa, perfectly bright, vast, and free from all defilement.
This light shines universally throughout the ten directions, completely extinguishing the darkness of the afflictions of sentient beings;
manifesting various supernormal powers, it then enters my body.
At that time, encountering this Perfect Light, my body and mind were at peace and joy arose;
I attained a hundred dharanis and oceans of samadhis, and universally beheld the Sugatas of the ten directions.
In every place where I practice walking meditation, I see all atoms without exception;
Within each and every one of those atoms, I behold Buddha-fields as numerous as those very atoms.
In some realms within a single mote of dust, there are countless lands that are entirely defiled, perpetually turbid and foul;
their sentient beings have no savior and undergo all manner of suffering, raising voices of lamentation and constantly wailing in grief.
In other lands, defilement and purity are intermingled; the sentient beings therein have little joy and much sorrow and pain.
Manifesting in the forms of Buddhas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas, he goes to those realms out of great compassion to deliver them.

There are lands that were once pure but later became defiled; others where men and women are dignified and lovely, filled with Bodhisattvas and endowed with all adornments, upholding the infinite teachings of the Buddhas.
Within each and every atom throughout the ten directions, there are infinite oceans of pure lands,
adorned by Vairocana’s universal cultivation of oceans of practices in the past.
In all lands throughout the ten directions, the Buddha sits upon the most supreme site of enlightenment;
having attained perfect awakening, he manifests spiritual powers and preaches the Dharma to tame and transform all classes of living beings.
I see the Celestial King Universal Savior of Majestic Virtue, Whose body goes everywhere to infinite lands;
Within the realm of Vairocana, He serves all Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had spoken these verses, he addressed the deity Viśvapadmasupratiṣṭhitaguṇaketurāja, saying:
"How rare, O Noble One!
You are able to dwell in this profound liberation."
"How long has it been since you attained this liberation?
What practices did you originally cultivate to achieve such purity?
The night goddess replied:
“Good son! This state is difficult to know; it cannot be fathomed by any in the world, whether devas, humans, or those of the two vehicles. Why is this?
This is because it is the realm of those who dwell in the practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
the realm of those who accord with the treasury of great compassion; the realm of those who rescue and protect all sentient beings;
the realm of those who can purify all three evil realms and eight difficult conditions; and the realm of those who can adorn all Buddha-fields with unsurpassed purity.
Because it is the sphere of activity for continuing the lineage of the Buddhas without interruption throughout all Buddha-fields;
because it is the sphere of activity for upholding the true Dharma of all Buddhas;

because it is the sphere of activity for cultivating the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout all eons to fulfill the ocean of great vows; because it is the sphere of activity for [all phenomena]... all dharmas.
Because it is the realm where the darkness of ignorance is extinguished by the light of pure wisdom throughout the ocean of realms;
because it is the realm where the ocean of skillful means of all three periods of time is universally illuminated by the radiance of a single thought of wisdom—
I shall now, relying on the Buddha’s majestic power, proclaim this for you.

"Good son! In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there was an eon named Stainless Perfection and a world named Vairocana Majestic Auspiciousness, wherein as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru appeared."

That Buddha-world has as its substance all kinds of fragrant-king maṇi-jewels and vajras; it is adorned with the various jewels of the palaces of devas and nāgas, and rests upon an ocean of stainless radiant maṇi-kings. Its shape is perfectly circular, pure and free from defilement.

It is covered above by clouds of canopies made of all kinds of necklaces and ornaments, and is encircled a thousand times by mountains of maṇi-wheels of every adornment. Within it, there are hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of four-continent worlds, all exquisitely adorned.

Some of these four-continent worlds are inhabited by sentient beings of evil karma; some are inhabited by sentient beings of mixed karma; some are inhabited by sentient beings of virtuous roots; and some four-continent worlds are exclusively inhabited by great bodhisattvas who are utterly pure.

"Good son! On the eastern edge of that world, at the side of the Cakravāḍa Mountains, there is a set of four continents named Ratnapradīpapuṣpadhvaja. The realm is pure, peaceful, secure, and prosperous; rice and grain grow without the need for plowing or sowing, all through the ripening of the superior power of past karma."

The palaces and towers were all wondrous and marvelous; rows of wish-fulfilling trees stood everywhere. Various kinds of incense trees constantly emitted clouds of fragrance, while various kinds of powdered-incense trees rained down clouds of powdered incense. Various kinds of garland trees constantly produced clouds of garlands, and various kinds of flower trees rained down inconceivable clouds of exquisite flowers. Various kinds of jewel trees rained down great maṇi gems and rare, wonderful treasures, their immeasurable colored lights shining brilliantly in every direction. Various musical-instrument trees produced all manner of music, emitting sublime sounds as they swayed in the wind. The light of the sun and moon and the sovereign maṇi-jewels illuminated everything universally; day and night they experienced bliss without interruption.

Within these four continents, there are a hundred trillion nayutas of royal kingdoms. Each kingdom is encircled by a thousand great rivers, all of which are covered with exquisite flowers that drift and sway with the current, emitting the sounds of celestial music. Along their banks, various jewel trees are planted in rows as magnificent adornments. Boats and ships come and go, where people enjoy playful diversions to their heart's content, utilizing all manner of resources to experience peace and happiness.

Between each river there are hundreds of billions of cities; within each city there are hundreds of billions of nayutas of villages. All such cities and villages are each surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of palaces and gardens as their retinue.

Within this Jambudvīpa of the four continents, there is a land named Ratnapuṣpadīpa, which is peaceful, prosperous, and joyful; its inhabitants are numerous and flourishing, its palaces are magnificent and well-adorned, and it is perfectly autonomous. The sentient beings therein fully practice the ten virtuous actions.

A wheel-turning monarch appeared therein, named Vairocana-ratnapadmagarbha; he was suddenly born by transformation within a lotus flower, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of greatness, endowed with the seven treasures, ruling over the four continents, and constantly instructing all living beings through the True Dharma.

The king had a thousand sons, handsome, brave, and strong, possessing sovereign power and capable of subduing enemies; he had a retinue of one hundred trillion nayutas of palace ladies and handmaidens.

They all shared the same roots of goodness as the king, practiced the same deeds, were born at the same time, and were adorned with the same precious ornaments and necklaces; they were upright and exquisite, like celestial maidens, their bodies the color of pure gold, constantly emitting radiance, and from every pore perpetually wafting subtle fragrances; they were accompanied by ten billion excellent ministers and valiant generals.

The king had a principal consort named Paripūrṇaśrīvaktrā, who was a jewel among women. She was exceptionally beautiful and sublime; those who beheld her never grew weary of looking. Most excellent and pure, her skin was golden, her eyes and hair were deep blue, and her voice was like the sound of Brahmā. Her body possessed a celestial fragrance, and she constantly emitted a radiance that illuminated a thousand yojanas.

His queen had a daughter named Samantānandaśrīpadmanetrā, whose physical form was upright and majestic, who was fully endowed with virtuous conduct, and whose marks and signs were perfect; she was like a wheel-turning monarch, such that sentient beings who beheld her could never tire of looking.
At that time, the lifespan of sentient beings was immeasurable, though some were of indeterminate duration and met with premature death;

they possessed various forms and colors, various voices, various names, and various clans and lineages; they differed in height and stature, large and small, brave and timid, foolish and wise, poor and wealthy, suffering and happy, and in their degrees of faith and inclination—indeed, all these infinite categories were entirely distinct from one another.
At that time, some person might say to another:
"My body is handsome, while your form is ugly.
Having spoken these words, they revile one another and accumulate unwholesome karma.
Due to these karmic causes, their lifespan, physical form, strength, and all pleasant things are entirely diminished.

Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation: The Chapter on the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra.
"At that time, to the north of the city of Ratnakusumapradīpa, there was a Bodhi tree named Universal Radiance Pervading the Clouds of Dharma and Sound Banner."

In every thought-moment, it manifests the adorned site of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas: its roots are formed by the king of *maṇi* jewels, adamantine and firm; its trunk is composed of all kinds of *maṇi* jewels; its leaves are made of various exquisite gems; and its branches, twigs, flowers, and fruits are distributed in successive order, all in perfect harmony.
It is perfectly adorned throughout the four directions, above, and below, emitting the radiant light of various colored jewel-flames;
it produces wondrous sounds, proclaiming the profound realms of the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddha-Tathāgatas.

Before that tree there was a fragrant pond named Jewel Flower Radiance Dharma Thunder Sound, filled with scented water and bordered by exquisite jewels. It was surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of jewel trees, each shaped like a bodhi tree, with necklaces of various jewels hanging down all around them.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable palaces and towers made of various jewels, which adorned the entire site of enlightenment.

Within those fragrant ponds emerged great lotus flowers named "Clouds of Adorned Realms Manifesting All Tathāgatas of the Three Times," from within which as many Tathāgatas appeared as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru.

The first of these Buddhas was named Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Auspicious Majestic Virtue King; upon this flower, he first attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and, for immeasurable thousands of years, expounded the sublime Dharma to bring sentient beings to maturity.
Before that Tathāgata attained Buddhahood, for ten thousand years, the King of Bodhi Trees emitted great radiance and manifested supernatural powers to bring sentient beings to maturity.
That is to say:

ten thousand years prior [to the Buddha's appearance], he emits a pure light named "Stainless Lamp for All Sentient Beings. If any sentient beings encounter this light, their minds awaken of themselves, and they know that the Buddha shall appear ten thousand years hence.

Nine thousand years prior, he emits a pure light named "Treasury of Complete and Stainless Auspiciousness. If any sentient beings encounter this light, they obtain the pure eye and see all forms, knowing that the Buddha shall appear nine thousand years hence.

Eight thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "The Sound of the Karmic Results of All Sentient Beings. Any sentient beings who encountered this light were all able to know for themselves the distinctions within the ocean of karma and its various retributions, and they knew that the Buddha would appear after eight thousand years.

Seven thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "The Sound Producing All Roots of Goodness. Any sentient beings who encountered this light had all their roots of goodness become fully perfected, and they knew that the Buddha would appear after seven thousand years.

Six thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "The Sound of the Buddha’s Inconceivable Realm. Any sentient beings who encountered this light found their minds to be vast and universally attained mastery, and they knew that the Buddha would appear after six thousand years.

Five thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "Sound Adorned with All Pure Buddha-fields. Any sentient beings who encountered this light all beheld all the pure Buddha-lands and knew that five thousand years hence a Buddha would appear.

Four thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "Lamp Without Confusion in the Realm of All Tathāgatas. Any sentient beings who encountered this light were all able to enter deeply into the realm of the Tathāgatas, traveling everywhere to pay homage to the Buddhas, and they knew that four thousand years hence a Buddha would appear.

Three thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "Universal Illumination of All Sentient Beings, Lamp Manifesting Before One the Three Times. Any sentient beings who encountered this light were all able to clearly perceive the ocean of past deeds of all Tathāgatas and knew that the Buddha would appear three thousand years hence.

Two thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "Lightning Lamp of Wisdom of the Three Times. Any sentient beings who encountered this light then saw the ocean of past corresponding practices of all Tathāgatas and knew that the Buddha would appear two thousand years hence.

One thousand years prior, he emitted a great light named "The Lamp of the Tathāgata’s Unobstructed Wisdom. If any sentient beings encountered this light, they would be endowed with the Universal Eye and be able to see the supernatural transformations of all Buddhas and purify all lands; they would know that a Buddha was destined to appear one thousand years hence.

One hundred years prior, he emitted a great light named "Causing All Sentient Beings to See the Buddha and Accumulate All Roots of Goodness. If any sentient beings encountered this light, they would achieve the Samādhi of Seeing the Buddha and know that a Buddha was destined to appear one hundred years hence.

Seven days later, he emitted a great light called "The Sound of Great Joy and Delight of All Sentient Beings. Any sentient being who encountered this light would then be able to see the Buddha, give rise to love and reverence, and know that the Buddha would appear after seven days.

"Good son! In this way, through these various kinds of immeasurable and boundless pure radiances, for ten thousand years and even down to seven days, he tames sentient beings and brings them to maturity."

When the seven days had passed, all worlds shook with a great tremor; they became entirely pure, free from all defilement and impurity. In every thought-moment, all the pure Buddha-lands of the ten directions appeared universally, as did the various adornments of those lands. If there were sentient beings whose faculties and natures were matured and who were destined to see a Buddha, they all proceeded to the site of enlightenment.

At that time, within that world, all the circular mountain ranges, all the Sumeru mountains, all the various mountains, all the rivers and seas, all the great earth, all the cities and towns, all the walls and ramparts, all the palaces, all the music, all the articles of utility, all the necklaces and ornaments, and all the speech, emitted sounds praising and describing the miraculous transformations and adornments of the spiritual powers of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.

Furthermore, they emitted clouds of all kinds of incense, clouds of all kinds of burning incense, clouds of all kinds of powdered incense, clouds of all kinds of unguents, clouds of all kinds of fragrant mani-jewels in various forms, clouds of all kinds of mani-garments, clouds of all kinds of jewel-flames, clouds of all kinds of flame-treasures, clouds of all kinds of necklaces, clouds of all kinds of exquisite flowers, clouds of all kinds of music, clouds of the light of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the halo of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the vow-sounds of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the ocean of vocal sounds of all Tathāgatas, and clouds of the colored radiance of the various marks and signs of all Tathāgatas, manifesting the inconceivable manifestations of the Tathāgatas appearing in the world.

"Good son! This Great Jewel Lotus King, which manifests the adorned realms of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, has as its retinue as many exquisite jewel lotuses as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, surrounding it on every side."
Upon each and every pedestal of those lotus flowers, there was a lion throne made of mani jewels;
upon each throne, a bodhisattva sat cross-legged.

“Good son! When that Tathāgata King of Universal Wisdom Jewel-Flame Auspicious Power attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi here, he simultaneously attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in all worlds throughout the ten directions; according to the minds of sentient beings, he appeared before them all to turn the wheel of Dharma.”
In each and every world, they cause immeasurable sentient beings to leave behind the suffering of the evil realms;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to be born among humans and devas;
and they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
May they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the practice of enlightenment through renunciation;
may they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the practice of enlightenment of the stainless, courageous banner;
may they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the practice of enlightenment of the pure light of Dharma.
They cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of majestic power and pure faculties;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of the power of conforming to equanimity;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of entering the city of Dharma through direct manifestation.
They cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of indestructible supernormal powers that reach everywhere;

they cause immeasurable sentient beings to give rise to a mind of rare wonder toward all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas throughout the ten directions, and to abide in the bodhi-practice of equanimity;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the bodhi-practice of the gateways of samādhi.
Causing immeasurable sentient beings to achieve the bodhi-practice that takes all pure realms as its object;
causing immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon bodhicitta;
and causing immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the bodhisattva path and cultivate the bodhisattva practices.
They cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide securely on the path of the pure pāramitās;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to dwell in the first stage of a bodhisattva;
and they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide securely in the second, third, and up to the tenth stage of a bodhisattva.
He causes immeasurable sentient beings to enter the sublime practices and vows of bodhisattvas;
he causes immeasurable sentient beings to dwell securely in the pure practices and vows of Samantabhadra. O noble son!

When that Tathāgata, King of Universal Wisdom, Jewel Flame, Auspicious Majesty, and Power, manifests such inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers of a Buddha to turn the wheel of Dharma, he—in each and every one of those worlds—tames, teaches, and brings to maturity immeasurable sentient beings, moment by moment, according to their respective needs.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, knowing that the sentient beings within the city of Ratnakusumapradīparāja were intoxicated by negligence due to their pride in their own physical appearance and various sensory realms, and had consequently given rise to arrogance;
in order to subdue those sentient beings, he manifested a wondrous body, exceptionally upright and extraordinary, and proceeded toward that city.

He emitted a great radiance that universally illumined all things, causing the splendor and majesty of the holy king’s light—as well as that of all his exquisite jewels, the sun, the moon, the stars, the jewel-trees, the precious robes, the *maṇi* gems, the necklaces, and the bodies of sentient beings—to become entirely invisible;
it was as if the rising sun eclipsed all other lights, or like a mass of ink set against Jambūnada gold.
At that time, each of the sentient beings thought to themselves: "Who is this?
Is it a deva?"
"Is this Brahmā?

Now he emits this light that eclipses everything, causing all the majesty, radiance, and physical beauty of our own bodies to become unmanifest; despite our various reflections, we are unable to comprehend it."
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, dwelling in the air above the palace of that wheel-turning monarch, addressed him, saying: "Great King!
"You should know that a Buddha has now appeared in your kingdom, beneath the Bodhi tree named Universal Radiance, Pervasive Illumination, Dharma-Cloud Sound Banner.

At that time, the Wheel-Turning King’s daughter, Samantasukhaśrīpadmanetrā, beheld the sovereign mastery of the light of the physical body manifested by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and heard the wondrous sounds emanating from the various necklaces and ornaments adorning her own person. She conceived a heart of love and reverence, a heart of joy, and a heart of deep faith, and made this aspiration:
"May all my roots of goodness enable me to obtain such a body, such adornments, such marks and signs, such majestic deportment, such supernormal powers, and such awesome virtue."

Now this Great Sage is able to emit a great radiance within the dark night of the long cycle of birth and death for all sentient beings, manifesting the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world. I pray that I, too, may likewise become a light of wisdom for all sentient beings, shattering all the darkness of ignorance;
and I pray that wherever I may take birth, I shall never be separated from this spiritual friend.

“Good son! At that time, the Universal Monarch Vairocana-ratnapadmagarbha-mañjuśrī-keśa, together with his precious queen, his thousand sons, his retinue, ministers, assistants, the seven treasures, the fourfold army, and the immeasurable multitudes within the city, were surrounded by attendants before and behind. By the king’s spiritual power, they all ascended into the air to a height of one yojana. Emitting a great radiance that illuminated the four continents, he caused everyone to behold him, desiring to lead all sentient beings together to see the Buddha.
He then praised him in verse: “The Buddha has now appeared in the world, Universally rescuing all classes of beings.”
You all should quickly resolve your minds and go to where the most excellent Teacher dwells.
Only after the passage of immeasurable *koṭi* eons does a Tathāgata appear in the world to reveal the profound and subtle Dharma,
universally bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
The Buddha observes all worlds, Perpetually obscured and deluded by the inversion of ignorance;
Subject to the oppression of birth and death and the suffering of saṃsāra, He gives rise to the great compassionate mind of rescue and protection.
Throughout countless tens of millions of koṭis of eons, You have cultivated various practices for awakening;
Having perfected the most supreme mind of great compassion, You universally extinguish the suffering of all sentient beings.
Head, eyes, ears, nose, body, hands, and feet— All such things as these he was able to relinquish,
In order to realize the nectar-like Buddha-enlightenment, Throughout immeasurable and boundless eons.
Throughout immeasurable koṭis of kalpas, a World-Honored Teacher is difficult to encounter;
seeing, hearing, making offerings to, or personally receiving his guidance brings benefit to all, never in vain.
I shall now go together with you to visit that most excellent Tamer of Men,
who has turned the unsurpassed Great Wheel of Dharma and attained Perfect Enlightenment beneath the Tree of Awakening after subduing the Māras.
You should contemplate the Buddha’s wondrous form-body, Which radiates nets of light without bound;
Its various exquisite colors are all pure, Eliminating the darkness of sentient beings' delusions and suffering.
From each and every pore, he universally emits countless clouds of light,
illuminating all living beings everywhere, causing them all to feel love, reverence, and joyful hearts.
Each of you should reflect upon this and arouse a vast and resolute mind of diligence;
immediately go together to that Tathāgata and, approaching him with sincerity, make offerings to him.

At that time, after the Wheel-Turning Sage King had praised the Buddha with verses and awakened all sentient beings within his realm, ten thousand kinds of great offering-clouds emerged from the roots of goodness of the Wheel-Turning King; they proceeded toward the site of enlightenment to where the Tathāgata was.
That is to say:

clouds of all kinds of precious canopies, clouds of all kinds of flower curtains, clouds of all kinds of precious garments, clouds of all kinds of seas of incense, clouds of all kinds of precious thrones, clouds of all kinds of precious banners, clouds of all kinds of palaces, clouds of all kinds of exquisite flowers, clouds of all kinds of nets of precious bells, and clouds of all kinds of ornaments, which completely adorned and embellished the void of space.

Having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Auspicious Majestic Virtue King, circumambulated him to the right countless hundreds of thousands of millions of times, and sat before the Buddha upon a mani-jewel lotus throne that radiates light illuminating the ten directions.
At that time, the daughter of the Wheel-Turning King, Samantasukhaśrīpadmanetra, immediately removed all the necklaces and various ornaments from her body and held them up to scatter as an offering.

At that time, the ornaments in the void transformed into a great mani-jewel canopy, with nets of mani-jewels of various colors hanging down all around, held together by all the dragon kings. All the palaces were arranged in rows within it, surrounded by a retinue of ten kinds of jewel canopies; its shape was like a multi-storied pavilion, pure both inside and out, with clouds of necklaces covering it everywhere, as well as various jewel trees, fragrant seas, mani-jewels, and diverse exquisite decorations that made it magnificent and beautiful.
Within this canopy stands a Bodhi tree, its branches and leaves lush and flourishing, universally covering the entire Dharma-realm, manifesting immeasurable adornments in every thought-moment.

Beneath this tree sits Vairocana Tathāgata, surrounded before and behind by Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; all of them have emerged from the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and abide in the inconceivable, non-differentiated dwellings of all Bodhisattvas.
One also beholds all the lords of the worlds with palms joined in reverence, gazing up at and surrounding the Tathāgata.
He also beheld the power of the sovereign spiritual transformations of all Tathāgatas;
he further beheld the successive formation and destruction of worlds throughout all kalpas;
and he likewise beheld the sequential appearance of all Buddhas in all those worlds.

Furthermore, they saw that in each and every one of those worlds, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva was making various offerings to all Tathāgatas and employing various means to discipline all sentient beings;
they also saw that all those bodhisattvas, as well as their own bodies, were entirely contained within the body of Samantabhadra;
and they also saw themselves before all Tathāgatas, before all Samantabhadras, before all bodhisattvas, and before all sentient beings.
Furthermore, he also saw that in each of all those worlds, there were various boundaries,
various supports, various shapes, various essential natures, various arrangements,
various adornments, various purities, and various decorations, equal in number to the atoms within a single buddha-field.
Clouds cover their summits; there are various names of kalpas, various appearances of Buddhas, various periods of the three times, various locations,
various ways of abiding in the dharma-realm, various ways of entering the dharma-realm,
various ways of abiding in space, various adornments of bodhisattvas, various dwelling places of bodhisattvas, and various...
The Tathāgata’s site of enlightenment; the various supernormal powers of the Tathāgatas;
the various lion thrones of the Tathāgatas; the various oceans of the Tathāgatas’ great assemblies; the various distinctions among the Tathāgatas’ retinues;
the various skillful means of the Tathāgatas; the various turnings of the wheel of Dharma by the Tathāgatas; and the various sublime voices of the Tathāgatas.
Having seen the sounds, the various oceans of the Tathāgatas' speech, and the various clouds of the Tathāgatas' sūtras,
their minds became pure and they gave rise to great joy.

At that time, that Tathāgata preached for this woman a sūtra named "The Sound of the Turning of the Dharma Wheel by All Tathāgatas," which had as its retinue as many sūtras as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields.

At that time, having heard this sutra, the woman immediately attained ten thousand gateways of samādhi. Her body and mind became supple and soft, devoid of any coarseness or rigidity, like one newly conceived in the womb, like one just born, or like the first sprout emerging from a śāla tree;
her heart in samādhi was likewise soft and lovely.

They are: the samādhi of directly beholding all Buddhas; the samādhi of universally illuminating all lands; the samādhi of deeply entering the gates of all three periods of time; the samādhi of expounding the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas; the samādhi of thoroughly knowing the ocean of vows of all Buddhas; the samādhi of awakening all sentient beings to cause them to emerge from the suffering of birth and death; the samādhi of constantly vowing to shatter the darkness of all sentient beings; the samādhi of constantly vowing to extinguish the suffering of all sentient beings; the samādhi of constantly vowing to produce the happiness of all sentient beings; the samādhi of teaching and transforming all sentient beings without ever becoming weary; the samādhi of the sovereign adornment of all Bodhisattvas dwelling in all stages; the samādhi of the unobstructed banner of all Bodhisattvas; and the samādhi of universally visiting all pure Buddha-lands.
Having attained these ten thousand samādhis, he further attained subtle meditative equipoise (*samāpatti*),
namely: the unmoving mind, the joyful mind, the comforting mind, the mind of universal illumination, the mind that accords with the instructions of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*),
the mind that takes as its object all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) which is profoundly deep, and the mind that accords with the practice of the immeasurable teaching of loving-kindness (*maitrī*).
A mind that has abandoned all attachment; a mind that does not dwell in any worldly realm; a mind that deeply enters the realm of the Tathāgatas;
a mind that universally illumines the ocean of the physical marks and signs of all Buddhas; a mind that is undistracted; a mind that is unshakable;
a mind that is without obstruction; a mind that is without pride or inferiority; and a mind that is free from weariness.
A mind that is irreversible; a mind that has attained mastery; a mind free from indolence; a mind that correctly contemplates the intrinsic nature of all phenomena;
a mind that dwells securely in the ocean of all dharma-doors; a mind that practices within the ocean of all dharma-doors;
a mind that thoroughly understands the ocean of all sentient beings; and a mind that protects and delivers the ocean of all sentient beings.
The mind that universally illumines all oceans of worlds; the mind that universally gives rise to all oceans of Buddha-vows;
the mind that completely shatters all mountains of obstacles; the mind that accumulates vast stores of merit; the mind that directly perceives the ten powers of the Tathāgata;
the mind that universally illumines the realm of Bodhisattvas; and the mind that increases the Bodhisattva’s factors conducive to enlightenment.
With a mind that universally takes as its object all directions and oceans,
he single-mindedly contemplates and observes all the great vows of Samantabhadra, and gives rise to an ocean of equal vows as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields of all Tathāgatas.
That is to say:
the vow to adorn and purify all Buddha-lands;
the vow to bring all sentient beings to maturity.
May I fully know all realms of phenomena;
may I universally enter the ocean of all realms of phenomena;
and may I cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva in all buddha-fields throughout all future eons.
I vow that until the end of all future kalpas, I shall never abandon any sentient being;
I vow to draw near to all Tathāgatas;
and I vow to serve all spiritual friends, causing them all to rejoice.
May I obtain offerings for all Tathāgatas, filling them all completely;
may I, in every thought-moment, cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva, increasing all-knowledge without interruption.
Having made such oceans of vows as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields, may I accomplish all the great vows of Samantabhadra.

Then, that Tathāgata further revealed and expounded for the girl the roots of goodness she had planted since first resolving her mind, the sublime practices she had cultivated, and the great fruits she had attained; causing her to awaken and develop profound faith and understanding, he enabled her to fulfill the ocean of all the Tathāgata’s perfect and vast vows, and to single-mindedly direct herself toward the stage of omniscience.
“Good son! Furthermore, ten great kalpas prior to this, there was a world named Sun-Disk Radiance Mani King, and the Buddha’s name was Indra-Banner Auspicious Sign.”
At that time, within the bequeathed Dharma of that Tathāgata, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra exhorted this woman, Padmanetra, to repair an old and damaged image of the Buddha upon a lotus throne;
having repaired it, she further painted it;
having painted it, she further adorned it with jewels, and then gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Good son! I recall that in the past, it was because of the spiritual friend Samantabhadra Bodhisattva that I planted these roots of goodness.

From that time forth, I have never fallen into the evil realms, but have always been born into the lineages of all celestial kings and human kings. In every place of birth, my physical form has been exceptionally sublime, upright and pleasing, with perfect features and characteristics that bring joy to those who behold me."

I constantly see the Buddha and am always able to draw near to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; may he cause me to remember and uphold the Dharma-gates I have attained, and even until now, continue to guide and awaken me, bringing me to maturity and causing me to give rise to joy.
“Good son, what do you think?
Was the universal monarch Vairocana-ratnapadmagarbha-saumyakeśa at that time anyone other than this person?”
The present Maitreya Bodhisattva is he.

At that time, the queen whose face was endowed with perfect auspiciousness was the night goddess named Ocean of Silent Sounds Endowed with Complete Merit; her current dwelling place is not far from here.
The maiden named Samantānandaśrīpadmanetra at that time was none other than myself.

In the past, when I was a maiden, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra exhorted me to repair an image of a lotus seat as a causal condition for supreme enlightenment, thereby causing me to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, I first resolved my mind toward enlightenment; thereafter, I was further guided so that I might behold the Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel-Flame Auspicious Majestic Virtue King. I untied the necklaces from my body and scattered them as an offering to the Buddha. Witnessing the Buddha’s supernatural transformations and hearing his preaching of the Dharma, I immediately attained the Bodhisattva liberation door of "Universally Manifesting in All Worlds to Subdue Sentient Beings. From then on, I beheld Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru, all of whom I honored, revered, and made offerings to. I listened to the various teachings of those Tathāgatas, rejoiced upon hearing the Dharma, and practiced according to their instructions. In every thought-moment, I constantly beheld all those Tathāgatas, as well as their Buddha-fields and the great assemblies of bodhisattvas.

“Good son! After that Vairocana-Tejas-Śrī World and its Stainless Perfection Eon have passed, there was next a world named Mani-Cakra-Vividha-Ratna-Varṇa-Vyūha, and an eon named Mahāprabha, in which five hundred Buddhas appeared; I served, honored, and made offerings to them all, causing them to rejoice.”
The first of those Buddhas was named Mahākaruṇāmeghadhvaja; at that time, I was a night goddess who saw the Buddha going forth and made offerings to him with reverence.
Subsequently, another Buddha appeared named Vajranārāyaṇadhvaja; at that time, I was a wheel-turning monarch who drew near to serve him and made offerings to him with reverence.
At that time, the Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "The Manifestation of All Buddhas," with as many sūtras as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields serving as its retinue;

I received and upheld them all. Subsequently, another Buddha appeared named "Vajra Unobstructed Virtue. At that time, I was a universal monarch (cakravartin) who reverently made offerings to him. That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named "Universally Illuminating the Faculties of All Beings," with as many sūtras as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru serving as its retinue; I received and upheld them all.

Next, a Buddha appeared named Jvālācalasri-vyūha (Auspicious Adornment of the Flame-Mountain). At that time, I was the daughter of a householder; I made offerings to and honored him, and that Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Sarvatryadhvāvabhāsa-garbha-vyūha-jambudvīpa* (The Adornment of the Treasury Illumining the Three Times Throughout Jambudvīpa), with as many sūtras as there are atoms in the universe as its retinue, all of which I received and upheld.

Next, a Buddha appeared named Sarvadharma-sāgara-abhyudgata-rāja (King Exalted Above the Ocean of All Dharmas). I was then a celestial king, and I honored and made offerings to him; that Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Sarvadharma-dhātu-pravicaya-jñāna* (Wisdom Discerning the Entire Dharma Realm), with five hundred sūtras as its retinue, all of which I received and upheld.

Next, a Buddha appeared named Gambhīradharmaśrīsamudraprabha. At that time, I was the daughter of a dragon king; I made offerings by raining down clouds of wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels. That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Tvaritavivardhanaprīti-sāgara*, with a retinue of hundreds of billions of nayutas of sūtras, all of which I received and upheld.

Next, a Buddha appeared named Ratnakūṭajvālādīpa. I was then a sea deity; I made offerings by raining down clouds of precious lotuses, drawing near to serve him with reverence and respect. That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Dharmadhātuprayogodadhiprabhāsa*, with a retinue of sūtras as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, all of which I received and upheld.

Next, a Buddha appeared named Merit-Ocean Radiance-Illumination-Perfect-Auspiciousness. At that time, I was a rishi possessing the five supernatural powers, manifesting great spiritual might and surrounded by a retinue of six thousand rishis. We rained down clouds of exquisite fragrant flowers from the peaks of high mountains as an offering. That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named Lamp of the Unattached Dharma, with six thousand sūtras as its retinue, all of which I received and upheld.

Next, there appeared a Buddha named Vairocana-Śrīgarbha. At that time, I was a presiding earth goddess named Samatānuśaṃsā, together with immeasurable earth goddesses. We made offerings by raining down clouds of all kinds of jewel-trees, clouds of all kinds of jewel-treasuries, clouds of all kinds of jewel-garlands, and clouds of all kinds of jewel-adornments. That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Sarvatathāgatajñānagarbhasambhava* (The Source of the Wisdom-Treasury of All Tathāgatas), with immeasurable sūtras as its retinue; I heard them all and retained them in memory without forgetting.
“Good son! Thus, there are five hundred Tathāgatas in succession; the name of the final Buddha is Dharmadhātu-gaganaratna-śaila-paripūrṇa-śrī-dīpa.”
At that time, I was a courtesan named Priyadarśana-śrī-mukhā.
Encountering the Buddha as he entered the city, I made offerings through song and dance; by the Buddha's majestic power, I leaped into the air and praised him with a thousand wondrous verses.

For my sake, the Buddha emitted a light from between his brows called "Adornment of Light Universally Illuminating the Dharma Realm. This light shone upon my body, pervading it entirely; touched by this light, I immediately attained liberation, which is called the "Gate of the Non-retrogressive Treasury of Skillful Means of the Dharma Realm."

“Good son! Within this world-system, there are as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field. All Tathāgatas appeared therein, and I served, honored, and made offerings to them all, causing them to rejoice.
Those Tathāgatas expounded various kinds of true Dharma for me; I have remembered it all, received and upheld it according to the Dharma, not forgetting even a single word or a single phrase.”
Before each and every one of those Tathāgatas, he extolled and praised all Buddha-dharmas, extensively performing beneficial deeds for immeasurable sentient beings;

before each and every one of those Tathāgatas, he attained the manifestation of the treasury of the dharma-realm of the three periods of time, dwelt in the vast body of the dharma-realm, entered the light of omniscience, and entered all the practices of Samantabhadra.

"Good son! By relying on the light of all-knowledge, in every thought-moment I behold immeasurable Buddhas. Having beheld these Buddhas, I have fully accomplished all the sublime practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—those which I had never before attained, never before seen, and never before heard."

"Why is this? Because they have attained the light of all-knowledge and because they manifest, in their distinctions, the gateways to the immeasurable and boundless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

At that time, the night goddess Sarvasattvaparitrāṇaśīlā, wishing to clarify once more the meaning of this gate of liberation, received the Buddha’s majestic power and spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
“Sudhana, you should listen as I speak of this profound dharma, difficult to enter and difficult to see,
which universally illuminates the three periods of time and is the gateway to the light of all differentiated wisdoms.”

Just as I first resolved upon the mind of enlightenment, Diligently seeking the Buddha’s wisdom and all its virtues, And realized boundless gates of liberation— I shall proclaim them for you; listen with focused attention.
