I recall that in the past, beyond eons as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, there was an eon named Vimalacakra.
The field was called Jayadhvajavyāptipradīpa; its adornments were vast and free from all defilement.
Within it, those possessing the Ten Powers appeared in the world, their number equal to the atoms within Mount Sumeru.
The first was Buddha Ratnārciśrīprabha; the second, Dharmarāja Guṇadhvaja;
the third, Dharmadhvaja Puṇyasumeru; the fourth, Abhayavikrāntarāja;
the fifth Buddha was named Śāntirāja; and the sixth Buddha was named Śāntinagara.
The seventh Tathāgata was named Mountain of Fame; the eighth Guide was Sumeru Virtue;
the ninth Buddha was named Auspicious Light; and the tenth was named Moon-Faced Buddha.
In the presence of these ten Buddha-Bhagavāns, I was awakened to the initial gateway;
thereafter, there were ten successive Buddhas who appeared in succession within the world.
The first Buddha was named Ākāśasthita; the second Tathāgata was named Samantaprabha;
the third was named Janmavihārasarvadik; the fourth Tathāgata was Samyaksmṛtisāgara;
the fifth Buddha was named Uccagātaprabha; and the sixth World-Honored One was Merumegha.
The seventh was the Tathāgata Flame of Dharma Light; The eighth was the Tathāgata Mountain of Renown;
The ninth was the King Born from the Lotus; The tenth was the Flower of the Great Compassionate Dharmadhātu.
The light from these ten oceans of Buddhas shines forth, Causing me to awaken and enter the second gate;
Thereafter, in continuous succession without interval, Ten more Buddhas appear one after another.
The first was Tathāgata Prabhāketudhvajarāja; the second Buddha was named Jñānaprabha;
the third Buddha was named Hitacitta; the fourth Tathāgata was Indraketuśrī;
the fifth Tathāgata was named Devajñāna; the sixth Buddha was titled Gurumativararāja.
The seventh Buddha is named Jñānaśrī; the eighth is titled Prabhākararāja;
the ninth is the Buddha Vīradevagati; and the tenth is Dharmadhātupadmottama.
These ten [Buddhas] can manifest the vast Dharma, enabling me to accomplish the third gate;
immediately thereafter, I shall again encounter ten Buddhas appearing in successive succession.
First was the Auspicious One of Jewel Flame Mountain; second was the Buddha Virtuous Auspiciousness;
third was the Buddha named Dharma Radiance; fourth was the Buddha named Lotus Treasury;
fifth was the Buddha Wondrous Eye of Wisdom Moon; sixth was the Tathāgata Fragrant Jewel Light.
The seventh Sugata was Meruśrī; the eighth was named Gandharvaprabha;
the ninth was Maṇigarbharāja Buddha; and the tenth was Samantatejorāja Buddha.
Thereafter, ten Buddhas appeared in succession, arising one after another in the world.
The first Buddha was named Vast Wisdom; the second Buddha was named Jewel Radiance;
the third Tathāgata was named Cloud of Merit; the fourth Buddha was named Supreme Mark.
The fifth was Duṣkarasampūrṇaprabha; the sixth Buddha was named Nārāyaṇa;
the seventh World-Honored One was Meruguṇa; the eighth was Guṇacakravālapati;
the ninth Tathāgata was Aparājitadhvaja; and the tenth Buddha was named Mahāvṛkṣarāja.
Thereafter, ten Buddhas appeared in succession, arising one after another in the world.
The first was named King Śāla of Imperial Virtue; the second was named Universal Manifestation of the World-Ruler’s Body;
the third Buddha was named Exalted Radiance; and the fourth Buddha was named Vajra-Light.
The fifth was the World-Honored One Bhūmītejas; the sixth, the King of Profound Dharma-Virtue;
the seventh, Dharmasāgara-Mahājñānaghoṣa; the eighth Buddha was named Merudhvaja;
the ninth Tathāgata was Jñānaprabhāsa; and the tenth was Ratnarāja-Śrī.
Following this, there were ten Buddhas who appeared in succession within the world.
First was Brahmāprabha, then Ākāśaghoṣa; third was Dharmadhātubimbaśrī, fourth was Paripūrṇaprabhāmaṇḍala; fifth was Sarvadigjñānaraśmidhvaja.
Sixth is Gaganapradīpa, seventh is Guṇarāja; Eighth is Samantāvabhāsaśrīprabha, ninth is Puṇyaprabhāśāntaguṇa; Tenth is Mahākaruṇāmeghaśrī.
After this, ten Buddhas appeared in succession, arising one after another in the world.
The first was Satyabalajñānāvabhāsa; the second, Sarvasattvāgratopagata;
the third was named Uccagāminprabha; and the fourth Buddha was named Prabhāśarīra.
The fifth was the Sugata Dharmasambhava; the sixth was named Vāyuvegavāhin;
the seventh was the World-Honored One Śrīlakṣaṇa; the eighth was the Tathāgata Vikrāntaketu;
the ninth Buddha was named Ratnāṅga; and the tenth was Samantatryadhvāvabhāsaprāpta.
Thereafter, ten Buddhas appeared in succession, arising one after another in the world.
The first Buddha was Praṇidhānasāgaralakṣmīpradīpa; the second Buddha was Śrīvajraparvata;
the third was Dṛḍhasumeruguṇa; and the fourth Buddha was named Smṛtidhvajarāja.
The fifth was the Tathāgata Dharmajñānaguru; The sixth Buddha was named Prajñāpradīpa;
The seventh Buddha was titled Guṇaprabhāketu; The eighth Buddha was named Vistīrṇajñāna;
The ninth was Jñānacaryadharmadhātumukha; The tenth was Dharmasāgarajñānaśrī.
After this, there were ten Buddhas who appeared in succession within the world.
The first was Puṇyaparvataguṇarāja; the next Buddha was named Jñānaśrī;
the third Tathāgata was Dharmacakravartin; the fourth was Ratnarājaśrī Buddha.
The fifth was Śrīguṇacakra; the sixth was Samantajñānārciḥprabha Buddha.
The seventh Buddha was named Sumerupradīpa; the eighth World-Honored One was Tvaritaprabha.
The ninth Tathāgata was Mahāpraśāntanirghoṣa; the tenth Buddha was named Śāntadhvaja.
11. Auspicious Lamp of Sentient Beings; 12. Swift Auspiciousness of Great Vows;
13. Banner of Invincible Power; 14. Ocean of the World-Honored One’s Wisdom-Flame.
All were preeminent leaders in the world, universally benefiting all sentient beings;
following these, there appeared in succession ten Buddhas who arose one after another in the world.
The first Buddha was named Dharmeśvara; the second was the Tathāgata Asaṅgajñāna;
the third was the World-Honored One Sāgarabuddhivikrīḍita; the fourth was the Tamer Guhyarutasvara;
the fifth was the Buddha Paripūrṇavākya; and the sixth was the Great Auspiciousness of Sublime Sound.
The seventh is the Buddha Wisdom Sovereign-Turning; The eighth is the Universal Manifestation Before All Beings;
The ninth is the Auspicious Body Equal to Sentient Beings; The tenth is named the Mountain of the Virtuous Self-Nature.
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru,
all the foremost Tathāgatas who universally act as lamps for the world— I have made offerings to them all, none in vain.
Furthermore, throughout as many eons as there are atoms in Buddha-fields,
I have made offerings to all the Tathāgatas therein, thereby entering this ocean of profound liberation.
Throughout such boundless eons, I have practiced and attained this gate of liberation;
having heard it now, you should practice swiftly, and before long you too shall attain it as I have.
“Good son! I only know this bodhisattva liberation door of universally manifesting in all worlds to discipline sentient beings.
As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who gather an ocean of boundless practices, give rise to various kinds of resolute minds, and manifest...”
Possessing various bodies, endowed with various faculties, fulfilling various aspirations, entering various samādhis,
manifesting various supernormal powers, accomplishing various skillful means, able to perform various benefits,
roaming into various treasuries of wisdom, illuminating various oceans of Dharma gates, and attaining various radiances of Dharma.
...traveling to oceans of various Buddha-fields, receiving various consecrations from Buddhas,
serving various spiritual friends, awakening to various gates of liberation, realizing various minds of mastery, initiating various unconditioned practices,
manifesting various inconceivable forms, and complying with the minds of various sentient beings, giving rise to various...
Manifesting transformation bodies, entering the various stages of bodhisattvas, knowing the causes and conditions of various dharmas,
abandoning various false discriminations, relying on various bodhisattva vows, and upholding the various bequeathed teachings of the Buddhas,
they dwell securely in the production of the wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? Good son!

Not far from here, within the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Samantaguṇālaṃkāraviśuddhavyūhasāgaraghoṣā, seated upon a lion throne of precious lotus-womb adorned with the king of maṇi-jewels of the banner of stellar light, surrounded before and behind by a retinue of ten million asaṃkhyeya night goddesses.
"Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing.
The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sutra, Scroll Twenty;
The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sutra, Scroll Twenty-one.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Prajna of Kasmira by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard from the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpramardanaśrī the liberation door of the Bodhisattva’s universal manifestation in all worlds to discipline sentient beings, as well as the samādhi of the presence of all Tathāgatas and the samādhi of transcending the adornments of all sentient beings—having attained these ten thousand samādhis—he practiced them all. He gave rise to profound faith and understanding; their radiance shone everywhere, he followed them universally, entered and traversed them, brought them forth extensively, and exercised mastery over their functions.

Proceeding gradually, he went to the place where the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, who is endowed with all virtues, was staying; he prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words: "Noble Lady!"
I have already first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
It is by relying on spiritual friends that I study the bodhisattva conduct, cultivate the bodhisattva conduct, enter the bodhisattva conduct, and abide in the bodhisattva conduct.

I aspire to give birth to the inconceivable Dharma of the ocean of all-knowledge; I only pray that you, out of compassion, will explain for me how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and how they should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the night goddess said to Sudhana:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
"Noble son! You are able to rely upon spiritual friends to seek the bodhisattva conduct. Noble son!"
"I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door called 'the adornment of vast joy arising in every thought-moment.
Sudhana said, "O Great Sage!"
What is the function of this door of liberation?
What sphere does it traverse?
By what means is it cultivated?
"What kind of observation do you practice?
The night goddess said, "Noble son!
I give rise to a mind of pure and equanimous aspiration; I give rise to a mind that is pure, firm, and adorned by being free from all worldly dust and defilement;
I give rise to a mind of resolute non-retrogression that is capable of accomplishing all difficult tasks;
I give rise to a mind that adorns all mountains of precious merit like Mount Sumeru...
I resolve upon a mind that is forever unmoving, like the golden wheel; I resolve upon a mind that dwells nowhere and clings to nothing in any place;
I resolve upon a mind that manifests before all sentient beings to provide universal protection and salvation;
I resolve upon a mind that beholds the ocean of all Buddhas without ever feeling satiety; I resolve upon seeking all...
With the mind of the Bodhisattva’s pure power of aspiration, I give rise to the mind that abides in the ocean of light of universal great wisdom;
I give rise to the mind that causes all sentient beings to transcend the wilderness of sorrow, affliction, birth, and death;
I give rise to the mind that causes all sentient beings to abandon the suffering of lamentation and grief; I give rise to the mind that causes one...
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon their minds that are attached to various unpleasant forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and mental objects;

I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon the suffering of being separated from those they love and encountering those they hate; I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon various evil karmas.
With the suffering of causes and conditions, ignorance, and so forth, I arouse the mind to act as a protector for all beings in the perilous difficulties of the evil destinies;
I arouse the mind to cause all sentient beings to emerge from the suffering of birth and death and to reveal the true path;
I arouse the mind to cause all sentient beings to abandon the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death.
I resolve to give rise to a mind that brings all sentient beings to the accomplishment of the unsurpassed Dharma-bliss of the Tathāgata;
I resolve to give rise to a mind that causes all sentient beings to experience pure and great joy;
I resolve to give rise to a mind that causes all sentient beings to practice the right path free from all calamities and obstacles.
Having generated this mind, I further preach the Dharma for them to lead them gradually to the stage of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*), as follows:

if I see sentient beings who delight in and are attached to the palaces, mansions, and dwellings in which they reside, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may thoroughly comprehend the fundamental nature of all phenomena and become free from all attachments;

if I see sentient beings who are yearning for and attached to their parents, brothers, and kinsmen, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may enter the pure assemblies of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

If I see sentient beings who are attached to their wives and children, with no thought of renouncing them, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to abandon the defilement of love within birth and death, to give rise to great compassion, and to attain equanimity and non-duality toward all sentient beings;
if I see sentient beings who are attached to marketplaces, villages, and social gatherings, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to join the assemblies of the holy ones;
if I see sentient beings who are greedily attached to material requisites, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to fulfill all the *pāramitās*.
If I see sentient beings who are attached to music, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to delight in the pure joy of the Dharma;
if I see sentient beings who are attached to the objects of the five desires, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to enter the realm of the Tathāgata;
if I see sentient beings who frequently give rise to anger, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to abide in the Tathāgata’s perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā).
If I see sentient beings whose minds are indolent, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the pure perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*);
if I see sentient beings whose minds are distracted, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the Tathāgata’s perfection of meditation (*dhyāna-pāramitā*);

if I see sentient beings who have entered the dense forest of views and are obscured by the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to emerge from that thicket and darkness.
If I see sentient beings lacking wisdom, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to accomplish the *prajñāpāramitā*;

if I see sentient beings defiled by and attached to the triple world, I preach the Dharma for them so that their minds will neither grasp nor reject within birth and death, thereby attaining abiding in the *upāyakauśalyapāramitā*;
if I see sentient beings with inferior aspirations, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to fulfill their vows for the *buddhabodhi*.
If I see sentient beings who seek only their own benefit, I preach the Dharma for them to inspire in them the vow to equally benefit all sentient beings;
if I see sentient beings whose resolve and aspiration are weak, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*);
if I see sentient beings shrouded in the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the Tathāgata’s ultimate, pure perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*).
If I see sentient beings with incomplete physical features, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the Tathāgata’s perfect and complete form-body;
if I see sentient beings with ugly appearances, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the unsurpassed, pure Dharma-body;
if I see sentient beings with coarse and unrefined physical features, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain subtle, golden-hued skin.
If I see sentient beings oppressed by various sufferings, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the most ultimate peace and happiness of the Tathāgata;
if I see sentient beings enjoying various forms of ease and happiness, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may abide in the bliss of omniscience;
if I see sentient beings afflicted by various illnesses and pains, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may achieve a body like a reflected image.
If I see sentient beings who have accumulated attachment to form, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to delight in the practices of all bodhisattvas;
if I see sentient beings oppressed by poverty, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to obtain the jewel-treasury of bodhisattva merits;

if I see sentient beings who take pleasure in dwelling in gardens and groves, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to make offerings to and serve the Buddhas while residing in the garden-enclosures of the Dharma.
If I see sentient beings traveling along roads, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to advance toward the path of omniscience;
if I see sentient beings who delight in dwelling in villages and towns, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to emerge from the triple world;
if I see sentient beings who delight in residing in settlements, I preach the Dharma for them to cause them to transcend the paths of the two vehicles and abide in the stage of the Tathāgata.
If I see sentient beings who delight in dwelling in cities and fortresses, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to dwell in the city of the Dharma King;
if I see sentient beings who delight in stopping at the four quarters, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain the wisdom of the equality of the three periods of time;
if I see sentient beings who delight in stopping in various directions, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to attain wisdom and perceive all phenomena.
If I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by greed, I preach for them the gate of the contemplation of impurity, so that they may abandon the thirst of birth and death;

if I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by anger, I preach for them the gate of the contemplation of great compassion, so that they may diligently practice until their minds are free from affliction and harm;
if I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by delusion, I preach the Dharma for them, so that they may attain the eye of wisdom and contemplate the ocean of all phenomena.
If I see sentient beings whose faculties are balanced, I preach the Dharma for them, enabling them to enter the ocean of all supreme wisdom and great vows;
if I see sentient beings who delight in the pleasures of birth and death, I preach the Dharma for them, causing them to feel weary of and detached from them;

if I see sentient beings who weary of the suffering of birth and death and are fit to be transformed by a Tathāgata, I preach the Dharma for them, leading them to realize non-arising while manifesting the taking of birth.
If I see sentient beings who are attached to the five aggregates, I preach the Dharma for them to enable them to abide in the realm of non-reliance;
if I see sentient beings whose minds are inferior, I reveal to them the path of supreme adornment;
if I see sentient beings whose minds give rise to arrogance, I preach for them the Tathāgata’s patience regarding the equality of all phenomena.
If I see sentient beings whose minds are deceitful and crooked, I preach for them the pure and straightforward mind of a bodhisattva. Good son!

By means of such immeasurable Dharma-gifts, I gather in all sentient beings; through various skillful means, I teach and subdue them, causing them to leave the evil realms, enjoy the pleasures of humans and devas, escape the bonds of the triple world, and abide in omniscience.
At that time, I immediately attained a vast ocean of light from the Dharma of great joy; it was swiftly cherished, profoundly perfect, and my mind became serene, tranquil, and blissful.
"Furthermore, good son!

I constantly observe the oceans of assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all bodhisattvas, who cultivate various vows and practices, manifest various pure bodies, possess various constant radiances, and emit various rays of light;
who enter the gates of omniscience through various skillful means and enter various samādhis."

They manifest various supernatural transformations, produce oceans of various sounds, possess bodies adorned with various ornaments, enter various doors of the Tathāgatas, travel to oceans of various lands, behold oceans of various Buddhas, attain oceans of various eloquences, illuminate various realms of liberation, obtain oceans of various lights of wisdom, and sport within oceans of various samādhis and various palaces of liberation.

They approach all-knowledge through various gateways; they cover the realm of space with clouds of adornments; they observe the various assemblies at sites of enlightenment; they gather from various worlds; they enter various buddha-fields; they proceed to various oceans of directions; they receive the commands of various Tathāgatas; they depart from the abodes of various Tathāgatas together with various bodhisattvas; they rain down clouds of various adornments; they enter the various skillful means of the Tathāgatas; they contemplate the various oceans of Dharma of the Tathāgatas; they reflect upon the various doors of the Tathāgatas’ supernormal powers; they accord with the various oceans of wisdom of the Tathāgatas; they go to the various sublime assemblies of the Tathāgatas; and they sit upon the various seats of adornment of the Tathāgatas.
"Good son! I observe this assembly at the site of enlightenment and, knowing that the Buddha’s spiritual power is immeasurable and boundless, I give rise to great joy. Good son!"
I observe that the Tathāgata Vairocana manifests inconceivable physical bodies in every thought-moment; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Again, I observe the Tathāgata emitting great rays of light in every thought-moment, filling the boundless and vast Dharma-realm; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.

Furthermore, I see from each and every pore of the Tathāgata an ocean of light, as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-lands, appearing in every thought-moment; each ray of light has as its retinue light-rays as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-lands, each pervading the entire Dharma-realm and extinguishing the suffering of all sentient beings; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, good son!

I observe that from the Tathāgata’s crown and both shoulders, there emerge in every thought-moment clouds of jewel-flame mountains, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, filling the entirety of the ten directions and all dharma-realms; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, good son!

I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there issue forth clouds of fragrant light as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, filling all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, O son of good family!

I observe each and every ocean of marks of the Tathāgata, from which, in every thought-moment, emerge clouds of Tathāgata-bodies adorned with all the marks, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, traveling everywhere throughout all worlds in the ten directions; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, O son of good family!

I observe each and every minor mark of the Tathāgata, from which, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of Tathāgata bodies with the radiance of minor marks as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, O son of good family!

I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of Buddha-transformations as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields. These manifest the Tathāgata’s journey from his first resolve to enlightenment, his cultivation of the pāramitās, his fulfillment of the path of adornment, his entry into the bodhisattva stages, and his mastery of the various spiritual powers of a bodhisattva. Having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, son of good family!

I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of bodies of celestial kings as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, along with the sovereign spiritual transformations of those celestial kings. These fill all the dharma-realms of the ten directions; to those who are to be liberated by the body of a celestial king, he appears before them and preaches the Dharma. Having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, son of good family!

I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there appear clouds of bodies of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of dragon kings, yakṣa kings, gandharva kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings, human kings, and Brahmā kings—equal in number to the atoms within all Buddha-fields. In every thought-moment, within his pores, he manifests such spiritual transformations, such physical forms, such voices, and such preaching of the Dharma. Having seen this, in every thought-moment, I give rise to great joy and vast faith and delight, the measure of which is equal to the *sarvajñatā* (omniscience) of the Dharma-realm.
That which was previously unattained is now for the first time attained;
that which was previously unresolved is now for the first time resolved;
that which was previously unrealized is now for the first time realized.
That which was previously unentered, one now enters for the first time;
that which was previously unfilled, one now fills for the first time;
that which was previously unseen, one now sees for the first time.
What was never heard before is now heard for the first time.

Why is this? Because one is able to fully comprehend the characteristics of the dharma-realm; because one knows that all dharmas possess but a single characteristic; because one is able to enter the path of the three periods of time with equanimity; and because one is able to expound all boundless dharmas.
“Good son! I have entered this ocean of light of liberation called ‘The Adornment of Vast Joy Arising Moment by Moment.
Furthermore, good son!”
This liberation is boundless, for it universally enters the gates of the entire dharma-realm;
this liberation is inexhaustible, for it equally gives rise to the mind of the nature of all-knowledge;
this liberation is immeasurable, for it is the sphere of objects known by the wisdom-eye of bodhisattvas.
This liberation is boundless, for it enters into the mental perceptions of all sentient beings throughout the limitless bounds;
this liberation is profound, for it is observed by tranquil wisdom;
this liberation is vast, for it pervades the entire realm of all Tathāgatas.
This liberation is indestructible, for it is known by the eye of wisdom of Bodhisattvas;
this liberation is bottomless, for it exhausts the very source and depths of the Dharma-realm;
this liberation is the Universal Gate, for within a single phenomenon it universally manifests all spiritual transformations.
This liberation is not empty in its essential nature, for all dharmas and the body of reality (dharmakāya) are equal and non-dual;
this liberation is ultimately without birth, for it thoroughly understands that all phenomena are like illusions;
this liberation is like a reflected image, for it is produced by the light of the vows of omniscience.
This liberation is like a magical transformation, for the practices of all bodhisattvas are wondrous transformations;
this liberation is like the great earth, for it is the place upon which all sentient beings rely;
this liberation is like the great waters, for it can moisten all things through great compassion.
This liberation is like a great fire, for it dries up the waters of sentient beings' craving;
this liberation is like a great wind, for it causes all sentient beings to swiftly proceed toward omniscience;
this liberation is like the great ocean, for it adorns all sentient beings with the jewels of manifold merits.
This liberation is like Mount Sumeru, for it emerges from the ocean of the jewels of all-knowledge;
this liberation is like a celestial palace, for it is adorned with all sublime dharmas;
this liberation is like space, for it universally accommodates the supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
This liberation is like a great cloud, for it universally rains down the rain of Dharma upon all sentient beings;
this liberation is like the pure sun, for it can shatter the darkness of ignorance within sentient beings;
this liberation is like the full moon, for it fulfills the vast ocean of merit and wisdom.
This liberation is like the Tathāgata, because it possesses correct and universal knowledge regarding all things;
this liberation is like one's own reflection, because it is manifested from one's own virtuous karma;
this liberation is like an echo, because it preaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate for each being.
This liberation is like a reflected image, for it manifests in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
this liberation is like the king of great trees, for it causes all the flowers of supernormal powers to bloom;
this liberation is like a vajra, for it has been indestructible from the very beginning.
This liberation is like a wish-fulfilling jewel, for it gives rise to immeasurable powers of mastery;
this liberation is like the stainless storehouse maṇi-jewel king, for it manifests all the supernatural transformations of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
this liberation is like the wonderful maṇi-jewel of the Banner of Joy, for it can equally produce the sounds of the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas.

"Good son! I now praise for you in various ways this gate of liberation as being peerless and rare, possessing true merit that is difficult to understand, difficult to enter, difficult to believe, and difficult to know. You should reflect upon it and, in accordance with it, awaken to and enter it."
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the Night Goddess:
"Noble Lady! How should one practice so as to attain this liberation and bring it to full perfection?"
The night goddess said:

"Good son! When a bodhisattva practices the ten great treasuries of Dharma, accumulating and perfecting them so that their radiance shines everywhere, delightfully giving rise to them, and possessing sovereign power, they are then able to accomplish this gate of liberation."
What are the ten? First, cultivating the vast dharma-treasury of giving, satisfying all according to the inclinations of sentient beings;
second, cultivating the vast dharma-treasury of pure precepts, universally entering the ocean of all Buddhas' merits.
Third, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of patience, which is able to contemplate universally the nature of all phenomena;
fourth, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of diligence, proceeding toward omniscience with never-receding persistence;
fifth, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of meditative concentration, which is able to extinguish the feverish afflictions of all sentient beings.
Sixth, by cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of prajñā, one is able to thoroughly know the ocean of all phenomena;
seventh, by cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of skillful means, one is able to universally mature the ocean of all sentient beings;

eighth, by cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of vows, one is able to universally enter the oceans of all Buddha-lands, practicing the bodhisattva path for the sake of all sentient beings throughout all future kalpas.

Ninth, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of all powers, which is able to manifest the ocean of teachings of all dharma-realms in every thought-moment, attaining equal and perfect enlightenment in all lands without ever ceasing;

tenth, they cultivate the vast Dharma-treasury of pure wisdom, which is able to attain the Tathāgata’s pure, wondrous wisdom, universally knowing all dharmas of the three periods of time without any obstruction.

"Good son! If bodhisattvas abide in these ten great treasuries of Dharma, they will then be able to obtain such liberation, purification, growth, accumulation, fulfillment, birth, firmness, vastness, accomplishment, stability, and perfection."
Sudhana said: "Noble One!
How long has it been since you first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
The night goddess said, “Good son!

To the east of this Flower Bank Adorned World-Ocean, passing through a thousand world-oceans, there is a world-ocean named Adorned with All Pure Radiance and Multitudes of Jewels. Within it is a world-system named Sound of Great Vow Radiance, and within that is a world named Adorned with Stainless Golden Light. It is composed of all-fragrant vajra-maṇi kings, shaped like a multi-storied pavilion, with clouds of various wondrous jewels forming its boundaries. It rests upon an ocean of all-jeweled necklaces, covered above by clouds of exquisite palaces; it is a mixture of the pure and the impure.”

In that world, in a remote past age, there was an eon named Universal Radiance Banner; there was a land named Universal Jewel Auspicious Treasury; there was a site of enlightenment named Multicolored Radiance of All Jewel Treasuries; and there was a Buddha named Non-retrogressive Wondrous Sound of the Dharma Realm who attained perfect enlightenment at this site.

At that time, I was a tree deity of the bodhi tree named Banner of the Light of Merit-Lamp, protecting the site of enlightenment. Seeing that Tathāgata attain perfect enlightenment and manifest various sovereign spiritual powers, I resolved my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. At that very moment, I attained a samādhi called Universally Illuminating the Ocean of the Tathāgata’s Merits.
In that place of enlightenment, there subsequently appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Dharma-Tree Majestic Virtue Mountain King (*Dharmadruma-tejo-megha-parvatarāja*).

At that time, my life having ended, I was reborn here as the night goddess of the place of enlightenment, named Auspicious Light of Merit and Wisdom (*Śrī-puṇya-jñāna-prabhā*). Seeing that Tathāgata turning the wheel of the true Dharma and manifesting great supernormal powers, I immediately attained a samādhi called Universally Illuminating All Realms Free from Greed (*Sarva-viṣaya-samanta-avabhāsa-vigata-rāga-gocara*).

Subsequently, there appeared in the world another Tathāgata named Sovereign Sound of the Ocean of All Dharmas (*Sarva-dharma-sāgara-nirghoṣarāja*). As a night goddess, because I was able to see this Buddha, I served him in various ways, making offerings and paying him respect with a heart full of joy; I immediately obtained a samādhi called Increasing the Ground of All Wholesome Dharmas (*Sarva-kuśala-dharma-vardhana-bhūmi*).

Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Ratnārci-dhvaja-rāja; as a night goddess, I was able to see this Buddha, serve and make offerings to him, and bring him joy, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi called "Universal Manifestation of the Clouds of Supernatural Radiance.

Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Guṇa-meru-prabhā-tejo-rāja; as a night goddess, I was able to see this Buddha, serve and make offerings to him, and bring him joy, whereby I then attained a samādhi called "Universally Illuminating the Ocean of All Buddhas."

Next, a Tathāgata appeared in the world named Dharmamegha-svararāja; as a night goddess, I was able to see that Buddha, serve and make offerings to him, and gladden his heart, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi called Lamp of the Ocean of All Dharmas.

Next, a Tathāgata appeared in the world named Jñānolkā-prabhārāja; as a night goddess, I was able to see that Buddha, serve and make offerings to him, and gladden his heart, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi called Light-Illuminating Lamp that Extinguishes the Suffering of All Sentient Beings.

Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Swift Banner of the Supernatural Powers of the Sublime Dharma; as a night goddess, I was able to see this Buddha, serve and make offerings to him, and with a heart of great joy, I immediately attained a samādhi called "The Radiant Treasury of the Conduct of the Tathāgatas of the Three Times.

Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Lion King of Courageous Wisdom and Lamp of the Dharma; as a night goddess, I was able to see this Buddha, serve and make offerings to him, and by causing him to feel great joy, I immediately attained a samādhi called "The Majestic Light of the Unobstructed Wheel of Wisdom of All Worlds."

Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named King Endowed with the Power of Wisdom and Majestic Virtue. At that time, I was a night goddess; because I was able to see this Buddha, I served and made offerings to him until my heart was filled with joy, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi called "Universal Illumination of the Images of the Faculties and Conduct of Beings Throughout the Three Times."
In this way, noble son!

Within that eon called Universal Radiance Banner in the world-system called Immaculate Golden Light Adornment, there appeared as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields; at that time, I—whether...
He may become a king of devas, or a king of nāgas, or a king of yakṣas, or a king of gandharvas, or a king of asuras, or a king of garuḍas,
or a king of kiṃnaras, or a king of mahoragas, or a king of humans, or a Brahmā king.
Whether manifesting as the body of a deva, or the body of a human, or the body of a man,
or the body of a woman, or the body of a boy, or the body of a girl,
they all used various kinds of offerings to reverently worship, honor, and serve those Tathāgatas, and also heard [their teachings].
He heard and received all the sublime Dharma taught by the Buddhas, retaining it in memory without forgetting.

At the end of his life there, he was reborn in this very world-system; for as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, he practiced the various sublime conducts of a Bodhisattva. Thereafter, at the end of his life, he was born in the Sahā world within this Flower Bank Adorned World-Ocean, where he encountered the Tathāgata Krakucchanda. He served and made offerings to him, bringing him joy, and attained a samādhi named "Radiance Free from All Dusty Images.
Next, he encountered the Tathāgata Kanakamuni, whom he served and made offerings to, bringing him joy, and attained a samādhi named "Universal Light Illuminating All Oceans of Lands."

Next, I encountered the Tathāgata Kāśyapa, whom I served and made offerings to, causing him to rejoice; I then attained a samādhi named "Proclaiming the Ocean of Wondrous Sounds of All Sentient Beings.

Subsequently, I encountered the Tathāgata Vairocana attaining perfect enlightenment at this very site of enlightenment, manifesting various supernatural powers and vast majestic might in every thought-moment. At that time, upon seeing him, I immediately attained this liberation door called "The Adornment of Producing Vast Joy in Every Thought-Moment. Having attained this liberation, I am able to enter into as many oceans of established dharma-realms as there are atoms in ten unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

I beheld that ocean of the established array of the entire Dharma-realm; within every single atom of all Buddha-lands, there were ten times the number of atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-lands of Buddhas’ realms. In each and every realm, the Tathāgata Vairocana sat at the site of enlightenment, attaining perfect awakening in every thought-moment and manifesting various spiritual transformations.

These manifested transformations each pervaded the entire ocean of the Dharma-realm. I also saw my own body present before all those Tathāgatas, and I heard the various teachings being proclaimed by all the Tathāgatas in all those worlds; I listened to them all, receiving and upholding them without forgetting.
"Furthermore, good son!

I further see that from every single pore of all those Tathāgatas, oceans of various emanations emerge, manifesting spiritual powers. Within the oceans of all dharma-realms, the oceans of all Buddha-lands, the varieties of all world-systems, and within all worlds, they turn the wheel of the sublime Dharma as is appropriate for each, according to the various types of birth, the various mental natures, and the various perceptions and conducts of sentient beings."
I have attained the power of the swift dhāraṇī, whereby I am able to receive and uphold all words and meanings, contemplating them with right mindfulness;
with clear and penetrating wisdom, I universally enter the treasury of all pure dharmas;
and with sovereign wisdom, I travel everywhere through the profound ocean of all dharmas.
By means of all-pervasive wisdom, I universally know the vast meanings of the three periods of time;
by means of impartial wisdom, I universally penetrate the non-differentiated Dharma of all Buddhas.
In this way, I am able to awaken to and understand all the Dharma-gates of the Buddhas.
Within each and every dharma-gate, one awakens to and understands all clouds of sūtras;
within each and every cloud of sūtras, one awakens to and understands all oceans of dharmas;
within each and every ocean of dharmas, one awakens to and understands all categories of dharmas.
Within each category of phenomena, one awakens to and understands the clouds of all phenomena;
within each cloud of phenomena, one awakens to and understands the streams of all phenomena;
within each stream of phenomena, there arises the ocean of love and joy for all phenomena.
Each ocean of delight in the Dharma gives birth to all the stages;
within each stage, there arises an ocean of all samādhis;
from each ocean of samādhis, one attains an ocean of visions of all Buddhas.
In each instance, one beholds an ocean of Buddhas and attains an ocean of light of omniscience;
each ocean of light of omniscience universally illumines the three periods of time and pervades the ten directions,
whereby one knows the ocean of past practices of immeasurable Tathāgatas, knows the ocean of all the former deeds of immeasurable Tathāgatas, and knows the immeasurable...
The Tathāgata’s perfection of giving, which is able to relinquish what is difficult to relinquish;
his knowledge of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ ocean of the perfection of pure ethical discipline; his knowledge of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ ocean of the perfection of pure patience;
his knowledge of the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ ocean of the perfection of vast diligence; his knowledge of the immeasurable Tathāgatas...
The ocean of the perfection of meditative concentration, perfected and purified; the ocean of the perfection of wisdom, knowing the immeasurable, profound modes of entry of the Tathāgatas;
the ocean of the perfection of skillful means, knowing the various methods of the immeasurable Tathāgatas;
the ocean of the perfection of vows, knowing the various increases of the immeasurable Tathāgatas; knowing the immeasurable Tathāgatas...
The ocean of the perfection of power through various accomplishments; the ocean of the knowledge of the various perfected perfections of wisdom of immeasurable Tathāgatas;

the ocean of the light of wisdom that universally illuminates the various unobstructed practices of immeasurable Tathāgatas as they transcended the bodhisattva stages in the past; and the knowledge of the various dwellings of immeasurable Tathāgatas in the past as bodhisattvas.
They practice the unimpeded conduct throughout oceans of immeasurable eons;
they manifest spiritual powers to know the various perfected bodhisattva stages of immeasurable Tathāgatas in the past;
and they know the various practices cultivated on the bodhisattva stages by immeasurable Tathāgatas in the past.
They know the various ways immeasurable Tathāgatas purified the bodhisattva stages in the past;
they know the various ways immeasurable Tathāgatas observed the bodhisattva stages in the past;
and they know that when immeasurable Tathāgatas were bodhisattvas in the past, they constantly beheld all Buddhas following them like shadows follow forms.
They know that when immeasurable Tathāgatas were bodhisattvas in the past, they saw the entire ocean of Buddhas and dwelt together with them throughout oceans of eons;
they know that when immeasurable Tathāgatas were bodhisattvas in the past, they manifested throughout oceans of lands by means of infinite bodies;
and they know that when immeasurable Tathāgatas were bodhisattvas in the past, they pervaded the entire dharma-realm while practicing vast and great deeds.
They know how immeasurable Tathāgatas, when they were bodhisattvas in the past, manifested various gates of skillful means to discipline and mature all sentient beings;
they know how immeasurable Tathāgatas emit great radiance that universally illumines all oceans of lands throughout the ten directions;
and they know how immeasurable Tathāgatas manifest great supernormal powers, appearing before all sentient beings everywhere.
They know the ground of the vast wisdom of immeasurable Tathāgatas, which is sovereign in its radiance;
they know the inconceivable spiritual transformations of immeasurable Tathāgatas as they attain perfect enlightenment;
and they know how to receive and uphold all the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma by immeasurable Tathāgatas, never forgetting or losing it.
They know the ocean of manifested marks of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the ocean of manifested bodies of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
and they know the vast spheres of activity of immeasurable Tathāgatas.

From the initial generation of the mind of enlightenment until the extinction of the Dharma, regarding all such dharmas, their diligent pursuit, and their corresponding skillful means, I know and see them all in every moment of thought, entering into them with profound realization.
“Good son! You ask me: ‘How long has it been since you first resolved to attain enlightenment?’”
As for those words, I recall that in the past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in two buddha-fields, as described above,
I was the bodhi-tree goddess named Banner of Perfect Radiance of the Lamp of Merit in the world called Stainless Golden Light Adornment;
there, I heard the various teachings of the Tathāgata Wondrous Sound of the Non-regressive Dharma-realm.
Having resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they practiced various bodhisattva deeds for as many eons as there are atoms in two buddha-fields; thereafter,
they were born within this Sahā world during the Bhadrakalpa, from the time of Kāśyapa Buddha until Śākyamuni Buddha, and in this...
All Tathāgatas who will appear throughout all future kalpas, I shall approach, serve, make offerings to, revere, and honor, causing them to rejoice;

just as I make offerings to all future Buddhas within this Bhadrakalpa of this world, so too shall I approach, serve, and make various kinds of offerings to all future Buddhas throughout all worlds and all kalpas.

"Good son! That world, Adorned with Stainless Golden Light, still exists today; Buddhas continue to appear there in uninterrupted succession. You should single-mindedly cultivate this gate of great courage and valor of a bodhisattva."
At that time, the Night Goddess Silent Ocean of Perfectly Endowed Virtuous Sound, wishing to restate the meaning of this gate of liberation, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"Sudhana, listen now as I speak of this pure and wondrous gate of liberation.
Having heard it, you shall feel love and joy; practice with ultimate diligence until you gain entry."
In the past, throughout an ocean of many eons, I practiced cultivation;
I gave rise to vast and profound faith, Constantly contemplating the nature of phenomena to bring it before me, Swiftly realizing all-knowledge, which is like space.
Toward all Buddhas of the three periods of time, I give rise to a mind of vast faith and joy;
may I serve and always remain in close proximity to their most supreme and pure retinues.
I have seen the Teachers of Gods and Humans in the past, And for the benefit of sentient beings, I made offerings to them all;
Having heard this vast and pure Dharma-gate, My heart feels love and reverence, and joy arises.
Always toward parents and teachers, They show respect and reverence to bring them joy;
With such a mind, never wearying or slackening, They are able to enter deeply into this liberation.
Furthermore, toward those who are aged, sick, or impoverished, whose faculties are uncontrolled and incomplete,
and who have undergone the cycle of rebirth for countless eons— may he compassionately pity and rescue them, bringing them peace and happiness.
Amidst the turbid kalpas of water, fire, kings, and thieves, and amidst the terrors of intoxicated elephants and ferocious beasts,
I formerly practiced within the ocean of existence, providing various forms of protection and rescue so that all might be spared and delivered.
The afflictions of the three realms of existence are ever-blazing, And various karmic obstacles constantly shroud and cover them;
Falling into the perilous difficulties of birth and death, I have in the past rescued them and caused those [afflictions] to be extinguished.
Within all terrors and evil destinies, where various sufferings and hardships perpetually succeed one another,
and birth, old age, sickness, and death afflict their bodies— I shall rescue them all and cause them to emerge.
May I, throughout all kalpas of the future, universally for the sake of all suffering sentient beings,
extinguish birth and death until nothing remains, so that they may attain the ultimate peace and happiness of Buddhahood.
“Good son! I know only this liberation door of the vast adornment of joy, which is swiftly produced in every thought-moment.

As for those Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who enter deeply into the ocean of all dharma-realms, who remain far removed from all internal and external suffering, who have forever eliminated all false conceptualizations, who are fully endowed with all Bodhisattva wisdom, who thoroughly know the number of all kalpas, and who universally behold the formation and destruction of all lands—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?”

"Noble son! In this pure and perfect assembly of the Tathāgata at the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Guardian of All Cities and Increaser of Majestic Virtue. Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
At that time, the youth Sudhana single-mindedly observed the body of the Night Goddess Śāntamati-samudra-guṇa-viśuddhā, joined his palms in reverence, and praised her with these verses:
"Because I have followed the instructions of my spiritual friend, I have now come to the presence of this celestial goddess.
Her body is boundless in measure, equal to Mount Sumeru; Seated upon her throne, she is adorned with every excellence."
Those who are attached to the marks of form, who reckon that various phenomena exist as a basis for reliance—
such people of wrong views, shallow understanding, and inferior wisdom, cannot comprehend the realm of the Honored One.

All the worlds, including gods and humans, though they constantly observe for boundless eons, cannot fathom the body of the Holy One; for its form and characteristics are immeasurable and inconceivable.
The Celestial One is able to remain far removed from all aggregates, And likewise does not rely upon the elements or sense-bases;
For the sake of all beings, he appears in the world, Manifesting various supernormal powers.
The supreme eye of wisdom is ever pure, Stainless, unmoving, and unattached;
It can perceive within every single atom The various supernatural powers of the Buddhas.
You, O Benevolent One, now embody the treasury of the True Dharma; your mind and wisdom are unimpeded and ever-pure.
Having attained the light of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, you further illuminate all living beings.
The mind can universally accumulate boundless karma, adorning all worlds;
realizing that all phenomena are but the mind, it manifests bodies equal in number to all sentient beings.
Understanding that the world is like a dream, That all Buddhas are like reflections,
And that all phenomena are like echoes— utterly empty— They manifest everywhere according to the mind, yet remain unattached.
The Celestial One is able to manifest universally for all sentient beings, appearing in body at every thought-moment with perpetual mastery;
dwelling in neither existence nor non-existence, he constantly hears the preaching of the Dharma throughout all directions.

Immeasurable oceans of lands, as numerous as atoms, And oceans of Sugatas and oceans of sentient beings— All these are contained within a single atom; Such is the power of this Honored One’s realm of liberation.

Then, having praised that goddess with these sublime verses, the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed upon her with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-one;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, in accordance with the practice of the liberation attained by the Night Goddess Silent Ocean of Perfected Merit, contemplated the Dharma-gate taught by that goddess; he did not forget or lose a single word or phrase.

Regarding the immeasurable profound mind, the immeasurable nature of phenomena, and all skillful means, spiritual powers, and wisdom, he recollected and investigated them continuously and without interruption. He made subtle distinctions, understood their profound depth, and with a vast mind, realized and dwelt therein.

Gradually proceeding, he went to the place where the Night Goddess Sarvarūpavilokitā-vīrya-utsāha-vardhanī resided; there he saw that goddess seated upon a lion throne within a great lotus treasury of mani-jewel kings, which universally illumined all palaces, surrounded before and behind by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of night goddesses.

He manifests a body that universally accords with the physical forms of all sentient beings; he manifests a body that appears before all sentient beings; he manifests a body unstained by any worldly realm; he manifests a body equal in number to all sentient beings; he manifests a body that transcends all worlds; he manifests a body that turns according to the needs of those to be tamed; he manifests a body that swiftly reaches all ten directions; he manifests a body that fulfills all great vows; he manifests a body that is the ultimate nature of a Tathāgata which extinguishes and removes all obstacles; and he manifests a body that ultimately teaches and brings all sentient beings to maturity.

Having seen this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; his aspirations were fulfilled, and he rejoiced immeasurably. He prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with palms joined before him, addressed him, saying:
"Noble One!..."

I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva, while practicing the bodhisattva conduct, benefits and brings peace and happiness to sentient beings.
How does one gather in sentient beings by means of the unsurpassed gathering?
How does one train in the bodhisattva path?
How does one abide in the bodhisattva activities?
How does one accord with the teachings of all Buddhas?
How does one draw near to the rank of the Dharma King?
I pray only that you will take pity on me and explain this for my sake.
At that time, the night goddess said to Sudhana:
“Excellent! Excellent!”

"Noble son! For the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings; for the sake of adorning and purifying all Buddha-fields; for the sake of making offerings to all Tathāgatas; because you wish to abide through all kalpas to rescue sentient beings; because you wish to guard and protect the lineage of all Buddhas; because you wish to universally enter the ten directions to cultivate all practices; because you wish to universally enter the ocean of all dharma-gates; because you wish to universally enter all objects of knowledge with a mind of equanimity; because you wish to universally hear and uphold the true wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; and because you wish to universally rain down the rain of Dharma according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings—you inquire about the gates of practice cultivated by the Bodhisattvas."

"Good son! I have attained the Bodhisattva liberation door of the Profound, Sovereign, and Lovely Melodious Voice. As a great Dharma teacher with a white silk cloth bound upon my head, my mind is unattached to all phenomena, for I am well able to reveal the profound Dharma-treasury of all Tathāgatas;
I possess the power of great vows and great compassion, causing all sentient beings to abide in the bodhicitta."
They are able to perform all deeds that benefit sentient beings, for they accumulate roots of goodness without ceasing;
they serve as masters who discipline all sentient beings, leading them to abide in the path of omniscience;
they act as great clouds of Dharma for all worlds, universally raining down the teachings of all the sūtras.
They act as the sun of the pure Dharma for all worlds, universally illuminating the world to cause the roots of goodness to arise;
their minds are impartial toward all worlds, universally causing sentient beings to increase in wholesome dharmas;
their minds are pure regarding all sensory objects, eliminating and extinguishing all unwholesome karma.
They act as great guides, leading sentient beings to enter into all virtuous practices;
they serve as the adornment of wisdom for all sentient beings, ensuring that all worlds are preceded by wisdom in their performance of all virtuous deeds;
and they constantly attend upon all spiritual friends in order to establish sentient beings in the Buddha's teaching.

"Good son! By means of these dharmas, I bestow gifts of Dharma upon sentient beings, causing them to give rise to pure qualities (*śukla-dharma*). Their resolve in seeking all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) becomes as firm as the Vajra-Nārāyaṇa treasury; they are well able to discern the power of the Buddha and the power of Māra; they constantly draw near to virtuous friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); they shatter the mountain ranges of all karmic and afflictive hindrances; they gather the dharmas that assist the path to all-knowledge; and their minds never abandon the ground of all-knowledge—the perfect, pure, and unobstructed dharma-gate."

“Good son! By means of such light of pure dharmas, I universally awaken all sentient beings, providing manifold benefits, accumulating roots of goodness, and increasing and perfecting the factors conducive to the path; at that time, I constantly perform ten kinds of observations of the dharma-realm.”
What are the ten? They are:
knowing that the dharma-realm is immeasurable, because one has attained the light of vast wisdom;
I know that the dharma-realm is boundless, for I behold all the Buddhas’ various spiritual transformations;
I know that the dharma-realm is limitless, for I universally enter all Buddha-lands to reverently make offerings to all Tathāgatas;
I know that the dharma-realm has no boundaries, for I universally manifest the practice of bodhisattva deeds throughout all oceans of worlds.
I know that the dharma-realm is uninterrupted, for I have entered the Tathāgata’s profound, equal, and variously perfected wisdom of non-interruption;

I know that the dharma-realm is of a single nature, for I have entered the Tathāgata’s perfected speech and sounds, which accord with the minds of sentient beings such that there is nothing they do not understand;
I know that the nature of the dharma-realm is pure, for I have entered the ocean of the Tathāgata’s past vows, ultimately to tame all sentient beings.
I know that the dharma-realm pervades all sentient beings, because the sublime practices of Samantabhadra are universally pervasive;
I know that the dharma-realm is a single adornment, because the spiritual powers of Samantabhadra skillfully adorn it;
I know that the dharma-realm is indestructible, because all roots of goodness fill the dharma-realm and are thus indestructible.

"Good son! By performing these ten kinds of observations of the dharma-realm, I have come to understand it in accordance with its nature; I have brought forth all vast roots of goodness, distinguished the factors that assist the path, clearly comprehended the supreme majesty and virtue of all Buddhas, and deeply entered the inconceivable realm of the Tathāgatas."
Furthermore, son of good family!

Through such conformable mental attention and correct mindfulness, I have attained the ten kinds of vast and majestic dharani-wheels of the Tathagata, and I universally expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.

What are these ten? They are: the dharani-wheel of universal entry into the ocean of all dharmas; the dharani-wheel of universally upholding the treasury of all dharmas; the dharani-wheel of universally receiving the clouds of all pure dharmas; the dharani-wheel of universally recollecting the lamp of wisdom of all Tathāgatas; the dharani-wheel of universally manifesting the sounds of the names of all Tathāgatas; the dharani-wheel of universally entering the ocean of the equal vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; the dharani-wheel of universally entering the ocean of practices of all vehicles and swiftly bringing them to fulfillment; the dharani-wheel of universally entering the ocean of karma of all sentient beings and purifying all defilements and obstructions; the dharani-wheel of swiftly revolving the ocean of karma to make it pure; and the dharani-wheel of swiftly giving birth to the courageous accomplishment of the knowledge of all-knowledge.
"Good son! These ten dharani-wheels have ten thousand dharani-wheels as their retinue, and they constantly expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings."
"Good son! For some sentient beings, I teach the Dharma of the wisdom of hearing; for some sentient beings, I teach the Dharma of the wisdom of reflection;
for some sentient beings, I teach the Dharma of the wisdom of cultivation; or for some sentient beings, I teach the Dharma of the ocean of existence."
For some sentient beings, they speak of the dharma of the ocean of all that exists; for some sentient beings, they speak of the dharma of the ocean of the names of a single Tathāgata;
for some sentient beings, they speak of the dharma of the ocean of the names of all Tathāgatas;
for some sentient beings, they speak of the dharma of a single world-ocean; or for some sentient beings, they speak of the dharma of all world-oceans. Or...

For the sake of sentient beings, he expounds the dharma of the ocean of prophecies of a single Buddha; or for the sake of sentient beings, he expounds the dharma of the ocean of prophecies of all Buddhas;
or for the sake of sentient beings, he expounds the dharma of the ocean of the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of a single Tathāgata;
or for the sake of sentient beings, he expounds the dharma of the ocean of the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas; or for the sake of sentient beings, he expounds...
Either the Dharma of the ocean of the wheel of the Dharma of a single Tathāgata, or for the sake of sentient beings he expounds the Dharma of the ocean of the wheels of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas;

or for the sake of sentient beings he expounds the Dharma of the ocean of the sūtras of a single Tathāgata, or for the sake of sentient beings he expounds the Dharma of the ocean of the sūtras of all Tathāgatas; or for the sake of sentient beings he expounds the assembly of a single Tathāgata.
The Dharma of the Ocean of Assemblies: for some sentient beings, he teaches the Dharma of the ocean of assemblies of all Tathāgatas;

for some sentient beings, he teaches the Dharma of the ocean of the single mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); for some sentient beings, he teaches the Dharma of the ocean of all minds of omniscience;
for some sentient beings, he teaches the Dharma of the departure via the Single Vehicle (*ekayāna*); or for some sentient beings...
I teach the Dharma of renunciation for all vehicles. Good son!
It is with these and other such ineffable Dharma-gates that I teach for the sake of sentient beings.

"Good son! I have entered such oceans of gateways into the non-differentiated Dharma-realm, wherein I preach the unsurpassed Dharma, universally and supremely gathering in all sentient beings, and shall abide in the practices of Samantabhadra throughout all kalpas of the future."

At that time, this liberation of the profound, sovereign, and lovely wondrous sound cultivated and increased all the gates of liberation of all bodhisattvas in every thought-moment, filling the entire dharma-realm in every thought-moment.
Then, the youth Sudhana said to the Night Goddess:
"How marvelous! O Noble One!"
"This gate of liberation is thus rare and thus profound; O Noble One, how long has it been since you realized it?
The night goddess replied, "O son of good family!..."
In the distant past, beyond world-systems as numerous as the atoms in a great trichiliocosm, there was an eon named Stainless Flame Light;

a world-system named Dharma-Realm Flame Light Auspicious Cloud, which had as its substance the transformation-mani-kings that manifest the ocean of karma of all sentient beings. It was shaped like a lotus, a mixture of the pure and the defiled, and rested upon a network of various fragrant mani-kings as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru.

It was adorned in succession by the wondrous jewel lotuses of the voices of the great vows of all Tathāgatas of the past; it was encircled by jewel lotus-rimmed mountains as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru, and interspersed with fragrant mani-jewels as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru.

There were as many sets of four continents as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru; in each set of four continents, there were unspeakably unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of cities.
"Good son! In that world there is a four-continent system named Variegated-Colored Exquisite Adornment Banner;
within it is a royal capital named Universal Jewel Kusuma Light."
Not far from there is a site of enlightenment named Universal Manifestation of the Palace Images of the Dharma King;
therein appear Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru, the first of whom is named Great Sound Light King of the Ocean of All Dharmas.

When that Buddha appeared in the world, there was a wheel-turning king named Sunlight of the Stainless Face. At the presence of that Buddha, he heard the *Sūtra of the Revolving Ocean of All Dharmas* and was able to receive and uphold it entirely. After the Buddha entered parinirvāṇa, the king left the household life to protect and maintain the True Dharma. When the Dharma was about to perish, there were a thousand distinct lineages of the Buddha’s True Dharma Eye, which divided into ten thousand gates, each teaching the Dharma in various ways according to what was appropriate for them.

Approaching the final kalpa when the five turbidities manifest, there will be many evil bhikṣus whose karmic afflictions and hindrances are heavy, bound by various fetters, and prone to much strife. Delighting in and attached to sensory objects, they will accept and take without satiety; they will not seek any superior merit, but instead delight in discoursing on kings, thieves, women, nations, oceans, and various other worldly matters. They will not abandon the nihilistic views of the non-Buddhists, their minds becoming stained with craving and attachment, unable to let go.
At that time, the bhikṣu King addressed him with the sound of the True Dharma, saying:
"How marvelous! How suffering!"
"The Buddha, throughout oceans of countless great kalpas, endured various sufferings to assemble this torch of Dharma; why do you all together seek to extinguish it?

Having spoken these words, he ascended into the air to a height of seven tala trees. From his body issued immeasurable clouds of flames of many colors, emitting great nets of light in various hues, causing immeasurable sentient beings to eliminate the heat of their afflictions and causing immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
By these causes and conditions, the teaching of that Tathāgata flourished once again for sixty thousand years.
At that time, there was among that assembly a bhikṣuṇī named Dharmacakra-nirmāṇa-prabhā, who was the daughter of this king and had a retinue of one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs.

Upon hearing the words of their father, the king, and witnessing his supernatural powers, radiance, and majestic authority, they all resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, never again to regress.

Each of those bhikṣuṇīs attained a samādhi called "Manifesting the Tathāgatas' Equal Birth," as well as a dhāraṇī called "Vajra-Light of All Tathāgatas Turning the Wheel of Dharma," and a prajñāpāramitā called "Universally Entering the Ocean of All Dharma-Gates."

At that time, the bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakra-nirmāṇa-prabhā immediately attained a samādhi called "Lamp of Radiant Light Producing All Buddha-Teachings," and further attained this profound, sovereign, and lovely liberation of wondrous sound.

Because they have attained this samādhi gate of liberation, their bodies and minds become supple, subtle, and blissful, whereby they are able to directly perceive all the supernatural powers and majestic might possessed by the Tathāgata Great Sound Radiance King of the Ocean of All Dharmas.
“Good son! What do you think?

Was that Cakravartin King Vimalavaktra-sūryaprabha—who, following that Tathāgata, turned the wheel of the true Dharma, and after his parinirvāṇa, flourished during the period of the final dharma, lit the great torch of the Dharma, and illuminated the world with its light—anyone else?”
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is this very person;
the bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakrapravartanavikurvaṇaprabhā is none other than myself;
and the hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs who were her retinue are these hundred thousand night goddesses present in this assembly.

At that time, I protected the Buddha-dharma, causing one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs to attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; furthermore, I caused them to attain the samādhi of the manifest vision of the equal birth of all Tathāgatas; furthermore, I caused them to attain the *dhāraṇī* of the vajra-light of the dharma-wheel of all Tathāgatas; and furthermore, I caused them to attain the *prajñāpāramitā* that universally enters the ocean of all dharma-gates.
"Good son! After that Tathāgata, another Buddha appeared in the world, named Vimaladharmaparvatāgra-jñānāvabhāsa.
I served and made offerings to him in various ways, causing his mind to be filled with joy."

next there arose a Buddha named Universal Wisdom Radiance Dharma-City Lamp. Good son!

Such Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru—the last of whom was named King of the Lamp of Wisdom in the City of the Dharma Realm—who appeared in the world during the eon called Stainless Flame Light, I have all honored, approached, and made offerings to; I have heard, received, and upheld the sublime Dharma they taught. I also went forth from home to study the Path under those various Tathāgatas, protecting and upholding their teachings, and entering this Bodhisattva liberation of the Profound, Sovereign, and Lovely Sublime Sound, whereby I have used various skillful means to teach and mature immeasurable sentient beings.
From that time until now, throughout as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, I have made offerings to all the Buddhas who appeared in the world and have practiced their teachings.

"Good son! Since that time, amidst all sentient beings who sleep in the darkness of ignorance during the night of saṃsāra, I alone have awakened; I cause all sentient beings to guard the city of the mind, to abandon the cities of the triple world, and to dwell in the unsurpassed city of the Dharma of omniscience."

"Good son! I know only this profound, sovereign, and lovely liberation of Wondrous Sound. As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they have abandoned all worldly, impure speech; they do not speak with duplicity, they restrain their vocal karma, they walk the straight path, they abide securely in the ultimate truth, they achieve perfection, and they are forever unbound by any speech."

In every thought-moment, they awaken to the intrinsic nature of all speech and enter deeply into the ocean of all sounds and voices. They comprehend the ocean of all sentient beings' secrets and clearly perceive the ocean of all dharma-gates. Universally encompassing the ocean of all equal dharmas, they give birth to various oceans of *dhāraṇīs* and have attained mastery. According to what is appropriate for the minds of sentient beings, they preach the Dharma; through skillful means, they ultimately subdue and bring sentient beings to maturity. Able to universally embrace all sentient beings, they skillfully cultivate the supreme deeds of Bodhisattvas and enter deeply into the various dharma-gates of Bodhisattvas. With extremely subtle wisdom, they are able to skillfully observe various wondrous matters and the treasuries of Bodhisattvas, and they can freely expound the teachings of all Bodhisattvas.
Why is this? Because they have already attained and perfected the *dhāraṇī* of all wheels of Dharma, they are named "Supremely Excellent and Truly Authentic Great Beings.
How then could I know or describe their meritorious conduct?

"Noble son! Within this assembly of the Buddha at the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhā. Go to her and ask: how should a bodhisattva study all-knowledge? How should they cultivate all-knowledge? And how should they guide all sentient beings so that they may awaken to and enter the city of all-knowledge?"
At that time, the Night Goddess who Protects All Cities and Increases Majestic Virtue, wishing to reiterate the meaning of this gate of liberation, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"The liberation of Bodhisattvas is profound and difficult to see; It is like space, the limit of equality and suchness.
Within the boundless Dharma-realm, they universally behold All the Buddhas of the three periods of time."
Giving birth to immeasurable liberations, They realize and enter the inconceivable true nature of phenomena;
Swiftly increasing unimpeded wisdom, They penetrate the path of compassion throughout the three periods of time.
Passing through as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system, there was an eon named Vimalaprabhā;
the world-system was called Dharmaprabhāśrīmegha, and the city was named Samantaratnakusuma.
Among them, various Buddhas appeared in the world, In number equal to the atoms of Mount Sumeru;
The Buddha named Dharma-Ocean Great Sound King Was the first to appear within this kalpa.
Down to the very last Buddha among them, named Dharmadhātu-jñāna-dīpa-rāja—
toward all such Tathāgatas as these, I have made offerings and listened to their Dharma.
I beheld the Buddha Dharma-sāgara-ghoṣa-rāja, his body universally manifesting in true golden color, adorned with all the marks like a mountain of jewels;
I resolved my mind, vowing to attain the teacherless Way.
Upon briefly beholding the body of that Tathāgata, I immediately gave rise to the vast mind of Bodhi;
I vowed to diligently seek all-knowledge, With a mind equal to space and the nature of the Dharma-realm.
Through this, one universally beholds the Buddhas of the three periods of time, as well as the ocean of all Bodhisattvas;
one also sees the oceans of lands and the oceans of sentient beings, and everywhere gives rise to the mind of great compassion.
According to what is appropriate for the minds of all sentient beings, A single body universally manifests in boundless lands;
Radiating light and shaking the earth throughout the ten directions, It awakens and enlightens all conscious beings.
Beholding the second Buddha, they draw near to him; likewise, they behold the Buddhas of the ocean of lands in the ten directions, until the final Buddha appears, named Dharma-realm Wisdom Lamp King.
In numbers as vast as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, they make offerings to all these Tathāgatas.
Throughout all lands, for the duration of infinitely subtle eons,
I have personally approached and reverently served all Tathāgatas, the lamps that illuminate the world, thereby purifying this liberation.

At that time, the youth Sudhana attained this bodhisattva liberation of the profound, sovereign, and lovely "Wonderful Sound"; he entered the ocean of boundless samādhis and accomplished the ocean of vast dhāraṇīs; furthermore, he attained the ocean of the bodhisattvas’ great supernormal powers and deeply entered the ocean of the bodhisattvas’ great eloquence, swiftly increasing the ocean of great joy.
He then observed the Night Goddess, Sovereign Increasing Majestic Power Who Guards All Cities, and praised her with these verses:
"You have traversed the vast and deep ocean of wisdom, And have crossed the boundless ocean of all realms of existence."
With a long life, free from affliction, and a body that is a treasury of wisdom, His majestic radiance shines everywhere like the full moon.
Awakened to the nature of phenomena as being like space, He enters the three periods of time universally without obstruction.
