In every thought-moment he universally takes all objects as his focus, Yet mind after mind remains tranquil and free from discrimination.
Observing that the nature of sentient beings is fundamentally non-existent, Great compassion constantly enters the ocean of sentient beings;
Sovereignly roaming through the gates of liberation, He extensively delivers the immeasurable multitudes of the deluded.
Contemplating and reflecting upon all phenomena, Realizing the profound nature of all dharmas,
Universally practicing all noble paths, Universally transforming sentient beings to bring them to liberation.

The Celestial One is the supreme Teacher and Tamer; He reveals the stainless wisdom of the Tathāgata, Universally for all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, Expounding the pure conduct that is free from defilement.
Having already dwelled in the path of all Tathāgatas’ vows, having already entered boundless and vast wisdom,
having already cultivated all the powers of the Buddhas, and having already witnessed the miraculous feats of the Buddhas—
the celestial deity’s mind is pure like space, universally free from all afflictions.
They thoroughly know the immeasurable lands of the three periods of time, as well as all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and sentient beings.
In a single thought-moment, they fully comprehend the oceans of days and nights, months, years, and eons;
they also know all categories of sentient beings, with their various names and characteristics each distinct.
Regarding the realms of birth and death of sentient beings in the ten directions— those with form, those without form, those with perception, and those without perception—
he fully understands them all in accordance with worldly conventions, and guides them to enter the path to Bodhi.
Having been born into the family of the Tathāgatas’ vows, Having entered the ocean of the merits of all Buddhas,
And having realized the equality of mind within the nature of phenomena, They manifest form bodies according to the inclinations of sentient beings.

Then, having spoken these sublime verses in praise of the night goddess, the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having attained this bodhisattva liberation of the profound, sovereign, and lovely wondrous sound, contemplated it with right mindfulness, causing it to increase and expand, and diligently manifested it through universal practice.

He immediately went to the presence of the Night Goddess Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃdarśanā, and saw her body within a pavilion formed by the branches of trees made of various precious fragrances; she was seated upon a lion throne of exquisite jewels and a wondrous treasury from a great precious tree, surrounded before and behind by ten thousand night goddesses.
The youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, joined his palms before him, and spoke these words: "Noble One!

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, how they should practice so as to achieve and increase it, and how they may attain all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*). I only pray that you will take pity on me and explain this for me."
The night goddess said: "Good son!

When the sun has set in this Sahā world, the lotuses have closed, and the multitudes of people have finished their excursions and sightseeing, I see all those sentient beings—whether on mountains, by waters, in cities, in wildernesses, or in foreign lands—in all such places, who have resolved to return to their dwellings but have lost their way. They are terrified and uneasy; I secretly protect them all, ensuring they are free from fear."
They emit light to reveal the right path and lead them to their destination;
they cause all beings to be freed from manifold sufferings and to dwell in peace and happiness day and night;
and if there are those afflicted by the pains of illness, they bring them peace and happiness even within their dreams.

"Good son! If there are sentient beings in the prime of their youth and endowed with fine appearance who are attached to indulgence and self-indulgence in the five desires, their minds intoxicated by arrogance, I manifest for them the signs of old age, sickness, and death to cause them to give rise to fear, so that they may abandon all evils, forever sever ignorance, and be freed from the terror of birth and death. Furthermore, I praise various roots of goodness to lead them to practice them;
for those who are stingy, I praise the virtue of giving."
For those who violate the precepts, they extol pure morality;
for those who harbor anger and malice, they cause them to practice loving-kindness and patience;
for those who are indolent, they cause them to arouse diligence.
If there are those who are distracted, they are led to cultivate meditative concentration;
if there are those who abide in wrong wisdom, they are led to study Prajñā;
if there are those who delight in the Hīnayāna, they are led to abide in the Mahāyāna and diligently practice all skillful means.
For those who delight in and are attached to the various realms of existence within the triple world, I cause them to abide in the Bodhisattva’s perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*);

for those sentient beings whose merit and wisdom are weak, who are oppressed by the bonds of karma and afflictions, and who lack mastery due to various obstacles, I cause them to abide in the Bodhisattva’s perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*);

and for those sentient beings whose minds are darkened, who lack wisdom, and who are obscured by various delusions through attachment to a self and what belongs to a self, I cause them to abide in the Bodhisattva’s perfection of knowledge (*jñāna-pāramitā*).
“Good son! I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door called ‘The Radiance of Vast Joyful Birth. Sudhana said:
"Noble One! What is the sphere of this gate of liberation?
The night goddess replied:
“Good son! Entering this liberation enables one to know the Tathāgata’s various accumulations of merit, his universal gathering of sentient beings, his skillful means, and the light of his wisdom.”

How are they universally encompassed? Good son! All the various pleasures experienced by all sentient beings are due to the power of the Tathāgata’s majestic virtue; because they accord with the Tathāgata’s teaching; because they practice the Tathāgata’s words; because they study the Tathāgata’s conduct; because they have obtained the power of the Tathāgata’s protection; because they cultivate the path sealed by the Tathāgata; because they plant roots of goodness of the same kind as the Tathāgata; because they praise the excellent fruits similar to those of the Tathāgata; because they guard the precepts and dharmas spoken by the Tathāgata; because they rejoice in the vast vows of the Tathāgata; because they are illuminated by the sun-like light of the Tathāgata’s impartial wisdom; and because they are encompassed by the power of the Tathāgata’s intrinsically pure and perfect karmic force.
For this reason, all the various forms of peace and happiness in the world appear and are accomplished.
How is this known to be so? Good son!

When I entered this liberation door of the light of vast joy arising from birth, I mindfully contemplated the ocean of bodhisattva practices cultivated by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana in the past; observing them in accordance with reality, I saw them all clearly.

"Good son! In the past, when the World-Honored One was a bodhisattva, he saw that all sentient beings were attached to 'self' and 'what belongs to self,' dwelling in the dark chamber of ignorance, entering the dense forest of various views, bound by craving and attachment, destroyed by anger, confounded by folly, and entangled by stinginess and jealousy. Their bodies and minds were oppressed and disturbed by manifold afflictions; they transmigrated through birth and death in poverty and hardship, unable to encounter the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
Having seen this, I gave rise to a heart of great compassion, desiring to benefit all sentient beings;
that is to say:
I gave rise to the vow to obtain all kinds of exquisite treasures and requisites to gather in the hearts of sentient beings, and the vow that all sentient beings...
A mind that fully possesses all necessities of life without deficiency; a mind free from attachment toward all matters;
a mind free from greedy defilement regarding all sensory objects; a mind free from stinginess regarding all possessions;
a mind free from doubt regarding all acts of giving; and a mind free from expectation regarding any karmic rewards.
A mind that harbors no envy for any worldly splendor; a mind that is undeluded regarding all causes and conditions;
a mind that gives rise to the observation of the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); a mind that gives rise to the rescue and protection of all sentient beings;
a mind that gives rise to the deep entry into the whirlpool of the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of all dharmas; and a mind that dwells among all sentient beings.
The mind of equal great loving-kindness; the mind of great compassion that gives rise to skillful means for the sake of all sentient beings;
the mind that gives rise to the great Dharma-canopy to universally cover all sentient beings so they may be free from feverish affliction;

the mind that gives rise to the great adamantine vajra of supreme wisdom to shatter the mountain-like great obstacles of the afflictions of all sentient beings; the mind that gives rise to [the resolve] to cause all sentient beings to quickly...
The mind that swiftly increases and expands great joy and bliss; the mind that gives rise to the vow that all sentient beings shall ultimately achieve supreme peace and happiness;
the mind that gives rise to the desire to rain down all manner of wealth and treasures according to the wishes of all sentient beings;
the mind that gives rise to the equal application of skillful means to bring all sentient beings to maturity; and the mind that causes all sentient beings to be fulfilled.
With a mind that values the wealth of the noble ones, they give rise to the aspiration that all sentient beings shall ultimately attain the fruit of the ten powers of wisdom.

Having given rise to such a mind, they obtain the power of a bodhisattva and manifest great spiritual transformations that pervade the most supreme dharma-realm of empty space. Before all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, they manifest all forms, all riches, and all acts of giving; from the great cloud of objectless compassion, they rain down universally all manner of precious necklaces and articles for livelihood, satisfying the desires of all sentient beings according to their hearts' wishes and causing them all to rejoice.

In this way, through the gateway of immeasurable giving, he constantly practices bestowing various kinds of wealth and material goods at all times without ever ceasing; he does so without regret or stinginess, continuously and without interruption.

By these skillful means, they universally gather in all sentient beings, teaching and transforming them until they are fully perfected and complete, causing them all to emerge from the hardships of birth and death. Providing protection and benefit, they do not expect any recompense; they maintain an equanimous intention and a mind free of discrimination, purifying the jewel-like minds of all sentient beings. They cause them to give rise to a single, profound, and secret root of goodness that is identical to that of all Buddhas. According to the minds of sentient beings, they provide various requisites to gather them in, increasing their omniscience and swiftly bringing the great ocean of merit to full completion.

In this way, in every thought-moment, the Bodhisattva exhaustively tames and matures all sentient beings throughout the entirety of the realms without exception, causing them all to attain supreme purity;
in every thought-moment, they adorn and purify all Buddha-fields, ensuring they are free from defilement;
and in every thought-moment, they universally enter all dharma-realms.
In every thought-moment, they pervade the entirety of the realm of empty space;
in every thought-moment, they universally enter all three periods of time;
in every thought-moment, they subdue sentient beings through the wisdom of skillful means.
In every thought-moment, they constantly and universally turn the non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma throughout all worlds;
in every thought-moment, they constantly and skillfully benefit all sentient beings through the path of omniscience;

in every thought-moment, they universally manifest the attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment as all Buddhas before all the various and diverse assemblies of beings throughout all worlds, for as long as all future eons endure.
In every thought-moment, they universally cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all worlds and all kalpas, giving rise to no dualistic notions, namely:

universally entering into the ocean of all vast world-systems—including all the various boundary-defined worlds within every kind of world-lineage, worlds of various adornments, worlds of various essential natures, worlds of various shapes, and worlds of various distributions; and, in every thought-moment, universally cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all worlds and all kalpas, giving rise to no dualistic notions, namely: universally entering into the ocean of all vast world-systems—including all the various boundary-defined worlds within every kind of world-lineage, worlds of various adornments, worlds of various essential natures, worlds of various shapes, and worlds of various distributions.

There are worlds that are defiled yet mixed with purity; there are worlds that are pure yet mixed with defilement; there are worlds that are exclusively defiled, and there are worlds that are exclusively pure. Some are vast, some are narrow; some are high, some are low; some are coarse, some are sublime; some are upright, some are tilted; some are inverted, some are face-up; some are circular, some are square, and some are neither circular nor square.

In all such worlds of various names, forms, and adornments, they practice all bodhisattva deeds from moment to moment, enter the bodhisattva abodes, manifest the power of bodhisattvas, and also manifest the bodies of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; according to the minds of sentient beings, they cause them to universally know and see, swiftly increasing the ocean-gates of merit and the wisdom of omniscience.

"Good son! When the Tathāgata Vairocana was practicing the bodhisattva path in past lives in this manner, he saw that sentient beings did not cultivate merit or virtue, lacked wisdom, were devoid of shame and remorse, and were attached to the self and what belongs to the self;
obscured by the cataracts of ignorance, they gave rise to various forms of improper reflection and entered into the evil nets of false views."
In the dense forest of ignorance, they fail to recognize cause and effect; following the karma of afflictions, their minds are deluded and they lack self-mastery.
Falling into the deep pits of the perilous cycle of birth and death, they undergo all manner of immeasurable sufferings.
[The Bodhisattva], giving rise to great compassion, cultivates and accumulates all the practices of the *pāramitās*, acting for the sake of all sentient beings.
They extol and praise firm roots of goodness, causing beings to dwell securely in a state far removed from the poverty and suffering of birth and death;
they cause them to diligently cultivate the dharmas that assist the path of merit and wisdom;

for their sake, they explain the various gateways of cause and effect, explain that karmic retribution is never contradictory, explain the points of realization within the Dharma, and explain the One [Vehicle].
He understands the desires and inclinations of all sentient beings and explains all the lands where they take birth;
he causes them not to sever the lineage of all Buddhas, causes them to protect all the Buddha-teachings, and causes them to abandon all evils.

Furthermore, it was to praise the dharmas that assist the path toward omniscience; to cause all sentient beings to give rise to joy in their hearts; to cause them to practice the gift of Dharma so as to universally gather in all; to cause them to initiate the conduct of omniscience; to cause them to study and train in the path of the *pāramitās* of the great bodhisattvas; to cause them to increase and perfect the ocean of all roots of goodness for omniscience; to cause them to fulfill all the treasures of the noble ones; to cause them to enter the gate of the Buddha’s sovereignty; to cause them to grasp immeasurable skillful means; to cause them to observe the majestic power of the Tathāgata; to cause them to draw near to and accord with the Tathāgata’s tranquil peace and happiness; and to cause them to dwell securely in the accomplishment of the various wisdoms of a bodhisattva.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-two;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-three.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśa, by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on Entering the Sphere of the Inconceivable Liberation:
The Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra," at that time, the youth Sudhana said: "Noble One!"
“Noble son, how long has it been since you first resolved to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and have cultivated these sublime practices?
The night goddess replied: “Noble son!”
As you have asked, this matter is difficult to know, difficult to believe, difficult to understand, difficult to realize, difficult to enter,
difficult to demonstrate, difficult to give rise to, and difficult to expound; it cannot be known by any in the world—
gods, humans, śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas— except through the majestic power of the Tathāgata.
Empowered by spiritual strength, sustained by virtuous friends, and having cultivated vast merit and wisdom, their minds are firm;
their aspirations are pure, free from inferiority, free from defilement, free from deceit, free from distraction, free from base stinginess, and free from extreme darkness. They have attained...
The mind that universally illuminates and causes all-knowledge to blossom; the mind that gives rise to universal benefit, happiness, and the maturation of all sentient beings;
the mind that cannot be destroyed by any afflictions or maras; the mind that sets out inevitably toward all-encompassing wisdom without obstruction;
and the mind that takes no pleasure in any worldly birth-and-death or defilements.
With a mind undefiled by worldly pleasure, they are able to joyfully contemplate the pure, wondrous bliss of all Tathāgatas;
they are able to diligently eliminate the ocean of sorrow, lamentation, and suffering of all sentient beings; they are able to cultivate the ocean of merit and dharmas of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
they are able to contemplate the reality-nature of all phenomena as the realm of emptiness; and they are able to be endowed with all [virtues].
With vast, profound, and pure faith and understanding, one can transcend the turbulent currents of all birth and death,
enter the ocean of wisdom of all Tathāgatas, reach with certainty the unsurpassed city of Dharma,
courageously enter the realm of the Tathāgatas, swiftly proceed toward the stages of wisdom of all Buddhas, and immediately accomplish everything.
One with the power of wisdom, who has attained ultimate mastery over the ten powers—
such a person is able to know this, enter into it, believe in it, understand it, uphold it, comprehend it, and practice in accordance with it.
Why is this? This is the sphere of the Tathāgata’s wisdom; even all bodhisattvas cannot know it, let alone other sentient beings.

Nevertheless, I shall now rely upon the Buddha’s majestic power, desiring to cause the minds of those sentient beings who are ready for transformation to be swiftly purified, and desiring to cause the minds of those sentient beings who cultivate roots of goodness to attain mastery. In accordance with your question, I shall proclaim it for you.

At that time, the Night Goddess Sarva-vṛkṣa-puṣpa-saṃkusumitānkuśeśvarā, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, surveyed the realm of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time and spoke these verses:
“O Son of the Buddha, regarding that which you now inquire about— The boundless and profound realm of all Buddhas—
Even in eons as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of inconceivable lands, One could not exhaustively expound it in its entirety.”
Those who are defiled by various evils—greed, hatred, and delusion; those shrouded by pride and the confusion of ignorance;
and sentient beings bound by the fetters of a stained mind—cannot know the tranquil Dharma of the Buddhas.
Those whose minds are turbid and agitated by flattery and deception, who are never parted from stinginess and envy,
and who are bound by the ropes of afflictions and karma— how could they ever understand the realm of the Buddha?
One who does not cling to the aggregates, elements, and sense bases, whose mind never abandons the view of a self,
and who possesses the perversions of mind, perception, and view— such a person can enter the Tathāgata’s ground of quiescence.
The realm of the Buddhas is tranquil and profoundly deep; its original nature is true, eternal, and free from conceptual discrimination.
Those who are attached to the existence of birth and death cannot enter this equality that relies on no dharma.
Born into the lineage of all Buddhas, Constantly guarded by all Tathāgatas,
Those who can uphold the treasury of the Dharma King’s teachings— This is the domain of the seer’s eye of wisdom.
Associating with true spiritual friends, delighting in the pure Dharma without weariness,
and single-mindedly seeking the power of the Buddha to receive the Cloud of Dharma— those who hear this teaching shall give rise to joy.
The mind is ever pure and free from conceptualization; unattached to all things like space, the lamp of wisdom sovereignly destroys ignorance—this is the realm of the stainless one.
Enveloping the world with great compassion, Pervading the ocean of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time,
Bestowing benefit and happiness according to their needs without limit— This is the realm of those who practice deeply.
The mind is always joyful and free from all attachments; one is able to relinquish everything that exists.
Delighting in preaching the Dharma, one bestows gifts equally upon all sentient beings—this is the realm of those who are unattached.
The mind is free from defilement and turbidity, detached from all faults; Thoroughly disciplined, it is without sorrow or regret;
Following the Buddha’s teachings, one is able to practice them fully— This is the realm of those who are stainless.
With a mind free from agitation and conceptualization, One can universally awaken to the nature of all phenomena;
Far removed from all delusions and karmic actions— This is the realm of those who have attained liberation.
With a mind free from weariness and ever without retreat, Vigorously and diligently cultivating all-knowledge,
Abiding securely within the supreme pure precepts— This is the domain of the Great Being.
Their minds enter deeply into all samādhis, Ultimately cool and free from feverish affliction;
Having cultivated the causes for the ocean of omniscience, This is the liberation of those who dwell in tranquility.
Thoroughly knowing the distinct characteristics of all phenomena, Skillfully entering the boundless and profound Dharma-realm,
Universally delivering all living beings without exception— This is the liberation of the Lamp of Wisdom.
Thoroughly realizing the true nature of sentient beings, they have no attachment to the ocean of existences;
appearing everywhere like reflections in the water of the mind—this is the liberation of the Guide.
Born from the ocean of all Buddhas of the three periods of time through the seeds of skillful means and vows,
practicing diligently throughout all kalpas and lands— this is the liberation of Samantabhadra.

Universally entering the gates of all dharma-realms, They see entirely the oceans of lands in the ten directions, And also behold the kalpas of formation and destruction therein; This is the realm of non-duality.

Within every atom of the oceans of lands in the ten directions, one sees the Buddhas sitting beneath the Bodhi tree, attaining equal and perfect enlightenment to transform all living beings; this is the realm of unimpeded vision.
For immeasurable oceans of great eons, you have drawn near to and served spiritual friends;
for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, you have sought the True Dharma, and having heard it, you remember it without any forgetfulness.
The vast realm of Vairocana is boundless, immeasurable, and inconceivable;
receiving the Buddha’s power, I shall explain it for you, so that your profound mind may become utterly pure.

“Good son! In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, there was an ocean of worlds named Vairocana-ocean-gold-maṇi-mountain. Within that ocean of worlds, a Buddha appeared, named Universal Illumination of the Dharma-realm Wisdom Mountain Tranquil Majestic Virtue King.”

"Good son! When that Buddha was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he was able to universally purify that ocean of worlds. Within that ocean of worlds, there were world-systems as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field; each world-system contained world-systems as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field; each world contained eons as numerous as the atoms within a world; and in each eon, immeasurable Tathāgatas appeared in the world. Each Tathāgata preached as many sūtras as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, and in each sūtra, they bestowed predictions of enlightenment upon as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a buddha-field. They manifested various supernatural powers of the Buddhas, taught various dharmas for taming sentient beings, turned the various wheels of the vehicles, and delivered oceans of immeasurable sentient beings."
"Good son! Within that ocean of world-systems called Vairocana-Ocean-True-Gold-Maṇi-Mountain, there is a world-system lineage named Universal Gate Manifesting Adorned Banner.

Within this world-system lineage, there is a world named All-Jeweled-Colored Auspicious Universal Radiance, which has as its substance the maṇi-kings that manifest the images of all transformation Buddhas, and whose shape is like a celestial city."

It was adorned with the king of mani-jewels manifesting the bodhimanda of all Tathāgatas, and it rested upon an ocean of all kinds of precious kusuma flowers, where the pure and the impure were intermingled.
In this world-system, there are four continents as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru. Among them, one four-continent system stands at the center, named Banner of All Jewel Mountains.
Each of its four continents is immeasurable hundreds of thousands of yojanas in length and breadth, and each contains ten thousand great cities.

Within Jambudvīpa, there is a royal capital named Cloud-Lamp Adorned with Wondrous Jewel Śāla Trees, surrounded by a retinue of ten thousand great cities. The lifespan of the people in Jambudvīpa is ten thousand years.

At that time, there was a wheel-turning monarch named Sarvadharmaparipūrṇaratnacchatramahāsiṃhanādanirghoṣa. This king possessed five hundred ministers, sixty thousand court ladies, and seven hundred princes; these princes were handsome and dignified in appearance, courageous, robust, and fierce, and they possessed great majestic power.
At that time, the majesty and virtue of that king pervaded all of Jambudvīpa, and he had no enemies. Then, as the kalpa of that world was nearing its end, the five turbidities arose:

the lifespan of all people became short, their wealth and resources were meager, and their physical appearance was coarse and ugly. In their walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, they experienced much suffering and little joy; they did not cultivate the ten wholesome paths of action but devoted themselves exclusively to evil deeds. They quarreled and contended with one another, vying to overthrow and seize each other's possessions. They practiced deception and fraudulence, using flowery and ornate speech to sow discord among others, uttering harsh and wicked words, envying the prosperity and excellence of others, and greedily seeking what was unlawful, plunging deeply into the dense forest and vast wilderness of false nets.

Due to these causes and conditions, wind and rain do not come at their proper times; the crops do not ripen, and medicinal herbs, flowers, gardens, groves, grasses, and trees all wither away. Food and clothing become scarce, and pestilential diseases abound. People flee in all four directions, finding no one to rely upon, until they all come together to surround the great capital city; numbering in the measureless, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis, they encircle it on all sides, crying out in loud voices.

Some raised both hands; some joined their palms; some struck their heads against the ground; some raised their hands to beat their chests; some knelt and wailed aloud; some leaped up and shouted loudly. Their hair was disheveled and matted; their garments were tattered and foul; their skin was cracked and withered; and their faces were devoid of luster.
“Those sentient beings, with various forms and appearances, producing various sounds, using various modes of speech, and engaging in various discourses, addressed the king, saying:
‘Great King!’”

"Great King! We are now poor, destitute, and exposed; we suffer from hunger, thirst, cold, and heat; we are emaciated by disease and oppressed by manifold sufferings. Various calamities press upon our bodies and minds; our lives will not last much longer. Without refuge or protection, with no one to whom we may appeal, we are as if in prison, with the signs of death appearing before us."

We have now come to take refuge in the Great King. Observing the Great King’s benevolence and wisdom, we conceive toward him the thought of finding peace and happiness, the thought of being cherished, the thought of being loved and respected, the thought of gaining our very lives, the thought of being accepted, the thought of finding a treasury of jewels, the thought of encountering a bridge or ford, the thought of meeting a path, the thought of finding a boat or raft, the thought of seeing a jewel island, the thought of acquiring wealth and profit, the thought of ascending to a celestial palace, the thought of being parted from enemies, and the thought of extinguishing all sufferings.

At that time, having heard these words, the Great King attained a million *asaṃkhyeya* gates of great compassion; with single-minded reflection and intentional observation, he uttered ten kinds of words of great compassion.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
"Alas! [the first].

Sentient beings have fallen into the bottomless, deep pit of birth and death; how shall I swiftly deliver and rescue them, enabling them to emerge and dwell securely in the ground of the Tathāgata’s all-encompassing wisdom?
Alas! Sentient beings are oppressed in body and mind by various afflictions; how shall I provide them with protection and establish them in the various paths of wholesome action?
How lamentable!

Sentient beings are constantly terrified by the various sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death; how shall I act as their refuge, enabling them to leave behind all fetters and attachments, and forever attain peace and security in both body and mind?
How lamentable!

Sentient beings are constantly oppressed and harmed in their bodies by the various terrors of the world; how shall I provide them with protection and deliverance, enabling them to escape all calamities and abide securely upon the path of the Tathāgata’s omniscience?

Alas! Sentient beings lack the eye of wisdom and are constantly shrouded by the doubts of the view of a self; how shall I employ skillful means to enable them to resolve their doubts and clear away the cataracts of their views?

Alas! Sentient beings are constantly deluded by the darkness of ignorance and remain far removed from wholesome dharmas. How shall I act as a torch of wisdom for them, illuminating their nescience so that they may behold the city of all-knowledge and attain ultimate liberation?

Alas! Sentient beings are constantly afflicted by various forms of stinginess, envy, flattery, and deception, which turbidly disturb their minds. How shall I enlighten them so that they may realize the pure Dharmakāya?

Alas! Sentient beings have for a long time drifted and drowned in the great ocean of birth and death within all worlds; how shall I act as their boat and raft to ferry them across universally, so that they may enter the ocean of all-knowledge?

Alas! The faculties of sentient beings are stubborn and rigid; they have distanced themselves from the Unsurpassed Great Teacher who can subdue them, and there is no one else in all the worlds capable of taming them. How shall I act as their subduer to cause them to bring all roots of goodness to maturity and become endowed with the great majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata?
How lamentable!

Sentient beings are like those who are blind and sightless; they do not see the true path and instead follow deviant tracks. How shall I open their eye of wisdom and act as their guide, enabling them to enter the gateway of all-knowledge?

At that time, having given rise to these ten kinds of great compassionate minds and having spoken these words, the Great King immediately beat the drum and issued a proclamation amidst the great assembly in the royal capital, so that all might hear and know:
"I now universally bestow upon all sentient beings; whatever they may require, I shall cause them all to be fully satisfied."

Immediately, he issued a decree throughout the great and small cities within Jambudvīpa, as well as all the villages and hamlets, commanding them to open their treasuries and bring forth all kinds of goods to be placed at the crossroads.
That is to say:

gold, silver, lapis lazuli, mani-jewels, and other precious gems; clothing, food and drink, flowers, incense, garlands, parasols, ointments, powdered incense, and various kinds of necklaces; palaces, houses, couches, bedding, and all manner of requisites—none were lacking.

They erected great luminous mani-jewel banners, whose light touched their bodies, making them entirely peaceful and secure, extinguishing darkness and opening up illumination; whatever they desired according to their hearts was completely fulfilled.

Furthermore, manifesting various physical forms according to the needs of beings, he serves, makes offerings to, and honors all sentient beings; he also bestows medicinal decoctions for the causes of illness and the necessities for sustaining life.

He provides various precious vessels filled with diverse treasures—namely, vajra-vessels filled with various fragrant jewels, and incense-vessels filled with various garments and exquisite mani-jewels. Adorned and magnificently decorated, there are palanquins, carriages, and vehicles, as well as necklaces of many jewels, jeweled canopies, and jeweled nets draped all around. He erects various tall and sublime banners; all such articles of daily life are opened from his treasuries and bestowed as gifts.

Furthermore, they are able to give away all villages, camps, cities, towns, mountains, marshes, forests, and thickets; as well as their wives, children, and retinues; and even their royal throne, head, eyes, ears, nose, lips, tongue, teeth, gums, hands, feet, skin, flesh, heart, kidneys, liver, lungs, large and small intestines, fat, marrow, tendons, veins, and every limb and member—giving up everything internal and external without exception.
"At that time, at the eastern gate of the city of Ratnavicitra-sāla-vyūha-pradīpa-rāja, named Maṇi-parvata-tejas, there was a site for almsgiving outside the gate.
Its ground was vast, pure, and level, free from pits, thorns, and gravel; everything there was made of exquisite [jewels]."
It was composed of jewels, strewn with various precious flowers, and incense of exquisite fragrance was being burned.
It was adorned and embellished by countless king-jewels of mani-gems; precious lamps were lit, radiating light everywhere.
Clouds of auspicious fragrant smoke from the jewel-flames filled the void, and immeasurable jewel-trees stood in successive rows, exquisitely divided.
Spread throughout and interspersed with various celestial and human palaces and towers, all magnificently adorned;
featuring diverse banners and streamers, and various silk canopies that constantly emit radiance;
covered above by nets of precious kusuma flowers and nets of every kind of king of incense.
The precious bells sway gently, producing wondrous sounds; countless hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of musical instruments constantly emit sublime tones.
All such things are adorned with exquisite jewels and are entirely accomplished as the fruit of the pure karma of bodhisattvas.

Within that assembly, lion thrones were set forth, with ground made of ten kinds of exquisite jewels. Ten-jeweled railings emitted great radiance, and ten kinds of jewel trees with lush, spreading branches surrounded them on all sides; they were magnificent in every way, subtle and firm. Beneath them were adamantine jewel wheels, supported and held up together by images of nāgas and devas made of all kinds of jewels. They were adorned with various precious objects, and within the latticed canopies, the marks of his virtuous qualities were inscribed, decorated with an intermingling of various colors.

All manner of jewel banners and jewel pennants were arranged in rows everywhere, while nets of various jewels, nets of maṇi jewels, nets of various jewel flowers, and nets of great maṇi kings covered them from above.

Immeasurable precious incenses constantly emit clouds of fragrance, and various precious garments are distributed everywhere. Hundreds of thousands of kinds of music surpass those of the devas, perpetually playing beautiful sounds that delight the human heart.

Furthermore, precious canopies are spread above, constantly emitting immeasurable jewel-flame radiance like Jambūnada gold—blazing and pure—with hanging flower-garlands and countless mani-jewel kings arranged in rows all around.
Various multicolored mani-jewel bells constantly emitted sublime sounds, exhorting all sentient beings to practice the ten virtuous deeds.

At that time, the King of Sublime Sound Who Roars the Great Lion’s Roar, Master of the Jewel Parasol of All Dharmas, sat upon his lion throne; he was endowed with exquisite color, possessed of upright features and perfect marks, most supremely pure, and peerless in the world.

He wore a crown made of Vairocana-maṇi-ratna-kings; his body was like that of Nārāyaṇa, indestructible and with every limb perfectly complete. Born into a royal lineage of universal goodness and virtue, he attained mastery over both wealth and the Dharma. Possessing unimpeded eloquence and clear, penetrating wisdom, he governed the kingdom with righteousness such that no one disobeyed his commands. All sentient beings praised that king for his immeasurable and boundless, most excellent merits; his radiance was so blazing and intense that it surpassed even Śakra, Lord of Devas, and those who beheld him never grew weary of the sight.
Constantly appearing in the air was a great wheel-canopy, with hundreds of thousands of *maṇi* jewel-treasuries serving as its spokes.

Adorned with countless jewel-flames and the majestic light of auspicious splendor, it was covered above by Jāmbūnada gold emitting pure radiance. Decorated with golden nets of various jewel-colors, pearl necklaces hung down all around, and jeweled cords suspended clusters of bells; these were exquisitely fashioned from various gems, constantly emitting wondrous sounds that surpassed all celestial music, awakening the world and proclaiming virtuous conduct.
Furthermore, there were exquisite fans woven from precious threads, fanned by fragrant breezes, which further magnified its majestic power.

"At that time, within this Jambudvīpa, immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of sentient beings—from various lands, various clans, various retinues, various appearances, various garments, various languages, various mental dispositions, and various inclinations—each seeking various treasures, various means of livelihood, and various enjoyments, all came together to this assembly to observe that king."

With various modes of speech, various expositions, various forms of eloquence, and various names and phrases, they all extolled this king as a man of great wisdom, a Sumeru of merit, a full white moon of supreme virtue, and a self-mastery master free from hindrance, who dwells in the vows of a bodhisattva and practices vast generosity.

At that time, seeing those who had gathered there to beg from him, the King gave rise to a heart of love and respect; he gave rise to a heart of compassion; he gave rise to a heart of joy; he gave rise to a heart of reverence; he gave rise to a vast heart; he gave rise to a heart regarding them as virtuous friends; he gave rise to a continuous heart; he gave rise to a heart of diligence; he gave rise to a heart of non-retrogression; he gave rise to a heart of relinquishment and giving; he gave rise to a pervasive heart; he gave rise to a heart of equanimity; he gave rise to a pure heart; he gave rise to a heart of accomplishment; he gave rise to a swift heart; and he gave rise to a heart that beholds various spiritual benefactors.

"Good son! At that time, when the king saw those beggars, his heart was filled with great joy; for even the pleasure experienced by a Wheel-Turning Sage King throughout the entirety of boundless eons could not equal it."

In this way, even the pleasures experienced by the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the King of the Yāma Heaven, and the King of the Tuṣita Heaven throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas cannot compare to it. Nor can the pleasures experienced by the King of Sunirmita Heaven over incalculable kalpas; nor the pleasures of sovereignty experienced by the King of Vaśavartin Heaven over immeasurable kalpas; nor the Brahma-pleasures experienced by the Great Brahma King over boundless kalpas; nor the celestial pleasures experienced by the King of Ābhāsvara Heaven over inconceivable kalpas; nor the celestial pleasures experienced by the King of Śubhakṛtsna Heaven over inexhaustible kalpas; nor even the bliss of dwelling in tranquility experienced by the Kings of the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens over unspeakable kalpas can equal it.

For example, suppose there is a person who is kind, compassionate, filial, and fraternal, who, having encountered the calamities of the world, has lost all their parents, brothers, sisters, wife, children, and both internal and external kinsmen. Suddenly, amidst the wilderness and on the roads, they encounter one another; they gaze upon, attend to, and embrace each other, their affection never reaching satiety.

At that time, when the great king saw the one who had come to beg, a heart of love and respect arose within him; he was filled with joy and exultation, and his sense of auspicious celebration was likewise so. Good son!

At that time, by virtue of a spiritual friend, the king’s aspiration for the Buddha’s bodhi increased; his faculties were perfected, his faith became pure, and his joy was fulfilled in an inconceivable manner.
Why is this? Because these great bodhisattvas diligently cultivate all practices and seek omniscience;
their resolve to benefit all sentient beings is free from weariness, and they vow to provide all sentient beings with an abundance of clothing, food, and drink.
May I attain the immeasurable, wondrous bliss of Bodhi; may I abandon all unwholesome states of mind; may I always aspire to accumulate all roots of goodness;
may I always aspire to rescue and protect all sentient beings; may I always delight in observing the path to Sarvajñā;
may I always delight in practicing the dharmas of omniscience, so as to bring fulfillment to all sentient beings.

As for their aspiration: having entered the great ocean of the merits of all Buddhas, shattered the mountains of all demonic activities and delusive obstacles, followed and upheld all Buddha-teachings, and traversed the unobstructed path of omniscience, they are able to enter deeply into the stream of omniscience;
the stream of all dharmas is ever present before them, and their great vows are... [unfailing].
Having reached the ultimate, you are a great man who abides in the dharma of a great being; you have accumulated the treasury of all universal gates of goodness.
You vow to abandon all hearts of attachment and remain unstained by any worldly realms.
Knowing that the nature of all phenomena is like space, you regard all those who come to beg as if they were your only son.
One should conceive of them as one's own parents, as a field of merit, as a virtuous friend,
as something difficult to encounter, as a source of benefit and grace, as a protector, as steadfast, as a guide, and as a Tathāgata;
without discriminating according to location, without selecting by lineage, and without choosing by physical appearance.
As beings arrive, he accords with their desires;

according to their locations and according to their countries and towns, he grants them whatever they seek and whatever they delight in. With a mind of great compassion that is impartial and unimpeded, and with the light of great equanimity illuminating all, he acts in accordance with the minds of sentient beings so that they lack for nothing.

To those seeking food and drink, he gave food and drink; to those seeking clothing, he gave clothing; to those seeking incense and flowers, he gave incense and flowers; to those seeking garlands and parasols, he gave garlands and parasols. Likewise, to those who sought banners and streamers, necklaces, palaces, gardens, elephants and horses, carriages, couches and seats, bedding and mats, gold, silver, *maṇi* jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, jade, conch shells, and all manner of precious treasures and storehouses—as well as his kinsmen, female attendants, queens and concubines, cities, villages, groves, and dwellings—he gave them all in this same way, universally bestowing them upon sentient beings.
At that time, there was a daughter of a householder in this assembly named Ratnaprabhā, who was surrounded by a retinue of sixty young maidens.

She was exceptionally beautiful and lovely, a sight for all to behold; her skin was golden, her eyes and hair were deep blue, and she was perfect in every way, endowed with all auspicious marks. Her body emitted a sublime fragrance, her voice was like the Brahma-sound, and she was adorned with exquisite, precious garments.

Constantly harboring a sense of shame and remorse, their right mindfulness remains undisturbed; possessing great wisdom, they are serene and composed in all movements and actions, fully endowed with dignified decorum. They revere their teachers and elders, being most excellent and pure, with minds free from negligence. Always mindful of practicing profound and wondrous conduct, they remember and do not forget the teachings they have heard. The roots of goodness from past lives moisten their hearts, such that no corresponding wondrous fruits fail to be accomplished. Pure and vast as space, they bring peace equally to all sentient beings, constantly beholding all Buddhas and seeking omniscience throughout the entirety of all realms without exception.
Not far from the king, he joined his palms in prostration and, with a heart of reverence, thought thus:
"I have gained a great benefit!
I have gained a great benefit!"
"I have now been able to see a great spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra); one who is most difficult to encounter, I have now encountered.

At that time, the woman conceived the thought of the King as her Great Teacher, the thought of him as the most supreme spiritual friend, the thought of his compassion, and the thought of his ability to provide protection. Her mind became upright and supremely pure; she gave rise to a heart of vast joy, immediately untied the necklace she wore upon herself, and presented it to the King, making this aspiration:

"Now this Great King is able to provide protection, benefit, and illumination for all immeasurable, boundless, masterless, and supportless sentient beings shrouded in ignorance, acting as their place of reliance. I pray that in the future I may likewise be so; may I fully achieve, in the future, the Dharma known by this Great King, the vehicle he carries, the path he cultivates, the physical marks he possesses, and the assemblies he gathers—all boundless and inexhaustible, invincible and indestructible."
"Wherever that Great King may be born, may I always be born following him.
*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*, Fascicle Twenty-three;
*The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*, Fascicle Twenty-four.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīr by Imperial Decree.
Chapter on Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation through the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra.
"At that time, the Great King, knowing that this young girl had conceived such a mind and made such a vow, observed her disposition and addressed her, saying:"
“O maiden! You should know that whatever you desire, I shall give it all to you.

I now relinquish everything I possess so that all sentient beings may attain universal fulfillment; with a mind of universal equality and free from discrimination, take as much as you wish according to your vows.”
At that time, the girl Ratnaprabhā, her mind purified by faith and filled with great joy, swiftly increased all her roots of goodness and praised the king with these sublime verses:

"In the past, when this great city of Śrāvastī had not yet seen the appearance of a majestic and holy king, all things therein were utterly unfit for use; it was as terrifying as the abode of hungry ghosts."
All sentient beings kill and harm one another; they steal, engage in lustful excess, and their natures are difficult to tame.
They speak with falsehood and unreality, harsh and evil words, as well as defiled, divisive, and meaningless speech.
Constantly delighting in greedily seizing the wealth and possessions of others, always harboring a mind of hatred and poisonous malice,
and relying on unwholesome conduct based on false views— from this, at the end of life, one falls into the evil realms.

These various classes of beings who act contrary to the Dharma, deluded by the darkness of ignorance, destroy the True Dharma and give rise to false views; because of this, the devas and nāgas do not send down rain.
Many years have passed without rain; the sprouts and stalks of the hundred grains all fail to grow.
Trees, medicinal herbs, and grasses are all withered and parched, and even the large and small springs and streams have run dry.
In days of yore, before Your Majesty had appeared, the rivers, ponds, and wells were all parched dry;
all the gardens and groves lay utterly desolate, with bleached bones strewn about like a wilderness.
Now that the Great King occupies the precious throne, his bounty extends to all living beings;
like thick clouds and nourishing rain, it covers the eight directions, filling the great earth and every land beneath it.
The Great King has arisen as the lord of the world; he has quelled all bandits and thieves and brought an end to fraud and deceit.
All prisons are now entirely empty, and no one who is solitary or destitute suffers from grief or fear.
In times past, the various classes of beings in this world delighted in killing one another and giving rise to enmity;
they devoured flesh and blood with unrestrained insatiability. Now, they all regard one another with hearts of loving-kindness.
In times past, all sentient beings within the realm were impoverished and naked, lacking clothing;
emaciated by hunger and thirst like hungry ghosts, they endured the suffering of cold with only grass to shield their bodies.
Now that the Great King has appeared in this world, Rice, grain, sweet fruits, and other delicacies grow spontaneously;
The Kalpavṛkṣa trees yield exquisite garments from their treasuries, And all men and women are adorned with finery.
In former times, they sought much and acted contrary to the Dharma, vying for slight profits and seizing one another’s goods;
now, all necessities are abundant and complete, and they dwell in sovereign joy as if in the heavens.
In the past, my deluded mind gave free rein as I committed various evils;
through negligence, I gave rise to excessive greed and defilement, engaging in sexual misconduct with the wives and concubines of others, and even committing various acts of aggression and plunder.
Now, when seeing other women whose features are beautiful and finely adorned, my mind remains ever pure and free from attachment; contented, I am like those in the Tuṣita Heaven.
In times past, the sentient beings of this world spoke falsely, with coarse and evil words, and were full of divisiveness;
they constantly gave rise to perverse thoughts that extinguished the True Dharma, being sycophantic, crooked, impure, and acting according to others' whims.
Now all classes of living beings have completely abandoned coarse and evil speech;
their voices are soft and pleasing to the heart, so that all who hear them find no lack of joy.
Now the Great King proclaims the wondrous sound of the Dharma; all sentient beings who hear it are filled with joy.
With the physical marks of the *kalaviṅka* and the Brahma-voice, no celestial music can equal it.
The supreme parasol upon the Great King’s head is adorned with every kind of exquisite jewel;
its auspicious pole is a treasury of lapis lazuli, covered by a net of various wonderful maṇi-gems.
The golden bells spontaneously produce wondrous sounds; their resonance transcends the world, peerless and matchless.
They proclaim all the teachings of the Buddhas and eliminate the delusions of all sentient beings.

Furthermore, this sound of the bell proclaims extensively: all the Buddhas throughout the oceans of kalpas in every land of the ten directions in the present, together with their retinues of great renown.
Furthermore, the sound of the bell sequentially proclaims all the buddhas and the names of their lands throughout every realm of the ten directions in the past,
as well as the wheels of Dharma they have turned, leaving nothing unexpressed.
From within the bell, the sound of the Wheel of Dharma further emerged;
its resonance pervaded the realm of Jambudvīpa, extensively explaining the various karmas upon which Brahmā, Śakra, and all sentient beings depend, each being distinct.
When humans and devas have heard this sound, each will come to know their own storehouse of karma;
leaving evil and turning toward the good, they will diligently practice and abide securely in the path to the bodhi of all Buddhas.
The king’s father was named Pure Radiance, and the king’s mother was named Lotus Light;
during a time when the five corruptions were rampant, he appeared as a king to govern the world.
At that time there was a vast garden; within the garden were five hundred lotus ponds, each surrounded by one hundred thousand trees, all covered with mani-flower lamps.
Upon the shore of each and every pond, there stands a magnificent hall supported by a thousand pillars;
its railings are fashioned from various precious gems, and the light of crescent-shaped flames constantly shines everywhere.
In that king’s final age, evil dharmas arose; for many years there was a drought with no timely rain.
All the waters of the ponds were completely dried up, and all the grasses and trees withered away.
Seven days before the Great King was to be born, first appeared auspicious and rare signs;
beings gazed upon them and said to one another: "The Savior of the World shall now appear."
At that time, in the middle of the night, the entire great earth shook;
therein was a jewel-lotus pond that emitted a great radiance like the appearance of the sun.
Surrounded by five hundred lotus ponds, filled with water possessing the eight virtues,
its flow extends throughout Jambudvīpa, moistening and refreshing all lands wherever it reaches.
All flowering groves and medicinal herbs, The sprouts, stalks, and crops of the hundred grains,
Along with all their branches, leaves, and fruits— All such things as these flourish in abundance.
The various ditches, pits, and mounds, Even all places high and low—
Throughout the entire land of Jambudvīpa, At this moment, there is not one that is not level.
All thorns and gravel, and all the various impurities found throughout Jambudvīpa— may these all,
within a single thought-moment, be transformed into a ground adorned with manifold jewels.
When sentient beings have seen him at that time, they rejoice together in celebration and offer praise, all saying:
"I have now obtained a great benefit, like a person parched with thirst longing for sweet water."
Then that sovereign, King Prabhāsa, immediately commanded his ministers and their retinues;
with a thousand koṭis of attendants preceding and following him in his ceremonial carriage, he went forth to tour the various gardens.
At that time, within five hundred ponds, there was a lotus pond named Joy;
upon its bank stood a Dharma Hall, where the King and his consort resided.
At that time, King Prabhāsa said to his consort: "I recall that seven nights ago, at midnight, the mountains and earth all shook, and a radiance appeared within this pond."
At that moment, within the Pond of Fragrant Joy, there suddenly sprang forth a precious lotus with a thousand petals;
its radiance ascended to the summit of Mount Sumeru, and its web of clouds shone like a thousand suns.
With the wondrous vajra-jewel as its stem, Jāmbūnada gold as its pedestal,
pure maṇi jewels as its petals, and a treasury of exquisite fragrant light as its filaments.
The Great King was born upon that lotus flower, sitting upright and motionless in the full-lotus posture;
adorned with the marks and signs of radiance, hundreds of thousands of celestial hosts all paid him reverence.

At that time, the former king was filled with great joy; he hurriedly entered the lotus pond to take him up in his own hands, holding him with both palms and presenting him to the Queen, saying: "This is your son; you should rejoice."
Hundreds of thousands of treasure-treasuries gush forth, and all the jewel-trees produce exquisite garments;
the devas vying with one another play subtle and wondrous music, filling the entirety of the realm of empty space.
All sentient beings throughout Jambudvīpa, having turned toward him in full devotion, were filled with joy;
with palms joined, they all spoke these words: "Excellent! The Savior of the World shall now appear!"
At that time, the King’s body emitted a great radiance, Universally illuminating all classes of beings;
In a single thought, he caused the bodily ailments and darkness Throughout the four continents to be entirely extinguished.
Yakṣas, rākṣasas, and piśācas, all venomous insects and various evil beasts—
those who seek to afflict and harm sentient beings— all conceal themselves and hide away.

May all decline, ruin, censure, suffering, and misfortunes, as well as various calamities and afflictions by disease, be entirely eliminated; may the world be peaceful and joyful, and all beings rejoice.
May all classes of sentient beings regard one another as their own parents;
free from all enmity and harm, may they give rise to a heart of loving-kindness, and with single-minded diligence, cultivate all-encompassing wisdom.
Great King, you have closed off all evil realms and opened the path for all devas and humans;
you benefit all suffering sentient beings and manifest and proclaim all-encompassing wisdom.
Now that we have been able to see the Great King, we have universally obtained all manner of wholesome benefits;
those who were without a lord, without a refuge, and without a guide, are all, according to their needs, established in peace and happiness.

At that time, after the maiden Ratnaprabhā had praised the King of Wondrous Sound, the Great Lion’s Roar of the Perfect Jewel Parasol of All Dharmas, with these sublime verses, she circumambulated him countless times, joined her palms in prostration, bowed her body in reverence, and withdrew to stand to one side.
Then, that great king surveyed her thoroughly and addressed the young girl, saying:
"Excellent, young girl!
That you are able to know and believe in the merits of others is truly rare."

Why is this? Because all sentient beings conceal their own faults, proclaim the shortcomings of others, claim to possess virtues themselves, and obscure the roots of goodness in others; they are unable to believe in or recognize the merits of others.

O maiden! You should know that all sentient beings are shrouded by the darkness of ignorance, bound by afflictions, devoid of shame and remorse, ignorant of how to repay kindness, lacking wisdom, with turbid and distracted minds, their natures unclear, originally lacking resolve and strength, and further regressing from their practice.

Such people do not believe or understand; they cannot comprehend the merits of Bodhisattvas and Tathāgatas, nor can they distinguish the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha—the most supreme fields of merit. They do not know the pure Dharma-gates, supernatural powers, or wisdom of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, nor do they contemplate them in accordance with reality.

"O maiden! You now resolutely seek to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; you are able to know such vast and profound merits of a bodhisattva, and you are able to believe in and understand them."
Now that you have been born here in this Jambudvīpa, you have resolved upon a courageous mind and cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva to universally gather in all sentient beings;
thus, your merit shall not be in vain. Just as you have vowed, all such virtues, such power of merit, and such benefits shall be fully realized for you, without exception.

After the King had praised the girl, he took an invaluable jewel-fire-light mani-gem and garments adorned with various exquisite colors, and with his own hands bestowed them upon the maiden Jewel-Light and her retinue, addressing each one individually:
"You maidens, each of you take these and put on these wondrous garments."
Then, the young maidens knelt with both knees upon the ground; with both hands they received and supported [the garment], placing it upon the crown of their heads before finally donning it.
Once they had finished dressing, they circumambulated the king to the right, prostrating themselves with their heads at his feet.
At that time, from within all those precious garments, the light of all the constellations shone forth everywhere. When the people saw this, they all said:
"These women are all exceedingly beautiful, adorned like the constellations in a clear night sky."
At that time, the night goddess said to Sudhana: "Good man,
what do you think?"
At that time, was the King of the Wondrous Sound of the Great Lion’s Roar, Perfect Jewel Canopy of All Dharmas, anyone else?
He was none other than the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana;
and the King of Radiance was King Śuddhodana.
The Lady Padmaprabhā was Queen Māyā; the maiden Ratnaprabhā was none other than myself;

and the sentient beings gathered by that king at that time through the four methods of attraction are precisely all these bodhisattvas assembled here in this great site of enlightenment within the Buddha’s assembly.

They have all attained non-retrogression in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, abiding either in the first Bodhisattva stage, the Stage of Extreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), or the Stage of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), or the Stage of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*), or the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), or the Stage Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*), or the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*), or the Stage of Far-Going (*dūraṅgamā-bhūmi*), or the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*), or the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), or the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*).

Each is fully endowed with various great vows, has accumulated various aids to the Path, cultivated various sublime practices, prepared various adornments, attained various purities, acquired various supernormal powers, traversed various spheres of mastery, and dwells in various liberations. They have come to this assembly from various locations, residing in various palaces of sublime Dharma.
At that time, the Night Goddess Analaṅkārasarvavṛkṣapraphullanasukhasaṃdarśanā, wishing to clarify the meaning of this gate of liberation for the youth Sudhana,

spoke these verses: "O Son of the Buddha, I possess vast eyes, Which can universally observe throughout the ten directions The various and vast oceans of world-systems, And sentient beings wandering through the five destinies."
I also see all the Buddhas of those lands, Each sitting beneath the Bodhi tree of tranquil extinction;
Their spiritual powers pervade the ten directions, As they preach the Dharma to discipline all classes of beings.
O Son of the Buddha, I possess a pure and wondrous ear, Which hears universally all inexhaustible sounds;
I also hear the various Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma, And am able to believe and accept them all with joy.
O Son of the Buddha, I possess the knowledge of others' minds, Which transcends the mental realms of all sentient beings;
Non-dual, unobstructed, and immeasurable, In a single thought-moment, I fully comprehend the ocean of all minds.

O Son of the Buddha, I possess the knowledge of past lives; I am able to know the oceans of kalpas of the past, The births experienced by myself and others— In a single thought-moment, I clearly understand them all.
O Son of the Buddha, in a single thought-moment I know all the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout infinite eons,
as well as the various spiritual powers of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and the multitudes of sentient beings revolving through the five realms of existence.
I also know those World-Honored Ones when they first made the vast vow for bodhi;
I know how they fully practiced the ocean of all conducts until they attained omniscience,
and I also know their stage of consecration where they were endowed with the peerless path to enlightenment.
The skillful means of their teaching are entirely not in vain; I understand them all clearly in a single thought-moment.
I also know the gates of skillful means of those Buddhas, as they turn the Great Dharma Wheel throughout the world.
Regarding the immeasurable merits of Nirvana and the duration for which the Dharma remains, I am able to comprehend them all.
They also know the ocean of various vehicles within the vast teachings tamed by those Buddhas;
they clearly understand all the diverse distinctions manifested throughout every world.
Throughout immeasurable and boundless eons, I have cultivated this liberation door of the light of joy;
now I shall explain its true meaning for you—you should cherish it and diligently practice and study it.

“Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva liberation door called ‘The Universal Radiance of the Treasury for Taming Sentient Beings through the Birth of Vast Joy. As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who attend upon and make offerings to all Tathāgatas, who enter the vast ocean of vows of omniscience, and who fulfill the ocean of vows of all Tathāgatas;
who attain courageous wisdom and, within a single bodhisattva stage, universally enter the ocean of all bodhisattva stages;”
Having attained pure vows, they universally enter the ocean of all bodhisattva practices through a single bodhisattva practice;
having attained the power of mastery, they universally enter the ocean of all bodhisattva doors of liberation through a single bodhisattva door of liberation;

they honor and revere all spiritual friends, increasing their roots of goodness without ever being weary; they serve all Buddhas and bodhisattvas, diligently seeking the Dharma-gates of omniscience, joyfully observing, contemplating with right mindfulness, their minds being resolute and always free from indolence.
They do not cling to any gain, honor, praise, or fame; they are forever free from greedy attachment to worldly necessities.

Like a wish-fulfilling jewel, they satisfy the hearts of sentient beings; their minds always delight in the ground of omniscience as they contemplate the Tathāgata’s powers, fearlessnesses, and unique Buddha-dharmas. Diligently seeking to fulfill all bodhisattva pāramitās, they remain far removed from flattery and illusion, acting exactly as they speak and always speaking the truth. They protect the lineage of the Buddhas, and regarding omniscience, their minds are as immovable as the king of great mountains.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
Son of good family!
Within this assembly of the Tathāgata at this site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Great Power of Vigor and Light of the Vows to Protect All Sentient Beings.
Go to him and ask: how does a bodhisattva teach and transform sentient beings, causing them to set out toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
And how does one adorn and purify all buddha-fields?
How does one serve all Tathāgatas?
How can one cause all Tathāgatas to be entirely delighted?
How can one diligently seek and practice the Buddha-dharma studied by all Bodhisattvas?

Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and, filled with deep longing and affection, took his leave and departed.

At that time, the youth Sudhana went to the place where the Night Goddess Rātridevatā, Sovereign of the Radiance of the Power of Diligence in Upholding the Great Vows for All Sentient Beings, was staying. He saw that Night Goddess seated amidst a great assembly upon a lion throne made of a treasury of *maṇi* jewels, which universally reflected the images of the palaces of all sentient beings and universally manifested the diverse images of the entire dharma-realm.
A net of mani-jewels covers its surface, manifesting bodies that display the reflections of all suns, moons, and stars;

manifesting bodies that appear universally according to the minds of sentient beings so that they may all see them; manifesting bodies that display forms corresponding to the diverse appearances of all sentient beings;
manifesting bodies that are oceans of infinite and vast colors and marks; and manifesting bodies that universally display all manner of characteristics and majesty.
The body of ritual conduct, manifesting everywhere throughout the ten directions as bodies able to respond to all beings;
the body manifesting everywhere to bring all sentient beings to maturity; the body of the Dharma-cloud of vast, swift, and rapid supernatural powers;
the body manifesting a continuous succession of benefiting sentient beings that pervades everywhere; the body constantly roaming through space to provide vast benefit; the body manifesting as one...
The body revered and prostrated to by all Buddhas; the body that manifests the increase of the roots of goodness in all sentient beings;
the body that manifests the upholding of the Buddha-dharma, never forgetting or losing it; the body that manifests the fulfillment of the vast vows of Bodhisattvas;
the body that manifests the universal radiance filling the ten directions; the body that manifests the universal illumination of the lamp of Dharma to extinguish [all darkness].
He manifests a body that dispels the darkness of the world; he manifests a body of profound, stainless wisdom that clearly realizes all phenomena are like illusions;
he manifests a body of the nature of reality (dharmatā) that is far removed from all dust and darkness; he manifests a body that gives birth to the Buddha-dharma and awakens all beings;

he manifests a body that universally illuminates all distinctions with the light of omniscience; he manifests a body that is ultimately free from affliction and defilement; he manifests an indestructible body.
He manifests a body that destroys all conditioned things yet is endowed with firmness; he manifests the Tathāgata’s body of sovereign power, which abides nowhere;
he manifests a body whose essence is non-conceptual and free from defilement; he manifests a body whose nature is fundamentally pure, illuminating all phenomena.

At that time, having seen the night goddess manifest such bodies as numerous as the atoms within those Buddha-fields, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself with single-minded devotion, casting his entire body to the ground;
after a long while, he rose, joined his palms in reverence, gazed up at her, and gave rise to ten kinds of mind toward the spiritual friend.
What are the ten? They are:
regarding spiritual friends with the same mind as one's own, so that they may cause me to be diligent in accomplishing all the factors conducive to the path to omniscience;
One should conceive toward spiritual friends the thought that they are the fruit of one's own karma, so as to cause me to draw near to them and give rise to pure and supreme roots of goodness;
one should conceive toward spiritual friends the thought that they are the adornment of bodhisattva conduct, so as to enable me to swiftly adorn all bodhisattva practices;
one should conceive toward spiritual friends the thought that they are the accomplishment of all Buddha-dharmas, so as to lead me to practice in accordance with the path of all Buddhas.
One should generate toward the spiritual friend a mind capable of producing the most supreme state, so that I may be born within the realm of the Buddha and illuminated by wisdom;
one should generate toward the spiritual friend a mind of renunciation, so that I may practice the renunciant conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
one should generate toward the spiritual friend a mind capable of fulfilling the ocean of merit and wisdom, so that I may accumulate and accomplish the pure dharmas of merit and wisdom.
One should conceive toward spiritual friends a mind of growth, so that my diligence may swiftly increase all-encompassing wisdom;
one should conceive toward spiritual friends a mind capable of fulfilling all roots of goodness, so that my aspirations may be entirely perfected and all sentient beings may give rise to joy;

one should conceive toward spiritual friends a mind capable of accomplishing great benefit, so that I may freely bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings, abide in all bodhisattva dharmas, and achieve the path of all-knowledge.
Having generated this mind, he attained the same practices as that night goddess and as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a buddha-field.
These were: the same mindfulness, because he constantly recollects all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time;
They share the same wisdom, for they discern and resolve the various gateways of the ocean of all dharmas;
they share the same skillful means regarding the goal, for they reveal the sublime wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
they share the same awakening, for through wisdom equal to space, they awaken to all teachings of the three periods of time.
They share the same faculties, for they have accomplished the pure light of bodhisattva wisdom that universally illumines the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings;
they share the same mind, for they are well able to cultivate unimpeded merit to adorn all bodhisattva paths;
they share the same realm, for the light of their wisdom universally illumines the realms traversed by all Tathāgatas.
They share the same teaching, for they attain omniscience and illuminate all aspects of the ocean of teachings;
they share the same meaning, for they are able to awaken to the self-nature of all phenomena through wisdom;
they share the same abiding in the Dharma, for they penetrate deeply into the ocean of all dharma-realms.
They are identical in valor, for they attain the uncommon dharmas that crush and destroy all mountains of obstacles;
they are identical in form-body, for they manifest various marks and signs according to the minds of sentient beings;
they are identical in the powers, for they diligently seek to accomplish all-knowledge power without ever regressing.
They share the same fearlessness, for their minds are pure like space, free from all obstructions;
they share the same vigor, for they practice the bodhisattva path through immeasurable eons without weariness;
they share the same eloquence, for they have attained the universally radiant wisdom that is unobstructed regarding all phenomena.
They are identical in equanimity, for their bodily marks are pure and no one in any world can surpass them;
they are identical in kind words, for whatever they speak causes all sentient beings to rejoice;
they are identical in sublime voices, for they can roar the lion’s roar, universally expounding the ocean of all Dharma-gates.
They share the same full sound, for they cause all sentient beings to understand according to their respective kinds through their perfect voice;
they share the same pure virtue, for they accord with and cultivate all the pure merits of the Tathāgatas;
they share the same pure karma, for they accomplish all the pure wholesome karmas of all Bodhisattvas.
They share the same stage of wisdom, receiving the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Buddhas for the sake of sentient beings;
they share the same pure conduct (*brahmacarya*), dwelling securely in the realm of wisdom practiced by all Tathāgatas;
they share the same great compassion, universally covering the ocean of sentient beings in all lands in every thought-moment.
They share the same great compassion, for they raise the great cloud of Dharma to universally shower the rain of Dharma and moisten all sentient beings;
they share the same physical karma, for through skillful means they teach and transform sentient beings to bring them to maturity;
they share the same verbal karma, for with voices that accord with the various classes of beings they expound all dharma-gates.
They share the same karma, for they universally gather all sentient beings and establish them within the realm of omniscience;
they share the same adornment, for they purely adorn all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions;
they share the same proximity, for they behold the appearance of all Buddhas in the world and draw near to them all.
They share the same exhortation, beseeching all Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings;
they share the same offering, constantly delighting in making offerings to and serving all Tathāgatas;
they share the same teaching and transformation, taming and bringing to maturity all sentient beings throughout the world.
