They are identical in radiance, for they are able to universally and sovereignly illumine all dharma-gates;
they are identical in samādhi, for they universally know the minds of sentient beings in all worlds throughout the ten directions;
they are identical in pervasiveness, for by the power of their sovereignty, they cultivate all practices throughout all lands.
They share the same dwelling place, because they abide in the ocean of the spiritual powers of all bodhisattvas;
they share the same retinue, because they dwell together with all bodhisattvas;
they share the same entry, because they universally enter the most subtle locations within worlds.
They share the same contemplation, for they universally know all vast Buddha-fields;
they go together, for they follow along to enter all oceans of Buddha-fields;
they share the same skillful means, for they are able to manifest themselves so as to pervade all Buddha-fields.
They are identical in their supreme transcendence, for there is nothing equal to them throughout all Buddha-fields;
they are identical in their non-retrogression, for they universally enter the ten directions with impartial majesty and power, free from obstruction;
they are identical in their destruction of darkness, for they have attained the universal radiance of the wisdom of all Buddhas who have realized enlightenment.
They are identical in the patience of non-arising, for they enter the ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas without attachment;
they are identical in universal pervasiveness, for they serve and make offerings to the Tathāgatas of unspeakably many lands;
they are identical in the realization of wisdom, for they accord with and thoroughly understand the ocean of all dharma-gates in constant succession.
They share the same practice, because they diligently seek and accord with all dharma-gates before them;
they share the same aspiration, because they universally and diligently seek the pure dharmas with profound longing;
they share the same purity, because they adorn their body, speech, and mind by accumulating the merits of the Buddhas.
They share the same sublime intention, for they possess the wisdom of correct discernment regarding all phenomena and are thus clearly enlightened;
they share the same diligence, for they zealously seek to accomplish all the roots of goodness of all Tathāgatas;
they share the same pure conduct, for they fulfill and perfect all the practices undertaken by Bodhisattvas.
They are identical in non-obstruction, for they awaken to and understand that all phenomena are devoid of marks;
they are identical in skillfulness, for they possess mastery of wisdom regarding all the teachings of the Tathāgata;
they are identical in accordance with aspiration, for they manifest realms according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings.
They share the same skillful means, for they have skillfully practiced all dharma-gates that ought to be cultivated;
they share the same protective mindfulness, for they have attained the protection and mindfulness of the sovereign power of all Buddhas;
they share the same entry into the stages, for they have attained entry into the stages wherein all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas abide.
They share the same dwelling, for they abide securely in the stage realized by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
they share the same prediction, for they are universally granted predictions by all Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
they share the same samādhi, for in a single thought-moment they universally enter the ocean of all samādhis.
They are identical in their establishment, for they manifest the various deeds of all Buddhas within a single moment;
they are identical in right mindfulness, for their right mindfulness accords with the gateways to the realm of all Tathāgatas;
they are identical in their practice, for throughout kalpas as numerous as those yet to come, they courageously and diligently cultivate all bodhisattva practices.
They share the same pure faith, because they swiftly love, revere, and take supreme delight in the immeasurable wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
they share the same relinquishment, because they eliminate all obstacles;
they share the same non-retrogression, because their wisdom is equal to the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
They share the same birth, for they manifest to bring all sentient beings to maturity;
they share the same abode, for they dwell securely in the skillful means of the Tathāgata’s omniscience;
they share the same realm, for they have attained mastery over the realm of the profound nature of phenomena.
They are identical in being without reliance, for they have forever extinguished the mind that serves as the basis for all attachment to existence;
they are identical in preaching the Dharma, for they have already deeply entered the equalizing wisdom of various dharma-gates;
they are identical in diligent cultivation, for within their own bodies they uphold the Buddha-dharma and are protected by its inherent majestic virtue.
They share the same supernormal powers, for they awaken sentient beings and cause them to cultivate all bodhisattva practices;
they share the same non-action, for they move unshakably and penetrate deeply into all oceans of lands throughout the ten directions;
they share the same spiritual power, for in a single thought-moment they travel everywhere through all oceans of worlds in the ten directions.
They are identical in their dhāraṇīs, for they have attained the universally illuminating gateway to the ocean of all dhāraṇīs;
they are identical in their secrets, for they thoroughly understand the wondrous dharma-gateways within all sūtras;
they are identical in their profundity, for they realize that all phenomena are free from characteristics and pure like space.
They are identical in radiance, for they emit great light that universally illumines all worlds throughout the ten directions;
they are identical in the light of wisdom, for they universally illuminate and reveal the essential nature of the minds of all sentient beings;

they are identical in their power to cause tremors, for they manifest supernatural powers and sovereign majesty for the sake of all sentient beings, universally shaking all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
They are identical in being non-futile, for they cause the minds of all sentient beings—who see, hear, or remember them in various places—to be entirely tamed;
they are identical in transcendence, for they universally fulfill the ocean of great vows of all bodhisattvas and bring to fruition the Tathāgata’s wisdom of the ten powers;
they are identical in joyful delight, for they reveal the teachings according to the inclinations of sentient beings' minds to bring them joy.

At that time, the youth Sudhana universally observed the Night Goddess Sovereign of the Radiance of the Power of Diligence in the Great Vow to Protect All Sentient Beings; he gave rise to those ten kinds of utterly pure minds and attained these practices shared by Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.
Having attained this practice, his mind became increasingly pure, and he gave rise to immeasurable and boundless joy toward the spiritual friend.
Baring his right shoulder, he prostrated at his feet, joined his palms in reverence, gazed up at him with single-minded devotion, and praised him in verse:
“I have generated a firm and sovereign resolve, Aiming to seek the unsurpassed Bodhi of the Buddha.”
Now, toward this noble spiritual friend, I give rise to a mind that perceives them as no different from myself.
Having encountered this virtuous friend, I shall gather all inexhaustible pure dharmas,
eliminate every stain of sin, and achieve the fruit of pure enlightenment.
Because I have encountered spiritual friends, I shall universally adorn my mind with merit;
throughout all lands for as many eons as remain until the end of the future, I will diligently cultivate the path that benefits sentient beings.
I call to mind the noble ones, my spiritual friends, who have gathered me in, benefited me, and brought me to fulfillment;
for the sake of gathering me, they have fully revealed the most excellent, peaceful, and true Dharma.
He closes off the perilous and evil realms, And reveals the pure and wondrous paths of humans and devas;
He also demonstrates to all Tathāgatas The path of untaught omniscience that they have realized.
The Noble One is rare and without peer; he is the Buddha’s most supreme treasury of merit.
Stainless and immeasurable like space, he brings forth the pure bliss of omniscience.
The Noble One’s ocean of merit is like space; that which I now behold is without limit.
In every moment of thought, he is able to bring forth all-pure roots of goodness and omniscience.
O Benevolent One, you now fulfill my perfections (pāramitā) and increase my inconceivable merit;
you cause me to don the silken crown of the Buddha’s sublime Dharma and lengthen my pure virtues.
I call to mind the noble ones, my spiritual friends, Who cause me to fulfill the wisdom of all Buddhas;
I now vow to rely upon them constantly, So that I may swiftly accomplish all pure qualities.
Because I have benefited from virtuous friends, I am fully endowed with all merits;
with joy, I universally teach and proclaim omniscience for the sake of all sentient beings.
You, O Benevolent One, now act as my teacher and model, Causing me to practice the unsurpassed Dharma;
Throughout countless billions of kalpas, I shall be unable to repay even a small portion of my teacher’s kindness and virtue.
At that time, having praised him with verses, Sudhana said:
"O Great Sage!
Regarding the inconceivable realm of the Bodhisattva that you have just manifested, I pray that you will explain this door of liberation for me; what is its name?"
"How long has it been since you first resolved to attain enlightenment?
How much longer will it be before you realize unexcelled, complete, and perfect awakening?
The night goddess replied:
“Good son! This gate of liberation is named ‘Universally Transforming Sentient Beings to Cause Them to Produce Roots of Goodness.

Because I have attained this gate of liberation, I have realized that the self-nature of all phenomena is equal; I have entered into the true nature of all phenomena and realized the dharma of non-reliance. Having abandoned the world, I fully know the distinctions between the characteristics of all phenomena; yet, while I am able to penetrate the fact that the natures of blue, yellow, red, and white are all unreal and without distinction, I constantly manifest immeasurable and innumerable pure physical bodies.”
That is to say: various physical bodies, non-unitary physical bodies, boundless physical bodies, pure physical bodies, physically adorned with all ornaments,
universally visible physical bodies, and physical bodies whose forms and characteristics are equal to those of all sentient beings.
The body that universally manifests before all sentient beings; the body whose radiance shines everywhere;
the body that all delight in beholding; the body that one never tires of seeing; the body with pure major and minor marks;
the body of pure light shining everywhere, free from all evils; and the body that powerfully and courageously manifests equality.
A body that is profound and difficult to attain in all worlds; a body that no one in all worlds can outshine or obscure;
a body that is inexhaustibly praised by all sentient beings; a body that contemplates various adornments in every thought-moment;
a body that manifests clouds of various forms and images; a body that appears in...
The form-body of various shapes and colors; the form-body that universally manifests immeasurable spiritual powers;
the form-body that universally radiates all manner of exquisite light; the form-body of all pure and wondrous adornments; the form-body that accords with and brings all sentient beings to maturity;
the form-body that appears before them to subdue them according to their inclinations and joys; and the form-body that...
The form-body that accomplishes the roots of goodness for those to be saved; the form-body that manifests unobstructed, universal radiance;
the form-body of vast light, pure and free from turbidity or defilement; the form-body of lovely and upright majesty that increases and is indestructible;
the form-body fully adorned, pure, and firm; and the inconceivable [form-body] revealed through skillful means.
The body of subtle and wondrous radiant color resulting from deliberation on the Dharma; the body whose color cannot be eclipsed by anything;
the body that can eclipse all other colors; the body free from all obscurations of darkness; the body capable of destroying all darkness;
the body that universally gathers all pure and white dharmas; and the body of a great ocean of merit endowed with sovereign power.
The physical body born from causes of past reverence and respect; the physical body arising from a mind as pure as space;
the physical body of supreme vastness surpassing exquisite jewels;
the physical body of an inexhaustible ocean of great merit; and the physical body of a universally manifesting ocean of great radiance.
The body of form that is without dependence and without distinction, equal toward all worlds; the body of form that pervades all worlds throughout the ten directions without obstruction;
the body of form that manifests oceans of various appearances in unspeakably unspeakable oceans of lands in every thought-moment;
and which increases the various hearts of joy in all sentient beings.
The form-body that gathers in the ocean of all sentient beings; the form-body that can, from within each and every pore, emit the lion’s roar to proclaim the ocean of the merits of all Buddhas;

the form-body that can purify the ocean of the profound faith and understanding of the mental natures of all sentient beings; and the form-body that definitively understands the meaning of all phenomena without obstruction.
The body that severs the net of doubt; the body that universally illuminates with various nets of light free from mental obstructions;
the body of pure radiance equal in measure to space; the body that emits the pure radiance of vast sovereign maṇi jewels;
the body that manifests the stainless reflections of the dharma-realm; and the body to which nothing in the world can be compared.
...the physical body adorned with various distinctions of wondrous marks; the physical body that universally illumines the ten directions;
the physical body that manifests at all times in accordance with sentient beings without ever ceasing; the physical body that gives rise to tranquility and subdues all sentient beings;
the physical body that is well able to eliminate all afflictions; all...
The form-body that is a field of merit for the virtues of sentient beings; the form-body capable of purifying all teachings;
the form-body seen by all sentient beings as never being in vain; the form-body manifesting the great wisdom, valor, and majestic power;
the form-body that is unobstructed and universally pervasive; and the form-body that displays the most supreme benefit for the world.
The form-body that universally gathers the ocean of great compassion; the form-body that universally gathers the king of mountains of great merit;
the form-body that universally illuminates and manifests the reflections of all realms of existence; the form-body that manifests the power of purifying great wisdom;
the form-body of right mindfulness that accords with all worlds; and the radiance of the marks of all jewels.
The form-body that reveals the treasury of Vairocana; the form-body that accords with the tranquility of all sentient beings;
the form-body in which the essential marks of omniscience are manifest;
the form-body whose smiling eyes cause all sentient beings to universally give rise to pure faith; and the universal radiance of the most supreme adornment of all jewels.
The form-body that neither grasps nor abandons the form-bodies of all sentient beings; the form-body that is indeterminate and free from attachment;
the form-body that manifests sovereign power through majestic empowerment; the form-body that displays the supernatural transformations of all dharmas;
the form-body illuminated by the light of the various roots of goodness of the Tathāgatas; [the form-body] that pervades the ocean of the Dharma-realm.
The physical body that remains far removed from all unwholesome forms; the physical body that universally manifests in the presence of the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas;
the physical body that manifests as an ocean of various wondrous colors capable of accomplishment;

the physical body that universally appears as the wondrous fruits corresponding to the outflow of virtuous conduct; and the physical body that tames sentient beings according to those who are to be transformed.
A physical body that all the world never tires of beholding; a physical body that emits various kinds of pure light-rays;
a physical body that displays the ocean of signs of all three periods of time; a physical body capable of emitting an ocean of flaming light-rays;
a physical body that displays an immeasurable and perfect ocean of light; and a physical body of all exquisite fragrant lights.
The color-body that clearly and universally transcends all worlds; the color-body from each and every pore manifesting clouds of solar discs as numerous as unspeakably many atoms;
the color-body of majestic power consisting of vast and stainless clouds of lunar discs;
the color-body of radiance consisting of clouds of exquisite flowers from Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, emitting immeasurable colors; and the manifestation of various kinds...
The body of radiant color from clouds of exquisite garlands; the body that displays clouds of all kinds of jewel lotuses;
the body that manifests clouds of all forms of burning incense pervading the entire Dharma-realm;

the body that, in every thought-moment, universally scatters clouds of treasuries of powdered incense, manifesting transformations that fill the ten directions; the body that manifests all Tathāgatas...
The body of the cloud-like form of vast vows that has come forth; the body that manifests all languages and universally expounds the ocean of Dharma;
the body of the cloud of forms manifesting the image of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

In every moment of thought, they manifest such various physical forms, filling all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, causing sentient beings to either behold their physical bodies, hear them preach the Dharma, follow and recollect them with mindfulness, attend upon and serve them, encounter their supernormal powers, or witness their transformations. Through these various kinds of inconceivable and sovereign majestic powers, all according to the inclinations of their hearts, beings attain awakening; they are tamed at the appropriate time, abandon unwholesome karma, and bring their virtuous conduct to fulfillment.

"Good son! You should know that this is accomplished through the power of various great vows in the past; through the power of the swiftness of all-knowledge; through the power of the vast liberation of a bodhisattva; through the power of great compassion that protects and saves sentient beings; through the power of great loving-kindness that brings peace and happiness to sentient beings; through the power of non-retrogression in diligent pursuit and conformity; and through the power of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas."
"Good son! Having entered this liberation, I thoroughly understand that the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is without differentiation, yet I am able to manifest immeasurable physical bodies;
within each and every body, I manifest an ocean of immeasurable physical forms."
From each and every mark, he universally emits immeasurable clouds of great light;
each ray of light illuminates and manifests immeasurable Buddha-fields;
in each and every field, immeasurable Buddhas appear and arise in the world.
Each and every Tathāgata manifests immeasurable great supernormal powers.

According to the differing mental activities of sentient beings, they bring about awakening and development of their roots of goodness from past lives: causing those who have not yet planted them to plant them, those who have already planted them to grow, and those who have already grown them to reach maturity.

In every moment of thought, they cause immeasurable sentient beings to attain non-retrogression in their progress toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and to dwell securely within various gates of liberation.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-four;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-five.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation," at that time,
the night goddess addressed Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!"
Regarding what you have asked—since when you first resolved to attain enlightenment and began practicing the bodhisattva path—I shall explain this matter to you by relying on the power of the Buddha.
“Good son! The Bodhisattva’s wheel of wisdom is quiescent and perfect, remaining far removed from all realms of conceptual discrimination.

Within the delusions of birth and death, one cannot use distinctions such as long or short, defiled or pure, broad or narrow, many or few—nor can one manifest or awaken sentient beings through such eons of conceptualization.”

Why is this? Because the wheel of wisdom of a bodhisattva is pure by nature; it is free from the net of all conceptual discrimination, transcends all mountains of obstruction, and shines universally upon those who are to be transformed according to their needs.
“Good son! For example, the orb of the sun has no inherent day or night; it is merely called ‘day’ when it rises and ‘night’ when it sets.

The wheel of a bodhisattva’s wisdom is likewise: it is without discrimination and without the three periods of time. Yet, by the power of the world and the majestic virtue of the bodhisattva’s wheel of wisdom, distinctions are established within that which is non-distinct in order to teach and transform sentient beings, speaking of their dwelling places, of prior and subsequent kalpas, and of the extent of defilement and purity.”

“Good son! It is like the orb of the sun, which dwells in the sky above Jambudvīpa; its reflection appears in all pure jewels, as well as in rivers, oceans, ponds, pools, vessels, and all pure waters. All sentient beings behold it with their own eyes, yet that solar orb does not come here.

In the same way, the sun-like orb of the Bodhisattva’s perfected pure wisdom emerges from the ocean of existence and dwells in the tranquil void of the Buddha’s true Dharma, without any dependence. Yet, for the sake of transforming and delivering all sentient beings, he takes birth according to their kind within the various realms of existence. In truth, he is not subject to birth and death, nor is he defiled or attached; he has no conceptual discriminations regarding long or short kalpas.”

Why is this? Because Bodhisattvas have ultimately abandoned all perversions of thought, mind, and view, attaining the vision of true stillness and perceiving the real nature of phenomena. They know that all worlds are like dreams and illusions, devoid of self or person; yet, by the power of their great compassion and great vows, they emit stainless light that is vast and perfect, manifesting before sentient beings to teach, transform, and subdue them.

“Good son! It is like a ferryman who, with a great ship upon a river, neither relies on this shore, nor clings to the opposite shore, nor dwells in the middle of the current as he ferries sentient beings across without rest;

so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who, with the ship of the pāramitās within the stream of birth and death, does not weary of birth and death, does not grasp at nirvāṇa, and does not dwell in the middle of the current as he ferries sentient beings across to reach the other shore without rest.”

Although throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons they have constantly applied themselves with diligence, cultivating the bodhisattva practices and transforming sentient beings, they have never made distinctions regarding the length or brevity of those eons.
"Good son! Just as in the great void, all worlds arise and perish within it without discrimination, for its intrinsic nature is pure;
it is unstained, undisturbed, unimpeded, and insatiable; it is neither long nor short, sustaining all lands throughout all kalpas until the end of the future."

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: with a vast and profound mind as equal to the realm of empty space, they raise the wind-circle of great vows to gather in all sentient beings, causing them to leave the evil realms and be born in the various happy destinies; they cause them all to dwell securely on the ground of all-knowledge, extinguishing the bonds of afflictions and the suffering of birth and death, yet without any heart of sorrow, joy, weariness, or fatigue.

“Good son! Just as a person created by magical illusion, though fully endowed with a physical body and all its limbs complete, lacks the ten things—namely, inhalation and exhalation, cold and heat, hunger and thirst, sorrow and joy, and birth and death;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva. By means of the equal Dharma-body of illusory wisdom, they manifest various forms and dwell for immeasurable kalpas within the realms of existence to teach and transform sentient beings. Within all the spheres of birth and death, they likewise lack these ten things, which are as follows:”
There is no elation, no dejection, no craving, no aversion, no suffering, no pleasure, no grasping, no relinquishing, no security, and no fear.

“Good son! Although the wisdom of a bodhisattva is thus profound and difficult to fathom, I shall, by relying on the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, explain it for you, so that all bodhisattvas in future ages may fulfill various gateways of vast vows and achieve and increase various powers.”
“Good son! In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, there was a world named Jewel Radiance, and its eon was named Sublime Light.
Within that eon, ten thousand buddhas appeared in the world:
the first of these buddhas was named Dharmacakra-Mahāghoṣa-Gaganameghapradīparāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, complete in the ten titles.
Within Jambudvīpa among those four continents, there was a royal capital named Sarvaratnavyūha-sarvapriya;
not far to the east of the city was a great forest named Subhāsa;
within that forest was a Bodhi tree named Ratnakusumamegha.
Beneath that tree was a lion throne named Vairocana-maṇi-rāja-padmagarbha.
At that time, the Tathāgata attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon this seat;

for a full hundred years he remained seated at the most excellent site of enlightenment, expounding the True Dharma for the sake of all bodhisattvas, devas, humans, and those in Jambudvīpa whose roots of goodness had been planted in the past and were now fully matured.
"At that time, there was a king named Prabhāsa;

the lifespan of the people of that age was ten thousand years. Among them, there were many who committed killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, frivolous talk, divisive speech, harsh speech, greed, anger, and wrong views; they were unfilial toward their parents and disrespectful toward śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas. Thus, all such evils increased and flourished."

At that time, desiring to subdue those sentient beings of evil nature and cause them to abide in the vast accomplishment of the ten wholesome paths of action, the king established prisons and confined them with shackles and fetters, wherein immeasurable sentient beings underwent suffering.

The king had a crown prince named Śaktimant, who was exceptionally handsome and outstanding, a sight that all people delighted to behold; he was most preeminent and pure, possessed of perfect and wondrous complexion, and was endowed with twenty-eight of the marks of a great man.

While dwelling within his own palace, surrounded by court ladies, he heard from afar the sounds of prisoners undergoing cruel and agonizing torture. His heart was moved by compassion, and he emerged from the palace to enter the prison. There he saw the various offenders bound together by shackles, manacles, and neck-yokes, cast into a dark and gloomy place; some were being scorched with fire, others smoked with fumes, some were being flogged and whipped, while others suffered the amputation of kneecaps or the cutting off of limbs. Naked, with disheveled hair, emaciated by hunger and thirst, their sinews severed and bones exposed, they wailed in extreme agony.
Having seen this, the Prince gave rise to a heart of pity and a resolve to benefit and protect them, comforting them with a fearless voice, saying:
"Do not be distressed, do not grieve or fear; I shall cause you all to attain complete liberation."
He then went to the king’s presence and addressed him, saying:
“The prisoners in the jail suffer such bitter torment that it is difficult for them to endure; I pray that you will grant them clemency and bestow upon them fearlessness.”
Then the king immediately assembled five hundred ministers and asked them,
"What do you say regarding this matter? The ministers replied:

"That criminal has privately stolen official property, plotted to usurp the royal throne, and illicitly entered the inner palace; his crimes deserve execution and he must not be pardoned to bring disorder to the royal law.
Anyone who shows mercy or attempts to rescue him shall likewise be put to death."
When the prince heard these words, his compassion became even more intense, and he said to the minister:
"As you have said, simply release the criminal; I shall undergo all the painful matters in his stead, and you may punish me as you see fit."

For the sake of liberating all sentient beings who are bound by suffering and affliction, I would not begrudge even the shattering of my body or the loss of my life; I must ensure that these offenders are all freed from their plight.
Why is this? If I do not rescue these sentient beings and bring them to liberation, how can I rescue the sentient beings suffering within the prison of the triple world?

All sentient beings within the triple world are bound by various cravings and attachments; they enter into the dense forests of manifold darkness, obscured by ignorance, impoverished and devoid of merit, falling into the evil realms. Their physical forms are base and ugly, their faculties are dissolute, and their minds are deluded; they do not seek the path out, lose the light of wisdom, and take pleasure in clinging to the three realms of existence. They sever all blessings and virtues, extinguish all wisdom, and have their minds turbidly disturbed by various afflictions. Dwelling in the prison of suffering, they enter the snare-net of Māra, subject to birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, vexation, and harm.
Being thus constantly oppressed by these various sufferings, how may I cause them to attain liberation?

For this reason, one should relinquish all precious wealth, kinsmen, wives, children, and even one’s own life to rescue and deliver them, so that those prisoners in hell may be freed from their suffering.
At that time, having heard these words, the ministers went together to the king’s presence and, raising their hands, cried out in a loud voice: "Great King!

You should know that if the Crown Prince, following his own whims, destroys the royal law, the calamity will extend to the myriad people; if the King cherishes him and does not swiftly punish and reprimand him, the King’s precious throne will likewise not endure for long.
Upon hearing these words, the king was filled with a towering rage and ordered that the crown prince and all the criminals be executed.

When the queen heard this, she wailed in grief and lamentation; she disfigured her appearance and cast off her finery, covering her body in dust. Accompanied by a thousand court ladies and her kinsfolk, she rushed to the king’s presence, threw herself prostrate upon the ground, bowed her head at the king’s feet, and addressed him together, saying:
"We pray only that Your Majesty, in your compassion, will forgive the crown prince and grant him his life."
The king immediately changed his mind and said to the crown prince:
"The crimes of these prisoners are such that they cannot be pardoned; therefore, I command you not to save these criminals. If you save them, I shall surely put you to death."

At that time, because the Prince desired to develop a vast and expansive mind, because he desired to seek exclusively for all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), because he desired to benefit all sentient beings, and because he desired to universally rescue and gather them through great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), his mind was firm and resolute, free from any retreat or timidity.
He spoke again to the king, saying:
"I pray that you forgive his crime; I shall take his place and undergo execution.
The king said:
"Your will be done. At that time, having seen that the Crown Prince was determined to save [the man] out of compassion, the Queen spoke again to the King, saying:
"I pray that you grant the Crown Prince permission to practice giving for half a month and cultivate merit as he pleases, and only thereafter shall he be executed."
The king immediately granted his permission.
At that time, the queen, her attendants, and the palace ladies, having received the king's consent, were filled with a mixture of grief and joy that they could not contain.
At that time, to the north of the capital city, there was a great park named Sūryaprabha, which had formerly been a place where various sages of antiquity gave alms.

The Prince went there and established a great assembly for giving; to those who required food he gave food, to those who required clothing he gave clothing, and even vehicles, flower garlands, necklaces, ointments, powdered incense, banners, pennants, precious parasols, and all other kinds of precious ornaments—whatever was sought, there was none not provided in full measure.

When half a month had passed, on the final day, the king and his ministers, the queen and her ladies-in-waiting, the elders and householders, the multitudes of the city and its suburbs, as well as the various non-Buddhist practitioners, all gathered together.

At that time, the Tathāgata Dharmacakra-Mahāghoṣa-Gaganameghapradīparāja, knowing that the time had come to discipline all sentient beings, immediately went to this site of giving together with a great assembly.

That is to say: surrounded by the kings of the devas, honored by the kings of the nāgas, protected by the kings of the yakṣas, praised by the kings of the gandharvas, prostrated with bowed heads by the kings of the asuras, scattering various precious flowers with pure hearts by the kings of the garuḍas, joyfully, lovingly, and respectfully singing hymns of praise and making exhortations by the kings of the kiṃnaras, and observing and gazing upon the Honored One’s countenance with single-minded devotion by the kings of the mahoragas—
he entered that great assembly together with this multitude.
"At that time, the prince and the great assembly saw from afar that the Tathāgata’s marks and signs were upright and majestic; his faculties were tranquil and settled, like a well-trained elephant;
his mind was free from defilement, like a pure pool;
and his majestic virtue was sovereign, like a great dragon king."
Manifesting great supernormal powers, he displays great mastery;
with various marks and signs of excellence, he adorns his body;
emitting great radiance, he universally illumines the world.
From every pore, clouds of fragrant flames issued forth, shaking the infinite Buddha-fields of the ten directions;
clouds of all manner of ornaments arose, raining down all types of adornments everywhere.
By the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual merit, all sentient beings who beheld them attained purity of mind, their joy increased, and their afflictions were extinguished.

At that time, having witnessed the various manifestations of the Tathāgata’s majestic power, the prince and the great assembly attained pure minds and rejoiced immeasurably. They immediately prostrated themselves before the Buddha with their five limbs touching the ground, bowed at his feet, and prepared an exceptionally sublime and pure seat. With palms joined in reverence, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Welcome, World-Honored One!"
"Welcome, Sugata!
We pray that you will compassionately accept us and take your seat upon this throne.

Through the Buddha’s supernatural power, the devas of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens immediately transformed this seat into a lion throne consisting of a treasury of fragrant maṇi-jewel lotuses. The Buddha sat upon it, and the assembly of bodhisattvas each took their respective seats, surrounding him on all sides in a magnificent retinue.

At that time, all sentient beings in the assembly, by virtue of beholding the Tathāgata, had their sufferings and afflictions extinguished; their defilements and obstructions were entirely removed, and their physical vessels became pure, becoming fit to receive the sublime Dharma.

At that time, Prince Śaktimān, seeing that the assembly of gods, humans, and all the lords of the world—kings, ministers, elders, householders, as well as all the youths, maidens, and various non-Buddhists—had gathered, surveyed them all. He then bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and with a single-minded focus upon the Buddha, praised him in verse:
“Brahmā, Śakra, the eight classes of beings, and the seers of five supernatural powers, Each with their various eloquences, together praise the Buddha.
With my meager strength, I now join in this praise, Like a bee following the flight of a garuḍa.”
With a body of molten gold and eyes like blue lotuses, you annihilate the armies of Māra and eliminate all faults;
your majestic deportance is solemn and pure, your virtues are full, and the light of your ten powers of wisdom shines eternally and universally.

Abiding in true, tranquil bliss, ignorance is exhausted; Able to remove the intoxication of desire and sever the causes of error, He cuts through the nets of craving to benefit all living beings, And the light of his ten powers of wisdom shines eternally and universally.
When the Sun Deity appears, though he can serve as a guiding light for the world, his mind is obscured by various delusions;
yet the Buddha-sun illuminates both self and others without exception.
The Lord of Māras dwells upon the Snowy Mountains, wearing dragon necklaces and garments of animal skins;
he is perpetually obscured by the allure of women, while the light of the Ten Powers’ wisdom shines everywhere at all times.
The Moonlight King illuminates the world, with the pure sky and its array of stars as his adornment;
though various delusions may shroud his mind, the Buddha-moon shines upon both self and others without exception.
Nārāyaṇa with eyes like blue lotuses, who eliminates the transformative powers of the asuras;
whose latent tendencies and intoxication are like a fetal womb, he constantly shines everywhere with the light of wisdom of the Ten Powers.
Śakra holds the vajra in his hand; his majestic power can shatter the asuras.
Yet his mind is often clouded and intoxicated by female beauty, while the light of the Ten Powers’ wisdom shines eternally and universally.
The Lord of the Thirty-three Heavens is preeminent in power; his majestic might can shatter the armies of the asuras.
Yet, because his heart was pierced by the arrow of deluded desire, the light of the Ten Powers’ wisdom shines eternally and universally upon him.
The Ṛṣis Kapiṃjala, Vāsu, and Aṅgiras, though possessing the spiritual powers of the five superknowledges that none could restrain, had their minds perpetually intoxicated by greed and delusion;
whereas the light of wisdom of the One of Ten Powers shines eternally and universally.
The Vaiśeṣikas, Sāṃkhyas, Māṇavas, and others— All those non-Buddhists who constantly follow their own tenets,
Entangled in the net of delusion and fallen into the mire of desire— Upon them the light of the Ten Powers' wisdom shines eternally and universally.
The four Vedas describe the establishment of the world, yet the supreme-bodied deity with eight faces and four arms is perpetually obscured by various forms of ignorance;
the light of the wisdom of the Ten Powers, however, shines eternally and universally.
The heterodox deity loves desire and lacks shame; Nārāyaṇa delights in killing and has no sense of remorse;
the Mother of Ghosts eats blood and harms oxen and sheep; Piṅgala craves wine and is constantly intoxicated.
Only the Tathāgata dwells eternally in the world; his eye of wisdom is ever-bright like the light of the sun.
Sentient beings, their minds shrouded by the darkness of ignorance, fail to see the Sugata and remain perpetually lost in delusion.
I am no kinsman to the Sugata, nor am I an enemy to the followers of other paths;
since those of other paths have not robbed me of my wealth, the Tathāgata likewise has not bestowed precious treasures upon me.
Relying solely on the World-Honored One’s pure speech, which definitively benefits all without distinction between enemy and kin,
and which washes away the defilements of delusion to reveal the source of the mind— I take refuge in the Peerless One.
Able to exhaust all kalpas of the future, Benefiting and bringing peace to all sentient beings,
Uprooting suffering and bestowing joy without weariness— Therefore, I prostrate to the Compassionate One.
Beholding the Tathāgata, the moon of tranquility, whether one gives rise to deep faith or doubt,
whether one feels reverence or arrogance, or harbors sorrow— in the end, all are equally endowed with the fruit of liberation.
The Buddha opens his vast blue-lotus eyes; his body, adorned with sublime marks and merit, is praised by humans and devas alike beyond measure—just as the myriad streams flow back to the great ocean.

By the slight portion of subtle roots of goodness produced through this brief praise of my tongue-faculty, I universally bestow them upon all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm; may they realize the Dharmakāya and attain perfect enlightenment.

“At that time, the Tathāgata Dharma-Wheel Great Sound Sky-Lamp King, knowing that this prince and all sentient beings in the assembly were capable of receiving the holy transformation, spoke a sūtra with a perfect voice named ‘The Universal Illumination of the Perfect Cause,’ causing all sentient beings to understand it according to their respective kinds.”
At that time, there were eighty nayutas of sentient beings in that assembly who, being far removed from dust and free from defilement, attained the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena;
immeasurable nayutas of sentient beings attained the stage of no-more-learning;
and ten thousand sentient beings dwelt in the Mahāyāna path, entered the conduct of Samantabhadra, and brought their great vows to fulfillment.
At that time, sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within a hundred Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions attained mental discipline within the Mahāyāna;
all sentient beings in the various Buddha-fields of immeasurable worlds were freed from the evil destinies;
and furthermore, immeasurable sentient beings beyond calculation were reborn in the heavens.
At this very moment, Prince Śaṃkha attained this bodhisattva liberation door of universally transforming sentient beings and causing them to give rise to roots of goodness. "Good son!
At that time, was the prince anyone else?

It was I myself. Because of the great compassion I aroused in the past, I sacrificed my body, life, wealth, and all my kinsmen, even my human peace, happiness, and lifespan, to rescue all sentient beings suffering in bondage within that prison and cause them all to attain liberation.
Opening the gates to practice great giving with a mind free from hindrance;
making offerings to the Buddhas to inspire joy in them;
and generating the bodhicitta—by these means, one attains this liberation.

"Good son! At that time, I acted solely for the benefit of all sentient beings; my mind was unattached to the triple world and had no point of reliance. I sought no karmic reward and harbored no expectations; I did not crave any worldly fame, nor did I wish to praise myself or disparage others. I had no attachment to any worldly wealth or treasures, and in the practice of giving, I remained free from a mind fixated on signs. Regarding the various objects of the world, I felt neither greedy attachment nor fear."

They take delight solely in the realm of the Tathāgata and purify the bodhicitta; their mental nature is as firm and solid as a diamond. They strive tirelessly to bring sentient beings to maturity and, through the power of great compassion, extinguish the suffering of sentient beings. Through the power of the Tathāgata, they develop their inner minds, observing the various pure practices of Bodhisattvas and adorning the essential path of the Mahāyāna. They constantly delight in observing the gates of omniscience, cultivating various ascetic practices to attain this liberation.
“Good son, what do you think? Were those five hundred ministers who,
at that time, spoke ill of King Prasenajit and sought to harm me anyone other than these very people?”
The five hundred evil bhikṣus who were once the followers of Devadatta are these very people.
Having been transformed, tamed, and brought to maturity by my teaching, they have all been granted the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

In a future age, after eons as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru have passed, there will be an eon named Good Radiance (*Suvimalaprabha*) and a world named Jewel Light (*Ratnaprabhā*), wherein they shall attain Buddhahood.
These five hundred buddhas appeared in the world in succession; the first Tathāgata was named Mahākāruṇika;
the second was named Sarvasattvārthakara-praṇidhicandrarāja;
the third was named Mahākāruṇikasimha.
The fourth was named Benefactor of All Worlds;
and so on, until the last, who was named King of Physicians.

Although the great compassion of those Buddhas is equal, yet for the sake of subduing sentient beings, there are various differences in their lands’ meritorious adornments, their lineages and parents, their taking of birth and actual delivery, their life as householders and their renunciation, their cultivation of the bodhisattva path, their proceeding to the site of enlightenment, their subduing of the demonic armies, their attainment of perfect awakening, their turning of the wheel of the true Dharma, their preaching of the sūtras, their speech and voices, their manifestation of supernatural powers, their display of great majesty, their assemblies of light, their lifespans and the duration of their teachings, and their respective names.
“Good son! Those sinners whom I saved were none other than the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, such as Krakucchanda and the rest.

At that time, there were ten million asaṃkhyeyas of great bodhisattvas who, seeing the boundless majesty and power of that Tathāgata, resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. These are the ones who now, throughout all worlds in the ten directions, practice the bodhisattva path, cultivating and increasing it; such bodhisattvas universally transform sentient beings, causing them to give rise to roots of goodness and attain liberation.”
At that time, King Prasenajit was none other than the great master of debate, the Nirgrantha Saccaka.

At that time, the king’s consort, the women of the inner palace, and their retinue were those sixty thousand disciples of the Nirgrantha who, together with their teacher, came to erect the banner of great debate and engaged in discussion with the Buddha; they were all subsequently subdued and received the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
All these people shall become buddhas; their various buddha-fields, various adornments, eon-numbers, and names shall each be distinct.

“Good son! At that time, after I had rescued those sinful people and brought them to liberation, my parents permitted me to renounce my kingdom, wife, children, wealth, and all my kinsmen, so that I might leave the household life and study the Path under the Tathāgata Dharmacakra-Mahāśabda-Gaganameghapradīpa-rāja.

Having purely cultivated the Brahma-faring for a thousand years, he immediately attained the accomplishment of ten billion gates of samādhi, ten billion gates of dhāraṇī, ten billion gates of supernormal powers, and ten billion great Dharma-treasuries of the Bodhisattvas. He was able to give rise to ten billion gates of vigor for seeking all-knowledge, purify ten billion gates of patience, increase ten billion gates of contemplative mind, accomplish ten billion powers of the Bodhisattvas, enter deeply into ten billion gates of the Bodhisattvas' knowledge of all modes, produce ten billion gates of Prajñāpāramitā, attain ten billion gates wherein the Buddhas of the ten directions appear before him, and be endowed with ten billion gates of the great vows of the Bodhisattvas.
Having accomplished and perfected such dharmas, in every thought-moment he illuminates ten billion buddha-fields in each of the ten directions;
in every thought-moment he travels to ten billion buddha-fields in each of the ten directions;
in every thought-moment he recollects the ten billion buddhas of the past and future kalpas throughout all worlds in the ten directions; and in every thought-moment...
They are able to know the ocean of the great transformations of ten billion Buddhas in all worlds throughout the ten directions; in every moment of thought,
they can see all sentient beings within the ten billion Buddha-fields of the ten directions— those of various classes and destinies, receiving their retributions according to their karma,
at the time of birth and the time of death, in good realms or evil realms, and with beautiful or ugly forms.
He clearly and fully understands all the various mental activities, various inclinations, various natures of mind, various faculties,
various karmic habituations, various births, various continuities,
and various accomplishments of those sentient beings, at the very moment they are ready to be tamed.
“Good son! After my life had ended at that time, I was once again born in this Jambudvīpa as a wheel-turning monarch.

Following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Dharmacakra-Mahāghoṣa-Gaganameghapradīparāja, I immediately thereafter encountered the Tathāgata Gaganocchraya-Śrījayarāja; I served and made offerings to him, causing him to rejoice.”

Next, he became Śakra, and at this very site of enlightenment, he encountered the Tathāgata King of the Treasury of the Lord of Śakra and Brahmā; he drew near to him, made offerings, and caused him to rejoice.

Next, he became the King of the Yāma Heaven, and in this very realm, he encountered the Tathāgata Mountain of Great Earthly Majestic Virtue and Auspiciousness; he drew near to him, made offerings, and caused him to rejoice.

Next, he became the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, and in this very realm, he encountered the Tathāgata Great Sound King of the Radiance of the Wheel of Dharma; he drew near to him, made offerings, and caused him to rejoice.

Next, he became the Heavenly King of Wondrous Transformations; in this very realm, he encountered the Tathāgata King of the Lamp of Space-Wisdom, whom he approached, served, and honored, causing him to rejoice.

Next, he became the Heavenly King of Mastery over Others' Emanations; in this very realm, he encountered the Tathāgata King of the Banner of Invincible Power, whom he approached, served, and honored, causing him to rejoice.
Next, he became an Asura King; in this very realm, he encountered the Tathāgata King of the Sound of All Dharmas, whom he approached, served, and honored, causing him to rejoice.

Next, he became the Great Brahma King; in this very realm, he encountered the Tathāgata Universal Manifestation of Transformational Reflections Dharma-Sound King, whom he approached, made offerings to, and caused to rejoice.

“Good son! In this world-system of Jewel Radiance, during the eon called Wondrous Light, ten thousand Buddhas appeared in the world; I drew near to each and every one of them, serving, honoring, and making offerings to them so as to bring them joy.

Subsequently, there was another eon named Sunlight; in that eon, one hundred thousand Buddhas appeared in the world. The first Tathāgata was named Auspicious Mountain of Wondrous Marks and Features. At that time, I was a king named Great Wisdom, and I served and made offerings to that Tathāgata, bringing him joy.”
Next, a Buddha appeared named Paripūrṇaskandha; at that time, I was a lay devotee (gṛhapati), and I approached him to make offerings so as to bring him joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Vimalakumāra; at that time, I was a minister, and I approached him to make offerings so as to bring him joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Vikrāntagāmin; at that time, I was a king of the asuras, and I approached him to make offerings so as to bring him joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Wonderful Light; I was a mountain deity, attending upon and making offerings to him so as to bring him joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Sumeru Appearance; I was a tree deity, attending upon and making offerings to him so as to bring him joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Undefiled Arm; I was a merchant leader, attending upon and making offerings to him so as to bring him joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Siṃhavikrāntagāmin; I was then a city deity, attending upon and making offerings to him so that he would feel joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Devendraratnaśikhin; I was then the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, attending upon and making offerings to him so that he would feel joy.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Dharmodgataśrī; I was then a Gandharva king, attending upon and making offerings to him so that he would feel joy.
Next, there appeared a Buddha named Universal Radiance Crown; at that time, I was a king of the kumbhāṇḍas, and I approached him to make offerings and bring him joy. Good son!
Within that eon, these ten Tathāgatas were the foremost; in this manner, I made offerings to all one hundred thousand Tathāgatas in succession.
"O son of good family!

In this world-system, there was subsequently an eon named *Sudarśanapuṣpa* (Wonderful Lotus), during which sixty billion Tathāgatas appeared in the world. Throughout that time, I constantly assumed various bodies and, through various modes of conduct, went before each and every one of those Buddhas to attend upon them, serve them, and honor them with various requisites to inspire their joy. I taught and tamed immeasurable sentient beings, causing them to mature in the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Furthermore, at each and every one of those Buddhas' abodes, I attained various gates of samādhi, various gates of dhāraṇī, various gates of supernormal powers, various gates of eloquence, various gates of all-knowledge, various gates of Dharma-illumination, and various gates of wisdom; these illumined the oceans of the ten directions, entered the oceans of Buddha-fields, beheld the oceans of all Buddhas, and manifested the profound, universally established, purely accomplished, and vastly increased [teachings].
Just as in this Wondrous Lotus Kalpa, I have approached and made offerings to that many Buddhas, causing them to rejoice.
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within all world-oceans in every place, for all Tathāgatas who appear in the world, I shall approach and make offerings to them, causing them to rejoice;

for each and every Tathāgata’s exposition of the sublime Dharma, I shall listen to it all, and having heard it, I shall believe and accept it, guard and maintain it, and explain it extensively for others, likewise bringing all sentient beings to transformation and maturity.
"In this way, at the abodes of all Tathāgatas, they have all cultivated this gate of liberation and further attained immeasurable skillful means for liberation.

At that time, the Night Goddess named Sovereign of the Radiance of Courageous Strength in the Diligence of Great Vows to Protect All Sentient Beings, wishing to restate the meaning of this gate of liberation, spoke these verses to Sudhana:
"You have aroused the great mind to become a sun for the world, And you ask me about this inconceivable gate of liberation.
I shall now speak for you by the power of the Buddha; you should listen with single-minded attention.
In the past, across boundless and vast eons, exceeding the number of atoms in an ocean of lands, there was a land named Jewel Radiance, and within it was an eon called Wondrous Light.
Within this Great Eon of Wondrous Light, ten thousand Tathāgatas appeared in the world;
I approached and made offerings to them all, and from them I cultivated this liberation.
At that time there was a royal capital named Priyavyūha, vast, level, and exceedingly magnificent;
it was inhabited by sentient beings of mixed karma, some with pure minds and others who committed evil.
At that time there was a king named Prabhāsa, who always governed the multitudes of living beings with the True Dharma;
his crown prince was named Vijayagāmin, whose physical form was upright and majestic, endowed with all the marks of excellence.
At that time, immeasurable people were imprisoned, destined for execution for violating the king’s commands;
having seen them, the Prince gave rise to compassion and addressed the king, entreating him to grant them clemency.
The king assembled his ministers to deliberate on what should be done; they all said, "The crown prince endangers the kingdom.
Such a criminal should be executed; how can you seek to save him all at once and grant him immunity?"
Then King Prasenajit said to the crown prince:
"If you would save him from his transgression, you must suffer for it yourself.
The prince’s compassionate concern grew even deeper; he vowed to rescue all sentient beings without ever retreating or faltering.
At that time, the king’s consorts and maidens all came to the king’s presence and said to him:
"We pray that you will release the crown prince for half a month, so that he may practice giving to sentient beings and cultivate merit."
Upon hearing this, the king immediately granted permission; he established a great assembly of almsgiving to relieve the poor and destitute.
There were no sentient beings who did not arrive, and whatever they requested was all provided to them.
Thus, when the half-month had come to its end and the time for the Prince’s execution was approaching,
a great multitude of hundreds of thousands of millions of people gazed upon him simultaneously, all wailing in lamentation.
The Buddha, knowing that the faculties of the assembly were about to ripen, came here out of compassion to transform all living beings;
manifesting great majestic adornments through supernatural transformations, there was none who did not draw near with reverence.
The Buddha, through the skillful means of his perfect voice, Shines the lamp of Dharma throughout the sūtras;
The minds of immeasurable beings are tamed, And all receive the prediction of their future enlightenment.

Upon hearing the Dharma, the Prince gave rise to joy; he resolved to awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, vowing to serve the Tathāgata and universally become a refuge for all sentient beings.
From this point on, I left the household life to dwell in reliance upon the Buddha, practicing the path to all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*).
At that time, I attained this liberation, whereby great compassion extensively saves all living beings.
Abiding therein for oceans of kalpas, They contemplate the true nature of all phenomena;
Constantly rescuing sentient beings from the ocean of suffering, They diligently cultivate the path to enlightenment.
All the Buddhas who appear throughout the kalpas, I shall serve them all without exception;
with a mind of pure faith and understanding, I shall hear, uphold, and protect the Dharma they teach.
Next, throughout oceans of immeasurable and boundless eons, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field,
for all the Buddhas appearing in the world, I shall make offerings to each one in this very same way.

I recall that in the past, when I was a crown prince, Seeing sentient beings bound in prison, I vowed to sacrifice my body to rescue them; It was because of this that I realized this gate of liberation.
For as many eons as there are atoms in Buddha-fields, they constantly practice throughout an ocean of vast kalpas;
in every thought-moment they cause their cultivation to increase, thereby accomplishing boundless skillful means.
All the Tathāgatas therein, I have seen them all and received their awakening;
they have caused me to further clarify this liberation, as well as its various powers of skillful means.
Throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, I have studied this inconceivable gate of liberation;
the ocean of all Buddhas' teachings is boundless, yet I am able to drink it all at once.
All the lands throughout the ten directions, his body enters them all without obstruction;
the various names of the realms across the three periods of time, he knows them all completely, moment by moment.
The oceans of all Buddhas throughout the three periods of time, I clearly perceive each and every one without exception;
I am also able to manifest my physical form, Universally proceeding to the abodes of those Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, throughout all lands in the ten directions, before all Buddhas, the Teachers,
they cause clouds of every kind of adornment to rain down universally, making offerings to all Unsurpassed Enlightened Ones.
Furthermore, with an ocean of boundless great questions, they entreated all the World-Honored Ones;
they received and upheld all the clouds of sublime Dharma produced by those Buddhas, never forgetting or losing them.
Furthermore, in immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions, before the assemblies of all Tathāgatas,
they sit upon seats adorned with myriad wonders and manifest various supernormal powers.
Furthermore, throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions, He manifests all manner of supernatural transformations:
From a single body he manifests infinite bodies, And within infinite bodies he manifests a single body.
Furthermore, from each and every pore, he emits countless great rays of light;
through various skillful means, he extinguishes the fires of affliction within sentient beings.
Furthermore, from within each and every pore, clouds of countless transformation bodies emerge,
filling all worlds throughout the ten directions, universally raining down the rain of Dharma to save all living beings.
All Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions, Entering this inconceivable door of liberation,
Exhausting all future lands and eons, Dwell securely and practice the bodhisattva deeds.
He preaches the Dharma according to the inclinations of their minds, causing them all to cast off the net of false views;
he shows them the path of the gods and the two vehicles, up to the Tathāgata’s omniscience.
In all places where sentient beings are born, He manifests infinite varieties of bodies;
Appearing in forms identical to each class of being, He preaches the Dharma universally according to their minds.
If one attains this gate of liberation, One dwells in an ocean of boundless merit;
Like the number of atoms in an ocean of lands, It is inconceivable and immeasurable.
“Good son! I know only this bodhisattva liberation door of universally transforming sentient beings to cause them to produce roots of goodness.
As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they transcend all worlds, manifest bodies in all realms of existence, and possess a wisdom-eye that is clear and penetrating.”
Forever free from the cataracts of delusion, they do not dwell upon objects of perception; being without obstruction, they thoroughly comprehend the self-nature of all phenomena.
They eliminate the dark ignorance of sentient beings, skillfully observe all phenomena, and through subtle contemplation of skillful means, they attain the wisdom of non-self and realize non-self.
The Dharma teaches and tames all sentient beings without ever ceasing; its mind always dwells peacefully in the dharma-gate of non-duality;
it attains indestructible faith in the realm of the Triple Gem; it thoroughly understands the arising and ceasing of all conditioned phenomena;
it skillfully explains the pure reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the three periods of time; and it universally enters the ocean of all verbal expressions.

How then could I know or describe that ocean of merit, that courageous wisdom, that sphere of mental activity, that realm of samādhi, that power of liberation, those gates of mastery, and those matters of supernormal power?

"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa, to the northwest of the Bodhi tree along the Ganges, in the city of Kapilavastu, there is a grove named Lumbinī. In that grove there is a deity named Wondrous Majestic Virtue Perfectly Adored."
Go to him and ask: How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva practice?
How is one born into the family of the Tathāgatas?
And how does one become an inexhaustible lamp, whose radiance illuminates the world?
"Throughout all kalpas of the future, how can you practice what is difficult to practice without ever becoming weary?

At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Five;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-Six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra, by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation: The Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra.

At that time, Sudhana the youth, with right mindfulness, contemplated the Night Goddess Radiance Protecting All Beings through the Power of Great Vows and Diligence. By the power of her liberation, she manifested bodies seen according to the minds of all sentient beings; she manifested bodies in forms equal to those of all sentient beings; she manifested bodies like an ocean of infinite colors and marks; and she manifested bodies like an ocean of majestic deportment in all places and secular customs.

She thus manifested such bodies through the Universal Gate, responding to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, maturing them through various skillful means, causing them to awaken, increasing their roots of goodness, leading them to practice in accordance with the Way, and enabling them to enter the profound liberation of Bodhisattvas.

In this way, with the power of right mindfulness, Sudhana recollected and discerned the liberation attained by that Night Goddess, as well as all her teachings—each and every word, phrase, name, characteristic, and essential nature. Through the power of dhāraṇī, he remembered and sustained them; through the power of wisdom and understanding, he clearly revealed them; and through the power of practice and vows, he gave rise to such vast conformity, thereby attaining immeasurable and supreme merits.
Traveling by stages, he crossed to the north of the Ganges River, entered the kingdom of Kośala, and headed toward the city of Kapilavastu, arriving at the Lumbinī grove.
Upon arrival, he circumambulated it to the right, seeking out the forest deity named Wondrous Virtue Perfectly Adorned and Dear to All.

He saw her beneath a great jewel tree within a magnificent and perfectly adorned jeweled pavilion, seated upon a lion throne of mani-gem treasury, surrounded before and behind by twenty billion nayutas of forest goddesses, as she extensively expounded the *Sūtra of the Ocean of Births of All Bodhisattvas*, causing them all to be born into the family of the Tathāgata and swiftly enter the great ocean of bodhisattva merit.
Having seen him, Sudhana prostrated at his feet, stood before him with palms joined, and spoke these words:
“O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas.”
"How does one practice the conduct of a bodhisattva?
How is it possible to become a great lamp of light that illuminates the world in various ways for all sentient beings?
At that time, the forest deity addressed Sudhana, saying:

“Good son! There are ten treasuries of rebirth for bodhisattvas; if bodhisattvas accomplish these dharmas, they can swiftly be born into the family of the Tathāgatas, increasing their bodhisattva roots of goodness in every thought-moment, without ceasing or slackening.”
Non-retrogressive and uninterrupted, free from weariness, free from bondage, free from doubt,
free from confusion, free from cowardice, free from vexation or regret, and free from loss; with the essence of all-knowledge equal to the realms of the ten directions,
they accord with the Buddha-sphere and enter the gateway of the Dharma-realm, never retreating from the vast mind of bodhicitta.
They increase all practices of the pāramitās, abandon all worldly destinies and categories of existence,
and swiftly enter the ground of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas. With the power of supernatural knowledges and wisdom constantly manifest before them,
they are able to accord with and enter all the various Buddha-dharmas, ultimately attaining the realm of the true meaning.

What are these ten? They are: the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who vows to constantly serve and attend all Buddhas; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who universally accomplishes the bodhicitta; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who practices skillful means by contemplating all dharma-gates; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who illuminates the three periods of time with a profound and pure mind; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who universally illuminates all things with impartial radiance; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who is born into the family of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who is universally adorned by the light of the Buddha’s power; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who minutely observes the universal gates of wisdom; the womb of birth of a bodhisattva whose various adornments are the transformations of the dharma-realm; and the womb of birth of a bodhisattva who swiftly traverses the stages of all Tathāgatas.
“Good son! What is called the ‘Treasury of Rebirth through the Vow to Constantly Serve All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas’? Good son!”
When this bodhisattva first resolves his mind on enlightenment, he makes this vow:
"I shall draw near to and serve all Buddhas and bodhisattvas; seeing all Buddhas directly, I shall always give rise to joy;
and in the presence of all Buddhas, with a heart of reverence, I shall honor and make offerings to them without ever feeling weary or satisfied."
They increase pure faith, so that their minds never regress;
they accumulate merit, which remains constant and uninterrupted.
This is for the sake of purifying the nature of omniscience and accumulating roots of goodness so that they may flourish.
“This is the first treasury of the birth of a bodhisattva.
What is called the treasury of the birth of a bodhisattva through the universal accomplishment of the bodhicitta? Good son!
This bodhisattva resolves upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, namely:
giving rise to a heart of profound and deep great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), because they are able to rescue and protect all sentient beings;
giving rise to a heart of making offerings to all Buddhas, so as to increase the joy of all Tathāgatas.
They give rise to the mind that diligently seeks the True Dharma, because they harbor no stinginess regarding anything whatsoever;
they give rise to the mind of vast undertaking, because they cause all-encompassing wisdom to manifest before them;
they give rise to the mind of perfect great compassion, because they universally embrace all sentient beings to bring them benefit.
They give rise to the mind that does not forsake sentient beings, for they have donned the firm armor of the vow to seek all-knowledge;
they give rise to a mind free from deceit and illusion, for they attain knowledge as it truly is and universally illumine all differentiated phenomena;
they give rise to a mind that acts according to their words, for they cultivate all the difficult practices and ascetic austerities of a bodhisattva.
They give rise to the mind that does not deceive any of the Buddhas, because they vow to constantly protect the great vows of all Tathāgatas;
they give rise to the great aspirational mind of omniscience, because they will tirelessly discipline sentient beings until the end of the future.

With these ten as the foremost, there are as many accumulations of the great merit of the bodhicitta as there are atoms in a buddha-field. If bodhisattvas accomplish these dharmas, they will always be born into the family of all Tathāgatas;
this is the second treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
“What is called the Bodhisattva’s treasury of birth through the skillful practice of contemplating all dharma-gates?
Son of good family!
This Bodhisattva gives rise to a mind of present observation toward the ocean of all dharma-gates;”
One should give rise to a mind of dedication toward accomplishment regarding the path to the perfection of all-knowledge;
give rise to a mind of right mindfulness and observation regarding the ocean of pure karmic activities in all modes of conduct;
and give rise to a mind of universal purity regarding the ocean of the various samādhis of all bodhisattvas.
Regarding the ocean of the various merits of all bodhisattvas, they give rise to a mind that practices until full completion;
regarding all bodhisattva paths, they give rise to a mind that adorns and brings them forth;
regarding the merit of diligence for omniscience, they give rise to a mind that blazes like the fire at the end of an eon, never ceasing.
Toward the realm of all sentient beings, they give rise to the mind that seeks to bring the practices of Samantabhadra to fulfillment;
within all modes of conduct, they give rise to the mind that cultivates the various merits of a bodhisattva;
and within the true Middle Way, they give rise to the mind that abandons both existence and non-existence to enter into true, correct contemplation.
This is the third treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called "the treasury of birth through which a bodhisattva, with a profoundly pure mind, universally illumines the three periods of time"? Good son!

This Bodhisattva accomplishes the pure, superior, and profound mind, attains the light of the Buddha’s Bodhi that shines everywhere, and enters deeply into the ocean of the Bodhisattva’s methods and skillful means.
His mind is as firm and solid as a diamond; he gathers in sentient beings and never abandons them until the very end.

He remains far removed from all rebirths within the realms of existence, accomplishes the various supernatural transformations of a Tathāgata, gives rise to the Bodhisattva’s supreme practices and vows, and is fully endowed with the sharp and keen faculties of a Bodhisattva. He increases the pure and wholesome mind of a Bodhisattva, achieves the power of immovable great vows, receives the protective mindfulness of all Tathāgatas, destroys all mountains of obstacles, and acts as a refuge for all sentient beings.
This is the fourth treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called the "treasury of birth through the universally illuminating light of equanimity"? Noble son!
This Bodhisattva fully cultivates an ocean of various skillful means to tame and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
they are able to relinquish everything they possess and achieve the boundless essence of pure precepts;
they abide in the realm of the Buddhas, are fully endowed with patience, and attain the light of forbearance regarding all Buddha-dharmas.
With the power of great diligence and courageous resolve, they advance toward the realization of the essence of all-knowledge;
through the diligent cultivation of the gates of pure samādhis, they achieve all supernatural powers and the power of wisdom;
with the light of wisdom, they illuminate the dharma-realm, attaining the radiant clarity that discerns the distinctions of all phenomena.
Having accomplished the pure, unobstructed eye, they behold the ocean of all the physical forms and marks of the Buddhas;

they penetrate all profound natures of phenomena (*dharmatā*) and, with sovereign mastery, teach and bring sentient beings to maturity, causing all in the world to give rise to joy, while diligently cultivating various gateways to the reality of the Dharma.
This is the fifth treasury of the Bodhisattva’s birth.

"What is meant by the 'Womb of Birth' wherein a Bodhisattva is born into the family of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time? Good son! This Bodhisattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas and dwells in accordance with the Tathāgatas;

they fulfill all supreme gateways of practice, possess the ocean of vows of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, and attain the purely singular roots of goodness of all Buddhas. They share the same essential nature as all Buddhas, accomplish supramundane practices of pure white dharmas, and abide securely in the vast merits of Samantabhadra. They enter the profound samādhis of all Buddhas and behold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas. They cause all sentient beings they transform to become completely pure, attain the Dharma-gateway of the Buddhas' equal dedication, and are able to respond to questions with inexhaustible eloquence."
This is the sixth treasury of birth for Bodhisattvas.
What is called the "treasury of birth adorned by the universal radiance of the Buddha's powers"?
Son of good family!
This bodhisattva deeply penetrates the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas; their light shines everywhere and their mind never regresses.
They travel through all Buddha-fields without any physical movement;
they serve and make offerings to the ocean-like assemblies of bodhisattvas without ever becoming weary.
They understand all phenomena as they truly are, like illusions; they know all worlds to be entirely like dreams;
they see the physical bodies manifested by all Buddhas, with all their marks and signs, as being like reflections and shadows;
and they know the miraculous displays performed by the supernatural powers of all Buddhas as being like magical transformations, through which they sport with sovereign ease.
Knowing that one takes birth in various realms of existence according to their kind, like reflections in a mirror;
