knowing that the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Buddhas causes sentient beings to hear it, like echoes in a valley; and through the power of skillful means, opening the gates of the Dharma-realm so that all may realize and enter it, reaching the further shore—this is the seventh treasury of the bodhisattva’s birth.
"What is called the 'Womb of Rebirth through the Gate of Universal Wisdom of Subtle Observation'?

Good son! This Bodhisattva, dwelling in the stage of youthful innocence, attains the various modes of conduct of a Bodhisattva; with all merits fully perfected, they subtly observe the gates of all-knowledge."
Within each and every gate, throughout immeasurable eons, they expound and analyze the boundless realms of conduct of Bodhisattvas;
they attain mastery of mind regarding the profound samādhis of all Bodhisattvas;
they accomplish the most supreme pāramitās; and in every thought-moment, they appear universally before all Tathāgatas in all worlds.
They are able to enter into the samādhi of equality and non-differentiation amidst all differentiated objects;
within the dharma of non-differentiated equality, they manifest the sovereign wisdom of differentiation;
and amidst immeasurable and boundless objects, they enter and emerge with mastery and without obstruction.
Within the absence of objective realms, they give rise to various differentiated perceptions;
within minute objects, they perceive vast realms;
and within vast realms, they perceive minute objects.
Knowing that all worlds are merely provisional designations, and penetrating that the causal conditions and characteristics of all phenomena arise solely as manifestations of one's own mind—
this is the eighth treasury of birth for Bodhisattvas.
“What is called the Bodhisattva’s treasury of various adornments for birth through the transformation of the Dharma-realm? Good son!
In every thought-moment, this bodhisattva adorns immeasurable Buddha-fields with various adornments, universally manifesting transformation bodies in accordance with sentient beings.”
Having attained the supreme perfection of fearlessness, they manifest the various majestic demeanors of all Buddhas and accomplish diverse skillful means;
relying upon the pure and unobstructed Dharma-realm, they manifest various forms and appearances according to the minds of sentient beings, so that all who behold them are without fail tamed;
they cause all to dwell securely in the inconceivable vehicle and fully expound the practices for attaining enlightenment.
They traverse the unobstructed path of omniscience, appearing in continuous succession to turn the wheel of Dharma;
they abide in the ocean of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge) which has neither center nor periphery, responding to those to be transformed without missing the proper time;
they are always able to benefit others through impartial right mindfulness, thereby accomplishing the treasury of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
This is the ninth treasury of birth for bodhisattvas.
What is called the "treasury of birth through swiftly traversing the stages of all Tathāgatas"? Good son!

This Bodhisattva has received the dharma of empowerment from all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, and fully knows the sequential order of the realm of the single essential nature of all Buddhas throughout the three periods of time.
That is to say:
knowing the sequential order of the continuous manifestation of all worlds according to the mind;
and knowing the sequential order of the continuous succession of birth and death for all sentient beings.
They know the sequential order of the continuous succession of the various mental thoughts of all sentient beings;
they know the sequential order of the continuous succession of all births taken by all bodhisattvas throughout past and future kalpas;
and they know the sequential order of the continuous succession of all practices performed by all bodhisattvas throughout past and future kalpas.
They know the continuous sequence of all the various spheres of wisdom cultivated by all bodhisattvas;
they know the continuous sequence of all Buddhas manifesting perfect enlightenment throughout past and future kalpas;
and they know the continuous sequence of skillfully approaching and making offerings to all phenomena according to their functional capacities.

They know all kalpas, from their past and future limits, whether in the process of formation or destruction, including their various phenomena and characteristics, as well as the continuous succession of their various names;

they know how to manifest perfect enlightenment according to those who are to be saved, through the adornment of merit, the awakening and disciplining of beings, the manifestation of majestic power, wisdom, and supernormal powers, and the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma, ensuring that all sentient beings approach and make offerings at the proper times without missing the continuous succession of these events, because they discipline infinite realms of sentient beings through skillful means.
This is the tenth treasury of the birth of a bodhisattva.
“Good son! These ten treasuries of the bodhisattva’s birth are those from which all bodhisattvas are born.

If bodhisattvas, desiring to accomplish vast enlightenment, cultivate, increase, and perfect these dharmas, they will be able to accumulate various merits; from within a single adornment, they will produce all adornments, universally adorning all buddha-fields.”
He manifests various transformed modes of conduct to universally subdue all realms of sentient beings, without ceasing throughout all future eons.
Through the various causes and conditions and various spheres of the ocean of all Buddhas' teachings, they flow on in succession without interruption; his present awakening is all-pervasive.
He manifests the inconceivable sovereign power of the Buddhas, which universally fills the void of the Dharma-realm.
Within the ocean of the mental activities of all sentient beings, they turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of gathering them in.

They draw near to and never forsake the presence of all Tathāgatas throughout all worlds in the ten directions; immeasurable clouds of Dharma appear everywhere before them, as they expound the ocean of all dharmas with pure voices.
Abiding in all places, their conduct is unimpeded, as they adorn various sites of enlightenment with the wondrous net of light of all dharmas.

In accordance with the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings, they expound the boundless and manifold treasuries of Dharma, manifesting the various realms of all Buddhas, and awakening all the world according to their needs.

At that time, the forest deity of the Lumbinī Grove, named Lovely and Revered Virtue (*Guṇarati*), wishing to further proclaim the meaning of the Bodhisattva’s vast treasury of birth, surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s spiritual power and spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"With a supreme, stainless, and profoundly pure mind, Never weary of beholding all Buddhas,
Vowing to offer constant worship throughout the future— This is the treasury of birth of this one of clear wisdom."

Within the ocean of all lands throughout the three periods of time, May all sentient beings and all Buddhas therein be universally rescued and protected, And may they always be beheld with reverence; This is the treasury of birth for those of renowned name.
Receiving the rain of the Dharma-clouds without ever being satiated, universally observing the three periods of time without attachment,
with body and mind as pure as space— this is the treasury of birth for those who are peerless.
The mind constantly dwells within the ocean of great compassion, Firm, stable, and lofty as Mount Sumeru;
Having mastered the gateway to all-knowledge, This is the treasury of births of the Sovereign One.
Great compassion pervades the ten directions; He universally practices the stainless pāramitās.
With the light of the Dharma, he illuminates all classes of beings; This heroic and valiant one is the treasury of birth.
Awakening to the self-nature of phenomena with an unimpeded mind, Born into the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
Deeply entering the dharma-realm with boundless wisdom— This is the treasury of birth for those of clear intelligence.
The Dharma-body is pure and the mind is free from attachment; It reaches everywhere throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions.
There is no power of all Buddhas that it does not accomplish— This is the inconceivable treasury of taking birth.
Entering the deep ocean of wisdom, they attain mastery; Abiding in the ocean of samādhi, they reach ultimate perfection.
Contemplating the gateway of skillful means of all-knowledge— This is truly the treasury of birth for those who possess wisdom.
Purifying all Buddha-fields, Bringing all sentient beings to maturity,
Manifesting the Buddha’s spiritual power in universal adornment— This is the treasury of birth for those of great renown.
Cultivating all the Buddha-dharmas and wisdoms, they swiftly and universally enter the stage of the Tathāgata;
realizing that the Dharma-realm is entirely without obstruction—this is the treasury of birth for true sons of the Buddha.
“Good son! If bodhisattvas possess these ten treasuries of birth, they will be born into the family of the Tathāgatas and act as great luminous lamps for all worlds.”

"Good son! I have attained this liberation door of the sovereign birth of all bodhisattvas; for immeasurable eons, I have sported with spiritual powers, manifesting the unobstructed realm of bodhisattvas."
Sudhana said: "Noble One! What is the scope of this gate of liberation?"
The forest deity replied:
“Good son! I previously made this vow:”
"May I always be able to approach and make offerings to all Bodhisattvas at the time they manifest their births; may I enter the immeasurable and vast ocean of births of the Tathāgata Vairocana."
By the power of his former vows, he has come to be born here in this Sahā world, within the Lumbinī Grove in the city of Kapilavastu, in Jambudvīpa among these four continents.
In this grove, he focused his mind exclusively on when the Bodhisattva would descend to be born;
after a hundred years had passed, he finally beheld the World-Honored One descending from Tuṣita Heaven to take birth.
“Good son! At that time, when the Bodhisattva was about to descend to be born, ten kinds of auspicious signs of adornment first appeared within this great forest. What are these ten?
That is to say:
first, the ground of this grove suddenly becomes level of its own accord, such that pits, hollows, mounds, and hills all disappear;
second, all the thorns, shards, rubble, and impure things within the grove likewise vanish from sight.
The ground is composed of vajra, adorned with various jewels, like the Nandana Grove, soft, fine, and exquisite.
Third, within the garden there are further jewel-tāla trees; their roots are deeply planted, reaching down to the water’s edge, arranged in successive rows as an adornment.

Fourth, within the grove there further appeared all manner of fragrant sprouts and all manner of fragrant treasuries—unguents, powdered incense, banners, pennants, precious canopies, and various exquisite mani-jewel images;
as well as diverse fragrant trees, their interlacing shade providing majestic adornment, surpassing all the fragrances possessed by humans and devas.
Fifth, within the grove there are further exquisite flower garlands and jewel ornaments, filling every place and distributed with subtle beauty.
Sixth, all the great jewel trees in the grove naturally blossom with *maṇi* jewels, and from between their flowers and leaves flow delicate strands of golden garlands.
Seventh, within the grove, all the ponds and pools were filled with exquisite flowers—supple, fresh, and pure—which sprang up from the earth and spread across the surface of the water.

Eighth, at that time, all the great celestial kings of the desire and form realms from this Sahā world, as well as all the lords of the world—including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others—without exception, gathered there and stood with palms joined.

Ninth, all the celestial maidens, nāga maidens, yakṣa maidens, gandharva maidens, and so forth, as well as the consorts of all the world-protectors throughout this trichiliocosm, were filled with joy; each holding various kinds of offerings, they stood respectfully facing the pi-lo-sha tree.

Tenth, all the Buddhas of the ten directions emitted from their navel-cakras a great light called "The Lamp of Various Sovereignities in the Birth of Bodhisattvas," which universally illuminated all things within the grove. Within each and every ray of light, there appeared all the miraculous manifestations of the Buddhas' births and nativities, as well as all the various merits of the bodhisattvas' births; furthermore, the diverse voices and sounds of the Buddhas issued forth, enabling all sentient beings to hear and behold them.

These are the ten kinds of auspicious signs that appear within the grove; once these signs have manifested, the various heavenly kings and world-protectors immediately know that the Bodhisattva is about to descend to be born.
When I saw these ten kinds of auspicious signs and this inconceivable realm, my heart was filled with joy, and I leaped for immeasurable delight.

“Good son! At that time, when the Bodhisattva’s mother, Lady Māyā, departed from the city of Kapilavastu and entered this grove, ten kinds of auspicious signs of radiant light appeared, illuminating all things universally. This caused all sentient beings to attain the light of the *dharmatā* of omniscience, swiftly increasing their joy, love, and reverence.”
What are these ten? They are as follows:
within this forest, the various jewel pavilions, the fragrant sprouts, and the fragrant treasuries all emit radiance, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions;
Furthermore, all the lotuses in every pond within this grove emitted radiance, and from within that radiance issued forth subtle and wondrous sounds, proclaiming the Tathāgata’s words of true Dharma;

moreover, they caused all bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds in all worlds throughout the ten directions to emit radiance that came to illuminate this Lumbinī Grove, filling it entirely without exception;

and they further caused all great bodhisattvas dwelling on the stages in all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions to manifest great spiritual transformations and emit great radiance that came to illuminate this Lumbinī Grove.

Furthermore, they caused all the great Bodhisattvas in all Buddha-fields of the ten directions who have perfected their practice by accomplishing all the perfections (pāramitās) to emit great radiance and come to illuminate this Lumbinī Grove;

they caused all the great Bodhisattvas in all Buddha-fields of the ten directions who abide in the ocean of great vows to emit all the light of sovereign, unimpeded vows and wisdom and come to illuminate this Lumbinī Grove;

and they caused all the great Bodhisattvas in all Buddha-fields of the ten directions who abide in the ocean of great compassion to emit all the light of vows and wisdom and come to illuminate this Lumbinī Grove.

Furthermore, he caused all the great bodhisattvas dwelling in the ocean of skillful means in all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions to emit various kinds of light of skillful means for taming sentient beings, which came to illuminate this Lumbinī grove;
he also caused all the great bodhisattvas in all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions to emit the light of the wisdom of true teaching, which came to illuminate this Lumbinī grove;

and he also caused all the great bodhisattvas in all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions to emit the light of the great wisdom of all Buddhas’ sovereign descent, renunciation, and attainment of enlightenment, which came to illuminate this Lumbinī grove.
When these ten kinds of light appeared, they universally caused the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings to be extinguished. "Good son!

At that time, after Queen Māyā had manifested these ten signs of light, as she was about to give birth beneath the Pīluśa tree, she further manifested ten kinds of vast and great miraculous transformations."
What are these ten? Good son, when the Bodhisattva was about to be born,

the celestial kings of the Form Realm and their sons, the gods of the Desire Realm and their consorts, as well as the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and all the lords of the world together with their retinues, all gathered like clouds for the sake of making offerings.

At that time, Lady Māyā’s physical appearance, majesty, and adornments were exceptionally sublime; every pore of her body emitted radiance like lamps, like the sun, or like a mass of molten gold, universally illuminating the trichiliocosm without obstruction. All other lights therein were completely eclipsed and ceased to appear, while she extinguished the afflictions of all sentient beings and the sufferings of the evil realms.
This was the first miraculous transformation at the time when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
"Furthermore, noble son!

At that time, within the womb of Lady Māyā, all the forms of the trichiliocosm were fully manifested. Within the various cities of the Jambudvīpa continents among the ten billion four-continent worlds therein, there were gardens, each with a different name;

in each one was a Lady Māyā, sitting beneath a tree, surrounded by all the lords of the world and their retinues, all manifesting the inconceivable signs of supernatural transformation as the Bodhisattva was about to be born."
This was the second miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.

"Furthermore, noble son, within every single pore of Lady Māyā’s body, there appeared the World-Honored One Vairocana, as he had previously cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva, approaching and making offerings to all Buddhas, and hearing the sounds of those Buddhas preaching the Dharma, which universally shook all worlds throughout the ten directions."

All manifested objects are like the reflections of space, the sun, the moon, the stars, clouds, and thunder that can appear within a clear mirror or pure water; likewise, the various deeds of supernatural power performed by the Tathāgata in the past, which were manifested from every pore of Queen Māyā’s body, were also thus.
This was the third miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
"Furthermore, noble son!

Within every single pore of Queen Māyā’s body, there appeared all the oceans of worlds, all the world-systems, the essential natures of worlds, and the shapes of worlds—along with the cities, villages, mountains, forests, rivers, seas, springs, streams, and ponds within those worlds—as well as the sentient beings being delivered therein, the number of kalpas traversed, the Buddhas who appeared, the pure lands entered, the bodies assumed, the lifespans experienced, the spiritual friends served, the Dharma gates attained, the practices and vows cultivated, and the fruits of realization obtained, from the first generation of the bodhicitta until the attainment of the stage of non-retrogression."
In all places and in every place of birth, Lady Māyā served as his mother.
In this way, all the realms of the Tathāgata’s past were manifested within a single pore;
this was the fourth miraculous transformation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
"Furthermore, noble son!

Within each and every pore of Lady Māyā, there appeared clearly and with perfect distinctness all the various physical forms, various appearances, various modes of deportment, and various matters concerning requisites, clothing, food and drink, suffering and pleasure, experienced by the Tathāgata during his past cultivation of the bodhisattva path throughout all his births.
This was the fifth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born."
"Furthermore, noble son!

Within every single pore of Queen Māyā’s body, there appeared all instances of the World-Honored One’s past cultivation of the practice of giving, wherein he relinquished what was most difficult to give:

his own body parts and limbs—head, eyes, ears, nose, lips, tongue, teeth, blood, flesh, marrow, liver, gallbladder, intestines, stomach, skin, sinews, and veins—as well as his wives, concubines, male and female attendants, palaces, cities, and all manner of precious treasures."
Gold, silver, lapis lazuli, conch shells, jade, necklaces, rings, pendants, clothing, food, drink, and all such internal and external objects;
he also perceives the various locations, physical forms, and languages of the recipients—
this is the sixth supernatural manifestation of the Bodhisattva when he is about to be born.
"Furthermore, noble son!

At that time, within this grove, there universally appeared all the various Buddha-fields, gardens, adornments, retinues, and their various banners, pennants, parasols, flower garlands, robes, ointments, powdered incense, mani-jewels, and so forth, as well as various necklaces and ornaments, and various musical performances, songs, and hymns of praise—all with sublime sounds filling the grove—enabling all sentient beings to hear and see them everywhere.
This was the seventh miraculous transformation of the Bodhisattva when he was about to be born."
"Furthermore, noble son!

From within the womb of Lady Māyā’s body, there appeared a palace and pavilion made of the king of *maṇi* jewels, which the Bodhisattva was destined to enjoy—a place surpassing all the abodes of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and human kings.

It was covered above by a net of *maṇi* kings and further adorned with various ornaments of *maṇi* kings in the forms of all humans and devas; it was perfumed with stainless, supreme, and wondrous fragrant kings, causing the minds of all sentient beings to become pure."
In this way, all these filled the forest, each distinct and without confusion;
this was the eighth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
"Furthermore, noble son!

From the womb of Lady Māyā emerged as many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as there are atoms in ten unspeakably unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields. The physical forms, features, complexions, radiance, movements, dignified deportment, spiritual powers, and retinues of all these bodhisattvas were entirely equal to those of the Bodhisattva Vairocana, without any difference; they all simultaneously offered praise to the Tathāgata.
This was the ninth miraculous manifestation at the time when the Bodhisattva was about to be born."
"Furthermore, noble son!

When Lady Māyā was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, suddenly before her, from the adamantine foundation, there emerged a great lotus called 'Treasury Adorned with All Jewel Kings. It had a stem made of the invincible diamond-mani-king jewel, a calyx made of the maṇi-king jewel of the ocean of reflections of sentient beings, filaments made of all the most exquisite maṇi-kings, and a pedestal made of the pure and stainless wish-fulfilling jewel-king. It possessed petals numbering as many as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, all formed of maṇis, adorned on all sides with radiant light flashing forth;
it had a net made of maṇi-jewel-kings draped all around, firm and indestructible."
A canopy made of vajra-jewel kings covered its top;
it was held up together by all the celestial kings,
while all the dragon kings raised great clouds of incense and showered down rain of fragrance.
All the devas rained down exquisite celestial flowers and various ornaments;
all the yakṣa kings respectfully surrounded him;
and all the gandharva kings produced sublime sounds, singing praises of all the merits the Bodhisattva had acquired through his past attendance upon and offerings to the Buddhas.
All the asura kings abandoned their prideful minds, bowing with reverence and joining their palms in prostration;
all the garuḍa kings held precious silk ribbons in their beaks, adorning the void;
and all the kiṃnara kings gave rise to hearts of joy, singing and praising the virtues of the Bodhisattva.
All the mahoraga kings were filled with joy; they raised great sounds, singing hymns of praise, and rained down clouds of all manner of precious ornaments.
This was the tenth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.

“Good son! I see Lady Māyā in this grove, on the verge of giving birth to the Bodhisattva, manifesting ten kinds of supernatural signs, inconceivable varieties of merit, and immeasurable radiance, without ever feeling satiety in her heart.”

Then Lady Māyā gave birth to the World-Honored One from her right side; he was like a pure solar disc appearing in the void, like auspicious clouds rising upon a high mountain peak, like flashes of lightning shining amidst dense clouds, or like a great torch lit in the darkness of night.
At that time, as the Bodhisattva was born from his mother’s side, the radiance of his physical marks was likewise so.

Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva, wishing to demonstrate that all dharmas are like shadows and reflections, like dreams and illusions—without going or coming, without arising or ceasing—manifested his birth.

“Good son! When I beheld the Tathāgata Vairocana manifesting the miracle of his initial birth in the Lumbinī Grove within Jambudvīpa among these four continents, I also saw the Tathāgata manifesting various miracles of his initial birth in the Lumbinī Groves of Jambudvīpas throughout the ten billion sets of four continents in the trichiliocosm;

I also saw him manifesting various miracles of his initial birth in Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within a trichiliocosm, in Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within a hundred Buddha-worlds, and even in Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within all worlds in the ten directions.”

He also saw, within every minute atom of the worlds throughout the ten directions, all the various and immeasurable Buddha-fields, each manifesting the various miraculous transformations of his birth and descent into life.

In this manner, from moment to moment until the end of the future, throughout all oceans of lands within every dharma-realm across the ten directions—in each and every atom, within infinite worlds—they manifest various miraculous transformations at their initial birth, continuing in succession without interruption.

Although in every moment of thought they universally manifest births and various miraculous transformations throughout the entire ocean of infinite lands, their minds remain unattached and free from all obstructions.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the forest goddess of the Lumbinī Grove, named Wondrous Virtue, Perfect Love, and Auspicious Fortune: "Noble Lady!
"How does a bodhisattva, dwelling in their final body, necessarily take birth within such a great clan?
The forest deity replied,
"O son of good family!"

When all Bodhisattvas are about to achieve perfect enlightenment, dwelling in their final existence, they are all born either in a royal palace or in the family of a great clan of Brahmins. Why is this?
It is for the sake of accomplishing various benefits and taming oneself and others so that they may reach maturity.
Good son, there are three kinds of dharmas that can benefit both oneself and others:
First, the cause and effect of maturation;
second, the cause and effect of merit;
third, the cause and effect of wisdom.
What is maturation? It is of eight kinds:
first, the perfection of lifespan;
Second, the perfection of physical form;
third, the perfection of lineage;
fourth, the perfection of sovereignty;
Fifth, the perfection of trustworthy speech;
sixth, the perfection of great power;
seventh, the perfection of the marks of a mahāpuruṣa.
Eighth, the perfection of heroic power.
"Good son, how does a bodhisattva achieve the perfection of lifespan?
That is to say:
having a long life and dwelling for a long time in the world.
What is meant by a bodhisattva’s perfection of physical form?
That is to say:
his physical form is upright and dignified, his marks and signs are exceptionally sublime, and people delight in beholding him, never wearying of it.
What is meant by a bodhisattva’s perfection of lineage?
That is to say:
being born into a noble and eminent family of the Kṣatriya caste or a Brāhmaṇa household.
What is the bodhisattva’s perfection of mastery?
That is to say:
attaining great wealth and status as well as a large retinue; having one's actions accord with one's will; and being honored and followed by others.
What is the bodhisattva’s perfection of authoritative speech?
That is to say:
their words are truthful and sincere, so that people necessarily believe and accept them;
when mediating disputes and litigation, their minds harbor no partiality toward high or low.
In all matters of decision and judgment, they are like those who hold a scale;
their words and deeds are never inconsistent, and they are free from seeking or flattery.
What is meant by a bodhisattva’s perfection of great power?
That is to say:
his reputation is lofty and far-reaching; he is courageous and diligent; his disposition is gentle and harmonious; he remains unmoved by praise or blame;
and in the arts and crafts, there is none who can surpass him.
When amidst great assemblies, he is universally respected.
What is the perfection of the marks of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
It is as follows:
Possessing the marks of a great man, he is free from all physical defects.
What is the perfection of a bodhisattva’s heroic power?
It is as follows:
The power of his retribution is preeminent; his body is always free from illness, and his mental power is courageous and robust, possessing superior capability.
These eight qualities constitute the perfection of a bodhisattva’s maturation (*vipāka*).
“Good son! How does a bodhisattva cultivate these eight kinds of causes for maturation?
They are as follows:”
When a bodhisattva gives rise to great compassion for all sentient beings and harbors no intent to harm, this is the cause for the perfection of lifespan.
If bodhisattvas, before images of Buddhas and bodhisattvas and in all dark places, bestow light and various kinds of fresh, clean clothing, this is the cause for the perfection of physical form.
If bodhisattvas, while situated among various classes of beings, always maintain a humble mind, this is the cause for the perfection of lineage.
If bodhisattvas provide whatever is desired to sentient beings who are impoverished and in distress, this is the cause for the perfection of sovereignty.
If bodhisattvas constantly cultivate truthful speech, harmonious speech, gentle speech, and unchanging speech, this constitutes the cause for the perfection of credible speech.

If bodhisattvas, desiring to assume a body in future lives endowed with various physical marks and preeminent virtues, give rise to great vows to make offerings to the Triple Gem, spiritual friends, parents, and teachers; and if they constantly do not abandon this resolve, serving and honoring them without interruption, this constitutes the cause for the perfection of great power.

If Bodhisattvas constantly delight in the male body with their minds, always feel revulsion toward the female form, and view feminine beauty with fear as if it were a fierce fire; if they conceive of the male body as a source of merit and also exhort sentient beings to loathe the female body and rejoice in the male form—this is the cause for the perfection of the male body.
If bodhisattvas constantly serve sentient beings with their own physical strength, attending to them by performing labor as appropriate;

if they massage, anoint, and wash their teachers, and provide various kinds of excellent food and drink to those who are hungry and thirsty, causing them all to be fully satisfied, bringing them peace and happiness, and increasing their physical vigor—this is the cause for the perfection of heroic power.
In this way, the bodhisattva cultivates these eight causes of maturation and brings forth their matured fruits. "Good son!
These eight causes of maturation further increase by means of three conditions, enabling them to bring forth matured fruits that are complete, vast, beneficial, and sublime."
What are the three? First, a pure mind; second, pure conduct; and third, a pure object.

If bodhisattvas possess a pure inner mind, they dedicate all their roots of goodness toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and the realization of the profound, single-flavor *dharmadhātu*. Their vast faith and joy are singular and unmixed; they diligently seek and practice without regard for body or life. They share the same resolve and conduct as spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), feel deep joy upon seeing fellow practitioners of the Dharma, and contemplate day and night, following [the path] in every thought-moment. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, their minds never know satiety—this is called the first arousal of a pure mind.

If bodhisattvas, regarding these very roots of goodness arising from such vast aspirations and inclinations, cultivate them over a long period of time without interruption from moment to moment, and through skillful means bring them all to fulfillment—causing those who have not yet undertaken their practice to undertake it, and causing those who have already undertaken it to become firm in it—this is the second purification of conduct.

If bodhisattvas cause the mind to be purified within all those spheres of activity, are able to correctly initiate and bring their conduct to pliancy, and thus seek the ultimate fruit, this is the third sphere of pure engagement.
“Good son! What is the matured fruit (*vipākaphala*) of a bodhisattva?

It means that by virtue of the bodhisattva’s perfection of lifespan, they are able to practice for a long duration without interruption; thus all roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) are accumulated and increased, enabling them to remain long in the world to benefit themselves and others. This is the fruit of the perfection of longevity.”

Furthermore, because the Bodhisattva’s physical appearance is so dignified and majestic, sentient beings love and revere him; consequently, the entire assembly comes to seek refuge in and look up to him, and there is nothing he says that they do not delight in hearing. Once they have heard the Dharma, they all practice it accordingly. This is the fruit of the perfection of physical appearance.

Furthermore, because the Bodhisattva’s lineage is authentic and genuine, he is revered by the world; this causes all sentient beings to comply with all his instructions, diligently practicing them so as to swiftly abandon all unwholesome karma and cultivate all wholesome karma—this is the fruit of the perfection of lineage.

Furthermore, because the Bodhisattva is fully endowed with the perfection of mastery over wealth and status, he is able to bestow various precious jewels and servants upon sentient beings, satisfying them all according to their needs;
by means of this integration, he subsequently disciplines and brings them to maturity—this is the fruit of the perfection of mastery.

Furthermore, because the bodhisattva has accomplished truthful speech, he is able to gather all sentient beings through affectionate words, taming and maturing them so that they accept his teachings with faith and all attain liberation; this is the fruit of the perfection of trustworthy speech.

Furthermore, because the bodhisattva possesses noble status, sovereignty, and great power, they are able to cause sentient beings to be moved by their virtue and follow their transformation; these beings develop a sense of shame and remorse, coming to revere and cherish them, such that whatever words the bodhisattva utters are followed without opposition. This is the fruit of the perfection of great power.

Furthermore, because the bodhisattva is fully endowed with the marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*) and possesses faculties that are perfected and without deficiency, he is thus a fit vessel for supreme merit; he strives with diligence to seek the realm of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā-viṣaya*);
he attains fearlessness and unobstructed conduct, thereby able to bring great benefit to all sentient beings;
and whatever he undertakes accords with his mind, being entirely free from hindrance.
No devas or humans in any world are able to revile or disparage him;
this is the fruit of the perfection of the marks of a Great Man.

Furthermore, because the Bodhisattva has accomplished heroic power (*vīrya*), he is universally able to accumulate all wholesome dharmas, brings peace and happiness to the realm of sentient beings, and through courageous diligence accomplishes wisdom and supernormal powers (*abhijñā*); this is the fruit of the perfection of heroic power.
This is called the cause and fruit of maturation (*vipāka*).
What are merit and wisdom? They are as follows:
The three pāramitās of giving, ethical discipline, and patience are called merit;
the pāramitā of wisdom is called knowledge;
and diligence and meditative concentration are called both merit and knowledge.
That is to say:

if one practices generosity, ethical discipline, patience, the immeasurables such as loving-kindness, and so forth by means of diligence, this is called merit; if, by means of diligence, one gives rise to hearing, reflection, and cultivation, this is called wisdom.

Furthermore, by virtue of diligent cultivation of skillfulness regarding the aggregates (*skandha*), skillfulness regarding the bases (*āyatana*), skillfulness regarding the elements (*dhātu*), skillfulness regarding dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), and skillfulness regarding what is possible and impossible (*sthānāsthāna-kauśalya*), one is able to know the four truths, wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, the superior and inferior nature of afflictions, and black and white karmic actions; the subtle observation of all these is termed "wisdom" (*jñāna*).
If one cultivates the four immeasurables based on meditative concentration, this is called merit;
if one cultivates prajñā and various skillful means based on meditative concentration, this is called wisdom.

Therefore, the Bodhisattva is able to bring great benefit to all sentient beings; among the great assemblies in all Buddha-fields, he acts as their leader, universally following and conforming to all Buddhas as they turn the wheel of the true Dharma.
He is able to discipline himself and also to discipline all sentient beings, causing them to swiftly enter the path to omniscience.
When a Bodhisattva accomplishes such various and sublime causes and effects, they are able to swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
*The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha*, Fascicle Twenty-six;
*The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha*, Fascicle Twenty-seven.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
Chapter on Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation through the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra.
At that time, the youth Sudhana addressed the forest deity, saying:
“Noble One! How long has it been since you attained this liberation?
The forest deity replied:
“Good son! In the distant past, more than a hundred million buddha-fields of atoms of kalpas ago, and even twice that number, there was a world named Universal Jewel and a kalpa named Joyful Delight;
eighty billion nayutas of buddhas appeared therein, the first of whom was named Sovereign Virtue of the Invincible Banner, complete with the ten titles.”

In that world, there is a continent of four quarters named Jambudvīpa of Various Adorned Radiance. In its center is a royal capital named Pure Adorned Sumeru Banner, where there dwells a king named Jewel Radiant Flame Eye.

At that time, the primary consort of that great king was named Great Flame Sovereign Joyful Light; just as Queen Māyā was the mother of Vairocana Tathāgata in this world’s Jambudvīpa, so too was the consort Great Flame Sovereign Joyful Light the mother of that first Sovereign Virtue Invincible Banner Tathāgata in the Jambudvīpa of the world Various Adorned Radiance. Thus it was.

“Good son! At that time, when Lady Joyful Light was about to give birth to that Bodhisattva, she was surrounded by twenty billion nayutas of female attendants as she proceeded to the Vast and Perfect Golden Flower Garden, manifesting various inconceivable supernatural transformations associated with the birth of a Bodhisattva.”
At that time, within that garden there was a pavilion named Pure Peak of Wondrous Jewels, and a great king of trees named All-Giver.

Then, the lady grasped a branch of that tree with her right hand and gave birth to the Bodhisattva from her right side. The devas received and supported him, bathing him with scented water, while all the lords of the world extensively presented offerings.
At that time, there was a wet nurse named Vimalaprabhā standing by his side;

then the devas bestowed [the child] upon the wet nurse, who received him with reverence, cradled him in her arms, and felt great joy, immediately attaining the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Universal Eye Realm.

By attaining this samādhi, one universally beholds all the infinite Buddhas of the worlds in the ten directions, and further attains this dharma-gate of liberation for sovereign rebirth in all places.

"Good son! Just as the consciousness at the moment of initial conception is swift and unimpeded, so too, by attaining this samādhi, one is able to swiftly behold the Buddhas of the ten directions; the miraculous manifestation of taking birth through the power of original vows is likewise so."
“Good son! What do you think?
Was that nurse named Vimalaprabhā at that time someone else? Could it have been anyone other than [me]?”
I am that very person!
Those twenty billion nayutas of female attendants at that time are now my retinue in this grove, namely these twenty billion nayutas of forest goddesses;
the lady Great Blazing Sovereign Joyful Light of that time is now Lady Māyā.
At that time, the great king named Jewel Radiant Eye was none other than the present King Śuddhodana.
O son of good family!
From that time forth, in every moment of thought, I have constantly beheld the ocean of great spiritual transformations of Vairocana Bodhisattva’s sovereign rebirths.

"Good son! Just as you see the World-Honored One Vairocana, in every thought-moment, manifesting oceans of gates of sovereign miraculous transformations through birth by power of his original vows within this Sahā world and within each atom of this world;

so too do you see the World-Honored One universally throughout all oceans of lands in the ten directions, manifesting sovereign miraculous transformations through birth within all worlds and their atoms, just as if seeing them in the present."

He also beheld the Tathāgata manifesting the sovereign spiritual transformations of taking birth throughout the worlds of the ten directions and within every single atom of those worlds, extending to the very end of the future.
"Good son! Just as you see the sovereign spiritual transformations of the present Buddha Vairocana manifesting births everywhere;

so too do you see all Buddhas of the ten directions, each riding upon their original vows, pervading all places throughout the limits of the past and future, manifesting sovereign spiritual transformations of taking birth within all worlds and within every atom of those worlds."

"They all attain the opportunity to draw near to, serve, and make offerings to the Buddhas, and to hear the wheels of Dharma turned by them; they are all able to receive, uphold, follow, and penetrate these teachings.
At that time, the forest deity Subhūṣitā, wishing to further proclaim the meaning of this liberation gate, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"Excellent, O Son of the Buddha, is the question you have asked, Concerning the most supreme realm of the Buddhas, which is difficult to know.
Generate deep respect and a mind of faith and joy; listen attentively as I explain this cause.

For eons as numerous as the atoms in a hundred million lands, and even twice that many, there was a subsequent eon named Joyful Delight, wherein eighty billion nayutas of Buddhas appeared in succession.
In the beginning, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, Named Sovereign Virtue Unconquerable Banner;
at that time, I was in that Golden Flower Garden, And beheld the signs of that Tathāgata’s birth.
At that time, I was his wet nurse, named Vimalajvālā, serving him with devotion;
the gods bestowed upon me the body of a Bodhisattva, resplendent with golden light, peerless and unsurpassed.
At that time, I received the Teacher of Gods and Men; holding him up, I gazed intently yet could not see the crown of his head.
His body’s dimensions extended boundlessly to the left and right, and his perfect marks were inconceivable.
Beholding that stainless and pure body, adorned with the most subtle and wondrous marks and signs,
like a statue of exquisite jewels or pure gold, he rejoiced and congratulated himself, giving rise to a pure mind.
Contemplating the myriad virtues of that Buddha, I increase the boundless, profound ocean of merit;
Beholding the Buddha’s peerless supernormal powers, I immediately give rise to the vast bodhicitta.
Dedicatedly seeking all the virtues of the Buddhas, Increasing all the great vows,
Adorning and purifying all lands as numerous as atoms, And eliminating all perilous and evil paths.
Throughout all lands in the ten directions, I make offerings to countless Buddhas;
Practicing universally to seek liberation, I vow to extinguish the suffering of all sentient beings.
Having heard those teachings, I was able to receive and uphold them, thereby attaining this inconceivable power of liberation;
for as many eons as there are atoms in billions of lands, I have fully cultivated the pure conduct of a bodhisattva.
The Buddhas who appeared in succession throughout the kalpas—each and every one of them I have made offerings to;
I have upheld their teachings and practiced them fully, adorning and purifying this ocean of liberation.

Throughout as many eons as there are atoms in billions of lands, I have upheld and practiced all the teachings of the Tathāgatas of the past, those Honored Ones of Ten Powers; thus is this wheel of liberation turned in purity.
In a single thought-moment, I am able to comprehend all things: within every atom of every Buddha-field, all the Tathāgatas, each adorning their respective oceans of lands.
All the Buddhas within those oceans of lands manifest their initial birth within pleasure groves;
the manifestations that appear in every thought-moment are inconceivable, through the power of vast and sovereign spiritual transformations.
I see bodhisattvas in billions of lands, single-mindedly seeking the supreme Buddha-enlightenment;
about to achieve perfect awakening, they dwell in celestial palaces, manifesting the inconceivable realms of all Buddhas.
In some, they see within an ocean of boundless lands the miraculous deeds of Buddhas taking birth,
surrounded by all their assemblies, as they extensively proclaim the True Dharma to bring about awakening.
In a single thought-moment, I am able to see everywhere Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in billions of lands,
Leaving home, subduing Māra, and sitting at the site of enlightenment, Manifesting all manner of Buddha-realms.
Or one may see within the atoms of all lands, Immeasurable Benevolent Honored Ones attaining perfect enlightenment,
Each manifesting inconceivable powers of skillful means To deliver and liberate all suffering sentient beings.
Or they see, within every single atom, all Buddhas turning the sublime wheel of Dharma,
universally raining down boundless nectar-like teachings with inexhaustible, subtle voices.
In every moment of thought, one beholds all the Buddha-fields, as numerous as the atoms within billions of lands;
in each, a Tathāgata appears taking birth, and likewise manifests parinirvāṇa, remaining entirely unattached.
In such immeasurable oceans of Buddha-fields, the Tathāgata manifests his initial birth;
I go to them all without dividing my body, appearing before each one to offer worship.
In inconceivable lands and all realms of existence, To infinite varieties of sentient beings,
He manifests before them all through skillful means, Raining down the great rain of Dharma to bring them awakening.
O Son of the Buddha, I am able to know all this— this most supreme and inconceivable gate of liberation—
which could not be fully revealed or extolled even throughout immeasurable billions of eons.
“Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva liberation-method of the sovereign spiritual transformation of manifesting birth throughout all places across immeasurable eons;
as for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are able to take a single thought-moment as the treasury from which all eons arise—”
Revealing and manifesting the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, universally manifesting births through skillful means,
vowing to constantly make offerings to all Buddhas, diligently striving until the ultimate realization of the Buddha-dharma is present before one,
manifesting bodies in all realms of existence like shadows, and sitting upon lotus thrones in the presence of all Buddhas to transform and mature beings according to their needs.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they universally manifest great spiritual transformations throughout the world; they perfect great wisdom and attain unimpeded penetration;
they achieve mastery over all samādhis; they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma;
they realize entry into the profound and unobstructed realm of reality (dharmadhātu); and they thoroughly understand the nature of the minds of all sentient beings, revealing the One [Vehicle].
Manifesting the characteristics of all merits, they give rise to the sovereign power of the vast mind; they attain the wisdom that subdues all māras and enemies,
enter in accordance with the realm of all Tathāgatas, and universally manifest form-bodies in response to all sentient beings.
How could I possibly know or describe such wisdom, merit, and conduct of a bodhisattva?

Noble son, to the southwest from here, in the city of Kapilavastu, there is a woman of the Śākya clan named Gopā. Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva matures sentient beings within the cycle of birth and death while practicing the bodhisattva path.

At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself before the goddess Lumbinī, circumambulated her to the right countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing and single-minded yearning.

At that time, the youth Sudhana went from the Lumbinī Grove toward the city of Kapilavastu. He contemplated and observed that divine abode, reflecting upon, practicing, expanding, and deeply entering the bodhisattva liberation of the sovereign spiritual transformations of the birth of all Buddhas; he remembered and upheld it without forgetting.
Gradually proceeding, he arrived at the Palace of Radiant Light Universally Manifesting the Reflections of the Dharma Realm, where the Bodhisattvas had assembled.
Within it was a presiding palace-deity named Sorrowless Virtue (*Aśoka-guṇa*), who, together with ten thousand other presiding palace-deities,
came forward to welcome Sudhana, speaking these words:

“Welcome, O noble being! You possess great wisdom and are courageous and fearless, able to cultivate the inconceivable liberation of the Bodhisattva’s sovereign mastery over the miraculous transformations of birth. Your mind never abandons vast vows; you skillfully observe the realms of all phenomena and your mind constantly dwells within the unsurpassed city of Dharma. Having entered the palace of the pure and wondrous Dharma, you reveal immeasurable skillful means to subdue sentient beings and lead them to realization. You have accomplished the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s merits and attained the Buddha’s inexhaustible, subtle, and wonderful eloquence. With the wheel of unimpeded wisdom, you turn according to the needs of sentient beings, causing them to rejoice and increase their great vows, as they dedicate themselves toward seeking the path of omniscience.”

I observe that you, O virtuous one, never for a moment abandon the profound practice; your deportment is tranquil and free from all defilements. Before long, you shall attain the unsurpassed, pure, and most excellent physical, vocal, and mental actions of a Tathāgata; your body shall be adorned with the primary and secondary marks, the light of the wisdom of the ten powers shall illuminate the ground of your mind, and you shall travel through the world as a great radiance.

I observe that you, O virtuous one, are courageous and diligent, such that you are difficult to thwart or destroy; before long, you shall universally behold all Buddhas of the three periods of time with their marks and signs fully perfected, universally hear the wheels of Dharma turned by all Buddhas, and universally be able to enjoy the bliss of all Bodhisattva meditative concentrations, liberations, and samādhis, entering the realm of the Tathāgatas in accordance with reality.

Why is this? Because you have already been able to see spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), drawing near to and serving them, honoring and making offerings to them, following their instructions, and recollecting their virtues; because you practice without interruption, free from sorrow and affliction, without slackening or retreating, and without obstacles; and because neither the gods, humans, Māras, nor Brahmās of all the worlds can create difficulties for you. Before long, you shall attain unsurpassed bodhi, and you shall also cause sentient beings to realize the fruit of Buddhahood.
Then, having heard these words, the youth Sudhana said: "Noble One!
May I fully attain all the various merits you have just described."
"O Noble One!

I vow to forever extinguish the heat of the afflictions of all sentient beings, to eliminate their various unwholesome karmas, to bestow supreme peace and happiness upon all sentient beings, and to cause all sentient beings to cultivate pure conduct."
"Noble One!

The minds of all sentient beings are constantly distracted; they give rise to afflictions and commit various evil deeds. Following their karma, they transmigrate and fall into the evil realms, where for a long night their bodies and minds endure manifold agonies. When Bodhisattvas see this, sorrow and distress arise in their hearts."

"Noble One! It is just as if a man had an only son whom he loved with the utmost affection; if he were suddenly to see that son’s limbs being severed by another, his heart would be so pierced with pain that he could find no peace.

In the same way, when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see sentient beings accumulating unwholesome karma, falling into the three evil realms, and undergoing various sufferings, their hearts are filled with great sorrow and distress, and they cannot find peace."

If one sees sentient beings give rise to the three kinds of wholesome conduct of body, speech, and mind, being reborn in the happy realms and experiencing physical and mental bliss, one gives rise to great joy.

Why is this? Because a bodhisattva does not seek omniscience for the sake of benefiting themselves alone; nor do they do so out of greed for the various pleasures of birth and death, nor out of greed for the pleasures of the five desires, nor again for the sake of seeking the joy of being surrounded by the affection, respect, and adornment of retinues in the desire realm. Furthermore, they do not turn according to the power of the fetters, latent tendencies, or the force of love and views arising from the inversion of perception, the inversion of mind, and the inversion of view. They have no greedy attachment in their hearts toward the bonds of affection for sentient beings, nor do they savor the bliss of the various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*). They are free from the various obstacles of weariness and retreat, and do not remain submerged in the flowing cycle of birth and death (*saṃsāra*).

The Bodhisattva perceives only that all sentient beings within the ocean of existence are oppressed by boundless sufferings; giving rise to great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), they vow to gather them all in and cause them to swiftly emerge from the great ocean of birth and death. Through the power of compassionate vows, they diligently practice various difficult and painful austerities, universally severing the afflictions of all sentient beings so that they may attain liberation and never again regress.
For this reason, they zealously seek the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*) and serve and make offerings to all Buddhas;
seeing the defiled and impure lands, they adorn and purify the oceans of Buddha-fields for their sake.
Seeing that the various names and appearances of sentient beings are all devoid of reality, he causes them all to attain the pure Dharma-body;
seeing that the bodies and minds of sentient beings are defiled, he causes them to attain the purity and adornment of the three karmas;
seeing that the mental activities of sentient beings are incomplete, he causes them all to attain pure fulfillment.

“Noble One! Thus, the bodhisattva possesses profound and deep great compassion for all sentient beings; able to perform all difficult and painful practices throughout boundless eons, his mind never tires or grows weary, and all that he undertakes is fully accomplished.”

They are like parents, and like nurses; they are like earth, water, fire, wind, and space; they are like the sun and the moon, and like the great ocean and the gods born together with us—capable of producing all manner of perfect benefits.
In what way is a bodhisattva like parents?
Because they establish others in the bodhicitta.
In what way is a bodhisattva like a wet-nurse?
This is for the purpose of causing them to accomplish the bodhisattva path.
"In what way is a bodhisattva like the great earth?
For example, the great earth possesses ten qualities; what are these ten?"
That is to say:
just as the great earth is vast and immeasurable, universally accomplishing all things;
so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, accomplishing an immeasurable and vast accumulation of merit, wisdom, and virtue.
Furthermore, just as the great earth can produce all manner of worldly requisites upon which all sentient beings depend for their survival,
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: they can produce the treasures of supramundane merit, namely,

the sublime requisites of the Dharma such as generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, and the factors of enlightenment, thereby nourishing the life of merit and wisdom of sentient beings.
Furthermore, just as the great earth benefits all equally, without sorrow or joy, and without conceptual discrimination;
so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: toward enemies and kin alike, they harbor neither love nor hatred, nor do they give rise to dualistic thoughts.
Furthermore, just as the great earth can receive the rain poured down by massive clouds,
so too does the bodhisattva-mahāsattva likewise receive the great Dharma-cloud rain of the Tathāgata.

Furthermore, just as all sentient beings rely upon the great earth for their dwelling, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva likewise; he serves as the basis for the various worldly and supramundane matters of happiness for all sentient beings.

Furthermore, just as all seeds depend upon the great earth to sprout and grow, so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: the seeds of all sentient beings' wholesome dharmas depend upon him for their growth and development.

Furthermore, just as the great earth is able to produce various jewels and all manner of precious vessels, so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: he is able to produce the various jewels of merit that serve as the vessels for sentient beings.
Furthermore, just as the great earth can produce various medicinal herbs to eliminate all diseases, so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
relying upon great compassion, they produce the medicine of the Dharma to eliminate the various grave illnesses of affliction.
Furthermore, just as the great earth remains unmoved despite being touched and disturbed by various venomous insects and crawling creatures, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
though his body and mind are constantly afflicted by all manner of internal and external sufferings, he never wavers.

Furthermore, just as the great earth is not startled, nor afraid, nor does it even have the perception of hearing when the great dragons roar with various evil sounds of thunder, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
amidst the various evil sounds of Māras and non-Buddhists, he is neither startled nor terrified, free from sorrow and fear, and without the perception of hearing them.
"Good son! These are the ten kinds of merit that a bodhisattva fulfills and perfects, which, like the great earth, are accomplished with mastery. Good son!"
How is it that a bodhisattva is like water?
Just as the great element of water causes all medicinal herbs, thickets, and the kings of great trees to sprout, grow, and flourish;

so too does the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, by means of the water of samādhi, produce all the various medicinal herbs of the factors conducive to enlightenment (bodhipakṣadharma), cause the great trees of merit and wisdom to grow, and bring to fruition the fruit of unsurpassed bodhi.
How is it that a bodhisattva is like fire?
Just as the element of fire can burn all impure things and can incinerate all the grasses, trees, and dense forests upon the great earth;

so too does the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, by means of the various fires of great wisdom, burn away all the afflictions, latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), habitual perfusions (*vāsanā*), and impure stains of sentient beings.
How is it that a bodhisattva is like the wind?

For example, the element of wind has no visible form, nor does it have a dwelling place; being without support or attachment, it can yet bring to completion all the palaces and the various mountains, great and small—such as Mount Sumeru—that exist upon the waters, on land, and in the air, yet no one at all can see them.

So too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: without depending on or attaching to anything anywhere, he can bring to completion the bodhisattva’s merits, such as the aggregates, elements, and sense bases, which cannot be seen by any in the world, whether Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
How is it that a bodhisattva is like space?

Just as the essence of space is without obstruction and all phenomena are accomplished in dependence upon it, so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: his fundamental nature is unobstructed, and all pure dharmas (*śukla-dharma*) are accomplished by means of it.
In what way is he like the moon?
Just as the lunar disc gradually increases from the first day until the fifteenth day until it becomes full, so too is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva:
from the first generation of the mind of awakening, all pure dharmas gradually increase until, upon attaining Buddhahood and sitting at the site of enlightenment, all merits are fully perfected.
In what way is he like the sun?
For example, when the solar orb appears, all darkness is entirely dispelled;
likewise, when the sun of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom manifests, the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings is entirely dispelled.
In what way is it like the ocean?
For example, just as the great ocean is by nature able to produce all manner of precious jewels, providing inexhaustible enjoyment for all sentient beings;

so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, who likewise produces from the ocean of merit and wisdom all jewels of virtuous qualities and knowledge, benefiting sentient beings without ever coming to an end.
What is meant by being like those born as celestial beings?
It is, for example, like two celestial beings who are born together with a human and follow that person, never parting from them, just as a shadow follows a form;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who constantly follows sentient beings, even into evil realms and perilous places, guarding and pursuing them so as not to let them fall.
"Furthermore, noble son!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva acts as a great shipmaster for all sentient beings, so that they may cross over the ocean of birth and death;
he acts as a place of refuge, so that they may be freed from the terrors of all demons and afflictions."
They are to be relied upon as protectors, for they cause the removal of feverish affliction and the attainment of coolness;
they are great ferries, for they lead all sentient beings into the ocean of Dharma;
they are sea-guides, for they cause them to reach the island of the Buddha’s Dharma-treasures.
They are pure lotuses, for they cause the mind of the merits of all Buddhas to blossom;
they are ornaments, for they are constantly adorned by the radiance of merit and wisdom;
they are delightful, for they cause the three karmas of Samantabhadra to become completely pure and majestic.
To be worthy of veneration, so as to inspire diligent abandonment of all evil deeds;
to be the conduct of Samantabhadra, so as to perfect the subtle and wondrously complete essence;
to be that which is joyfully beheld, so that whatever is desired shall manifest without exception.
They are a great radiance, because they universally emit the blazing flames of the light of wisdom;
they are great luminous lamps, because they illuminate various phenomena so that all may be thoroughly understood;
they are capable illuminators, because they cause the nature of the bodhicitta to be clear and pure.
He is a great heroic general, for he crushes and destroys all demonic activities;
he is a sun-jewel, for he can emit the radiant net of the flames of wisdom;
he is a moon-love jewel, for he emits the cooling light that pervades the entire dharma-realm.
They act as great clouds and rains, for they are able to rain down the nectar-like Dharma upon all beings. Noble One!

When a bodhisattva cultivates these various practices in this manner, they cause all sentient beings to give rise to love and reverence, and they bring them to the full accomplishment of the joy of the true Dharma.

At that time, the spirit Aśokaśrī, together with her retinue of ten thousand spirits, stood by the side of the road. Hearing Sudhana’s own description of the characteristics of the bodhicitta he had generated, she attained what she had never experienced before and was filled with leaping joy.

She immediately scattered upon Sudhana all kinds of exquisite celestial flower garlands, ointments, powdered incense, and precious ornaments that surpassed those of the gods; she followed him in circumambulation and entered the Bodhisattva palace, where she spoke these verses:
“For the sake of all sentient beings, You have resolved your mind to seek perfect awakening.”
Throughout inexhaustible eons, you shall serve as the great lamp of brilliance for the world.
Within immeasurable billions of eons, you would be difficult to behold;
now the sun of great wisdom has risen, illuminating the world.
Seeing all sentient beings shrouded by the darkness of ignorance,
you were able to give rise to great compassion and tread the path of no teacher.
With a pure mind, you single-mindedly sought the virtues of the Buddha.
You are able to serve spiritual friends, disregarding even your own body and life.
Your mind, regarding the world, has no dependence and nothing to which it clings;
it is resolutely and ever stainless, pure as space.
You cultivate the practice of supreme wisdom, Turning the sublime wheel of merit;
You radiate the great light of primordial awareness, Universally illuminating that which is without limit.
You do not depart from the world, Yet you remain unattached to the world.
Like the wind wandering through space, your course is unimpeded.
As you advance toward enlightenment, your courageous progress is invincible;
like the blazing fire at the end of an eon, nothing can extinguish it.
Fearless as a lion, firm and solid as a diamond,
your wisdom and conduct are likewise such that nothing can move them.
Within the dharma-realm of the ten directions, all the teachings of the Buddhas—
"By serving spiritual friends, you shall be able to enter all [realms].
At that time, the spirit Anuttaraguṇa, having praised Sudhana’s meritorious conduct with these sublime verses,
delighted in hearing the True Dharma and followed after Sudhana like a shadow follows a form, never parting from him.
At that time, the youth Sudhana entered the Palace of Light Reflecting the Images of the Dharma-realm and surveyed everywhere for the Śākya maiden Gopā;

he saw her within the hall, amidst a great assembly of all bodhisattvas, seated upon a great lion throne of the lotus-womb made of the king of mani jewels that manifests the images of all palaces, surrounded by a retinue of eighty-four thousand court ladies.

None of these court ladies were not born from the Śākya clan; they had all cultivated the bodhisattva practices in the past and planted together all the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva. Through giving, kind speech, beneficial action, and cooperation, they gathered in all classes of beings.

The realm of omniscience was ever present before them, and they had already accumulated the various practices for the awakening of a Buddha. They constantly dwelt in impartiality and inexhaustible great compassion, universally gathering in all sentient beings as if they were an only child. Their hearts of loving-kindness were fulfilled, vast and pure, able to universally accord with all sentient beings. In the past, they had cultivated and accumulated various inconceivable skillful means.

They have all attained non-retrogression in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, deeply entered the various *pāramitās* of the bodhisattvas, and fully cultivated all the bodhisattva training rules (*śikṣāpada*). Their minds are always far removed from conceptual construction and attachment; they feel weary of and renounce birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*), and love and delight in the True Dharma. Although they traverse the various realms of existence, their minds are ever pure. They constantly and diligently observe the single-flavored *dharmadhātu*, swiftly seeking the path to *sarvajñatā*. Free from the nets of all hindrances and transcending all calamities and difficulties, they attain the pure *dharmakāya* and manifest in infinite forms. They discipline and bring to maturity all worlds, accomplishing a great ocean of profound merit. Born from the conduct of Samantabhadra, they swiftly increase their courageous and mighty strength, and the lamp of wisdom and the sun of insight become perfectly full and universally illuminate.

At that time, the youth Sudhana went forward and prostrated himself at the feet of the Śākya maiden Gopā; he circumambulated her to the right, stood with palms joined, and spoke these words: "Noble Lady!"

I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva, while within birth and death, can remain unattached to the faults and afflictions of birth and death.
How does a bodhisattva realize the intrinsic nature of phenomena and yet remain unattached to the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
How does a bodhisattva abide in the stage of a Buddha and yet universally enter all the stages of bodhisattvas?
How does a bodhisattva, while abiding in the stage of a bodhisattva, enter the various realms of a Buddha?
How does a bodhisattva transcend the world and yet accomplish worldly dharmas?
How does a bodhisattva realize the dharma-body (dharmakāya) and yet manifest various form-bodies (rūpakāya)?
How does a bodhisattva attain the signless dharma (animitta-dharma) and yet manifest various physical forms in accordance with sentient beings?
How does a bodhisattva know that dharmas are ineffable yet extensively expound all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings?
How does a bodhisattva know that sentient beings are empty yet never abandon the work of transforming sentient beings?
How does a bodhisattva constantly know that all buddhas are neither born nor extinguished, yet diligently make offerings to them without ever regressing?
How does a bodhisattva transcend all illusory realms, yet constantly manifest illusions to discipline sentient beings?
How does a bodhisattva, while deeply believing that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is like space, achieve boundless skillful means and wisdom?
How does a bodhisattva know that all phenomena are without attachment, yet constantly make offerings to all Buddhas with a profound mind that never regresses?
“How does a bodhisattva deeply enter into all conditioned activities (*saṃskāra*) as being without karma and without retribution, yet cultivate virtuous deeds without ceasing?
Then, that Śākya maiden said to Sudhana: “Excellent!”
Excellent, noble son!

You are now able to inquire about the essence and characteristics of the various types of practices cultivated by all bodhisattvas. Only one who is capable of cultivating the practices and vows of Samantabhadra can give rise to such a question.
Listen attentively now and reflect upon it well!
I shall, by the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, proclaim it for you.
O son of good family!
If bodhisattvas cultivate ten dharmas, they will be able to fulfill the conduct of the Bodhisattva Indrajāla-sarvajñatā-prabhā-śrī-dhvaja. What are these ten?
First, relying upon spiritual friends;
second, attaining vast faith and understanding;
third, giving rise to pure aspiration.
Fourth, the accumulation of vast merit and wisdom;
fifth, hearing the true Dharma from the Buddhas;
sixth, drawing near to the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Seventh, they practice the sublime conduct of Bodhisattvas together;
eighth, they receive the shared protection and mindfulness of the Buddhas;
ninth, their great compassion and original vows are entirely purified.
Tenth, they are able to permanently sever birth and death through the power of wisdom.
If bodhisattvas accomplish this dharma, they will be able to fulfill the conduct of the Bodhisattva Indrājāla-samantaprajñāprabhā-dhvaja.

"Good son! If bodhisattvas draw near to and serve spiritual friends, they will be able to practice with diligence and courageous non-retrogression, cultivating and giving rise to the vast, equal, and inexhaustible Buddha-dharma."
“O Son of the Buddha!
Furthermore, a bodhisattva serves a spiritual friend through ten practices, constantly causing them to rejoice. What are these ten?
First, to have no attachment or parsimony regarding one's body, life, or wealth;
second, to have no mind of greedy seeking for worldly requisites;
third, to know that the fundamental nature of all phenomena is equal.
Fourth, never to retreat from or abandon the vow for omniscience;
fifth, always delighting in observing the dharma-realm of true reality;
sixth, never feeling weary of or seeking to escape the ocean of existence.
Seventh, knowing that all phenomena abide nowhere, like empty space;
eighth, giving rise to the unobstructed great vows of a bodhisattva;
ninth, universally manifesting one’s body throughout the oceans of all lands.
Tenth: Purifying and Cultivating the Bodhisattva’s Wheel of Unobstructed Wisdom. Good son!
By means of these ten dharmas, one serves all true spiritual friends, causing them all to rejoice; one acts without opposition and proceeds toward omniscience.
At that time, the Śākya maiden Gopā, wishing to restate this meaning, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Dedicatedly seeking the Buddha-wisdom to benefit all beings, Universally serving all spiritual friends,
Upright, free from flattery, and without indolence— This is the world-transcending conduct of the Indra-net.”
Vast resolve, ever pure, pervading the three periods of time like space,
reaching into Buddha-fields, Buddhas, and sentient beings— this is the practice of the Banner of Universal Wisdom Light.
Their aspiration and joy are vast, equal to space; Free from defilement, tranquil, and boundless.
Having cultivated merit under all Buddhas, This practice moves through the world as a cloud of bodies.
The Bodhisattva accumulates all-knowledge and an inconceivable ocean of merit;
with a body of pure merit and wisdom, they perform this unattached conduct throughout the world.
Able to listen to the True Dharma from all Tathāgatas without ever feeling weary or satisfied,
generating understanding according to what is heard as the lamp of wisdom— this practice universally illuminates all conduct in the world.
All Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, In a single thought-moment, one approaches them all;
With a mind that never abandons constant and profound reflection— This is the great vow and practice directed toward Bodhi.
They go everywhere to the abodes of all Tathāgatas, Together cultivating the ocean of Bodhisattva skillful means;
Their oceans of samādhis and vows are all boundless— This is the conduct of the world, like the conduct of Indra’s net.
Having attained the empowerment of all Buddhas, they practice the path of Samantabhadra everywhere;
throughout boundless kalpas until the end of the future, they manifest these practices in the world through their emanations.
Beholding all sentient beings undergoing manifold sufferings, He gives rise to great compassion and appears in the world;
Proclaiming the light of the Dharma to dispel the darkness, This practice is the sun of wisdom moving through the world.

Seeing all sentient beings fallen into the various realms of existence, I shall gather the boundless, wondrous Wheel of Dharma, Causing them to forever sever the stream of birth and death; This is the practice of the conduct of Samantabhadra.
When Bodhisattvas practice these ten dharmas, they are able to manifest universally before all sentient beings;
throughout the various realms within the ocean of existence, they deliver and liberate all classes of living beings.
By the power of great compassion and skillful means, they universally manifest various adorned bodies;
according to the inclinations of beings, they turn the wondrous Wheel of Dharma, causing all to advance toward the path of Bodhi.
At that time, having spoken these verses, Gopā addressed the youth Sudhana, saying: "Noble son!
I have attained the liberation door called 'The Ocean of Samādhi Realms of All Bodhisattvas.'"
Sudhana said: "O Great Sage! What is the scope of this liberation gate?"

He replied, "Good son! Having entered this liberation, I know that in this Sahā world, beyond unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-land atoms of kalpas, there are all the various types of sentient beings within each and every kalpa— those who perform good and evil deeds, die here and are born there, and receive their various retributions among the realms of existence, as well as those who cultivate dhyāna, liberation, samādhi, and samāpatti."
