They are able to universally approach the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas; according to those sentient beings who are ready to be transformed, they expound the True Dharma to bring them all to maturity.
Throughout the ocean of all kalpas until the end of the future, they cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva without ever ceasing, fulfilling the vast vows of Samantabhadra.

“Good son! As for that maiden Samantavyūhaśrī at that time, who provided the four requisites to the Tathāgata Sūryagātraprabhāsa for as long as her life lasted—could she have been anyone else? It was none other than myself.”
I am that very person.
Son of good family!

After that Buddha passed into extinction, another Buddha appeared in this world named Pure Body (*Vimalakāya*). I drew near to and made offerings to that Buddha, hearing and upholding the Dharma, and likewise practiced the bodhisattva path for the sake of sentient beings.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Sarvajñābimbacandradeha, whom I approached and made offerings to;
next, a Buddha appeared named Jāmbūnadasuvarṇaprabhārāja;
next, a Buddha appeared named Mahābrahmasvaralakṣaṇavyūhadeha.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Various Flames of Wondrous Moonlight;
next, a Buddha appeared named High Peak of Wondrous Wisdom Observing Banner;
next, a Buddha appeared named King of the Radiance of Vast Wisdom.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Nārāyaṇa-vajra-vīrya-bala;
next, a Buddha appeared named Jñāna-bala-aparājita;
next, a Buddha appeared named Samantāvalokana-jñāna.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Vast Wisdom Auspicious Cloud;
next, a Buddha appeared named Fearless Wisdom Radiant Body;
next, a Buddha appeared named Pure Wisdom Flame-Light Cloud.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Guṇadhvaja;
next, a Buddha appeared named Jñānasūryadhvaja;
next, a Buddha appeared named Padmavikāsakāya.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Puṇyavyūhaprabhāsa;
next, a Buddha appeared named Jñānajvālamegha;
next, a Buddha appeared named Vairocanacandra.
Next, a Buddha appeared named King of Great Sound Adorned with Canopies;
next, a Buddha appeared named Universal Wisdom Light of Great Heroism;
next, a Buddha appeared named King of the Moon of Wisdom regarding the Realm of the Dharma-dhātu.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Universal Manifestation of Reflections that Awakens Sentient Beings with a Mind Like Space;
next, a Buddha appeared named Fragrance of the Quiescence of the Characteristics of Speech;
next, a Buddha appeared named Universal Resounding of the Sound of Accordant Tranquility.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Solid Wisdom Unobstructed Light-Net;
next, a Buddha appeared named Ambrosia Mountain Majestic Virtue King;
next, a Buddha appeared named Dharma Ocean Thunder Sound.
Next, a Buddha appeared, named Buddha-Void-Space-Light-Illuminating-Crest;
next, a Buddha appeared, named Moonlight-Urṇā-Cloud;
next, a Buddha appeared, named Moon-Face-Magnificent-Perfection.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Kusumaprabha-sujñāna; next, a Buddha appeared named Ratnārciśaila-śrītejas;
next, a Buddha appeared named Vipulaguṇajyotiḥprabha.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Sarvajñānasamādhiśarīra;
next, a Buddha appeared named Jvālāparipūrṇakāya;
next, a Buddha appeared named Varatarateja-ratnaprabhāsa.
Next, a Buddha appeared, named Universal Wisdom Swiftly Moving;
next, a Buddha appeared, named Lamp of the Ocean Gate of Radiant Flames;
next, a Buddha appeared, named King of the Wondrous Sound of the Great Dharma Palace.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Banner of Incomparable Virtue and Renown;
next, a Buddha appeared named Long Arms;
next, a Buddha appeared named Moon of the Spiritual Transformations of Pure Original Vows.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Lamp of the True Meaning of Space-Wisdom;
next, a Buddha appeared named Sovereign King of Space Above the Dharma;
next, a Buddha appeared named King of the Virtue-Treasury of Vairocana.
Next, a Buddha appeared named Narayana-dharmarāśi;
next, a Buddha appeared named Sarvayāna-jñānakūṭadhvaja;
next, a Buddha appeared named Dharmasāgara-suvimalapadma.
In this manner, sixty hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* Tathāgatas appeared successively in that eon; I drew near to them all, attending to and making offerings to each of them.
The last of those Buddhas was named Vast Joyful Manifestation of Majestic Virtue (*Vipula-pramoda-abhyudgata-tejas*), and he appeared in the world at this very place.

At that time, when that Buddha entered the royal city, I was the principal queen of the king; together with the Great King, I made offerings to that Buddha with various requisites. In the presence of that Buddha, I heard a Dharma-door called "The Lamp of the Birth and Manifestation of All Tathāgatas," and immediately attained a distinct eye of wisdom called the "Gate of Liberation through Contemplating the Subtle Realms of the Ocean of Samādhis of All Bodhisattvas."

“Good son! At that time, I attained this liberation in that realm. Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, I constantly practiced it diligently together with bodhisattvas. During all those kalpas, there were immeasurable and boundless Buddhas; I approached and made offerings to each and every one of them, receiving and practicing their teachings.”
In some kalpas, they serve one Buddha;
in some kalpas, they serve two Buddhas;
and in some kalpas, they serve three Buddhas.
Some may serve and attend upon unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas within a single kalpa;
some may encounter as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a Buddha-field within a single kalpa—I have personally approached, served, and made offerings to all such Buddhas.
I am still unable to know the bodhisattva’s physical form, size, appearance, as well as the fruits of his actions of body, speech, and mind, nor the spheres of his samādhis and liberations.

"Good son! If there are sentient beings who see a bodhisattva practicing various deeds for the sake of all-knowledge—whether they act in opposition or accord, or whether they harbor doubt or faith—the bodhisattva employs various mundane and supramundane skillful means to gather them in as his retinue, causing them to attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

“Good son! Having attained this liberation of the subtle realm of the ocean of samādhis that contemplates all bodhisattvas from the presence of the Tathāgata Vast Joyful Manifestation of Majestic Power, I have constantly practiced it together with bodhisattvas for as many eons as there are atoms in a hundred buddha-fields. During those eons, I have personally approached, served, and made offerings to every Buddha who appeared in the world.”

Those Tathāgatas each expound sūtras through various gateways; by practicing in accordance with them and maintaining them in mind without forgetting, this liberation is made to increase and expand further and further.

By this, one is able to know various sūtras, attain various bodies of merit, obtain various gates of liberation, behold various oceans of the three periods of time, visit various oceans of Buddha-lands, witness various instances of attaining perfect enlightenment, enter various assemblies of Buddhas, give rise to various bodhisattva vows, practice various bodhisattva conducts, and fulfill various bodhisattva liberations; yet, one is still unable to know the Samantabhadra liberation accomplished by the Bodhisattvas.

Why is this? Because the realm of the Bodhisattva’s Samantabhadra-liberation and supernormal powers is like great empty space, like the names of sentient beings, like the ocean of the three periods of time, like the ocean of the ten directions, and like the ocean of the Dharma-realm; it is immeasurable, boundless, and without limit.
"Good son! You should know that the Dharma-door of Samantabhadra’s liberation attained by a bodhisattva is equal to the realm of all Tathāgatas. Good son!"

For as many eons as there are atoms in those Buddha-fields, I have observed all the spheres of experience of the Bodhisattva’s body without ever becoming weary; it is like a person of great desire who, in a gathering of men and women, feels mutual passion and gives rise to immeasurable conceptualizations and perceptions in every thought-moment, turning according to those objects without end.
I am likewise; throughout those kalpas, as I observe the body of a bodhisattva, in every single pore and in every moment of thought,
I see immeasurable and boundless vast worlds with their various arisings,
various establishments, various adornments, various shapes, various bases of dwelling, and various dimensions.
In various kalpas and aeons, with various boundaries, various mountains and seas, various great earths,
various cloud-canopies, various names, and various appearances of Buddhas,
they manifest various great supernatural powers within various great assemblies and expound various sūtras at various sites of enlightenment.
He establishes various teachings of the vehicles, opens various gates of expedient means, radiates various wheels of light,
adorns various Buddha-worlds, and institutes various methods of consecration.

Furthermore, within each and every pore of the Bodhisattva, in every moment of thought, one constantly beholds boundless oceans of Buddhas in the ten directions, seated upon various sites of enlightenment, manifesting various supernatural transformations, turning various wheels of Dharma, and preaching various sūtras, in continuous succession without ever ceasing.

Furthermore, within every single pore of the Bodhisattva, in every thought-moment, they constantly perceive the oceans of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions—their various dwellings, various forms, various modes of conduct, various activities, various faculties, and various mental capacities.

Furthermore, within each and every pore of the Bodhisattva, one sees the oceans of all Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time, their infinite and boundless gateways of practice, their infinite and boundless oceans of great vows, their infinite and boundless Bodhisattva stages, their infinite and boundless perfections, their infinite and boundless accounts of past lives, their infinite and boundless practices for adorning lands, their infinite and boundless gateways of great kindness, their infinite and boundless clouds of great compassion, their infinite and boundless oceans of diligence, and their infinite and boundless minds of great joy; in every thought-moment, they gather in boundless sentient beings through skillful means to subdue them, causing them all to reach maturity.
“Good son! For as many eons as there are atoms in those Buddha-fields, in every thought-moment I have thus observed all the realms within each and every pore of the Bodhisattva;
places already traversed were not traversed again, and places already seen were not seen again.”
What he had already heard, he did not hear again;
what he had already attained, he did not attain again;
even until he saw Prince Siddhārtha within the inner palace, surrounded by court ladies.

By the power of my liberation, I observe each and every pore of the Bodhisattva and see that all dharma-realms of the three periods of time are boundless; their spheres of activity penetrate deeply into the infinite.

"Good son! I have attained only this liberation door of observing the subtle realm of the great ocean of samādhis of bodhisattvas. As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they are able to fully accomplish oceans of skillful means and so forth for all sentient beings; they manifest bodies according to their types and dwell before all sentient beings, expounding the various teachings of the vehicles according to the diverse faculties and natures of those beings."

From every single pore, they are able to produce infinite oceans of clouds of manifested forms and appearances; they know that all phenomena are fundamentally pure, having non-existence as their very nature; they know that all sentient beings are identical to space, having signlessness as their characteristic; they abide in non-discriminative, ultimate liberation, manifesting a vast realm without center or periphery;

they know that the Buddha’s spiritual power is ultimately suchness (*tathatā*), and are able to universally manifest spiritual transformations in accordance with great vows; in a single thought-moment, they can enter the vast Dharma-realm, causing all phenomena to revolve according to their mastery;

they attain the universal gate of wisdom regarding all phenomena, are able to sport freely through all the bodhisattva stages, remain far removed from all afflictions and fetters, and obtain pure, perfect wisdom and supernormal powers.

Knowing that all sentient beings are ultimately quiescent, they manifest bodies everywhere to bring joy to all; they share a single, equal object of focus with all bodhisattvas, constantly gathering together and never parting.

Having attained great supernormal powers, they are ultimately non-regressive; they travel freely through all worlds, manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment in accordance with the needs of sentient beings, sitting universally in the assemblies of all sites of enlightenment, and manifesting birth throughout all realms of existence.

Riding upon the wheel of non-retrogression, they practice the conduct of a bodhisattva; those who see or hear them gain benefit as from the king of medicinal trees, fulfilling the hearts of sentient beings like a wish-fulfilling jewel; with a single voice they universally proclaim the Dharma, causing all to rejoice.

Regarding the ground of great wisdom, all phenomena are established therein; through the supernatural power of the illusion of wisdom, it pervades the entire Dharma-realm. How could I possibly know or describe such meritorious virtues of the bodhisattva’s practice of wisdom?
At that time, the Śākya maiden Gopā said to Sudhana: "Noble son!

In this world, there is a great lion throne made of Vairocana-maṇi-jewel lotus-blossoms upon which the Buddha’s mother, Māyā, is seated. Go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva practices so as to remain unstained by any worldly realms?'"
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of mastery so as to remain free from dust and defilement amidst all phenomena?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of faith and joy so as to serve and attend upon all Buddhas constantly without weariness or rest?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of courageous progress and accomplish all the activities of a bodhisattva?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of pure wisdom and remain far removed from all afflictions and obstacles?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of profound understanding, such that upon hearing the Dharma, they naturally achieve awakening?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of presence, thereby accomplishing the wisdom of a bodhisattva’s discernment?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of omnipresence, so as to go everywhere to the abodes of all Tathāgatas?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of great vows, so as to universally encompass the realms of all sentient beings?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of non-retrogression, so as to cultivate the bodhisattva practices throughout all future kalpas?
How does a bodhisattva attain the power of observation, so as to see all phenomena without any obstruction?
How does a bodhisattva enter the wisdom of dependent origination and perceive that all phenomena are entirely devoid of a self?
How does a bodhisattva attain the wisdom of conformity and skillfully understand all mundane and supramundane phenomena?
How does a bodhisattva attain subtle wisdom and skillfully observe the essential nature of all phenomena?
How does a bodhisattva attain the wisdom of supernormal powers and proclaim the various secrets for the sake of sentient beings?
How does a bodhisattva give rise to great vows so as to increase the roots of goodness of all sentient beings without ever ceasing?
How does a bodhisattva draw near to, serve, and attend upon all buddhas and bodhisattvas, as well as all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, constantly and without interruption?
At that time, the Śākya maiden Gopā, wishing to further proclaim the meaning of this gate of liberation, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, spoke these verses to Sudhana:
"If there are sentient beings who see a Bodhisattva Cultivating and accumulating various practices for enlightenment,
Whether they give rise to unwholesome or wholesome thoughts, The Bodhisattva gathers them all in to bring them benefit."
In the past, there were as many eons as there are atoms in a hundred buddha-fields, and even more than that number of dust motes;
in those times, there was an eon named Equal Pure Adornment, and a field named Supreme Sumeru Light.
In that kalpa, thirty-six billion nayutas of Buddhas appeared in the world;
the last to appear was the Teacher of Gods and Humans, named Dharmadhvaja, the Lamp of the World.
At that time, after that Buddha had entered nirvana, there was a king named Jñānatejorājaśikhin who ruled over Jambudvīpa with sovereign power and was able to crush all his enemies.
At that time, the king had five hundred sons, handsome and valiant, invincible to all;
their wisdom, talent, and skillfulness all surpassed those of men, such that sentient beings gazed upon them without ever tiring.
That king and his son were pure in heart; they conceived deep faith in the Buddha’s Dharma, upholding, protecting, and practicing it with courageous diligence that never faltered.
At that time, the prince was named Jvālāprabha; adorned with the thirty-two marks of excellence, his stainless merits were all perfected, and he was well able to benefit all living beings.
Together with his five billion followers, he heard the Dharma, left the household life, and practiced the Way;
all cultivated the pure conduct with diligent effort, valiantly upholding the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, there was a royal capital named Jñānavṛkṣa (Wisdom Tree), surrounded by a full billion cities;
it possessed a forest named Śāntamahāśrī (Tranquil Great Auspiciousness), adorned with jewel trees, all of them most excellent and wondrous.
The son of the Buddha Jvālāprabha dwells therein, Proclaiming the Buddha’s true Dharma for the sake of the multitudes;
His eloquence and wisdom are inexhaustible, Causing all who hear it to eliminate their afflictions.
At times, when the Bodhisattva went forth to beg for alms, he would take up his robe and bowl and enter the royal city;
his deportment was tranquil and his gait composed, as he gazed steadily with right observation and an undisturbed mind.
At that time, in that city, there was an elder named Saṃkīrtitānandaketu;
while I was still a young girl living at home, my name was Vimalasūryaprabhāsaśrī.
At that time, I saw from afar this son of the Buddha, whose mindfulness and wisdom were pure and ever-present;
his faculties were well-subdued and his appearance was dignified and serene, and all his deportment was tranquil.
Next, he went for alms and arrived at my door; upon seeing him, I immediately felt a sense of attachment.
I untied the necklaces and ornaments adorning my body and joyfully offered them, along with a pearl, into his bowl.
Although at that time I made offerings with a mind of defiled attachment, because I served the true son of the Buddha,
Jyotiṣprabha, I did not pass through the three evil realms, but was constantly reborn among gods and humans.
Throughout two hundred and fifty great kalpas, wherever she was born as a woman, she was always preeminent;
she constantly beheld the place where Flame-Light practiced and studied, her body adorned with the marks of excellence and free from defilement.
After those two hundred and fifty kalpas had passed, she was next born into the family of the mother of Bhadrapāla;
as a young girl, her appearance was upright and dignified, and her name was Mañjuśrī, endowed with radiant beauty.
Beholding that Crown Prince, the Lord of Majestic Virtue, he gave rise to a heart of reverence, love, and respect;
wishing to serve him and practice together, he was fortunately accepted due to his past causes.
At that time, I followed the Prince and together went to the Tathāgata of Victorious Solar Body;
there I immediately gave rise to the vast mind of bodhicitta, making offerings and hearing the Dharma with joy.
All the Buddhas who appeared in that kalpa— sixty thousand koṭis of nayutas—
the last Buddha being named Liberation Light— I made offerings to them all in succession.
In the presence of that final Tathāgata, he attained a mind purified by awakening;
observing that the nature of all phenomena is without arising, he perfected his recollection of past lives and eliminated all afflictions.
They immediately attain the ocean of bodhisattva samādhis, Observing the subtle gates of liberation;
In a single thought-moment, they can enter The inconceivable oceans of lands throughout the ten directions.
Universally beholding all worlds, whether they be defiled or pure,
one feels no aversion toward the defiled lands and no attachment to the pure lands.
I see all the oceans of lands throughout the ten directions, And all the sites of enlightenment in every world;
The Tathāgatas sit everywhere, radiating light— All of this I am able to comprehend in a single thought-instant.
The ocean-like assemblies of that Buddha, I am able to enter them all in a single thought;
I also know the practices cultivated by those assemblies, as well as their powers of samādhi, liberation, and supernormal faculties.
All the vast practices of those assemblies, The various stages, perfections, and skillful means,
And their boundless oceans of vows— In every thought-moment, I enter deeply into them all.
I contemplate the marks and signs of the Bodhisattva’s body;
within each and every pore, the miraculous deeds performed throughout kalpas of practicing all wondrous conducts cannot have their limits found.
Within each and every pore are lands beyond description and measure;
therein, the wheels of earth, water, fire, and wind are held with subtle precision, without intermingling.
The worlds therein are established with forms, dimensions, names, and essences all distinct;
within those lands, the bodies of various sentient beings possess infinite colors, marks, and adornments.
Furthermore, by the power of this liberation, I see entirely the oceans of lands in the ten directions;
Buddhas manifest transformations that fill them all, taming every realm of sentient beings.
Though they have practiced for immeasurable eons and witnessed the supernatural powers of those Buddhas,
they still cannot know the path traversed by this bodhisattva’s body, mind, and wisdom.

At that time, having heard this Dharma, the youth Sudhana prostrated at Gopā’s feet, circumambulated her hundreds of thousands of times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and departed with a mind full of longing and single-minded attachment.
The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Scroll Twenty-Nine;
The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Scroll Thirty.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.

In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation," at that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded intent, desired to go and approach the Buddha’s mother, Lady Māyā; immediately, he attained the boundless right knowledge that minutely observes the realms of all Buddhas.
He formed this thought:
"By what skillful means may I come to see this spiritual friend?

This spiritual friend is far removed from the world, dwelling in non-dwelling, transcending the six sense bases, free from all attachments, unstained by the mire of desire, abiding in the unobstructed path, knowing reality as it is, and possessing the pure Dharma-body."

They manifest transformation bodies through karma that is like an illusion; they observe the world with wisdom that is like an illusion; they manifest form bodies through vows that are like an illusion; and they empower themselves through the majestic power of the Buddhas.
This spiritual friend possesses a body born at will;

This spiritual friend possesses a body that is without birth or cessation, a body without coming or going, a body that is neither empty nor real, a body that does not change or decay, a body without arising or ending, an inconceivable body, a body whose all characteristics are but a single characteristic, a body that dwells in liberation having distanced itself from the two extremes, a body without a place of dependence, an inexhaustible body, a body that manifests universally like a shadow yet is free from discrimination, a body that transcends discursive thought and investigation like what is seen in a dream, a body that neither enters nor exits like a reflection in a mirror, a body that manifests transformations throughout the ten directions, a body that remains unchanged throughout the three periods of time, a body that is neither mind nor form, and a body without differentiation. The conduct of this spiritual friend is unimpeded, like space; it transcends the range of all worldly vision and is visible only to the pure eyes of Samantabhadra.
How may I now draw near to such a person, serve and make offerings to them so as to bring them joy?
How may I dwell together with them and observe their appearance?
While staying among that assembly, how can one listen to their voices,
contemplate their speech, and receive their instructions?
At the moment the youth Sudhana had this thought, there was a city-ruling goddess named Ratnanetra.
Surrounded by a retinue of deities from the City of Immeasurability, they manifested their forms in the midst of the sky, adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments;

each manifesting immeasurable and extraordinary physical bodies, they held in their hands immeasurable celestial jewel-flowers and scattered them over Sudhana with a heart of reverence, speaking these words:
"O noble son!..."
You should skillfully guard the city of the mind, which means not being covetous of any realm of birth and death;
you should adorn the city of the mind, which means observing and seeking the ten powers of the Tathāgata;
you should purify the city of the mind, which means ultimately remaining far removed from stinginess, envy, flattery, and deception.
One should purify the city of the mind, which means contemplating the true nature of all phenomena;
one should expand the city of the mind, which means accomplishing all factors conducive to enlightenment through great diligence;
one should adorn the city of the mind, which means establishing the palaces of mastery over all meditative concentrations and liberations.
One should illuminate the city of the mind, which means universally entering the bodhimanda of all Tathāgatas to hear and receive the Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā;
one should augment the city of the mind, which means being universally able to give birth to the ocean of all skillful means of the Tathāgatas;
one should fortify the city of the mind, which means constantly and diligently practicing and increasing the pure vows and conduct of Samantabhadra.
One should guard the city of the mind, meaning one is always able to repel the afflictions, evil associates, and all the armies of Māra;
one should clear and illuminate the city of the mind, meaning one opens the way for the universal wisdom-light of all Buddhas;
one should skillfully repair the city of the mind, meaning one receives and upholds the nectar-like Dharma rain of all Buddhas.
One should support the city of the mind, which means having deep faith in the ocean of all Buddhas' merits;
one should expand the city of the mind, which means that great compassion pervades all worlds;
one should universally cover the city of the mind, which means gathering all wholesome dharmas to cover it from above.
One should broaden the city of the mind, which means to feel great compassion and pity for all sentient beings;
one should open the city of the mind, which means to relinquish all that one possesses and bestow gifts upon all sentient beings as appropriate;
one should closely guard the city of the mind, which means to prevent the realms of evil desires pertaining to birth and death from entering.
One should fortify the city of the mind by severing all unwholesome dharmas, which are the root of saṃsāra;
one should stabilize the city of the mind by gathering all the factors conducive to the path to omniscience, never regressing;
and one should establish the city of the mind by maintaining right mindfulness of the perfect realm of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
One should purify the city of the mind, which means clearly understanding all the wheels of Dharma of the Tathāgatas and all the Dharma-gates contained within the sūtras;

one should partition the city of the mind, which means being able to universally instruct and reveal [the truth] to all sentient beings, causing them all to perceive the path to *sarvajñatā* (omniscience);
one should maintain the city of the mind, which means universally encompassing the ocean of great vows of all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
One should cause the city of the mind to be rich and full, meaning to accumulate the vast mass of merit and wisdom that pervades the entire dharma-realm;
one should cause the city of the mind to be clear and lucid, meaning to universally know the faculties, inclinations, afflictions, and other dharmas of all sentient beings;
one should cause the city of the mind to be sovereign, meaning to universally encompass all the ten directions of the dharma-realm.
One should cause the city of the mind to be pure, which means maintaining right mindfulness of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
one should know the intrinsic nature of the city of the mind, which means knowing that all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature;
one should know the city of the mind to be like an illusion, which means comprehending the nature of all phenomena through omniscience.

“Good son! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can thus purify the city of the mind, they will be able to accumulate all roots of goodness and, according to their practice, will be able to realize and enter them all.”
Why is this? Because it eliminates all obstacles and difficulties, namely:

the obstacle to seeing the Buddha; the obstacle to hearing the Dharma; the obstacle to approaching and making offerings to the Tathāgatas; the obstacle to employing skillful means to gather in sentient beings; and the obstacle to adorning and purifying various Buddha-lands.

"Good son! Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva is free from such obstacles and difficulties, if they give rise to the aspiration to seek a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), they will see one without effort, and shall eventually attain all-knowledge (sarvajñatā)."
At that time, there were two body-host deities named Padmaśrī and Supuṣpābhāsa, surrounded before and behind by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of body-host deities;
emerging from the site of enlightenment, they remained in mid-air and, before Sudhana, praised Lady Māyā with various sublime voices.
At that time, the various hosts of deities each emitted from their ear-ornaments a light of nets of flames made of pure, multicolored jewels;
they emitted a light of clouds and nets of fragrant flames of various jewels in immeasurable colors; they emitted a light of nets of stainless and pure flames in immeasurable colors;
and they emitted a light in immeasurable colors capable of universally revealing the minds of sentient beings.
The nature is pure and luminous, emitting immeasurable colors of light that swiftly increase the radiance of joyful love;
emitting immeasurable colors of light that can remove the heat of affliction and bring cooling relief; emitting immeasurable colors of light that can universally manifest pure illumination;
and emitting immeasurable colors of jewel-flame light that courageously appears within the realm of non-attachment.
Then, Mañjuśrī emitted such various and manifold great nets of light in all colors,
which universally illumined boundless and vast Buddha-fields, enabling Sudhana to see all the Buddhas present in every land throughout the ten directions.

Those rays of light circled the world to the right; after completing one circuit, they returned and entered the crown of Sudhana’s head, eventually pervading all the pores of his body. Because Sudhana the youth was thus illuminated by these rays of light, he immediately attained ten kinds of Dharma-eye.
They are as follows:
he attained the eye of pure radiance, because he was forever free from the darkness of all ignorance;...
They attain the eye free from cataracts, because they are able to comprehend the nature of all sentient beings;
they attain the stainless eye, because they are able to contemplate the gateways to the nature of all phenomena;
they attain the pure wisdom-eye, because they are able to contemplate the nature of all buddha-fields.
They attain the eye of Vairocana, for they are able to see the pure Dharma-body of the Tathāgata;
they attain the eye of universal radiance, for they see the Buddha’s impartial and inconceivable body of wondrous form;
they attain the eye of unimpeded light, for they observe the signs of formation and destruction within all boundless oceans of lands.
They attain the eye of universal illumination, seeing all Buddhas arise great skillful means and turn the wheel of the true Dharma, thereby giving birth to various sūtras;
they attain the eye of universal realms, seeing the supernatural powers and majestic virtue of immeasurable Buddhas as they subdue all sentient beings;
they attain the eye of universal vision, observing the appearance of all Tathāgatas in the world throughout all various lands.

At that time, there was a rākṣasa king named Wondrous Eye (Sudarśana), who guarded the Dharma Hall of the Bodhisattvas; together with his retinue of ten thousand rākṣasas, he stood in the sky and scattered divine kusuma flowers—lovely and exquisite—and various wonderful incenses over Sudhana.
He spoke these words:
"Good son! When a bodhisattva is fully endowed with ten dharmas, they will be able to draw near to spiritual friends."
What are the ten? They are:
being free from all flattery and deception, because their mind is honest and straightforward, and is always pure;
They are free from all conceptual discrimination because they universally embrace all sentient beings with impartial great compassion;
they awaken to the self-nature of phenomena because they know that the nature of sentient beings lacks any reality;
and they know there is no coming or going because their resolve for omniscience never regresses.
Possessing the power of faith and understanding, because they universally enter the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas;
having attained the eye of pure wisdom, because they comprehend that the nature of all phenomena is non-arising;
abiding in impartial compassion, because they cause all sentient beings everywhere to attain the ultimate truth.
They open the light of wisdom, for they can clear away all delusive objects within their own minds;
they act as clouds of coolness, raining down nectar to wash away afflictions;
and they serve as vast eyes, penetratingly discerning all phenomena, for their minds always accord with spiritual friends.
If bodhisattvas are fully endowed with these ten dharmas, they will be able to draw near to spiritual friends.
Furthermore, son of good family!
When Bodhisattvas achieve ten kinds of samādhi, they constantly perceive all spiritual friends through subtle observation.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The samādhi of the pure wheel of the inexhaustible emptiness of phenomena;
the samādhi of manifestly beholding the oceans of all Buddha-fields in the ten directions;
and the samādhi of never abandoning or lacking any of the various spheres of experience.
The samādhi of universally beholding the manifestation of all Tathāgatas;
the samādhi of universally gathering the ocean-treasury of all merit and wisdom;
and the samādhi of never abandoning spiritual friends with one's mind.
The samādhi of constantly recollecting that the merits of all Tathāgatas arise from spiritual friends;
the samādhi of recollecting never abandoning spiritual friends;
and the samādhi of recollecting always remaining close to, and making equal offerings to, all spiritual friends.
Within the skillful practice of attending upon spiritual friends, one’s body knows no weariness and the mind knows no satiety; this is the samādhi that is free from all faults. Good son!
When a bodhisattva accomplishes these thirteen samādhis, they constantly gain proximity to all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).

Furthermore, they attain the samādhi of the spiritual friend who constantly turns the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; having attained this samādhi, they fully know that the essential nature of all Buddhas is equal and pervasive in all places, and they constantly encounter all spiritual friends.
When these words were spoken, the youth Sudhana looked up into the sky and replied to him, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
Out of compassion and for the sake of gathering me in, you have revealed various doors of skillful means, enabling me to see a true spiritual friend.
I pray that you will explain this to me in detail:
how may I go to the place where the spiritual friend dwells?
"In which direction, in which city, or in which village should one seek a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)?
By what means can one draw near to such spiritual friends?
The rākṣasa replied:
“Good son! You should humbly prostrate yourself everywhere throughout the ten directions, seeking spiritual friends within all realms as far as the limits of space;
you should act with courageous mastery, traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions to seek spiritual friends.”
"Give rise to a mind of swift diligence; give rise to a mind of compliance as you seek a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra);
observe the body and mind as being like a shadow or a dream as you seek a spiritual friend.
At that time, Sudhana, having received the instructions of the rākṣasī, practiced in accordance with them, and immediately beheld a great jewel lotus springing forth from the earth.

Its stem is of vajra, its leaves are of mani, and its pedestal is made of the Vairocana Jewel King; it has a treasury of mani jewel kings that manifest the ocean of sentient beings, and its filaments are of various colored precious incenses, all covered above by countless jeweled nets.
Upon that terrace was a multi-storied pavilion named "Treasury Containing the Dharma Realms of the Ten Directions," adorned with all manner of wondrous marvels;

its floor was made of vajra, its thousand pillars were arranged in rows, and everything was fashioned from maṇi jewels. Its walls were made of Jāmbūnada gold, with various precious necklaces hanging down on all four sides, and great maṇi banners of diverse jewel colors were distributed in rows, providing universal adornment. It was further embellished on all sides by countless exquisite jeweled steps and railings.

Within that pavilion was a lotus throne made of the king of wish-fulfilling jewels, adorned with various kinds of precious gems. It was surrounded on all sides by exquisite jewel railings, decorated with alternating rows of star-bannered *maṇi* kings. Various colored jeweled garments were spread both inside and out; jeweled canopies and nets hung with clusters of precious bells covered it from above, while jeweled silk banners dangled everywhere, their light streaming and their sounds resonating as they were stirred by a gentle breeze.

From within the jeweled flower-banners fell a rain of many wonderful flowers; from the jeweled bells and chimes issued beautiful sounds; from between the jeweled doors and windows hung various necklaces, and from within the *maṇi* bodies flowed scented water.
From the mouth of the Vairocana-jewel elephant issued a lattice of lotus flowers.
The lion-thrones of various colored vajra-jewels emit clouds of exquisite fragrances;
the forms of Brahmā deities, adorned with various wondrous jewel-wheels, produce sounds according to all desires and proclaim the teachings of great compassion;
and the vajra-jewel bells produce the sounds of the great vows of all bodhisattvas.
From within the Jewel Moon Banner, emanated forms of the Buddha emerged in continuous succession;
the Pure Treasury Jewel King manifested the sequence of births of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
and the Sun Treasury Maṇi emitted great radiance, universally illuminating all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions.
The Universal Radiance Mani Jewel King emits the perfect light of all Buddhas;
the Vairocana Mani Jewel King raises clouds of offerings to worship all Tathāgatas;
and the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel King manifests the spiritual transformations of Samantabhadra in every thought-moment, filling the entire Dharma-realm.

From the precious king Sumeru emerge celestial palaces, universally manifesting clouds of transformation bodies of all the hosts of Śakra-devānām-indra; the various exquisite voices of the celestial maidens sing praises of the Tathāgata’s inconceivable and subtle merits.

At that time, Sudhana saw such a seat, surrounded on all sides by immeasurable and inconceivable numbers of jewel-adorned seats. Upon that seat sat Lady Māyā, manifesting a pure form-body before all the assembled beings. That is to say:
she manifested a form-body that transcends the three realms, for she has already emerged from all states of existence;
she manifested a form-body that accords with the inclinations of the mind, for she is unattached to any worldly realm.
The universally pervasive form-body, because it is equal in number to all sentient beings;
the form-body of vast power, because it causes all sentient beings to possess merit and virtue;
the incomparable form-body, because it causes all sentient beings to eliminate inverted views.
The body of immeasurable forms, because it manifests in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
the body of boundless marks, because it universally manifests the marks that subdue sentient beings;
the body of universal manifestation, because it manifests through great mastery.
The body that transforms all forms, because it manifests before beings according to what is appropriate for them;
the body that constantly manifests, because it is inexhaustible throughout the entire realm of sentient beings;
the body of abiding bliss, because those who approach, see, or hear it attain peace and happiness.
The physical body that is never exhausted, because it ultimately perceives all things universally as being like space;
the physical body of great majestic power, because it eliminates the false dharmas of sentient beings;
the physical body that has no departure, because it does not cease within any realm of existence.
The form-body has no coming, for it does not emerge from any world;
it is an unborn form-body, for there is no origination;
it is an undestroyed form-body, for it is eternally quiescent.
It is not a substantial body of form, because it is attained through suchness;
it is not an insubstantial body of form, because it manifests in accordance with the world;
it is an immovable body of form, because it is forever free from arising and ceasing.
The indestructible body of form, because the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is indestructible;
the signless body of form, because the path of language is severed;
the single-marked body of form, because signlessness is its mark.
The form-body is like a reflected image, for it manifests in accordance with the mind;
it is like an illusory form, for it is produced by illusory wisdom;
it is like a mirage, for it is sustained solely by conceptualization.
The form-body is like a shadow, for it manifests in birth according to vows;
the form-body is like a dream, for it appears in accordance with the mind;
the form-body is the dharma-realm, for its nature is pure like space.
The body of great compassion, because it constantly protects all sentient beings;
the unimpeded body, because it pervades the entire dharma-realm;
the boundless body, because it universally purifies all sentient beings.
The immeasurable form-body, because it transcends verbal expression;
the non-abiding form-body, because it tames sentient beings;
the non-reliant form-body, because it vows to deliver the world.
The form-body without location, because it constantly transforms sentient beings;
the form-body without birth, because it is accomplished through illusory vows;
the form-body without superior, because it transcends all worlds.
The body of reality as it is, because it is manifested by a concentrated mind;
the non-arising body, because it appears in accordance with the karma of sentient beings;
the wish-fulfilling gem body, because it universally fulfills the aspirations of all sentient beings.
The non-conceptual body, because it arises solely in accordance with the aspirations of sentient beings;
the body free from conceptualization, because no sentient beings can know it;
the body free from falsehood, because it is forever detached from the provisional dharmas of sentient beings.
The eternal and inexhaustible body, because it reaches the limit of birth and death for all sentient beings;
the pure body, because it is non-discriminative like that of the Tathāgata.
When the youth Sudhana beheld Māyādevī, he saw that all these manifested bodies were ultimately not form, for all their physical characteristics were like reflections.
Ultimately it is not sensation, for all worldly sensations have been transformed and extinguished;
ultimately it is not perception, for it manifests only in accordance with the perceptions of sentient beings;
ultimately it is not volitional formations, for it is accomplished by depending on karma that is like an illusion.
Ultimately it is not consciousness, because the bodhisattva’s vow-knowledge is empty and devoid of intrinsic nature;
because all worldly speech has been severed;
and because the various fevers and afflictions of birth and death have been extinguished.
Because she dwells in the body of supreme, most peaceful extinction (*parama-śānti-nirvāṇa-kāya*).

At that time, the youth Sudhana again beheld Lady Māyā manifesting, according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, various female forms—both those belonging to the world and those transcending the world—with sovereign freedom, just like all worldly beings.

That is to say: they may manifest in the form of a māra-maiden; or manifest in the form of a goddess from the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations (Paranirmita-vaśavartin); or manifest in the form of a goddess from the Heaven of Delighting in Transformations (Nirmāṇarati); or manifest in the form of a goddess from Tuṣita Heaven; or manifest in the form of a goddess from Yāma Heaven; or manifest in the form of a goddess from Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; or manifest in the form of a goddess from the Heaven of the Four Great Kings; or manifest in the forms of female nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
In all places, they manifest such similar female bodies as well as bodies that transcend them, thereby benefiting sentient beings.
Gathering all-knowledge, they practice the pāramitā of giving with equanimity; their great compassion universally covers all worlds, giving birth to the immeasurable merits of the Tathāgata;

they cultivate and increase the wisdom of all-knowledge, observing and contemplating the true nature of all phenomena, attaining the ocean of profound patience; with diligent and rapid effort, never wearying or resting, they constantly turn the pure, non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma;
they subtly and thoroughly understand the nature of all phenomena, abiding in the realm of the samādhi of equality.
They attain the perfect radiance of the Tathāgata’s samādhi, which dries up the vast ocean of sentient beings’ afflictions;

they skillfully understand all Buddha-dharmas and constantly contemplate the true reality of phenomena with wisdom; they behold all Tathāgatas without ever feeling weary or satisfied; they know the sequence of the appearance of Buddhas throughout the three periods of time; the Buddha-samādhis are always manifest before them; they universally gather immeasurable paths of purity; they traverse the space-like realm of all Buddhas; according to the inclinations of sentient beings, they universally gather and sustain them, maturing them through various skillful means;

they enter the immeasurable, pure Dharma-body of the Buddhas, fulfill great vows, purify all Buddha-lands, and ultimately subdue all sentient beings; their minds constantly and universally enter the realms of all Buddhas, giving rise to all the spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas.
Having already attained the Dharma-body, pure and untainted, they constantly manifest immeasurable form-bodies;

they sport in the various sovereign powers of the Tathāgatas, subduing the power of Māra’s enmity, accomplishing the power of roots of goodness, giving birth to the power of the True Dharma, and being fully endowed with the powers of all Buddhas. They attain the sovereign power of all Bodhisattvas and swiftly increase the power of omniscience.

They attain the light of Buddha-wisdom that universally illumines all things, thoroughly knowing the various distinctions within the ocean-like minds, faculties, natures, and inclinations of immeasurable sentient beings. Their bodies fill the ocean of lands throughout the ten directions, and they also know the characteristics of the formation and destruction of all lands; with their vast eyes, they behold the oceans of the ten directions.
They know the ocean of the three periods of time through all-pervasive wisdom;
they universally serve the ocean of all Buddhas with their bodies;
and their minds constantly receive and uphold the ocean of all dharmas.

May I cultivate and perfect all the various merits of all Tathāgatas; may I accord with and give rise to all the bodhisattva wisdoms that assist the path; may I always delight in observing all the practices of the *pāramitās* undertaken by all bodhisattvas from their first resolve;

may I give birth to all the bodhisattva stages and accumulate all the masses of merit of all bodhisattvas; may I be courageous and diligent with a mind free from fear, universally accomplishing the path to enlightenment of all bodhisattvas; may I constantly and diligently protect all sentient beings; may I always delight in praising the merits of all Buddhas; may my radiance shine universally upon all worlds; and may I become the mother of all bodhisattvas.
At that time, the youth Sudhana saw Lady Māyā pervading all places, manifesting such gates of skillful means as are equal in number to the atoms within Jambudvīpa.

Having seen this, Sudhana manifested as many bodies as were manifested by Lady Māyā; in every place, before each Māyā, he paid respectful homage and immediately realized immeasurable and innumerable gateways of samādhi, discerning, observing, practicing, and entering them.
Rising from samādhi, he circumambulated Māyā and her retinue three times to the right, stood with palms joined, and said:
"O Great Sage!
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva has instructed me to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and to diligently seek out spiritual friends."
Receiving their instructions, I have gone to visit, attend upon, serve, and make offerings to each and every spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) without fail.

Thus, passing from one to another, I have gradually arrived here. I only pray that the Great Sage will proclaim for me how a bodhisattva should study the bodhisattva conduct so as to achieve the wisdom of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna).
Lady Māyā said to Sudhana: "Good son!
I have accomplished the bodhisattva liberation gate called 'The Adornment of the Magical Illusion of the Wisdom of Great Vows'; therefore, I am constantly the mother of all bodhisattvas."

"Good son! Just as I was born from the right side of Queen Māyā in the city of Kapilavastu within this Jambudvīpa, as Prince Siddhārtha, manifesting inconceivable and vast adornments through the sovereign spiritual transformations of a Bodhisattva’s birth;

even so, throughout this entire ocean of worlds, for all the Vairocana Tathāgatas dwelling in their final bodies and manifesting the sovereign spiritual transformations of birth, I have been the mother for each and every one of them."
All those bodhisattvas enter my body and are born from my right side, attaining all-knowledge.
Furthermore, noble son,

when the Bodhisattva was about to descend to be born in King Śuddhodana’s palace, I saw that every single pore of the Bodhisattva’s body emitted light called the "Wheel of Merit for the Birth of All Tathāgatas."

Within each and every one of his pores, there appeared the meritorious adornments of the spiritual transformations of birth undergone by as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
All those rays of light universally illumined all worlds; having illuminated the worlds, they entered the crown of my head and even into all the pores of my body.

“Good son! Furthermore, within that light, there are universally manifested the names of all bodhisattvas, as well as their vast adornments of the miraculous transformations of birth, their palaces, retinues, and their enjoyment of the five desires;

moreover, one sees bodhisattvas renouncing their thrones to leave the household life, proceeding to the site of enlightenment, and having vanquished the armies of Māra, attaining equal and perfect awakening; seated upon the lion throne, surrounded before and behind by various bodhisattvas, and attended and made offerings to by various world-ruling lords, they turn the wheel of the true Dharma for the great assembly.”

Furthermore, they saw all such matters as the Tathāgata’s past cultivation of the bodhisattva path: his honoring and making offerings to various Buddhas; his resolution to attain bodhicitta and purify buddha-fields; his manifestation of immeasurable transformation bodies in every thought-moment, pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions; his various displays of birth and adornment through emanations; his attainment of unexcelled enlightenment; his turning of the wondrous wheel of Dharma; and even his final manifestation of parinirvāṇa—all these great and divine transformations were seen by them without exception.
"Furthermore, noble son!
When that wondrous radiance entered my body, although the dimensions of my physical form did not exceed their original state, in reality I had already transcended all worlds."

Why is this? At that time, my body was equal in measure to empty space; within the womb, it could entirely accommodate the palaces of the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, due to the great supernormal power of sovereign birth and adornment.

"Good son! At that time, when the Bodhisattva was about to descend from the Tuṣita Heaven, there were bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields who surrounded him before and behind. All of them shared the same vows, the same conduct, the same roots of goodness, the same adornments, the same liberation, the same wisdom, the same dwelling on the stages, the same supernormal powers, the same manifestations, the same majestic power, the same purity of the dharma-body, and the same majesty of the form-body; indeed, they were entirely equal to him even in the merit, conduct, and vows of Samantabhadra."

Furthermore, there were eighty thousand great nāga kings, with Sāgara Nāgarāja as their leader, along with various world-protectors, each riding upon diverse mani-palatial towers, all coming together to attend upon, serve, and make offerings to him.

At that time, by means of his supernormal powers, the Bodhisattva universally manifested himself in all the Tuṣita palaces together with the other Bodhisattvas. Within each palace, he manifested the images of his taking birth within the Jambudvīpas of all worlds throughout the ten directions, displaying inconceivable and manifold miraculous transformations. He taught and tamed immeasurable sentient beings, causing them to awaken and refrain from negligence, to abandon all indolence, and to remain free from attachment.

Furthermore, by means of his supernormal power, he emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated the world, destroying all darkness, extinguishing all suffering and affliction, and liberating beings from the realms of desire. He caused all sentient beings to recognize all their karmic actions from past lives, so that they might forever emerge from the evil paths.

Moreover, for the sake of protecting and rescuing all sentient beings, he manifested various miraculous transformations before them, displaying such extraordinary and marvelous feats. Together with his retinue, he descended from the celestial palace and entered my body.
Those bodhisattvas manifest great supernatural powers within my womb, traveling with sovereign ease;
they may take a single step across a trichiliocosm, or even take a single step across as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields.

Furthermore, in every moment of thought, from worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields in the ten directions—wherein reside the assemblies of Bodhisattvas in the presence of all Tathāgatas, as well as the Four Heavenly Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods, and even the Brahmā kings of the Form Realm—all come desiring to behold the vast and great miraculous transformations of the Bodhisattva dwelling in the womb, to pay respectful homage and offerings, and to hear and receive the True Dharma; they all enter my body.

Although my belly can entirely contain such an assembly, my body neither becomes vast nor does it become cramped; each of those bodhisattvas perceives themselves as being situated within their own pure and magnificently adorned assembly hall and place of practice.
“Good son! Just as I was the mother for the Bodhisattva’s birth within this Jambudvīpa of the four continents,
it is exactly the same for all the Jambudvīpas within the four continents of the ten billion worlds throughout the trichiliocosm.”
However, this body of mine is fundamentally neither dual nor singular; it does not abide in a single place, nor does it abide in many places.
Why is this? Because I have cultivated the liberation door of the adornment of the illusory wisdom of the great vows of a bodhisattva.
"Good son! Just as I am now the mother of the World-Honored One Vairocana, so too was I the mother of all the immeasurable Buddhas of the past."

"Good son! In the past, I was once a deity of a lotus pond. At that time, a bodhisattva suddenly manifested by transformation within a lotus calyx; I immediately cradled him, attended to him, and nurtured him, so that all the world collectively called me the 'Mother of the Bodhisattva.

Furthermore, in the past, I was a deity of the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). At that time, a bodhisattva suddenly manifested by transformation within my womb; the world likewise called me the 'Mother of the Bodhisattva.'"

"Good son! All such immeasurable bodhisattvas dwelling in their final bodies, who manifest great supernormal transformations through various skillful means in this world regarding their taking of birth—I have been the mother of them all."

"Good son! Within this world during the Bhadrakalpa, when Krakucchanda Tathāgata, Kanakamuni Tathāgata, Kāśyapa Tathāgata, and now the present World-Honored One Śākyamuni Tathāgata first appeared and manifested birth, I was their mother."

At that time, the youth Sudhana said to Lady Māyā: "O Noble One!
How long has it been since you attained this bodhisattva liberation called 'the adornment of the magical illusion of the wisdom of great vows'?"
He replied: "Good son!

In the distant past, beyond an incalculable number of eons—beyond what can be known by the supernatural powers or the divine eye of a bodhisattva in their final birth—there was an eon named Pure Light, and a world named Sumeru Virtue."
Although there are various mountains and the five realms of existence dwell together therein, that land is free from all impurities and evils;
it is composed of various jewels, pure and perfect, adorned with lovely beauty.
Within that world-system, there are ten trillion sets of four continents.
There was a four-continent world-system named Fragrant Wind Majestic Lion Banner, within which were eight billion royal cities;
among them was a city named Supreme Endowed Banner,
where there was a wheel-turning king named Valiant Diligence Great Majesty.
To the north of that king’s city was a site of enlightenment named *Vicitra-varṇa-prabhā* (Light of Various Wondrous Colors);
the deity of that site was named *Śrī-netrā* (Auspicious Eye).

At that time, there was a bodhisattva named *Vimaladhvaja* (Stainless Banner) who sat at the site of enlightenment, about to achieve perfect awakening. Then an evil Māra named *Suvarṇaprabhā* (Golden Light), together with his retinue of immeasurable māra-armies in various forms, arrived at the bodhisattva’s location, intending to cause disruption and confusion.

That Wheel-Turning King, having already attained the sovereign power of a bodhisattva’s supernormal knowledges, manifested a great host of troops through his great spiritual transformations—many times greater in number than the enemy—to crush that demonic army. As they surrounded the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), all the demons were struck with terror and fled in every direction; thus, that bodhisattva was able to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, having witnessed these events, the deity of the site of enlightenment was filled with immeasurable joy and conceived the thought of the king as her own son.
She prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and made this vow:
"May this wheel-turning sage king of great majesty and virtue always be my son in every place where he is born; until he attains Buddhahood, may I always be his mother."
Having made this vow, he further encountered ten nayutas of buddhas at this very site of enlightenment, serving and making offerings to them so as to bring them joy.
“Good son! What do you think? Is that deity of the site of enlightenment anyone other than a person?”
I am that very person.
As for the Wheel-Turning King, he is now the World-Honored One, Vairocana Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.

Since I first made my vow before him, this Buddha, the World-Honored One, has been born in all realms throughout the lands of the ten directions; with courageous diligence, he has planted various roots of goodness, made offerings to Tathāgatas, cultivated the practices of a Bodhisattva, and taught and matured all sentient beings, even manifesting his dwelling in his final body. In every thought-moment, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, he manifests the miraculous transformations of a Bodhisattva’s birth, always being my son, while I have always been his mother.

"Good son! In the past and present, throughout the infinite worlds of the ten directions, whenever all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, were about to attain Buddhahood, they all emitted various kinds of vast and great light from their navels, which came to illuminate my body and the palaces where my retinue and I resided;
I served as the mother for them in their final births."
“Good son! I know only this bodhisattva liberation door called ‘the Adornment of the Illusory Wisdom of Great Vows.
As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possess the treasury of great compassion and, by means of all-knowledge, teach and discipline all sentient beings without ever becoming weary;”
Abiding in the practice of patience, they always know contentment;
partaking of the flavor of ambrosia, their minds are inexhaustible;
all Māras and evil persons cannot disturb them, for their minds are unshakable and without...
Light and agile, with a mind free from high or low, free from flattery and illusion, and free from the conduct of dense forests, they enter hundreds of thousands of samādhis in every thought-moment;
in every thought-moment they behold hundreds of thousands of Buddhas; in every thought-moment they realize the powers of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas;
in every thought-moment they can shake hundreds of thousands of worlds; and in every thought-moment they traverse hundreds of thousands [of lands].
In every thought-moment, he illuminates hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields; in every thought-moment, he brings to maturity hundreds of thousands of sentient beings;
in every thought-moment, he dwells with mastery for hundreds of thousands of eons; in every thought-moment, he deeply penetrates hundreds of thousands of past and future eons respectively;
in every thought-moment, he profoundly understands hundreds of thousands of Dharma-gates; and in every thought-moment, he manifests hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
In every thought-moment, his body manifests hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas as his retinue.

By the power of his mastery, in every thought-moment, he universally manifests within each and every pore the miraculous transformations of immeasurable Buddhas; regarding the Triple Gem, he has attained ultimate accomplishment and possesses indestructible, profound faith.

They are skillfully aware of the various stages of the arising and ceasing of all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*); they are skillfully aware of the nature of all phenomena as being fundamentally unarisen; they are skillfully aware of the various transformations, formations, and disintegrations of the world; they are skillfully aware of the distinctions in the births resulting from various karmas; they are skillfully aware of the various limits of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa; they are skillfully aware of the various differences between the defilement and purity of Buddha-fields; they are skillfully aware of the various practices cultivated by all bodhisattvas of the past and future; and they are skillfully aware that all phenomena are signless and inexhaustible. How then could I know or speak of the merits of the wisdom and conduct of those bodhisattvas?
"Good son! In this Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, there is a king named Samprajanyasampanna;
that king has a daughter named Devendraprabhā."
“Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.

At that time, the youth Sudhana respectfully received his instruction, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with deep affection and longing, gazed up at him with single-minded devotion before taking his leave and departing.

At that time, Sudhana, following the instructions of his spiritual friend, went at once to the palace of the Heavenly King Samantabhadra in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. There he saw the goddess, prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her, and stood before her with palms joined, saying: "Noble Lady!"
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice,
nor how one should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. The goddess replied, "Good son! "
"I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door of the pure adornment of unimpeded mindfulness.
Sudhana said, "Noble One!"
"What is the sphere of this gate of liberation?
By practicing what dharma does one attain this liberation?
The goddess replied:
“Good son! By diligently practicing immeasurable and inconceivable Dharma-gates, a bodhisattva attains this liberation.
If you wish to enter this gate of liberation, you should likewise practice and study with such diligent effort.”
How does one diligently cultivate the inconceivable dharma-gate?
It is as follows:
you should diligently cultivate the wisdom regarding the meanings of all inconceivable dharmas.
This means that one should awaken to all phenomena as they truly are—namely, their distinctions, their essential characteristics, and their true nature.
You should diligently cultivate the protection of the True Dharma;
that is, when various sublime teachings are slandered by others, you should refute them with reason and manifest the ultimate meaning.
You should diligently cultivate the discipline of manifest and unmanifest form;
that is to say, by minutely examining—whether natural or proscribed, with fault or without fault—that it remains free from any deficiency.
You should diligently cultivate the dharma of non-contention;
that is, you should always remain far removed from the various worldly, frivolous, and diverse forms of speech, as well as from unbeneficial assemblies.
You should diligently cultivate abiding in the stage of patience.
This means that because one can thoroughly examine and endure various forms of suffering that oppress both body and mind,
you should diligently cultivate patience toward all objects; that is,
by remaining unshaken in your inner mind and constantly practicing forbearance even when faced with abusive speech, insults, enmity, and malice.
You should diligently cultivate the understanding of subtle phenomena;

that is to say, you should know the aggregates, elements, and sense bases, as well as their arising and ceasing, because you have thoroughly realized that their essential nature and characteristics are unapprehendable.
"You should diligently cultivate the skillful phrases of the Dharma;
that is, you should be skillfully able to proclaim various Dharma gates so as to manifest their true nature and characteristics.
You should diligently cultivate the harmonious and the non-harmonious."
This means that one understands the nature of all phenomena to be unassailable, as it is devoid of increase or decrease, separation or union, and so forth.
You should diligently cultivate the wisdom that contemplates the past;
this means minutely observing the various causes of karma, such that there is nothing—whether virtuous or non-virtuous—that remains unknown.
You should diligently cultivate the wisdom that reaches the limits of the future;
that is to say, because you must minutely observe the various conditions of karma and be without ignorance regarding the characteristics of their retributions.
You should diligently cultivate the equality of the three periods of time.
This means that although the modes of activity across the three periods of time differ from one another, they do so only because there are distinctions among the phenomena that abide therein.
You should diligently cultivate the purity of the three spheres;
that is, because the nature of all phenomena—past, present, and future—is unapprehendable and transcends mind and intellect.
You should diligently cultivate the dharma of the mind’s abiding;
that is, by universally understanding that the characteristics and intrinsic nature of the mind—whether internal, external, or intermediate—are unapprehendable.
You should diligently cultivate the guarding of majestic deportment;
that is, by observing with subtle discernment at all times so that the actions of body, speech, and mind do not become deluded.
"You should diligently cultivate pure deportment;
that is to say, closely guarding the doors of the sense faculties, concealing wholesome qualities, and constantly confessing all unwholesome states.
You should diligently cultivate the abandonment of unwholesome dharmas."
This means that you should not dwell together with the various evil dharmas of foolish ordinary beings, but should instead remain constantly awakened;
you should diligently cultivate and accumulate the practices of a bodhisattva,
which means universally understanding and practicing all manner of heroic and strenuous deeds, including those that are difficult to perform.
You should diligently cultivate reverence for your elders and superiors;
that is to say, by providing seats, bedding, and requisites, attending to them, welcoming them, and remaining humble in body and mind without indolence.
You should diligently cultivate the gathering and maintenance of body and mind.
This means that one is able to universally uphold all pure dharmas, because they are constantly understood without being lost or destroyed.
You should diligently cultivate the wisdom that accords with awakening;
this means that regarding all mundane and supramundane dharmas, you awaken to them in accordance with their nature and characteristics.
You should diligently cultivate the entry into the profound Dharma;
that is, by thoroughly comprehending the characteristics of all phenomena subject to arising and ceasing, you cause the mind to increase in the wisdom of non-arising.
You should diligently cultivate the Dharma-wisdom of sounds.
This refers to expounding various dharma-gates as they truly are, in order to reveal the reality of all speech.
"You should diligently cultivate detachment from what is unbeneficial;
that is, by means of various skillful methods, you should cause both yourself and others to transcend all unbeneficial states of existence."
You should diligently cultivate the assembly of great beings;
that is, by drawing near to, serving, and constantly making offerings to all Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.
You should diligently cultivate the practice of distancing yourself from evil associates;
that is, by remaining far removed from those base beings who delight in giving rise to views of nihilism or eternalism, as well as those who are indolent and so forth.
You should diligently cultivate the practice of not relying on ordinary worldlings.
This means that one perceives the dharmas of ordinary beings as all being associated with ignorance due to their many faults;
therefore, you should diligently cultivate a mind of constant non-contempt.
This means that regarding all sentient beings, you should realize the equality of their nature and not give rise to feelings of disdain toward those who are poor or lowly.
You should diligently cultivate compassion for those who violate the precepts;
that is, by means of great loving-kindness and compassion, you should rescue those who have committed offenses and establish them within the pure morality of a bodhisattva.
You should diligently cultivate the increasing power of loving-kindness and compassion.
This means observing the sentient beings of the ten directions and the three periods of time, and being able to rescue and protect them from their various afflictions.
"You should diligently cultivate the gathering of wealth and Dharma;
that is, by gathering sentient beings through material goods and food and drink, you cause them to enter the profound and true Dharma."
You should diligently cultivate the practice of acting according to what has been taught;
that is, by cultivating various kinds of goodness to develop your own mind, so that it may become fully flourishing and perfect.
You should diligently cultivate the wholesome roots associated with the past.
This means that by seeking skill in the knowledge of past lives and being well-versed in the teachings, one is able to know the formations associated with the past; therefore,
you should diligently cultivate the joy of solitude and tranquility,
meaning you should distance yourself from the various idle conversations found in crowds and always delight in associating with pure and wholesome dharmas.
You should diligently cultivate fewness of desires and contentment;
that is to say, regarding clothing, food and drink, bedding, and medicine, you should personally practice and teach others to know moderation and sufficiency.
You should diligently cultivate the practices of yoga;
that is, you should constantly and diligently practice the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment so as to bring them into correspondence with your mind.
You should also diligently cultivate the spheres of activity of a bodhisattva.
This refers to the ten pāramitās as the gateway to all practices, which one must cultivate fully to bring them to perfection.
You should diligently practice the dharmas of the bodhisattva stages;
that is, you must realize and understand the characteristics of entering, abiding in, and emerging from the ten stages of wisdom, as well as the attainment of their fruits.
You should diligently cultivate the entry into the stage of a Tathāgata;
that is to say, because you shall realize the various essences and functions of both the wisdom of enlightenment and the obstacles to be abandoned.
You should diligently cultivate the dharmas that are difficult to comprehend.
This is because all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas fully understand the inconceivable.
You should diligently cultivate the non-apprehension of all marks;
that is, you should practice the awakening to the nature and characteristics of all phenomena as being like illusions, like dreams, and identical to the true mark (dharmatā).
"You should diligently cultivate the wisdom of the dharma of liberation;
that is, the vajra-samādhi which shatters the habitual tendencies of dust, because its tranquil wisdom is unmoving amidst delusive thoughts. Good son!"

There are inconceivable varieties of Dharma-gates, as numerous as the atoms within such Buddha-fields, which I have all diligently cultivated to attain this liberation; if you are able to practice them, you too shall likewise realize it.
"Good son! Regarding the realm of liberation you have just asked about, this realm of liberation of mine is boundless.
Furthermore, good son!"

By virtue of having attained this power of liberation, I recollect a past age; at that time there was an eon named Utpalā, and during that eon, I served and made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.

From the initial renunciation of the household life until those Tathāgatas reached the end of their Dharma, I have in every case gazed upon, protected, and made offerings to them; I have constructed monasteries and provided all necessary requisites.

Furthermore, from the time those Tathāgatas were Bodhisattvas entering their mothers’ wombs, at the time of their birth, when they took seven steps, when they uttered the lion’s roar, during their period as youths, while dwelling in the palace, when they grew weary of kingship and first left home, when they went to the Bodhi tree and attained perfect enlightenment, when they turned the wheel of the sublime Dharma, and when they manifested the spiritual transformations of a Buddha to teach, transform, and subdue all sentient beings—I have clearly remembered all such deeds performed throughout their careers, from their first aspiration to practice the Bodhisattva path until the exhaustion of the Dharma, without omission, always keeping them present before me, mindful and never forgetting.

Furthermore, I recall a past kalpa named Good Ground (*Sudhara*), during which kalpa I again encountered Buddhas, Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges Rivers, whom I served and made offerings to.
Furthermore, I recall an eon named Subhavyūha, during which I encountered as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as there are atoms in ten Buddha-worlds, whom I served and made offerings to.
