Although they cultivate the four formless absorptions, because of their great compassion, they do not abide in the dwelling place of those who dwell in the formless realm;
although they diligently cultivate calm abiding and insight, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, they do not realize the dwelling place of those who have attained liberation;
although they practice equanimity, because of their great compassion, they do not abandon any activity for transforming sentient beings—this is the dwelling place of such beings.
This is the dwelling place of those who, though contemplating emptiness, do not give rise to the view of emptiness;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing signlessness, constantly teach and transform sentient beings attached to signs;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing wishlessness, do not abandon any of the bodhi-related vows and practices.

Although he has attained mastery over all karma and afflictions, this is the dwelling place where he manifests conformity to karma and afflictions for the sake of teaching and maturing sentient beings;
although he is free from birth and death, this is the dwelling place where he manifests the experience of birth and death for the sake of transforming sentient beings;
although he has already transcended all realms of existence, this is the dwelling place where he manifests entry into those realms for the sake of transforming sentient beings.
This is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing loving-kindness, harbor no attachment toward sentient beings;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing compassion, harbor no grasping toward sentient beings;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing sympathetic joy, constantly regard suffering sentient beings with a heart of pity.
This is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing equanimity, do not abandon the work of benefiting others;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing the nine successive meditative attainments, do not weary of taking birth in the desire realm;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though knowing that all phenomena are without arising or ceasing, do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
This is the dwelling place of those who, though they enter the three gates of liberation, do not grasp at the liberation of the śrāvakas;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though they contemplate the four noble truths, do not abide in the holy fruits of the Lesser Vehicle;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though they contemplate profound dependent origination, do not abide in ultimate cessation. This is...
This is the dwelling place of those who, though practicing the Eightfold Noble Path, do not seek to transcend the world forever;
this is the dwelling place of those who, though transcending the stage of ordinary beings, do not fall into the stages of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas;

this is the dwelling place of those who, though contemplating the five aggregates of clinging, do not bring about the eternal extinction of the aggregates; this is the dwelling place of those who, though transcending...
This is the dwelling place of those who have emerged from the four māras yet do not discriminate among the realms of the māras;
it is the dwelling place of those who, though not attached to the six sense bases, do not eternally extinguish them;

it is the dwelling place of those who, though abiding in true thusness (*tathatā*), do not fall into the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); it is [the dwelling place of those who], though teaching all vehicles, yet...
This great celestial palace is the dwelling place of those who have abandoned the Mahāyāna;
it is the dwelling place of those who abide in all such immeasurable virtues.
At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms, gazed up with single-minded reverence, and spoke these verses:
"This is the pure wisdom of great compassion, The Honored Maitreya who benefits the world.
The eldest son of the Buddhas within the stage of consecration, He enters the realm of the Buddhas through contemplative reflection."
All the sons of the Buddhas of great renown, Dwelling in the liberation gate of the realm of great wisdom,
Wandering through the dharma-realm with minds free from attachment— This is the dwelling place of those who are peerless.
Generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom;
skillful means, vows, power, and supernormal knowledges—this is the dwelling place of those who are fully endowed with all such Mahāyāna perfections.
Your wisdom is as vast as space, universally knowing all phenomena of the three periods of time;
unimpeded, independent, and without grasping, you thoroughly understand the abodes of all beings in existence.
Skillfully understanding all phenomena, Which are without intrinsic nature, without arising, and without basis—
Like a bird flying through the sky with mastery, This is the dwelling place of fearlessness.
Having realized the true nature of the three poisons, one discerns that they arise falsely through causes and conditions;
yet, one does not seek liberation out of aversion toward them—this is the dwelling place of those who dwell in tranquility.
The three gates of liberation, the eightfold noble path, The aggregates, bases, elements, and dependent origination—
One who can contemplate all these without falling into quiescence Is the dwelling place of the skillful person.
The lands of the ten directions and all sentient beings, He observes them all with unimpeded wisdom;
Realizing their nature is entirely empty and free from discrimination— This is the dwelling place of the one who abides in tranquil extinction.
Universally traversing the dharma-realm without any obstruction, yet the nature of such practice cannot be apprehended;
like the wind moving through space, there is nowhere it travels—this is the dwelling place of those who are without dependence.

Beholding everywhere the multitudes of beings in the evil realms, suffering all manner of agonizing pains with no place of refuge, he emits the great light of compassion to utterly extinguish them; this is the dwelling place of the one who feels such pity.
Seeing all sentient beings have lost the right path, like those born blind treading a perilous road, he leads them into the city of liberation; this is the dwelling place of the Great Guide.

Seeing all sentient beings fallen into the net of Māra, constantly oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, and death, he brings them liberation and peace; this is the dwelling place of the valiant hero.
Seeing all sentient beings afflicted by the disease of delusion, he gives rise to a vast heart of compassion;
with the nectar-like medicine of wisdom, he eradicates it—this is the dwelling place of the Great King of Physicians.
Seeing all sentient beings in the ocean of existence, Sinking and drowning in distress, undergoing manifold sufferings, He rescues them with the great compassionate Dharma-ship;
This is the dwelling place of the one who skillfully ferries others across.
Seeing all sentient beings within the ocean of delusion, They are able to give rise to the wondrous jewel-mind of bodhicitta;
Entering therein to rescue and deliver them all— This is the dwelling place of the skillful fisherman.
With eyes of great compassion and constant vows, He universally observes all sentient beings;
Drawing them forth from the ocean of existence— This is the abode of the King of the Garuḍas.

Just as the sun and moon dwell in the void, illuminating the entire world without exception, so too is the radiance of the light of aspiration and wisdom; this is the dwelling place of those who illuminate the world.
For the sake of transforming a single sentient being, a bodhisattva remains throughout all future incalculable eons;
as it is for one person, so it is for all—this is the dwelling place of the Savior of the World.
Transforming sentient beings within a single buddha-field, without ceasing throughout all future kalpas;
as it is in one field, so it is in the ten directions—this is the dwelling place of the firm resolve.
The teachings proclaimed by all Buddhas of the ten directions, They receive in their entirety while seated upon a single seat;
Until the end of future kalpas, their resolve knows no weariness— This is the dwelling place of those who are oceans of wisdom.
Wandering through all oceans of worlds, universally entering all oceans of sites of enlightenment,
making offerings to all oceans of Tathāgatas— this is the dwelling place of the practitioner.
Practicing an ocean of all sublime conducts, Arousing an ocean of boundless great vows,
Passing through such oceans of many eons— This is the dwelling place of those who possess these merits.
Upon the tip of a single hair, there are immeasurable lands; Buddhas, sentient beings, and eons are beyond description.
Thus he perceives clearly and pervasively everywhere—this is the dwelling place of the unimpeded eye.
In a single thought-moment, they universally encompass boundless eons, The lands, the Buddhas, and all sentient beings;
The unimpeded pāramitās of merit and wisdom— This is the dwelling place of these virtuous ones.

If the Buddha-fields of the ten directions were ground into dust, and all the great oceans were measured by drops from a single hair, the number of vows made by Bodhisattvas would be thus; this is the dwelling place of those who are unimpeded.
Having accomplished the gates of dhāraṇī and samādhi, As well as great vows, all dhyānas, and liberations,
Abiding in each for boundless eons— This is the dwelling place of the true sons of the Buddha.
Innumerable and boundless sons of the Buddha, Teaching various dharmas to deliver sentient beings,
And also expounding the myriad arts and crafts of the world— This is the dwelling place of the practitioner.
Having accomplished the wisdom of skillful means regarding supernormal powers, they practice the wondrous Dharma-gate that is like an illusion;
manifesting births throughout the five destinies of the ten directions—this is the dwelling place of those who are unimpeded.
From the first moment the Bodhisattva resolves upon enlightenment, they fully practice all deeds;
manifesting infinite transformation bodies throughout the Dharma-realm—this is the dwelling place of those possessed of such spiritual power.

In a single thought, the path to enlightenment is accomplished; Universally performing boundless deeds of wisdom, The worldly mind’s deliberations go utterly mad— This is the dwelling place of those whose measure is unfathomable.
Having accomplished unimpeded supernormal powers, they travel throughout the dharma-realm without exception;
their minds never grasp at anything—this is the dwelling place of those with pure wisdom.
The Bodhisattva practices unimpeded wisdom, entering all lands without attachment;
with non-dual knowledge they illuminate everywhere—this is the dwelling place of those who are selfless.

The wisdom of equality that realizes the nature is like space; Primordially quiescent and without dependence, one constantly dwells within such a sphere— This is the abode of the person free from defilement.
Universally beholding all sentient beings undergoing manifold sufferings, they give rise to a mind of great compassion, benevolence, and wisdom;
vowing to constantly benefit all worlds—this is the dwelling place of those who possess such pity and mercy.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here universally manifest before all sentient beings;
like the orbs of the sun and moon, they everywhere dispel the darkness of birth and death.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here universally accord with the minds of sentient beings.
Manifesting immeasurable bodies, they fill the lands of the ten directions.
Abiding here, the sons of the Buddha travel throughout all worlds at the abodes of all Tathāgatas for immeasurable and innumerable eons.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here weigh and measure the realm of the Buddhas;
throughout immeasurable and innumerable eons, their minds never grow weary.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here enter samādhi in every thought-moment.
Each and every gate of samādhi Reveals and clarifies the realm of all Buddhas.
The Buddha-sons dwelling herein Completely know all lands,
Immeasurable and innumerable eons, And the names of sentient beings and Buddhas.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here, in a single thought-moment, encompass all kalpas;
they remain far removed from all delusive thoughts while remaining in accord with sentient beings.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here cultivate all samādhis.
Within each and every thought-moment, they thoroughly understand the phenomena of the three periods of time.
Abiding here, the sons of the Buddha sit with their bodies unmoving in the full lotus posture,
yet they manifest universally in all lands, benefiting sentient beings across all realms of existence.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here drink from the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas;
they enter deeply into the ocean of wisdom and are fully endowed with the ocean of merit.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here know completely the number of all buddha-fields.
The number of worlds, the number of sentient beings, and the inconceivable number of Buddhas—
dwelling here, the sons of the Buddha can comprehend them all in a single thought.
Within all three periods of time, they fully understand the formation and destruction of all lands.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here universally know the practices and vows of the Buddhas,
the conduct cultivated by Bodhisattvas, and the faculties, natures, and inclinations of all sentient beings.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here perceive within a single atom—
The sites of enlightenment in immeasurable lands, sentient beings, and all kalpas—
just as within a single atom, so it is with every atom;
all varieties are fully present, everywhere without obstruction.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here universally observe all phenomena:
sentient beings, lands, and worlds; they are without arising and without existence.
They contemplate the equality of sentient beings, the equality of phenomena, and the equality of the Tathāgatas.
The lands, the vows, and all such things— Throughout the three times, they are entirely equal.
The Buddha-sons dwelling herein Transform and guide all sentient beings,
Make offerings to all Tathāgatas, And contemplate the nature of all phenomena.
Throughout immeasurable tens of millions of kalpas, the vows, wisdom, and practices they have cultivated are vast and beyond measure; their praise can never be exhausted.
Those great heroes and sages act without any obstruction.
Abiding within this state, I join my palms in reverent salutation.
To the eldest son of all Buddhas, the noble and virtuous Lord Maitreya, I now pay homage with deep respect; may you deign to look upon me with compassion.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-Four;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-Five.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśa, by Imperial Decree.
The Chapter on Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation and the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra.

At that time, after Sudhana had praised all the bodhisattvas within the Great Pavilion of the Adorned Treasury of Vairocana with such infinite dharmas of praise and eulogy, he prostrated himself reverently before the pavilion. Standing there with single-minded devotion, bowing his body and joining his palms, he gazed up with longing, desiring to see Maitreya Bodhisattva and to attend upon and make offerings to him.

Then he saw Maitreya Bodhisattva coming from a separate location outside the pavilion, surrounded before and behind by immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans; by Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors; by his immeasurable retinue of relatives—both internal and external—from his place of birth; by a multitude of brahmins; and by countless hundreds of thousands of other sentient beings, all approaching together toward the great pavilion.
Having seen this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he immediately stepped forward to pay homage, prostrating himself so that his five limbs touched the ground.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva observed Sudhana and pointed him out to the great assembly, praising his truly immeasurable merit and speaking these verses:
“Behold Sudhana, Whose wisdom and mind are pure.”
To seek the practice for awakening, you have come to attend upon me.
Welcome, O you of perfected compassion; welcome, O you of pure pity;
welcome, O you with eyes of tranquility, who practice without weariness.
Welcome, O one of pure intent; welcome, O one of vast mind.
Welcome, O one with non-retrogressive faculties, who practices without weariness.
Welcome, O one of unshakable conduct, who ever seeks out virtuous friends.
Having realized the world, your mind is untainted; you tame all living beings.
Welcome to those who practice the wondrous path; welcome to those who abide in merit.
Welcome to those who advance toward the fruit of Buddhahood; may you be the refuge for the world.
Welcome, you whose essence is virtue; Welcome, nourished by the Dharma;
Welcome, you of boundless conduct, Hard to behold in this world.
Welcome, free from delusion, Like a lotus flower dwelling in the world.
Regarding gain and loss, defamation and praise, and so forth—there is no discrimination toward any of these.
Welcome all who come to bestow peace and happiness; they are gentle and pliant, capable of receiving transformation.
Deceit, guile, anger, and pride—their minds have entirely eliminated all such things.
Welcome, true son of the Buddha! You travel everywhere throughout the ten directions, increasing all merits with a mind that is supple, gentle, and free from weariness.
Welcome, you who possess the wisdom of the three times; you thoroughly know all phenomena.
Universally giving birth to the treasury of merit, Practicing without weariness or fatigue—
Mañjuśrī, Guṇamegha, and all other sons of the Buddhas,
Have successively led you here to show you the realm of non-obstruction.
Fully cultivating the bodhisattva practices, universally gathering all living beings,
vast and inconceivable, they have now come to my presence.
Seeking the pure realm of all Tathāgatas, they have come.
I ask why you have come to my presence, having made such vast vows.
You have come to my presence because you wish to practice and learn all the deeds and activities accomplished by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
Since you have come to me, desiring the subtle and wondrous Dharma from a spiritual friend and wishing to undertake the conduct of a bodhisattva,
you should keep in mind that spiritual friends are praised by all Buddhas.
"May you attain enlightenment and come to my side.
You have remembered your spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), who gave birth to me like a parent and nurtured me like a nurse, increasing the factors of enlightenment."
Like a physician treating all ailments, like the heavens showering down nectar,
like the sun revealing the right path, like the moon turning its pure wheel,
like a mountain that does not waver, and like the ocean that neither increases nor decreases.
Like a ferryman who brings others across, he has come to my presence.
Behold the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra): he is like a great and valiant general, like a great caravan leader, and like a great guide.
It can raise the banner of the True Dharma, It can manifest the virtues of the Buddhas,
It can extinguish all evil realms, It can open the gates to the happy destinies,
It can reveal the bodies of all Buddhas, And it can guard the treasuries of all Buddhas.
They are able to uphold all the Buddha-dharmas; for this reason, I pray that you will look upon and serve me.
Desiring to fulfill the wisdom of all Buddhas, desiring to possess a handsome body, and desiring to be born into a noble family, they have come to my presence.
You all observe this person: having drawn near to a spiritual friend, he follows all that they practice and study, acting in complete accordance with it.
By virtue of past causes and conditions of merit, Mañjuśrī has caused him to resolve his mind upon enlightenment.
Following them with no opposition, practicing without weariness or indolence;
abandoning parents, kinsmen, palaces, and wealth— all of these— humbly seeking out spiritual friends.
Having thus purified the mind and forever departed from the worldly body,
one shall be born in a Buddha-land and receive all supreme karmic rewards.
When Sudhana beholds sentient beings suffering the pains of birth, old age, sickness, and death,
To give rise to the mind of great compassion, He diligently cultivates the unsurpassed path.
Seeing sentient beings constantly transmigrating Through the five realms of existence,
Sudhana seeks adamantine wisdom To shatter their wheel of suffering.
Sudhana saw that the fields of the minds of sentient beings were extremely overgrown and defiled;
to remove the thorns of the three poisons, he sought exclusively for the plow of sharp wisdom.
Sentient beings dwell in the darkness of ignorance, blind and lost on the right path.
Sudhana acts as the guide, showing them the place of peace and security.
With the armor of patience and the vehicle of liberation, and with wisdom as his sharp sword,
he is able to destroy the thieves of affliction within the three realms of existence.
Sudhana, the master of the Dharma-ship, universally rescues all sentient beings,
enabling them to cross the ocean of ignorance and swiftly reach the island of pure jewels.
Sudhana, the sun of perfect enlightenment, possesses the great wheel of wisdom-light and vast vows.
Traversing the emptiness of the dharma-realm, He universally illuminates the abodes of the deluded masses.
Sudhana is the moon of perfect enlightenment; His white dharmas are entirely complete.
With the cooling light of the samādhi of compassion, He shines equally upon the minds of all sentient beings.
The ocean of Sudhana’s supreme wisdom rests upon the foundation of a straightforward mind;
as his bodhisattva practices gradually deepen, he brings forth the manifold jewels of the Dharma.
Sudhana, the great-hearted dragon, soars into the void of the dharma-realm.
Raising clouds and pouring down sweet rain, they bring all fruits to fruition.
So too does Sudhana kindle the lamp of Dharma: faith is the wick, compassion the oil, mindfulness the vessel, and merit the light, which extinguishes the darkness of the three poisons.
The kalala of the awakened mind, with compassion as the amnion and loving-kindness as the flesh,
With the factors of enlightenment as its limbs and joints, grows within the Tathāgatagarbha.
It increases the treasury of merit and the treasury of pure wisdom.
Revealing the treasury of skillful means, Giving birth to the treasury of great vows.
Such magnificent adornments as these, Which rescue and protect all sentient beings,
Are difficult to hear and difficult to see Among all gods and humans.
Such is the tree of wisdom: its roots are deep and immovable;
as its manifold practices gradually increase, it provides universal shade for all living beings.
Desiring to give birth to all virtues, and desiring to inquire into all dharmas,
Desiring to sever all doubts, one should single-mindedly seek a virtuous friend.
Desiring to shatter the demons of delusion, desiring to remove the stains of various views,
and desiring to untie the bonds of sentient beings, one should single-mindedly seek a virtuous friend.
One shall extinguish all evil realms, And show the path to humans and devas;
Causing them to cultivate meritorious deeds, So they may swiftly enter the city of Nirvāṇa.
One shall liberate them from all places of suffering, And grant them places of peace and bliss.
Severing all fetters and attachments, May the three realms of existence be forever extinguished.
One should cross over the perils of various views, And cut through the net of views;
One should dry up the waters of craving and desire, And show the path to the threefold way.
You shall become a refuge and savior for the world; you shall become the light of the world;
you shall become the teacher of the three realms, showing them the place of liberation.
You shall also cause the world to universally abandon all conceptual attachments.
Universally awakening from the sleep of afflictions, Universally emerging from the mire of craving and desire.
One should thoroughly understand all various phenomena, And one should purify all various buddha-fields.
When everything is brought to ultimate perfection, The mind experiences great joy.
Your conduct is exceedingly gentle and harmonious, and your mind is most pure;
whatever merits you wish to cultivate shall all be brought to fulfillment.
Before long, you shall behold the Buddhas and thoroughly comprehend all dharmas.
Purifying the ocean of all buddha-fields, Accomplishing great awakening,
Adorning the ocean of merit and wisdom, Liberating the ocean of sentient beings,
Perfecting the ocean of all practices— May you become an ocean of enlightenment.
One shall reach the shore of merit; one shall give birth to all wholesome qualities;
one shall become equal to the sons of the Buddha—such is the firm resolve of the mind.
One shall sever all delusions; one shall purify all karma.
One shall subdue all māras and fulfill such vows as these;
one shall give birth to the path of sublime wisdom and open the path of the True Dharma;
before long, one shall abandon the paths of delusion, karma, and all suffering.
The wheel of all sentient beings is submerged and deluded within the wheel of existence;
you should turn the wheel of Dharma to cause them to sever the wheel of suffering.
You should uphold the seed of the Buddha; you should purify the seed of the Dharma.
You are able to gather the seeds of the Saṃgha, pervading all three periods of time;
you shall sever the net of craving, you shall tear asunder the net of views,
you shall rescue those within the net of suffering, and you shall fulfill this net of vows.
One shall deliver the realm of sentient beings; one shall purify the realm of the land;
one shall gather the realm of wisdom; one shall fulfill this realm of the mind;
one shall cause sentient beings to rejoice; one shall cause Bodhisattvas to rejoice.
One shall cause all Buddhas to rejoice; one shall achieve this joy;
one shall see all realms of existence; one shall see all buddha-fields;
one shall see all phenomena; and one shall achieve this vision of a Buddha.
One should emit light that shatters darkness; one should emit light that cools the heat;
one should emit light that extinguishes evil, cleansing away the suffering of the three realms of existence.
One should open the gate to the celestial realms; one should open the gate to the Buddha-way.
One should reveal the gateways of liberation, enabling all sentient beings to enter them;
one should demonstrate the true path and sever all false paths.
By practicing diligently in this manner, one shall accomplish the Way of Bodhi.
One should cultivate an ocean of merit, And cross over the ocean of the three realms of existence,
Causing the ocean of all living beings To emerge from the ocean of manifold sufferings.
Within the ocean of sentient beings, One should dry up and exhaust the ocean of afflictions.
May you cultivate the ocean of all practices, And swiftly enter the ocean of great wisdom.
You shall increase the ocean of wisdom; You shall cultivate the ocean of practice;
The ocean of the great vows of all Buddhas— You shall fulfill them all.
You shall enter the ocean of lands; you shall contemplate the ocean of assemblies.
With the power of wisdom, you shall drink deeply from the ocean of all dharmas.
You shall behold the clouds of Buddhas and raise clouds of offerings.
One should listen to the cloud of the sublime Dharma, And one should give rise to this cloud of vows.
Universally wandering through the chambers of the three realms of existence, Universally destroying the chambers of all delusions,
And universally entering the chamber of the Tathāgata— One should practice such a path.
Universally entering the gates of samādhi, Universally roaming through the gates of liberation,
Universally abiding in the gates of supernormal powers, They travel throughout the entire dharma-realm.
They appear universally before all sentient beings, And stand universally before all Buddhas.
Just as the light of the sun and moon, may you achieve such power;
Your conduct shall be free from agitation and your conduct free from attachment;
Like a bird moving through the void, may you achieve this wondrous function.
Just as the net of Indra, so do the nets of lands abide;
you should go to them all, unimpeded like the wind.
You should enter the Dharma-realm and travel everywhere throughout all worlds.
Universally beholding the Buddhas of the three periods of time, your heart gives rise to great joy.
Regarding all dharma-gates— those already attained and those yet to be attained—
you should experience great exultation, free from both greed and weariness.
You are a vessel of merit, capable of following the teachings of all Buddhas and able to cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva; thus you have been able to behold this marvel.
Such sons of the Buddha are difficult to encounter even in hundreds of millions of eons.
How much more so when you behold his merits and the various sublime paths he has cultivated.
Born among human beings, you have gained great benefit from all that is wholesome;
you have been able to see Mañjuśrī and others, and their immeasurable virtues.
Having already left behind all evil realms, Having already emerged from all places of difficulty, Having already transcended all suffering and affliction— Excellent! Do not be indolent!
Having already left the stage of ordinary beings, You now abide upon the stage of a bodhisattva.
When you have fulfilled the stage of wisdom, you shall swiftly enter the stage of the Tathāgata.
The conduct of Bodhisattvas is like the ocean, and the Buddha’s wisdom is equal to space;
since your aspiration is likewise so, you should give rise to great joy.
With the faculties free from indolence, their resolve ever firm,
and drawing near to spiritual friends, they shall before long achieve full perfection.
All the various practices of the Bodhisattvas are for the sake of taming sentient beings.
Universally practicing all dharma-gates, Be careful not to give rise to doubt or confusion.
You possess inconceivable merit And true, authentic faith;
Therefore, on this very day, You are able to see these sons of the Buddhas.
You see all these sons of the Buddhas, who have all attained vast and great benefits;
every one of their great vows, they all believe and accept.
Within the three realms of existence, you have practiced and become a wondrous vessel.
Therefore, O sons of the Buddha, I show you this gate of liberation.
A person who is not a vessel for the Dharma, even if dwelling together with the sons of the Buddha for immeasurable eons, shall never know its realm.
You see these sons of the Buddhas, Who have heard such a Dharma as this— A rarity in this world;
you should give rise to great joy and celebration.
The Buddhas protect and mind you; The Bodhisattvas embrace and sustain you.
Able to practice in accordance with his teaching—how excellent is this abiding in the life-span!
Having been born into the family of Bodhisattvas, having already perfected the virtues of a Bodhisattva, and having grown within the lineage of the Tathāgata—one should rejoice; how excellent!
The Buddhas are our compassionate fathers; the Bodhisattvas are our celestial kin;
the factors of enlightenment are our relatives, who nurture our true intent.
Having already possessed the seed of a Bodhisattva, they cause the lineage of the Dharma King to flourish.
Having fully possessed the virtues of a Dharma King, great joy pervades your entire being;
having accomplished the most supreme task— extraordinary and inconceivable—
you shall before long attain it all and ascend to the rank of consecration.
Just as the seed is sown, so shall the fruit surely be obtained;
I now congratulate and comfort you—you should be greatly rejoiced.
Immeasurable bodhisattvas have practiced the Way for immeasurable eons.
Unable to accomplish this practice, you have now all attained it.
Through the power of firm progress born of faith and joy, Sudhana has accomplished this practice;
if anyone possesses a heart of reverence and admiration, they too should train in this way.
All practices of merit arise from aspiration and desire;
Sudhana has already understood this, and always delights in diligently cultivating it.
Just as a dragon spreads dense clouds, It will surely pour down a great rain.
When a bodhisattva gives rise to the wisdom of aspiration, they resolutely cultivate all practices.
If there is a spiritual friend who shows you the conduct of Samantabhadra,
you should serve them well and take care not to give rise to doubt or confusion.
Throughout immeasurable eons, you have recklessly cast away your body for the sake of desire;
now, seeking bodhi, this renunciation is truly virtuous.
Throughout immeasurable eons, you have fully endured the sufferings of birth and death.
Never having served the Buddhas, you have not heard of such a practice.
Now that you have obtained a human body and encountered a Buddha and a spiritual friend,
and are able to hear and receive these practices for awakening— how could you not be joyful?
Though one may encounter the appearance of a Buddha in the world and meet with virtuous friends,
if the mind is not pure, one will not hear such a Dharma.
If, toward virtuous friends, one possesses a heart of faith, joy, and respect, [one shall hear it].
Free from doubt and without weariness, one then hears such a Dharma as this.
If there are those who hear this Dharma and give rise to a heart of aspirational vows,
you should know that such persons have already attained vast and great benefit.
You have now entered this practice, most supreme and inconceivable;
welcome to you among men, for your merit shall surely reach fulfillment.
With such purity of mind, you shall always remain near to the Buddhas.
They also draw near to all bodhisattvas and will certainly attain enlightenment.
If one enters this Dharma-gate, they will possess all merits,
forever leave behind all evil realms, and never again undergo any suffering.
Before long, casting off this body, one will be reborn in a Buddha-land,
constantly beholding the Buddhas of the ten directions as well as all the Bodhisattvas.
This is due to the power of past causes and present pure understanding, as well as the strength of attending upon virtuous friends.
Increase all merits, like lotuses growing in water;
delight in spiritual friends, diligently make offerings to all Buddhas,
listen to the Dharma with a focused mind, and practice constantly without weariness.
You are a true vessel for the Dharma; you shall possess all dharmas, you shall cultivate all paths, and you shall fulfill all vows.
With a mind of faith and understanding, you have come to pay homage to me.
Before long you shall enter universally The assemblies of all Buddhas.
Excellent, true children of the Buddha, Who revere all Buddhas!
Before long, having perfected all practices, You will reach the shore of the Buddha’s virtues.
"You should go to the one of great wisdom, Mañjuśrī;
he shall cause you to attain the profound and wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, before the assembled multitude, praised Sudhana’s treasury of great merit, which was perfectly adorned with the realm of non-attachment.

Upon hearing those instructions, Sudhana followed his guidance; displaying the most excellent skillful means and offering words of consolation, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness. His body hair stood on end, tears flowed profusely, and he wept with choked sobs. Rising to his feet, he joined his palms, gazed up at him with reverence, and circumambulated him countless times.
By the power of Mañjuśrī’s mental resolve, various flowers, necklaces, and diverse wonderful jewels suddenly filled his hands without him even realizing it.
Delighted and overjoyed, Sudhana could not contain himself; he immediately offered them by scattering them over the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya.
Then, Maitreya Bodhisattva placed his hand upon Sudhana’s head and spoke these verses for him:
“Excellent, excellent, true son of the Buddha! You universally exert all your faculties without weariness.
Before long you shall be endowed with all virtues, Just like Mañjuśrī and myself.”
At that time, having heard this praise, the youth Sudhana replied in verse:
"I contemplate spiritual friends, Whom it is difficult to encounter even in billions of eons;
Having now gained the opportunity to draw near to them all, I have come to the presence of Your Honor."
"Because of Mañjuśrī, I have seen those who are difficult to see;
may I soon behold that Honored One of Great Merit once again.
At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in reverence and addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva once more, saying:
“O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva practice.”
"How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
I have heard that the Great Sage is well able to provide instruction; I only pray that you will, out of compassion, explain it for me.
"Great Sage! [he continued.]
All the Tathāgatas bestowed a prediction upon the Venerable One, that in one more birth he would attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
if in one more birth he were to attain unsurpassed enlightenment, he would then have already transcended all the dwelling places of Bodhisattvas,
would have already surpassed all the Bodhisattva stages of the state beyond birth (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and would have already perfected everything.
Having perfected the pāramitās, they have already deeply entered all gateways of patience; they have already fulfilled all bodhisattva stages;
they have already sported within all gateways of liberation; they have already accomplished all dharmas of samādhi;
they have already attained mastery over all bodhisattva practices; and they have already realized all...
Possessing the eloquence of dhāraṇīs, they have attained mastery within the sovereignty of all bodhisattvas;
they have already accumulated all the factors conducive to enlightenment for bodhisattvas;
they have already sported in all the wisdom and skillful means of bodhisattvas; and they have already brought forth all the great wisdom, skillfulness, and supernormal powers.

Having already accomplished all the training precepts that bodhisattvas should study, they have thereby purified all the sublime practices performed by bodhisattvas; they have thereby fulfilled all the great vows undertaken by bodhisattvas;
they have thereby received the predictions of all Buddhas; they have thereby understood all the gateways of the various vehicles; they have thereby...
Being worthy of the protective mindfulness of all Tathāgatas, one has already been able to encompass the bodhi of all Buddhas,
has already been able to uphold the treasury of all Buddha-dharmas, has already been able to receive the secret teachings of all Buddhas,
has already been able to turn the secret wheel of all Bodhisattvas, and has already been able to shatter afflictions...
Having already acted as a great heroic general who vexes the armies of Māra, one has thus become a great guide capable of leading others out of the wilderness of birth and death;
one has thus become a great King of Physicians capable of treating the grave illnesses of all afflictions;
one has thus become the most supreme among all sentient beings; and one has thus attained sovereignty among all the lords of the world.
Having already attained the foremost rank among all noble ones, one has thereby become most preeminent among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
one has become a helmsman within the ocean of birth and death;
one has already cast the net for subduing all sentient beings; and one has already been able to observe all sentient beings.
Having already been able to encompass the entire realm of sentient beings, having already been able to protect the entire assembly of bodhisattvas,
having already been able to discuss all matters concerning bodhisattvas, having already been able to go to the abodes of all Tathāgatas,
having already been able to dwell in the assemblies of all Tathāgatas, he has already been able to manifest...
Standing before all sentient beings, he has already been able to know that all phenomena are like illusions and mirages;
he has already been able to contemplate all phenomena as being like reflections; he has already been able to remain unstained by and unattached to all worldly dharmas;
he has already been able to realize the non-arising nature of all phenomena; and he has already been able to purify the one...
The body, speech, and mind of all bodhisattvas have already been able to shatter all māras through the vajra-samādhi;
they have already been able to know the original source of all pure dharmas; they have already been able to realize the immovable nature of all marks;
they have already been able to practice the pāramitās without regression; they have already been able to contemplate...
Since all phenomena are impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self, one has already been able to give rise to all roots of goodness pertaining to the stages of all Buddhas;
one has already been able to cultivate the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment through yogic practice;
one has already reached the further shore of all bodhisattva realms; and one has universally known that the nature of all afflictions is quiescent.
Through cessation, one is already able to abide in the adamantine samādhi, immovable;
one is already able to realize that the minds of the three periods of time are all ungraspable; one is already able to realize the bodhicitta that is as immovable as a mountain;
one is already able to be without attachment to any worldly dharmas; and one is already able to transcend all māras.
Regarding their spheres of activity: they have already been able to abide in the sphere of all Buddhas; they have already been able to reach the unimpeded sphere of all Bodhisattvas;
they have already been able to diligently make offerings to all Buddhas; they have already attained the same essential nature as all Buddha-dharmas;
they have already bound the ceremonial silk ribbons of all Buddha-dharmas; they have already received [the empowerment] from all Buddhas...

Having received empowerment, they abide in the rank of all Dharma Kings; having entered the sphere of the wisdom of omniscience, they have given birth to all Buddha-dharmas and have trodden the station of the knowledge of all modes.
“Great Sage! How does a bodhisattva study the bodhisattva practice?
How does a bodhisattva cultivate the bodhisattva path so that, according to their cultivation, they are able to swiftly realize all Buddha-dharmas?”

How does a bodhisattva fully comprehend all Buddha-dharmas, swiftly deliver all sentient beings they have in mind, causing them all to ultimately reach the other shore; how can they universally fulfill all great vows they have made, universally bring to ultimate completion all practices they have initiated, universally comfort all devas and humans, not betray themselves, not sever the Three Jewels, not render the lineage of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in vain, and be able to uphold the Dharma-eye of all Buddhas?
"I pray that you will explain all such matters as these!
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva surveyed the entire assembly at the site of enlightenment and, pointing toward Sudhana, spoke these words:
"O virtuous ones!
"Do you all now see this youth who has come to me to inquire about the conduct of a bodhisattva, desiring to universally accomplish all merits?
O virtuous ones!"
This youth is courageous and diligent, his aspirations are pure and unadulterated, and his profound resolve is firm and steadfast, never regressing;

he possesses sublime hope and is never satiated in mind. Like a mountain, he is immovable; like one whose hair is on fire, he acts with urgency. He delights in approaching and associating with spiritual friends, seeking them out everywhere to serve and make offerings to them, inquiring after the essentials of the Dharma, and receiving and upholding it without loss.
Virtuous ones, you should know:

this youth, in the past at the City of Blessings, received the instruction and guidance of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, which caused him to resolve his mind toward enlightenment. He then traveled from place to place, seeking out spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) through one hundred and ten cities, before finally arriving at my dwelling, never for a moment giving rise to a thought of weariness or indolence.

"O noble ones! This son of good family is truly rare; he has set out upon the Great Vehicle and dwells within the realm of the Buddhas. Mounted upon the great vow, he cultivates practices of a similar nature and rouses great valor. Clad in the armor of great compassion, he protects and rescues sentient beings with a heart of great loving-kindness. He exerts great diligence in cultivating the *pāramitās*, acts as a great caravan leader to protect all beings, and serves as a great Dharma-ship to ferry them across the ocean of existence. He universally gathers the jewels of all merit and wisdom, cultivates all vast dharmas that assist the path, and increases and accomplishes all virtues."
Such a person is difficult to hear of, difficult to see, difficult to draw near, and difficult to practice with.

Why is this? Because this son of good family desires to rescue and protect all sentient beings, to transcend all evil realms, to leave behind all perilous difficulties, to shatter the darkness of ignorance, to emerge from the wilderness of birth and death, to still the wheel of rebirth in the various destinies, to cross beyond the realm of Māra, to abandon places of attachment, to remain unstained by worldly dharmas, to emerge from the mire of desire, to sever the yoke of greed, to untie the bonds of views, to demolish the house of conceptualization, to cut off the path of delusion, to topple the banner of pride, to extract the arrows of confusion, to remove the cover of sleep, to clear away the mountains of hindrances, to tear asunder the net of craving, to loosen the knots of folly, to escape the flow of existence, to depart from flattery and illusion, to purify the stains of the mind, to sever doubt and suspicion, and to reach nirvāṇa.
"O virtuous ones! This Great Being has constructed a great Dharma-ship for those being swept away by the four torrents;
he has established a great Dharma-bridge for those submerged in the mire of views."
For those fallen into the dark gloom of ignorance, he kindles the lamp of great wisdom;
for those wandering through the wilderness of all saṃsāra, he shows them the noble path;
for those afflicted by the grave illness of all delusions and karma, he provides the medicine of the Dharma.
For those who encounter all the calamities and hardships of birth and death, I provide them with the nectar of immortality;
for those who have entered the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion, I douse them with the water of meditative concentration;
and for those burdened by much anxiety and affliction, I console and encourage them until they find peace.
For those bound in the prison of existence, he instructs them so they may be released;
for those fettered by views, he bestows the sword of wisdom;
for those dwelling in the city of the realms, he shows them the gate of liberation.
For those in peril, he guides them to a place of peace;
for those who fear the thieves of the fetters, he bestows the dharma of fearlessness;
for those fallen into evil destinies, he extends the hand of the Dharma.
For those who are afflicted by the aggregates, he shows them the city of Nirvāṇa;
for those entwined by the serpents of the elements, he liberates them through the Noble Path;
and for those attached to the empty village of the six sense bases, he leads them out with the light of wisdom.
To those dwelling on deviant paths, he causes them to enter the correct crossing;
to those who associate with evil friends, he shows them virtuous friends;
to those who delight in mundane dharmas, he instructs them in the joy of the noble Dharma.
For those who are attached to the cities of birth-and-death and existence, he causes them to enter the city of omniscience.
"O virtuous ones! This Great Being thus diligently seeks various skillful means, vowing to rescue and protect all sentient beings."
From birth, they maintain an uninterrupted succession of the arousal of the bodhicitta;
they never cease from pure conduct; they seek the path of the Mahāyāna without ever becoming weary; they receive and uphold all great clouds of Dharma;
they constantly and diligently accumulate the factors that assist the path; they bring everything to perfection without abandoning the yoke of goodness; and they always delight in all things.
In this gate of pure Dharma, they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva with courageous diligence, seeking them with tireless effort in every thought-moment without ever regressing.
They give rise to all virtuous deeds and bring their great vows to fulfillment;
they never grow weary of seeing spiritual friends and never grow fatigued in serving them, even as they hear all the instructions of those spiritual friends.
“...he always reflects upon and acts in accordance with [the teachings], never contravening them.
‘O virtuous ones! This son of good family is most difficult to encounter. If there are sentient beings who can resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, they are truly rare in this world.’”

How much more so for one who, having already resolved their mind [on enlightenment], is further able to thus diligently and vigorously collect all Buddha-dharmas for the sake of benefiting sentient beings; you should know that such a person is doubly rare.

Furthermore, they are able to thus earnestly seek and delight in the path of all bodhisattvas, are able to thus increase and purify all bodhisattva practices, and are able to thus draw near to, serve, and attend upon all spiritual friends. Moreover—
One should be able to act thus as if putting out a fire on one's head, remain as immovable as a mountain,
further be able to thus comply with the instructions of all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), further be able to thus firmly cultivate all paths of the Buddha,
further be able to thus accumulate all factors conducive to enlightenment (bodhipākṣikadharma), and further be able to thus take no pleasure in anything.
Regarding fame, profit, and honor, they are likewise able not to abandon the bodhisattva’s single-minded resolve;
they are likewise able to find no pleasure in the household life, no joy in wealth and nobility, no greed for enjoyments,
no attachment to sensual delights, no longing for parents, relatives, or friends, and no regard for any worldly riches.
As for beings, those who merely delight in seeking companions among bodhisattvas, and who furthermore disregard their very bodies and lives,
wishing only to diligently cultivate the path to omniscience— know that such individuals are progressively and increasingly difficult to find.
“O virtuous ones!

Other bodhisattvas must pass through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas before they can fulfill the vows and practices of a bodhisattva, and before they can draw near to the enlightenment of all Buddhas;”

Within a single lifetime, this son of good family is able to adorn and purify all Buddha-fields; is able to teach and transform all sentient beings; is able to penetrate deeply into the Dharma-realm through wisdom; is able to accomplish all perfections (*pāramitās*); is able to expand the net of all practices; is able to fulfill all great vows; is able to transcend all demonic activities; is able to serve all spiritual friends, causing them to rejoice; is able to purify all Bodhisattva practices, making them complete; and is able to cultivate the various practices of Samantabhadra, bringing them to fulfillment.

At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, having thus praised the various merits of the youth Sudhana, caused immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings within the assembly to firmly establish their resolve for unsurpassed bodhicitta, and addressed Sudhana, saying: "Excellent!
Excellent! Son of good family!

It is for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all the world, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, and for the sake of diligently seeking all Buddha-dharmas that you have resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

“Good son! You have obtained a great benefit; you have well attained a human body; you have well maintained your life-span; you have well encountered the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world; and you have well seen Mañjuśrī, the great spiritual friend.”
Your body is itself a true and excellent vessel for the Dharma, moistened by all roots of goodness.

You are sustained by the support of pure dharmas; your faith and delight are vast, and your wisdom and understanding are pure. You have already obtained the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas and have been fully embraced by virtuous friends.
Why is this? It is because one is able to give rise to the great bodhicitta. "Good son!
The bodhicitta is like a seed, for it can give birth to all the dharmas of the Buddhas;
the bodhicitta is like a fertile field, for it can cause the pure and white dharmas of sentient beings to grow;
the bodhicitta is like the great earth, for it can support all worlds.
The bodhicitta is like great water, for it can wash away all the stains of affliction;
the bodhicitta is like a great wind, for it moves everywhere throughout the world without obstruction;
the bodhicitta is like a great fire, for it can burn away the fuel of all views.
The bodhicitta is like the pure sun, for it universally illumines all worlds;
the bodhicitta is like the full moon, for it is able to universally perfect all pure and white dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a bright lamp, for it can emit the various radiances of the Dharma.
The bodhicitta is like a pure eye, for it perceives all places, whether level or rugged;
the bodhicitta is like a great highway, for it enables all to enter the city of great wisdom;
the bodhicitta is like a correct ferry, for it causes one to leave behind all erroneous dharmas.
The bodhicitta is like a great vehicle, for it can universally transport all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like a gateway, for it reveals and opens up all bodhisattva practices;
the bodhicitta is like a palace, for it provides a dwelling place for the cultivation of samādhi dharmas.
The bodhicitta is like a garden, for therein one sports and enjoys the bliss of the Dharma;
the bodhicitta is like a dwelling, for it brings peace and security to all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is a place of refuge, for it benefits all worlds.
The bodhicitta is the foundation, for it is the basis upon which all bodhisattva practices rest;
the bodhicitta is like a strict father, for it instructs and guides all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like a compassionate mother, for it nurtures and brings forth the various roots of goodness of the bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like a wet nurse, for it nurtures and protects all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like a virtuous friend, for it brings benefit and fulfillment to all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like a sovereign, for it surpasses all those of the two vehicles.
The bodhicitta is like a sovereign king, for it attains mastery over all vows;
the bodhicitta is like the great ocean, for it universally gives birth to all merits;
the bodhicitta is like Mount Sumeru, for its mind is impartial toward all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is like the Iron Ring Mountains, for it sustains and upholds all worlds;
the bodhicitta is like the Great Snowy Mountains, for it nurtures and develops all medicinal herbs of wisdom;
the bodhicitta is like the Fragrant Mountain, for it gives rise to the fragrance of all meritorious virtues.
The bodhicitta is like the great void, for its sublime virtues are vast and boundless;
the bodhicitta is like a wondrous lotus, for it is unstained by any worldly phenomena;
the bodhicitta is like a well-trained elephant of wisdom, for its mind is virtuous and compliant, free from wildness or ferocity.
The bodhicitta is like a fine and noble horse, for it is far removed from all evil natures;
the bodhicitta is like a charioteer, for it protects all Mahāyāna teachings;
the bodhicitta is like an excellent medicine, for it can cure the disease of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like a pit or a trap, for it causes all unwholesome dharmas to fall into ruin;
the bodhicitta is like a vajra, for it can pierce through all dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a casket of incense, for it can store the fragrance of all merits.
The bodhicitta is like a wondrous flower, for it is that which all the world delights to behold;
the bodhicitta is like white sandalwood, for it removes the heat of all desires and brings about refreshing coolness;
the bodhicitta is like black aloeswood, for it is able to permeate the entire dharma-realm with its pervasive fragrance.
The bodhicitta is like the sovereign medicinal king *sudarśana*, for it can destroy all diseases of affliction;
the bodhicitta is like the *vighuṣṭa* medicine, for it can extract all arrows of delusion;
the bodhicitta is like the mental consciousness, for it serves as the basis for all the sense faculties.
The bodhicitta is like Śakra, for it is the most honored and supreme among all lords;
the bodhicitta is like Vaiśravaṇa, for it can sever all suffering of poverty;
the bodhicitta is like Puṇyadattā, for it is adorned with all meritorious virtues.
The bodhicitta is like an ornament, for it adorns all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is like the fire at the end of an eon, for it can incinerate all conditioned phenomena;
the bodhicitta is like a rootless medicinal herb, for it nurtures and grows all the qualities of a Buddha.
The bodhicitta is like the dragon-gem, for it can dissolve all the poisons of affliction;
the bodhicitta is like the water-clearing jewel, for it can clarify the turbidity of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like the wish-fulfilling gem, for it provides for all who are impoverished.
The bodhicitta is like a vessel of the virtuous, for it fulfills the aspirations of all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like a wish-fulfilling tree, for it can rain down all manner of ornaments;
the bodhicitta is like a garment of goose feathers, for it is not defiled by the impurities of birth and death.
The bodhicitta is like white cotton thread, for its nature has been pure from the very beginning;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp plow, for it can cultivate the fields of all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like Nārāyaṇa, for it can destroy the enemy of all views of self.
The bodhicitta is like a swift arrow, for it can shatter all forms of suffering;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp spear, for it can pierce the armor of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like sturdy armor, for it can protect the mind that accords with reality.
The bodhicitta is like a sharp blade, for it can sever the heads of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a keen sword, for it can cut through the armor of all pride;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp sickle, for it can reap the subtle latent tendencies.
The bodhicitta is like the banner of a valiant general, for it can subdue all the armies of Māra;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp saw, for it can cut down the tree of ignorance;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp axe, for it can fell the trees of all suffering.
The bodhicitta is like a weapon, for it can ward off all calamities;
the bodhicitta is like skillful hands, for it protects the body of the perfections of all-knowledge;
the bodhicitta is like excellent feet, for it establishes the body of all meritorious virtues.
The bodhicitta is like a golden lancet, for it can remove the cataracts of all ignorance;
the bodhicitta is like tongs, for it can extract the thorns of all views of a self;
the bodhicitta is like bedding, for it brings rest and alleviates the various toils and sufferings of birth and death.
The bodhicitta is like a spiritual friend, for it can untie all the bonds of birth and death;
the bodhicitta is like excellent treasure, for it can eliminate all states of poverty;
the bodhicitta is like a guide, for it well knows the essential path by which Bodhisattvas emerge [from saṃsāra].
The bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure, for it yields the wealth of merit without exhaustion;
the bodhicitta is like a gushing spring, for it yields the water of wisdom without end;
the bodhicitta is like a clear mirror, for it universally manifests the images of all dharma-gates.
The bodhicitta is like a lotus flower, for it is unstained by any defilement of sin;
the bodhicitta is like a great river, for it flows to lead forth and encompass all dharmas of deliverance;
the bodhicitta is like a great dragon king, for it can rain down the rain of all sublime dharmas.
The bodhicitta is like the life-faculty, for it sustains the body of the Bodhisattva’s great compassion;
the bodhicitta is like ambrosia, for it enables one to abide in the realm of immortality;
the bodhicitta is like a great net, for it universally gathers in all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is like a lasso, for it gathers in all those who are to be converted;
the bodhicitta is like a hook and bait, for it draws forth those dwelling within the abyss of existence;
the bodhicitta is like the agada medicine, for it can eliminate the disease of delusion and bring about eternal peace and security.
The bodhicitta is like an antidote that neutralizes poison, for it can completely eliminate the poison of craving and attachment;
the bodhicitta is like a master of vidyā-mantras, for it can extinguish all evil thoughts and deliberations;
the bodhicitta is like a swift wind, for it can disperse the mists of all obstacles.
The bodhicitta is like a great island of jewels, for it gives birth to all the jewels of the factors of enlightenment;
the bodhicitta is like a fine seed, for it gives birth to all pure and white dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a dwelling, for it is the locus upon which all qualities of merit rely.
The bodhicitta is like a marketplace, for it is the place where the Bodhisattva merchant-leader conducts his trade;
the bodhicitta is like an alchemical elixir, for it can purify the stains of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like fine honey, for it perfects the flavor of all meritorious qualities.
The bodhicitta is like a correct path, for it causes all bodhisattvas to enter the city of wisdom;
the bodhicitta is like an excellent vessel, for it can hold all pure and white dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like seasonal rain, for it can extinguish the dust of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like a dwelling place, for it is that upon which all bodhisattvas rely and abide;
the bodhicitta is like a magnet, for it attracts the fruit of all liberation;
the bodhicitta is like pure lapis lazuli, for its intrinsic nature is luminously pure and free from all defilements.
The bodhicitta is like the sapphire, for it transcends the worldly wisdom of the two vehicles;
the bodhicitta is like the drum that strikes the watches of the night, for it awakens all sentient beings from the sleep of afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like pure water, for its nature is inherently limpid and free from defilement.
The bodhicitta is like Jāmbūnada gold, for it outshines all conditioned virtues;
the bodhicitta is like the king of great mountains, for it rises above all worlds;
the bodhicitta is a place of refuge, for it does not reject any who come to it.
The bodhicitta is a source of benefit, for it can eliminate all causes of decline and affliction;
the bodhicitta is a sublime jewel, for it can cause all minds to rejoice;
the bodhicitta is like a great assembly of giving, for it fills the hearts of all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is supremely exalted, for no mind among sentient beings can equal it;
the bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure, for it can encompass all the qualities of a Buddha;
the bodhicitta is like a skillful recitation, for it universally encompasses all the practices and vows of a Bodhisattva.
The bodhicitta is like a guardian, for it accords with and nurtures all dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a benefactor, for it can turn back all unwholesome dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like Indra’s net, for it can subdue the asuras of the afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like the wind of Varuṇa, for it can move all those who are to be transformed;
the bodhicitta is like the fire of Indra, for it can burn away all afflictions and habitual tendencies;
the bodhicitta is like a stūpa of the Buddha, for it should be venerated by all the world.
“Good son! The bodhicitta accomplishes such immeasurable and boundless, most supreme merits;
to state the essentials, you should know that it is entirely equal to all the merits of the Buddha-dharma.”
Why is this? Because the wheel of all bodhisattva practices arises from the bodhicitta, and all Tathāgatas of the three times and ten directions are born from the bodhicitta.
Therefore, good son!

If there are those who are able to resolve their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they have already given birth to immeasurable merit and are universally able to encompass the path to all-knowledge.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-Five;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-Six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśī, by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation," at that time,
Maitreya Bodhisattva again addressed the youth Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!"
For example, suppose there is a person who obtains the medicine of fearlessness and is freed from five kinds of terrors. What are these five?
They are as follows:
Fire cannot burn it, poison cannot affect it, the blade cannot wound it, water cannot sweep it away, and smoke cannot suffocate it;
likewise, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, having obtained the medicinal herb of the bodhicitta of omniscience, is free from the five fears.

What are these five? They are: not being burned by the fires of the three poisons; not being struck by the poison of the five desires; not being wounded by the sword of delusion; not being swept away by the currents of existence; and not being harmed or熏 (xūn) by the smoke of discursive thought and examination.
“Good son! For example, if there is a person who obtains the medicine of liberation, they will never encounter untimely calamities;

so it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who likewise obtains the medicine of the wisdom of liberation through the bodhicitta, forever remaining free from all untimely calamities of birth and death.”
“Good son! It is like a person who carries the mahā-aṅga medicine; wherever it is, all venomous snakes, upon smelling the fragrance of this medicine, immediately depart from afar.

In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva likewise carries the great mahā-aṅga medicine of the bodhicitta; when all the venomous snakes of the various afflictions smell its fragrance, they are entirely dispersed and extinguished.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who possesses the invincible medicine; no enemy whatsoever can overcome them.
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva likewise possesses the invincible medicine of the bodhicitta, and is able to completely subdue all the armies of Māra.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who carries the *vighuṣma* medicine, which can cause poisoned arrows to fall away naturally;
so too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, who carries the *vighuṣma* medicine of the bodhicitta, causing the arrows of greed, hatred, delusion, and all false views to fall away naturally.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who possesses the *sudarśana* medicine, which can eliminate all existing ailments;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who possesses the *sudarśana* king of medicines that is the bodhicitta, and thereby completely eliminates all diseases of the afflictions (*kleśa*).”

“Good son! It is like a medicinal tree named Śatana; if one takes its bark to apply to a wound, the wound is immediately healed and restored to its former state, leaving no scar. Yet, as the bark is taken, it grows back again, never being exhausted.

In the same way, the Great Wisdom Tree born from the Bodhicitta of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: if there are those who see it and give rise to faith, the wounds of their afflictions and karma are all completely eliminated, yet the All-Knowledge Tree suffers no loss whatsoever.”

“Good son! It is like a medicinal tree named ‘Root-Attainment’ (*siddhamūla*); by its power, it causes all the roots, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits of every tree in Jambudvīpa to grow and reach fulfillment.

In the same way, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s tree of the bodhicitta, through its supreme power, is able to cause all the roots of goodness belonging to śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, those in training (*śaikṣa*), those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*), and all bodhisattvas to grow and reach fulfillment.”
“Good son! It is like a medicine named Ārāma; if it is applied to the body, both body and mind become fully capable.
In the same way, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva obtains the Ārāma medicine of the bodhicitta, it causes their body and mind to possess superior capability and increases wholesome dharmas.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who obtains the medicinal herb of mindfulness-power, which can cause the power of their mind’s mindfulness to become pure;

so it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, who likewise obtains the wondrous medicine of the power of mindfulness of the bodhicitta, whereby the mind is free from obstruction and the power of mindfulness is purified.”
“Good son! It is like a medicine called ‘Great Lotus,’ which anyone who takes it will live for an eon;

likewise, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva takes the medicine of the Great Lotus of the Bodhicitta, they gain mastery over their lifespan throughout incalculable eons while cultivating and accumulating the various practices of the pāramitās.”
“Good son! It is like a person who, possessing the elixir that renders one invisible, cannot be seen by any human or non-human being in the world;
likewise, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva holds the wondrous elixir of the bodhicitta, he may wander through all manner of realms, yet none of the Māras can perceive him.”

“Good son! It is as if there were a jewel in the ocean called ‘Universal Gatherer of All Treasures. As long as this jewel remains, all other treasures will never be lost or scattered. Even if the kalpa-fire were to burn the world, it would be impossible for it to cause even a single drop of this ocean to diminish, let alone to dry it up entirely.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s jewel of the bodhicitta is also like this: dwelling within the great ocean of the bodhisattva’s vow for the wisdom of omniscience, if one constantly maintains it without allowing it to decline or be lost, there is no possibility whatsoever that it could destroy even a single root of goodness of a bodhisattva;
however, if one lets that mind regress and abandons omniscience, then all wholesome dharmas will immediately disperse and perish.

“Good son! It is like a mani jewel named ‘Universal Gathering of Light,’ which, when used to adorn the body with a necklace, outshines all other precious ornaments so that their radiance no longer appears.

In the same way, the bodhicitta jewel of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva adorns the nature of the mind, outshining all the mental jewels of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, such that all their ornaments are rendered lusterless.”
“Good son! Suppose there is a precious jewel called ‘Water-Cleanser’; if this jewel is placed in turbid water, by the power of the jewel, the water immediately becomes clear and pure.
The bodhicitta-jewel of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also like this: it can purify all the defilements and turbidity of the afflictions.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains the jewel that dwells in water; if they bind it upon their body and enter the great ocean, they may travel about at will, unharmed by the water.
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva obtains the wondrous jewel of the bodhicitta—the wisdom of omniscience—and enters the ocean of all saṃsāra, sporting therein with mastery, never to sink.

“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a dragon-jewel and enters a dragon palace; while dwelling and traveling upon the great ocean, by the power of that jewel, no dragons, snakes, or aquatic creatures can cause him harm.

So it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: having obtained the great dragon-jewel of the bodhicitta and the wisdom of omniscience, he enters the realm of desire within the waters of delusion and craving, where the dragons and snakes of afflictions and karma cannot cause him harm.”
“Good son! Just as Śakra, wearing a maṇi crown that adorns his head, outshines all other hosts of devas;

so too is the bodhisattva mahāsattva: wearing the precious crown of the great vow for the omniscience of all-knowledge—the bodhicitta—bound upon the crown of his mind, he transcends all sentient beings of the triple world.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*), which eliminates all suffering of poverty;

so too is the bodhisattva mahāsattva, who obtains the wish-fulfilling jewel of the bodhicitta and the knowledge of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), producing the requisites for the wholesome dharmas of a bodhisattva and remaining far removed from all fear of wrong livelihood (*mithyājīva*).”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a sun-crystal gem; when held toward the sunlight, it produces fire.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva obtains the sun-crystal gem of the nature of omniscience that is the bodhicitta; when held toward the light of wisdom, it produces the fire of wisdom.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a moon-lover jewel (candrakānta-maṇi); when held toward the light of the moon, it produces water.

In the same way, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva obtains the moon-essence jewel of the bodhicitta; holding this heart-jewel, it reflects the light of dedication and produces the water of all vows for roots of goodness.
“Good son! For example, just as a dragon king wears a crown of wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels upon his head and remains far removed from all fear of enemies;
so too is it with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, who wears the precious crown of the bodhicitta and great compassion, remaining far removed from all the hardships of the evil realms.”

“Good son! It is like a precious jewel named ‘Treasury Adorning All Worlds. If anyone obtains it, all their desires will be completely fulfilled; yet this jewel’s utility is inexhaustible and its substance does not diminish.

The jewel of the bodhicitta of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: if anyone obtains it, all their aspirations will be fully realized; yet the utility of the bodhicitta is inexhaustible and its substance does not diminish.”
“Good son! Just as a wheel-turning monarch possesses a maṇi-jewel which, when placed within his palace, radiates great light and destroys all darkness;

so too is the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Possessing the great maṇi-jewel of the bodhicitta and the wisdom of omniscience, while dwelling in the desire realm, he radiates the great light of wisdom and completely destroys the dark ignorance of all realms of existence.”
“Good son! For example, if there is a great indranīla mani jewel, whatever is touched by its light immediately becomes the same color as it;

so too is the jewel of omniscience that is the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva. When one observes all phenomena and dedicates the roots of goodness toward omniscience, everything without exception becomes identical to the color of the bodhicitta of the wisdom of omniscience.”

“Good son! Just as a lapis lazuli gem, even after remaining amidst impurities for hundreds of thousands of years, is not defiled by foul odors or filth because its nature is ultimately stainless and fundamentally pure;

so too is the jewel of omniscience produced by the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva. Even while dwelling within the desire realm for hundreds of thousands of kalpas, it is not defiled by the faults and afflictions of the desire realm, being ultimately stainless and fundamentally pure like the nature of the dharmadhātu.”
“Good son! For example, there is a jewel named Pure Radiance that is able to outshine the colors of all other jewels;

likewise, the jewel of the bodhicitta and the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatā) of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also thus, for it is able to outshine all the merits of ordinary beings and those of the two vehicles—both those in training (śaikṣa) and those beyond training (aśaikṣa).”
“Good son! For example, there is a jewel named ‘Flame’ that is able to completely extinguish all darkness;
likewise, the jewel of the omniscience of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: when it accords with contemplative practice, it can extinguish all the black darkness of ignorance.”
“Good son! For example, within the great ocean there is a priceless jewel which a merchant obtains and carries on a ship into the city;
among all the hundreds of thousands of kinds of *maṇi* gems, its radiance, color, and value are peerless.”

The jewel of the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is likewise: dwelling within the great ocean of birth and death, riding upon the ship of great vows, with a continuous deep resolve, they enter the city of liberation; no merit possessed by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas can equal it.

“Good son! Suppose there is a precious jewel called the Sovereign King (Vaiśrāvaṇarāja), which resides in Jambudvīpa, forty thousand yojanas from the orbs of the sun and moon. All the adornments within the palaces of the sun and moon are fully reflected in its image.

It is the same with the Sovereign King Jewel of the pure merit of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s resolve for bodhicitta and the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna). Abiding within saṃsāra, it illuminates the emptiness of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), and the reflections and adornments of all the pure realms and merits of the sun and moon of Buddha-wisdom all appear therein.”

“Good son! It is like a precious jewel named Sovereign King (Īśvararāja); wherever it is illuminated by the light of the sun and moon, the value of all other treasures, clothing, and such items cannot possibly equal it.”
