Great compassion is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for it gives rise to the family of the four means of attraction;
contemplation according to reality is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for it gives rise to the family of the perfection of wisdom;
the Great Vehicle is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for it gives rise to the family of skillful means.
Maturing sentient beings is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for it gives birth to the family of perfectly awakened ones;
wisdom and skillful means are the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for they give birth to the family of the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena;
the practice of all dharmas is the birthplace of bodhisattvas, for they give birth to the family of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
"Good son! These are the ten places of rebirth for bodhisattvas. Furthermore, good son!"
For the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is the mother; skillful means (upāyakauśalya) is the father; the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) is the wet nurse;
the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā) is the foster mother; the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā) is the ornament;
and the perfection of diligence (vīryapāramitā) is the nurturer. As for the perfection of meditation (dhyāna)...
The pāramitās are the washermen; spiritual friends are the teachers; all factors of enlightenment are companions;
all wholesome dharmas are kinsmen; all bodhisattvas are brothers; the bodhicitta is the household;
practice in accordance with reality is the family tradition; and the wholesome dharmas of the stages are...
Abiding in the household means attaining the various stages of patience (*kṣānti*); having great vows manifest before one is the family lineage;
fulfilling all practices with pure wisdom is in accordance with the family dharma; exhorting others to diligent cultivation without severing the Mahāyāna is the succession of the family estate;
and the Bodhisattva bound to one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*), consecrated by the water of the Dharma, is the crown prince.
To accomplish vast and true bodhi is to purify one's lineage.
Son of good family!
In this way, the bodhisattva transcends the stage of ordinary beings and enters the rank of bodhisattvas.
Born into the family of the Tathāgatas, they abide in the lineage of the Buddhas;
they are able to cultivate all practices and ensure that the Three Jewels are never interrupted;
they are skillfully able to protect the clan of Bodhisattvas and purify the seed of Bodhisattvas.
Born into a noble and preeminent station, one is free from the faults and evils of birth within all worlds;
among all devas, humans, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas, one possesses a perfect lineage and achieves the most supreme Buddha-lineage;
having attained the treasury of great vows, one is universally able to give rise to all bodhisattva practices.
“Good son! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva has accomplished such a noble and eminent family,
because he understands through wisdom that all phenomena are like reflections, he feels no aversion or contempt for the places of birth within the world.
Because they know all phenomena to be like magical transformations, they are unstained by any realm of existence;
because they have realized that all phenomena are without self, they tame sentient beings with minds free from weariness;
and because their essential nature is great compassion, they do not seek personal extinction but instead embrace and sustain sentient beings.
Because they thoroughly understand that birth and death are like a dream, they pass through all kalpas without feverish distress;
because they know that the five aggregates are entirely like an illusion, they manifest within birth and death without weariness;
because they know that the elements and sense bases are themselves the Dharma-realm, they remain free from the sores of attachment toward all objective realms.
Because they know all perceptions to be like a mirage, they enter the various realms of existence without giving rise to delusion;
because they realize that all phenomena are like illusions, they enter the realm of Māra with sovereign mastery and remain untainted;
because they have accomplished the pure and wondrous essence of the Dharma-body, no afflictions can deceive them.
Because they have accomplished all practices that lead everywhere, they attain mastery over all places of birth.
"Good son! My body is born universally throughout the entire dharma-realm;

He equalizes the diverse physical forms of all sentient beings; he equalizes the various and distinct voices of all sentient beings; he equalizes the manifold names and titles of all sentient beings; he equalizes the various inclinations and desires of all sentient beings; he equalizes the various modes of conduct through which he follows the world to teach and subdue beings; he equalizes the manifestation of pure births for all sentient beings; he equalizes the entry into the profound and superior understandings of all sentient beings; and he equalizes the transformations of the great vows of all bodhisattvas. Within such immeasurable categories, he manifests his body, with its various marks and various majestic virtues, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
“Good son! In order to bring to maturity those who previously practiced the same deeds as I but have now fallen away from the bodhicitta, I manifest birth within this Jambudvīpa;

and desiring to discipline my parents, kinsmen, and brahmins so that they may abandon pride regarding their lineage and be born into the family of the Tathāgata, I was born into a brahmin family in the village of Vāsava in the kingdom of Mālava.”

"Good son! Whether I am in the southern quarter or dwelling here within this Great Pavilion of Vairocana’s Adorned Treasury, I teach and discipline sentient beings through various skillful means, according to the inclinations of their minds."

“Good son! It is for the sake of conforming to all sentient beings; for the sake of maturing those devas of the Tuṣita Heaven who share the same practice as me; for the sake of manifesting the transformations of a Bodhisattva’s adornment of merit and wisdom so as to surpass all realms of desire; to cause them to abandon the thirst and craving for sensual pleasures; to cause them to illuminate the fact that all conditioned formations are impermanent; to cause them to know that the prosperity of devas must inevitably decline; to manifest the auspicious signs of descending to birth and to proclaim the Dharma-gate of Great Wisdom together with the Bodhisattvas in their final birth; to gather in and sustain all sentient beings born in every place of existence; and to transform those sent by Śākyamuni Tathāgata so that they may all awaken like lotuses in full bloom—it is for these reasons that I pass away from here and am born in the Tuṣita Heaven.”
“Good son! When my vows are fulfilled and I attain bodhi, you and Mañjuśrī shall both come to see me. Good son!”
"You should go to the place of the great bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and ask him:
'How should a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct?
How does one deeply enter the gateway of Samantabhadra’s conduct?'"
How is it produced? How is it matured? How is it expanded?
What is purification?
What is conformity? What is fulfillment?
"Good son! He shall analyze and reveal it for you. Why is this?"
Good son! The most supreme great vows of Mañjuśrī are not something that can be possessed by any other bodhisattvas, even those numbering in the hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas.
Good son! Mañjuśrī’s conduct is vast, immeasurable, and boundless;
his vows are limitless, continuing without interruption.
He is constantly able to give birth to all the most supreme merits of Bodhisattvas;
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva is constantly the mother of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas, causing them to realize and enter the profound principle;
he is constantly the teacher of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Bodhisattvas, causing them to diligently cultivate and deeply realize and enter [the truth].
They constantly turn the wheel of Dharma throughout the ten directions to teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
they constantly serve as Dharma teachers in all worlds throughout the ten directions;
and they are constantly praised within the great assemblies of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all Buddhas.
Abiding in profound wisdom, they perceive the true nature of phenomena;
having long ago entered deeply into the realm of all liberations, they have perfected all the practices performed by Samantabhadra.

"Noble son! The spiritual friend Mañjuśrī can cause you to be born into the family of the Tathāgata; he can increase all your roots of goodness; he can initiate the factors conducive to enlightenment within you; he can reveal to you your true spiritual friends; he can exhort you to cultivate all meritorious virtues; he can lead you to enter deeply into the net of great vows; he can establish you in the gateway of great vows; he can enable you to hear the profound and secret meanings of the Bodhisattvas; and he can reveal to you the inconceivable practices of a Bodhisattva, as well as those with whom you shared a common birth and common practice in the past."
Therefore, son of good family!
You should go to the place where the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī resides; do not give rise to weariness.
Mañjuśrī shall cause you to attain all meritorious virtues.

Why is this? All those spiritual friends whom you previously encountered, all the bodhisattva practices you heard, all the profound gates of liberation you entered, and all the oceans of great vows you fulfilled—these were entirely due to the majestic spiritual power of Mañjuśrī;
Mañjuśrī has attained ultimate perfection in every respect.
Then, the youth Sudhana circumambulated Maitreya to the right countless times, prostrated at his feet, gazed up at him with earnest devotion, and departed with a heart full of longing.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had traveled through one hundred and ten cities,
he arrived at the city of Sumana and stood at its gate;
there he contemplated Mañjuśrī, recollecting him with focused mindfulness, observing him everywhere, and longing to behold him in person.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, from a distance of one hundred and ten yojanas, extended his right hand from afar to the city of Sumana and touched Sudhana’s head, saying: "Excellent!
Excellent, son of good family!

If one is devoid of the root of faith, the mind becomes weary and disheartened, one’s resolve is inferior, one’s meritorious practices are incomplete, and one falls away from diligent effort; if one finds contentment in meager roots of goodness, fails to properly initiate all vows of practice, and is unable to draw near to spiritual friends—[then such a person cannot attain this samādhi].

Because of this, they are unable to comprehend such a nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), such a principle (*naya*), such a dharma-gate (*dharmaparyāya*), such a sphere (*viṣaya*), or such a dwelling place (*vihāra*);

whether it be knowing them universally, knowing them partially, knowing them profoundly, exhausting their source and bottom, observing them, realizing them, or attaining them—they are entirely incapable of doing so.
At that time, Mañjuśrī proclaimed this Dharma, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening him;
he caused the youth Sudhana to become fully perfected in countless Dharma-gates and endowed with the boundless light of great wisdom.

They deeply enter various gateways of Buddha-recollection, the gateway of boundless dharanis, the gateway of boundless eloquence, the gateway of boundless samadhis, the gateway of boundless supernormal powers, and the gateway of boundless vows and wisdom;
they deeply enter the wheel of all practices and vows of Samantabhadra;
and they extol all the skillful means of Mañjuśrī’s original dwelling land.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī:
"Noble One! How does one achieve mastery over the excellence of a noble one’s land?"
Mañjuśrī said to Sudhana, “Son of good family!
There are ten dharmas that a bodhisattva must fully perfect to attain my buddha-field and skillfully accomplish it.”
Sudhana said, "What are these ten? Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva replied:

“Good son! First is the dharma of the realization of non-arising, fully perfected; second is the dharma of non-extinction; third is the dharma of non-destruction; fourth is the dharma of no coming or going; fifth is the dharma that transcends the realm of verbal expression; sixth is the dharma for which there is no path of verbal expression; seventh is the dharma free from conceptual proliferation; eighth is the ineffable dharma; ninth is the dharma of tranquility; and tenth is the dharma of the noble ones.”
"If bodhisattvas are fully perfected in these ten dharmas, they will attain the skillful accomplishment of my buddha-field.
Sudhana said, "Noble One, what is the meaning of 'buddha-field' that you have spoken of?"
Mañjuśrī said: "This is the meaning of the dwelling places of all bodhisattvas. Sudhana said:
“What is the dwelling place of all bodhisattvas? Mañjuśrī replied, “Noble son!
The supreme ultimate truth is the dwelling place of the bodhisattva; why is this?
O son of good family!

The supreme ultimate truth is unborn, unceasing, indestructible, imperishable, neither coming nor going; such words are not the domain of speech, beyond the reach of verbal expression, incapable of being designated, and not something known through conceptual proliferation or intellectual speculation.
It is primordially without speech, its essential nature is quiescent, and it is realized only within by the noble ones themselves.
"Good son! It is because of this most supreme ultimate truth that the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, appear in the world;
whether a Buddha appears in the world or does not appear, it cannot be destroyed."

"Good son! All bodhisattvas, desiring to realize and enter the ultimate truth (paramārtha), renounce great wealth and power, as well as their youth and royal thrones. They are able to perform various difficult ascetic practices, shave off their hair and beards, don the dharma robes, and with right faith leave the household life. They single-mindedly seek the wondrous Way, practicing with diligence and without slackening, as if their heads or clothes were on fire."
"Good son! If there were no ultimate truth (paramārtha), for what purpose would the holy life (brahmacarya) that is cultivated be used?
Upon what would the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world depend?"

"Good son! Because they have deep faith in the existence of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), they cause all bodhisattvas to be fully perfected in these ten kinds of dharmas. Therefore, you should know and see them in this way, and explain them in this way, so as to skillfully achieve perfection within my buddha-field."
Sudhana the youth said: "Noble One!
By practicing what Dharma shall one obtain a noble and wondrous land such as yours?"

Mañjuśrī said: "If bodhisattvas can remain free from pride toward all things, give rise to a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings, and practice true offerings to the Tathāgatas, they shall attain my buddha-field."
Sudhana the youth said: "Noble One!
What is meant by being free from a mind of pride, giving rise to a mind of equanimity, and practicing true worship?"
Mañjuśrī said: "Good son! If a bodhisattva thoroughly contemplates and fully perfects ten dharmas, they will be able to accomplish a mind free from arrogance."
What are the ten? First, with a single-minded focus, one contemplates and clearly observes the realm of the body, thinking:
"I have now left the household life; I am no different from a dead man."
Why is this? It is because one has renounced all things—parents, loved ones, friends, kinsmen, and everything else.
By reflecting in this way, one becomes free from arrogance.
Second, one contemplates: "I now wear robes of dyed color; my movements and deportment are unlike those of the world. By contemplating in this way, one becomes free from pride.
Third, one reflects: "I have already discarded my physical beauty and, holding an alms bowl, I beg from others. Reflecting in this way, one becomes free from pride.
Fourth, one should reflect: "I am now begging for food like a *caṇḍāla*. By reflecting in this way, one causes the mind to become humble and attains freedom from arrogance.
Fifth, one reflects: "In order to seek solid food to nourish my body and my life-span, these are entirely in the hands of others. Reflecting in this way, one becomes free from arrogance.

Sixth, one contemplates that the food begged is the remains of what humans and animals have already consumed; since I only obtain food when they have discarded it, by reflecting in this way, one becomes free from arrogance.
Seventh, one reflects: "I should now show reverence and make offerings to my teachers and elders so as to bring them joy. Reflecting in this way, one becomes free from arrogance.

Eighth, one reflects: "I now wish to cause my fellow practitioners of the holy life to give rise to joy; therefore, I shall be fully endowed with dignified deportment and never violate the prescribed rules. Reflecting in this way, one becomes free from arrogance.
Ninth, one reflects: "I have now left the household life, yet within the Buddha-dharma I have not attained even a small portion. Reflecting thus, one attains freedom from pride. Tenth, one reflects:
"All sentient beings harbor anger and resentment toward me, yet I always practice patient endurance. Reflecting thus, one attains freedom from pride.
"Good son! These are the ten dharmas which a bodhisattva contemplates; when they are fully perfected, one is able to accomplish a mind free from pride.
Furthermore, good son!"
If Bodhisattvas possess ten dharmas that are fully perfected, they will attain a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings.
What are these ten? First, they act with impartiality toward all sentient beings.
Second, having no hindrance in one's mind toward all sentient beings;
third, having no weariness in one's mind toward all sentient beings;
fourth, fully practicing the six pāramitās for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.
Fifth, for the sake of all sentient beings, they gather all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvajñā*), yet they do not rely upon the characteristic of non-duality;
sixth, they universally observe that sentient beings are identical to suchness (*tathatā*), remaining free from discrimination;
seventh, they thoroughly comprehend that the essential nature of sentient beings is equal, and are thus able to realize and enter the mind-nature of equality.
Eighth, may they vow that all sentient beings together attain liberation from the great fire of birth and death;
ninth, having themselves attained liberation, may they further be able to pull out all sentient beings;
tenth, may they impartially establish all sentient beings in a state free from sorrow and affliction.
“Good son! It is like a householder or a layman in the world who fathers five sons, loving them equally and providing them with resources and necessities without any distinction;
yet those sons are foolish, young, and ignorant, unable to discern anything for themselves in any situation.”
At that time, a fire suddenly broke out within the house of that elder, and his sons were each staying in different places.
"Good son, what do you think?"
"At that time, did that elder have a preference among his sons' minds, such that there was a sequence of priority?
Sudhana replied, "That elder’s mind was equal toward them all without priority; he rescued and delivered whichever one approached him first."
Mañjuśrī said: "Good son, it is the same for the bodhisattva-mahāsattva."

All sentient beings dwell within the house of birth and death; there, the fierce fires of the three poisons suddenly arise. Their minds are ignorant and dark, devoid of discernment, as each is born into one of the five destinies according to the power of their karma.

Bodhisattvas, with an impartial mind, tame and bring them to maturity; yet, they first rescue and mature those whom they encounter through close association, establishing them within the realm of tranquility.
“Good son! These are the ten dharmas by which a bodhisattva is fully perfected and achieves equanimity toward all sentient beings.
Furthermore, good son!”
If Bodhisattvas possess ten dharmas that are fully perfected, they shall achieve the practice of making true offerings to all Tathāgatas.
What are these ten?
First, making offerings through the Dharma;
second, practicing all forms of conduct;
third, impartially benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings.
Fourth, to gather others through compliance with a heart of compassion;
fifth, to comply with all things through the power of the Tathāgata;
sixth, not to abandon the exhortation to cultivate all wholesome dharmas.
Seventh, not abandoning any bodhisattva activity;
eighth, being able to act according to what one says and being able to speak according to how one acts;
ninth, cultivating [the path] extensively over a long period of time with a mind free from weariness.
Tenth, one never abandons the great bodhicitta.
If bodhisattvas possess these ten dharmas, they are able to accomplish the offering to the Tathāgata;
it is not by means of wealth, food, drink, or clothing that one is called a true offering.
Why is this? Because the Tathāgata reveres and honors the Dharma;
just as a filial son honors his parents, following their countenance and never for a moment letting his mind stray from them.
Furthermore, if there is a person who honors their parents, their children will in turn respect that person even more;
the Tathāgatas, the Buddhas, are likewise so.
If sentient beings make offerings to the Dharma, they truly accomplish the offering to the Tathāgatas, because the Tathāgatas hold the Dharma in the highest esteem.
"Good son! The Tathāgata comes from the midst of practice;
if one can practice, this constitutes the accomplishment of making offerings to the Tathāgata."
The appearance of the Buddhas in the world is fundamentally for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings;
it is for the sake of gathering in sentient beings through compassion;
and it is for the sake of providing the power that accords with, facilitates, and brings them joy.
Good son! If one does not encourage the cultivation of all wholesome dharmas, nor bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings;
and if one abandons the deeds practiced by a bodhisattva, then one likewise cannot bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
Furthermore, if one cannot practice as taught, nor teach as one practices, one will likewise be unable to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings;
if the mind becomes inferior and gives rise to weariness and aversion, one will likewise be unable to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings;
and if one momentarily abandons the bodhicitta, one will likewise be unable to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
Why is this? Good son!

For a bodhisattva, desiring to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, diligently seeks anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; if there were no sentient beings, no bodhisattva would ever achieve perfect enlightenment.
"Good son! You should understand the offering of Dharma in this way; only then will you achieve the fulfillment of making offerings to the Tathāgata.
It is not by means of worldly wealth, treasures, food, or drink that one is said to make an offering."
“Good son! These are the ten dharmas by which a bodhisattva is fully endowed and can thus accomplish the making of offerings to the Tathāgata.

At that time, Mañjuśrī, having revealed such immeasurable and boundless subtle and wondrous meanings of the Dharma and having exhorted Sudhana to practice them, withdrew his supernormal power and suddenly disappeared.
At that time, the youth Sudhana saw as many spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm; he approached, served, and made offerings to them all, causing them to rejoice.
He followed and practiced their instructions, increasing and seeking after the intent for omniscience (sarvajñatā). He gave rise to a resolute understanding regarding the realm of the Buddha;

the ocean of his great compassion (mahākaruṇā-citta) became vast enough to contain and give birth to all things, while the clouds of his great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) universally covered everything. Toward the vast cloud-like body of Vairocana, he increased his love and reverence.

They dwell with minds always settled in the unimpeded liberations of all bodhisattvas; they swiftly give birth to the Tathāgata’s pure eye of universal non-attachment, observing the great ocean of perfected merit and virtue cultivated by all Buddhas; they have deep faith in the essence of omniscience developed through the Tathāgata’s accumulation of practices; they diligently and swiftly increase the dharmas that assist the path to omniscience; they are skillfully able to dedicate [merit] toward the pure and profound resolve of all bodhisattvas; they well understand the uninterrupted succession of all Tathāgatas throughout the three periods of time; they enter deeply into the ocean of the teachings of all Buddha-dharmas; and they accord with and comprehend the wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas.

They appear universally throughout all worlds like reflections; they enter deeply into the ocean of all bodhisattva vows; they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all kalpas; they attain the wisdom of universal gates and illumine the realm of the Tathāgatas; they increase all the faculties of bodhisattvas and obtain the pure radiance of omniscience, which shines universally upon all dharma-realms in the ten directions;
in all lands, they teach and transform sentient beings, giving rise to the mind of practice and accomplishing their benefit;
they are able to accord with and understand the various types of birth and death, and they shatter the mountains of all obstacles consisting of afflictions and karma.

In accordance with the realization of unobstructed dharmas, they enter the ground of equality within the treasury of the dharma-realm; they abide eternally in the liberation of bodhisattvas that is quiescent, diligently seek the spheres of all Tathāgatas, and are sustained by the majestic empowerment of all Buddhas.

The youth Sudhana engaged in such subtle observations and dwelt in the profound realm of Samantabhadra; he then heard the name of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, as well as his Samantabhadra-conduct and supreme great vows;
from the initial resolve, the most excellent aids to the path, the most excellent manifest production of merit, and his subtle deportment;

and he heard of all the stages of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, including the locations of those stages, the distinctions between them, the mastery of conduct within the stages, the distinct dwellings of the stages, the valor of the stages, the majesty of the stages, and the common abiding of the stages.
Having heard this, he yearned with thirsting longing to see Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Thereupon,
before the Tathāgata’s lion throne in the Vajra-ocean-treasury Bodhimanda, upon a seat of universal jewel-lotus treasury,
he gave rise to a mind as vast as the realm of empty space, a mind that uproots all present attachments, and a mind that gathers into one...
A mind untainted by any virtues; a mind free of conceptualization regarding the purification of all buddha-fields; a mind of joy that comprehends all phenomena;
a mind unimpeded in observing all objects; a mind that pervades all directions; a mind unobstructed in performing all practices;
a mind of sovereign mastery in sublime conduct within the sphere of all-knowledge; and a mind that contemplates the one...
The mind that clearly understands and purifies the adornments of all bodhisattva sites of enlightenment; the vast mind that enters deeply into the ocean of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas;
the pervasive mind that tames and brings to maturity all sentient beings; the immeasurable mind that purifies all Buddha-fields;
the mind that understands all assemblies to be like reflections; and the mind that abides through all kalpas without...
Exerting their whole hearts, they brought to ultimate fulfillment the Tathāgata’s powers, fearlessnesses, and unique Buddha-dharmas, as well as the mind of non-retrogression.
Because he was moistened by his own roots of goodness, and because of the empowering grace of all the Tathāgatas, the youth Sudhana gave rise to such a mind.
Due to the power of the roots of goodness shared with Samantabhadra,
there are ten kinds of auspicious signs when one wishes to see Samantabhadra. What are these ten?
First, seeing all Buddha-fields as pure, with the adornments of the bodhimaṇḍas of all Tathāgatas;
second, seeing all Buddha-fields as pure, devoid of all evil realms and various heterogeneous beings;
third, seeing all Buddha-fields as pure, adorned with various wondrous lotus flowers.
Fourth, they see all Buddha-fields as pure, and all sentient beings with bodies and minds cooled and refreshed;
fifth, they see all Buddha-fields as pure, having various jewels as their substance, adorned with colors and forms;
sixth, they see all Buddha-fields as pure, with all sentient beings having their bodies adorned with various colors, forms, and marks of excellence.
Seventh, they see all Buddha-fields as pure, with clouds of various adornments universally covering them;
eighth, they see all Buddha-fields as pure, where all sentient beings give rise to mutual compassion and benefit one another;
ninth, they see all Buddha-fields as pure, with the physical forms of the bodhimaṇḍas magnificently adorned.
Tenth, they see all Buddha-fields as pure, and their minds always accord with and mindfully recollect all Buddhas;
these are the ten.
Furthermore, they see ten kinds of signs of great radiance. What are the ten?
First, he saw from within every single atom of all worlds emerge clouds of light-nets of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, shining everywhere;

second, he saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of circular halos of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, infinite and countless, with various colors and forms pervading the entire Dharma-realm;
third, he saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of various precious images of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
Fourth, he saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of various wheels of light-flames of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm;

fifth, he saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of various exquisite incenses, ointments, burning perfumes, and flower garlands, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading all Dharma-realms throughout the ten directions and emitting great sounds that praise the vast ocean of merit of all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra;

sixth, he saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of various suns, moons, stars, and luminosity, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, all radiating the light of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and filling the entire Dharma-realm.

Seventh, they saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of lamps in the forms of all kinds of sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, which, like the light of a Buddha, universally illumined the Dharma-realm;

eighth, they saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of mani-jewels reflecting the images of the bodies of all Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the entire Dharma-realm;

ninth, they saw from within each and every atom emerge clouds of radiant bodies manifesting the images of all Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, like a great rain from vast clouds, universally proclaiming the great vows and the power of majesty of all Tathāgatas.

Tenth: within each and every atom, one sees clouds of bodies that are images of the perfect radiance of all manner of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, manifesting various transformations according to the needs of sentient beings so that all may give rise to love and joy; such deeds pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
This is the tenth.
At that time, having seen these ten kinds of radiant signs, the youth Sudhana thought to himself:
"I shall now certainly behold the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra."
At that time, Sudhana dwelt in the power of the universal illumination of his own roots of goodness; he dwelt in the power of the protective mindfulness of all Tathāgatas;
he was able to produce the light of universal wisdom of the Buddha-dharma, which clearly illuminated the practices of Samantabhadra before him;
and he deeply entered the boundless vows of Samantabhadra.
With deep faith and understanding in the realm of all Tathāgatas;

having attained the power of certainty regarding the vast realm of all Bodhisattvas, they cultivate and realize the perception of Samantabhadra; they enter deeply into the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes, universally gathering and pacifying all the sense faculties; they give rise to great diligence without regression, manifesting their bodies and minds throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
and with the universal eye, they observe all Buddhas, the assemblies of Bodhisattvas, and all manner of adornments in the ten directions.
Regarding all objective realms, one should cultivate the perception that they are all the manifestation of Samantabhadra;

with the eye of wisdom, one observes the path traversed by Samantabhadra from his first resolution for enlightenment—his mind vast as space, his great compassion firm as a diamond, and his majestic power sustaining all through the limits of the future—vowing never to abandon the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra with a mind of equanimity, in every thought-moment conforming to pure sovereignty, always dwelling securely in the realm of the Tathāgata, and accomplishing the various stages of wisdom of Samantabhadra.
Having thus observed with complete perfection,

the youth Sudhana saw the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra before the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana, seated upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury, surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas;
his physical form was extraordinary and peerless in the world, and his various spheres of wisdom and merit were inconceivable.
All Bodhisattvas observe this with subtle discernment; it is boundless and equal to all Tathāgatas, without distinction.

Sudhana saw that from every single pore of Samantabhadra’s body, in every moment of thought, there issued forth clouds of various radiances as numerous as the atoms within all worlds, pervading the Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and all worlds, universally illuminating and extinguishing the suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings.

He saw that from every single pore, in every moment of thought, there issued forth clouds of circular halos of various colors as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, causing all Bodhisattvas to swiftly increase their vast and great joy.

He saw that from every single pore on the crown of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s head and his two shoulders, there issued forth, in every thought-moment, clouds of various colored fragrant flames as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands; these pervaded the entire Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas, raining down great showers of fragrance that universally perfumed them.

He saw that from every single pore, in every thought-moment, there issued forth clouds of various flowers as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands; these pervaded the entire Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, raining down a multitude of wondrous blossoms.

In every single pore, in every thought-moment, he saw clouds of variously adorned incense trees, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, emerge and pervade the entire Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and all the assembly sites of the Tathāgatas, raining down inexhaustible ointments, powdered incenses, and treasuries of manifold exquisite fragrances;

in every single pore, in every thought-moment, he saw clouds of various garments, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, emerge and pervade the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, raining down myriad exquisite robes that universally cover and adorn all.

In every single pore, in every thought-moment, he saw clouds of various silken banners as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands, clouds of various miscellaneous jewel necklaces, and clouds of various wish-fulfilling jewels emerge, pervading the Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas. They universally rained down all manner of necklaces and silken banners, causing all sentient beings to achieve joy and delight.

In every single pore, in every thought-moment, he saw clouds of various jewel trees as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands emerge, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space. Furthermore, from within the treasuries of all these jewel trees, clouds of light from all the stars flowed forth in various adornments, raining down exquisite jewels upon the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.

He saw from every single pore, in every moment of thought, clouds of bodies of various gods of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields emerging and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of space, praising the bodhicitta;

he saw from every single pore, in every moment of thought, clouds of bodies of various Brahma-heaven retinues as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields emerging and requesting all Tathāgatas to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma;

he saw from every single pore, in every moment of thought, clouds of bodies of various gods of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields emerging and protecting and upholding the sublime Dharma spoken by all Tathāgatas.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of all Buddha-fields throughout the three periods of time, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space; these provided support for those beings who had no support, protection for those who had no protection, and a refuge for those who had no refuge.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of pure Buddha-fields, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, emerging moment by moment and pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space; therein all Buddhas appeared, along with assemblies of Bodhisattvas and pure sites of enlightenment, causing all sentient beings to love, respect, believe in, and delight in them, so that they all attained purity.

He saw that from every single pore, in every moment of thought, there issued forth clouds of pure and impure Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, causing all defiled sentient beings to attain purity;

he saw that from every single pore, in every moment of thought, there issued forth clouds of impure and pure Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, causing all purely defiled sentient beings to attain purity;

he saw that from every single pore, in every moment of thought, there issued forth clouds of the bodies of sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, teaching and transforming all sentient beings according to their needs, causing them to reach maturity in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

In every single pore, he saw clouds of various bodhisattva bodies, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, emerging moment by moment and pervading the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, extolling the various names of all Buddhas and causing all sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness;

in every single pore, he saw clouds of various bodhisattva bodies, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, emerging moment by moment and pervading the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, proclaiming and manifesting the roots of goodness produced by all Buddhas and bodhisattvas from their first resolve through the purification of their buddha-fields.

He saw from each and every pore, in every thought-moment, emerge clouds of various Bodhisattva bodies as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, pervading all Buddha-lands throughout the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space; in each and every land, they proclaimed the ocean of all Bodhisattva vows in order to purify the sublime practices of Samantabhadra.

He saw from each and every pore, in every thought-moment, emerge clouds of the practices of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, causing all sentient beings to joyfully cultivate them and swiftly attain the perfection of the essence of omniscience.

In every single pore, within each and every thought-moment, he beholds clouds of bodies of perfect enlightenment, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, emerging from them; these manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment in all Buddha-fields, displaying the knowledge of all modes, causing all bodhisattvas to universally assemble the Great Dharma, swiftly increase their realization, and attain immediate awakening.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Thirty-Eight;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Thirty-Nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation," at that time,
the youth Sudhana, beholding such a sphere of the sovereign spiritual powers of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, was filled with joy and leaped for gladness, pervading his entire body and mind.
Observing again and yet again, he saw that within each and every part of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s body, each and every limb and joint, and each and every pore, there were entire trichiliocosms.

Within it, all things—the great oceans of earth, water, fire, and wind; the four continents; Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, and the various jewel mountains; lands, cities, palaces, gardens, and groves; even the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, and King Yama; the eight classes of devas and nāgas, humans and non-humans; all forms and colors existing within the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; the sun, moon, and stars; wind, clouds, thunder, and lightning; day and night, months, seasons, and years and kalpas; the appearance of Buddhas in the world, the assemblies of bodhisattvas, and the adornments of the sites of enlightenment—all such matters were clearly seen.
Just as this world is seen to end in the eastern direction, so it is with all various worlds.
As it is in the east, so it is in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.

Just as one sees the present worlds of the ten directions, so too does one see all worlds throughout the limits of the past and the limits of the future, continuing in succession without interruption.
Each is distinct yet mutually interpenetrates one another without becoming confused.

Just as these playful supernatural powers are manifested here upon this Lion Throne of the Jewel Lotus Treasury of Vairocana Tathāgata, so too are all such playful supernatural powers manifested at the abode of the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī in the world Padmaśrī to the east; it is exactly the same.

Just as it was in the presence of the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī, so it was throughout the eastern direction, and likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—in all worlds, it was exactly the same.

In this way, within every single atom of all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions, there are assemblies of Buddhas of the entire Dharma-realm; at each Buddha’s location, Samantabhadra sits upon a lion throne of precious lotus flowers, manifesting all manner of playful supernatural powers—all of which are likewise thus.
Furthermore, within each and every body of Samantabhadra, one perceives all realms of the three periods of time, appearing like reflections in a clear mirror;
namely: all Buddha-lands, all requisites, all sentient beings, the appearance of all Buddhas, and the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, they hear the various sounds of all sentient beings; the sounds of all Buddhas; the sounds of all Tathāgatas turning the wheel of Dharma; the sounds of all Tathāgatas sporting in supernatural powers;

and the sounds of all Bodhisattvas’ skillful exhortations and instructions—namely, such sounds as the supernatural realms of all Bodhisattvas, the wisdom-powers of Bodhisattvas, the universal assemblies of Bodhisattvas, the preaching of the Dharma by Bodhisattvas, and the playful manifestations of Bodhisattvas.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having seen and heard of such immeasurable and inconceivable playful supernatural powers of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, immediately attained ten kinds of wisdom-paramitas. What are these ten?
First, the perfection of wisdom that causes the body to pervade all Buddha-fields in every moment of thought;
second, the perfection of wisdom that is able to go to the presence of all Buddhas in every moment of thought;
third, the perfection of wisdom that is able to make offerings to all Tathāgatas in every moment of thought.
Fourth is the perfection of wisdom of hearing, receiving, and upholding the Dharma from all Tathāgatas throughout every thought-moment;
fifth is the perfection of wisdom of subtly observing all the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas throughout every thought-moment;
sixth is the perfection of wisdom of knowing the inconceivable matters of the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas throughout every thought-moment.
Seventh is the perfection of wisdom of inexhaustible eloquence, which expounds a single phrase of Dharma in every thought-moment until the end of the future;
eighth is the perfection of wisdom that contemplates all phenomena with the ocean of wisdom manifesting before one in every thought-moment;
ninth is the perfection of wisdom that attains the ocean of teachings of the entire dharma-realm in every thought-moment.
Tenth, the perfection of wisdom that, in every moment of thought, knows how to cause all sentient beings to be free from the notion of "sentient being";
eleventh, the perfection of wisdom that, in every moment of thought, brings before one the conduct of Samantabhadra’s wisdom.

Once the youth Sudhana had obtained this, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva extended his right hand and stroked Sudhana’s crown; Sudhana immediately attained profound entry into as many great samādhis as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields.
Each [samādhi] has as its retinue as many samādhis as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields;
within each and every samādhi, one attains all the various oceans of worlds— as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields— which were never before seen or heard,
and beholds the great assemblies of Buddhas therein, increasing the lineage of all Buddhas.
The aids to omniscience, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, manifest; the dharma-gates of omniscience, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, appear;
the initial arousal of the mind toward omniscience, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, is accomplished;
and the great vows of omniscience, as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, are deeply entered.
Oceans [of merit], giving birth to the paths of transcendence for all-knowledge as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields;
practicing the bodhisattva conduct of all-knowledge as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields;
perfecting the powers of swiftness of all-knowledge as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields; and attaining [the qualities] of all Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms...
The light of universal illumination of all-knowledge, as numerous as atoms, shines everywhere;

just as the Dharma-door obtained by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra when he rubbed the crown of Sudhana’s head at the place of Vairocana Buddha in this Sahā world, so too, in all worlds throughout the ten directions, and within every single atom of those worlds, in all worlds and at the places of all Buddhas, the Dharma-doors obtained by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra when he likewise rubbed the crown of Sudhana’s head are exactly equal.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed Sudhana, saying: "Good son!
Do you see this power of my spiritual transformations?"
Sudhana replied, "Noble One! Indeed, I have seen it."
"This matter of inconceivable great supernormal power can only be known by one who has attained the wisdom of a Buddha.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said to Sudhana: "Good man!"
Throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons, I have practiced the bodhisattva path, seeking all-knowledge;
in each and every eon, for the sake of purifying the bodhicitta, I have served unspeakably unspeakable Tathāgatas;

and in each and every eon, for the sake of accumulating the merit and virtue necessary for all-knowledge, I have established unspeakably unspeakable assemblies of vast giving, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields, which are supreme and peerless in all worlds, all of which I have dedicated to all sentient beings.

In each and every eon, for the sake of seeking the dharma of omniscience, he practiced great renunciation by giving away wealth and possessions as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;

in each and every eon, for the sake of seeking the wisdom of a Buddha, he gave as alms lands, royal thrones, villages, camps, cities, towns, settlements, palaces, wives, children, retinues, and even his own body, limbs, members, eyes, ears, noses, tongues, and even his very life, all as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
in each and every eon, for the sake of seeking the head of omniscience, he gave as alms heads as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

In each and every eon, for the sake of seeking all-knowledge, he reverently honored, respected, served, and made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, presenting them with the finest garments, bedding, and medicines, and providing everything they required. Within their teachings, he left the household life to study the Path, upholding the Dharma instructions and practicing in accordance with them.
“Good son! Throughout those oceans of great kalpas, I recall that never for even a single thought-moment have I failed to accord with the Buddha’s teachings.

During those kalpas, I have never for a single thought-moment given rise to a mind of anger or harm, nor a mind of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’ nor a mind of distinction between self and others. Never for a single thought-moment have I been separated from the bodhicitta, nor have I given rise to weariness within saṃsāra, nor a base mind, nor a mind of indolence, nor a mind of obstruction, nor a mind of delusion.”
Abiding solely in the unsurpassed, indestructible nature of omniscience, the Great Bodhicitta. Good son!
I universally purify all Buddha-fields; with great compassion, I rescue and protect sentient beings, teaching and transforming them to bring them to maturity and purity.

I have made offerings to and served all Buddhas and all spiritual friends; in the presence of those Buddhas and spiritual friends, for the sake of seeking the True Dharma, I have propagated, proclaimed, and protected it, being able to relinquish everything internal and external, even my own body and life, without any stinginess.

Such practices of immeasurable, corresponding perfection—were one to explain their causes and conditions throughout oceans of kalpas, those oceans of kalpas might come to an end, but these [practices] could never be exhausted.

"Good son! Within the ocean of my Dharma, there is not a single word or a single phrase that was not sought by relinquishing the rank of a Wheel-Turning King, nor was it sought without relinquishing all that one possesses."

"Good son! The Dharma I seek is solely for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings. With continuous mindfulness, I observe with subtle discernment so that the most supreme Dharma may swiftly manifest before me.

I vow to illuminate and reveal all worlds with the light of wisdom; I vow to manifest supramundane knowledge; I vow to cause all sentient beings to attain peace and happiness; and I vow to universally praise all the merits of all Tathāgatas."

Such gateways of practices corresponding to my past perfections as these could not be fully described even in an ocean of eons as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Therefore, noble son!

By means of the power of having thus accumulated the factors conducive to the path, the power of increasing all roots of goodness, the power of vast and profound faith, the power of practicing all meritorious virtues, the power of observing all phenomena as they truly are, the power of accomplishing the eye of all-encompassing wisdom, the power of being sustained by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, the power evoked by various great vows, the immovable power of boundless great compassion, the power of the supernormal knowledge that can completely purify sublime wisdom, and the power of being sustained by various spiritual friends;

by these and other such powers, I have attained this ultimate, pure Dharma-body equal throughout the three periods of time, as well as the unsurpassed, pure form-body that transcends all worlds, yet manifests forms everywhere in accordance with the diverse inclinations and joys of sentient beings.
Entering all lands and pervading all places, he is universally able to manifest spiritual powers in accordance with the needs of beings, causing all sentient beings to rejoice without exception.
"O son of good family!
"Do you see this body of mine, which is perfect, vast, and majestic?
You should contemplate and observe it with subtle discernment. Noble son!"

This wondrous body of mine has been accomplished over an ocean of boundless eons; it is difficult to appear and difficult to behold throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of eons.
Good son! If there are sentient beings who have not planted roots of goodness or have planted only few roots of goodness, they do not even hear my name, let alone see my body.
"Good son! If there are sentient beings who hear my name, they shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Whether they see me, or think of me, or welcome me, or see me off, or follow me for even a brief moment, or even in their dreams, it shall be the same for them all."
There are sentient beings who, by recollecting me for a single day and night and practicing in accordance with that, attain maturity;

or those who attain maturity by recollecting me for seven days and nights, half a month, one month, half a year, one year, a hundred years, a thousand years, one eon, a hundred eons, or even for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
or those who attain maturity by recollecting me for a single lifetime, a hundred lifetimes, or even for as many lifetimes as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Whether they see my halo, or see me emitting light, or see my physical body, or see my supernormal powers shaking the Buddha-fields, or feel fear, or feel joy—they all attain maturity.
"Good son! By means of such skillful gates as these, numbering as many as the atoms within Buddha-fields, I cause all sentient beings to attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Furthermore, good son!
If there are sentient beings who see or hear of my pure land, they will certainly be born within my pure land;
if there are sentient beings who see or hear of my pure body, they will certainly be born within my pure body."
"Good son! You should observe this body of mine, which possesses great majesty and is utterly pure.
At that time, the youth Sudhana minutely observed the body of Samantabhadra and saw within each and every pore unspeakably unspeakable oceans of Buddha-fields.
In each and every ocean of lands, Buddhas appear in the world, filling them entirely, surrounded by oceans of assemblies of great Bodhisattvas;

those oceans of lands have various foundations, various shapes, various adornments, and are encircled by various great mountains; they are covered above by various clouds of colors, and there are various appearances of Buddhas and various preachings of the Dharma—such matters as these are each different.
As it is with one pore, so it is with all pores, with each of the primary marks, with each of the secondary signs, and with every single limb and joint—all are likewise thus.

Furthermore, he saw Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, from within each and every ocean of worlds, manifest clouds of transformation bodies of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings, causing them to attain maturity in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, because the youth Sudhana followed the skillful guidance and instruction of Samantabhadra, he entered the body of Samantabhadra and into all the worlds within the pores of his hair throughout the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings.

Furthermore, the roots of goodness and the light of wisdom accumulated and increased by the youth Sudhana as he visited, approached, served, and made offerings to as many spiritual friends as there are atoms in a Buddha-field do not equal even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, nor even a hundred-thousand-billionth part, nor any numerical, calculable, fractional, or *upaniṣad* part of the roots of goodness obtained by merely seeing Samantabhadra Bodhisattva for a moment.
From the time the youth Sudhana first resolved upon enlightenment until he beheld Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the oceans of lands he entered during that interval were continuous and uninterrupted;

yet now, within a single pore of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the oceans of Buddha-lands he enters in a single thought-moment are continuous and uninterrupted, exceeding the former by unspeakably unspeakable multiples. As it is with one pore, so it is with all pores.

When the youth Sudhana took a single step within the world-systems of the pores of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, he passed through worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields. Traveling in this manner until the end of all future kalpas, he would still be unable to know the limits of the various oceans of lands within a single pore—their continuous succession, their treasuries, their distinctions, their gateways of emergence, their formation, their destruction, and their adornments;

nor could he know the limits of the oceans of Buddhas appearing therein—their continuous succession, their treasuries of appearance, their distinctions, their gateways of emergence, their birth, and their cessation.

Furthermore, they cannot know the limits of the continuous succession of the ocean-like assemblies of bodhisattvas at the site of enlightenment; nor can they know the ocean-treasury of the assembly of bodhisattvas, the distinctions within the ocean of the assembly of bodhisattvas, the gateways for the emergence of the ocean of the assembly of bodhisattvas, the gathering of the ocean of the assembly of bodhisattvas, or the dispersal of the ocean of the assembly of bodhisattvas.

Nor can they know their entry into the realms of sentient beings, their knowledge of the faculties of sentient beings, their teaching and taming of all realms of sentient beings, or the wisdom that awakens and matures all sentient beings. They likewise cannot know the sovereign supernormal powers in which bodhisattvas dwell, nor the various stages and paths entered by bodhisattvas;
regarding such oceans as these, they are entirely unable to know their ultimate limits.

Within the lands within the pores of Samantabhadra, the youth Sudhana traveled for a single day in some lands, or for one year in others, continuing in this manner until for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands;
yet he neither moved nor departed, but in every thought-moment pervaded the boundless ocean of lands, teaching and taming all sentient beings, leading them toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the youth Sudhana sequentially attained the ocean of all practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, all of which were entirely equal:

equal to Samantabhadra; equal to all Buddhas; equal in a single body filling all worlds; equal in the perfection of all practices; equal in the manifestation of perfect enlightenment; equal in the great functioning of supernormal powers; equal in various wheels of Dharma; equal in pure eloquence; equal in the production of speech; equal in various sounds; equal in the powers and fearlessnesses; equal in various Buddha-abodes; and equal in great kindness and great compassion;
thus, even unto inconceivable liberation and mastery, they were all entirely equal.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra surveyed the entire assembly of bodhisattvas and the youth Sudhana, and spoke these verses:
“You all should cast off the stains of doubt, And listen with single-minded concentration and without distraction.
I shall speak of the Tathāgata’s fulfillment of all perfections, The true path to universal liberation.”
The supramundane, well-tamed, and supreme Great Being, whose mind is as pure as space,
constantly radiates the great light of the sun of wisdom, universally illuminating the world and dispelling the darkness of delusion.
The Tathāgata is difficult to see or hear; after immeasurable billions of kalpas, he is now encountered.
Like the udumbara flower appearing but once in an age, one should therefore listen to the virtues of the Buddha.
Conforming to all the activities of the world, like a conjured being manifesting various deeds,
he acts solely to gladden the minds of sentient beings, never giving rise to a single thought of discrimination.
At that time, having heard these words, all the bodhisattvas, with single-minded longing and devotion, made great vows, desiring to hear the merits of the Tathāgata’s true meaning and reality.

They all thought: “The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra has perfected all practices; his essential nature is pure; he acts according to what he says, and speaks according to what he does; he is praised by all the Tathāgatas.”
Having formed this thought, they gave rise to a profound yearning and reverence.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—perfected in all manner of merit and adorned with wisdom, his body and mind like a lotus flower, unstained by any of the defilements of the triple world—addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"All of you should listen with single-minded attention; I now wish to speak of a single drop from the ocean of the Buddha’s merits."
Then he spoke these verses:
“The Buddha’s wisdom is as vast and equal as space, Pervading the minds of all sentient beings.
He understands that worldly delusions are entirely non-existent, And thus gives rise to no various discriminatory thoughts.”
In a single thought-moment, they fully know the dharmas of the three periods of time, And likewise comprehend the faculties of all sentient beings;
Like a skillful master of great illusion, They manifest boundless manifestations in every thought-moment.
According to the diverse mental activities of sentient beings, And by the power of their past karma, vows, and aspirations, What they perceive each differs;
Yet the Buddha remains tranquil, without a single stirring thought.
In some places, one sees Buddhas seated, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions;
yet others, whose minds are not pure, do not see a Buddha for immeasurable eons.
But those who possess the resolute understanding that there is no self may, in a single thought-moment, give rise to the vision of the Tathāgata.
Some, possessing a defiled mind of flattery and deception, may seek with single-minded devotion for billions of eons yet be unable to encounter him;
others hear the Buddha’s voice in every place, its exquisite melody gladdening the heart.
Yet some, despite hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons, do not hear it because their minds are impure.
Or one may see great Bodhisattvas of pure virtue, filling the three thousandfold world system;
having all fully perfected the practices of Samantabhadra, the Tathāgata sits majestically amidst them.
Some see this realm as peerless and sublime, adorned and purified by the Buddha over immeasurable eons;
therein, the most supreme Honored One, Vairocana, awakened and attained Bodhi.
Or one may see a supreme and wondrous lotus land, where the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī dwells,
surrounded by an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas, all of whom diligently cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra.
Some see the Buddha Amitāyus, surrounded by Avalokiteśvara and others,
all of whom abide in the stage of consecration, pervading the infinite lands of the ten directions.
Some may see this trichiliocosm as being fully adorned like the Land of Wonderful Joy,
with the Tathāgata Akṣobhya dwelling within it, together with bodhisattvas such as Gandhahastin.
Some see the Great Renowned Moon-Awakened One, together with Bodhisattvas such as Vajradhvaja,
abiding in a sublime adornment like a perfect mirror, pervading the pure lands throughout the ten directions.
Or they see the World-Honored One, Sūryagarbha, dwelling in the pure land of Universal Radiance,
surrounded by bodhisattvas who have received empowerment, filling the ten directions as he preaches the Dharma.
In some places he sees the Buddha Great Blazing Vajra, together with Bodhisattvas such as Jñānaketu,
traveling throughout all vast lands, preaching the Dharma to eliminate the darkness of sentient beings.
Upon each and every tip of a hair, unspeakably many Buddhas, endowed with the thirty-two marks,
are surrounded by assemblies of bodhisattvas, preaching various teachings to deliver sentient beings.
In each and every pore of the Buddhas, I see vast lands fully adorned;
within them dwell immeasurable Buddhas, filled with pure sons of the Buddha.
Or one may see the equal realms of the ten directions, all contained within a single atom;
therein dwell immeasurable bodhisattvas, who have cultivated all practices for unspeakable eons.
Some see, within the space of a single hair-tip, Immeasurable oceans of lands of subtle atoms,
Each distinct according to the various karmas that arise, Where Vairocana turns the wheel of Dharma.
Some worlds are impure, while some pure lands are formed of various jewels;
the Tathāgata dwells for immeasurable eons, manifesting all manner of deeds even unto his parinirvāṇa.
Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they manifest various inconceivable displays;
according to the differences in the mental capacities and wisdom of sentient beings, there are none whom they do not transform and purify.
Thus the Unsurpassed Great Tamer pervades the lands of the ten directions;
manifesting various supernormal powers, I shall speak of but a small portion—listen now.
Some see Śākyamuni having already attained the Way of Buddhahood after inconceivable eons;
some see him now just beginning as a bodhisattva, benefiting all sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
and some see this Lion of the Śākyas making offerings to various Buddhas while practicing the Path.
Sometimes they see the Most Honored One among men manifesting various supernatural powers;
sometimes they see him practicing giving or maintaining the precepts, or patience, diligence, or the various dhyānas;
through wisdom, skillful means, vows, power, and knowledge, he manifests everything in accordance with the minds of sentient beings.
Some see the ultimate perfection, while others see them dwelling securely in the various stages;
the dhāraṇīs, samādhis, supernormal powers, and wisdom—all these are manifested without exception.
Some manifest practicing for immeasurable eons, abiding in the bodhisattva stage of endurance;
some are seen abiding on the stage of non-retrogression; some manifest the dharma-water being poured upon their crowns;
some manifest the bodies of Brahmā, Śakra, or the World-Protectors; and some manifest as kṣatriyas or brahmins.
Adorned with various forms and marks, he is like a magician manifesting many images:
sometimes appearing as he first descends from Tuṣita; sometimes seen within the palace among his consorts;
sometimes seen renouncing all worldly splendors and leaving the royal palace to practice the Way.
Some see him at birth, others see his passing; some see him manifesting renunciation and practicing extraordinary conduct;
some see him seated beneath the Bodhi tree, subduing the demonic armies and attaining perfect enlightenment;
some see the Buddha’s initial entry into parinirvāṇa, while others see stūpas arising throughout the world.
Sometimes one sees an image standing within a stūpa; Or he manifests various forms and colors according to sentient beings.
Sometimes one sees the Tathāgata Amitāyus Bestowing the sublime prediction upon all bodhisattvas, Becoming a true and great guide, Next to succeed him in abiding in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Some see him, throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, having performed the work of a Buddha and entered parinirvāṇa;
some see him now first attaining bodhi; some see him correctly practicing all sublime deeds;
some see the Tathāgata, the pure moon, dwelling in the Brahma world or the palace of Māra.
In the palace of Īśvara and the Tuṣita heaven, he manifests various kinds of supernatural transformations.
Sometimes he is seen in the Tuṣita palace, surrounded by immeasurable devas;
for their sake he preaches the Dharma to bring them joy, as all with pure hearts make offerings to the Buddha.
Or seen dwelling in the Yāma Heaven, In the realms of the Trāyastriṃśa, the World-Protectors, and the nāgas;
In all such celestial palaces, There is not one in which his image does not appear.
Or, at the presence of the World-Honored One Dīpaṃkara, He scattered flowers and spread his hair as an offering;
From that time forth, he realized the profound and wondrous Dharma, And constantly used this path to transform all living beings.
Some see him as having entered parinirvāṇa long ago; some see him as having first attained bodhi;
some see him dwelling for immeasurable kalpas; and some see him entering extinction in a mere moment.
His physical marks, radiance, and lifespan, his wisdom, bodhi, and nirvāṇa—[all are seen thus].
The majestic deportment and voices that transform the assemblies—each and every one of these is immeasurable.
Some manifest bodies of extreme vastness, like the great jewel mountain Sumeru;
others are seen sitting cross-legged, unmoving, filling boundless worlds.
Some see a halo extending one fathom; some see it spanning thousands, tens of thousands, and millions of yojanas;
some see it illuminating immeasurable lands, or see it filling all buddha-fields.
Some see the Buddha’s lifespan as eighty years; others see it lasting hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, and billions of years.
Some may abide for inconceivable eons, and thus successively doubling beyond this.
The Buddha’s wisdom penetrates all with purity and non-obstruction; in a single kṣaṇa, he universally comprehends the dharmas of the three periods of time.
All arise from the causes and conditions of mind and consciousness; they are subject to arising and ceasing, impermanent, and devoid of self-nature.
Attaining perfect enlightenment within a single land, so it is in all lands;
each enters into every other, manifesting in accordance with the minds of sentient beings.
The Tathāgata abides in the unsurpassed path, Having accomplished the ten powers and the four fearlessnesses;
With perfected wisdom free from all obstruction, He turns the Dharma wheel of twelve aspects.
Universally knowing suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, And minutely discerning the dharma of dependent origination,
With unimpeded eloquence in explaining the meaning of dharmas, He fearlessly proclaims them far and wide because of this.
All phenomena are selfless and devoid of marks; the nature of karma neither arises nor perishes.
All things are utterly remote like space, yet the Buddha can discern them through skillful means.
The Tathāgata thus turns the wheel of Dharma, universally shaking all lands throughout the ten directions;
palaces, mountains, and rivers all tremble, yet he causes no sentient being to feel alarm or fear.
The Tathāgata universally proclaims a vast and sublime sound, causing all to understand according to their faculties and inclinations;
he causes them all to resolve their minds and eliminate the defilements of delusion, yet the Buddha never gives rise to a single thought of intentionality.
Some hear of generosity, morality, patience, diligence, Meditative concentration, wisdom, and skillful means;
Some hear of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, In various words and distinct sounds;
Some hear of the four foundations of mindfulness and the four right efforts, The bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, and the Path.
The various recollections, supernormal powers, tranquility, insight, and so forth— The immeasurable skillful means and all dharma-gates.
To the dragons, spirits, the eight classes of beings, humans, non-humans, And the hosts of devas such as Brahmā, Śakra, and the World-Protectors—
The Buddha preaches the Dharma for them with a single voice, Causing each to understand according to their own kind.
Whether there be greed, hatred, and delusion, Or anger, concealment, stinginess, envy, pride, and flattery—
For the eighty-four thousand varieties of afflictions, He causes them to hear the teaching of their respective remedies.
If pure and wholesome dharmas have not yet been cultivated, cause them to hear the exposition of the ten precepts;
for those who are already capable of practicing generosity and self-restraint, cause them to hear the sound of quiescent nirvāṇa.
If there are those whose resolve is weak and who lack compassion, who loathe birth and death and seek only their own escape,
let them hear the teaching of the three gates of liberation, so that they may emerge from suffering and attain the bliss of nirvana.
If there are those who possess little desire by nature, who weary of and turn their backs on the three realms of existence in pursuit of tranquility,
cause them to hear the exposition of dependent origination, so that they may attain liberation by means of the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle.
If there are those with pure and vast minds, who have perfected the merits of generosity and precepts,
who draw near to the Tathāgata and possess compassion, may they hear the sound of the Mahāyāna being proclaimed.
In some lands, they hear of the One Vehicle; in others, two, three, four, or five, and so on until there is no limit—this is entirely the power of the Tathāgata’s skillful means.
Nirvāṇa is quiescent and without distinction; it is only the excellence or inferiority of wisdom and practice that creates difference.
It is like the nature of space, which is one and the same, yet the flight of birds—whether far or near—is each distinct.
The Buddha’s body and voice are likewise: they pervade the entirety of the realm of empty space;
yet according to the differences in the mental faculties and wisdom of sentient beings, what is heard and what is seen each varies.
The Buddha, having cultivated all practices in the past, Is able to manifest wondrous sounds according to the inclinations of others;
Without mental calculation of "this" or "that," He considers not who he should speak for, nor whom he should not.
The Tathāgata’s face emits great rays of light, numbering eighty-four thousand;
the Dharma-gates he teaches are likewise so, universally illuminating the world and eliminating afflictions.
Perfectly pure in merit and wisdom, you always accord with the three worlds;
like space, you are free from defilement, yet you manifest for the sake of sentient beings.
He manifests the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death, And likewise manifests dwelling in the world throughout his lifespan;
Though he appears in such ways in accordance with the world, His essential nature is pure like space.
All lands are without limit, and the faculties and inclinations of sentient beings are likewise immeasurable;
with the eye of Tathāgata-wisdom, he sees them all clearly, and according to what is needed for their transformation, he reveals the Buddha-way.
Throughout the entirety of the empty realms of the ten directions, among all the assemblies of humans and devas,
according to their various differing forms and appearances, the Buddha manifests his body in just the same way.
If one is among the great assembly of śramaṇas, shaving off beard and hair and donning the kāṣāya robe,
holding the robes and bowl and guarding the sense faculties, one shall cause them to rejoice and bring their afflictions to rest.
When he associates with brahmins, he manifests a lean and emaciated body;
holding a staff and carrying a water jar, he is ever pure, endowed with wisdom, and skilled in eloquent discourse.
Exhaling the old and inhaling the new to satisfy himself, he draws in the wind and drinks the dew as his sustenance;
whether sitting or standing, he remains unmoving, manifesting various ascetic practices to subdue those of heterodox paths.

Some uphold those precepts and act as teachers of the world; they are well-versed in medical arts and various treatises, including writing, mathematics, astronomy, and the signs of the earth, as well as the auspicious and inauspicious omens of the body—there is nothing they do not understand.
They enter deeply into the various dhyānas and liberations, The practices of samādhi, supernatural powers, and wisdom;
Through conversation, chanting, and shared play, They employ skillful means to cause all to abide in the Buddha-way.
Sometimes he manifests noble robes to adorn his body, with a flower crown upon his head shaded by a high parasol;
surrounded on all sides by the fourfold army, he assembles the multitudes, proclaims his majesty, and subdues the minor kings.
