Sometimes he acts as a judge to hear lawsuits and decide legal cases; through many skillful means, he restrains evil and encourages goodness.
Whether granting or withholding [punishment or favor], he is always clear and discerning, causing all to respond with joy and reverence, fully accepting his authority.
Sometimes acting as chief ministers and counselors, they skillfully employ the governance and legal systems of various kings;
their benefits for the ten directions are universal and pervasive, and they thoroughly understand all worldly matters without exception.
Sometimes appearing as minor kings scattered like grains of millet, or as flying universal monarchs (cakravartin),
they cause all the princes and retinues of court ladies to receive their transformative teachings and practice them with devotion.
Sometimes he becomes one of the Four World-Protecting Heavenly Kings, or a lord of yakṣas, nāgas, and the like;
for each of their assemblies he preaches the Dharma, causing them all to rejoice greatly.
Sometimes he becomes the Great Heavenly King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, dwelling in the Sudharma Hall and the Nandana Garden;
wearing a flower crown upon his head, he proclaims the wondrous Dharma, which all the devas revere and look up to, unable to fathom.
Sometimes dwelling in the heavens of Yāma or Tuṣita, or in the abodes of Nirmāṇarati, Vaśavartin, or the Māras,
they reside in palaces of maṇi jewels, preaching the practice of truth to bring about subduing.
Sometimes he goes into the assemblies of the Brahma heavens, preaching the four immeasurables and the various paths of dhyāna;
he causes all to rejoice and then departs, yet no one knows the manner of his coming and going.
Or reaching as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven, he speaks for them of the precious flowers of the factors of enlightenment and other immeasurable noble virtues;
only then does he depart, leaving those who lack wisdom behind.
As seen by the Tathāgata’s unimpeded wisdom, all sentient beings therein are taught and brought to maturity through various means and boundless doors of skillful expedient.
Just as a master illusionist, skilled in magical arts, manifests various illusory phenomena,
so too does the Buddha transform sentient beings, manifesting for them all manner of bodies.
Like the pure lunar disc in the void, causing the beings of the world to see its waxing and waning;
it manifests its reflection in all rivers and ponds, while all the stars are eclipsed by its brilliance.
The moon of the Tathāgata’s wisdom appears in the world, yet through skillful means it displays both waxing and waning;
in the water of the Bodhisattvas’ minds its reflection appears, while the constellations of the two vehicles lack its radiance and color.
Just as the great ocean is filled with jewels, pure, unturbid, and boundless,
so do all sentient beings throughout the four continents manifest their reflections therein.
The ocean of the Buddha’s bodily merits is likewise: stainless, unclouded, and boundless;
throughout all sentient beings within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), there is none in whom his image does not appear.

Just as the pure sun emits a thousand rays, Remaining unmoved from its original place yet pervading the ten directions, The radiance of the Buddha-sun is likewise: Neither going nor coming, it dispels the darkness of the world.
Just as when a dragon king sends down a great rain, it does not emerge from his body nor from his mind,
yet it is able to moisten and saturate everywhere, washing away the scorching heat and bringing refreshing coolness.
The Dharma rain of the Tathāgata is likewise: it does not issue from the body or mind of the Buddha, yet it can awaken all sentient beings and completely extinguish the fires of the three poisons.
The Tathāgata’s pure and wondrous Dharma-body Is peerless throughout all the three realms;
Transcending the path of worldly language, Its fundamental nature is neither existent nor non-existent.
Though there is nothing to rely upon, yet there is nothing not relied upon; thus there is neither coming nor going.
Like space, like the sun, and like a dream—thus should one contemplate the body of the Buddha.
All phenomena within the three realms, whether existent or non-existent, cannot serve as analogies for the Buddha;
just as among the birds and beasts of the mountains and forests, there is none that dwells by relying upon space.
The mani-jewels of the great ocean possess infinite colors, and the distinctions of the Buddha’s body are likewise so;
the Tathāgata is neither form nor non-form, appearing according to what is appropriate, yet dwelling nowhere.
Space, suchness, and the limit of reality, Nirvana, the dharma-nature,
and cessation— Only such true dharmas as these Can be manifested by the Tathāgata.

The atoms within all lands may be counted, The waters within the great oceans may be drunk dry, Space may be measured and the wind may be bound; Yet no one can fully describe the virtues of the Buddha.

If there are those who hear of this ocean of merit and can give rise to a heart of joy, faith, and delight, they shall obtain everything as it has been extolled; be careful not to harbor doubts regarding this.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-nine;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Forty.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kapiśī by Imperial Decree.
In the "Chapter on the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra for Entering the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation," at that time,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, having praised the supreme merits of the Tathāgata, addressed the bodhisattvas and Sudhana, saying:
"O sons of good family!

As for the merits of the Tathāgata, even if all the Buddhas of the ten directions were to continuously expound them for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands, they could never be exhausted.
If one wishes to accomplish this gateway of merit, one should cultivate ten kinds of vast practices and vows.

What are these ten? First, prostrating to all Buddhas; second, praising the Tathāgatas; third, extensively making offerings; fourth, repenting of karmic obstructions; fifth, rejoicing in merits; sixth, requesting the turning of the wheel of Dharma; seventh, requesting the Buddhas to remain in the world; eighth, constantly following the Buddhas in their learning; ninth, always acting in accordance with sentient beings; tenth, universally dedicating [all merit].
Sudhana said: "O Great Sage!
How does one perform prostration, and so forth, up to the dedication of merit?"
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said to Sudhana:
"Good son, as for what is called 'paying homage to all Buddhas':”

To all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time across the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—I, by the power of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, give rise to profound faith and understanding as if they were standing before my very eyes; with pure actions of body, speech, and mind, I constantly practice prostration and respect.

At the site of each and every Buddha, I manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands; with each body, I universally prostrate to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands.
Even if the realm of empty space were to end, my prostrations would then end; yet because the realm of empty space can never be exhausted, these prostrations and respects of mine are without end.
In this way, until the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, my prostrations shall come to an end.

Yet, because the realm of sentient beings and even their afflictions have no end, these prostrations of mine are without limit; they continue from thought to thought without interruption, and my physical, verbal, and mental actions never grow weary or exhausted.
"Furthermore, good son, regarding what is called 'praising the Tathāgata':

within every single atom of all the lands throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, as far as the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space extends, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in all worlds; and at the site of each Buddha, there are assemblies of Bodhisattvas surrounding them like an ocean. I shall, with profound and supreme resolve, perceive and know them all directly before me."

Each, by means of the subtle tongue-roots of the goddess Sarasvatī that transcend all, produced from each individual tongue-root an ocean of inexhaustible sounds; from each sound emerged an ocean of all verbal expressions, extolling and praising the oceans of merits of all Tathāgatas, continuing without interruption until the end of the future, pervading the entire Dharma-realm without exception.

Even if the realm of space were exhausted, the realm of sentient beings were exhausted, the karma of sentient beings were exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings were exhausted, my praise would come to an end.

Yet, because the realm of space and even the afflictions have no end, this praise of mine is without exhaustion; it continues from thought-moment to thought-moment without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary.
"Furthermore, good son! Regarding what is called 'extensively cultivating offerings':

within every single atom of all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time across the entire Dharma-realm and space-realm—wherein each atom contains as many Buddhas as there are atoms in all worlds, and each Buddha is surrounded by an ocean-like assembly of various Bodhisattvas—I, through the power of Samantabhadra’s vows and practices, give rise to profound faith and understanding and perceive them directly before me, making offerings with all manner of supreme and exquisite articles of worship."
That is to say:

clouds of flowers, clouds of garlands, clouds of celestial music, clouds of celestial parasols, clouds of celestial garments, and clouds of various celestial incenses—unguents, burning incense, and powdered incense—each of these clouds being as vast in measure as Sumeru, the King of Mountains;

and lighting various lamps—butter lamps, oil lamps, and lamps of various fragrant oils—with each lamp-wick as large as Mount Sumeru and each lamp-oil as deep as the waters of the great ocean, constantly making offerings with such articles of worship.
"Good son! Among all forms of offering, the offering of the Dharma is supreme.
That is to say:"

These are: the offering of practicing as taught; the offering of benefiting sentient beings; the offering of gathering in sentient beings; the offering of taking on the suffering of sentient beings; the offering of diligently cultivating roots of goodness; the offering of not abandoning the bodhisattva deeds; and the offering of not departing from the bodhicitta.

Good son! Compared to the merit of the aforementioned immeasurable offerings, the merit of a single moment of Dharma-offering exceeds it such that the former does not equal even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta part, a kāla part, a calculation part, a number part, a comparison part, or even an upaniṣad part of the latter.
Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas hold the Dharma in high esteem, and because it is through practicing according to the teachings that all Buddhas are born.
If Bodhisattvas practice the offering of the Dharma, they thereby achieve the offering to the Tathāgatas; for such practice is the true offering.

This vast and supreme offering shall only come to an end when the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted; only then will my offering reach its end.

Since the realm of empty space and even the afflictions are inexhaustible, this offering of mine is likewise inexhaustible; it continues from moment to moment without interruption, and my physical, verbal, and mental actions are never weary or exhausted.
"Furthermore, good son, regarding what is called 'repenting and eliminating karmic obstacles':

the bodhisattva reflects to himself, 'Throughout the beginningless kalpas of the past, due to greed, anger, and ignorance, I have produced all manner of evil karma through body, speech, and mind, in measureless and boundless quantities.'"
If these evil karmas possessed a substantial form or characteristic, the entire realm of empty space could not contain them.

Now, with my three karmas entirely purified, I sincerely repent before all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the lands of atoms pervading the entire Dharma-realm; henceforth I shall not create them again, but shall forever abide in the merit of all pure precepts.

Thus, my repentance shall end only when the realm of empty space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted.

Since the realm of empty space and even the afflictions of sentient beings can never be exhausted, this repentance of mine is without end; it continues from thought to thought without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind are never weary or exhausted.
"Furthermore, good son, as for what is called 'the merit of sympathetic joy' (anumodana):"

I rejoice in all the roots of goodness of all the Buddha-Tathāgatas throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—in all Buddha-lands of the ten directions and the three periods of time, as numerous as the atoms within them—from their first aspiration for omniscience until they diligently cultivated masses of merit, disregarding their own bodies and lives, passing through unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-lands, in each and every kalpa relinquishing heads, eyes, hands, and feet as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands; through such difficult practices and asceticisms, they perfected various gates of the pāramitās, entered various stages of Bodhisattva wisdom, accomplished the unsurpassed enlightenment and parinirvāṇa of all Buddhas, and distributed their relics—all these roots of goodness I rejoice in with full accord.

Furthermore, regarding all the merits of every kind of being within the six realms and four modes of birth across all worlds in the ten directions—even down to a single speck of dust—I rejoice in them all.
I rejoice in all the merits of all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas—those still in training and those beyond training—throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time.

I rejoice in all the immeasurable difficult practices and ascetic austerities cultivated by all bodhisattvas, and in their vast merits as they aspire for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Thus, even when the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, my rejoicing shall never come to an end; it shall continue from moment to moment without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind shall never grow weary or exhausted.
"Furthermore, good son! Regarding the request to turn the wheel of Dharma:

within every single atom of all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time across the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—each containing unspeakably unspeakable numbers of vast Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms of those lands—and within each such land, in every thought-moment, there are Buddhas attaining perfect enlightenment, surrounded by oceans of assemblies of Bodhisattvas; with my body, speech, and mind, through various skillful means, I earnestly entreat them to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma."

Thus, even when the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, I shall constantly exhort all Buddhas to turn the wheel of the True Dharma without end; moment after moment, in continuous succession without interruption, my actions of body, speech, and mind shall never grow weary or exhausted.
"Furthermore, good son! Regarding what is called 'entreaty for the Buddhas to remain in the world':

for all the Tathāgatas throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—in all ten directions and three periods of time—within Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms of a single minute particle, who are about to manifest *parinirvāṇa*, as well as all Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, those in training (*śaikṣa*), and those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*), and even all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*)—I entreat them all not to enter *nirvāṇa*, so that they may bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings for as many eons as there are atoms in all Buddha-lands."

Even when the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, my this exhortation shall never come to an end; it shall continue from thought-moment to thought-moment without interruption, and my physical, verbal, and mental actions shall never grow weary or exhausted.
"Furthermore, good son! As for the phrase 'constantly following and learning from the Buddha':

in this Sahā world, Vairocana Tathāgata, from his first generation of the bodhicitta, practiced with diligence without regression, offering up unspeakably unspeakable numbers of bodies and lives as acts of giving;

They flayed their skin to make paper, broke their bones to make pens, and drew their blood to make ink, copying the scriptures until they were piled as high as Mount Sumeru; for the sake of honoring the Dharma, they did not spare even their own bodies or lives, let alone their kingships, cities, villages, palaces, gardens, and all other possessions, nor any other various difficult practices and asceticisms, up to and including attaining great enlightenment under the tree, manifesting various supernatural powers, performing various transformations, appearing in various Buddha-bodies, and dwelling amidst various assemblies.

Sometimes he dwells in the assembly circles of all the great bodhisattvas; sometimes in the assembly circles of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; sometimes in the assembly circles of universal monarchs, minor kings, and their retinues; sometimes in the assembly circles of kṣatriyas, brahmins, elders, and householders; and even sometimes in the assembly circles of the eight classes of beings—devas, nāgas, and so forth—including humans and non-humans.

Abiding within such various assemblies, with a perfect voice like the roar of a great thundercloud, he brings sentient beings to maturity according to their inclinations, even manifesting entry into parinirvāṇa.
All of this I have studied and followed.

Just as the World-Honored One Vairocana does now, so too do all Tathāgatas within every atom of all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time across the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of space; in every thought-moment, I study and follow them all.

Even if the realm of space were to end, the realm of sentient beings were to end, the karma of sentient beings were to end, and the afflictions of sentient beings were to end, my emulation of this practice would never come to an end; it continues from thought to thought without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or exhausted.
"Furthermore, good son! As for 'constantly conforming to sentient beings':
this refers to all the various distinctions among sentient beings throughout the ocean of lands in the ten directions, as far as the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space. That is to say:
There are those born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, and born by transformation;
some are born and dwell depending on earth, water, fire, or wind, while others are born and dwell depending on space or various plants and trees—
beings of diverse kinds, diverse physical forms, diverse shapes, and diverse appearances.
With various lifespans, various species, various names, various mental dispositions, various cognitions and views,
various desires and inclinations, various mental activities, various modes of deportment, various garments,
and various foods and drinks, they dwell in various villages, camps, and settlements.
...cities, towns, and palaces, as well as all the eight classes of devas and nāgas, humans, and non-humans;
those without feet, with two feet, four feet, or many feet; those with form and without form;
those with perception, without perception, and neither with nor without perception—all such categories as these, I—
They all act in accordance with them, performing various services and various offerings,
just as they would honor their parents, serve their teachers and elders, or attend upon Arhats and even Tathāgatas, without any difference.

For those suffering from illness, he acts as a skilled physician; for those who have lost their way, he shows them the correct path; in the darkness of night, he provides illumination; and for those who are impoverished, he enables them to find hidden treasures. In this manner, the Bodhisattva impartially benefits all sentient beings.
Why is this? If a bodhisattva can accord with sentient beings, they are thereby acceding to and making offerings to all Buddhas;
if they honor and serve sentient beings, they are thereby honoring and serving the Tathāgatas.
If one causes sentient beings to give rise to joy, then one causes all Tathāgatas to rejoice.
Why is this? Because all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, take great compassion as their very essence.
Out of sentient beings, one gives rise to great compassion; out of great compassion, one generates the bodhicitta; and by means of the bodhicitta, one achieves equal and perfect enlightenment.
It is like a great king of trees in a vast wilderness of sand and gravel: if its roots receive water, its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits will all flourish and grow luxuriantly.
The King of Bodhi Trees in the wilderness of birth and death is likewise so.

All sentient beings constitute its roots, while all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas constitute its flowers and fruits. By nourishing sentient beings with the water of great compassion, one is able to bring to fruition the flowers and fruits of the wisdom of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Why is this? Because if bodhisattvas benefit sentient beings with the water of great compassion, they will be able to accomplish *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Therefore, enlightenment belongs to sentient beings; if there were no sentient beings, no bodhisattva would ever be able to achieve unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Good son!
You should understand this matter in this way:

because one’s mind is impartial toward all sentient beings, one is able to accomplish the perfection of great compassion; and because one follows after sentient beings with a heart of great compassion, one is able to accomplish the making of offerings to the Tathāgata.

In this way, the bodhisattva accords with sentient beings; even when the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, my accord with them remains without end. Moment after moment it continues in succession without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or fatigued.
"Furthermore, good son! Regarding what is called 'universally dedicating':

all merits from the initial prostration through to the practice of compliance are entirely dedicated to all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space. One vows that these sentient beings may always attain peace and happiness, and be free from all illness and suffering."
May all attempts to commit unwholesome deeds fail to be accomplished, and may all wholesome karmas they cultivate quickly reach fulfillment;
may the gates to all evil realms be closed, and the true path to the human and celestial realms and to nirvāṇa be revealed;
and if there are sentient beings who, due to the accumulation of various evil karmas, experience all manner of most grievous fruits of suffering, may I take them all upon myself in their stead.
May all those sentient beings attain complete liberation and ultimately achieve unsurpassed bodhi.

When the Bodhisattva practices dedication in this manner, even if the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, my dedication shall never come to an end. It continues from moment to moment without interruption, and in the actions of body, speech, and mind, there is no weariness or fatigue.
"Good son! These are the ten great vows of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, fully perfected and complete.

If Bodhisattvas accord with and enter into these great vows, they will be able to bring all sentient beings to maturity; they will be able to accord with *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; and they will be able to fulfill the ocean of practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."
Therefore, son of good family,
you should understand this meaning in this way:

If there were a son or daughter of good family who, with the most excellent and wondrous seven treasures filling all worlds throughout the ten directions—as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields—and with the most supreme peace and happiness of all humans and devas, were to bestow these upon all sentient beings in those worlds and make offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in those worlds, continuing this without interruption for as many eons as there are atoms in those Buddha-fields; compared to the merit obtained by such a person, if another person were to hear the name of this *Vow-King Sūtra* just once, the former merit would not equal even one hundredth part of the latter, nor one thousandth part, nor even one *upaniṣad*-part.

Furthermore, if there are those who, with deep faith, uphold, recite, or even transcribe a single four-line verse of this Great Vow, they will swiftly be able to extinguish the five deeds of immediate retribution. All physical and mental illnesses of the world, various forms of suffering and affliction, and even all evil karma as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, shall all be eliminated.

All demonic armies, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, bhūtas, and other blood-drinking, flesh-eating malevolent spirits and ghosts will all keep their distance; or, at times, they may resolve to draw near and provide protection.

Therefore, if there are those who recite this vow, they shall proceed through the world without obstruction, like the moon emerging from the clouds and mist. They will be praised by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; all humans and devas should pay them homage, and all sentient beings should offer them sustenance.

This son of good family has well attained a human body and perfected all the merits of Samantabhadra. Before long, he shall become like the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and swiftly achieve a subtle and wondrous form-body, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man. Whether born among humans or devas, wherever he may be, he will always dwell in a preeminent lineage. He is able to destroy all evil realms, distance himself from all evil friends, subdue all heterodox teachers, and liberate himself from all afflictions. Like a lion king crushing a herd of beasts, he is worthy of receiving the offerings of all sentient beings.

Furthermore, when this person approaches the end of life, at the final moment, all their faculties will completely disintegrate; all kinsmen and relatives will abandon them; and all power and majesty will utterly vanish. From the high ministers and great officials to those within and without the palace precincts, as well as elephants, horses, chariots, and precious hidden treasures—none of these will follow after them. Only this King of Vows will not forsake them, leading them from the front at all times.

In a single kṣaṇa, one attains rebirth in the World of Ultimate Bliss; having arrived, one immediately beholds Amitābha Buddha, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and others—all these bodhisattvas being of exquisite and dignified appearance, fully endowed with merit, and surrounding him.
That person sees themselves born within a lotus flower and receives a prophecy from the Buddha;

having received the prophecy, after the passage of countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas, they universally bring benefit to sentient beings throughout unspeakably unspeakable worlds in the ten directions by the power of their wisdom, acting in accordance with the minds of those beings.
Before long, you shall sit at the site of enlightenment, subdue the armies of Māra, attain equal and perfect awakening, and turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma.

You will be able to cause sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field to resolve upon Bodhicitta; according to their faculties and natures, you will teach and transform them until they reach maturity, continuing thus through the ocean-like kalpas of the future to extensively benefit all sentient beings.

"Good son! If those sentient beings hear or believe this King of Great Vows, uphold, recite, and read it, and explain it extensively for others, the merit they possess is such that none except the Buddha, the World-Honored One, can know it."

Therefore, upon hearing this King of Vows, you should not give rise to doubt; you should receive it with careful attention. Having received it, you should be able to read it; having read it, you should be able to recite it; having recited it, you should be able to uphold it, and even transcribe it and explain it extensively for others.
In a single thought-moment, all the practices and vows of these people shall be fulfilled, and the mass of merit they obtain will be immeasurable and boundless.

They will be able to rescue sentient beings from the great ocean of suffering of the afflictions, enabling them to transcend it and all attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, wishing to reiterate this meaning, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“In all worlds throughout the ten directions, To all the Lions among Men of the three periods of time,
With my pure body, speech, and mind, I prostrate to each and every one without exception.”
By the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra’s vows and conduct, I appear before all Tathāgatas;
From one body, I manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms of all lands, Each bowing in worship to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of all lands.
Within a single atom are Buddhas as numerous as atoms, each dwelling amidst an assembly of Bodhisattvas;
so it is with every atom throughout the inexhaustible Dharma-realm—deeply believe that all Buddhas completely fill them.
Each, with oceans of all manner of sounds, universally produces inexhaustible, wondrous speech,
praising the Buddha’s ocean of profound merit throughout all kalpas of the future.
With the most excellent and wondrous flower garlands, Music, perfumes, and parasols—
With such supreme articles of adornment, I make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
With the most excellent garments and the most excellent incense, with powdered incense, burning incense, and lamps,
each as vast as Mount Sumeru, I offer them all to all the Tathāgatas.
With a mind of vast and supreme resolve, I have deep faith in all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
Through the power of Samantabhadra’s practices and vows, I universally make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed,
hatred, and delusion, Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now repent for them all.
I rejoice in all the merits of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, of those on the two vehicles—
both those still training and those beyond training— and of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
To all the lamps of the world throughout the ten directions, Who first achieved the realization of Bodhi, I now entreat them all:
Please turn the supreme and wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
Whenever the Buddhas wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I entreat them all with utmost sincerity:
May you remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in a buddha-field, To bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
All merit from prostrations, praises, and offerings; Entreaties for the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma;
Rejoicing in and repenting of all roots of goodness— I dedicate them to all sentient beings and the path of Buddhahood.
Following the training of all Tathāgatas, I cultivate the perfect conduct of Samantabhadra;
I make offerings to all Tathāgatas of the past, as well as to the Buddhas of the ten directions in the present.
The future teachers of gods and humans, whose every aspiration is perfectly fulfilled—
may I follow them all throughout the three times and swiftly attain great enlightenment.
All lands throughout the ten directions, vast, pure, and wondrously adorned,
with Tathāgatas surrounded by assemblies, are all beneath the sovereign Bodhi trees.
May all sentient beings throughout the ten directions be free from suffering and affliction, always dwelling in peace and happiness;
may they obtain the benefits of the profound and true Dharma, extinguishing all defilements without exception.
When I practice for the sake of Bodhi, may I attain the memory of past lives throughout all realms of existence;
may I always leave the household life to cultivate pure precepts—stainless, unbroken, and without flaw or leakage.
Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and kumbhāṇḍas, Even humans and non-humans—
The speech of all sentient beings whatsoever, He expounds the Dharma through all their various sounds.
Diligently cultivating the pure pāramitās, Never forgetting the bodhicitta,
Extinguishing all obscurations and defilements without remainder, All sublime practices are fully accomplished.
From all afflictions, karmic actions, and demonic realms, they attain liberation within the paths of the world;
like a lotus flower unsullied by water, and like the sun and moon that do not abide in the sky.
Completely removing all suffering of the evil realms, Equally bestowing happiness upon all living beings,
Thus passing through eons as numerous as the atoms of a world-system, Their benefit to the ten directions remains forever inexhaustible.
I shall always accord with all sentient beings, throughout all future kalpas until the very end;
constantly practicing the vast conduct of Samantabhadra, may I perfect unsurpassed, great Bodhi.
May all those who walk with me gather together in every place;
may our actions of body, speech, and mind be equal, and may we practice and study all vows and conduct in common.
May all spiritual friends who benefit me Reveal to me the practices of Samantabhadra;
May they always wish to assemble with me, And may they always give rise to a heart of joy toward me.
May I always behold all the Tathāgatas, surrounded by their assemblies of Buddha-sons;
may I offer vast and magnificent offerings to them all, without weariness throughout the entirety of future kalpas.
May I uphold the subtle and wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas, Illuminating all practices leading to Bodhi;
May I ultimately purify the path of Samantabhadra, Constantly practicing it throughout all future kalpas.
Throughout all realms of existence, the merit and wisdom I have cultivated are ever inexhaustible;
through concentration, wisdom, skillful means, and liberation, I have attained a treasury of infinite virtues.
Within a single atom are lands as numerous as atoms; In each and every land are inconceivable Buddhas;
Amidst the assemblies surrounding each Buddha, I see them constantly expounding the practices of Bodhi.
Throughout all the oceans of lands in the ten directions, And within every single tip of a hair— the oceans of the three periods of time—
The oceans of Buddhas and the oceans of lands, I have universally practiced throughout oceans of kalpas.
The speech of all Tathāgatas is utterly pure; A single word contains an ocean of myriad sounds.
According to the inclinations and voices of sentient beings, Each and every stream flows forth as an ocean of the Buddhas' eloquence.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, within that inexhaustible ocean of speech, constantly turn the wondrous Dharma wheel of the principle;
through my profound power of wisdom, I am able to enter it universally.
I am able to penetrate deeply into the future, Making all kalpas as a single thought-instant;
All kalpas throughout the three periods of time, I enter them all within the space of a single thought-instant.
In a single thought-moment, I see all the Lions among Men throughout the three periods of time;
I also constantly enter the Buddha’s realm, with its liberation like an illusion and its majestic powers.
Within a single atom at the tip of a hair, I manifest adorned lands of the three periods of time;
into every atom of all the lands of the ten directions, as numerous as hairs, I enter deeply to adorn and purify them.
To all the Lamps that Illuminate the World in the future, Who shall attain enlightenment, turn the wheel of Dharma, awaken all beings, And,
having perfected the Buddha-work, demonstrate parinirvāṇa— I shall go before them all and draw near.
The power of swift and all-pervading spiritual penetrations, The power of universal entry into the Great Vehicle,
The power of universally cultivating wisdom and merit, The power of great compassion that covers all with majestic spirit,
The power of supreme blessings that adorn all with purity, And the power of wisdom that is unattached and independent.
Through the power of meditative concentration, wisdom, and skillful means, He is universally able to accumulate the power of bodhi;
The power of purifying all wholesome karma, The power of destroying all afflictions, The power of subduing all māras, And the power of fulfilling all practices of Samantabhadra.
Universally able to adorn and purify the oceans of all lands, Liberating the ocean of all sentient beings,
Skillfully able to discern the ocean of all dharmas, Able to penetrate deeply into the ocean of wisdom,
Universally able to purify the ocean of all practices, Bringing to fulfillment the ocean of all vows.
I have approached and made offerings to oceans of Buddhas, Practicing without weariness throughout oceans of kalpas.
All the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, And their supreme bodhi, practices, and vows—
I have fully honored and cultivated them all, Awakening to bodhi through the conduct of Samantabhadra.
All Tathāgatas have an eldest son, Whose name is the Honored One Samantabhadra;
I now dedicate all my roots of goodness, Vowing that all my practices of wisdom may be identical to his.
May my body, speech, and mind be ever pure, And likewise may all my actions and buddha-fields be so;
Possessing such wisdom as that of Samantabhadra, May I become equal to him in every respect.
I shall practice the universally pure conduct of Samantabhadra;
fulfilling all the great vows of Mañjuśrī without exception, I shall remain ever tireless throughout the kalpas of the future.
My practice is immeasurable, and I have attained immeasurable merits;
dwelling securely within immeasurable modes of conduct, I have thoroughly mastered all supernormal powers.
The courageous wisdom of Mañjuśrī, And the wise conduct of Samantabhadra—likewise so;
I now dedicate all my roots of goodness, Always practicing and learning in accordance with them all.
Praised by all Buddhas of the three periods of time— Such supreme and great vows as these,
I now dedicate all my roots of goodness In order to attain the extraordinary conduct of Samantabhadra.
May I, when the time comes for my life to end, Have all obstacles completely removed;
May I behold that Buddha Amitābha face-to-face, And immediately attain rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Once I have been reborn in that land, may these great vows be fulfilled before my eyes;
may everything be perfectly accomplished without exception, bringing benefit and happiness to the entire realm of sentient beings.
The assembly of that Buddha was entirely pure; at that time, I was born from a sublime lotus flower.
I personally beheld the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Light, who bestowed upon me the prophecy of awakening in my very presence.
Having received the prophecy from that Tathāgata, they manifest countless hundreds of koṭis of transformation bodies;
with vast and great power of wisdom pervading the ten directions, they universally benefit the realms of all sentient beings.
Until the realm of empty space is exhausted, And until sentient beings, karma, and afflictions are all exhausted—
As long as all these remain inexhaustible, May my vows likewise endure forever without end.
All the boundless lands throughout the ten directions, adorned with myriad jewels as offerings to the Tathāgata,
bestowing the most supreme peace and happiness upon devas and humans, for as many eons as there are atoms in all those lands.
If a person hears this King of Supreme Vows but once and is able to give rise to faith,
seeking supreme bodhicitta with yearning, they shall obtain supreme merit exceeding that [of the former].
Thus one shall always distance oneself from evil associates, forever leave behind all evil realms,
and swiftly behold the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Light, by possessing this most supreme vow of Samantabhadra.
This person has well attained a supreme lifespan; this person has come well to birth among human beings.
Before long, this person shall achieve accomplishment, just like the conduct of that Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
In the past, through the power of a lack of wisdom, I committed the most heinous five acts of immediate retribution;
Yet by reciting this King of Samantabhadra’s Great Vows, They are all swiftly extinguished in a single thought-moment.
His lineage, appearance, and physical form, as well as his marks and wisdom, are all perfectly complete;
no demons or non-Buddhists can defeat him, and he is worthy of being honored by the three realms.
Swiftly proceed to the great King of Trees; having sat there, subdue the hosts of Māra, attain equal and perfect enlightenment, turn the wheel of Dharma, and universally benefit all sentient beings.
If a person recites, upholds, and expounds these vows of Samantabhadra, the karmic fruit thereof can only be realized by a Buddha; they will certainly attain the supreme path of Bodhi.
If a person recites these vows of Samantabhadra, I declare that even a small portion of their roots of goodness will,
in a single thought-moment, become entirely perfected, fulfilling the pure vows for the benefit of all sentient beings.
This sublime conduct of Samantabhadra, I dedicate all its boundless and supreme merit;
may all sentient beings drowning in suffering swiftly proceed to the buddha-field of Amitābha.

At that time, after the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra had spoken these pure verses of the King of Vast Vows of Samantabhadra before the Tathāgata, the youth Sudhana leaped for joy immeasurably, and all the bodhisattvas were filled with great delight.
The Tathāgata praised him, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!"

At that time, while the World-Honored One was expounding this supreme Dharma-gate of the inconceivable realm of liberation for the assembly of noble Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, there were those with Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva as their leader—the great Bodhisattvas and the six thousand bhikṣus whom they had brought to maturity;
those with Maitreya Bodhisattva as their leader—all the great Bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa;

and those with Vimalasamantabhadra Bodhisattva as their leader—all the great Bodhisattvas who are in their final birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*) and abide in the stage of consecration (*abhiṣeka*), as well as the entire multitude of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, numbering as many as the atoms within all the oceans of lands, who had gathered from various worlds throughout the ten directions.

With the Greatly Wise Śāriputra and Mahāmaudgalyāyana as their leaders, the great śrāvakas, along with all the lords of the world among gods and humans, and the entire assembly of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly delighted; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.

The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra, Fascicle Forty. Written by hand by Śrīsvayambhūsimhavikrāntagāmin, a Great Vehicle practitioner of supreme conduct who possesses profound faith in the Dharma of the Most Excellent Sugata and serves as a pure Lion King, this is respectfully offered to the Great Auspicious Heavenly Son of the Great Tang, the Great Country of China, from among the fifty-five noble spiritual friends described in the hundred-thousand verses of the *Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra* concerning the conduct of the youth Sudhana in approaching and serving spiritual friends as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field: the "Chapter on the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra Entering the Sphere of Inconceivable Liberation. May it be respectfully presented.

I humbly pray that the merit and blessings of the Holy King of this Great Nation may rise higher than Mount Sumeru and be deeper and broader than the four great oceans; that the lands of the ten directions may become one single family;

and that through the merit of transcribing this sutra, may those immeasurable accumulations of blessing gather, equaling the entirety of the ocean of worlds within the realm of space and the inexhaustible realm of sentient beings, so that all may become like the youth Sudhana:

attaining the Buddha’s right view, being fully endowed with wisdom, meeting inconceivable true spiritual friends with whom they feel mutual joy, receiving the Buddha’s vast and universal radiance, becoming free from all attachments, and accomplishing the supreme vows and practices of the stainless Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

I humbly pray that through the merit of having transcribed and offered this Mahāyāna sūtra, at the time when Maitreya Tathāgata attains Buddhahood, I may early behold the Great Holy Heavenly King at the Dragon Flower Assembly; may I obtain the wisdom of recollecting past lives and recognize him upon seeing him; may we together receive the Buddha’s prediction, and throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasive Dharma-realm, may all future sentient beings be widely delivered so that they may swiftly attain Buddhahood.

On the eighteenth day of the eleventh month in the eleventh year of the Zhenyuan era, the Sanskrit manuscripts were presented for imperial inspection. On the fifth day of the sixth month in the twelfth year, by imperial decree, the translation was undertaken at Chongfu Temple in Chang’an. It was completed on the twenty-fourth day of the second month in the fourteenth year and submitted to the throne.
The Tripiṭaka Master from Kaśmīra, the Śramaṇa Prajña, recipient of the purple robe, proclaimed the Sanskrit text;
the Śramaṇa Guangji of Tiangong Monastery in the Eastern Capital provided the oral translation; the Śramaṇa Yuanzhao, recipient of the purple robe of Ximing Monastery, received the dictation;
the Śramaṇa Zhirou of Baoshou Monastery performed the revision and arrangement; and the Śramaṇa Zhitong of Baoshou Monastery performed the final revision at Zhengjue Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture.
Śramaṇa Daohong, editor of the text; Śramaṇa Jianxu of Jing Temple, editor of the commentary;
Śramaṇa Daozhang of Dajue Temple, proofreader and verifier of the meaning; Śramaṇa Datong of Qianfu Temple, verifier of the Chan principles;
Śramaṇa Chengguan of Chongfu Temple in Taiyuan Prefecture, final arbiter; Śramaṇa Xusu of Qianfu Temple, final arbiter; and the Official in Charge of Supervision.

May the King’s fortune extend for ten thousand ages, and may the civil and military officials forever dwell in their positions of emolument.

We prostrate ourselves and pray that our late teachers and parents may attain rebirth in the Highest Realm (*uttama-pūjā-gati*), and that all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm may equally partake in this benefit. With my own hand, I have transcribed this newly translated scripture to fill the gaps in the entire canon at the Eastern Pavilion of the Bodhi Monastery in Ximing Temple. May I fulfill my original vow to attend the Buddhas as they appear in the world throughout the coming kalpas, accompany them in their descent into the world, together emerge from the source of suffering, and ascend in unison to Perfect Enlightenment.

Furthermore, may the Three Jewels increase in brilliance, the Wheel of Dharma turn eternally, and these scriptures remain long to uphold the temple, perpetually aspiring to transmit the Lamp of Wisdom. Until the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, may this vow never end.

In the original preface, Dao’an concludes by saying: "I, Dao’an, have presumptuously joined the ranks of the monastic community and am honored to be a descendant of the patriarchs. Although I have seen my nature and practiced cultivation, I have not yet attained the stages of cause and fruition. Yet, were it not for relying on the sutras to chant and propagate the teachings of the vehicle, I could never repay the Buddha’s kindness. I have observed with great concern that the woodblocks for the Tripitaka at Fabao Temple in Sike Creek, Huzhou Prefecture, were destroyed by the fires of war, leaving not a single character remaining. I have repeatedly received requests from Master Sizong of Jitang at Damingqing Temple in Hangzhou Prefecture, who has gathered various mountain Chan masters and virtuous elders to join their voices in exhortation. They say that such a great causal connection is rarely undertaken in this world; if the venerable Gushan and the Baiyun lineage could collaborate to carve the blocks and circulate the teachings, it would truly continue the Buddha’s life-force for both the mundane and supramundane realms. Having received these instructions, Dao’an further reflected to himself:
"The printing blocks for the Tathāgata’s Great Canon are truly not a minor undertaking; how could they be within the capacity of Dao’an’s meager strength?"

He immediately consulted with the monks of the hermitage and the lay devotees (upāsakas); they were all delighted and, giving rise to a rare aspiration, contributed their labor and resources to further my vow.

Furthermore, he received the protection and mindfulness of the General Superintendent of the Buddhist Teachings across the various circuits of Jianghuai, who granted me official credentials and submitted a petition on my behalf to escort me for an audience with the Imperial Preceptor (Shangshi) at the Eight Banners.
The Emperor has issued a sacred edict to protect and sustain the Zen school, thereby accomplishing this supreme undertaking.

Following the commencement of the construction, I pray that all Buddhas, dragon deities, and virtuous spiritual friends will bestow their grace upon me, so that from beginning to end, such conditions may be fulfilled, and my mind remains free of regression or hindrance.

By means of this vast merit, we respectfully pray for the eternal peace and longevity of the Emperor, that the Empress may share his years, and that the Crown Prince and all the Princes may live for a thousand autumns. We further pray for the promotion of rank and the increase of emolument for the civil and military officials. We also extol the Great Imperial Preceptor of the Great Yuan, the National Preceptor of the Great Yuan, the Yanba Shangshi, and the Universal Overseer of Buddhist Teachings throughout the various circuits of Jianghuai—the Grand Master for Upholding the Doctrine and Spreading the Teaching—and the Universal Overseer of Buddhist Teachings throughout the various circuits of Jianghuai—the Grand Master Yongfu—so that they may extensively expound the Vehicle of the Doctrine and together increase their lifespan and fortune. Furthermore, we hope for harmony in the seasons and bountiful harvests, for the abundance of goods and the well-being of the people, so that the four debts of gratitude and all beings within the three realms may fully receive this grace, and all sentient beings may ascend to the other shore.

Written on an auspicious day in the twelfth month of the sixteenth year of the Zhizheng era (the Jimao year), at which time the conditions were ripe.
As previously recorded, our late Master, the Venerable Huizhao Daoshi, considering the gravity of the responsibility for the teachings upon himself, once entrusted me with these words:

“I have accepted the invitations from the masters of various mountains of both Chan and doctrinal schools, as well as from the monasteries of our own sect, to jointly carve the printing blocks for the entire Tripitaka of the Tathāgata. To disseminate the teachings is truly no small karmic connection.”
I am now advanced in years and infirm; I rely entirely upon you and your followers to act with one heart and united effort to fulfill my wish.
Once the construction begins, external affairs shall be overseen and held responsible by the Chief Administrator (Du-si), while internal matters shall be managed and supervised by you.
"You ought to disregard your own life so that we may accomplish our purpose from beginning to end, together repaying the Buddha’s kindness so that our efforts are not in vain.

Following this resolve, I diligently received my teacher's instructions, never daring to slacken even slightly. Unbeknownst to me, my late preceptor, the Venerable Master, passed away in the spring of the eighteenth year of the Zhizhi era at Dayanshou Temple in Dadu. Subsequently, there were four successive lineages of those who held the position of Abbot of the Monastic Registry:
the first successor was my elder brother, Yuetan (Moon Pond), named Ruyi;...
In the autumn of the twenty-first year of the Zhizhi era, Yuetan entered nirvana at the temple; it was then passed to Ruizhi.
In the spring of the following year, Yousou Ruxian succeeded him;
in the winter of the twenty-sixth year of the Zhizhi era, Yousou retired from his position, and Ruizhi once again succeeded to the previous office.

Each reverently received the imperial decree to protect and uphold the religious teachings and accomplish this great cause, beginning from the year Dingchou and ending in Gengyin, for a total of fourteen years.
On the anniversary of the birth of the Crown Prince and the various princes, as well as the promotion of civil and military officials to higher ranks and emoluments,

we humbly pray that under the heavens of Yao and the suns of Shun, the unified realm of mountains and rivers may flourish greatly, and that Your Sacred Son and Divine Descendants may together extend their blessings and long life for a thousand autumns.

In civil affairs, he ranks among the most eminent; in military matters, he stands among those of exceptional merit. Armies chant songs of victory, and the people rest secure in their ordinary occupations. The Buddha-Dharma abides eternally in the world, its appearance being that of a sage of supreme virtue who serves as the teacher of emperors.

He presides over and protects the monastic community, causing the ocean of the teachings to flow forth. Furthermore, it is hoped that those who contribute their strength and wealth will be adorned with blessings and wisdom; that all who hear or see this shall find benefit for body and mind; that the four debts of gratitude may be universally repaid and the three realms of existence fully sustained; and that all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm may together perfect the state of the Omniscient One.
